english: ‘Since I was appointed by the king as a fitting friend for thee, therefore I have a wish to speak to thee in this friendliness of my heart.

sanskrit: ahitāt pratiṣedhaśca hite cānupravartanam | vyasane cāparityāgastrividhaṃ mitralakṣaṇam ||
english: ‘To hinder from what is disadvantageous, to urge to what is advantageous — and not to forsake in misfortune, — these are the three marks of a friend.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ maitrīṃ pratijñāya puruṣārthātparāṅmukham | yadi tvāṃ samupekṣeyaṃ na bhavenmitratā mayi ||
english: ‘If I, after having promised my friendship, were not to heed when thou turnest away from the great end of man, there would be no friendship in me.

sanskrit: tadbravīmi suhṛdbhūtvā taruṇasya vapuṣmataḥ | idaṃ na pratirūpaṃ te strīṣvadākṣiṇyamīdṛśam ||
english: ‘Therefore I speak as thy friend, — such rudeness as this to women is not befitting for one young in years and graceful in person.

sanskrit: anṛtenāpi nārīṇāṃ yuktaṃ samanuvartanam | tadvrīḍāparihārārthamātmaratyarthameva ca ||
english: ‘It is right to woo a woman even by guile, this is useful both for getting rid of shame and for one’s own enjoyment.

sanskrit: saṃnatiscānuvṛttiśca strīṇāṃ hṛdayabaṃdhanam | snehasya hi guṇā yonirmānakāmāśca yoṣitaḥ ||
english: ‘Reverential behaviour and compliance with her wishes are what binds a woman’s heart; good qualities truly are a cause of love, and women love respect.

sanskrit: tadarhasi viśālākṣa hṛdaye 'pi parāṅmukhe | rūpasyāsyānurūpeṇa dākṣiṇyenānuvartitum ||
english: ‘Wilt thou not then, O large-eyed prince, even if thy heart is unwilling, seek to please them with a courtesy worthy of this beauty of thine?

sanskrit: dākṣiṇyamauṣadhaṃ strīṇāṃ dākṣiṇyaṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ param | dākṣiṇyarahitaṃ rūpaṃ niṣpuṣpamiva kānanam ||
english: ‘Courtesy is the balm of women, courtesy is the best ornament; beauty without courtesy is like a grove without flowers.

sanskrit: kiṃ vā dākṣiṇyamātreṇa bhāvenāstu parigrahaḥ | viṣayān durlabhāṃllabdhvā na hyavajñātumarhasi ||
english: ‘But of what use is courtesy by itself? let it be assisted by the heart’s feelings; surely, when worldly objects so hard to attain are in thy grasp, thou wilt not despise them.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ paramiti jñātvā devo 'pi hi puraṃdaraḥ | gautamasya muneḥ patnīmahalyāṃ cakame purā ||
english: ‘Knowing that pleasure was the best of objects, even the god Puraṃdara (Indra) wooed in olden time Ahalyā the wife of the saint Gautama.

sanskrit: agastyaḥ prārthayāmāsa somabhāryāṃ ca rohiṇīm | tasmāt tatsadṛśaṃ lebhe lopāmudrāmiti śrutiḥ ||
english: ‘So too Agastya wooed Rohiṇī, the wife of Soma; and therefore, as Śruti saith, a like thing befell Lopāmudrā.

sanskrit: autathyasya ca bhāryāyāṃ mamatāyāṃ mahātapāḥ | mārutyāṃ janayāmāsa bharadvājaṃ vṛhaspatiḥ ||
english: ‘The great ascetic Vṛhaspati begot Bharadvāja on Mamatā the daughter of the Maruts, the wife of Autathya.

sanskrit: vṛhaspatermahiṣyāṃ ca juhvatyāṃ juhvatāṃ varaḥ | budhaṃ vibudhadharmāṇaṃ janayāmāsa caṃdramāḥ ||
english: ‘The Moon, the best of offerers, begat Budha of divine nature on the spouse of Vṛhaspati as she was offering a libation.

sanskrit: kālīm caiva purā kanyāṃ jalaprabhavasaṃbhavām | jagāma yamunātīre jātarāgaḥ parāśaraḥ ||
english: ‘So too in old time Parāśara, overpowered by passion on the bank of the Yamunā, lay with the maiden Kālī who was the daughter of the son of the Water (Agni).

sanskrit: mātaṃgyāmakṣamālāyāṃ garhitāyāṃ riraṃsayā | kapiṃjalādaṃ tanayaṃ vasiṣṭho 'janayanmuniḥ ||
english: ‘The sage Vaśiṣṭha through lust begot a son Kapiñjalāda on Akṣamālā a despised low-caste woman.

sanskrit: yayātiścaiva rājarṣirvayasyapi vinirgate | viśvācyāpsarasā sārdhaṃ reme caitrarathe vane ||
english: ‘And the seer-king Yayāti, even when the vigour of his prime was gone, sported in the Caitraratha forest with the Apsaras Viśvācī.

sanskrit: strīsaṃsargaṃ vināśāṃtaṃ pāṃḍurjñātvāpi kauravaḥ | mādrīrūpaguṇākṣiptaḥ siṣeve kāmajaṃ sukham ||
english: ‘And the Kaurava king Pāṇḍu, though he knew that intercourse with his wife would end in death, yet overcome by the beauty and good qualities of Mādrī yielded to the pleasures of love.

sanskrit: karālajanakaścaiva hṛtvā brāhmaṇakanyakām | avāpa bhraṃśam apyeva na tu tyajecca manmatham ||
english: ‘And so Karālajanaka, when he carried off the Brāhman’s daughter, incurred loss of caste thereby, but he would not give up his love.

sanskrit: evamādyā mahātmāno viṣayān garhitānapi | ratihetorbubhujire prāgeva guṇasaṃhitān ||
english: ‘Great heroes such as these pursued even contemptible desires for the sake of pleasure, how much more so when they are praiseworthy of their kind?

sanskrit: tvaṃ punarnyāyataḥ prāptān balavān rūpavān yuvā | viṣayānavajānāsi yatra saktamidaṃ jagat ||
english: ‘And yet thou, a young man, possessed of strength and beauty, despisest enjoyments which rightly belong to thee, and to which the whole world is devoted.’

sanskrit: iti śrutvā vacastasya ślakṣṇamāgamasaṃhitam | meghastanitanirghoṣaḥ kumāraḥ pratyabhāṣata ||
english: Having heard these specious words of his, well-supported by sacred tradition, the prince made reply, in a voice like the thundering of a cloud:

sanskrit: upapannamidaṃ vākyaṃ sauhārdavyaṃjakaṃ tvayi | atra ca tvānuneṣyāmi yatra mā duṣṭhu manyase ||
english: ‘This speech manifesting affection is well-befitting in thee; but I will convince thee as to where thou wrongly judgest me.

sanskrit: nāvajānāmi viṣayāñjāne lokaṃ tadātmakam | anityaṃ tu jaganmatvā nātra me ramate manaḥ ||
english: ‘I do not despise worldly objects, I know that all mankind are bound up therein; but remembering that the world is transitory, my mind cannot find pleasure in them.

sanskrit: jarā vyādhiśca mṛtyuśca yadi na syādidaṃ trayam | mamāpi hi manojñeṣu viṣayeṣu ratirbhavet ||
english: ‘Old age, disease, and death — if these three things did not exist, I too should find my enjoyment in the objects that please the mind.

sanskrit: nityaṃ yadyapi hi strīṇāmetadeva vapurbhavet | sasaṃvitkasya kāmeṣu tathāpi na ratiḥ kṣamā ||
english: ‘Yet even though this beauty of women were to remain perpetual, still delight in the pleasures of desire would not be worthy of the wise man.

sanskrit: yadā tu jarayā pītaṃ rūpamāsāṃ bhaviṣyati | ātmano 'pyanabhipretaṃ mohāttatra ratirbhavet ||
english: ‘But since their beauty will be drunk up by old age, to delight therein through infatuation cannot be a thing approved even by thyself.

sanskrit: mṛtyuvyādhijarādharmo mṛtyuvyādhijarātmabhiḥ | ramamāṇo 'pyasaṃvignaḥ samāno mṛgapakṣibhiḥ ||
english: ‘He who himself subject to death, disease, and old age, can sport undisturbed with those whose very nature implies death, disease, and old age, such a man is on a level with birds and beasts.

sanskrit: yadapyāttha mahātmānaste 'pi kāmātmakā iti | saṃvego 'tra na kartavyo yadā teṣāmapi kṣayaḥ ||
english: ‘And as for what thou sayest as to even those great men having become victims to desire, do not be bewildered by them, for destruction was also their lot.

sanskrit: māhātmyaṃ na ca tanmanye yatra sāmānyataḥ kṣayaḥ | viṣayeṣu prasaktirvā yuktirvā nātmavattayā ||
english: ‘Real greatness is not to be found there, where there is universally destruction, or where there is attachment to earthly objects, or a want of self-control.

sanskrit: yadapyātthānṛtenāpi strījane vartyatāmiti | anṛtaṃ nāvagacchāmi dākṣiṇyenāpi kiṃcana ||
english: ‘And when thou sayest, “Let one deal with women even by guile,” I know nought about guile, even if it be accompanied with courtesy.

sanskrit: na cānuvartanaṃ tanme rucitaṃ yatra nārjavam | sarvabhāvena saṃparko yadi nāsti dhigastu tat ||
english: ‘That compliance too with a woman’s wishes pleases me not, if truthfulness be not there; if there be not a union with one’s whole soul and nature, then “out upon it” say I.

sanskrit: anṛte śraddadhānasya saktasyādoṣadarśinaḥ | kiṃ hi vaṃcayitavyaṃ syājjātarāgasya cetasaḥ ||
english: ‘A soul overpowered by passion, believing in falsehood, carried away by attachment and blind to the faults of its objects, — what is there in it worth being deceived?

sanskrit: vaṃcayaṃti ca yadyeva jātarāgāḥ parasparam | nanu naiva kṣamaṃ draṣṭuṃ narāḥ strīṇāṃ nṛṇām striyaḥ ||
english: ‘And if the victims of passion do deceive one another, — are not men unfit for women to look at and women for men?

sanskrit: tadevaṃ sati duḥkhārttaṃ jarāmaraṇabhoginam | na māṃ kāmeṣvanāryeṣu pratārayitumarhasi ||
english: Since then these things are so, thou surely wouldest not lead me astray into ignoble pleasures, — me afflicted by sorrow, and subject to old age and death?

sanskrit: aho 'tidhīraṃ balavacca te manaścaleṣu kāmeṣu ca sāradarśinaḥ | bhaye 'pi tīvre viṣayeṣu sajjase nirīkṣamāṇo maraṇādhvani prajāḥ ||
english: ‘Ah! thy mind must be very firm and strong, if thou canst find substance in the transitory pleasures of sense; even in the midst of violent alarm thou canst cling to worldly objects, when thou seest all created beings in the road of death.

sanskrit: ahaṃ punarbhīruratīvaviklavo jarāvipadvyādhibhayaṃ viciṃtayan | labhe na śāṃtiṃ na dhṛtiṃ kuto ratiṃ niśāmayan dīptamivāgninā jagat ||
english: ‘But I am fearful and exceedingly bewildered, as I ponder the terrors of old age, death, and disease; I can find no peace, no self-command, much less can I find pleasure, while I see the world as it were ablaze with fire.

sanskrit: asaṃśayaṃ mṛtyuriti prajānato narasya rāgo hṛdi yasya jāyate | ayomayīṃ tasya paraimi cetanāṃ mahābhaye rakṣati yo na roditi ||
english: ‘If desire arises in the heart of the man, who knows that death is certain, — I think that his soul must be made of iron, who restrains it in this great terror and does not weep.’

sanskrit: athau kumāraśca viniścayātmikāṃ cakāra kāmāśrayaghātinīṃ kathām | janasya cakṣurgamanīyamaṃḍalo mahīdharaṃ cāstamiyāya bhāskaraḥ ||
english: Then the prince uttered a discourse full of resolve and abolishing the objects of desire; and the lord of day, whose orb is the worthy centre of human eyes, departed to the Western Mountain.

sanskrit: tato vṛthādhāritabhūṣaṇasrajaḥ kalāguṇaiśca praṇayaiśca niṣphalaiḥ | sva eva bhāve vinigṛhya manmathaṃ puraṃ yayurbhagnamanorathāḥ striyaḥ ||
english: And the women, having worn their garlands and ornaments in vain, with their graceful arts and endearments all fruitless, concealing their love deep in their hearts,  returned to the city with broken hopes.

sanskrit: tataḥ purodyānagatāṃ janaśriyaṃ nirīkṣya sāyaṃ pratisaṃhṛtāṃ punaḥ | anityatāṃ sarvagatāṃ viciṃtayan viveśa dhiṣṇyaṃ kṣitipālakātmajaḥ ||
english: Having thus seen the beauty  of the troop of women who had gone out to the city-garden, now withdrawn in the evening, — the prince, pondering the transitoriness which envelopes all things, entered his dwelling.

sanskrit: tato mārabalaṃ jitvā dhairyeṇa ca śamena ca | paramārthaṃ vijijñāsuḥ sa dadhyau dhyānakovidaḥ ||
english: Then, having conquered the hosts of Māra by his firmness and calmness, he the great master of meditation set himself to meditate, longing to know the supreme end.

sanskrit: sarveṣu dhyānavidhiṣu prāpya caiśvaryamuttamam | sasmāra prathame yāme pūrvajanmaparaṃparām ||
english: And having attained the highest mastery in all kinds of meditation, he remembered in the first watch the continuous series of all his former births.

sanskrit: amutrāhamayaṃ nāma cyutastasmādihāgataḥ | iti janmasahasrāṇi sasmārānubhavanniva ||
english: ‘In such a place I was so and so by name, and from thence I passed and came hither,’ thus he remembered his thousands of births, experiencing each as it were over again.

sanskrit: smṛtvā janma ca mṛtyuṃ ca tāsu tāsūpapattiṣu | tataḥ sattveṣu kāruṇyaṃ cakāra karuṇātmakaḥ ||
english: And having remembered each birth and each death in all those various transmigrations, the compassionate one then felt compassion for all living beings.

sanskrit: kṛtveha svajanotsargaṃ punaranyatra ca kriyāḥ | atrāṇaḥ khalu loko 'yaṃ paribhramati cakravat ||
english: Having wilfully rejected the good guides in this life and done all kinds of actions in various lives, this world of living beings rolls on helplessly, like a wheel.

sanskrit: ityevaṃ smaratastasya babhūva niyatātmanaḥ | kadalīgarbhaniḥsāraḥ saṃsāra iti niścayaḥ ||
english: As he thus remembered, to him in his strong self-control came the conviction, ‘All existence is insubstantial, like the fruit of a plantain.’

sanskrit: dvitīye tvāgate yāme so 'dvitīyaparākramaḥ | divyaṃ cakṣuḥ paraṃ lebhe sarvacakṣuṣmatāṃ varaḥ ||
english: When the second watch came, he, possessed of unequalled energy, received a pre-eminent divine sight, like the highest of all sight-gifted beings.

sanskrit: tatastena sa divyena pariśuddhena cakṣuṣā | dadarśa nikhilaṃ lokamādarśa iva nirmale ||
english: Then by that divine perfectly pure sight he beheld the whole world as in a spotless mirror.

sanskrit: sattvānāṃ paśyatastasya nikṛṣṭotkṛṣṭakarmaṇām | pracyutiṃ copapattiṃ ca vavṛdhe karuṇātmatā ||
english: As he saw the various transmigrations and rebirths of the various beings with their several lower or higher merits from their actions, compassion grew up more within him.

sanskrit: ime duṣkṛtakarmāṇaḥ prāṇino yāṃti durgatim | ime 'nye śubhakarmāṇaḥ pratiṣṭhaṃte tripiṣṭape ||
english: ‘These living beings, under the influence of evil actions, pass into wretched worlds, — these others, under the influence of good actions, go forward in heaven.

sanskrit: upapannāḥ pratibhaye narake bhṛśadāruṇe | amī duḥkhairbahuvidhaiḥ pīḍyaṃte kṛpaṇaṃ vata ||
english: ‘The one, being born in a dreadful hell full of terrors, are miserably tortured, alas! by many kinds of suffering;

sanskrit: pāyyaṃte kvathitaṃ kecidagnivarṇamayorasam | āropyaṃte ruvaṃto 'nye niṣṭaptastaṃbhamāyasam ||
english: ‘Some are made to drink molten iron of the colour of fire, others are lifted aloft screaming on a red-hot iron pillar;

sanskrit: pacyaṃte piṣṭavatkecidayaskuṃbhīṣvavāṅmukhāḥ | dahyaṃte karuṇaṃ keciddīpteṣvaṃgārarāśiṣu ||
english: ‘Others are baked like flour, thrown with their heads downwards into iron jars; others are miserably burned in heaps of heated charcoal;

sanskrit: kecittīkṣṇairayodaṃṣṭrairbhakṣyaṃte dāruṇaiḥ śvabhiḥ | keciddhṛṣṭairayastuṃḍairvāyasairāyasairiva ||
english: ‘Some are devoured by fierce dreadful dogs with iron teeth, others by gloating crows with iron beaks and all made as it were of iron;

sanskrit: keciddāhapariśrāṃtāḥ śītacchāyābhikāṃkṣiṇaḥ | asipatraṃ vanaṃ nīlaṃ baddhā iva viśaṃtyamī ||
english: ‘Some, wearied of being burned, long for cold shade; these enter like bound captives into a dark blue wood with swords for leaves.

sanskrit: pāṭyaṃte dāruvat kecitkuṭhārairbahubāhavaḥ | duḥkhe 'pi na vipadyaṃte karmabhirdhāritāsavaḥ ||
english: ‘Others having many arms are split like timber with axes, but even in that agony they do not die, being supported in their vital powers by their previous actions.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ syāditi yatkarma kṛtaṃ duḥkhanivṛttaye | phalaṃ tasyedamavaśairduḥkhamevopabhujyate ||
english: ‘Whatever deed was done only to hinder pain with the hope that it might bring pleasure, its result is now experienced by these helpless victims as simple pain.

sanskrit: sukhārthamaśubhaṃ kṛtvā ya ete bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ | āsvādaḥ sa kimeteṣāṃ karoti sukhamaṇvapi ||
english: These who did something evil for the sake of pleasure and are now grievously pained, — does that old taste produce even an atom of pleasure to them now?

sanskrit: hasadbhiryatkṛtaṃ karma kaluṣaṃ kaluṣātmabhiḥ | etatpariṇate kāle krośadbhiranubhūyate ||
english: ‘The wicked deed which was done by the wicked-hearted in glee, — its consequences are reaped by them in the fulness of time with cries.

sanskrit: yadyeva pāpakarmāṇaḥ paśyeyuḥ karmaṇāṃ phalam | vameyuruṣṇarudhiraṃ marmasvabhihatā iva ||
english: ‘If only evil doers could see the fruits of their actions, they would vomit hot blood as if they were smitten in a vital part.

sanskrit: śārīrebhyo 'pi duḥkhebhyo nārakebhyo manasvinaḥ | anāryaiḥ saha saṃvāso mama kṛcchratamo mataḥ || |
english: ‘And worse still than all these bodily tortures in hell seems to me the association of an intelligent man with the base.

sanskrit: ime 'nye karmabhiścitraiścittavispaṃdasaṃbhavaiḥ | tiryagyonau vicitrāyāmupapannāstapasvinaḥ ||
english: ‘Others also, through various actions arising from the spasmodic violence of their minds, are born miserable in the wombs of various beasts.

sanskrit: māṃsatvagbāladaṃtārthaṃ vairādapi madādapi | hanyaṃte kṛpaṇā yatra baṃdhūnāṃ paśyatāmapi ||
english: ‘There the poor wretches are killed even in the sight of their kindred, for the sake of their flesh, their skin, their hair, or their teeth, or through hatred or for mere pleasure.

sanskrit: aśaknuvaṃto 'pyavaśāḥ kṣuttarṣaśramapīḍitāḥ | go 'śvabhūtāśca vāhyaṃte pratodakṣatamūrtayaḥ ||
english: ‘Even though powerless and helpless, oppressed by hunger, thirst, and fatigue, they are driven along as oxen and horses, their bodies wounded with goads.

sanskrit: vāhyaṃte gajabhūtāśca balīyāṃso 'pi durbalaiḥ | aṃkuśakliṣṭamūrdhānastāḍitāḥ pādapārṣṇibhiḥ ||
english: ‘They are driven along, when born as elephants, by weaker creatures than themselves for all their strength, — their heads tormented by the hook and their bodies kicked by foot and heel.

sanskrit: satsvapyanyeṣu duḥkheṣu duḥkhaṃ yatra viśeṣataḥ | parasparavirodhācca parādhīnatayaiva ca ||
english: ‘And with all these other miseries there is an especial misery arising from mutual enmity and from subjection to a master.

sanskrit: khasthāḥ khasthairhi bādhyaṃte jalasthā jalacāribhiḥ | sthalasthāḥ sthalasaṃsthaistu prāpyaṃte cetaretaraiḥ ||
english: ‘Air-dwellers are oppressed by air-dwellers, the denizens of water by the denizens of water, those that dwell on dry land are made to suffer by the dwellers on dry land in mutual hostility.

sanskrit: upapannāstathā ceme mātsaryākrāṃtacetasaḥ | pitṛloke nirāloke kṛpaṇaṃ bhuṃjate phalam ||
english: ‘And others there are who, when born again, with their minds filled with envy, reap the miserable fruit of their actions in a world of the Pitṛs destitute of all light;

sanskrit: sūcīchidropamamukhāḥ parvatopamakukṣayaḥ | kṣuttarṣajanitairduḥkhaiḥ pīḍyaṃte duḥkhabhāginaḥ ||
english: ‘Having mouths as small as the eye of a needle and bellies as big as a mountain, these miserable wretches are tortured with the pains of hunger and thirst.

sanskrit: puruṣo yadi jānīta mātsaryasyedṛśaṃ phalam | sarvathā śivivaddadyāccharīrāvayavānapi ||
english: ‘If a man only knew that such was the consequence of selfishness, he would always give to others even pieces of his own body like Śibi.

sanskrit: āśayā samabhikrāṃtā ghāryamāṇāḥ svakarmabhiḥ | labhaṃte na hyamī bhoktuṃ pravṛddhānyaśucīnyapi ||
english: ‘Rushing up filled with hope but held back by their former deeds, they try in vain to eat anything large, however impure.

sanskrit: ime 'nye narakaṃ prāpya garbhasaṃjñe 'śucihrade | upapannā manuṣyeṣu duḥkhamarchaṃti jaṃtavaḥ ||
english: ‘Others, having found a hell in an impure lake called the womb, are born amongst men and there suffer anguish.

sanskrit: sa rājavatsaḥ pṛthupīnavakṣāstau havyamaṃtrādhikṛtau vihāya | uttīrya gaṃgāṃ pracalattaraṃgāṃ śrīmadgṛhaṃ rājagṛhaṃ jagāma ||
english: The prince, he of the broad and lusty chest, having thus dismissed the minister and the priest, crossed the Ganges with its speeding waves and went to Rājagṛha with its beautiful palaces.

sanskrit: śailaiḥ suguptaṃ ca vibhūṣitaṃ ca dhṛtaṃ ca pūtaṃ ca śivaistapodaiḥ | paṃcācalāṃkaṃ nagaraṃ prapede śāṃtaḥ svayaṃbhūriva nākapṛṣṭham ||
english: He reached the city distinguished by the five hills, well guarded and adorned with mountains, and supported and hallowed by auspicious sacred places,  — like Brahman  in a holy calm going to the uppermost heaven.

sanskrit: gāṃbhīryamojaśca niśāmya tasya vapuśca dīptaṃ puruṣānatītya | visismiye tatra janastadānīṃ sthāṇuvratasyeva vṛṣadhvajasya ||
english: Having heard of his majesty and strength, and his splendid beauty, surpassing all other men, the people of that region were all astonished as at him who has a bull for his sign and is immovable in his vow.

sanskrit: taṃ prekṣya yo 'nyena yayau sa tasthau yaścātra tasthau pathi so 'nvagacchat | drutaṃ yayau yaṃ sadayaṃ sadhīraṃ yaḥ kaścidāste sma sa cotpapāta ||
english: On seeing him, he who was going elsewhere stood still, and he who was standing there followed him in the way; he who was walking gently and gravely ran quickly, and he who was sitting at once sprang up.

sanskrit: kaścittamānarca janaḥ karābhyāṃ satkṛtya kaścicchirasā vavaṃde | snigdhena kaścidvacasābhyanaṃdannaivaṃ jagāmāpratipūjya kaścit ||
english: Some people reverenced him with their hands, others in worship saluted him with their heads, some addressed him with affectionate words, — not one went on without paying him homage.

sanskrit: taṃ jihriyuḥ prekṣya vicitraveṣāḥ prakīrṇavācaḥ pathi maunamīyuḥ | dharmasya sākṣādiva saṃnikarṣānna kaścidanyāyamatirbabhūva ||
english: Those who were wearing gay-coloured dresses were ashamed when they saw him, those who were talking on random subjects fell to silence on the road; no one indulged in an improper thought, as at the presence of Religion herself embodied.

sanskrit: anyakriyāṇāmapi rājamārge strīṇāṃ nṛṇāṃ vā bahumānapūrvam | tadeva kalpaṃ naradevasūtraṃ nirīkṣamāṇā na tu tasya dṛṣṭiḥ ||
english: In the men and the women on the highway, even though they were intent on other business, that conduct alone with the profoundest reverence seemed proper which is enjoined by the rules of royal homage; but his eyes never looked upon them.

sanskrit: bhruvau lalāṭaṃ mukhamīkṣaṇaṃ vā vapuḥ karau vā caraṇau gatiṃ vā | yadeva yastasya dadarśa tatra tadeva tasyānubabaṃdha cakṣuḥ ||
english: His brows, his forehead, his mouth, or his eyes, — his body, his hands, his feet, or his gait, — whatever part of him any one beheld, that at once riveted his eyes.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā śubhorṇabhruvamāyatākṣaṃ jvalaccharīraṃ śubhajālahastam | taṃ bhikṣuveśaṃ kṣitipālanārhaṃ saṃcukṣubhe rājagṛhasya lakṣmīḥ ||
english: Having beheld him with the beautiful circle of hair between his brows  and with long eyes, with his radiant body and his hands showing a graceful membrane between the fingers, — so worthy of ruling the earth and yet wearing a mendicant’s dress, — the Goddess of Rājagṛha was herself perturbed.

sanskrit: śreṇyo 'tha bhartā magadhājirasya vāhyādvimānādvipulaṃ janaugham | dadarśa papraccha ca tasya hetuṃ tatastamasmai puruṣaḥ śaśaṃsa ||
english: Then Śreṇya,  the lord of the court of the Magadhas, beheld from the outside of his palace the immense concourse of people, and asked the reason of it; and thus did a man recount it to him:

sanskrit: jñānaṃ paraṃ vā pṛthivīśriyaṃ vā viprairya ukto 'dhigamiṣyatīti | sa eva śākyādhipatestanūjo nirīkṣyate pravrajito janena ||
english: ‘He who was thus foretold by the Brāhmans, “he will either attain supreme wisdom or the empire of the earth,” — it is he, the son of the king of the Śākyas, who is the ascetic whom the people are gazing at.’

sanskrit: tataḥ śrutārtho manasā gatārtho rājā babhāṣe puruṣaṃ tameva | vijñāyatāṃ kva pratigacchatīti tathetyathainaṃ puruṣo 'nvagacchat ||
english: The king, having heard this and perceived its meaning with his mind, thus at once spoke to that man: ‘Let it be known whither he is going;’ and the man, receiving the command, followed the prince.

sanskrit: alolacakṣuryugamātradarśī nivṛttavāgyaṃtritamaṃdagāmī | cacāra bhikṣāṃ sa tu bhikṣuvaryo nidhāya gātrāṇi calaṃ ca cetaḥ ||
english: With unrestless eyes, seeing only a yoke’s length before him,  with his voice hushed, and his walk slow and measured, he, the noblest of mendicants, went begging alms, keeping his limbs and his wandering thoughts under control.

sanskrit: ādāya bhaikṣaṃ ca yathopapannaṃ yayau gireḥ prasravaṇaṃ viviktam | nyāyena tatrābhyavahṛtya cainanmahīdharaṃ pāṃḍavamāruroha ||
english: Having received such alms as were offered, he retired to a lonely cascade of the mountain; and having eaten it there in the fitting manner, he ascended the mountain Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: tasminvane lodhravanopagūḍhe mayūranādapratipūrṇakuṃje | kāṣāyavāsāḥ sa babhau nṛsūryo yathodayasyopari bālasūryaḥ ||
english: In that wood, thickly filled with lodhra trees, having its thickets resonant with the notes of the peacocks, he the sun of mankind shone, wearing his red dress, like the morning sun above the eastern mountain.

sanskrit: tatraivamālokya sa rājabhṛtyaḥ śreṇyāya rājñe kathayāṃ cakāra | saṃśrutya rājā sa ca bāhumānyāttatra pratasthe nibhṛtānuyātraḥ ||
english: That royal attendant, having thus watched him there, related it all to the king Śreṇya; and the king, when he heard it, in his deep veneration, started himself to go thither with a modest retinue.

sanskrit: sa pāṃḍavaṃ pāṃḍavatulyavīryaḥ śailottamaṃ śailasamānavarṣmā | maulīdharaḥ siṃhagatirnṛsiṃhaścalatsaṭaḥ siṃha ivāruroha ||
english: He who was like the Pāṇḍavas in heroism, and like a mountain in stature, ascended Pāṇḍava, that noblest of mountains, — a crown-wearer, of lion-like gait, a lion among men, as a maned lion ascends a mountain.

sanskrit: calasya tasyopari śṛṃgabhūtaṃ śāṃteṃdriyaṃ paśyati bodhisattvam | paryaṃkamāsthāya virocamānaṃ śaśāṃkamudyaṃtamivābhrakūṭāt ||
english: There he beheld the Bodhisattva, resplendent as he sat on his hams, with subdued senses, as if the mountain were moving,  and he himself were a peak thereof, — like the moon rising from the top of a cloud.

sanskrit: taṃ rūpalakṣmyā ca śamena caiva dharmasya nirmāṇamivopadiṣṭam | savismayaḥ praśrayavān nareṃdraḥ svayaṃbhuvaṃ śakra ivopatasthe ||
english: Him, distinguished by his beauty of form and perfect tranquillity as the very creation of Religion herself, — filled with astonishment and affectionate regard the king of men approached, as Indra the self-existent (Brahman).

sanskrit: taṃ nyāyato nyāyavatāṃ variṣṭhaḥ sametya papraccha ca dhātusāmyam | sa cāpyavocatsadṛśena sāmnā nṛpaṃ manaḥsvāsthyamanāmayaṃ ca ||
english: He, the chief of the courteous, having courteously drawn nigh to him, inquired as to the equilibrium of his bodily humours; and the other with equal gentleness assured the king of his health of mind and freedom from all ailments.

sanskrit: tataḥ śucau vāraṇakarṇanīle śilātale 'sau niṣasāda rājā | nṛpopaviśyānumataśca tasya bhāvaṃ vijijñāsuridaṃ babhāṣe ||
english: Then the king sat down on the clean surface of the rock, dark blue like an elephant’s ear; and being seated,  with the other’s assent, he thus spoke, desiring to know his state of mind:

sanskrit: prītiḥ parā me bhavataḥ kulena kramāgatā caiva parīkṣitā ca | jātā vivakṣā suta yā yato me tasmādidaṃ snehavaco nibodha ||
english: ‘I have a strong friendship with thy family, come down by inheritance and well proved; since from this a desire to speak to thee, my son, has arisen in me, therefore listen to my words of affection.

sanskrit: ādityapūrvaṃ vipulaṃ kulaṃ te navaṃ vayo dīptamidaṃ vapuśca | kasmādiyaṃ te matirakrameṇa bhaikṣāka evābhiratā na rājye ||
english: ‘When I consider thy widespread race, beginning with the sun, thy fresh youth, and thy conspicuous beauty, — whence comes this resolve of thine so out of all harmony with the rest, set wholly on a mendicant’s life, not on a kingdom?

sanskrit: gātraṃ hi te lohitacaṃdanārhaṃ kāṣāyasaṃśleṣamanarhametat | hastaḥ prajāpālanayogya eṣa bhoktuṃ na cārhaḥ paradattamannam ||
english: ‘Thy limbs are worthy of red sandal-wood  perfumes, — they do not deserve the rough contact of red cloth; this hand is fit to protect subjects, it deserves not to hold food given by another.

sanskrit: tatsaumya rājyaṃ yadi paitṛkaṃ tvaṃ snehātpiturnecchasi vikrameṇa | na ca kṣamaṃ marṣayituṃ matiste bhuktvārdhamasmadviṣayasya śīghram ||
english: ‘If therefore, gentle youth, through thy love for thy father thou desirest not thy paternal kingdom in thy generosity, — then at any rate thy choice must not be excused, — accepting forthwith one half of my kingdom.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi na syātsvajanāvamardaḥ kālakrameṇāpi śamaśrayā śrīḥ | tasmātkuruṣva praṇayaṃ mayi tvaṃ sadbhiḥ sahīyā hi satāṃ samṛddhiḥ ||
english: ‘If thou actest thus there will be no violence shown to thine own people, and by the mere lapse of time imperial power at last flies for refuge to the tranquil mind; therefore be pleased to do me a kindness, — the prosperity of the good becomes very powerful, when aided by the good.

sanskrit: atha tvidānīṃ kulagarvitatvādasmāsu viśraṃbhaguṇo na te 'sti | vyūhānyanekāni vigāhya vāṇairmayā sahāyena parāñjigīṣa ||
english: ‘But if from thy pride of race thou dost not now feel confidence in me, then plunge with thy arrows into countless armies, and with me as thy ally seek to conquer thy foes.

sanskrit: tadbuddhimatrānyatarāṃ vṛṇīṣva dharmārthakāmān vidhivadbhajasva | vyatyasya rāgādi ha hi trivargaṃ pretyeha vibhraṃśamavāpnuvaṃti ||
english: ‘Choose thou therefore one of these ends, pursue according to rule religious merit, wealth, and pleasure; for these, love and the rest, in reverse order, are the three objects in life; when men die they pass into dissolution as far as regards this world.

sanskrit: yo hyarthadharmau paripīḍya kāmaḥ syāddharmakāmye paribhūya cārthaḥ | kāmārthayoścoparameṇa dharmastyājyaḥ sa kṛtsno yadi kāṃkṣitārthaḥ ||
english: ‘That which is pleasure when it has overpowered wealth and merit, is wealth when it has conquered merit and pleasure; so too it is merit, when pleasure and wealth fall into abeyance; but all would have to be alike abandoned, if thy desired end  were obtained.

sanskrit: tasmāttrivargasya niṣevaṇena tvaṃ rūpametatsaphalaṃ kuruṣva | dharmārthakāmādhigamaṃ hyanūnaṃ nṛṇāmanūnaṃ puruṣārthamāhuḥ ||
english: ‘Do thou therefore by pursuing the three objects of life, cause this beauty of thine to bear its fruit; they say that when the attainment of religion, wealth, and pleasure is complete in all its parts, then the end of man is complete.

sanskrit: tanniṣphalau nārhasi kartumetau pīnau bhujau cāpavikarṣaṇārhau | māṃdhātṛvajjetumimau hi yogyau lokāni hi trīṇi hi kiṃ punargām ||
english: ‘Do not thou let these two brawny arms lie useless which are worthy to draw the bow; they are well fitted like Māndhātṛ’s to conquer the three worlds, much more the earth.

sanskrit: snehena khalvetadahaṃ bravīmi naiśvaryarāgeṇa na vismayena | imaṃ hi dṛṣṭvā tava bhikṣuveśaṃ jātānukaṃpo 'smyapi cāgatāśruḥ ||
english: ‘I speak this to you out of affection, — not through love of dominion or through astonishment; beholding this mendicant-dress of thine, I am filled with compassion and I shed tears.

sanskrit: tadbhuṃkṣva bhikṣāśramakāma kāmānkāle 'si kartā priyadharma dharmam | yāvatsvavaṃśapratirūparūpaṃ na te jarābhyetyabhibhūya bhūyaḥ ||
english: ‘O thou who desirest the mendicant’s stage of life enjoy pleasures now; in due time, O thou lover of religion, thou shalt practise religion; — ere old age comes on and overcomes this thy beauty, well worthy of thy illustrious race.

sanskrit: śaknoti jīrṇaḥ khalu dharmamāptuṃ kāmopabhogeṣvagatirjarāyāḥ | ataśca yūnaḥ kathayaṃti kāmānmadhyasya vittaṃ sthavirasya dharmam ||
english: ‘The old man can obtain merit by religion; old age is helpless for the enjoyment of pleasures; therefore they say that pleasures belong to the young man, wealth to the middle-aged, and religion to the old.

sanskrit: dharmasya cārthasya ca jīvaloke pratyarthibhūtāni hi yauvanāni | saṃrakṣyamāṇānyapi durgrahāṇi kāmā yatastena yathā haraṃti ||
english: ‘Youth in this present world is the enemy of religion and wealth, — since pleasures, however we guard them, are hard to hold, therefore, wherever pleasures are to be found, there they seize them.

sanskrit: vayāṃsi jīrṇāni vimarśayaṃti dhīrāṇyavasthānaparāyaṇāni | alpena yatnena śamātmakāni bhavaṃtyagatyeva ca lajjayā ca ||
english: ‘Old age is prone to reflection’,  it is grave and intent on remaining quiet; it attains unimpassionedness with but little effort, unavoidably, and for very shame.

sanskrit: ataśca lolaṃ viṣayapradhānaṃ pramattamakṣāṃtamadīrghadarśi | bahucchalaṃ yauvanamabhyatītya nistīrya kāṃtāramivāśvasaṃti ||
english: ‘Therefore having passed through the deceptive period of youth, fickle, intent on external objects, heedless, impatient, not looking at the distance, — they take breath like men who have escaped safe through a forest.

sanskrit: tasmādadhīraṃ capalapramādi navaṃ vayastāvadidaṃ vyapaitu | kāmasya pūrvaṃ hi vayaḥ śaravyaṃ na śakyate rakṣitumiṃdriyebhyaḥ ||
english: ‘Let therefore this fickle time of youth first pass by, reckless and giddy, — our early years are the mark for pleasure, they cannot be kept from the power of the senses.

sanskrit: athau cikīrṣā tava dharma eva yajasva yajñaṃ kuladharma eṣaḥ | yajñairadhiṣṭhāya hi nākapṛṣṭhaṃ yayau marutvānapi nākapṛṣṭham ||
english: Or if religion is really thy one aim, then offer sacrifices, — this is thy family’s immemorial custom, — climbing to highest heaven by sacrifices, even Indra, the lord of the winds, went thus to highest heaven.

sanskrit: suvarṇakeyūravidaṣṭabāhavo maṇipradīpojjvalacitramaulayaḥ | nṛparṣayastāṃ hi gatiṃ gatā makhaiḥ śrameṇa yāmeva mahārṣayo yayuḥ ||
english: ‘With their arms pressed  by golden bracelets, and their variegated diadems resplendent with the light of gems, royal sages have reached the same goal by sacrifices which great sages reached by self-mortification.’

sanskrit: ityevaṃ magadhapatir[vaco]  babhāṣe yaḥ samyagvalabhidiva dhruvaṃ babhāṣe | tacchrutvā na sa vicacāra rājasūnuḥ kailāso giririva naikacitrasānuḥ ||
english: Thus spoke the monarch of the Magadhas, who spoke well and strongly like Indra;  but having heard it, the prince did not falter, (firm) like the mountain Kailāsa, having its many summits variegated (with lines of metals).

sanskrit: ā janmano janmajarāṃtakasya tasyātmajasyātmajitaḥ sa rājā | ahanyahanyarthagajāśvamitrairvṛddhiṃ yayau siṃdharivāṃbuvegaiḥ ||
english: From the time of the birth of that son of his, who, the true master of himself, was to end all birth and old age, the king increased day by day in wealth, elephants, horses, and friends as a river increases with its influx of waters.

sanskrit: dhanasya ratnasya ca tasya tasya kṛtākṛtasyaiva ca kāṃcanasya | tadā hi naikātmanidhīnavāpi manorathasyāpyatibhārabhūtān ||
english: Of different kinds of wealth and jewels, and of gold, wrought or unwrought, he found  treasures of manifold variety,  surpassing even the capacity of his desires.

sanskrit: ye padmakalpairapi ca dvipeṃdrairna maṃḍalaṃ śakyamihābhinetum | madotkaṭā haimavatā gajāste vināpi yatnādupatasthurenam ||
english: Elephants from Himavat, raging with rut, whom not even princes of elephants like Padma  could teach to go round in circles, came without any effort and waited on him.

sanskrit: nānāṃkacihnairnavahemabhāṃḍairabhūṣitairlaṃbasaṭaistathānyaiḥ | saṃcukṣubhe cāsya puraṃ turaṃgairbalena maitryā ca dhanena cāptaiḥ ||
english: His city was all astir with the crowds of horses, some adorned with various marks and decked with new golden trappings, others unadorned and with long flowing manes, — suitable alike in strength, gentleness, and costly ornaments.

sanskrit: puṣṭāśca tuṣṭāśca tadāsya rājye sādhvyo 'rajaskā guṇavatpayaskāḥ | udagravatsaiḥ sahitā babhūvurbahvyo bahukṣīraduhaśca gāvaḥ ||
english: And many fertile cows, with tall calves, gathered in his kingdom, well nourished and happy, gentle and without fierceness, and producing excellent milk.

sanskrit: madhyasthatāṃ tasya ripurjagāma madhyasvabhāvaḥ prayayau suhṛttvam | viśeṣato dārḍhyamiyāya mitraṃ dvāvasya pakṣāvaparastu nāśam ||
english: His enemies became indifferent; indifference grew into friendship; his friends became specially united; were there two sides, — one passed into oblivion.

sanskrit: tathāsya maṃdānilameghaśabdaḥ saudāminīkuṃḍalamaṃḍitāṃgaḥ | vināśmavarṣāśanipātadoṣaiḥ kāle ca deśe pravavarṣa devaḥ ||
english: Heaven rained in his kingdom in due time and place, with the sound of gentle winds and clouds, and adorned with wreaths of lightning, and without any drawback of showers of stones or thunderbolts.

sanskrit: ruroha saṃyak phalavadyathārtu tadākṛtenāpi kṛṣiśrameṇa | tā eva caivauṣadhayo rasena sāreṇa caivābhyadhikā babhūvuḥ ||
english: A fruitful crop sprang up according to season, even without the labour of ploughing;  and the old plants grew more vigorous in juice and substance.

sanskrit: śarīrasaṃdehakare 'pi kāle saṃgrāmasaṃmarda iva pravṛtte | svasthāḥ sukhaṃ caiva nirāmayaṃ ca prajajñire garbhadharāśca nāryaḥ ||
english: Even at that crisis which threatens danger to the body like the collision of battle, pregnant women brought forth in good health, in safety, and without sickness.

sanskrit: yacca pratibhvo vibhave 'pi śakye na prārthayaṃti sma narāḥ parebhyaḥ | abhyarthitaḥ sūkṣmadhano 'pi cāyaṃ tadā na kaścidvimukho babhūva ||
english: And whereas men do not willingly ask from others, even where a surety’s property is available,  — at that time even one possessed of slender means turned not his face away when solicited.

sanskrit: nāśe vadho baṃdhuṣu nāpyadātā naivāvrato nānṛtiko na hiṃsraḥ | āsīttadā kaścana tasya rājye rājño yayāteriva nāhuṣasya ||
english: There was no ruin nor murder,  — nay, there was not even one ungenerous to his kinsmen, no breaker of obligations, none untruthful nor injurious, — as in the days of Yayāti the son of Nahuṣa.

sanskrit: udyānadevāyatanāśramāṇāṃ kūpaprapāpuṣkariṇīvanānām | cakruḥ kriyāstatra ca dharmakāmāḥ pratyakṣataḥ svargamivopalabhya ||
english: Those who sought religious merit performed sacred works and made gardens, temples, and hermitages, wells, cisterns, lakes, and groves, having beheld heaven as it were visible before their eyes.

sanskrit: muktaśca durbhikṣabhayāmayebhyo hṛṣṭo janaḥ svargamivābhireme | patnīṃ patirvā mahiṣī patiṃ vā parasparaṃ na vyabhiceratuśca ||
english: The people, delivered from famine, fear, and sickness, dwelt happily as in heaven; and in mutual contentment husband transgressed not against wife, nor wife against husband.

sanskrit: kaścitsiṣeve rataye na kāmaṃ kāmārthamarthaṃ na jugopa kaścit | kaściddhanārthaṃ na cacāra dharmaṃ dharmāya kaścinna cakāra hiṃsām ||
english: None pursued love for mere sensual pleasure; none hoarded wealth for the sake of desires; none practised religious duties for the sake of gaining wealth; none injured living beings for the sake of religious duty.

sanskrit: steyādibhiścāpyabhitaśca naṣṭaṃ svasthaṃ svacakraṃ paracakramuktam | kṣemaṃ subhikṣaṃ ca babhūva tasya purāṇyaraṇyāni yathaiva rāṣṭre ||
english: On every side theft and its kindred vices disappeared; his own dominion was in peace and at rest from foreign interference;  prosperity and plenty belonged to him, and the cities in his realm were (healthy) like the forests.

sanskrit: tadā hi tajjanmani tasya rājño manorivādityasutasya rājye | cacāra harṣaḥ praṇanāśa pāpmā jajvāla dharmaḥ kaluṣaḥ śaśāma ||
english: When that son was born it was in that monarch’s kingdom as in the reign of Manu the son of the Sun, — gladness went everywhere and evil perished; right blazed abroad and sin was still.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhā rājasutasya tasya sarvārthasiddhiśca yato babhūva | tato nṛpastasya sutasya nāma sarvārthasiddho 'yamiti pracakre ||
english: Since at the birth of this son of the king such a universal accomplishment of all objects took place, the king in consequence caused the prince’s name to be Sarvārthasiddha.

sanskrit: devī tu māyā vibudharṣikalpaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśālaṃ tanayaprabhāvam | jātaṃ praharṣaṃ na śaśāka soḍhuṃ tato 'vināśāya divaṃ jagāma ||
english: But the queen Māyā, having seen the great glory of her new-born son, like some Ṛṣi of the gods, could not sustain the joy which it brought; and that she might not die she went to heaven.

sanskrit: tataḥ kumāraṃ suragarbhakalpaṃ snehena bhāvena ca nirviśeṣam | mātṛṣvasā mātṛsamaprabhāvā saṃvardhayāmātmajavadbabhūva ||
english: Then the queen’s sister, with an influence like a mother’s, undistinguished from the real mother in her affection or tenderness, brought up as her own son the young prince who was like the offspring of the gods.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa bālārka ivodayasthaḥ samīrito vahnirivānilena | krameṇa samyagvavṛdhe kumārastārādhipaḥ pakṣa ivātamaske ||
english: Then like the young sun on the eastern mountain or the fire when fanned by the wind, the prince gradually grew in all due perfection, like the moon in the fortnight of brightness.

sanskrit: tato mahārhāṇi ca candanāni ratnāvalīścauṣadhibhiḥ sagarbhāḥ | mṛgaprayuktānrathakāṃśca haimānācakrire 'smai suhṛdālayebhyaḥ ||
english: Then they brought him as presents from the houses of his friends costly unguents of sandalwood, and strings of gems exactly like wreaths of plants, and little golden carriages yoked with deer;

sanskrit: vayo 'nurūpāṇi ca bhūṣaṇāni hiraṇmayā hastimṛgāśvakāśca | rathāśca gāvo vasanaprayuktā gaṃtrīśca cāmīkararūpyacitrāḥ ||
english: Ornaments also suitable to his age, and elephants, deer, and horses made of gold,  carriages and oxen decked with rich garments, and carts  gay with silver and gold.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa taistairviṣayopacārairvayo 'nurūpairupacaryamāṇaḥ | bālo 'pyabālapratimo babhūva dhṛtyā ca śaucena dhiyā śriyā ca ||
english: Thus indulged with all sorts of such objects to please the senses as were suitable to his years, child as he was, he behaved not like a child in gravity, purity, wisdom, and dignity.

sanskrit: vayaśca kaumāramatītya madhyaṃ saṃprāpya bālaḥ sa hi rājasūnuḥ | alpairahobhirbahuvarṣagamyā jagrāha vidyāḥ svakulānurūpāḥ ||
english: When he had passed the period of childhood and reached that of middle youth, the young prince learned in a few days the various sciences suitable to his race, which generally took many years to master.

sanskrit: naiḥśreyasaṃ tasya tu bhavyamarthaṃ śrutvā purastādasitānmahārṣeḥ | kāmeṣu saṃgaṃ janayāṃbabhūva vṛddhirbhavacchākyakulasya rājñaḥ ||
english: But having heard before from the great seer Asita his destined future which was to embrace transcendental happiness, the anxious care  of the king of the present Śākya race turned the prince to sensual pleasures.

sanskrit: kulāttato 'smai sthiraśīlasaṃyutātsādhvīṃ vapurhrīvinayopapannām | yaśodharāṃ nāma yaśoviśālāṃ tulyābhidhānaṃ śriyamājuhāva ||
english: Then he sought for him from a family of unblemished moral excellence a bride possessed of beauty, modesty, and gentle bearing, of wide-spread glory, Yaśodharā by name, having a name well worthy of her, a very goddess of good fortune.

sanskrit: athāparaṃ bhūmipateḥ priyo 'yaṃ sanatkumārapratimaḥ kumāraḥ | sārdhaṃ tayā śākyanareṃdravadhvā śacyā sahasrākṣa ivābhireme ||
english: Then after that the prince, beloved of the king his father, he who was like Sanatkumāra, rejoiced in the society of that Śākya princess as the thousand-eyed (Indra) rejoiced with his bride Śacī.

sanskrit: kiṃcinmanaḥkṣobhakaraṃ pratīpaṃ kathaṃca paśyediti so 'nuciṃtya | vāsaṃ nṛpo hyādiśati sma tasmai harmyodareṣveva na bhūpracāram ||
english: ‘He might perchance see some inauspicious sight which could disturb his mind,’ — thus reflecting the king had a dwelling prepared for him apart from the busy press in the recesses of the palace.

sanskrit: tataḥ śarattoyadapāṃḍareṣu bhūmau vimāneṣviva raṃjiteṣu | harmyeṣu sarvartusukhāśrayeṣu strīṇāmudārairvijahāra tūryaiḥ ||
english: Then he spent his time in those royal apartments, furnished with the delights proper for every season, gaily decorated like heavenly chariots upon the earth, and bright like the clouds of autumn, amidst the splendid musical concerts of singing-women.

sanskrit: kalairhi cāmīkarabaddhakakṣairnārīkarāgrābhihatairmṛdaṃgaiḥ | varāpsaronṛtyasamaiśca nṛtyaiḥ kailāsavattadbhavanaṃ rarāja ||
english: With the softly-sounding tambourines beaten by the tips of the women’s hands, and ornamented with golden rims, and with the dances which were like the dances of the heavenly nymphs, that palace shone like Mount Kailāsa.

sanskrit: vāgbhiḥ kalābhirlalitaiśca hārairmadaiḥ sakhelairmadhuraiśca hāsaiḥ | taṃ tatra nāryo ramayāṃbabhūvurbhrūvaṃcitairardhanirīkṣitaiśca ||
english: There the women delighted him with their soft voices, their beautiful pearl-garlands, their playful intoxication, their sweet laughter, and their stolen glances concealed by their brows.

sanskrit: tataśca kāmāśrayapaṃḍitābhiḥ strībhirgṛhīto ratikarkaśābhiḥ | vimānapṛṣṭhānna mahīṃ jagāma vimānapṛṣthādiva puṇyakarmā ||
english: Borne in the arms of these women well-skilled in the ways of love, and reckless in the pursuit of pleasure, he fell from the roof of a pavilion and yet reached not the ground, like a holy sage stepping from a heavenly chariot.

sanskrit: nṛpastu tasyaiva vivṛddhihetostadbhāvinārthena ca codyamānaḥ | śame 'bhireme virarāma pāpādbheje damaṃ saṃvibabhāja sādhūn ||
english: Meanwhile the king for the sake of ensuring his son’s prosperity and stirred in heart by the destiny which had been predicted for him, delighted himself in perfect calm, ceased from all evil, practised all self-restraint, and rewarded the good.

sanskrit: nādhīravat kāmasukhe sasaṃje na saṃraraṃje viṣamaṃ jananyām | dhṛtyeṃdriyāśvāṃścapalān vijigye baṃdhūṃśca paurāṃśca guṇairjigāya ||
english: He turned to no sensual pleasures like one wanting in self-control; he felt no violent delight in any state of birth;  he subdued by firmness the restless horses of the senses; and he surpassed his kindred and citizens by his virtues.

sanskrit: nādhyaiṣṭa duḥkhāya parasya vidyāṃ jñānaṃ śivaṃ yattu tadadhyagīṣṭa | svābhyaḥ prajābhyo hi yathā tathaiva sarvaprajābhyaḥ śivamāśaśaṃse ||
english: He sought not learning to vex another; such knowledge as was beneficent, that only he studied; he wished well to all mankind as much as to his own subjects.

sanskrit: taṃ bhāsuraṃ cāṃgirasādhidevaṃ yathāvadānarca tadāyuṣe saḥ | juhāva havyānyakṛśe kṛśānau dadau dvijebhyaḥ kṛśanaṃ ca gāśca ||
english: He worshipped also duly the brilliant (Agni) that tutelary god of the Aṅgirasas, for his son’s long life; and he offered oblations in a large fire, and gave gold  and cows to the Brāhmans.

sanskrit: sasnau śarīraṃ pavituṃ manaśca tīrthāṃbubhiścaiva guṇāṃbubhiśca | vedopadiṣṭaṃ samamātmajaṃ ca somaṃ papau śāṃtisukhaṃ ca hārdam ||
english: He bathed to purify his body and mind with the waters of holy places and of holy feelings; and at the same time he drank the soma-juice as enjoined by the Veda, and the heartfelt self-produced happiness of perfect calm.

sanskrit: sāṃtvaṃ babhāṣe na ca nārthavadyajjajalpa tattvaṃ na ca vipriyaṃ yat | sāṃtvaṃ hyatatvaṃ paruṣaṃ ca tattvaṃ hriyāśakannātmana eva vaktum ||
english: He only spoke what was pleasant and not unprofitable; he discoursed about what was true and not ill-natured, he could not speak even to himself for very shame a false pleasant thing or a harsh truth.

sanskrit: iṣṭeṣvaniṣṭeṣu ca kāryavatsu na rāgadoṣāśrayatāṃ prapede | śivaṃ siṣeve 'vyavahāralabdhaṃ yajñaṃ hi mene na tathā yathāvat ||
english: In things which required to be done, whether they were pleasant or disagreeable, he found no reason either for desire or dislike; he pursued the advantageous which could be attained without litigation;  he did not so highly value sacrifice.

sanskrit: āśāvate cābhigatāya sadyo deyāṃbubhistarṣamacecchidiṣṭa | yuddhādṛte vṛttaparaśvadhena dvidarpamudvṛttamabebhidiṣṭa ||
english: When a suppliant came to him with a petition, he at once hastened to quench his thirst with the water sprinkled on his gift;  and without fighting, by the battle-axe of his demeanour he smote down the arrogant armed with  double pride.

sanskrit: ekaṃ vininye sa jugopa sapta saptaiva tatyāja rarakṣa paṃca | prāpa trivargaṃ bubudhe trivargaṃ jajñe dvivargaṃ prajahau dvivargam ||
english: Thus he took away the one, and protected the seven; he abandoned the seven and kept the five; he obtained the set of three and learned the set of three; he understood the two and abandoned the two.

sanskrit: kṛtāgaso 'pi pratipādya vadhyānnājīghanannāpi ruṣā dadarśa | babaṃdha sāṃtvena phalena caitāṃstyāgo 'pi teṣāṃ hyanapāyadṛṣṭaḥ ||
english: Guilty persons, even though he had sentenced them to death, he did not cause to be killed nor even looked on them with anger; he bound them with gentle words and with the reform produced in their character, — even their release was accompanied by no inflicted injury.

sanskrit: ārṣāṇyacārītparamavratāni vairāṇyahāsīccirasaṃbhṛtāni | yaśāṃsi cāpadguṇagaṃdhavaṃti rajāṃsyahāsīnmalinīkarāṇi ||
english: He performed great religious vows prescribed by ancient seers; he threw aside hostile feelings long cherished; he acquired glory redolent with the fragrance of virtue; he relinquished all passions involving defilement.

sanskrit: na cājihīrṣīdbalimapravṛttaṃ na cācikīrṣītparavastvabhidhyām | na cāvivakṣīddviṣatāmadharmaṃ na cādidhakṣīddhṛdayena manyum ||
english: He desired not to take his tribute of one-sixth without acting as the guardian of his people;  he had no wish to covet another’s property; he desired not to mention the wrong-doing of his enemies; nor did he wish to fan wrath in his heart.

sanskrit: tasmiṃstathā bhūmipatau pravṛtte bhṛtyāśca paurāśca tathaiva ceruḥ | śamātmake cetasi viprasanne prayuktayogasya yatheṃdriyāṇi ||
english: When the monarch himself was thus employed his servants and citizens followed his example, like the senses of one absorbed in contemplation whose mind is abstracted in profound repose.

sanskrit: kāle tataścārupayodharāyāṃ yaśodharāyāṃ suyaśodharāyām | śauddhodanerāhusapatnavaktro jajñe suto rāhula eva nāmnā ||
english: In course of time to the fair-bosomed Yaśodharā, — who was truly glorious in accordance with her name, — there was born from the son of Śuddhodana a son named Rāhula, with a face like the enemy of Rāhu.

sanskrit: atheṣṭaputraḥ paramapratītaḥ kulasya vṛddhiṃ prati bhūmipālaḥ | yathaiva putraprasave nanaṃda tathaiva pautraprasave nanaṃda ||
english: Then the king who from regard to the welfare of his race had longed for a son and been exceedingly delighted [at his coming], — as he had rejoiced at the birth of his son, so did he now rejoice at the birth of his grandson.

sanskrit: pautrasya me putragato mamaiva snehaḥ kathaṃ syāditi jātaharṣaḥ | kāle sa taṃ taṃ vidhimālalaṃbe putrapriyaḥ svargamivārurukṣan ||
english: ‘O how can I feel that love which my son feels for my grandson?’ Thus thinking in his joy he at the due time attended to every enjoined rite like one who fondly loves his son and is about to rise to heaven.

sanskrit: sthitvā pathi prāthamakalpikānāṃ rājarṣabhāṇāṃ yaśasānvitānām | śuklānyamuktvāpi tapāṃsyatapta yajñe ca hiṃsārahitairayaṣṭa ||
english: Standing in the paths of the pre-eminent kings who flourished in primaeval ages, he practised austerities without laying aside his white garments, and he offered in sacrifice only those things which involved no injury to living creatures.

sanskrit: ajājvaliṣṭātha sa puṇyakarmā nṛpaśriyā caiva tapaḥśriyā ca | kulena vṛttena dhiyā ca dīptastejaḥ sahasrāṃśurivotsisṛkṣuḥ ||
english: He of holy deeds shone forth gloriously, in the splendour of royalty and the splendour of penances, conspicuous by his family and his own conduct and wisdom, and desirous to diffuse brightness like the sun.

sanskrit: svāyaṃbhuvaṃ cārcikamarcayitvā jajāpa putrasthitaye sthitaśrīḥ | cakāra karmāṇi ca duṣkarāṇi prajāḥ sisṛkṣuḥ ka ivādikāle ||
english: Having offered worship, he whose own glory was secure muttered repetitions of Vedic texts to Svayambhū for the safety of his son, and performed various ceremonies hard to be accomplished, like the god Ka in the first aeon wishing to create living beings.

sanskrit: tatjyāja śastraṃ vimamarśa śāstraṃ śamaṃ siṣeve niyamaṃ viṣehe | vaśīva kaṃcidviṣayaṃ na bheje piteva sarvānviṣayān dadarśa ||
english: He laid aside weapons and pondered the Śāstra, he practised perfect calm and underwent various observances, like a hermit he refused all objects of sense, he viewed all his kingdoms  like a father.

sanskrit: babhāra rājyaṃ sa hi putrahetoḥ putraṃ kulārthaṃ yaśase kulaṃ tu | svargāya śabdaṃ divamātmahetordharmārthamātmasthitimācakāṃkṣa ||
english: He endured the kingdom for the sake of his son, his son for his family, his family for fame, fame for heaven, heaven for the soul, — he only desired the soul’s continuance for the sake of duty.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa dharmaṃ vividhaṃ cakāra sadbhirnipātaṃ śrutitaśca siddham | dṛṣṭvā kathaṃ putramukhaṃ suto me vanaṃ na yāyāditi nāthamānaḥ ||
english: Thus did he practise the various observances as followed by the pious and established from revelation, he asking himself, ‘now that he has seen the face of his son, how may my son be stopped from going to the forest?’

sanskrit: rirakṣiṣaṃtaḥ śriyamātmasaṃsthā rakṣaṃti putrān bhuvi bhūmipālāḥ | putraṃ nareṃdraḥ sa tu dharmakāmo rarakṣa dharmādviṣayeṣvamuṃcat ||
english: The prudent  kings of the earth, who wish to guard their prosperity, watch over their sons in the world; but this king, though loving religion, kept his son from religion and set him free towards all objects of pleasure.

sanskrit: tasminśca bodhāya kṛtapratijñe rājarṣivaṃśaprabhave mahārṣau | tatropaviṣṭe prajaharṣa lokastatrāsa saddharmaripustu māraḥ ||
english: When the great sage, sprung from a line of royal sages, sat down there with his soul fully resolved to obtain the highest knowledge, the whole world rejoiced; but Māra, the enemy of the good law, was afraid.

sanskrit: yaṃ kāmadevaṃ pravadaṃti loke citrāyudhaṃ puṣpaśaraṃ tathaiva | kāmapracārādhipatiṃ tameva mokṣadviṣaṃ māramudāharaṃti ||
english: He whom they call in the world Kāmadeva, the owner of the various weapons, the flower-arrowed, the lord of the course of desire, — it is he whom they also style Māra the enemy of liberation.

sanskrit: tasyātmajā vibhramaharṣadarpāstisro ratiprītitṛṣaśca kanyāḥ | papracchurenaṃ manaso vikāraṃ sa tāṃśca tāścaiva vaco babhāṣe ||
english: His three sons, Confusion, Gaiety, and Pride, and his three daughters, Lust, Delight, and Thirst,  asked of him the reason of his despondency, and he thus made answer unto them:

sanskrit: asau munirniścayavarma bibhrat sattvāyudhaṃ buddhiśaraṃ vikṛṣya | jigīṣurāste viṣayānmadīyān tasmādayaṃ me manaso viṣādaḥ ||
english: ‘This sage, wearing the armour of resolution, and having drawn the arrow of wisdom with the barb of truth, sits yonder intending to conquer my realms, — hence is this despondency of my mind.

sanskrit: yadi hyasau māmabhibhūya yāti lokāya cākhyātyapavargamārgam | śūnyastato 'yaṃ viṣayo mamādya vṛttāccyutasyeva videhabhartuḥ ||
english: ‘If he succeeds in overcoming me and proclaims to the world the path of final bliss, all this my realm will to-day become empty, as did that of the disembodied lord when he violated the rules of his station.

sanskrit: tadyāvadevaiṣa na labdhacakṣurmadgocare tiṣṭhati yāvadeva | yāsyāmi tāvadvratamasya bhettuṃ setuṃ nadīvega ivābhivṛddhaḥ ||
english: ‘While, therefore, he stands within my reach and while his spiritual eyesight is not yet attained, I will assail him to break his vow as the swollen might of a river assails a dam.’

sanskrit: tato dhanuḥ puṣpamayaṃ gṛhītvā śarāṃstathā mohakarāṃśca paṃca | so 'śvatthamūlaṃ sasuto 'bhyagacchadasvāsthyakārī manasaḥ prajānām ||
english: Then having seized his flower-made bow and his five infatuating arrows, he drew near to the root of the Aśvattha tree with his children, he the great disturber of the minds of living beings.

sanskrit: atha praśāṃtaṃ munimāsanasthaṃ pāraṃ titīrṣuṃ bhavasāgarasya | viṣajya savyaṃ karamāyudhāgre krīḍañśareṇedamuvāca māraḥ ||
english: Having fixed his left hand on the end of the barb and playing with the arrow, Māra thus addressed the calm seer as he sat on his seat, preparing to cross to the further side of the ocean of existence:

sanskrit: uttiṣṭha bhoḥ kṣatriya mṛtyubhīta varasva dharmaṃ tyaja mokṣadharmam | vāṇaiśca [yajñaiśca]  vinīya lokān lokān parān prāpnuhi vāsavasya ||
english: ‘Up, up, O thou Kṣatriya, afraid of death! follow thine own duty and abandon this law of liberation! and having conquered the lower worlds by thy arrows [and sacrifices], proceed to gain the higher worlds of Indra.

sanskrit: paṃthā hi niryātumayaṃ yaśasyo yo vāhitaḥ pūrvatamairnareṃdraiḥ | jātasya rājarṣikule viśāle bhaikṣākamaślāghyamidaṃ prapattum ||
english: ‘That is a glorious path to travel, which has been followed by former leaders of men; this mendicant life is ill-suited for one born in the noble family of a royal sage to follow.

sanskrit: athādya nottiṣṭhasi niścitātmā bhava sthiro mā vimucaḥ pratijñām | mayodyato hyeṣa śaraḥ sa eva yaḥ sūryake mīnaripau vimuktaḥ ||
english: ‘But if thou wilt not rise, strong in thy purpose, — then be firm if thou wilt and quit not thy resolve, — this arrow is uplifted by me, — it is the very one which was shot against Sūryaka,  the enemy of the fish.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭaḥ sa cānena kathaṃcidaiḍaḥ somasya naptāpyabhavadvicittaḥ | sa cābhavacchāṃtanurasvataṃtraḥ kṣīṇe yuge kiṃ vata durbalo 'nyaḥ ||
english: ‘So too, I think, when somewhat probed by this weapon, even the son of Iḍā,  the grandson of the moon, became mad; and Sāntanu  also lost his self-control, — how much more then one of feebler powers now that the age has grown degenerate?

sanskrit: tatkṣipramuttiṣṭha labhasva saṃjñāṃ vāṇo hyayaṃ tiṣṭhati lelihānaḥ | priyābhidheyeṣu ratipriyeṣu yaṃ cakravākeṣvapi notsṛjāmi ||
english: ‘Therefore quickly rise up and come to thyself - for this arrow is ready, darting out its tongue, which I do not launch even against the cakravāka birds, tenderly attached as they are and well deserving the name of lovers.’

sanskrit: ityevamukto 'pi yadā nirāstho naivāsanaṃ śākyamunirbibheda | śaraṃ tato 'smai visasarja māraḥ kanyāśca kṛtvā purataḥ sutāṃśca ||
english: But when, even though thus addressed, the Śākya saint unheeding did not change his posture, then Māra discharged his arrow at him, setting in front of him his daughters and his sons.

sanskrit: tasmiṃstu vāṇe 'pi sa vipramukte cakāra nāsthāṃ na dhṛteścacāla | dṛṣṭvā tathainaṃ viṣasāda māraściṃtāparītaśca śanairjagāda ||
english: But even when that arrow was shot he gave no heed and swerved not from his firmness; and Māra, beholding him thus, sank down, and slowly thus spoke, full of thought:

sanskrit: śaileṃdraputrīṃ prati yena viddho devo 'pi śaṃbhuścalito babhūva | na ciṃtayatyeṣa tameva vāṇaṃ kiṃ syādacitto na śaraḥ sa eṣaḥ ||
english: ‘He does not even notice that arrow by which the god Śambhu was pierced with love for the daughter of the mountain  and shaken in his vow; can he be destitute of all feeling? is not this that very arrow?

sanskrit: tasmādayaṃ nārhati puṣpavāṇaṃ na harṣaṇaṃ nāpi raterniyogam | arhatyayaṃ bhūtagaṇairaśeṣaiḥ saṃtrāsanātarjanatāḍanāni ||
english: ‘He is not worthy of my flower-shaft, nor my arrow “gladdener,” nor the sending of my daughter Rati (to tempt him); he deserves the alarms and rebukes and blows from all the gathered hosts of the demons.’

sanskrit: sasmāra māraśca tataḥ svasainyaṃ vidhvaṃsanaṃ śākyamuneścikīrṣan | nānāśrayāścānucarāḥ parīyuḥ śaradrumaprāsagadāsihastāḥ ||
english: Then Māra called to mind his own army, wishing to work the overthrow of the Śākya saint; and his followers swarmed round, wearing different forms and carrying arrows, trees, darts, clubs, and swords in their hands;

sanskrit: varāhamīnāśvakharoṣṭravaktrā vyāghrarkṣasiṃhadviradānanāśca | ekekṣaṇā naikamukhāstriśīrṣā laṃbodarāścaiva pṛṣodarāśca ||
english: Having the faces of boars, fishes, horses, asses, and camels, of tigers, bears, lions, and elephants, — one-eyed, many-faced, three-headed, — with protuberant bellies and speckled bellies;

sanskrit: ajāsu saktā ghaṭajānavaśca daṃṣṭrāyudhāścaiva nakhāyudhāśca | kabaṃdhahastā bahumūrtayaśca bhagnārdhavaktrāśca mahāmukhāśca ||
english: Blended with goats, with knees swollen like pots, armed with tusks and with claws, carrying headless trunks in their hands, and assuming many forms, with half-mutilated faces, and with monstrous mouths;

sanskrit: tāmrāruṇā lohitaviṃducitrāḥ khaṭvāṃgahastā haridhūmrakeśāḥ | laṃbasrajo vāraṇalaṃbakarṇāścarmāṃbarāścaiva niraṃbarāśca ||
english: Copper-red, covered with red spots, bearing clubs in their hands, with yellow or smoke-coloured hair, with wreaths dangling down, with long pendulous ears like elephants, clothed in leather or wearing no clothes at all;

sanskrit: śvetārdhavaktrā haritārdhakāyāstāmrāśca dhūmrā harayo 'sitāśca | vyāḍottarāsaṃgabhujāstathaiva praghuṣṭaghaṃṭākulamekhalāśca ||
english: Having half their faces white or half their bodies green, — red and smoke-coloured, yellow and black, — with arms reaching out longer than a serpent, and with girdles jingling with rattling bells.

sanskrit: tālapramāṇāśca gṛhītaśūlā daṃṣṭrākarālāśca śiśupramāṇāḥ | urabhravaktrāśca vihaṃgamāśca mārjāravaktrāśca manuṣyakāyāḥ ||
english: Some were as tall as palm-trees, carrying spears, — others were of the size of children with projecting teeth, others birds with the faces of rams, others with men’s bodies and cats’ faces;

sanskrit: prakīrṇakeśāḥ śikhino 'rdhamuṃḍā rajjvaṃbarā vyākulaveṣṭanāśca | prahṛṣṭavaktrā bhṛkuṭīmukhāśca tejoharāścaiva manoharāśca ||
english: With dishevelled hair, or with topknots, or half-bald, with rope-garments or with head-dress all in confusion, — with triumphant faces or frowning faces, — wasting the strength or fascinating the mind.

sanskrit: kecidvrajaṃto bhṛśamāvavalguranyo 'nyamāpupluvire tathānye | cikrīḍurākāśagatāśca kecitkecicca cerustarumastakeṣu ||
english: Some as they went leaped about wildly, others danced upon one another, some sported about in the sky, others went along on the tops of the trees.

sanskrit: nanarta kaścidbhramayaṃstriśūlaṃ kaściddha pusphūrja gadāṃ vikarṣan | harṣeṇa kaścidvṛṣavannanarta kaścitprajajvāla tanūruhebhyaḥ ||
english: One danced, shaking a trident, another made a crash, dragging a club, another bounded for joy like a bull, another blazed out flames from every hair.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhā bhūtagaṇāḥ samaṃtāttadbodhimūlaṃ parivārya tasthuḥ | jighṛkṣavaścaiva jighāṃsavaśca bharturniyogaṃ paripālayaṃtaḥ ||
english: Such were the troops of demons who encircled the root of the Bodhi tree on every side, eager to seize it and to destroy it, awaiting the command of their lord.

sanskrit: taṃ prekṣya mārasya ca pūrvarātre śākyarṣabhasyaiva ca yuddhakālam | na dyauścakāśe pṛthivī cakaṃpe prajajvaluścaiva diśaḥ saśabdāḥ ||
english: Beholding in the first half of the night that battle of Māra and the bull of the Śākya race, the heavens did not shine and the earth shook and the (ten) regions of space flashed flame and roared.

sanskrit: viṣvagvavau vāyurudīrṇavegastārā na rejurna babhau śaśāṃkaḥ | tamaśca bhūyo vitatāra rātreḥ sarve ca saṃcukṣubhire samudrāḥ ||
english: A wind of intense violence blew in all directions,  the stars did not shine, the moon gave no light, and a deeper darkness of night spread around, and all the oceans were agitated.

sanskrit: mahībhṛto dharmaparāśca nāgā mahāmunervighnamamṛṣyamāṇāḥ | māraṃ prati krodhavivṛttanetrā niḥśaśvasuścaiva jajṛṃbhire ca ||
english: The mountain deities  and the Nāgas who honoured the Law, indignant at the attack on the saint, rolling their eyes in anger against Māra, heaved deep sighs and opened their mouths wide.

sanskrit: śuddhādhivāsā vibudharṣayastu saddharmasiddhyarthamiva pravṛttāḥ | māre 'nukaṃpāṃ manasā pracakrurvirāgabhāvāttu na roṣamīyuḥ ||
english: But the god-sages, the Śuddhādhivāsas,  being as it were absorbed in the perfect accomplishment of the good Law, felt only a pity for Māra in their minds and through their absolute passionlessness were unruffled by anger.

sanskrit: tadbodhimūlaṃ samavekṣya kīrṇaṃ hiṃsātmanā mārabalena tena | dharmātmabhirlokavimokṣakāmairbabhūva hāhākṛtamaṃtarīkṣam ||
english: When they saw the foot of the Bodhi tree crowded with that host of Māra, intent on doing harm, — the sky was filled with the cry raised by all the virtuous beings who desired the world’s liberation.

sanskrit: upaplutaṃ dharmavidastu tasya dṛṣṭvā sthitaṃ mārabalaṃ mahārṣiḥ | na cukṣubhe nāpi yayau vikāraṃ madhye gavāṃ siṃha ivopaviṣṭaḥ ||
english: But the great sage  having beheld that army of Māra thus engaged in an attack on the knower of the Law,  remained untroubled and suffered no perturbation, like a lion seated in the midst of oxen.

sanskrit: mārastato bhūtacamūmudīrṇāmājñāpayāmāsa bhayāya tasya | svaiḥ svaiḥ prabhāvairatha sāsya senā taddhairyabhedāya matiṃ cakāra ||
english: Then Māra commanded his excited army of demons to terrify him; and forthwith that host resolved to break down his determination with their various powers.

sanskrit: keciccalannaikavilaṃbijihvāstīkṣṇogradaṃṣṭrā harimaṃḍalākṣāḥ | vidāritāsyāḥ sthiraśaṃkukarṇāḥ saṃtrāsayaṃtaḥ kila nāma tasthuḥ ||
english: Some with many tongues hanging out and shaking, with sharp-pointed savage teeth and eyes like the disk of the sun, with wide-yawning mouths and upright ears like spikes, — they stood round trying to frighten him.

sanskrit: tebhyaḥ sthitebhyaḥ sa tathāvidhebhyaḥ rūpeṇa bhāvena ca dāruṇebhyaḥ | na vivyathe nodvivije mahārṣiḥ krīḍan subālebhya ivoddhatebhyaḥ ||
english: Before these monsters standing there, so dreadful in form and disposition, the great sage remained unalarmed and untroubled, sporting with them as if they had been only rude children.

sanskrit: kaścittato raudravivṛttadṛṣṭistasmai gadāmudyamayāṃcakāra | tastaṃbha bāhuḥ sagadastato 'sya puraṃdarasyeva purā savajraḥ ||
english: Then one of them, with his eyes rolling wildly, lifted up a club against him; but his arm with the club was instantly paralysed, as was Indra’s of old with its thunderbolt.

sanskrit: kecitsamudyamya śilāstarūṃśca viṣehire naiva munau vimoktum | petuḥ savṛkṣāḥ saśilāstathaiva vajrāvabhagnā iva viṃdhyapādāḥ ||
english: Some, having lifted up stones and trees, found themselves unable to throw them against the sage; down they fell, with their trees and their stones, like the roots of the Vindhya shattered by the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: kaiścitsamutpatya nabho vimuktāḥ śilāśca vṛkṣāśca paraśvadhāśca | tasthurnabhasyeva na cāvapetuḥ saṃdhyābhrapādā iva naikavarṇāḥ ||
english: Others, leaping up into the sky, flung rocks, trees, and axes; these remained in the sky and did not fall down, like the many-coloured rays of the evening clouds.

sanskrit: cikṣepa tasyopari dīptamanyaḥ kaḍaṃgaraṃ parvataśṛṃgamātram | yanmuktamātraṃ gaganasthameva tasyānubhāvācchatadhā babhūva ||
english: Another hurled upon him a mass of blazing straw as big as a mountain-peak, which, as soon as it was thrown, while it hung poised in the sky, was shattered into a hundred fragments by the sage’s power.

sanskrit: kaścijjvalannarka ivoditaḥ khādaṃgāravarṣaṃ mahadutsasarja | cūrnāni cāmīkarakaṃdarāṇāṃ kalpātyaye meruriva pradīptaḥ ||
english: One, rising up like the sun in full splendour, rained down from the sky a great shower of live embers, as at the end of an aeon blazing Meru showers down the pulverised scoriae of the golden valleys.

sanskrit: tadbodhimūle pravikīryamāṇamaṃgāravarṣaṃ tu savisphuliṃgam | maitrīvihārādṛṣisattamasya babhūva raktotpalapatravarṣaḥ ||
english: But that shower of embers full of sparks, when scattered at the foot of the Bodhi tree, became a shower of red lotus-petals through the operation of the great saint’s boundless charity.

sanskrit: śarīracittavyasanātapaistairevaṃvidhaistaiśca nipātyamānaiḥ | naivāsanācchākyamuniścacāla svaṃ niścayaṃ baṃdhumivopaguhya ||
english: But with all these various scorching assaults on his body and his mind, and all these missiles showered down upon him, the Śākya saint did not in the least degree move from his posture, clasping firmly his resolution as a kinsman.

sanskrit: athāpare nirjagalurmukhebhyaḥ sarpānvijīrṇebhya iva drumebhyaḥ | te maṃtrabaddhā iva tatsamīpe na śaśvasurnotsasṛjurna celuḥ ||
english: Then others spat out serpents from their mouths as from old decayed trunks of trees; but, as if held fast by a charm, near him they neither breathed nor discharged venom nor moved.

sanskrit: bhūtvāpare vāridharā vṛhaṃtaḥ savidyutaḥ sāśanicaṃḍaghoṣāḥ | tasmin drume tatyajuraśmavarṣaṃ tatpuṣpavarṣaṃ ruciraṃ babhūva ||
english: Others, having become great clouds, emitting lightning and uttering the fierce roar of thunderbolts, poured a shower of stones upon that tree, — but it turned to a pleasant shower of flowers.

sanskrit: cāpe 'tha vāṇo nihito 'pareṇa jajvāla tatraiva na niṣpapāta | anīśvarasyātmani dhūryamāṇo durmarṣaṇasyeva narasya manyuḥ ||
english: Another set an arrow in his bow, — there it gleamed but it did not issue forth, like the anger which falls slack  in the soul of an ill-tempered impotent man.

sanskrit: paṃceṣavo 'nyena tu vipramuktāstasthurnayatyeva munau na petuḥ | saṃsārabhīrorviṣayapravṛttau paṃceṃdriyāṇīva parīkṣakasya ||
english: But five arrows shot by another stood motionless and fell not, through the saint’s ruling guidance, — like the five senses of him who is well experienced in the course of worldly objects and is afraid of embodied existence.

sanskrit: jighāṃsayānyaḥ prasasāra ruṣṭo gadāṃ gṛhītvābhimukho mahārṣeḥ | so 'prāptakālo vivaśaḥ papāta doṣeṣvivānarthakareṣu lokaḥ ||
english: Another, full of anger, rushed towards the great saint, having seized a club with a desire to smite him; but he fell powerless without finding an opportunity, like mankind in the presence of faults which cause failure.

sanskrit: strī meghakālī tu kapālahastā kartuṃ mahārṣeḥ kila mohacittam | babhrāma tatrāniyataṃ na tasthau calātmano buddhirivāgameṣu ||
english: But a woman named Meghakālī, bearing a skull in her hand, in order to infatuate the mind of the sage, flitted about unsettled and stayed not in one spot, like the mind of the fickle student over the sacred texts.

sanskrit: kaścitpradīptaṃ praṇidhāya cakṣurnetrāgnināśīviṣavaddidhakṣuḥ | tatraiva nāsīttamṛṣiṃ dadarśa kāmātmakaḥ śreya ivopadiṣṭam ||
english: Another, fixing a kindling eye, wished to burn him with the fire of his glance like a poisonous serpent; but he saw the sage and lo! he was not there, like the votary of pleasure when true happiness is pointed out to him.

sanskrit: gurvīṃ śilāmudyamayaṃstathānyaḥ śaśrāma moghaṃ vihataprayatnaḥ | niḥśreyasaṃ jñānasamādhigamyaṃ kāyaklamairdharmamivāptukāmaḥ ||
english: Another, lifting up a heavy rock, wearied himself to no purpose, having his efforts baffled, like one who wishes to obtain by bodily fatigue that condition of supreme happiness which is only to be reached by meditation and knowledge.

sanskrit: tarakṣusiṃhākṛtayastathānye praṇeduruccairmahataḥ praṇādān | sattvāni yaiḥ saṃcukucuḥ samaṃtādvajrāhatā dyauḥ phalatīti matvā ||
english: Others, wearing the forms of hyenas and lions, uttered loudly fierce howls, which caused all beings round to quail with terror, as thinking that the heavens were smitten with a thunderbolt and were bursting.

sanskrit: mṛgā gajāścārttaravān sṛjaṃto vidudruvuścaiva nililyire ca | rātrau ca tasyāmahanīva digbhyaḥ khagā ruvaṃtaḥ paripeturārttāḥ ||
english: Deer and elephants uttering cries of pain ran about or lay down, — in that night as if it were day screaming birds flew around disturbed in all directions.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ praṇādaistu tathāvidhaistaiḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣvapi kaṃpiteṣu | munirna tatrāsa na saṃcukoca ravairgarutmāniva vāyasānām ||
english: But amidst all these various sounds which they made, although all living creatures were shaken, the saint trembled not nor quailed, like Garuḍa at the noise of crows.

sanskrit: bhayāvahebhyaḥ pariṣadgaṇebhyo yathā yathā naiva munirbibhāya | tathā tathā dharmabhṛtāṃ sapatnaḥ śokācca roṣācca sasāra māraḥ ||
english: The less the saint feared the frightful hosts of that multitude, the more did Māra, the enemy of the righteous, continue his attacks in grief and anger.

sanskrit: bhūtaṃ tataḥ kiṃcidadṛśyarūpaṃ viśiṣṭarūpaṃ gaganasthameva | dṛṣṭvārṣaye drugdhamavairaruṣṭaṃ māraṃ babhāṣe mahatā svareṇa ||
english: Then some being of invisible shape, but of pre-eminent glory, standing in the heavens, — beholding Māra thus malevolent against the seer, — addressed him in a loud voice, unruffled by enmity:

sanskrit: moghaṃ śramaṃ nārhasi māra kartuṃ hiṃsrātmatāmutsṛja gaccha śarma | naiṣa tvayā kaṃpayituṃ hi śakyo mahāgirirmerurivānilena ||
english: ‘Take not on thyself, O Māra, this vain fatigue, — throw aside thy malevolence and retire to peace;  this sage cannot be shaken by thee any more than the mighty mountain Meru by the wind.

sanskrit: apyuṣṇabhāvaṃ jvalanaḥ prajahyādāpo dravatvaṃ pṛthivī sthiratvam | anekakalpācitapuṇyakarmā na tveva jahyādvyavasāyameṣaḥ ||
english: ‘Even fire might lose its hot nature, water its fluidity, earth its steadiness, but never will he abandon his resolution, who has acquired his merit by a long course of actions through unnumbered aeons.

sanskrit: yo niścayo hyasya parākramaśca tejaśca yadyā ca dayā prajāsu | aprāpya notthāsyati tattvameṣa tamāṃsyahatveva sahasraraśmiḥ ||
english: ‘Such is that purpose of his, that heroic effort, that glorious strength, that compassion for all beings, — until he attains the highest wisdom, he will never rise from his seat, just as the sun does not rise, without dispelling the darkness.

sanskrit: kāṣṭhaṃ hi mathnan labhate hutāśaṃ bhūmiṃ khanan viṃdati cāpi toyam | nirbaṃdhinaḥ kiṃca na nāsya sādhyaṃ nyāyena yuktaṃ ca kṛtaṃ ca sarvam ||
english: ‘One who rubs the two pieces of wood obtains the fire, one who digs the earth finds at last the water, — and to him in his perseverance there is nothing unattainable, — all things to him are reasonable and possible.

sanskrit: tallokamārttaṃ karuṇāyamāno rogeṣu rāgādiṣu vartamānam | mahābhiṣagnārhati vighnameṣa jñānauṣadhārthaṃ parikhidyamānaḥ ||
english: ‘Pitying the world lying distressed amidst diseases and passions, he, the great physician, ought not to be hindered, who undergoes all his labours for the sake of the remedy knowledge.

sanskrit: hṛte ca loke bahubhiḥ kumārgaiḥ sanmārgamanvicchati yaḥ śrameṇa | sa daiśikaḥ kṣobhayituṃ na yuktaṃ sudeśikaḥ sārtha iva pranaṣṭe ||
english: ‘He who toilsomely pursues the one good path, when all the world is carried away in devious tracks, — he the guide should not be disturbed, like a right informant when the caravan has lost its way.

sanskrit: sattveṣu naṣṭeṣu mahāṃdhakārairjñānapradīpaḥ kriyamāṇa eṣaḥ | āryasya nirvāpayituṃ na sādhu prajvālyamānastamasīva dīpaḥ ||
english: ‘He who is made a lamp of knowledge when all beings are lost in the great darkness, — it is not for a right-minded soul to try to quench him, — like a lamp kindled in the gloom of night.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca saṃsāramaye mahaughe magnaṃ jagatpāramaviṃdamānam | yaścedamuttārayituṃ pravṛttaḥ kaścinnayettasya tu pāpamāryaḥ ||
english: ‘He who, when he beholds the world drowned in the great flood of existence and unable to reach the further shore, strives to bring them safely across, — would any right-minded soul offer him wrong?

sanskrit: kṣamāśipho dhairyavigāḍhamūlaścāritrapuṣpaḥ smṛtibuddhiśākhaḥ | jñānadrumo dharmaphalapradātā notpāṭanaṃ hyarhati vardhamānaḥ ||
english: ‘The tree of knowledge, whose roots go deep in firmness, and whose fibres are patience, — whose flowers are moral actions and whose branches are memory and thought, — and which gives out the law as its fruit, — surely when it is growing it should not be cut down.

sanskrit: baddhāṃ dṛḍhaiścetasi mohapāśairyasya prajāṃ mokṣayituṃ manīṣā | tasmin jighāṃsā tava nopapannā śrāṃte jagadbaṃdhanamokṣahetoḥ ||
english: ‘Him whose one desire is to deliver mankind bound in soul by the fast snares of illusion, — thy wish to overthrow him is not worthy, wearied as he is for the sake of unloosing the bonds of the world.

sanskrit: bodhāya karmāṇi hi yānyanena kṛtāni teṣāṃ niyato 'dya kālaḥ | sthāne tathāsminnupaviṣṭa eṣa yathaiva pūrve munayastathaiva ||
english: ‘To-day is the appointed period of all those actions which have been performed by him for the sake of knowledge, — he is now seated on this seat just as all the previous saints have sat.

sanskrit: eṣā hi nābhirvasudhātalasya kṛtsnena yuktā parameṇa dhāmnā | bhūmerato 'nyo 'sti hi na pradeśo veśaṃ samādherviṣayo hitasya ||
english: ‘This is the navel of the earth’s surface, endued with all the highest glory; there is no other spot of the earth than this, — the home of contemplation, the realm of well-being.

sanskrit: tanmā kṛthāḥ śokamupehi śāṃtiṃ mā bhūnmahimnā tava māra mānaḥ | viśraṃbhituṃ na kṣamamadhruvā śrīścale pade kiṃ padamabhyupaiṣi ||
english: ‘Give not way, then, to grief but put on calm; let not thy greatness, O Māra, be mixed with pride; it is not well to be confident, — fortune is unstable, — why dost thou accept a position on a tottering base?’

sanskrit: tataḥ sa saṃśrutya ca tasya tadvaco mahāmuneḥ prekṣya ca niṣprakaṃpatām | jagāma māro vimanā hatodyamaḥ śarairjagaccetasi yairvihanyase ||
english: Having listened to his words, and having seen the unshaken firmness of the great saint, Māra departed dispirited and broken in purpose  with those very arrows by which, O world, thou art smitten in thy heart.

sanskrit: gatapraharṣā viphalīkṛtaśramā praviddhapāṣāṇakaḍaṃgaradrumā | diśaḥ pradudrāva tato 'sya sā camūrhatāśrayeva dviṣatā dviṣaccamūḥ ||
english: With their triumph at an end, their labour all fruitless, and all their stones, straw, and trees thrown away, that host of his fled in all directions, like some hostile army when its camp has been destroyed by the enemy.

sanskrit: dravati saparapakṣe nirjite puṣpaketau jayati jitatamaske nīrajaske mahārṣau | yuvatiriva sahāsā dyauścakāśe sacaṃdrā  surabhi ca jalagarbhaṃ puṣpavarṣaṃ papāta ||
english: When the flower-armed god  thus fled away vanquished with his hostile forces and the passionless sage remained victorious, having conquered all the power of darkness, the heavens shone out with the moon like a maiden with a smile, and a sweet-smelling shower of flowers fell down wet with dew.

sanskrit: tathāpi pāpīyasi nirjite gate diśaḥ praseduḥ prababhau niśākaraḥ | divo nipeturbhuvi puṣpavṛṣṭayo rarāja yoṣeva vikalmaṣā niśā |
english: When the wicked one thus fled vanquished, the different regions of the sky grew clear, the moon shone forth, showers of flowers fell down from the sky upon the earth, and the night gleamed out like a spotless maiden.

sanskrit: śriyaṃ parārdhyāṃ vidadhadvidhātṛjit tamo nirasyannabhibhūtabhānubhṛt | nudannidāghaṃ jitacārucaṃdramāḥ sa vaṃdyate 'rhanniha yasya nopamā ||
english: That Arhat is here saluted, who has no counterpart, — who, as bestowing the supreme happiness, surpasses (Brahman) the Creator, — who, as driving away darkness, vanquishes the sun, — and, as dispelling all burning heat, surpasses the beautiful moon.

sanskrit: āsīdviśālonnatasānulakṣmyā payodapaṃktyeva parītapārśvam | udagradhiṣṇyaṃ gagaṇe 'vagāḍhaṃ puraṃ maharṣeḥ kapilasya vastu ||
english: There was a city, the dwelling-place  of the great saint Kapila, having its sides surrounded by the beauty of a lofty broad table-land as by a line of clouds, and itself, with its high-soaring palaces,  immersed in the sky.

sanskrit: sitonnateneva nayena hṛtvā kailāsaśailasya yadabhraśobhām | bhramādupetān vahadaṃbuvāhān saṃbhāvanāṃ vā saphalīcakāra ||
english: By its pure and lofty system of government it, as it were, stole the splendour of the clouds of Mount Kailāsa, and while it bore the clouds which came to it through a mistake, it fulfilled the imagination which had led them thither.

sanskrit: ratnaprabhodbhāsini yatra lebhe tamo na dāridryamivāvakāśam | parārdhyapauraiḥ sahavāsatoṣāt kṛtasmitevātirarāja lakṣmīḥ ||
english: In that city, shining with the splendour of gems, darkness like poverty could find no place; prosperity shone resplendently, as with a smile, from the joy of dwelling with such surpassingly excellent citizens.
