sanskrit: yadvedikātoraṇasiṃhakarṇairatnairdadhānaṃ prativeśama śobhām | jagatyadṛṣṭveva samānamanyatspardhāṃ svagehairmitha eva cakre ||
english: With its festive arbours, its arched gateways and pinnacles,  it was radiant with jewels in every dwelling; and unable to find any other rival in the world, it could only feel emulation with its own houses.

sanskrit: rāmāmukheṃdūn paribhūtapadmān yatrāpayāto 'pyavimanya bhānuḥ | saṃtāpayogādiva vāri veṣṭuṃ paścātsamudrābhimukhaḥ pratasthe ||
english: There the sun, even although he had retired, was unable to scorn the moon-like faces of its women which put the lotuses to shame, and as if from the access of passion, hurried towards the western ocean to enter the (cooling) water.

sanskrit: śakyārjitānāṃ yaśasāṃ janena dṛṣṭvāṃtabhāvaṃ gamito 'yamindraḥ | iti dhvajaiścārucalatpatākairyanmārṣṭumasyāṃkamivodayacchat ||
english: ‘Yonder Indra has been utterly annihilated by the people when they saw the glories  acquired by the Sakyas,’-uttering this scoff, the city strove by its banners with gay-fluttering streamers to wipe away every mark of his existence.

sanskrit: kṛtvāpi rātrau kumudaprahāsamiṃdoḥ karairyadrajatālayasthaiḥ | sauvarṇaharmyeṣu gatārkapādairdivā sarojadyutimālalaṃbe ||
english: After mocking the water-lilies even at night by the moonbeams which rest on its silver pavilions, — by day it assumed the brightness of the lotuses through the sunbeams falling on its golden palaces.

sanskrit: mahībṛtāṃ mūrdhni kṛtābhiṣekaḥ śuddhodano nāma nṛpo 'rkabaṃdhuḥ | adhyāśayo vā sphuṭapudarīkaṃ purādhirājaṃ tadalaṃcakāra ||
english: A king, by name Śuddhodana, of the kindred of the sun, anointed to stand at the head of earths monarchs, — ruling over the city, adorned it, as a bee-inmate a full-blown lotus.

sanskrit: bhūbhṛtparārdhyo 'pi sapakṣa eva pravṛttadāno 'pi madānupetaḥ | īśo 'pi nityaṃ samaḍṛṣṭipātaḥ saumyasvabhāvo 'pi pṛthupratāpaḥ ||
english: The very best of kings with his train ever near him,  — intent on liberality yet devoid of pride;  a sovereign, yet with an ever equal eye thrown on all,  — of gentle nature and yet with wide-reaching majesty.

sanskrit: bhujena yasyābhihatāḥ pataṃto dviṣaddvipeṃdrāḥ samarāṃgaṇeṣu | udvāṃtamuktāprakaraiḥ śirobhirbhaktyeva puṣpāṃjalibhiḥ praṇemuḥ ||
english: Falling smitten by his arm in the arena of battle, the lordly elephants of his enemies bowed prostrate with their heads pouring forth quantities of pearls as if they were offering handfuls of flowers in homage.

sanskrit: atipratāpādavadhūya śatrūnmahoparāgāniva tigmabhānuḥ | udyotayāmāsa janaṃ samaṃtātpradarśayannāśrayaṇīyamārgān ||
english: Having dispersed his enemies by his preeminent majesty as the sun disperses the gloom of an eclipse, he illuminated his people on every side, showing them the paths which they were to follow.

sanskrit: dharmārthakāmā viṣayaṃ mitho 'nyaṃ na veśamācakramurasya nītyā | vispardhamānā iva tūgrasiddheḥ sugocare dīptatarā babhūvuḥ ||
english: Duty, wealth, and pleasure under his guidance assumed mutually each other’s object, but not the outward dress; yet as if they still vied together they shone all the brighter in the glorious career of their triumphant success.

sanskrit: udārasaṃkhyaiḥ sacivāirasaṃkhyaiḥ kṛtāgrabhāvaḥ sa udagrabhāvaḥ | śaśī yathā bhairakṛtānyathābhaiḥ śakyeṃdrarājaḥ sutarāṃ rarāja ||
english: He, the monarch of the Śākyas, of native pre-eminence, but whose actual pre-eminence was brought about by his numberless councillors of exalted wisdom, shone forth all the more gloriously, like the moon amidst the stars shining with a light like its own.

sanskrit: tasyātiśobhāvisṛtātiśobhā raviprabhevāstatamaḥ prabhāvā | samagradevīnivahāgradevī babhūva māyāpagateva māyā ||
english: To him there was a queen, named Māyā, as if free from all deceit (māyā) — an effulgence proceeding from his effulgence, like the splendour of the sun when it is free from all the influence of darkness, a chief queen in the united assembly of all queens.

sanskrit: prajāsu māteva hitapravṛttā gurau jane bhaktirivānuvṛttā | lakṣmīrivādhīśakule kṛtābhā jagatyabhūduttamadevatā yā ||
english: Like a mother to her subjects, intent on their welfare, — devoted to all worthy of reverence like devotion itself, — shining on her lord’s family like the goddess of prosperity, — she was the most eminent of goddesses to the whole world.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ sadā strīcaritaṃ tamisraṃ tathāpi tāṃ prapya bhṛśaṃ vireje | na hīṃdulekhāmupagamya śubhāṃ naktaṃ tathā saṃtamasatvameti ||
english: Verily the life of women is always darkness, yet when it encountered her, it shone brilliantly; thus the night does not retain its gloom, when it meets with the radiant crescent of the moon.

sanskrit: atīṃdriyenātmani duṣkuho 'yaṃ mayā jano yojayituṃ na śakyaḥ | itīva sūkṣmāṃ prakṛtiṃ vihāya dharmeṇa sākṣādvihitā svamūrtiḥ ||
english: ‘This people, being hard to be roused to wonder in their souls, cannot be influenced by me if I come to them as beyond their senses,’ - so saying, Duty abandoned her own subtile nature and made her form visible.

sanskrit: cyuto 'tha kāyāttuṣitāt trilokīmudyotayannuttamabodhisattvaḥ | viveśa tasyāḥ smṛta eva kukṣau naṃdāguhāyāmiva nāgarājaḥ ||
english: Then falling from the host of beings in the Tuṣita heaven,  and illumining the three worlds, the most excellent of Bodhisattvas suddenly entered at a thought into her womb, like the Nāga-king entering the cave of Nandā.

sanskrit: rakṣāvidhānaṃ prati lokapālā lokaikanāthasya divo 'bhijagmuḥ | sarvatra bhāṃto 'pi hi caṃdrapādā bhajaṃti kailāsagirau viśeṣam ||
english: The guardians of the world hastened from heaven to mount watch over the world’s one true ruler; thus the moonbeams, though they shine everywhere, are especially bright on Mount Kailāsa.

sanskrit: mayāpi taṃ kukṣigataṃ dadhānā vidyudvilāsaṃ jaladāvalīva | dānābhivarṣaiḥ parito janānāṃ dāridryatāpaṃ śamayāṃcakāra ||
english: Māyā also, holding him in her womb, like a line of clouds holding a lightning-flash, relieved the people around her from the sufferings of poverty by raining showers of gifts.

sanskrit: sātaḥ purajanā devī kadācidatha luṃbinīm | jagāmānumate rājñaḥ saṃbhūtottamadohadā ||
english: Then one day by the king’s permission the queen, having a great longing in her mind, went with the inmates of the gynaeceum into the garden Lumbinī.

sanskrit: śākhāmālaṃbamānāyāḥ puṣpabhārāvalaṃbinīm | devyāḥ kukṣiṃ vibhidyāśu bodhisattvo viniryayau ||
english: As the queen supported herself by a bough which hung laden with a weight of flowers, the Bodhisattva suddenly came forth, cleaving open her womb.

sanskrit: tataḥ prasannaśca babhūva puṣyastasyāśca devyā vratasaṃskṛtāyāḥ | pārśvātsuto lokahitāya jajñe nirvedanaṃ caiva nirāmayaṃ ca ||
english: At that time the constellation Puṣya was auspicious, and from the side of the queen, who was purified by her vow, her son was born for the welfare of the world, without pain and without illness.

sanskrit: prātaḥ payodādiva tigmabhānuḥ samudbhavanso 'pi ca mātṛkukṣeḥ | sphuranmayūkhairvihatāṃdhakāraiścakāra lokaṃ kanakāvadātam ||
english: Like the sun bursting from a cloud in the morning, — so he too, when he was born from his mother’s womb, made the world bright like gold, bursting forth with his rays which dispelled the darkness.

sanskrit: surapradhānaiḥ paridhāryamāṇo dehāṃśujālairanuraṃjayaṃstān | saṃdhyābhrajāloparisaṃniviṣṭaṃ navoḍurājaṃ vijigāya lakṣmyā ||
english: Carried about by the chief suras, and delighting them with the rays that streamed from his body, he surpassed in beauty the new moon as it rests on a mass of evening clouds.

sanskrit: ūroryathaurvasya pṛthośca hastānmāṃdhāturiṃdrapratimasya mūrdhnaḥ | kakṣīvataścaiva bhujāṃsadeśāttathāvidhaṃ tasya babhūva janma ||
english: As was Aurva’s birth from the thigh,  and Pṛthu’s from the hand,  and Māndhātṛ’s, who was like Indra himself, from the forehead,  and Kakṣīvat’s from the upper end of the arm,  — thus too was his birth (miraculous).

sanskrit: krameṇa garbhādabhiniḥsṛtaḥ san babhau gataḥ khādiva yonyajātaḥ | kalpeṣvanekeṣviva bhāvitātmā yaḥ saṃprajānan suṣuve na mūḍhaḥ ||
english: Having thus in due time issued from the womb, he shone as if he had come down from heaven, he who had not been born in the natural way, — he who was born full of wisdom, not foolish, as if his mind had been purified by countless aeons of contemplation.

sanskrit: dīptyā ca dhairyeṇa śriyā rarāja bālo ravirbhūmimivāvatīrṇaḥ | tathātidīpto 'pi nirīkṣyamāṇo jahāra cakṣūṃṣi yathā śaśāṃkaḥ ||
english: With glory, fortitude, and beauty he shone like the young sun descended upon the earth; when he was gazed at, though of such surpassing brightness, he attracted all eyes like the moon.

sanskrit: sa hi svagātraprabhayojjvalaṃtyā dīpaprabhāṃ bhāskaravanmumoṣa | mahārhajāṃbūnadacāruvarṇo vidyotayāmāsa diśaśca sarvāḥ ||
english: With the radiant splendour of his limbs he extinguished like the sun the splendour of the lamps; with his beautiful hue as of precious gold he illuminated all the quarters of space.

sanskrit: anākulānyabjasamudgatāni niṣpeṣavaṃtyāyatavikramāṇi | tathaiva dhīrāṇi padāni sapta saptarṣitārāsadṛśo jagāma ||
english: Unflurried, with the lotus-sign in high relief,  far-striding, set down with a stamp, — seven such firm footsteps did he then take, — he who was like the constellation of the seven Ṛṣis.

sanskrit: bodhāya jāto 'smi jagaddhitārthamaṃtyā tathotpattiriyaṃ mameti | caturdiśaṃ siṃhagatirvilokya vāṇīṃ ca bhavyārthakarīmuvāca ||
english: ‘I am born for supreme knowledge, for the welfare of the world, — thus this is my last birth,’ thus did he of lion gait, gazing at the four quarters, utter a voice full of auspicious meaning.

sanskrit: khātprasrute caṃdramarīciśubhre dve vāridhāre śiśiroṣṇavīrye | śarīrasaukhyārthamanuttarasya nipetaturmūrdhani tasya saumye ||
english: Two streams of water bursting from heaven, bright as the moon’s rays, having the power of heat and cold, fell down upon that peerless one’s benign head to give refreshment to his body.

sanskrit: śrīmadvitāne kanakojjvalāṃge vaiḍūryapāde śayane śayānam | yadgauravātkāṃcanapadmahastā yakṣādhipāḥ saṃparivārya tasthuḥ ||
english: His body lay on a bed with a royal canopy and a frame shining with gold, and supported by feet of lapis lazuli, and in his honour the yakṣa-lords stood round guarding him with golden lotuses in their hands.

sanskrit: māyātanūjasya divaukasaḥ khe yasya prabhāvātpraṇataiḥ śirobhiḥ | ādhārayan pāṇdaramātapatraṃ bodhāya jepuḥ paramāśiṣaśca ||
english: The gods in homage to the son of Māyā, with their heads bowed at his majesty, held up a white umbrella in the sky and muttered the highest blessings on his supreme wisdom.

sanskrit: mahoragā dharmaviśeṣatarṣādbuddheṣvatīteṣu kṛtādhikārāḥ | yamavyajan bhaktiviśiṣṭanetrā maṃdārapuṣpaiḥ samavākiraṃśca ||
english: The great dragons  in their great thirst for the Law,  — they who had had the privilege of waiting on the past Buddhas, — gazing with eyes of intent devotion, fanned  him and strewed Mandāra flowers over him.

sanskrit: tathāgatotpādaguṇena tuṣṭāḥ śuddhādhivāsāśca viśuddhasattvāḥ | devā nanaṃdurvigate 'pi rāge magnasya duḥkhe jagato hitāya ||
english: Gladdened through the influence of the birth of the Tathāgata, the gods of pure natures and inhabiting pure abodes  were filled with joy, though all passion was extinguished, for the sake of the world  drowned in sorrow.

sanskrit: yasmin prasūte girirājakīlā vātāhatā nauriva bhūścacāla | sacaṃdanā cotpalapadmagarbhā papāta vṛṣṭirgagaṇādanabhrāt ||
english: When he was born, the earth, though fastened down by (Himālaya) the monarch of mountains, shook like a ship tossed by the wind; and from a cloudless sky there fell a shower full of lotuses and water-lilies, and perfumed with sandalwood.

sanskrit: vātā vavuḥ sparśasukhā manojñā divyāni vāsāṃsyavapātayaṃtaḥ | sūryaḥ sa evābhyadhikaṃ cakāśe jajvāla saumyārciranīrito 'gniḥ ||
english: Pleasant breezes blew soft to the touch, dropping down heavenly garments; the very sun, though still the same, shone with augmented light, and fire gleamed, unstirred, with a gentle lustre.

sanskrit: prāguttare cāvasathapradeśe kūpaḥ svayaṃ prādurabhūtsitāṃbuḥ | aṃtaḥ purāṇyāgatavismayāni yasmin kriyāstīrtha iva pracakruḥ ||
english: In the north-eastern part of the dwelling a well of pure water appeared of its own accord, wherein the inhabitants of the gynaeceum, filled with wonder, performed their rites as in a sacred bathing-place.

sanskrit: dharmārthibhirbhūtagaṇaiśca divyaistaddarśanārthaṃ balamāpa pūraḥ | kautūhalenaiva ca pādapaiśca prapūjayāmāsa sagaṃdhapuṣpaiḥ ||
english: Through the troops of heavenly visitants, who came seeking religious merit, the pool itself received strength to behold Buddha, and by means of its trees bearing flowers and perfumes it eagerly offered him worship.

sanskrit: puṣpadumāḥ svaṃ kusumaṃ pukulluḥ sasīraṇodrāmitadiksugaṃdhi | susaṃbhramadnṛgavadhūpagītaṃ bhujaṃgaṃvṛdāpihitāttavātam ||
english: The flowering trees at once produced their blossoms, while their fragrance was borne aloft in all directions by the wind, accompanied by the songs of bewildered female bees, while the air was inhaled and absorbed by the many snakes (gathering near).

sanskrit: kvacit kvaṇattūryamṛdaṃgagītairvīṇāmukuṃdāmurajādibhiśca | svīṇāṃ calatkuṃḍalabhūṣitānāṃ virājitaṃ cobhayapārścatastat ||
english: Sometimes there resounded  on both sides songs mingled with musical instruments and tabours, and lutes also, drums, tambourines, and the rest, from women adorned with dancing bracelets.

sanskrit: yadrājaśāstraṃ bhṛguraṃgirā vā na cakraturvaṃśakarāvṛṣī tau | tayoḥ sutau tau ca sasarjatustatkālena śukraśca bṛhaspatiśca ||
english: ‘That royal law which neither Bhṛgu nor Aṅgiras ever made, those two great seers the founders of families, their two sons Śukra and Vṛhaspati left revealed at the end.

sanskrit: sārasvataścāpi jagāda naṣṭaṃ vedaṃ punaryaṃ dadṛśurna pūrvam | vyāsastathainaṃ bahudhā cakāra na yaṃ vaśiṣṭhaḥ kṛtavānaśaktiḥ ||
english: ‘Yea, the son of Sarasvatī  I proclaimed that lost Veda which they had never seen in former ages, — Vyāsa rehearsed that in many forms, which Vaśiṣṭha helpless could not compile;

sanskrit: vālmīkinādaśca sasarja padyaṃ jagraṃtha yanna cyavano mahārṣiḥ | cikitsitaṃ yacca cakāra nātriḥ paścāttadātreya ṛṣirjagāda ||
english: ‘The voice of Vālmīki uttered its poetry which the great seer Cyavana could not compose; and that medicine which Atri never invented the wise son of Atri  proclaimed after him;

sanskrit: yacca dvijatvaṃ kuśiko na lebhe tadgādhanaḥ sūnuravāpa rājan | velāṃ samudre sagaraśca dadhre nekṣvākavo yāṃ prathamaṃ babaṃdhuḥ ||
english: ‘That Brahmanhood which Kuśika never attained, — his son, O king, found out the means to gain it; (so) Sagara made a bound for the ocean, which even the Ikṣvākus had not fixed before him.

sanskrit: ācāryakaṃ yogavidhau dvijānāmaprāptamanyairjanako jagāma | khyātāni karmāṇi ca yāni śauraiḥ śūrādayasteṣvabalā babhūvuḥ ||
english: ‘Janaka attained a power of instructing the twice-born in the rules of Yoga which none other had ever reached;  and the famed feats of the grandson of Śūra  (Kriṣṇa) Śūra and his peers were powerless to accomplish.

sanskrit: tasmātpramāṇaṃ na vayo na kālaḥ kaścitkvacicchraiṣṭhyamupaiti loke | rājñāmṛṣīṇāṃ ca hitāni tāni kṛtāni putrairakṛtāni pūrvaiḥ ||
english: ‘Therefore it is not age nor years which are the criterion; different persons win pre-eminence in the world at different places; those mighty exploits worthy of kings and sages, when left undone by the ancestors, have been done by the sons.’

sanskrit: evaṃ nṛpaḥ pratyayitairdvijaistairāśvāsitaścāpyabhinaṃditaśca | śaṃkāmaniṣṭāṃ vijahau manastaḥ praharṣamevādhikamāruroha ||
english: The king, being thus consoled and congratulated by those well-trusted Brāhmans, dismissed from his mind all unwelcome suspicion and rose to a still higher degree of joy;

sanskrit: prītaśca tebhyo dvijasattamebhyaḥ satkārapūrvaṃ pradadau dhanāni | bhūyādayaṃ bhūmipatiryathokto yāyājjarāmetya vanāni ceti ||
english: And well-pleased he gave to those most excellent of the twice-born rich treasures with all due honour, — ‘May he become the ruler of the earth according to your words, and may he retire to the woods when he attains old age.’

sanskrit: athau nimittaiśca tapobalācca tajjanma janmāṃtakarasya buddhvā | śākyeśvarasyālayamājagāma saddharmatarṣādasito mahārṣiḥ ||
english: Then having learned by signs and through the power of his penances this birth of him who was to destroy all birth, the great seer Asita in his thirst for the excellent Law  came to the palace of the Śākya king.

sanskrit: taṃ brahmavidbrahmavidāṃ jvalaṃtaṃ brāhmyā śriyā caiva tapaḥśriyā ca | rājño gururgauravasatkriyābhyāṃ praveśayāmāsa nareṃdrasadma ||
english: Him shining with the glory of sacred knowledge and ascetic observances, the king’s own priest, — himself a special student among the students of sacred knowledge, — introduced into the royal palace with all due reverence and respect.

sanskrit: sa pārthivāṃtaḥpurasaṃnikarṣaṃ kumārajanmāgataharṣavegam | viveśa dhīro balasaṃjñayaiva tapaḥprakarṣācca jarāśrayācca ||
english: He entered into the precincts of the king’s gynaeceum, which was all astir with the joy arisen from the birth of the young prince, — grave from his consciousness of power, his pre-eminence in asceticism, and the weight of old age.

sanskrit: tato nṛpastaṃ munimāsanasthaṃ pādyārghyapūrvaṃ pratipūjya samyak | nimaṃtrayāmāsa yathopacāraṃ purā vasiṣṭhaṃ sa ivāṃtidevaḥ ||
english: Then the king, having duly honoured the sage, who was seated in his seat, with water for the feet and an arghya offering, invited him (to speak) with all ceremonies of respect, as did Antideva  in olden time to Vaśiṣṭha:

sanskrit: dhanyo 'smyanugrāhyamidaṃ kulaṃ me yanmāṃ didṛkṣurbhagavānupetaḥ | ājñāpyatāṃ kiṃ karavāṇi saumya śiṣyo 'smi viśraṃbhitumarhasīti ||
english: ‘I am indeed fortunate, this my family is the object of high favour, that thou shouldst have come to visit me; be pleased to command what I should do, O benign one; I am thy disciple, be pleased to show thy confidence in me.’

sanskrit: evaṃ nṛpeṇopanimaṃtritaḥ sansarveṇa bhāvena muniryathāvat | savismayotphullaviśāladṛṣṭirgaṃbhīradhīrāṇi vacāṃsyuvāca ||
english: The sage, being thus invited by the king, filled with intense feeling as was due, uttered his deep and solemn words, having his large eyes opened wide with wonder:

sanskrit: mahātmani tvayyupapannametat priyātithau tyāgini dharmakāme | sattvānvayajñānavayo 'nurūpā snigdhā yadevaṃ mayi te matiḥ syāt ||
english: ‘This is indeed worthy of thee, great-souled as thou art, fond of guests, liberal and a lover of duty, — that thy mind should be thus kind towards me, in full accordance with thy nature, family, wisdom, and age.

sanskrit: etacca tadyena nṛparṣayaste dharmeṇa sūkṣmāṇi dhanānyapāsya | nityaṃ tyajaṃto vidhivadbabhūvustapobhirāḍhyā vibhavairdaridrāḥ ||
english: ‘This is the true way in which those seer kings of old, rejecting through duty all trivial riches,  have ever flung them away as was right, — being poor in outward substance but rich in ascetic endurance.

sanskrit: prayojanaṃ yattu mamopayāne tanme śṛṇu prītimupehi ca tvam | divyā mayā divyapathe śrutā vāgbodhāya jātastanayastaveti ||
english: ‘But hear now the motive for my coming and rejoice thereat; a heavenly voice has been heard by me in the heavenly path, that thy son has been born for the sake of supreme knowledge.

sanskrit: śrutvā vacastacca manaśca yuktvā jñātvā nimittaiśca tato 'smyupetaḥ | didṛkṣayā śākyakuladhvajasya śakradhvajasyeva samucchritasya ||
english: ‘Having heard that voice and applied my mind thereto, and having known its truth by signs, I am now come hither, with a longing to see the banner of the Śākya race, as if it were Indra’s banner being set up.’

sanskrit: ityetadevaṃ vacanaṃ niśamya praharṣasaṃbhrāṃtagatirnareṃdraḥ | ādāya dhātryaṃkagataṃ kumāraṃ saṃdarśayāmāsa tapodhanāya ||
english: Having heard this address of his, the king, with his steps bewildered with joy, took the prince, who lay on his nurse’s side, and showed him to the holy ascetic.

sanskrit: cakrāṃkapādaṃ sa tathā mahārṣirjālāvanaddhāṃgulipāṇipādam | sorṇabhruvaṃ vāraṇavastikośaṃ savismayaṃ rājasutaṃ dadarśa ||
english: Thus the great seer beheld the king’s son with wonder, — his foot marked with a wheel, his fingers and toes webbed, with a circle of hair between his eyebrows, and signs of vigour like an elephant.

sanskrit: dhātryaṃkasaṃviṣṭamavekṣya cainaṃ devyaṃkasaṃviṣṭamivāgnisūnum | babhūva pakṣmāṃtarivāṃcitāśrurniśvasya caivaṃ tridivonmukho 'bhūt ||
english: Having beheld him seated on his nurse’s side, like the son of Agni (Skanda) seated on Devī’s side, he stood with the tears hanging on the ends of his eyelashes,  and sighing he looked up towards heaven.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvāsitaṃ tvaśrupariplutākṣaṃ snehāttu putrasya nṛpaścakaṃpe | sagadgadaṃ bāṣpakaṣāyakaṃṭhaḥ papraccha ca prāṃjalirānatāṃgaḥ ||
english: But seeing Asita with his eyes thus filled with tears, the king was agitated through his love for his son, and with his hands clasped and his body bowed he thus asked him in a broken voice choked with weeping,

sanskrit: svalpāṃtaraṃ yasya vapurmuneḥ syādbahvadbhutaṃ yasya ca janma dīptam | yasyottamaṃ bhāvinamāttha cārthaṃ taṃ prekṣya kasmāttava dhīra vāṣpaḥ ||
english: ‘One whose beauty has little to distinguish it from that of a divine sage,  and whose brilliant birth has been so wonderful, and for whom thou hast prophesied a transcendent future, — wherefore, on seeing him, do tears come to thee, O reverend one?

sanskrit: api sthirāyurbhagavan kumāraḥ kaccinna śokāya mama prasūtaḥ | labdhaḥ kathaṃcit salilāṃjalirme na khalvimaṃ pātumupaiti kālaḥ ||
english: ‘Is the prince, O holy man, destined to a long life? Surely he cannot be born for my sorrow.  I have with difficulty obtained a handful of water, surely it is not death which comes to drink it.

sanskrit: apyakṣayaṃ me yaśaso nidhānaṃ kacciddhruvo me kulahastasāraḥ | api prayāsyāmi sukhaṃ paratra supte 'pi putre 'nimiṣaikacakṣuḥ ||
english: ‘Tell me, is the hoard of my fame free from destruction? Is this chief prize of my family secure ? Shall I ever depart happily to another life, — I who keep one eye ever awake, even when my son is asleep?

sanskrit: kaccinna me jātamaphullameva kulaprabālaṃ pariśoṣabhāgi | kṣipraṃ vibho brūhi na me 'sti śāṃtiḥ snehaṃ sute vetsi hi bāṃdhavānām ||
english: ‘Surely this young shoot of my family is not born barren, destined only to wither! Speak quickly, my lord, I cannot wait; thou well knowest the love of near kindred for a son.’

sanskrit: ityāgatāvegamaniṣṭabuddhyā buddhvā nareṃdraṃ sa* munirbabhāṣe | mā bhūnmatiste nṛpa kācidanyā niḥsaṃśayaṃ tadyadavocamasmi ||
english: Knowing the king to be thus agitated through his fear of some impending evil, the sage thus addressed him: ‘Let not thy mind, O monarch, be disturbed, — all that I have said is certainly true.

sanskrit: nāsyānyathātvaṃ prati vikriyā me svāṃ vaṃcanāṃ tu prati viklavo 'smi | kālo hi me yātumayaṃ ca jāto jātikṣayasyāsulabhasya boddhā ||
english: ‘I have no feeling of fear as to his being subject to change, but I am distressed for mine own disappointment. It is my time to depart, and this child is now born, — he who knows that mystery hard to attain, the means of destroying birth.

sanskrit: vihāya rājyaṃ viṣayeṣvanāsthastīvraiḥ prayatnairadhigamya tattvam | jagatyayaṃ mohatamo nihaṃtuṃ jvaliṣyati jñānamayo hi sūryaḥ ||
english: Having forsaken his kingdom, indifferent to all worldly objects, and having attained the highest truth by strenuous efforts, he will shine forth as a sun of knowledge to destroy the darkness of illusion in the world.

sanskrit: duḥkhārṇavādvyādhivikīrṇaphenājjarātaraṃgānmaraṇogravegāt | uttārayiṣyatyayamuhyamānamārttaṃ jagajjñānamahāplavena ||
english: ‘He will deliver by the boat of knowledge the distressed world, borne helplessly along, from the ocean of misery which throws up sickness as its foam, tossing with the waves of old age, and rushing with the dreadful onflow of death.

sanskrit: prajñāṃbuvegāṃ sthiraśīlavaprāṃ samādhiśītāṃ vratacakravākām | asyottamāṃ dharmanadīṃ pravṛttāṃ tṛṣṇārditaḥ pāsyati jīvalokaḥ ||
english: ‘The thirsty world of living beings will drink the flowing stream of his Law, bursting forth with the water of wisdom, enclosed by the banks of strong moral rules, delightfully cool with contemplation, and filled with religious vows as with ruddy geese.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ saha ca kathāṃ tāmāśvāsya sa sātavāhanastasyāḥ / tadbhāṣayāvatāraṃ vaktuṃ cakre kathāpīṭham //
english: And having recovered the sense of that tale with their help, Sātavāhana composed the book named Kathāpīṭha, in order to show how the tale came to be first made known in the Paiśācha language.

sanskrit: sā ca citrarasanirbharā kathā vismṛtāmarakathā kutūhalāt / tadvidhāya nagare nirantarāṃ khyātimatra bhuvanatraye gatā //
english: Now that tale was so full of various interest that men were so taken with it as to forget the tales of the gods, and after producing that effect in the city it attained uninterrupted renown in the three worlds.

sanskrit: prathamas taraṅgaḥ / gaurīnavapariṣvaṅge vibhoḥ svedāmbu pātu vaḥ / netrāgnibhītyā kāmena vāruṇastramivāhitam //
english: [Additional note: The Paiśāchī language] INVOCATION MAY the water of Śiva’s sweat, fresh from the embrace of Gaurī,[1] which the God of Love when afraid of the fire of Śiva’s eye employs as his aqueous weapon, protect you.

sanskrit: kailāse dhūrjaṭervaktrātpuṣpadantaṃ gaṇottamam / tasmādvararucībhūtātkāṇabhūtiṃ ca bhūtale // kāṇabhūterguṇāḍhyaṃ ca guṇāḍhyātsātavāhanam / yatprāptaṃ śṛṇutedaṃ tadvidyādharakathādbhutam //
english: Listen to the following tale of the Vidyādharas, which the excellent Gaṇa Puṣpadanta heard on Mount Kailāsa from the god of the matted locks, and which Kāṇabhūti heard on the earth from the same Puṣpadanta after he had become Vararuci, and which Guṇāḍhya heard from Kāṇabhūti, and Sātavāhana heard from Guṇāḍhya.

sanskrit: asti vatsa iti khyāto deśo darpopaśāntaye / svargasya nirmito dhātrā pratimalla iva kṣitau //
english: Story of Udayana, King of Vatsa [M] (Main story line continued) There is a land[2] famous under the name of Vatsa, that appears as if it had been made by the Creator as an earthly rival to dash the pride of heaven.

sanskrit: kauśāmbī nāma tatrāsti madhyabhāge mahāpurī / lakṣmīvilāsavasatirbhūtalasyeva karṇikā //
english: In the centre of it is a great city named Kauśāmbī, the favourite dwelling-place of the Goddess of Prosperity;

sanskrit: tasyāṃ rājā śatānīkaḥ pāṇḍavānvayasaṃbhavaḥ / janamejayaputro 'bhūtpautro rājñaḥ parīkṣitaḥ //
english: In it dwelt a king named Śatānīka, sprung from the Pāṇḍava family; he was the son of Janamejaya, and the grandson of King Parīkṣit, who was the great-grandson of Abhimanyu.

sanskrit: abhimanyuprapautraśca yasyādipuruṣo 'rjunaḥ / tripurāribhujastambhadṛṣṭadordaṇḍavikramaḥ //
english: The first progenitor of his race was Arjuna, the might of whose strong arm was tested in a struggle with the mighty arms of Śiva[3];

sanskrit: kalatraṃ bhūrabhūttasya rājñī viṣṇumatī tathā / ekā ratnāni suṣuve na tāvadaparā sutam //
english: his wife was the earth, and also Viṣṇumatī his queen: the first produced jewels, but the second did not produce a son.

sanskrit: ekadā mṛgayāsaṅgādbhrāmyataścāsya bhūpateḥ / abhūcchāṇḍilyamuninā samaṃ paricayo vane //
english: Once on a time, as that king was roaming about in his passion for the chase, he made acquaintance in the forest with the hermit Śāṇḍilya.

sanskrit: so 'sya putrārthino rājñaḥ kauśāmbīmetya sādhitam / mantrapūtaṃ caruṃ rājñīṃ prāśayanmunisattamaḥ //
english: That worthy sage, finding out that the king desired a son, came to Kauśāmbī and administered to his queen an artfully prepared oblation[4] consecrated with mystic verses.

sanskrit: tatastasya suto jajñe sahasrānīkasaṃjñakaḥ / śuśubhe sa pitā tena vinayena guṇo yathā //
english: Then he had a son born to him called Sahasrānīka. And his father was adorned by him as excellence is by modesty.

sanskrit: yuvarājaṃ kramātkṛtvā śatānīko 'tha taṃ sutam / saṃbhogaireva rājābhūnna tu bhūbhāracintanaiḥ //
english: Then in course of time Śatānīka made that son crown prince and, though he still enjoyed kingly pleasures, ceased to trouble himself about the cares of government.

sanskrit: athāsuraiḥ samaṃ yuddhe prāpte sāhāyakecchayā / dūtastasmai visṛṣṭo 'bhūdrājñe śakreṇa mātaliḥ //
english: Then a war arose between the gods and Asuras, and Indra sent Mātali as a messenger to that king begging for aid.

sanskrit: tato yugaṃdharākhyasya haste dhūryasya mantriṇaḥ / supratīkābhidhānasya mukhyasenāpateśca saḥ // samarpya putraṃ rājyaṃ ca nihantumasurānraṇe / śakrāntikaṃ śatānīkaḥ saha mātalinā yayau //
english: Then he committed his son and his kingdom to the care of his principal minister, who was called Yogandhara, and his commander-in-chief, whose name was Supratīka, and went to Indra with Mātali to slay the Asuras in fight.

sanskrit: asurān yamadaṃṣṭrādīn bahūn paśyati vāsave / hatvā tatraiva saṅgrāme prāpa mṛtyuṃ sa bhūpatiḥ //
english: That king, having slain many Asuras, of whom Yamadaṃṣṭra was the chief, under the eyes of Indra, met death in that very battle.

sanskrit: mātalyānītadehaṃ ca devī taṃ nṛpamanvagāt / rājalakṣmīśca tatputraṃ sahasrānīkamāśrayat //
english: The king’s body was brought back by Mātali, and the queen burnt herself with it, and the royal dignity descended to his son Sahasrānīka.

sanskrit: citraṃ tasminsamārūḍhe pitryaṃ siṃhāsanaṃ nṛpe / bhareṇa sarvato rājñāṃ śirāṃsi natimāyayuḥ //
english: Wonderful to say, when that king ascended his father’s throne the heads of the kings on every side of his dominions were bent down with the weight.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakraḥ suhṛtputraṃ vipakṣavijayotsave / svargaṃ sahasrānīkaṃ taṃ nināya preṣya mātalim //
english: Then Indra sent Mātali, and brought to heaven that Sahasrānīka, as being the son of his friend, that he might be present at the great feast which he was holding to celebrate his victory over his foes.

sanskrit: sa tatra nandane devān krīḍataḥ kāminīsakhān / dṛṣṭvā svocitabhāryārthī rājā śokam ivāviśat //
english: There the king saw the gods, attended by their fair ones, sporting in the garden of Nandana, and desiring for himself a suitable wife, fell into low spirits.

sanskrit: vijñāyaitamabhiprāyaṃ tamuvācātha vāsavaḥ / rājannalaṃ viṣādena vāñcheyaṃ tava setsyati //
english: Then Indra, perceiving this desire of his, said to him: “King, away with despondency; this desire of thine shall be accomplished.

sanskrit: utpannā hi kṣitau bhāryā tulyā te pūrvanirmitā / imaṃ ca śṛṇu vṛttāntamatra te varṇayāmyaham // purā pitāmahaṃ draṣṭumagacchaṃ tatsabhāmaham / vidhūmo nāma paścācca mamaiko vasurāgamat //
english: For there has been born upon the earth one who was long ago ordained a suitable match for thee. For listen to the following history, which I now proceed to relate to thee:— “Long ago I went to the Court of Brahmā in order to visit him, and a certain Vasu named Vidhūma followed me.

sanskrit: sthiteṣvasmāsu tatraiva viriñcaṃ draṣṭumapsarāḥ / āgādalambuṣā nāma vātavisraṃsitāṃśukā //
english: While we were there an Apsaras named Alambuṣā came to see Brahmā, and her robe was blown aside by the wind.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvaiva sa kāmasya vaśaṃ vasurupāgamat / sāpyapsarā jhagityāsīttadrūpākṛṣṭalocanā //
english: And the Vasu when he beheld her was overpowered by love, and the Apsaras too had her eyes immediately attracted by his form.

sanskrit: tad ālokya mamāpaśya nmukhaṃ kamalasaṃbhavaḥ / abhiprāyaṃ viditvāsya tāvahaṃ śaptavān krudhā // martyaloke 'vatāro 'stu yuvayoravinītayoḥ / bhaviṣyathaśca tatraiva yuvāṃ bhāryāpatī iti // sa vasustvaṃ samutpannaḥ sahasrānīkabhūpate / śatānīkasya tanayo bhūṣaṇaṃ śaśinaḥ kule //
english: The lotus-sprung god[5] when he beheld that looked me full in the face, and I, knowing his meaning, in wrath cursed those two: ‘Be born, you two shameless creatures, into the world of mortals, and there become man and wife.’ That Vasu has been born as thou, Sahasrānīka, the son of Śatānīka, an ornament to the race of the moon.

sanskrit: sāpyapsarā ayodhyāyāṃ kṛtavarmanṛpātmajā / jātā mṛgāvatī nāma sā te bhāryā bhaviṣyati // itīndravākyapavanairudbhūto hṛdi bhūpateḥ / sasnehe tasya jhagiti prājvalanmadanānalaḥ //
english: And that Apsaras too has been born in Ayodhyā as the daughter of King Kṛtavarman, Mṛgāvatī by name, she shall be thy wife.” By these words of Indra the flame of love was fanned in the passionate[6] heart of the king and burst out into full blaze;

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃmānya śakreṇa preṣitastadrathena saḥ / saha mātalinā rājā pratasthe svāṃ purīṃ prati //
english: Indra then dismissed the king from heaven with all due honour in his own chariot, and he set out with Mātali[7] for his capital.

sanskrit: gacchantaṃ cāpsarāḥ prītyā tamuvāca tilottamā / rājanvakṣyāmi te kiṃcitpratīkṣasva manāgiti //
english: But as he was starting the Apsaras Tilottamā said to him out of affection: “King, I have somewhat to say to thee;

sanskrit: tadaśrutvaiva hi yayau sa tāṃ dhyāyanmṛgāvatīm / tataḥ sā lajjitā kopāttaṃ śaśāpa tilottamā //
english: wait a moment.” But he, thinking on Mṛgāvatī, went off without hearing what she said;

sanskrit: yayā hṛtamanā rājan na śṛṇoṣi vaco mama / tasyāścaturdaśasamā viyogaste bhaviṣyati // mātalistacca śuśrāva sa ca rājā priyotsukaḥ / yayau rathena kauśāmbīmayodhyāṃ manasā punaḥ //
english: then Tilottamā in her rage cursed him: “King, thou shalt be separated for fourteen years from her who has so engrossed thy mind that thou dost not hear my speech.” Now Mātali heard that curse, but the king, yearning for his beloved, did not. In the chariot he went to Kauśāmbī, but in spirit he went to Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: tato yugaṃdharādibhyo mantribhyo vāsavācchrutam / mṛgāvatīgataṃ sarvaṃ śaśaṃsotsukayā dhiyā //
english: Then the king told with longing heart all that he had heard from Indra with reference to Mṛgāvatī to his ministers, Yogandhara and the others;

sanskrit: yācituṃ tāṃ sa kanyāṃ ca tatpituḥ kṛtavarmaṇaḥ / ayodhyāṃ prāhiṇoddūtaṃ kālakṣepāsaho nṛpaḥ //
english: and not being able to endure delay, he sent an ambassador to Ayodhyā to ask her father Kṛtavarman for the hand of that maiden.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā ca taddūtācchrutvā saṃdeśamabhyadhāt / harṣāddevyai kalāvatyai tataḥ sāpyenamabravīt // rājan sahasrānīkāya deyāvaśyaṃ mṛgāvatī / imam arthaṃ ca me svapne jāne ko 'py avadad dvijaḥ // atha hṛṣṭo mṛgāvatyā nṛttagītādikauśalam / rūpaṃ cāpratimaṃ tasmai dūtāyādarśayan nṛpaḥ //
english: And Kṛtavarman having heard from the ambassador his commission, told in his joy the Queen Kalāvatī, and then she said to him: “King, we ought certainly to give Mṛgāvatī to Sahasrānīka, and, I remember, a certain Brāhman told me this very thing in a dream.” Then in his delight the king showed to the ambassador Mṛgāvatī’s wonderful skill in dancing, singing and other accomplishments, and her matchless beauty;

sanskrit: dadau tāṃ ca sa kāntānāṃ kalānām ekam āspadam / kṛtavarmā sutāṃ tasmai rājñe mūrtim ivaindavīm //
english: so the King Kṛtavarman gave to Sahasrānīka that daughter of his who was unequalled as a mine of graceful arts, and who shone like an incarnation of the moon.

sanskrit: parasparaguṇāvāptyai sa śrutaprajñayoriva / abhūt sahasrānīkasya mṛgāvatyāś ca saṃgamaḥ //
english: That marriage of Sahasrānīka and Mṛgāvatī was one in which the good qualities of either party supplemented those of the other, and might be compared to the union of learning and intelligence.

sanskrit: atha tasyācirādrājño mantriṇāṃ jajñire sutāḥ / jajñe yugaṃdharasyāpi putro yaugandharāyaṇaḥ //
english: Not long after sons were born to the king’s ministers; Yogandhara had a son born to him named Yaugandharāyaṇa;

sanskrit: supratīkasya putraśca rumaṇvānityajāyata / yo 'sya narmasuhṛttasya putro 'jani vasantakaḥ //
english: and Supratīka had a son born to him named Rumaṇvat. And to the king’s master of the revels was born a son named Vasantaka.

sanskrit: tatastasyāpi divasaiḥ sahasrānīkabhūpateḥ / babhāra garbhamāpāṇḍumukhī rājñī mṛgāvatī // yayāce sātha bhartāraṃ darśanātṛptalocanam / dohadaṃ rudhirāpūrṇalīlāvāpīnimajjanam //
english: Then in a few days Mṛgāvatī became slightly pale and promised to bear a child to King Sahasrānīka. And then she asked the king, who was never tired of looking at her, to gratify her longing[8] by filling a tank of blood for her to bathe in.

sanskrit: sa cecchāṃ pūrayan rājñyā lākṣādirasanirbharām / cakāra dhārmiko rājā vāpīṃ raktāvṛtām iva //
english: [also see notes on the magical properties of blood] Accordingly the king, who was a righteous man, in order to gratify her desire, had a tank filled with the juice of lac and other red extracts, so that it seemed to be full of blood.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ snāntīmakasmācca lākṣāliptāṃ nipatya tām / garuḍānvayajaḥ pakṣī jahārāmiṣaśaṅkayā //
english: And while she was bathing in that lake, and covered with red dye, a bird of the race of Garuḍa[9] suddenly pounced upon her and carried her off, thinking she was raw flesh.

sanskrit: pakṣiṇā kvāpi nītāṃ tāmanveṣṭumiva tatkṣaṇam / yayau sahasrānīkasya dhairyaṃ vihvalacetasā //
english: As soon as she was carried away in some unknown direction by the bird the king became distracted, and his self-command forsook him as if in order to go in search of her.

sanskrit: priyānuraktaṃ ceto 'pi nūnaṃ tasya patattriṇā / jahre yena sa niḥsaṃjñaḥ papāta bhuvi bhūpatiḥ // kṣaṇācca labdhasaṃjñe 'sminrājñi buddhvā prabhāvataḥ / avatīrya dyumārgeṇa tatra mātalirāyayau //
english: His heart was so attached to his beloved that it was in very truth carried off by that bird, and thus he fell senseless upon the earth. As soon as he had recovered his senses, Mātali, who had discovered all by his divine power, descended through the air and came where the king was.

sanskrit: sa rājānaṃ samāśvāsya sāvadhiṃ prāgyathā śrutam / tasmai tilottamāśāpaṃ kathayitvā tato 'gamat //
english: He consoled the king, and told him the curse of Tilottamā with its destined end, as he had heard it long ago, and then he took his departure.

sanskrit: hā priye pūrṇakāmā sā jātā pāpā tilottamā / ityādi ca sa śokārto vilalāpa mahīpatiḥ // vijñātaśāpavṛttānto bodhitaśca sa mantribhiḥ / kathaṃcijjīvitaṃ dadhne punaḥ saṃgamavāñchayā //
english: Then the king, tormented with grief, lamented on this wise: “Alas, my beloved, that wicked Tilottamā has accomplished her desire.” But having learned the facts about the curse, and having received advice from his ministers, he managed, though with difficulty, to retain his life through hope of a future reunion.

sanskrit: tāṃ ca rājñīṃ sa pakṣīndraḥ kṣaṇānnītvā mṛgāvatīm / jīvantīṃ vīkṣya tatyāja daivādudayaparvate //
english: But that bird which had carried off Mṛgāvatī, as soon as it found out that she was alive, abandoned her, and, as fate would have it, left her on the mountain where the sun rises.

sanskrit: tyaktvā tasmin gate cātha rājñī śokabhayākulā / dadarśānātham ātmānaṃ durgamādritaṭasthitam //
english: And when the bird let her drop and departed, the queen, distracted with grief and fear, saw that she was left unprotected on the slope of a trackless mountain.

sanskrit: ekākinīm ekavastrāṃ krandantīm atha tāṃ vane / grāsīkartuṃ pravṛtto 'bhūdutthāyājagaro mahān //
english: While she was weeping in the forest, alone, with only one garment to cover her, an enormous serpent rose up and prepared to swallow her.

sanskrit: nihatyājagaraṃ taṃ ca śubodarkā tathaiva sā / divyena mocitā puṃsāṃ dṛṣṭanaṣṭena kenacit //
english: Then she for whom prosperity was reserved in the future was delivered by some heavenly hero who came down and slew the serpent and disappeared almost as soon as he was seen.

sanskrit: tato vanagajasyāgre sā svayaṃ maraṇārthinī / ātmānamakṣipatso 'pi rarakṣa dayayeva tām //
english: Thereupon she, longing for death, flung herself down in front of a wild elephant, but even he spared her as if out of compassion.

sanskrit: citraṃ yacchvāpado 'pyenāṃ patitāmapi gocare / nāvadhīdathavā kiṃ hi na bhavedīśvarecchayā //
english: Wonderful was it that even a wild beast did not slay her when she fell in his way! Or rather it was not to be wondered at.

sanskrit: atha prapātābhimukhī bālā garbhabharālasā / smarantī taṃ ca bhartāraṃ muktakaṇṭhaṃ ruroda sā //
english: What cannot the will of Śiva effect? Then the girl, tardy with the weight of her womb, desiring to hurl herself down from a precipice, and thinking upon that lord of hers, wept aloud;

sanskrit: tacchrutvā muniputro 'tha tatraikastāṃ samāyayau / āgataḥ phalamūlārthaṃ śucaṃ mūrtimatīmiva //
english: and a hermit’s son, who had wandered there in search of roots and fruits, hearing that, came up, and found her looking like the incarnation of sorrow.

sanskrit: sa ca pṛṣṭvā yathāvṛttamāśvāsya ca kathaṃcana / jamadagnyāśramaṃ rājñīṃ nināyaināṃ dayārdradhīḥ //
english: And he, after questioning the queen about her adventures, and comforting her as well as he could, with a heart melted with compassion led her off to the hermitage of Jamadagni.

sanskrit: tatra mūrtamivāśvāsaṃ jamadagniṃ dadarśa sā / tejasā sthirabālārkaṃ kurvāṇamudayācalam //
english: There she beheld Jamadagni, looking like the incarnation of comfort, whose brightness so illumined the eastern mountain that it seemed as if the rising sun ever rested on it.

sanskrit: so 'pi tāṃ pādapatitāṃ munirāśritavatsalaḥ / rājñīṃ viyogaduḥkhārtāṃ divyadṛṣṭirabhāṣata // iha te janitā putri putro vaṃśadharaḥ pituḥ / bhaviṣyati ca bhartā te saṃgamo mā śucaṃ kṛthāḥ //
english: When she fell at his feet, that hermit who was kind to all who came to him for help, and possessed heavenly insight, said to her who was tortured with the pain of separation: “Here there shall be born to thee, my daughter, a son who shall uphold the family of his father, and thou shalt be reunited to thy husband;

sanskrit: ityuktā muninā sādhvī sā jagrāha mṛgāvatī / āśrame 'vasthitiṃ tasminnāśāṃ ca priyasaṃgame //
english: therefore weep not.” When that virtuous woman heard that speech of the hermit’s she took up her abode in that hermitage, and entertained hope of a reunion with her beloved.

sanskrit: tataśca divasaistatra ślāghanīyamaninditā / satsaṃgatirivācāraṃ putraratnamasūta sā //
english: And some days after the blameless one gave birth to a charmingly beautiful son, as association with the good produces good manners.

sanskrit: śrīmānudayano nāmnā rājā jāto mahāyaśāḥ / bhaviṣyati ca putro 'sya sarvavidyādharādhipaḥ // ity antarikṣād udabhūt tasmin kāle sarasvatī / ādadhānā mṛgāvatyāś cittavismṛtam utsavam //
english: At that moment a voice was heard from heaven: “An august king of great renown has been born, Udayana by name, and his son shall be monarch of all the Vidyādharas.” That voice restored to the heart of Mṛgāvatī joy which she had long forgotten.

sanskrit: kramādudayanaḥ so 'tha bālastasmiṃstapovane / avardhata nijaiḥ sārdhaṃ vayasyair iva sadguṇaiḥ //
english: Gradually that boy grew up to size and strength in that grove of asceticism, accompanied by his own excellent qualities as playmates.

sanskrit: kṛvā kṣatrocitānsarvānsaṃskārāñjamadagninā / vyanīyata sa vidyāsu dhanurvede ca vīryavān //
english: And the heroic child had the sacraments appropriate to a member of the warrior caste performed for him by Jamadagni, and was instructed by him in the sciences and the practice of archery.

sanskrit: kṛṣṭvā ca svakarānmātā tasya snehānmṛgāvatī / sahasrānīkanāmāṅkaṃ cakāra kaṭakaṃ kare //
english: And out of love for him Mṛgāvatī drew off from her own wrist, and placed on his, a bracelet marked with the name of Sahasrānīka.

sanskrit: hariṇākheṭake jātu bhrāmyannudayano 'tha saḥ / śabareṇa haṭhākrāntamaṭavyāṃ sarpamaikṣata // sadayaḥ sundare tasminsarpe taṃ śabaraṃ ca saḥ / uvāca mucyatāmeṣa sarpo madvacanāditi // tataḥ sa śabaro 'vādījjīvikeyaṃ mama prabho / kṛpaṇo 'haṃ hi jīvāmi bhujagaṃ khelayansadā //
english: Then that Udayana, roaming about once upon a time in pursuit of deer, beheld in the forest a snake that had been forcibly captured by a Śavara.[10] And he, feeling pity for the beautiful snake, said to that Śavara: “Let go this snake to please me.” Then that Śavara said: “My lord, this is my livelihood, for I am a poor man, and I always maintain myself by exhibiting dancing snakes.

sanskrit: vipanne pannage pūrvaṃ mantrauṣadhibalādayam / vaṣṭabdhaśca mayā labdhaś cinvataitāṃ mahāṭavīm // śrutvetyudayanasyāgī dattvāsmai śabarāya tam / kaṭakaṃ jananīdattaṃ sa taṃ sarpamamocayat //
english: The snake I previously had having died, I searched through the great wood, and finding this one, overpowered him by charms and captured him.” When he heard this, the generous Udayana gave that Śavara the bracelet which his mother had bestowed on him, and persuaded him to set the snake at liberty.

sanskrit: gṛhītakaṭake yāte śabare purato gatim / kṛtvā sa bhujagaḥ prīto jagādodayanaṃ tadā // vasunemiriti khyāto jyeṣṭho bhrātāsmi vāsukeḥ / imāṃ vīṇāṃ gṛhāṇa tvaṃ mattaḥ saṃrakṣitāttvayā // tantrīnirghoṣaramyāṃ ca śrutibhāgavibhājitām / tāmbūlīśca sahāmlānamālātilakayuktibhiḥ // tadyukto jamadagnestaṃ nāgotkṣiptaḥ sa cāśramam / āgādudayano māturdṛśi varṣannivāmṛtam //
english: The Śavara took the bracelet and departed, and then the snake, being pleased with Udayana, bowed before him and said as follows:— “I am the eldest brother of Vāsuki,[11] called Vasunemi: receive from me, whom thou hast preserved, this lute, sweet in the sounding of its strings, divided according to the division of the quarter-tones, and betel leaf, together with the art of weaving unfading garlands and adorning the forehead with marks that never become indistinct.” Then Udayana, furnished with all these, and dismissed by the snake, returned to the hermitage of Jamadagni, raining nectar, so to speak, into the eyes of his mother.

sanskrit: atrāntare sa śabaro 'pyaṭavīṃ prāpya paryaṭan / ādāyodayanātprāptaṃ kaṭakaṃ tadvidhervaśāt // vikrīṇānaśca tattatra rājanāmāṅkamāpaṇe / vaṣṭabhya rājapuruṣairninye rājakulaṃ ca saḥ //
english: [also see notes on snakes] In the meantime that Śavara who had lighted on this forest, and while roaming about in it had obtained the bracelet from Udayana by the will of fate, was caught attempting to sell this ornament, marked with the king’s name, in the market, and was arrested by the police, and brought up in court before the King.

sanskrit: kutastvayedaṃ kaṭakaṃ saṃprāptamiti tatra saḥ / rājñā sahasrānīkena svayaṃ śokād apṛcchata //
english: Then King Sahasrānīka himself asked him in sorrow whence he had obtained the bracelet.

sanskrit: athodayādrau sarpasya grahaṇātprabhṛti svakam / kaṭakaprāptivṛttāntaṃ śabaraḥ sa jagāda tam //
english: Then that Śavara told him the whole story of his obtaining possession of the bracelet, beginning with his capture of the snake upon the eastern mountain.

sanskrit: tadbuddhvā śabarāddṛṣṭvā dayitāvalayaṃ ca tam / vicāra dolām ārohat sahasrānīkabhūpatiḥ //
english: Hearing that from the Śavara, and beholding that bracelet of his beloved, King Sahasrānīka ascended the swing of doubt.

sanskrit: kṣīṇaḥ śāpaḥ sa te rājannudayādrau ca sā sthitā / jamadagnyāśrame jāyā saputrā te mṛgāvatī // iti divyā tadā vāṇī nandayāmāsa taṃ nṛpam / viprayoganidāghārtaṃ vāridhāreva barhiṇam // athotkaṇṭhādīrghe kathamapi dine 'sminnavasite tamevāgre kṛtvā śabaramaparedyuḥ sa nṛpatiḥ / sahasrānīkastāṃ sarabhasamavāptuṃ priyatamāṃ pratasthe tatsainyaiḥ samamudayaśailāśramapadam //
english: Then a divine voice from heaven delighted the king, who was tortured with the fire of separation, as do the raindrops the peacock when afflicted with the heat, uttering these words: “Thy curse is at an end, O king, and that wife of thine, Mṛgāvatī, is residing in the hermitage of Jamadagni together with thy son.” Then that day at last came to an end, though being made long by anxious expectation, and on the morrow that King Sahasrānīka, making the Śavara show him the way, set out with his army for that hermitage on the eastern mountain, in order quickly to recover his beloved wife.

sanskrit: iti mahākaviśrīsomadevabhaṭṭaviracite kathāsaritsāgare kathāmukhalambake prathamas taraṅgaḥ / dvitīyas taraṅgaḥ / gatvātha dūramadhvānaṃ rājā vasatimagrahīt / dine tasmin sa kasmiṃścid araṇyasarasastaṭe //
english: [Additional note: the Garuḍa bird] [M] (Main story line continued) AFTER he had gone a long distance, the king encamped that day in a certain forest on the border of a lake.

sanskrit: śayanīyagataḥ śrāntastatra sevārasāgatam / sāyaṃ saṃgatakaṃ nāma jagāda kathakaṃ nṛpaḥ // kathāmākhyāhi me kāṃciddhṛdayasya vinodinīm / mṛgāvatīmukhāmbhojadarśanotsavakāṅkṣiṇaḥ // atha saṃgatako 'vādīddeva kiṃ tapyase vṛthā / āsanna eva devyāste kṣīṇaśāpaḥ samāgamaḥ //
english: He went to bed weary, and in the evening he said to Saṃgataka, a story-teller who had come to him on account of the pleasure he took in his service: “Tell me some tale that will gladden my heart, for I am longing for the joy of beholding the lotus-face of Mṛgāvatī.” Then Saṃgataka said: “King, why do you grieve without cause? The union with your queen, which will mark the termination of your curse, is nigh at hand.

sanskrit: saṃyogā viprayogāśca bhavanti bahavo nṛṇām / tatha cātra kathāmekāṃ kathayāmi śṛṇu prabho //
english: Human beings experience many unions and separations; and I will tell you a story to illustrate this. Listen, my lord.

sanskrit: mālave yajñasomākhyo dvijaḥ kaścidabhūtpurā / tasya ca dvau sutau sādhorjāyete sma janapriyau //
english: Once on a time there lived in the country of Mālava a Brāhman named Yajñasoma. And that good man had two sons born to him, beloved by men.

sanskrit: ekastayorabhūnnāmnā kālanemiriti śrutaḥ / dvitīyaścāpi vigatabhaya ityākhyayābhavat //
english: One of them was known as Kālanemi and the second was named Vigatabhaya.

sanskrit: pitari svargate tau ca bhrātarau tīrṇaśaiśavau / vidyāprāptyai prayayatuḥ puraṃ pāṭaliputrakam //
english: Now when their father had gone to heaven, those two brothers, having passed through the age of childhood, went to the city of Pāṭaliputra to acquire learning.

sanskrit: tatraivopāttavidyābhyāmupādhyāyo nije sute / devaśarmā dadau tābhyāṃ mūrte vidye ivāpare //
english: And when they had completed their studies their teacher Devaśarman gave them his own two daughters, like another couple of sciences incarnate in bodily form.

sanskrit: athānyān vīkṣya tānāḍhyān gṛhasthān īrṣyayā śriyam / homaiḥ sa sādhayām āsa kālanemiḥ kṛtavrataḥ //
english: Then seeing that the householders around him were rich, Kālanemi through envy made a vow and propitiated the Goddess of Fortune with burnt-offerings.

sanskrit: sā ca tuṣṭā satī sākṣādevaṃ śrīstamabhāṣata / bhūri prāpsyasi vittaṃ ca putraṃ ca pṛthivīpatim //
english: And the goddess being satisfied appeared in bodily form and said to him: “Thou shalt obtain great wealth and a son who shall rule the earth;

sanskrit: kiṃ tvante caurasadṛśo vadhastava bhaviṣyati / hutamagnau tvayā yasmadamarṣakaluṣātmanā //
english: but at last thou shalt be put to death like a robber, because thou hast offered flesh in the fire with impure motives.”[1] When she had said this, the goddess disappeared;

sanskrit: ityuktvāntardadhe lakṣmīḥ kālanemirapi kramāt / mahādhano 'bhūt kiṃ cāsya dinaiḥ putro 'pyajāyata //
english: and Kālanemi in course of time became very rich; moreover, after some days a son was born to him.

sanskrit: śrīvarādeṣa saṃprāpta iti nāmnā tamātmajam / śrīdattamakarotso 'pi pitā pūrṇamanorathaḥ //
english: So the father, whose desires were now accomplished, called that son Śrīdatta,[2] because he had been obtained by the favour of the Goddess of Fortune.

sanskrit: kramātsa vṛddhiṃ saṃprāptaḥ śrīdatto brāhmaṇo 'pi san / astreṃṣu bāhuyuddheṣu babhūvāpratimo bhuvi //
english: In course of time Śrīdatta grew up, and though a Brāhman, became matchless upon earth in the use of weapons, and in boxing and wrestling.

sanskrit: kālanemeratha bhrātā tīrthārthī sarpabhakṣitām / bhāryāmuddiśya vigatabhayo deśāntaraṃ yayau //
english: Then Kālanemi’s brother Vigatabhaya went to a foreign land, having become desirous of visiting places of pilgrimage, through sorrow’ for his wife, who had died of the bite of a snake.

sanskrit: śrīdatto 'pi guṇajñena rājñā vallabhaśaktinā / tatra vikramaśakteḥ sa svaputrasya kṛtaḥ sakhā //
english: Moreover, the king of the land, Vallabhaśakti, who appreciated good qualities, made Śrīdatta the companion of his son Vikramaśakti.

sanskrit: rājaputreṇa tenāsya sahavāso 'bhimāninā / bālye duryodhaneneva bhīmasyāsīttarasvinā //
english: So he had to live with a haughty prince, as the impetuous Bhīma lived in his youth with Duryodhana.

sanskrit: dvāvetasyātha mittratvaṃ viprasyāvantideśajau / kṣatriyau bāhuśālī ca vajramuṣṭiśca jagmatuḥ //
english: Then two Kṣatriyas, natives of Avanti, Bāhuśālin and Vajramuṣṭi, became friends of that Brāhman.

sanskrit: bāhuyuddhajitāścānye dākṣiṇātyā guṇapriyāḥ / svayaṃvarasuhṛttvena mantriputrāstamāśrayan //
english: And some other men from the Deccan, sons of ministers, having been conquered by him in wrestling, resorted to him out of spontaneous friendship, as they knew how to value merit.

sanskrit: mahābalavyāghrabhaṭāvupendrabala ityapi / tathā niṣṭhurako nāma sauhārdaṃ tasya cakrire //
english: Mahābala and Vyāghrabhaṭa, and also Upendrabala and a man named Niṣṭhuraka, became his friends.

sanskrit: kadācidatha varṣāsu vihartuṃ jāhnavītaṭe / śrīdattaḥ saha tairmitrai rājaputrasakho yayau //
english: One day, as years rolled on, Śrīdatta, being in attendance on the prince, went with him and those friends to sport on the bank of the Ganges;

sanskrit: svabhṛtyāstatra taṃ cakrurnijaṃ rājasutaṃ nṛpam / śrīdatto 'pi sa tatkālaṃ rājā mittrairakalpyata //
english: then the prince’s own servants made him king, and at the same time Śrīdatta was chosen king by his friends.

sanskrit: tāvatā jātaroṣeṇa rājaputreṇa tena saḥ / vipravīro raṇāyāśu samāhūto madaspṛśā // sa tena bāhuyuddhena śrīdattenātha nirjitaḥ / cakāra hṛdi vadhyaṃ tu varddhamānaṃ kalaṅkitam //
english: This made the prince angry, and in overweening confidence he at once challenged that Brāhman hero to fight. Then being conquered by him in wrestling, and so disgraced, he made up his mind that this rising hero should be put to death.

sanskrit: jñātvā ca tamabhiprāyaṃ rājaputrasya śaṅkitaḥ / śrīdattaḥ saha tairmittraistatsamīpādapāsarat //
english: But Śrīdatta found out that intention of the prince’s, and withdrew in alarm with those friends of his from his presence.

sanskrit: upasarpansa cāpaśyadgaṅgāmadhyagatāṃ striyam / hriyamāṇāṃ jalaughena sāgarasthāmiva śriyam //
english: And as he was going along he saw in the middle of the Ganges a woman being dragged under by the stream, looking like the Goddess of Fortune in the middle of the sea.

sanskrit: tataś cāvatatāraitām uddhartuṃ jalamadhyataḥ / ṣaḍbāhuśālipramukhān sthāpayitvā taṭe sakhīn //
english: And then he plunged in to pull her out of the water, leaving Bāhuśālin and his five other friends on the bank.

sanskrit: tāṃ ca keśeṣvapi prāptāṃ nimagnāṃ dūramambhasi / anusartuṃ striyaṃ so 'pi vīrastatraiva magnavān //
english: Then that woman, though he seized her by the hair, sank deep in the water; and he dived as deep in order to follow her.

sanskrit: nimajjya ca dadarśātra sa śrīdattaḥ kṣaḍāditi / śaivaṃ devakulaṃ divyaṃ na punarvāri na striyam // taddṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryaṃ śrānto natvā vṛṣadhvajam / udyāne sundare tatra tāṃ nināya vibhāvarīm //
english: And after he had dived a long way he suddenly saw a splendid temple of Śiva, but no water and no woman.[3] After beholding that wonderful sight, being wearied out, he paid his adorations to the god whose emblem is a bull, and spent that night in a beautiful garden attached to the temple.

sanskrit: prāptaśca devamīśānaṃ sā pūjayitumāgatā / dadṛśe tena mūrteva rūpaśrīḥ strīguṇānvitā //
english: And in the morning that lady was seen by him, having come to worship the god Śiva, like the incarnate splendour of beauty attended by all womanly perfections.

sanskrit: īśvaraṃ pūjayitvā ca sā tato nijamandiram / yayāvindumukhī so 'pi śrīdatto 'nujagāma tām //
english: And after she had worshipped the god, the moon-faced one departed to her own house, and Śrīdatta for his part followed her.

sanskrit: dadarśa mandiraṃ tacca tasyāḥ surapuropamam / praviveśa ca saṃbhrāntā sāvamāneva māninī //
english: And he saw that palace of hers resembling the city of the gods, which the haughty beauty entered hurriedly in a contemptuous manner.

sanskrit: sāpyasaṃbhāṣamāṇaiva tamantarvāsaveśmani / tanvī nyapīdat paryaṅke strīsahasropasevitā //
english: And without deigning to address him, the graceful lady sat down on a sofa in the inner part of the house, waited upon by thousands of women.

sanskrit: śrīdatto 'pi sa tatraiva niṣasāda tadantike / athākasmāt pravavṛtte tayā sādhvyā praroditum //
english: And Śrīdatta also took a seat near her. Then suddenly that virtuous lady began to weep.

sanskrit: nipetuḥ stanayos tasyāḥ saṃtaptā bāṣpabindavaḥ / śrīdattasya ca tatkālaṃ kāruṇyaṃ hṛdaye gatam //
english: The teardrops fell in an unceasing shower on her bosom, and that moment pity entered into the heart of Śrīdatta.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa caināṃ papraccha kā tvaṃ duḥkhaṃ ca kiṃ tava / vada sundari śakto 'haṃ tannivārayituṃ yataḥ // tataḥ kathaṃcit sāvādīd vayaṃ daityapater bale / pautryo daśaśataṃ tāsāṃ jyeṣṭhā vidyutprabhetyaham //
english: And then he said to her: “Who art thou, and what is thy sorrow? Tell me, fair one, for I am able to remove it.” Then she said reluctantly: “We are the thousand granddaughters of Bali,[4] the king of the Daityas, and I am the eldest of all, and my name is Vidyutprabhā.

sanskrit: sa naḥ pitāmaho nīto viṣṇunā dīrghabandhanam / pitā ca bāhuyuddhena hatastenaiva śauriṇā //
english: That grandfather of ours was carried off by Viṣṇu to long imprisonment, and the same hero slew our father in a wrestling match.

sanskrit: taṃ hatvā tena ca nijātpurānnirvāsitā vayam / praveśarodhakṛttatra siṃhaśca sthāpito 'ntare //
english: And after he had slain him he excluded us from our own city, and he placed a lion in it to prevent us from entering.[5] The lion occupies that place, and grief our hearts.

sanskrit: āvṛtaṃ tatpadaṃ tena duḥkhena hṛdayaṃ ca naḥ / sa ca yakṣaḥ kuberasya śāpāsiṃhatvamāgataḥ // martyaiścābhibhavastasya śāpāntaḥ kathitaḥ purā / purapraveśopāyārthe vijñapto viṣṇur ādiśat //
english: It is a Yakṣa that was made a lion by the curse of Kuvera, and long ago it was predicted that the Yakṣa’s curse should end when he was conquered by some mortal; so Viṣṇu deigned to inform us on our humbly asking him how we might be enabled to enter our city.

sanskrit: ataḥ sa śatrurasmākaṃ kesarī jīyatāṃ tvayā / tadarthameva cānīto mayā vīra bhavāniha //
english: Therefore subdue that lion, our enemy: it was for that reason, O hero, that I enticed you hither.

sanskrit: mṛgāṅkakākhyaṃ khaḍgaṃ ca jitāttasmādavāpsyasi / pṛthivīṃ yatprabhāveṇa jitvā rājā bhaviṣyasi // tacchrutvā sa tathetyatra śrīdatto 'tītataddinaḥ / anyedyurdaityakanyāstāḥ kṛtvāgre tatpuraṃ yayau // jigāya bāhuyuddhena tatra taṃ siṃham uddhatam / so 'pi śāpavimuktaḥ san babhūva puruṣākṛtiḥ //
english: And when you have overcome him you will obtain from him a sword named Mṛgāṅka,[6] by the virtue of which you shall conquer the world and become a king.” When he heard that, Śrīdatta agreed to undertake the adventure, and after that day had passed, on the morrow he took those Daitya maidens with him as guides, and went to that city, and there he overcame in wrestling that haughty lion.

sanskrit: dattvā cāsmai sa khaḍgaṃ svaṃ tuṣṭaḥ śāpāntakāriṇe / sahāsurāṅganāduḥkhabhāreṇādarśanaṃ yayau //
english: He being freed from his curse assumed a human form, and out of gratitude gave his sword to the man who had put an end to his curse, and then disappeared together with the burden of the sorrow' of the great Asura’s daughter.

sanskrit: so 'tha sānujayā sākaṃ śrīdatto daityakanyayā / bahirgatamivānantaṃ tadviveśa purottamam //
english: Then that Śrīdatta, together with the Daitya’s daughter, who was accompanied by her younger sisters, entered that splendid city, which looked like the serpent Ananta[7] having emerged from the earth.

sanskrit: aṅgulīyaṃ viṣaghnaṃ ca sāsmai daityasutā dadau / tataḥ so 'tra sthitastasyāṃ sābhilāṣo 'bhavadyuvā // sātha yuktyā jagādainaṃ vāpyāṃ snānamitaḥ kuru / adāyainaṃ ca majjestvaṃ khaḍgaṃ grāhabhayāpaham // tatheti vāpyāṃ magnaḥ sañ śrīdatto jāhnavītaṭāt / tasmād eva samuttasthau yasmāt pūrvam avātarat //
english: And that Daitya maiden gave him a ring that destroyed the effect of poison. [also see notes on poison detectors] Then that young man, remaining there, fell in love with her. And she cunningly said to him: “Bathe in this tank, and when you dive in take with you this sword[8] to keep off the danger of crocodiles.” He consented, and diving into the tank rose upon that very bank of the Ganges from which he first plunged in.

sanskrit: khaḍgāṅgulīyake paśyan pātālād utthito 'tha saḥ / viṣaṇṇo vismitaś cāsīd vañcito 'surakanyayā //
english: Then he, seeing the ring and the sword, felt astonishment at having emerged from the lower regions, and despondency at having been tricked by the Asura maid.

sanskrit: tatastānsuhṛdo 'nveṣṭuṃ svagṛhābhimukhaṃ yayau / gacchanniṣṭhurakākhyaṃ ca mittraṃ mārge dadarśa saḥ //
english: Then he went towards his own house to look for his friends, and as he was going he saw on the way his friend Niṣṭhuraka.

sanskrit: sa copetya praṇamyātha nītvaikānte ca satvaram / taṃ pṛṣṭasvajanodantamevaṃ niṣṭhurako 'bravīt // gaṅgāntas tvāṃ tadā magnam anviṣya divasān bahūn / svaśirāṃsi śucā chettum abhūma vayam udyatāḥ // na putrāḥ sāhasaṃ kāryaṃ jīvanneṣyati vaḥ sakhā / ity antarikṣā dvāṇī nas tam udyogaṃ nyavārayat // tataśca tvatpituḥ pārśvamasmākaṃ pratigacchatām / mārge satvaramabhyetya pumāneko 'bravīdidam // nagaraṃ na praveṣṭavyaṃ yuṣmābhiriha sāṃpratam / yato vallabhaśaktiḥ sa vipanno 'tra mahīpatiḥ //
english: Niṣṭhuraka came up to him and saluted him, and quickly took him aside into a lonely place, and when asked by him for news of his relations gave him this answer: “On that occasion when you plunged into the Ganges we searched for you for many days, and out of grief we were preparing to cut off our heads, but a voice from heaven forbade that attempt of ours, saying: ‘My sons, do no rash act, your friend shall return alive.’ And then we were returning into the presence of your father when on the way a man hurriedly advanced to meet us and said this: ‘You must not enter this city at present, for the king of it, Vallabhaśakti, is dead, and the ministers have with one accord conferred the royal dignity on Vikramaśakti.

sanskrit: śrīdattaḥ kva sa te putra iti cāmarṣanirbharaḥ / tamapṛcchatsa cāpyenaṃ nāhaṃ vedmītyabhāṣata // pracchādito 'munā putra iti tena niṣūditaḥ / kālanemiḥ sa śūlāyāṃ rājñā caura iti krudhā //
english: Now the day after he was made king he went to the house of Kālanemi and, full of wrath, asked where his son Śrīdatta was, and he replied: “I do not know.” Then the king in a rage, supposing he had concealed his son, had him put to death by impalement as a thief.

sanskrit: taddṛṣṭvā tasya bhāryāyāḥ svayaṃ hṛdayamasphuṭat / pāpaṃ pāpāntarākṣepakrūraṃ hi krūrakarmaṇām //
english: When his wife saw that, her heart broke. Men of cruel deeds must always pile one evil upon another in long succession;

sanskrit: iti tenoditāḥ puṃsā śokārtāste nijāṃ bhuvam / bāhuśālyādayaḥ pañca saṃmantryojjayinīṃ gatāḥ // pracchannaḥ sthāpitaścāhaṃ tvadarthamiha taiḥ sakhe / tadehi tāvad gacchāvas tatraiva suhṛdantikam //
english: and so Vikramaśakti is searching for Śrīdatta to slay him, and you are his friends, therefore leave this place.’ When the man had given us this warning, Bāhuśālin and his four companions, being grieved, went by common consent to their own home in Ujjayinī. And they left me here in concealment, my friend, for your sake.

sanskrit: evaṃ niṣṭhurakāc chrutvā pitarāv anuśocya saḥ / nidadhe pratikārāsthām iva khaḍge dṛśaṃ muhuḥ //
english: So come, let us go to that very place to meet our friends.” Having heard this from Niṣṭhuraka, and having bewailed his parents, Śrīdatta cast many a look at his sword, as if reposing in that his hope of vengeance;

sanskrit: kālaṃ pratīkṣamāṇo 'tha vīro niṣṭhurakānvitaḥ / pratasthe tān sakhīn prāptuṃ sa tām ujjayinīṃ purīm //
english: then the hero, biding his time, set out, accompanied by Niṣṭhuraka, for that city of Ujjayinī in order to meet his friends.

sanskrit: āmajjanāntaṃ vṛttāntaṃ sakhyus tasya ca varṇayan / śrīdattaḥ sa dadarśaikāṃ krośantīmabalāṃ pathi // abalā bhraṣṭamārgāhaṃ mālavaṃ prasthiteti tām / bruvantīṃ dayayā so 'tha sahapasthāyinīṃ vyadhāt //
english: And as he was relating to his friend his adventures from the time of his plunging into the stream, Śrīdatta beheld a woman weeping in the road; when she said, “I am a woman going to Ujjayinī and I have lost my way,” Śrīdatta out of pity made her journey along with him.

sanskrit: tayā dayānurodhācca striyā niṣṭhurakānvitaḥ / kasmiṃścicchūnyanagare dine tasminnuvāsa saḥ //
english: He and Niṣṭhuraka, together with that woman, whom he kept with him out of compassion, halted that day in a certain deserted town.

sanskrit: tatra rātrāvakasmācca muktanidro dadarśa tām / striyaṃ niṣṭhurakaṃ hatvā harṣāttanmāṃsamaśnatīm // udatiṣṭhat samākṛṣya so 'tha khaḍgaṃ mṛgāṅkakam / sāpi strī rākṣasīrūpaṃ ghoraṃ svaṃ pratyapadyata //
english: There he suddenly woke up in the night and beheld that the woman had slain Niṣṭhuraka and was devouring his flesh with the utmost delight. Then he rose up, drawing his sword Mṛgāṅka, and that woman assumed her own terrible form, that of a Rākṣasī,[9] and he seized that night-wanderer by her hair, to slay her.

sanskrit: sa ca keśeṣu jagrāha nihantuṃ tāṃ niśācarīm / tatkṣaṇaṃ divyarūpatvaṃ saṃprāptā tamuvāca sā //
english: That moment she assumed a heavenly shape and said to him: “Slay me not, mighty hero, let me go;

sanskrit: mā māṃ vadhīrmahābhāga muñca naivāsmi rākṣasī / ayamevaṃvidhaḥ śāpo mamābhūtkauśikānmuneḥ //
english: I am not a Rākṣasī; the hermit Viśvāmitra imposed this condition on me by a curse.

sanskrit: tapasyato hi tasyāhaṃ dhanādhipatināmunā / vighnāya preṣitā pūrvaṃ tatpadaprāptikāṅkṣiṇaḥ //
english: For once, when he was performing austerities from a desire to attain the position of the God of Wealth, I was sent by the god to impede him.

sanskrit: tataḥ kāntena rūpeṇa taṃ kṣobhayitumakṣamā / lajjitā trāsayantyenamakārṣaṃ bhairavaṃ vapuḥ //
english: Then finding that I was not able to seduce him with my alluring form, being abashed, I assumed, in order to terrify him, a formidable shape.

sanskrit: taddṛṣṭvā sa muniḥ śāpaṃ sadṛśaṃ mayyatho dadhe / rākṣasī bhava pāpe tvaṃ nighnantī mānuṣāniti // tvattaḥ keśagrahe prāpte śāpāntaṃ me sa cākarot / ityahaṃ rākṣasībhāvamimaṃ kaṣṭamupāgamam //
english: When he saw this, that hermit laid on me a curse suitable to my offence, exclaiming: ‘Wicked one, become a Rākṣasī and slay men.’ And he appointed my curse should end when you took hold of my hair; accordingly I assumed this detestable condition of a Rākṣasī, and I have devoured all the inhabitants of this town.

sanskrit: mayaiva nagaraṃ caitadgrastamadya ca me cirāt / tvayā kṛtaḥ sa śāpāntastadgṛhāṇādhunā varam // iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā śrīdattaḥ sādaro 'bhyadhāt / kimanyena vareṇādhya jīvatveṣa sakhā mama //
english: Now to-day, after a long time, you have brought my curse to an end in the manner foretold, therefore receive now some boon.” When he heard that speech of hers, Śrīdatta said respectfully: “Mother, grant that my friend may be restored to life.

sanskrit: evamastviti sā cāsmai varaṃ dattvā tirodhadhe / akṣatāṅgaḥ sa cottasthau jīvanniṣṭhurakaḥ punaḥ //
english: What need have I of any other boon?” “So be it,” she said, and after granting the boon disappeared. And Niṣṭhuraka rose up again alive without a scratch on his body.

sanskrit: tenaiva saha ca prātaḥ prahṛṣṭo vismitaśca saḥ / tataḥ pratasthe śrīdattaḥ prāpa cojjayinīṃ kramāt //
english: Then Śrīdatta set out the next morning with him delighted and astonished and at last reached Ujjayinī.

sanskrit: tatra saṃbhāvayāmāsa sakhīnmārgonmukhānsa tān / darśanena yathāyāto nīlakaṇṭhānivāmbudaḥ // kṛtātithyavidhiścāsau svagṛhaṃ bāhuśālinā / nīto 'bhūtkathitāśeṣanijavṛttāntakautukaḥ //
english: There he revived by his appearance the spirits of his friends, who were anxiously expecting him, as the arrival of the cloud revives the peacocks. And after he had told all the wonders of his adventures Bāhuśālin went through the usual formalities of hospitality, taking him to his own home.

sanskrit: tatropacaryamāṇaḥ san pitṛbhyāṃ bāhuśālinaḥ / sa uvāsa samaṃ mittraiḥ śrīdattaḥ svagṛhe yathā //
english: There Śrīdatta was taken care of by the parents of Bāhuśālin, and lived with his friends as comfortably as if he were in his own house.

sanskrit: kadācitso 'tha saṃprāpte madhumāsamahotsave / yātrāmupavane draṣṭuṃ jagāma sakhibhiḥ saha //
english: Once on a time, when the great feast of springtide[10] had arrived, he went with his friends to behold some festal rejoicings in a garden.

sanskrit: tatra kanyāṃ dadarśaikāṃ rājñaḥ śrībimbakeḥ sutām / āgatāmākṛtimatīṃ sākṣādiva madhuśriyam //
english: There he beheld a maiden, the daughter of King Bimbaki, who had come to see the show, looking like the Goddess of the Splendour of Spring present in bodily form.

sanskrit: sā mṛgāṅkavatī nāma hṛdayaṃ tasya tatkṣaṇam / viveśa dattamārgeva dṛṣṭyāsya savikāsayā //
english: She, by name Mṛgāṅkavatī, that moment penetrated into his heart, as if through the openings left by the expansion of his eye.

sanskrit: tasyā api muhuḥ snigdhā prathamapremaśaṃsinī / nyastā taṃ prati dūtīva dṛṣṭiścakre gatāgatam //
english: Her passionate look, too, indicative of the beginning of love, fixed on him, went and returned like a confidante.

sanskrit: praviṣṭāṃ vṛkṣagahanaṃ tāmapaśyannatha kṣaṇāt / śrīdattaḥ śūnyahṛdayo diśo 'pi na dadarśa saḥ //
english: When she entered a thicket of trees, Śrīdatta, not beholding her, suddenly felt his heart so empty that he did not know where he was.

sanskrit: jñātaṃ mayā te hṛdayaṃ sakhe māpahnavaṃ kṛthāḥ / tadehi tatra gacchāvo yatra rājasutā gatā // ityuktaśceṅgitajñena suhṛdā bāhuśālinā / tatheti sa yayau tasyāḥ saṃnikarṣaṃ suhṛtsakhaḥ //
english: His friend Bāhuśālin, who thoroughly understood the language of gestures, said to him: “My friend, I know your heart, do not deny your passion, therefore come, let us go to that part of the garden where the king’s daughter is.” He consented and went near her, accompanied by his friend.

sanskrit: hā kaṣṭamahinā daṣṭā rājaputrīti tatkṣaṇam / ākranda udabhūttatra śrīdattahṛdayajvaraḥ // viṣaghnamaṅgulīyaṃ ca vidyā ca suhṛdo 'sya me / astīti gatvā jagade kañcukī bāhuśālinā // sa ca tatkṣaṇamabhyetya kañcukī caraṇānataḥ / nikaṭaṃ rājaduhituḥ śrīdattamanayaddrutam //
english: That moment a cry was heard there which gave great pain to the heart of Śrīdatta: “Alas, the princess has been bitten by a snake!” Bāhuśālin then went and said to the chamberlain: “My friend here possesses a ring that counteracts the effects of poison, and also healing spells.” Immediately the chamberlain came and, bowing at his feet, quickly led Śrīdatta to the princess.

sanskrit: so 'pi tasyāstadaṅgulyāṃ nicikṣepāṅgulīyakam / tato jajāpa vidyāṃ ca tena pratyujjijīva sā //
english: He placed the ring on her finger and then muttered his spells, so that she revived.

sanskrit: atha sarvajane hṛṣṭe śrīdattastutitatpare / tatraiva jñātavṛttānto rājā bimbakirāyayau //
english: Then all the attendants were delighted, and loud in praise of Śrīdatta, and the King Bimbaki hearing the circumstances came to the place.

sanskrit: tenāsau sakhibhiḥ sārdhamagṛhītāṅgulīyakaḥ / pratyājagāma śrīdatto bhavanaṃ bāhuśālinaḥ //
english: Accordingly Śrīdatta returned with his friends to the house of Bāhuśālin without taking back the ring.

sanskrit: tatra tasmai suvarṇādi yatprītaḥ prāhiṇonnṛpaḥ / tadbāhuśālinaḥ pitre samagraṃ sa samarpayat //
english: And all the gold and other presents which the delighted king sent to him there he handed over to the father of Bāhuśālin.

sanskrit: atha tāṃ cintayan kāntāṃ sa tathā paryatapyata / yathā kiṃkāryatāmūḍhā vayasyas tasya jajñire //
english: Then, thinking upon that fair one, he was so much afflicted that his friends became utterly bewildered as to what to do with him.

sanskrit: tato bhāvanikā nāma rājaputryāḥ priyā sakhī / aṅgulīyārpaṇavyājāttasyāntikamupāyayau // uvāca cainaṃ matsakhyās tasyāḥ subhaga sāṃpratam / tvaṃ vā prāṇaprado bhartā mṛtyurvāpyeṣa niścayaḥ // ityukte bhāvanikayā śrīdattaḥ sa ca sāpi ca / bāhuśālī ca te 'nye ca mantraṃ saṃbhūya cakrire // harāmo nibhṛtaṃ yuktyā rājaputrīmimāṃ vayam / nivāsahetor guptaṃ ca gacchāmo mathurāmitaḥ // iti saṃmantrite samyakkāyasiddhyai ca saṃvidi / anyonyaṃ sthāpitāyāṃ sā yayau bhāvanikā tataḥ //
english: Then a dear friend of the princess, Bhāvanikā by name, came to him on pretence of returning the ring, and said to him: “That friend of mine, illustrious sir, has made up her mind that either you must save her life by becoming her husband, or she will be married to her grave.” When Bhāvanikā had said this Śrīdatta and Bāhuśālin and the others quickly put their heads together and came to the following resolution:— “We will carry off this princess secretly by a stratagem, and will go unperceived from here to Mathurā and live there.” The plan having been thoroughly talked over, and the conspirators having agreed with one another what each was to do in order to carry it out, Bhāvanikā then departed.

sanskrit: anyedyurbāhuśālī ca vayasyatritayānvitaḥ / vaṇijyāvyapadeśena jagāma mathurāṃ prati //
english: And the next day Bāhuśālin, accompanied by three of his friends, went to Mathurā on pretext of trafficking, and as he went he posted in concealment at intervals swift horses for the conveyance of the princess.

sanskrit: śrīdatto 'pi tataḥ kācmidduhitrā sahitāṃ striyam / sāyaṃ rājasutāvāse pāyayitvā madhu nyadhāt // tato 'tra dīpoddeśena dattvāgniṃ vāsaveśmani / pracchannaṃ bhāvanikayā ninye rājasutā bahiḥ //
english: But Śrīdatta then brought at eventide a woman with her daughter into the palace of the princess, after making them both drink spirits, and then Bhāvanikā, on pretence of lighting up the palace, set fire to it, and secretly conveyed the princess out of it;

sanskrit: tatkṣaṇaṃ tāṃ ca saṃprāpya śrīdattaḥ sa bahiḥ sthitaḥ / prākprasthitasya nikaṭaṃ prāhiṇodbāhuśālinaḥ // dadau mitradvayaṃ cāsyāḥ paścādbhāvanikāṃ tathā / tanmandire ca dagdhā sā kṣībā strī sutayā saha //
english: and that moment Śrīdatta, who was remaining outside, received her, and sent her on to Bāhuśālin, who had started in the morning, and directed two of his friends to attend on her and also Bhāvanikā. Now that drunken woman and her daughter were burnt in the palace of the princess, and people supposed that the princess had been burnt with her friend.

sanskrit: lokastu tāṃ sakhīyuktāṃ mene dagdhāṃ nṛpātmajām / prātaśca pūrvavattatra śrīdatto dadṛśe janaiḥ //
english: But Śrīdatta took care to show himself in the morning, as before, in the city;

sanskrit: tato rātrau dvitīyasyāṃ sa gṛhītamṛgāṅkakaḥ / śrīdattaḥ prayayau pūrvaprasthitāṃ tāṃ priyāṃ prati //
english: then on the second night, taking with him his sword Mṛgāṅka, he started to follow his beloved, who had set out before him.

sanskrit: tayā ca rātryātikramya dūramadhvānam utsukaḥ / vindhyāṭavīmatha prāpa sa prātaḥ prahare gate //
english: And in his eagerness he accomplished a great distance that night, and when the morning watch[11] had passed he reached the Vindhya forest.

sanskrit: tatrādāvanimittāni paścāt pathi dadarśa tān / sarvān prahārābhihatān sahabhāvanikān sakhīn // te ca dṛṣṭvā nijagadustaṃ saṃbhrāntamupāgatam / muṣitāḥ smo nipatyādya bahvaśvārohasenayā //
english: There he first beheld unlucky omens, and afterwards he saw all those friends of his, together with Bhāvanikā, lying in the road gashed with wounds. And when he came up all distracted they said to him: “We were robbed to-day by a large troop of horsemen that set upon us.

sanskrit: ekena cāśvāroheṇa rājaputrī bhayākulā / asmāsvetadavastheṣu nītāśvamadhiropya sā //
english: And after we were reduced to this state one of the horsemen threw the terrified princess on his horse and carried her off.

sanskrit: dūraṃ na yāvan nītā ca tāvadgacchānayā diśā / asmākamantike mā sthāḥ sarvathābhyadhikā ca sā // iti taiḥ preṣito mittrairmuhuḥ paśyanvivṛtya saḥ / javena rājatanayāṃ śrīdatto 'nusasāra tām //
english: So before she has been carried a great distance, go in this direction; do not remain near us, she is certainly of more importance than we.” Being urged on with these words by his friends, Śrīdatta rapidly followed after the princess, but could not help frequently turning round to look at them.

sanskrit: gatvā sudūraṃ lebhe ca tāmaśvārohavāhinīm / yuvānamekaṃ tanmadhye kṣatriyaṃ sa dadarśa ca //
english: And after he had gone a considerable distance he caught up that troop of cavalry, and he saw a young man of the warrior caste in the midst of it.

sanskrit: tenopari ruraṃgasya gṛhītāṃ taṃ nṛpātmajām / apaśyacca yayau cāsya kṣatrayūno 'ntikaṃ kramāt // sāntvena rājaputrīṃ tāmamuñcantaṃ ca pādataḥ / aśvādākṣipya dṛṣadi śrīdattastamacūrṇayat //
english: And he beheld that princess held by him upon his horse. So he slowly approached that young warrior; and when soft words would not induce him to let the princess go, he hurled him from his horse with a blow of his foot and dashed him to pieces on a rock.

sanskrit: taṃ hatvā ca tam evāśvam āruhya nijaghāna tān / anyān api bahūn kruddhān aśvārohān pradhāvitān //
english: And after he had slain him he mounted on his horse and slew a great number of the other horsemen who charged him in anger.

sanskrit: hataśeṣāstataste ca taddṛṣṭvā tasya tādṛśam / vīrasyāmānuṣaṃ vīryaṃ palāyya sabhayaṃ yayuḥ //
english: And then those who remained alive, seeing that the might which the hero displayed was more than human, fled away in terror;

sanskrit: sa cāpi turagārūḍho rājaputryā tayā saha / mṛgāṅkavatyā śrīdattaḥ prayayau tān sakhīn prati // stokaṃ gatvā ca tasyāśvaḥ saṃgrāme vraṇito bhṛśam / sabhāryasyāvatīrṇasya papāta prāpa pañcatām //
english: and Śrīdatta mounted on the horse with the Princess Mṛgāṅkavatī and set out to find those friends of his. And after he had gone a little way he and his wife got off the horse, which had been severely wounded in the fight, and soon after it fell down and died.

sanskrit: tatkālaṃ cāsya tatraiva sā mṛgāṅkavatī priyā / trāsāyāsapariśrāntā tṛṣārtā samapadyata //
english: And then his beloved Mṛgāṅkavatī, exhausted with fear and exertion, became very thirsty.

sanskrit: sthāpayitvā ca tāṃ tatra gatvā dūramitastataḥ / jalamanviṣyataścāsya savitāstamupāyayau //
english: And leaving her there, he roamed a long distance hither and thither, and while he was looking for water the sun set.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa labdhe 'pi jale mārganāśavaśādbhraman / cakravākavadutkūjaṃstāṃ nināya niśāṃ vane //
english: Then he discovered that though he had found water he had lost his way, and he passed that night in the wood roaming about, moaning aloud like a Cakravāka.[12] And in the morning he reached that place, which was easy to recognise by the carcase of the horse.

sanskrit: prātaḥ prāpa ca tatsthānaṃ patitāśvopalakṣitam / na ca tatra kacitkāntāṃ rājaputrīṃ dadarśa tām //
english: And nowhere there did he behold his beloved princess.
