sanskrit: tataḥ sa mohād vinyasya bhuvi khaḍgaṃ mṛgāṅkakam / vṛkṣāgramārurohaināmavekṣitumitastataḥ // tatkṣaṇaṃ tena mārgeṇa ko 'pyagācchavarādhipaḥ / sa cāgatyaiva jagrāha vṛkṣamūlānmṛgāṅkakam //
english: Then in his distraction he placed his sword Mṛgāṅka on the ground and climbed to the top of a tree, in order to cast his eye in all directions for her. That very moment a certain Śavara chieftain passed that way, and he came up and took the sword from the foot of the tree.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvāpi sa vṛkṣāgrādavatīryaiva pṛṣṭavān / priyāpravṛttimatyārtaḥ śrīdattaḥ śavarādhipam //
english: Beholding that Śavara chieftain, Śrīdatta came down from the top of the tree and in great grief asked him for news of his beloved.

sanskrit: itastvaṃ gaccha matpallīṃ jāne sā tatra te gatā / ahaṃ tatraiva caiṣyāmi dāsyāsyasimimaṃ ca te //
english: The Śavara chieftain said: “Leave this place and come to my village; I have no doubt she whom you seek has gone there;

sanskrit: ityuktvā preṣitastena śabareṇa sa cotsukaḥ / śrīdattastāṃ yayau pallīṃ tadīyaiḥ puruṣaiḥ saha // śramaṃ tāvadvimuñceti tatroktaḥ puruṣaiśca taiḥ / prāpya pallīpatergehaṃ śrānto nidrāṃ kṣaṇādyayau //
english: and I shall come there and return you this sword.” When the Śavara chieftain urged him to go with these words, Śrīdatta, being himself all eagerness, went to that village with the chief’s men. And there those men said to him: “Sleep off your fatigue.” And when he reached the house of the chief of the village, being tired, he went to sleep in an instant.

sanskrit: prabuddhaśca dadarśa svau pādau nigaḍasaṃyutau / alabdhatadgatī kāntāprāptyupāyodyamāviva //
english: And when he woke up he saw his two feet fastened with fetters, like the two efforts he had made in order to obtain his beloved, which failed to reach their object.

sanskrit: atha kṣaṇaṃ dattasukhāṃ kṣaṇāntaravimāthinīm / daivasyeva gatiṃ tatra tasthau śocansa tāṃ priyām //
english: Then he remained there weeping for his darling, who, like the course of destiny, had for a moment brought him joy, and the next moment blasted his hopes.

sanskrit: ekadā tamuvācaitya ceṭī mocanikābhidhā / āgato 'si mahābhāga kutreha bata mṛtyave //
english: One day a serving-maid of the name of Mocanikā came to him and said: “Illustrious sir, unwittingly you have come hither to your death.

sanskrit: kāryasiddhyai sa hi kāpi prayātaḥ śabarādhipaḥ / āgatya caṇḍikāyāstvāmupahārīkariṣyati // etadarthaṃ hi tena tvamito vindhyāṭavītaṭāt / prāpya yuktyā visṛjyeha nītaḥ saṃprati bandhanam //
english: For the Śavara chieftain has gone somewhither to accomplish certain weighty affairs, and when he returns he will offer you to Caṇḍikā.[13] For with that object he decoyed you here by a stratagem from this slope of the wild Vindhya hill, and immediately threw you into the chains in which you now are.

sanskrit: bhagavatyupahāratve yata evāsi kalpitaḥ / ata eva sadā vastrairbhojanaiścopacaryase //
english: And it is because you are intended to be offered as a victim to the goddess that you are continually served with garments and food.

sanskrit: ekastu muktyupāyaste vidyate yadi manyase / astyasya sundarī nāma śabarādhipateḥ sutā // atyarthaṃ sā ca dṛṣṭvā tvāṃ jāyate madanāturā / tāṃ bhajasva vayasyāṃ me tataḥ kṣemamavāpsyasi // tayetyukto vimuktyarthī sa śrīdattastatheti tām / gāndharvavidhinā guptaṃ bhāryāṃ vyadhita sundarīm //
english: But I know of only one expedient for delivering you, if you agree to it. This Śavara chieftain has a daughter named Sundarī, and she having seen you is becoming exceedingly lovesick; marry her who is my friend, then you will obtain deliverance.”[14] When she said this to him Śrīdatta consented, desiring to be set at liberty, and secretly made that Sundarī his wife by the gāndharva form of marriage.

sanskrit: rātrau rātrau ca sā tasya bandhanāni nyavārayat / acirācca sagarbhā sā sundarī samapadyata //
english: And every night she removed his chains, and in a short time Sundarī became pregnant.

sanskrit: tatsarvamatha tanmātā buddhvā mocanikāmukhāt / jāmātṛsnehato gatvā svairaṃ śrīdattamabravīt // putra śrīcaṇḍanāmāsau kopanaḥ sundarīpitā / na tvāṃ kṣameta tadgaccha vismartavyā na sundarī //
english: Then her mother, having heard the whole story from the mouth of Mocanikā, out of love for her son-in-law Śrīdatta, went and of her own accord said to him: “My son, Śrīcaṇḍa, the father of Sundarī, is a wrathful man, and will show thee no mercy;

sanskrit: ityuktvā mocitaḥ śvaśrvā khaḍgaṃ śrīcaṇḍahastagam / sundaryai nijamāvedya śrīdattaḥ prayayau tataḥ //
english: but thou must not forget Sundarī.” When his mother-in-law had said this, she set him at liberty, and Śrīdatta departed, after telling Sundarī that the sword which was in her father’s possession really belonged to himself.

sanskrit: viveśa cādyāṃ tāmeva cintākrānto nijāṭavīm / mṛgāṅkavatyāḥ padavīṃ tasya jijñāsituṃ punaḥ //
english: So he again entered, full of anxiety, that forest in which he had before wandered about, in order again to search for traces of Mṛgāṅkavatī.

sanskrit: nimittaṃ ca śubhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tamevoddeśamāyayau / yatrāsyāśvo mṛtaḥ so 'tha yatra sā hāritā vadhūḥ // tatra caikaṃ dadarśārāllubdhakaṃ saṃmukhāgatam / dṛṣṭvā ca pṛṣṭavāṃstasyāḥ pravṛttiṃ hariṇīdṛśaḥ //
english: And having seen an auspicious omen he came to that same place where that horse of his died before, and whence his wife was carried off. And there he saw near him[15] a hunter coming towards him, and when he saw him he asked him for news of that gazelle-eyed lady.

sanskrit: kiṃ śrīdattastvamityukto lubdhakena ca tatra saḥ / sa eva mandabhāgyo 'hamityuvāca viniḥśvasan // tataḥ sa lubdhako 'vādīttarhi vacmi sakhe śṛṇu / dṛṣṭā sā te mayā bhāryā krandantī tvāmitastataḥ // pṛṣṭvā tataśca vṛttāntamāśvāsya ca kṛpākulaḥ / nijāṃ pallīmito 'raṇyāddīnāṃ tāṃ nītavānaham //
english: Then the hunter asked him: “Are you Śrīdatta?” and he, sighing, replied: “I am that unfortunate man.” Then that hunter said: “Listen, friend, I have somewhat to tell you. I saw that wife of yours wandering hither and thither lamenting your absence, and having asked her her story, and consoled her, moved with compassion I took her out of this wood to my own village.

sanskrit: tatra cālokya taruṇān pulindān sabhayena sā / mathurānikaṭaṃ grāmaṃ nītā nāgasthalaṃ mayā // tatra ca sthāpitā gehe sthavirasya dvijanmanaḥ / viśvadattābhidhānasya nyāsīkṛtya sagauravam //
english: But when I saw the young Pulindas[16] there I was afraid, and I took her to a village named Nāgasthala, near Mathurā.[17] And then I placed her in the house of an old Brāhman named Viśvadatta, commending her with all due respect to his care.

sanskrit: tataś cāham ihāyāto buddhvā tvannāma tanmukhāt / tām anveṣṭuṃ tato gaccha śīghraṃ nāgasthalaṃ prati // ityukto lubdhakenāśu sa śrīdattastato yayau / taṃ ca nāgasthalaṃ prāpadaparedyurdinātyaye //
english: And thence I came here, having learnt your name from her lips. Therefore you had better go quickly to Nāgasthala to search for her.” When the hunter had told him this Śrīdatta quickly set out, and he reached Nāgasthala in the evening of the second day.

sanskrit: tacchrutvā viśvadattastaṃ śrīdattaṃ nijagāda saḥ / mathurāyāṃ suhṛnme 'sti brāhmaṇo guṇināṃ priyaḥ // upādhyāyaśca mantrī ca śūrasenasya bhūpateḥ / tasya haste tvadīyā sā gṛhiṇī sthāpitā mayā //
english: Then he entered the house of Viśvadatta and when he saw him said: “Give me my wife, who was placed here by the hunter.” Viśvadatta when he heard that answered him: “I have a friend in Mathurā, a Brāhman, dear to all virtuous men, the spiritual preceptor and minister of the King Śūrasena;

sanskrit: bhayaṃ hi vijano grāmo na tadrakṣākṣamo bhavet / tatprātastatra gaccha tvamadya viśramyatāmiha //
english: in his care I placed your wife; for this village is an out-of-the-way place and would not afford her protection.

sanskrit: ityukto viśvadattena sa nītvātraiva tāṃ niśām / prātaḥ pratasthe prāpacca mathurāmapare dine //
english: So go to that city to-morrow morning, but to-day rest here.” When Viśvadatta said this, he spent that night there, and the next morning he set off, and reached Mathurā on the second day.

sanskrit: dīrghādhvamalinastasminnagare bahireva saḥ / snānaṃ cakre pariśrānto nirmale dīrghikājale //
english: Being weary and dusty with the long journey, he bathed outside that city in the pellucid water of a lake.

sanskrit: tata evāmbumadhyācca vastraṃ cauraniveśitam / prāptavānañcalagranthibaddhahāramaśaṅkitam // atha tadvastramādāya sa taṃ hāramalakṣayan / priyāṃ didṛkṣuḥ śrīdatto viveśa mathurāṃ purīm //
english: And he drew out of the middle of the lake a garment placed there by some robbers, not suspecting any harm. But in one corner of the garment, which was knotted up, a necklace was concealed.[18] Then Śrīdatta took that garment, and in his eagerness to meet his wife did not notice the necklace, and so entered the city of Mathurā.

sanskrit: tatra tatpratyabhijñāya vastraṃ hāramavāpya ca / sa caura ityavaṣṭabhya ninye nagararakṣibhiḥ // darśitaśca tathābhūto nagarādhipateśca taiḥ / tenāpyāvedito rājñe rājāpyasyādiśadvadham // tato vadhyabhuvaṃ hantuṃ nīyamānaṃ dadarśa tam / sā mṛgāṅkavatī dūrātpaścātprahataḍiṇḍimam //
english: Then the city police recognised the garment, and finding the necklace, arrested Śrīdatta as a thief, and carried him off, and brought him before the chief magistrate exactly as he was found with the garment in his possession; by him he was handed up to the king, and the king ordered him to be put to death.[19] Then as he was being led off to the place of execution, with the drum being beaten behind him,[20] his wife Mṛgāṅkavatī saw him in the distance.

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ me nīyate bhartā vadhāyeti sasaṃbhramam / sā gatvā mantrimukhyaṃ tamabravīdyadgṛhe sthitā // nivārya vadhakānso 'tha mantrī vijñapya bhūpatim / śrīdattaṃ mocayitvā taṃ vadhādānāyayadgṛham //
english: She went in a state of the utmost distraction and said to the chief minister, in whose house she was residing: “Yonder is my husband being led off to execution.” Then that minister went and ordered the executioners to desist, and by making a representation to the king got Śrīdatta pardoned, and had him brought to his house.

sanskrit: kathaṃ so 'yaṃ pitṛvyo me gatvā deśāntaraṃ purā / ihaiva daivādvigatabhayaḥ prāpto 'dya mantritām // iti taṃ mantriṇaṃ so 'tha śrīdattas tadgṛhāgataḥ / pratyabhijñātavān pṛṣṭvā papātāsya ca pādayoḥ // so 'pi taṃ pratyabhijñāya bhrātuḥ putraṃ savismayaḥ / kaṇṭhe jagrāha sarvaṃ ca vṛttāntaṃ paripṛṣṭavān //
english: And when Śrīdatta reached his house, and saw that minister, he recognised him and fell at his feet, exclaiming: “What! is this my uncle Vigatabhaya, who long ago went to a foreign country, and do I now by good luck find him established in the position of a minister?” He too recognised, to his astonishment, Śrīdatta as his brother’s son, and embraced him, and questioned him about all his adventures.

sanskrit: tatastasmai sa nikhilaṃ śrīdattaḥ svapiturvadhāt / ārabhya nijavṛttāntaṃ pitṛvyāya nyavedayat //
english: Then Śrīdatta related to his uncle his whole history, beginning with the execution of his father.

sanskrit: so 'pi muktvāśru vijane bhrātuḥ putraṃ tamabhyadhāt / adhṛtiṃ mā kṛthāḥ putra mama siddhā hi yakṣiṇī //
english: And he, after weeping, said to his nephew in private: “Do not despond, my son, for I once brought a female Yakṣa into subjection by means of magic;

sanskrit: pañca vājisahasrāṇi hemakoṭīśca sapta sā / prādānmahyamaputrāya tattavaivākhilaṃ dhanam //
english: and she gave me, though I have no son, five thousand horses and seventy millions of gold pieces;

sanskrit: ityuktvā sa pitṛvyastāṃ śrīdattāyārpayatpriyām / śrīdatto 'pyāttavibhavastatra tāṃ pariṇītavān //
english: and all that wealth is at your disposal.” After telling him this, his uncle brought him his beloved, and he, having obtained wealth, married her on the spot.

sanskrit: tataśca tasthau tatraiva saṃgataḥ kāntayā tayā / mṛgāṅgavatyā sānando rātryeva kumudākaraḥ //
english: And then he remained there in joy, united with that beloved Mṛgāṅkavatī as a bed of white lotuses[21] with the night.

sanskrit: bāhuśālyādicintā tu tasyābhūtpūrṇasaṃpadaḥ / indoḥ kalaṅkalekheva hṛdi mālinyadāyinī //
english: But even when his happiness was at its full, anxiety for Bāhuśālin and his companions clouded his heart, as a spot of darkness does the full moon.

sanskrit: ekadā sa pitṛvyastaṃ rahaḥ śrīdattamabhyadhāt / putra rājñaḥ sutāstyasya śūrasenasya kanyakā // mayā cāvantideśe sā neyā dātuṃ tadājñayā / tattenaivāpadeśena hṛtvā tubhyaṃ dadāmi tām //
english: Now one day his uncle said secretly to Śrīdatta: “My son, the King Śūrasena has a maiden daughter, and in accordance with his orders I have to take her to the land of Avanti to give her away in marriage; so I will take her away on that very pretext, and marry her to you.

sanskrit: tatastadanuge prāpte bale sati ca māmake / yadrājyaṃ te śriyādiṣṭaṃ tatprāpsyasyacirāditi // niścityaitacca tāṃ kanyāṃ gṛhītvā yayatustataḥ / śrīdattastatpitṛvyaśca sasainyau saparigrahau //
english: Then, when you have got possession of the force that follows her, with mine already at your disposal, you will soon gain the kingdom that was promised you by the goddess Srī.” Having resolved on this, and having taken that maiden, Śrīdatta and his uncle set out with their army and their attendants.

sanskrit: tato vindhyāṭavīm etau prāptamātrāvatarkitau / caurasenātimahatī rurodha śaravarṣiṇī //
english: But as soon as they had reached the Vindhya forest, before they were aware of the danger, a large army of brigands set upon them showering arrows.

sanskrit: prahāramūrcchitaṃ baddhvā śrīdattaṃ bhagnasainikam / ninyuścaurāḥ svapallīṃ te svīkṛtya sakalaṃ dhanam //
english: After routing Śrīdatta’s force and seizing all the wealth, they bound Śrīdatta himself, who had fainted from his wounds, and carried him off to their village.

sanskrit: te ca taṃ prāpayāmāsuścaṇḍikāsadma bhīṣaṇam / upahārāya ghaṇṭānāṃ nādairmṛtyurivāhvayat //
english: And they took him to the awful temple of Durgā, in order to offer him up in sacrifice, and, as it were, summoned Death with the sound of their gongs.

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyacca taṃ patnī sā pallīpatiputrikā / sundarī draṣṭumāyātā devīṃ bālasutānvitā //
english: There Sundarī saw him, one of his wives, the daughter of the chief of the village, who had come with her young son to visit the shrine of the goddess.

sanskrit: niṣiddhavatyā madhyasthāndasyūnānandapūrṇayā / sa śrīdattastayā sākaṃ tanmandiramathāviśat //
english: Full of joy she ordered the brigands who were between her and her husband to stand aside, and then Śrīdatta entered her palace with her.

sanskrit: tadaiva pallīrājyaṃ tat prāpa pitrā yad arpitam / prāg evānanyaputreṇa sundaryai gacchatā divam //
english: Immediately Śrīdatta obtained the sovereignty of that village, which Sundarī’s father, having no son, bequeathed to her when he went to heaven.

sanskrit: taṃ ca caurasamākrāntaṃ sapitṛvyaparicchadam / sakalatraṃ ca lebhe 'sau taṃ khaḍgaṃ ca mṛgāṅkakam //
english: So Śrīdatta recovered his wife and his sword Mṛgāṅka, and also his uncle and his followers, who had been overpowered by the robbers.

sanskrit: taraiva śūrasenasya sutāṃ tāṃ pariṇīya ca / śrīdatto 'pi mahānrājā nagare samapadyata //
english: And while he was in that town he married the daughter of Śūrasena, and became a great king there.

sanskrit: prajighāya sa dūtāṃśca tataḥ śvaśurayostayoḥ / bimbakestasya tasyāpi śūrasenasya bhūpateḥ // tamupājagmatustau ca senāsamudayānvitau / taṃ vijñāyaiva saṃbandhaṃ mudā duhitṛvatsalau // te 'pi rūḍhavraṇāḥ svasthāstadviyuktā vayasyakāḥ / bāhuśāliprabhṛtayastadbuddhvā tamupāyayuḥ //
english: And from that place he sent ambassadors to his two fathers-in-law, to Bimbaki and King Śūrasena. And they, being very fond of their daughters, gladly recognised him as a connection, and came to him accompanied by the whole of their armies. And his friends Bāhuśālin and the others, who had been separated from him, when they heard what had happened, came to him with their wounds healed and in good health.

sanskrit: atha śvaśurasaṃyukto gatvā taṃ pitṛghātinam / cakre vikramaśaktiṃ sa vīraḥ krodhānalāhutim //
english: Then the hero marched, united with his fathers-in-law, and made that Vikramaśakti, who had put his father to death, a burnt-offering in the flame of his wrath.

sanskrit: tataśca sābdhivalayāṃ śrīdattaḥ prāpya medinīm / nananda virahottīrṇaḥ sa mṛgāṅkavatīsakhaḥ //
english: And then Śrīdatta, having gained dominion over the sea-encircled earth, and deliverance from the sorrow’ of separation, joyed in the society of Mṛgāṅkavatī.

sanskrit: itthaṃ narapate dīrghaviyogavyasanārṇavam / taranti ca labhante ca kalyāṇaṃ dhīracetasaḥ //
english: Even so, my king, do men of firm resolution cross the calamitous sea of separation and obtain prosperity.

sanskrit: iti saṃgatakācchrutvā kathāṃ sa dayitotsukaḥ / tāṃ nināya niśāṃ mārge sahasrānīkabhūpatiḥ // tato manorathārūḍhaḥ puraḥ prahitamānasaḥ / prātaḥ sahasrānīko 'sau pratasthe svāṃ priyāṃ prati //
english: [M] (Main story line continued) After hearing this tale from Saṃgataka, the King Sahasrānīka, though longing for the sight of his beloved one, managed to get through that night on the journey. Then, engrossed with his desire, sending his thoughts on before, in the morning Sahasrānīka set out to meet his darling.

sanskrit: dinaiḥ katipayaistaṃ ca jamadagneravāpa saḥ / mṛgairapi parityaktacāpalaṃ śānamāśramam //
english: And in a few' days he reached that peaceful hermitage of Jamadagni, in which even the deer laid aside their wantonness.

sanskrit: dadarśa kalpitātithyaṃ jamadagniṃ ca tatra tam / praṇataḥ pāvanālokamākāraṃ tapasāmiva //
english: And there he beheld with reverence that Jamadagni, the sight of whom was sanctifying, like the incarnate form of penance, who received him hospitably.

sanskrit: sa ca tasmai munī rājñe saputrāṃ tāṃ samarpayat / cirānmṛgāvatīṃ rājñīṃ sānandāmiva nirvṛtim //
english: And the hermit handed over to him that Queen Mṛgāvatī with her son, regained by the king after long separation, like tranquillity with joy.

sanskrit: śāpānte tac ca daṃpatyostayor anyonyadarśanam / ānandabāṣpapūrṇāyāṃ vavarṣevāmṛtaṃ dṛśi //
english: And that sight which the husband and wife obtained of one another, now that the curse had ceased, rained, as it were, nectar into their eyes, which were filled with tears of joy.

sanskrit: tatpūrvadarśanaṃ putramāliṅgyodayanaṃ sa tam / mumoca nṛpatiḥ kṛcchrādromāñceneva kīlitam // tataḥ sodayanāṃ rājñīṃ tāmādāya mṛgāvatīm / ā tapovanamudvāṣpairanuyāto mṛgairapi // āmantrya jamadagniṃ ca pratasthe svāṃ purīṃ prati / praśāntādāśramāttasmātsahasrānīkabhūpatiḥ //
english: And the king embracing that son Udayana, whom he now beheld for the first time, could with difficulty let him go, as he was, so to speak, riveted to his body with his own hairs that stood erect from joy.[22] Then King Sahasrānīka took his Queen Mṛgāvatī with Udayana, and, bidding adieu to Jamadagni, set out from that tranquil hermitage for his own city, and even the deer followed him as far as the border of the hermitage with tearful eyes.

sanskrit: śṛṇvan virahavṛttāni priyāyā varṇayaṃś ca saḥ / uttoraṇapatākāṃ tāṃ kauśāmbīṃ prāptavān kramāt //
english: Beguiling the way by listening to the adventures of his beloved wife during the period of separation, and by relating his own, he at length reached the city of Kauśāmbī, in which triumphal arches were erected and banners displayed.

sanskrit: samaṃ ca patnīputrābhyāṃ praviveśa sa tāṃ purīm / pīyamāna ivotpakṣmarājibhiḥ pauralocanaiḥ //
english: And he entered that city in company with his wife and child, being, so to speak, devoured[23] by the eyes of the citizens, that had the fringe of their lashes elevated.

sanskrit: abhyaṣiñcacca taṃ tatra jhagityudayanaṃ sutam / yauvarājye mahārājaḥ preryamāṇaḥ sa tadguṇaiḥ //
english: And immediately the king appointed his son Udayana crown prince, being incited to it by his excellent qualities.

sanskrit: svamantriputrāṃs tasmai sa mantrahetoḥ samarpayat / vasantakarumaṇvantau tathā yaugandharāyaṇam //
english: And he assigned to him as advisers the sons of his own ministers, Vasantaka and Rumaṇvat and Yaugandharāyaṇa.

sanskrit: ebhirmantrivaraireṣa kṛtsnāṃ prāpsyati medinīm / iti vāgudabhūddivyā puṣpavṛṣṭyā samaṃ tadā // tataḥ sute nyastabharaḥ sa rājā cirakāṅkṣitam / jīvalokasukhaṃ bheje mṛgāvatyā tayā saha //
english: Then a rain of flowers fell, and a celestial voice was heard: “By the help of these excellent ministers, the prince shall obtain dominion over the whole earth.” Then the king devolved on his son the cares of empire, and enjoyed in the society of Mṛgāvatī the long-desired pleasures of the world.

sanskrit: atha tasya jarāṃ praśāntidūtīm upayātāṃ kṣitipasya karṇamūlam / sahasaiva vilokya jātakopā bata dūre viṣayaspṛhā babhūva //
english: At last the desire of earthly enjoyment, beholding suddenly that old age, the harbinger of composure, had reached the root of the king’s ear,[24] became enraged and fled far from him.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ kalyāṇaṃ tanayam anuraktaprakṛtikaṃ niveśya sve rājye jagadudayahetor udayanam / sahasrānīko 'sau sacivasahitaḥ sapriyatamo mahāprasthānāya kṣitipatir agacchad dhimagirim //
english: Then that King Sahasrānīka established in his throne his excellent son Udayana,[25] whom the subjects loved so well, to ensure the world’s prosperity, and, accompanied by his ministers and his beloved wife, ascended the Himālaya to prepare for the last great journey.

sanskrit: iti mahākaviśrīsomadevabhaṭṭaviracite kathāsaritsāgare kathāmukhalambake dvitīyas taraṅgaḥ / tṛtīyas taraṅgaḥ / tataḥ sa vatsarājyaṃ ca prāpya pitrā samarpitam / kauśāmbyavasthitaḥ samyakchaśāsodayanaḥ prajāḥ //
english: [M] (Main story line continued) THEN Udayana took the kingdom of Vatsa, which his father had bequeathed to him, and, establishing himself in Kauśāmbī, ruled his subjects well.

sanskrit: yaugandharāyaṇādyeṣu bharaṃ vinyasya mantriṣu / babhūva sa śanai rājā sukheṣvekāntatatparaḥ //
english: But gradually he began to devolve the cares of empire upon his ministers, Yaugandharāyaṇa and others, and gave himself up entirely to pleasures.

sanskrit: sadā siṣeve mṛgayāṃ vīṇāṃ ghoṣavatīṃ ca tām / dattāṃ vāsukinā pūrvaṃ naktaṃdinamavādayat //
english: He was continually engaged in the chase, and day and night he played on the melodious lute which Vāsuki[1] gave him long ago;

sanskrit: tattantrīkalanirhrādamohamantravaśīkṛtān / anināya ca saṃyamya sadā mattān vanadvipān // sa vāranārīvaktrendupratimālamkṛtāṃ surām / mantriṇāṃ ca mukhacchāyāṃ vatsarājaḥ samaṃ papau //
english: and he subdued evermore infuriated wild elephants, overpowered by the fascinating spell of its strings’ dulcet sound, and, taming them, brought them home.[2] That King of Vatsa drank wine adorned by the reflection of the moon-faces of fair women, and at the same time robbed his ministers’ faces of their cheerful hue.[3] Only one anxiety had he to bear;

sanskrit: kularūpānurūpā me bhāryā kvāpi na vidyate / ekā vāsavadattākhyā kanyakā śrūyate param // kathaṃ prāpyeta sā ceti cintāmekāmuvāha saḥ / so 'pi caṇḍamahāsena ujjayinyām acintayat // tulyo madduhiturbhartā jagatyasminna vidyate / asti codayano nāma vipakṣaḥ sa ca me sadā //
english: he kept thinking: “Nowhere is a wife found equal to me in birth and personal appearance; the maiden named Vāsavadattā alone has a liking for me,[4] but how is she to be obtained?” Caṇḍamahāsena also, in Ujjayinī, thought: “There is no suitable husband to be found for my daughter in the world, except one Udayana by name, and he has ever been my enemy.

sanskrit: tatkathaṃ nāma jāmātā vaśyaśca niyataṃ bhavet / upāyas tv eka evāsti yad aṭavyāṃ bhramaty asau //
english: Then how can I make him my son-in-law and my submissive ally? There is only one device which can effect it.

sanskrit: ekākī dviradān badhnan mṛgayāvyasanī nṛpaḥ / tena cchidreṇa taṃ yuktyāvaṣṭabhyānāyayāmy aham //
english: He wanders about alone in the forest capturing elephants, for he is a king addicted to the vice of hunting; I will make use of this failing of his to entrap him and bring him here by a stratagem;

sanskrit: gāndharvajñasya tasyaitāṃ sutāṃ śiṣyīkaromi ca / tataś cāsyāṃ svayaṃ tasya cakṣuḥ snihyed asaṃśayam // evaṃ sa mama jāmātā vaśyaś ca niyataṃ bhavet / nānyo 'styupāyaḥ ko 'pyatra yena vaśyo bhavecca saḥ // iti saṃcintya tatsiddhyai sa gatvā caṇḍikāgṛham / caṇḍīmabhyarcya tuṣṭāva cakre 'syā upayācitam //
english: and, as he is acquainted with music, I will make this daughter of mine his pupil, and then his eye will without doubt be charmed with her, and he will certainly become my son-in-law, and my obedient ally. No other artifice seems applicable in this case for making him submissive to my will.” Having thus reflected, he went to the temple of Durgā, in order that his scheme might be blessed with success, and, after worship and praise, offered a prayer to the goddess.

sanskrit: etatsaṃpatsyate rājannacirādvāñchitaṃ tava / iti śuśrāva tatrāsāvaśarīrāṃ sarasvatīm // tatastuṣṭaḥ samāgatya buddhadattena mantriṇā / saha caṇḍamahāsenastamevārthamacintayat // mānoddhato vītalobho raktabhṛtyo mahābalaḥ / asādhyo 'pi sa sāmādeḥ sāmnā tāvannirūpyatām // iti saṃmantrya sa nṛpo dūtamekaṃ samādiśat / gaccha madvacanādbrūhi vatsarājamidaṃ vacaḥ // matputrī tava gāndharve śiṣyā bhavitumicchati / snehas te 'smāsu cettatvaṃ tām ihaivaitya śikṣaya //
english: And there he heard a bodiless voice saying: “This desire of thine, O king, shall shortly be accomplished.” Then he returned satisfied, and deliberated over that very matter with the minister Buddhadatta,[5] saying: “That prince is elated with pride, he is free from avarice, his subjects are attached to him, and he is of great power, therefore he cannot be reached by any of the four usual expedients beginning with negotiation, nevertheless let negotiation be tried first.”[6] Having thus deliberated, the king gave this order to an ambassador: “Go and give the King of Vatsa this message from me: ‘My daughter desires to be thy pupil in music;

sanskrit: ityuktvā preṣitastena dūto gatvā nyavedayat / kauśāmbyāṃ vatsarājāya saṃdeśaṃ taṃ tathaiva saḥ //
english: if thou love us, come here and teach her.’” When sent off by the king with this message, the ambassador went and repeated it to the King of Vatsa in Kauśāmbī exactly as it was delivered;

sanskrit: vatsarājo 'pi tacchrutvā dūtādanucitaṃ vacaḥ / yaugandharāyaṇasyedamekānte mantriṇo 'bravīt // kimetattena saṃdiṣṭaṃ sadarpaṃ mama bhūbhujā / evaṃ saṃdiśatastasya ko 'bhiprāyo durātmanaḥ // ityukto vatsarājena tadā yaugandharāyaṇaḥ / uvācainaṃ mahāmantrīṃ sa svāmihitaniṣṭhuraḥ // bhuvi vyasanitākhyātiḥ prarūḍhā te lateva yā / idaṃ tasyā mahārāja kaṣāyakaṭukaṃ phalam //
english: and the King of Vatsa, after hearing this uncourteous message from the ambassador, repeated it in private to the minister Yaugandharāyaṇa, saying: “Why did that monarch send me that insolent message? What can be the villain’s object in making such a proposal?” When the king asked him this question, the great minister Yaugandharāyaṇa, who was stern to his master for his good, thus answered him: “Your reputation for vice[7] has shot up in the earth like a creeper, and this, O king, is its biting bitter fruit.

sanskrit: sa hi tvāṃ rāgiṇaṃ matvā kanyāratnena lobhayan / nītvā caṇḍamahāseno baddhvā svīkartumicchati //
english: For that King Caṇḍamahāsena, thinking that you are the slave of your passions, intends to ensnare you by means of his beautiful daughter, throw you into prison, and so make you his unresisting instrument.

sanskrit: ity ukto mantriṇā dhīraḥ pratidūtaṃ vyasarjayat / sa vatsarājas taṃ caṇḍamahāsenanṛpaṃ prati // saṃdideśa ca yadyasti vāñchā macchiṣyatāṃ prati / tvatputryāstadihaivaiṣā bhavatā preṣyatāmiti // evaṃ kṛtvā ca sacivānvatsarājo jagāda saḥ / yāmi caṇḍamahāsenamiha baddhvānayāmi tam // tac chrutvā tam uvācāgryo mantrī yaugandharāyaṇaḥ / na caitac chakyate rājan kartuṃ naiva ca yujyate //
english: Therefore abandon kingly vices, for kings that fall into them are easily captured by their enemies, even as elephants are taken in pits.” When his minister had said this to him, the resolute King of Vatsa sent in return an ambassador to Caṇḍamahāsena with the following reply: — “If thy daughter desires to become my pupil, then send her here.” When he had sent this reply, that King of Vatsa said to his ministers: “I will march and bring Caṇḍamahāsena here in chains.” When he heard that, the head minister Yaugandharāyaṇa said: “That is not a fitting thing to do, my king, nor is it in thy power to do it.

sanskrit: sa hi prabhāvavānrājā svīkāryaśca tava prabho / tathā ca tadgataṃ sarvaṃ śṛṇvidaṃ kathayāmi te // astīhojjayinī nāma nagarī bhūṣaṇaṃ bhuvaḥ / hasantīva sudhādhautaiḥ pāsādairamarāvatīm //
english: And in proof of this hear his whole history, which I now proceed to relate to thee: There is in this land a city named Ujjayinī, the ornament of the earth, that, so to speak, laughs to scorn with its palaces of enamelled whiteness[8] Amarāvatī, the city of the gods.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ vasati viśveśo mahākālavapuḥ svayam / śithilīkṛtakailāsanivāsavyasano haraḥ //
english: In that city dwells Śiva himself, the lord of existence, under the form of Mahākāla,[9] when he desists from the kingly vice of absenting himself on the heights of Mount Kailāsa.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ mahendravarmākhyo rājābhūdbhūbhṛtāṃ varaḥ / jayasenābhidhāno 'sya babhūva sadṛśaḥ sutaḥ //
english: In that city lived a king named Mahendravarman, best of monarchs, and he had a son like himself, named Jayasena.

sanskrit: jayasenasya tasyātha putro 'pratimadorbalaḥ / samutpanno mahāsenanāmā nṛpatikuñjaraḥ //
english: Then to that Jayasena was born a son named Mahāsena, matchless in strength of arm, an elephant among monarchs.

sanskrit: so 'tha rājā svarājyaṃ tat pālayan samacintayat / na me khaḍgo 'nurūpo 'sti na ca bhāryā kulodgatā // iti saṃcintya sa nṛpaścaṇḍikāgṛhamāgamat / tatrautiṣṭhannirāhāro devīmārādhayaṃściram //
english: And that king, while cherishing his realm, reflected: “I have not a sword worthy of me,[10] nor a wife of good family.” Thus reflecting, that monarch went to the temple of Durgā, and there he remained without food, propitiating for a long time the goddess.

sanskrit: utkṛtyātha svamāṃsāni homakarma sa cākarot / tataḥ prasannā sākṣātsa devī caṇḍī tamabhyadhāt //
english: Then he cut off pieces of his own flesh and offered a burnt-offering with them, whereupon the goddess Durgā, being pleased, appeared in visible shape and said to him: “I am pleased with thee;

sanskrit: prītāsmi te gṛhāṇemaṃ putra khaḍgottamaṃ mama / etatprabhāvāc chatrūṇām ajeyas tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi //
english: receive from me this excellent sword; by means of its magic power thou shalt be invincible to all thy enemies.

sanskrit: kiṃ cāṅgāravatīṃ nāma kanyāṃ trailokyasundarīm / aṅgārakāsurasutāṃ śīghraṃ bhāryāmavāpsyasi //
english: Moreover, thou shalt soon obtain as a wife Aṅgāravatī, the daughter of the Asura Aṅgāraka, the most beautiful maiden in the three worlds.

sanskrit: atīva caṇḍaṃ karmeha kṛtaṃ caitadyatastvayā / ataścaṇḍamahāsena ityākhyā te bhaviṣyati // ityuktvā dattakhaḍgā sā devī tasya tiro 'bhavat / rājñaḥ saṃkalpasaṃpattihṛṣṭirāvirabhūtpunaḥ //
english: And since thou didst here perform this very cruel penance, therefore thy name shall be Caṇḍamahāsena.” Having said this and given him the sword, the goddess disappeared. But in the king there appeared joy at the fulfilment of his desire.

sanskrit: sa khaḍgo mattahastīndro naḍāgiririti prabho / dve tasya ratne śakrasya kuliśairāvaṇāviva //
english: He now possessed, O king, two jewels, his sword and a furious elephant named Naḍāgiri, which were to him what the thunderbolt and Airāvata are to Indra.

sanskrit: tayoḥ prabhāvātsukhitaḥ kadācitso 'tha bhūpatiḥ / agāccaṇḍamahāseno mṛgayāyai mahāṭavīm //
english: Then that king, delighting in the power of these two, one day went to a great forest to hunt;

sanskrit: atipramāṇaṃ tatraikaṃ varāhaṃ ghoramaikṣata / naiśaṃ tama ivākāṇḍe divā piṇḍatvamāgatam //
english: and there he beheld an enormous and terrible wild boar; like the darkness of the night suddenly condensed into a solid mass in the daytime.

sanskrit: sa varāhaḥ śarairasya tīkṣṇairapyakṛtavraṇaḥ / āhatya syandanaṃ rājñaḥ palāyya bilamāviśat // rājāpi ratham utsṛjya tam evānusaran krudhā / dhanur dvitīyas tatraiva prāviśat sa bilāntaram //
english: That boar was not wounded by the king’s arrows, in spite of their sharpness, but after breaking the king’s chariot[11] fled and entered a cavern. The king, leaving that car of his, in revengeful pursuit of the boar, entered into that cavern with only his bow to aid him.

sanskrit: dūraṃ praviśya cāpaśyatkāntaṃ puravaraṃ mahat / savismayo nyaṣīdacca tadantardīrghikātaṭe //
english: And after he had gone a long distance he beheld a great and splendid capital, and astonished he sat down inside the city on the bank of a lake.

sanskrit: tatrasthaḥ kanyakāmekāmapaśyatstrīśatānvitām / saṃcarantīṃ smarasyeva dhairyanirbhedinīmiṣum //
english: While there he beheld a maiden moving along, surrounded by hundreds of women, like the arrow of love that cleaves the armour of self-restraint.

sanskrit: sāpi premarasāsāravarṣiṇā cakṣuṣā muhuḥ / snapayantīva rājānaṃ śanakaistamupāgamat // kastvaṃ subhaga kasmācca praviṣṭo 'sīha sāṃpratam / ityuktaḥ sa tayā rājā yathātattvamavarṇayat //
english: She slowly approached the king, bathing him, so to speak, again and again in a look that rained in showers the nectar of love.[12] She said: “Who art thou, illustrious sir, and for what reason hast thou entered our home on this occasion?” The king, being thus questioned by her, told her the whole truth;

sanskrit: tacchrutvā netrayugalātsarāgādaśrusaṃtatim / hṛdayāddhīratāṃ cāpi samaṃ kanyā mumoca sā //
english: hearing which, she let fall from her eyes a passionate flood of tears, and from her heart all self-control.

sanskrit: kā tvaṃ rodiṣi kasmācca pṛṣṭā teneti bhūbhṛtā / sā taṃ pratyabravīdevaṃ manmahājñānuvartinī // yo varāhaḥ praviṣṭo 'tra sa daityo 'ṅgārakābhidhaḥ / ahaṃ caitasya tanayā nāmnāṅgāravatī nṛpa //
english: The king said: “Who art thou, and why dost thou weep?” When he asked her this question she, being a prisoner to love at his will, answered him: “The boar that entered here is the Daitya Aṅgāraka by name. And I am his daughter, O king, and my name is Aṅgāravatī.

sanskrit: vajrasāramayaś cāsau rājaputrīr imāḥ śatam / ācchidya rājñāṃ gehebhyaḥ parivāraṃ vyadhān mama //
english: And he is of adamantine frame, and has carried off these hundred princesses from the palaces of kings and appointed them to attend on me.

sanskrit: kiṃ caiṣa rākṣasībhūtaḥ śāpadoṣānmahāsuraḥ / tṛṣṇāśramārtaś cādya tvāṃ prāpyāpi tyaktavānayam //
english: Moreover, this great Asura has become a Rākṣasa owing to a curse, but to-day, as he was exhausted with thirst and fatigue, even when he found you, he spared you.

sanskrit: idānīṃ cāstavārāharūpo viśrāmyati svayam / suptotthitaśca niyataṃ tvayi pāpaṃ samācaret //
english: At present he has put off the form of a boar and is resting in his proper shape, but when he wakes up from his sleep he will without fail do you an injury.

sanskrit: iti me tava kalyāṇamapaśyantyā galantyamī / saṃtāpakvathitāḥ prāṇā iva bāṣpāmbubindavaḥ // ityaṅgāravatīvākyaṃ śrutvā rājā jagāda tām / yadi mayyasti te snehastadidaṃ madvacaḥ kuru //
english: It is for this reason that I see no hope of a happy issue for you, and so these teardrops fall from my eyes like my vital spirits boiled with the fire of grief.” When he heard this speech of Aṅgāravatī’s the king said to her: “If you love me, do this which I ask you.

sanskrit: prabuddhasyāsya gatvā tvaṃ rudihi svapituḥ puraḥ / tataśca niyataṃ sa tvāṃ pṛcchedudvegakāraṇam //
english: When your father awakes, go and weep in front of him, and then he will certainly ask you the cause of your agitation;

sanskrit: tvāṃ cennipātayetkaścittato me kā gatirbhavet / etadduḥkhaṃ mametyevaṃ sa ca vācyastvayā tataḥ // evaṃ kṛte 'sti kalyāṇaṃ tavāpi ca mamāpi ca / ityuktā tena sā rājñā tathetyaṅgīcakāra tam //
english: then you must say: ‘If someone were to slay thee, what would become of me?[13] This is the cause of my grief.’ If you do this there will be a happy issue both for you and me.” When the king said this to her she promised him that she would do what he wished.

sanskrit: taṃ ca cchannamavasthāpya rājānaṃ pāpaśaṅkinī / agādasurakanyā sa prasuptasyāntikaṃ pituḥ //
english: And that Asura maiden, apprehending misfortune, placed the king in concealment and went near her sleeping father.

sanskrit: so 'pi daiyaḥ prabubudhe prārebhe sā ca roditum / kiṃ putri rodiṣītyevaṃ sa ca tāmabravīttataḥ // hanyāttvāṃ ko'pi cettāta tadā me kā gatirbhavet / ityārtyā tamavāditsā sa vihasya tato 'bravīt // ko māṃ vyāpādayetputri sarvo vajramayo hyaham / vāmahaste 'sti me chidraṃ tacca cāpena rakṣyate //
english: Then the Daitya woke up, and she began to weep. And then he said to her: “Why do you weep, my daughter?” She, with affected grief, said to him: “If someone were to slay thee, what would become of me?” Then he burst out laughing and said: “Who could possibly slay me, my daughter?—for I am cased in adamant all over;

sanskrit: itthamāśvāsayāmāsa sa daityastāṃ nijāṃ sutām / etacca nikhilaṃ tena rājñā channena śuśruve //
english: only in my left hand is there an unguarded place, but that is protected by the bow.” In these words the Daitya consoled his daughter, and all this was heard by the king in his concealment.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṣaṇādivotthāya kṛtvā snānaṃ sa dānavaḥ / kṛtamaunaḥ pravavṛtte devaṃ pūjayituṃ haram //
english: Immediately afterwards the Dānava rose up and took his bath, and proceeded in devout silence to worship the god Śiva.

sanskrit: tatkālaṃ prakaṭībhūya sa rājākṛṣṭakārmukaḥ / upetya prasabhaṃ daityaṃ raṇāyāhvayate sma tam //
english: At that moment the king appeared with his bow bent, and rushing up impetuously towards the Daitya, challenged him to fight.

sanskrit: rājāpi laghuhastatvātkare tatraiva tatkṣaṇam / tasminmarmaṇi taṃ daityaṃ pṛṣatkena jaghāna saḥ //
english: The king for his part, being very quick, immediately smote him with an arrow in that hand which was his vital part.

sanskrit: sa ca marmāhato ghoraṃ rāvaṃ kṛtvā mahāsuraḥ / aṅgārako 'patadbhūmau niryajjīvo jagāda ca // tṛṣito 'haṃ hato yena sa māmadbhirna tarpayet / pratyabdaṃ yadi tattasya naśyeyuḥ pañca mantriṇaḥ // ityuktvā pañcatāṃ prāpa sa daityaḥ so 'pi tatsutām / tāmaṅgāravatīṃ rājā gṛhītvojjayinīṃ yayau //
english: And that great Asura Aṅgāraka, being pierced in the vital spot, immediately uttered a terrible cry and fell on the ground, and exclaimed, as his life departed: “If that man who has slain me when thirsty does not offer water to my manes every year, then his five ministers shall perish.” After he had said this that Daitya died, and the king, taking his daughter Aṅgāravatī as a prize, returned to Ujjayinī.

sanskrit: pariṇītavatastasya tatra tāṃ daityakanyakām / jātau dvau tanayau caṇḍamahāsenasya bhūpateḥ // eko gopālako nāma dvitīyaḥ pālakastathā / tayorindrotsavaṃ cāsau jātayorakaronnṛpaḥ //
english: There the king Caṇḍamahāsena married that Daitya maiden, and two sons were born to him, the first named Gopālaka and the second Pālaka; and when they were born he held a feast in honour of Indra on their account.

sanskrit: tatastaṃ nṛpatiṃ svapne tuṣṭo vakti sma vāsavaḥ / prāpsyasyananyasadṛśīṃ matprasādātsutāmiti // tataḥ kālena jātāsya rājñaḥ kanyā tu tanvyatha / apūrvā nirmitā dhātrā candrasyevāparā tanuḥ // kāmadevāvatāro 'syāḥ putro vidyādharādhipaḥ / bhaviṣyatīti tatkālamudabhūdbhāratī divaḥ // dattā me vāsavenaiṣā tuṣṭeneti sa bhūpatiḥ / nāmnā vāsavadattāṃ tāṃ tanayāmakarottadā //
english: Then Indra, being pleased, said to that king in a dream: “By my favour thou shalt obtain a matchless daughter.” Then in course of time a graceful daughter was born to that king, like a second and more wonderful shape of the moon made by the Creator. And on that occasion a voice was heard from heaven: “She shall give birth to a son, who shall be a very incarnation of the God of Love, and king of the Vidyādharas.” Then the king gave that daughter the name of Vāsavadattā, because she was given by Indra being pleased with him.

sanskrit: sā ca tasya pitur gehe pradeyā saṃprati sthitā / prāṅmanthād arṇavasyeva kamalā kukṣikoṭare //
english: [M] (Main story line continued) And that maiden still remains unmarried in the house of her father, like the Goddess of Prosperity in the hollow cavity of the ocean before it was churned.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhaprabhāvaścaṇḍamahāsenabhūpatiḥ sa kila / deva na śakyo jetuṃ yathā tathā durgadeśasthaḥ //
english: That King Caṇḍamahāsena cannot indeed be conquered by you, O king; in the first place, because he is so powerful, and, in the next place, because his realm is situated in a difficult country.

sanskrit: kiṃ ca sa rājanvāñchati dātuṃ tubhyaṃ sadaiva tanayāṃ tām / prārthayate tu sa rājā nijapakṣamahodayaṃ mānī //
english: Moreover, he is ever longing to give you that daughter of his in marriage, but, being a proud monarch, he desires the triumph of himself and his adherents.

sanskrit: sā cāvaśyaṃ manye vāsavadattā tvayaiva pariṇeyā / sa sapadi vāsavadattāhṛtahṛdayo vatsarājo 'bhūt // iti mahākaviśrīsomadevabhaṭṭaviracite kathāsaritsāgare kathāmukhalambake tṛtīyas taraṅgaḥ / caturthas taraṅgaḥ / atrāntare sa vatseśapratidūtastadabravīt / gatvā prativacaścaṇḍamahāsenāya bhūbhṛte //
english: But I think you must certainly marry that Vāsavadattā.” When he heard this that king immediately lost his heart to Vāsavadattā.[14] [Additional note: the “external soul” motif] [M] (Main story line continued) IN the meanwhile the ambassador sent by the King of Vatsa in answer to Caṇḍamahāsena’s embassy went and told that monarch his master’s reply.

sanskrit: so 'pi caṇḍamahāsenastacchrutvaiva vyacintayat / sa tāvadiha nāyāti mānī vatseśvaro bhṛśam //
english: Caṇḍamahāsena for his part, on hearing it, began to reflect: “It is certain that that proud King of Vatsa will not come here.

sanskrit: kanyā hi tatra na preṣyā bhavedevaṃ hi lāghavam / tasmādbaddhvaiva taṃ yuktyā nṛpamānāyayāmyaham //
english: And I cannot send my daughter to his Court; such conduct would be unbecoming;

sanskrit: iti saṃcintya saṃmantrya sa rājā mantribhiḥ saha / akārayatsvasadṛśaṃ mahāntaṃ yantrahastinam // taṃ cāntarvīrapuruṣaiḥ kṛtvā channairadhiṣṭhitam / vindhyāṭavyāṃ sa nidadhe rājā yantramayaṃ gajam //
english: so I must capture him by some stratagem and bring him here as a prisoner.” Having thus reflected and deliberated with his ministers, the king had made a large artificial elephant like his own, and, after filling it with concealed warriors, he placed it in the Vindhya forest.

sanskrit: tatra taṃ cārapuruṣāḥ paśyanti sma vidūrataḥ / gajabandharasāsaktavatsarājopajīvinaḥ //
english: There the scouts kept in his pay by the King of Vatsa, who was passionately fond of the sport of elephant-catching, discerned it from a distance[1];

sanskrit: te ca tvaritamāgatya vatsarājaṃ vyajijñapan / deva dṛṣṭo gajo 'smābhireko vindhyavane bhraman // asminniyati bhūloke naiva yo 'nyatra dṛśyate / varṣmaṇā vyāptagagano vindhyādririva jaṅgamaḥ // tataścāravacaḥ śrutvā vatsarājo jaharṣa saḥ / tebhyaḥ suvarṇalakṣaṃ ca pradadau pāritoṣikam //
english: and they came with speed and informed the King of Vatsa in these words: “O king, we have seen a single elephant roaming in the Vindhya forest, such that nowhere else in this wide world is his equal to be found, filling the sky with his stature, like a moving peak of the Vindhya range.” Then the king rejoiced on hearing this report from the scouts, and he gave them a hundred thousand gold pieces by way of reward.

sanskrit: taṃ cedgajendraṃ prāpsyāmi pratimallaṃ naḍāgireḥ / tataścaṇḍamahāseno vaśyo bhavati me dhruvam // tato vāsavadattāṃ tāṃ sa svayaṃ me prayacchati / iti saṃcintayanso 'tha rājā tāmanayanniśām // prātaśca mantrivacanaṃ nyakṛtvā gajatṛṣṇayā / puraskṛtyaiva tāṃścārānyayau vindhyāṭavīṃ prati //
english: The king spent that night in thinking: “If I obtain that mighty elephant, a fit match for Naḍāgiri, then that Caṇḍamahāsena will certainly be in my power, and then he will of his own accord give me his daughter Vāsavadattā.” So in the morning he started for the Vindhya forest, making these scouts show him the way, disregarding, in his ardent desire to capture the elephant, Elephant the advice of his ministers.

sanskrit: prasthānalagnasya phalaṃ kanyālābhaṃ sabandhanam / yadūcurgaṇakāstasya tatsa naiva vyacārayat //
english: He did not pay any attention to the fact that the astrologers said that the position of the heavenly bodies at the moment of his departure portended the acquisition of a maiden together with imprisonment.

sanskrit: prāpya vindhyāṭavīṃ tasya gajasya kṣobhaśaṅkayā / vatsarājaḥ sa sainyāni dūrādeva nyavārayat // cāramātrasahāyastu vīṇāṃ ghoṣavatīṃ dadhat / nijavyasanavistīrṇāṃ tāṃ viveśa mahāṭavīm //
english: When the King of Vatsa reached the Vindhya forest he made his troops halt at a distance, through fear of alarming that elephant, and, accompanied by the scouts only, holding in his hand his melodious lute, he entered that great forest boundless as his own kingly vice.

sanskrit: vindhyasya dakṣiṇe pārśve dūrācāraiḥ pradarśitam / gajaṃ satyagajābhāsaṃ taṃ dadarśa sa bhūpatiḥ //
english: The king saw on the southern slope of the Vindhya range that elephant looking like a real one, pointed out to him by his scouts from a distance.

sanskrit: ekākī vādayanvīṇāṃ cintayan bandhanāni saḥ / madhuradhvani gāyaṃś ca śanair upajagāma tam //
english: He slowly approached it, alone, playing on his lute, thinking how he should bind it, and singing in melodious tones.

sanskrit: gāndharvadattacittatvātsaṃdhyādhvāntavaśācca saḥ / na taṃ vanagajaṃ rājā māyāgajamalakṣayat //
english: As his mind was fixed on his music, and the shades of evening were setting in, that king did not perceive that the supposed elephant was an artificial one.

sanskrit: so 'pi hastī tamutkarṇatālo gītarasādiva / upetyopetya vicalandūramākṛṣṭavānnṛpam // tato 'kasmācca nirgatya tasmādyantramayādgajāt / vatseśvaraṃ taṃ saṃnaddhāḥ puruṣāḥ paryavārayan // tāndṛṣṭvā nṛpatiḥ kopādākṛṣṭacchuriko 'tha saḥ / agrasthānyodhayannanyairetya paścādagṛhyata //
english: The elephant,[2] too, for its part, lifting up its ears and flapping them, as if through delight in the music, kept advancing and then retiring, and so drew the king to a great distance. And then, suddenly issuing from that artificial elephant, a body of soldiers in full armour surrounded that King of Vatsa. When he beheld them, the king in a rage drew his hunting-knife, but while he was fighting with those in front of him he was seized by others coming up behind.

sanskrit: saṃketamilitaiścānyairyodhāstaiḥ sainikaiḥ saha / ninyurvatseśvaraṃ caṇḍamahāsenāntikaṃ ca tam // so 'pi caṇḍamahāseno nirgayāgre kṛtādaraḥ / vatseśena samaṃ tena viveśojjayinīṃ purīm //
english: And those warriors, with the help of others, who appeared at a concerted signal, carried that King of Vatsa into the presence of Caṇḍamahāsena. Caṇḍamahāsena for his part came out to meet him with the utmost respect, and entered with him the city of Ujjayinī.

sanskrit: sa tatra tadṛśe paurairavamānakalaṅkitaḥ / śaśīva locanānando vatsarājo navāgataḥ //
english: Then the newly arrived King of Vatsa was beheld by the citizens, like the moon, pleasing to the eyes, though spotted with humiliation.

sanskrit: tato 'sya guṇarāgeṇa vadhamāśaṅkya tatra te / paurāḥ saṃbhūya sakalāścakrurmaraṇaniścayam // na me vatseśvaro vadhyaḥ saṃdheya iti tān bruvan / so 'tha caṇḍamahāsenaḥ paurān kṣobhād avārayat //
english: Then all the citizens, suspecting that he was to be put to death, through regard for his virtues assembled and determined to commit suicide.[3] Then the King Caṇḍamahāsena put a stop to the agitation of the citizens by informing them that he did not intend to put the monarch of Vatsa to death, but to win him over.

sanskrit: tato vāsavadattāṃ tāṃ sutāṃ tatraiva bhūpatiḥ / vatsarājāya gāndharvaśikṣāhetoḥ samarpayat //
english: So the king made over his daughter Vāsavadattā on the spot to the King of Vatsa to be taught music, and said to him: “Prince, teach this lady music;

sanskrit: uvāca cainaṃ gāndharvaṃ tvametāṃ śikṣaya prabho / tataḥ prāpsyasi kalyāṇaṃ mā viṣādaṃ kṛthā iti //
english: in this way you will obtain a happy issue to your adventure;

sanskrit: tasya dṛṣṭvā tu tāṃ kanyāṃ vatsarājasya mānasam / tathā snehāktamabhavanna yahā manyumaikṣata //
english: do not despond.” But when he beheld that fair lady the mind of the King of Vatsa was so steeped in love that he put out of sight his anger;

sanskrit: tasyāś ca cakṣurmanasī saha taṃ prati jagmatuḥ / hriyā cakṣur nivavṛtte manas tu na kathaṃcana //
english: and her heart and mind turned towards him together; her eye was then averted through modesty, but her mind not at all.

sanskrit: atha vāsavadattāṃ tāṃ gāpayaṃstadgatekṣaṇaḥ / tatra gāndharvaśālāyāṃ vatsarāja uvāsa saḥ //
english: So the King of Vatsa dwelt in the concert-room of Caṇḍamahāsena’s palace, teaching Vāsavadattā to sing, with his eyes fixed ever on her.

sanskrit: aṅke ghoṣavatī tasya kaṇṭhe gītaśrutistathā / puro vāsavadattā ca tasthau cetovinodinī //
english: In his lap was his lute, in his throat the quarter-tone of vocal music, and in front of him stood Vāsavadattā, delighting his heart.

sanskrit: sā ca vāsavadattāsya paricaryāparābhavat / takṣmīriva tadekāgrā baddhasyāpyanapāyinī //
english: And that princess was devoted in her attentions to him, resembling the Goddess of Fortune in that she was firmly attached to him, and did not leave him though he was a captive.

sanskrit: atrāntare ca kauśāmbyāṃ vatsarājānuge jane / āvṛtte taṃ prabhuṃ buddhvā baddhaṃ rāṣṭraṃ pracukṣubhe //
english: In the meanwhile the men who had accompanied the king returned to Kauśāmbī, and the country, hearing of the captivity of the monarch, was thrown into a state of great excitement.

sanskrit: ujjayinyāmavaskandaṃ dātumaicchansamantataḥ / vatseśvarānurāgeṇa kruddhāḥ prakṛtayastadā //
english: Then the enraged subjects, out of love for the King of Vatsa, wanted to make a general[4] assault on Ujjayinī.

sanskrit: naiva caṇḍamahāseno balasādhyo mahān hi saḥ / na caivaṃ vatsarājasya śarīre kuśalaṃ bhavet // tasmānna yukto 'vaskando buddhisādhyamidaṃ punaḥ / iti prakṛtayaḥ kṣobhānnavāryanta rumaṇvatā //
english: But Rumaṇvat checked the impetuous fury of the subjects by telling them that Caṇḍamahāsena was not to be overcome by force, for he was a mighty monarch, and besides that an assault was not advisable, for it might endanger the safety of the King of Vatsa;

sanskrit: tato 'nuraktamālokya rāṣṭramavyabhicāri tat / rumaṇvadādīn āha sma dhīro yaugandharāyaṇaḥ // ihaiva sarvair yuṣmābhiḥ sthātavyaṃ satatodyataiḥ / rakṣaṇīyamidaṃ rāṣṭraṃ kāle kāryaśca vikramaḥ //
english: The calm and resolute Yaugandharāyaṇa, seeing that the country was loyal, and would not swerve from its allegiance, said to Rumaṇvat and the others: “All of you must remain here, ever on the alert; you must guard this country, and when a fit occasion comes you must display your prowess;

sanskrit: vasantakadvitīyaśca gatvāhaṃ prajñayā svayā / vatseśaṃ mocayitvā tamānayāmi na saṃśayaḥ //
english: but I will go, accompanied by Vasantaka only, and will without fail accomplish by my wisdom the deliverance of the king and bring him home.

sanskrit: jalāhatau viśeṣeṇa vaidyutāgneriva dyutiḥ / āpadi sphurati prajñā yasya dhīraḥ sa eva hi //
english: For he is a truly firm and resolute man, whose wisdom shines forth in adversity, as the lightning flash is especially brilliant during pelting rain.

sanskrit: prākārabhañjanānyogāṃstathā nigaḍabhañjanān / adarśanaprayogāṃśca jāne 'hamupayoginaḥ // ityuktvā prakṛtīḥ kṛtvā hastanyastā rumaṇvataḥ / yaugandharāyaṇaḥ prāyāt kauśāmbyāḥ savasantakaḥ //
english: I know spells for breaking through walls, and for rending fetters, and receipts for becoming invisible, serviceable at need.” Having said this, and entrusted to Rumaṇvat the care of the subjects, Yaugandharāyaṇa set out for Kauśāmbī with Vasantaka.

sanskrit: praviveśa ca tenaiva saha vindhyamahāṭavīm / svaprajñāmiva sattāḍhyāṃ svanītimiva durgamām //
english: And with him he entered the Vindhya forest, full of life,[5] like his wisdom, intricate and trackless as his policy.

sanskrit: tatra vatseśamittrasya vindhyaprāgbhāravāsinaḥ / gṛhaṃ pulindakākhyasya pulindādhipateragāt //
english: Then he visited the palace of the King of the Pulindas, Pulindaka by name, who dwelt on a peak of the Vindhya range, and was an ally of the King of Vatsa.

sanskrit: taṃ sajjaṃ sthāpayitvā ca pahā tenāgamiṣyataḥ / vatsarājasya rakṣārthaṃ bhūrisainyasamanvitam // gatvā vasantakasakhastato yaugandharāyaṇaḥ / ujjayinyāṃ mahākālaśmaśānaṃ prāpa sa kramāt // viveśa tacca vetālaiḥ kravyagandhibhirāvṛtam / itastatastamaḥ śyāmaiścitādhūmairivāparaiḥ //
english: He first placed him, with a large force at his heels, in readiness to protect the King of Vatsa when he returned that way, and then he went on, accompanied by Vasantaka, and at last arrived at the burning-ground of Mahākāla in Ujjayinī, which was densely tenanted by vampires[6] that smelt of carrion, and hovered hither and thither, black as night, rivalling the smoke-wreaths of the funeral pyres.

sanskrit: tatrainaṃ darśanaprīto mittrabhāvāya tatkṣaṇam / yogeśvarākhyo vṛtavānabhyetya brahmarākṣasaḥ //
english: And there a Brāhman-Rākṣasa[7] of the name of Yogeśvara immediately came up to him, delighted to see him, and admitted him into his friendship;

sanskrit: tenopadiṣṭayā yuktyā tato yaugandharāyaṇaḥ / na cakārātmanaḥ sadyo rūpasya parivartanam //
english: then Yaugandharāyaṇa by means of a charm, which he taught him, suddenly altered his shape.

sanskrit: babhūva tena vikṛtaḥ kubjo vṛddhaśca tatkṣaṇāt / unmattaveṣaḥ khalvāṭo hāsyasaṃjananaḥ param // tayaiva yuktyā sa tadā sirānaddhapṛthūdaram / cakre vasantakasyāpi rūpaṃ danturadurmukham //
english: That charm immediately made him deformed, hunchbacked and old, and besides gave him the appearance of a madman, so that he produced loud laughter in those who beheld him.[8] And in the same way Yaugandharāyaṇa, by means of that very charm, gave Vasantaka a body full of outstanding veins, with a large stomach, and an ugly mouth with projecting teeth;

sanskrit: tato rājakuladvāramādau preṣya vasantakam / viveśojjayinīṃ tāṃ sa tādṛgyaugandharāyaṇaḥ //
english: then he sent Vasantaka on in front to the gate of the king’s palace, and entered Ujjayinī with such an appearance as I have described.

sanskrit: nṛtyan gāyaṃś ca tatrāsau baṭubhiḥ parivāritaḥ / dṛṣṭaḥ sakautukaṃ sarvairyayau rājagṛhaṃ prati //
english: There he, singing and dancing, surrounded by Brāhman boys, beheld with curiosity by all, made his way to the king’s palace.

sanskrit: tatra rājāvarodhānāṃ tenāsau kṛtakautukaḥ / agādvāsavadattāyāḥ śanaiḥ śravaṇagocaram //
english: And there he excited by that behaviour the curiosity of the king’s wives, and was at last heard of by Vāsavadattā.

sanskrit: sā tamānāyayāmāsa ceṭikāṃ preṣya satvaram / gāndharvaśālāṃ narmaikasādaraṃ hi navaṃ vayaḥ // sa ca tatra gato vṛddhaṃ vatsarājaṃ dadarśa tam / unmattaveṣo vigaladvāṣpo yaugandharāyaṇaḥ //
english: She quickly sent a maid and had him brought to the concert-room. For youth is twin brother to mirth.[9] And when Yaugandharāyaṇa came there and beheld the King of Vatsa in fetters, though he had assumed the appearance of a madman, he could not help shedding tears.

sanskrit: cakāra tasmai saṃjñāṃ ca vatsarājāya so 'pi tam / pratyabhijñātavānrājā veṣapracchannamāgatam //
english: And he made a sign to the King of Vatsa, who quickly recognised him, though he had come in disguise.

sanskrit: tato vāsavadattāṃ ca tacceṭīḥ prati cātmanaḥ / adarśanaṃ yuktibalād vyadhād yaugandharāyaṇaḥ //
english: Then Yaugandharāyaṇa by means of his magic power made himself invisible to Vāsavadattā and her maids.

sanskrit: rājā tveko dadarśainaṃ tāśca sarvāḥ savismayam / vadanti sma gato 'kasmādunmattaḥ kvāpyasāviti // tacchrutvā taṃ ca dṛṣṭāgre matvā yogabalena tat / yuktyā vāsavadattāṃ tāṃ vatsarājo 'bravīdidam // gatvā sarasvatīpūjāmādāyāgaccha dārike / tacchrutvā sā tathetyuktvā savayasyā viniryayau //
english: So the king alone saw him, and they all said with astonishment: “That maniac has suddenly escaped somewhere or other.” Then the King of Vatsa hearing them say that, and seeing Yaugandharāyaṇa in front of him, understood that this was due to magic, and cunningly said to Vāsavadattā: “Go, my good girl, and bring the requisites for the worship of Sarasvatī.” When she heard that she said, “So I will,” and went out with her companions.

sanskrit: yathocitamupetyātha dadau vatseśvarāya saḥ / yaugandharāyaṇas tasmai yogān nigaḍabhañjanān //
english: Then Yaugandharāyaṇa approached the king and communicated to him, according to the prescribed form, spells for breaking chains;

sanskrit: anyānvāsavadattāyā vīṇātantrīniyojitān / vaśīkaraṇayogāṃśca rājñe 'smai sa samārpayat //
english: and at the same time he furnished him with other charms for winning the heart of Vāsavadattā, which were attached to the strings of the lute;

sanskrit: vyajijñapacca taṃ rājannihāyāto vasantakaḥ / dvāri sthito 'nyarūpeṇa taṃ kuruṣvāntike dvijam //
english: and informed him that Vasantaka had come there and was standing outside the door in a changed form, and recommended him to have that Brāhman summoned to him.

sanskrit: yadā vāsavadatteyaṃ tvayi visrambhameṣyati / tadā vakṣyāmi yadahaṃ tatkuryāstiṣṭha sāṃpratam //
english: At the same time he said: “When this lady Vāsavadattā shall come to repose confidence in you, then you must do what I tell you;

sanskrit: ityuktvā niryayau śīghraṃ tato yaugandharāyaṇaḥ / agādvāsavadattā ca pūjāmādāya tatkṣaṇāt //
english: at the present remain quiet.” Having said this, Yaugandharāyaṇa quickly went out, and immediately Vāsavadattā entered with the requisites for the worship of Sarasvatī.

sanskrit: so 'tha tāmavadadrājā bahirdvāri dvijaḥ sthitaḥ / sarasvatyarcane so 'smindakṣiṇārthe praveśyatām // tatheti dvāradeśātsa tatra vāsavadattayā / virūpāmākṛtiṃ bibhradānāyyata vasantakaḥ // sa cānītastamālokya vatseśamarudacchucā / tataścāpratibhedāya sa rājā nijagāda tam //
english: Then the king said to her: “There is a Brāhman standing outside the door, let him be brought in to celebrate this ceremony in honour of Sarasvatī, in order that he may obtain a sacrificial fee.” Vāsavadattā consented, and had Vasantaka, who wore a deformed shape, summoned from the door into the music-hall. And when he was brought and saw the King of Vatsa, he wept for sorrow;

sanskrit: he brahmanrogavairūpyaṃ sarvametadahaṃ tava / nivārayāmi mā rodīstiṣṭhehaiva mamāntike //
english: and then the king said to him, in order that the secret might not be discovered: “O Brāhman, I will remove all this deformity of thine produced by sickness;

sanskrit: mahān prasādo deveti sa covāca vasantakaḥ / so 'tha taṃ vikṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājā smitamukho 'bhavat //
english: And when he saw that, Vasantaka guessed what was in the king’s mind, and laughed so that the deformity of his distorted face was increased;

sanskrit: taṃ hasantaṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā krīḍanīyakasaṃnibham / tatra vāsavadattāpi jahāsa ca tutoṣa ca //
english: and thereupon Vāsavadattā, beholding him grinning like a doll, burst out laughing also, and was much delighted.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā narmaṇā bālā taṃ papraccha vasantakam / kiṃ vijñānaṃ vijānāsi bho brahman kathyatām iti // kathāḥ kathayituṃ devi jānāmīti sa cāvadat / kathāṃ kathaya tarhokāmiti sāpi tato 'bravīt // tatastāṃ rājatanayāṃ rañjayansa vasantakaḥ / hāsyavaicitrasarasām imām akathayat kathām //
english: Then the young lady asked Vasantaka in fun the following question:— “Brāhman, what science are you familiar with? Tell us.” So he said: “Princess, I am an adept at telling tales.” Then she said: “Come, tell me a tale.” Then, in order to please that princess, Vasantaka told the following tale, which was charming by its comic humour and variety.

sanskrit: astīha mathurā nāma purī kaṃsārijanmabhūḥ / tasyāṃ rūpaṇiketyāsītkhyātā vāravilāsinī //
english: There is in this country a city named Mathurā, the bith-place of Kṛṣṇa; in it there was a courtesan known by the name of Rūpiṇikā;

sanskrit: tasyā makaradaṃṣṭrākhyā mātābhūdvṛddhakuṭṭanī / tadguṇākṛṣyamāṇānāṃ yūnāṃ dṛśi viṣacchaṭā //
english: she had for a mother an old bawd named Makaradaṃṣṭrā, who seemed a lump of poison in the eyes of the young men attracted by her daughter’s charms.

sanskrit: pūjākāle surakulaṃ svaniyogāya jātu sā / gatā rūpaṇikā dūrādekaṃ puruṣamaikṣata //
english: One day Rūpiṇikā went at the time of worship to the temple to perform her duty,[10] and beheld from a distance a young man.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭaḥ subhagastasyā viveśa hṛdayaṃ tathā / yathā mātrā kṛtāste 'smādupadeśā viniryayuḥ //
english: When she saw that handsome young fellow, he made such an impression upon her heart that all her mother’s instructions vanished from it.

sanskrit: ceṭikāmatha sāvādīdgaccha madvacanādamum / puruṣaṃ brūhi madgehe tvayādyāgamyatāmiti // tatheti ceṭikā sā ca gatvā tasmai tad abravīt / tataḥ sa kiṃcid vimṛśan puruṣas tām abhāṣata //
english: Then she said to her maid: “Go and tell this man from me that he is to come to my house to-day.” The maid said, “So I will,” and immediately went and told him. Then the man thought a little and said to her: “I am a Brāhman named Lohajaṅgha[11];

sanskrit: lohajaṅghābhidhāno 'smi brāhmaṇo nāsti me dhanam / tadāḍhyajanalabhye hi ko 'haṃ rūpaṇikāgṛhe // na dhanaṃ vāñchyate tvattaḥ svāminyetyudite tayā / sa lohajaṅghas tadvākyaṃ tatheti pratyapadyata //
english: I have no wealth; then what business have I in the house of Rūpiṇikā, which is only to be entered by the rich?” The maid said: “My mistress does not desire wealth from you.” Whereupon Lohajaṅgha consented to do as she wished.

sanskrit: tataśceṭīmukhādbuddhvā tacca sā gṛhamutsukā / gatvā rūpaṇikā tatsthau tanmārganyastalocanā //
english: When she heard that from the maid, Rūpiṇikā went home in a state of excitement, and remained with her eyes fixed on the path by which he would come.

sanskrit: kṣaṇācca lohajaṅgho 'tha tasyāmandiramāyayau / kuto 'yamiti kuṭṭanyā dṛṣṭo makaradaṃṣṭrayā //
english: And soon Lohajaṅgha came to her house, while the bawd Makaradaṃṣṭrā looked at him, and wondered where he came from.

sanskrit: sāpi rūpaṇikā dṛṣṭvā svayamutthāya sādarā / vāsaveśmāntaraṃ hṛṣṭā kaṇṭhe lagnā nināya tam //
english: Rūpiṇikā for her part, when she saw him, rose up to meet him herself with the utmost respect, and clinging to his neck in her joy led him to her own private apartments.

sanskrit: tatra sā lohajaṅghasya tasya saubhāgyasaṃpadā / vaśīkṛtā satī nānyatphalaṃ janmanyamanyata //
english: Then she was captivated with Lohajaṅgha’s wealth of accomplishments, and considered that she had been only born to love him.

sanskrit: tatastayā nivṛttānyapuruṣāsaṅgayā saha / yathāsukhaṃ sa tatraiva tasthau tanmandire yuvā //
english: So she avoided the society of other men, and that young fellow lived with her in her house in great comfort.

sanskrit: taddṛṣṭvā śikṣitāśeṣaveṣayoṣijjagāda tām / mātā makaradaṃṣṭrā sā khinnā rūpaṇikāṃ rahaḥ // kimayaṃ nirdhanaḥ putri sevyate puruṣastvayā / śavaṃ spṛśanti sujanā gaṇikā na tu nirdhanam //
english: Rūpiṇikā’s mother Makaradaṃṣṭrā, who had trained up many courtesans, was annoyed when she saw this, and said to her in private: “My daughter, why do you associate with a poor man? Courtesans of good taste embrace a corpse in preference to a poor man.

sanskrit: kānurāgaḥ kva veśyātvamiti te vismṛtaṃ katham / saṃdhyeva rāgiṇī veśyā na ciraṃ putri dīpyate //
english: What business has a courtesan like you with affection?[12] How have you come to forget that great principle? The light of a red[13] sunset lasts but a short time, and so does the splendour of a courtesan who gives way to affection.

sanskrit: naṭīva kṛtrimaṃ prema gaṇikārthāya darśayet / tadenaṃ nirdhanaṃ muñca mā kṛthā nāśamātmanaḥ // iti mātṛvacaḥ śrutvā ruṣā rūpaṇikābravīt / maivaṃ vādīrmama hyeṣa prāṇebhyo 'pyadhikaḥ priyaḥ //
english: A courtesan, like an actress, should exhibit an assumed affection in order to get wealth; so forsake this pauper, do not ruin yourself.” When she heard this speech of her mother’s, Rūpiṇikā said in a rage: “Do not talk in this way, for I love him more than my life.

sanskrit: dhanamasti ca me bhūri kimanyena karomyaham / tadamba naiva vaktavyā bhūyo 'pyevamahaṃ tvayā // tacchrutvā lohajaṅghasya nirvāsanavidhau krudhā / tasthau makaradaṃṣṭrā sā tasyopāyaṃ vicinvatī //
english: And as for wealth, I have plenty, what do I want with more? So you must not speak to me again, mother, in this way.” When she heard this, Makaradaṃṣṭrā was in a rage, and she remained thinking over some device for getting rid of this Lohajaṅgha.

sanskrit: atha mārgāgataṃ kaṃcitkṣīṇakoṣaṃ dadarśa sā / rājaputraṃ parivṛtaṃ puruṣaiḥ śastrapāṇibhiḥ //
english: Then she saw coming along the road a certain Rājpūt, who had spent all his wealth, surrounded by retainers with swords in their hands.

sanskrit: upagamya drutaṃ taṃ ca nītvaikānte jagāda sā / nirdhanena mamaikena kāmukenāvṛtaṃ gṛham //
english: So she went up to him quickly and, taking him aside, said: “My house is beset by a certain poor lover.

sanskrit: tattvamāgaccha tatrādya tathā ca kuru yena saḥ / gṛhānmama nivarteta madīyāṃ ca sutāṃ bhaja // tatheti rājaputro 'tha praviveśa sa tadgṛham / tasmin kṣaṇe rūpaṇikā tasthau devakule ca sā //
english: So come there yourself to-day, and take such order with him that he shall depart from my house, and do you possess my daughter.” “Agreed,” said the Rājpūt, and entered that house.

sanskrit: lohajaṅghaśca tatkālaṃ bahiḥ kvāpi sthito 'bhavat / kṣaṇāntare ca niḥśaṅkastatraiva samupāyayau //
english: At that precise moment Rūpiṇikā was in the temple, and Lohajaṅgha meanwhile was absent somewhere, and, suspecting nothing, he returned to the house a moment afterwards.

sanskrit: tatkṣaṇaṃ rājaputrasya tasya bhṛtyaiḥ pradhāvya saḥ / dṛḍhaṃ pādaprahārādyaiḥ sarveṣvaṅgeṣv atāḍyata // tatas tair eva cāmedhyapūrṇe kṣiptaḥ sa khātake / lohajaṅghaḥ kathamapi prapalāyitavāṃstataḥ //
english: Immediately the retainers of the Rājpūt ran upon him, and gave him severe kicks and blows on all his limbs, and then they threw him into a ditch full of all kinds of impurities, and Lohajaṅgha with difficulty escaped from it.

sanskrit: athāgatā rūpaṇikā tadbuddhvā śokavihvalā / sābhūdvīkṣyātha sa yayau rājaputro yathāgatam //
english: Then Rūpiṇikā returned to the house, and when she heard what had taken place she was distracted with grief, so the Rājpūt, seeing that, returned as he came.

sanskrit: lohajaṅgho 'pi kuṭṭanyā prasahya sa khalīkṛtaḥ / gantuṃ pravavṛte tīrthaṃ prāṇāṃstyaktuṃ viyogavān // gacchannaṭavyāṃ saṃtaptaḥ kuṭṭanīmanyunā hṛdi / tvaci ca grīṣmatāpena cchāyāmabhilalāṣa saḥ //
english: Lohajaṅgha, after suffering this brutal outrage by the machinations of the bawd, set out for some holy place of pilgrimage, in order to leave his life there, now that he was separated from his beloved. As he was going along in the wild country,[14] with his heart burning with anger against the bawd, and his skin with the heat of the summer, he longed for shade.

sanskrit: tarumaprāpnuvanso 'tha lebhe hastikalevaram / jaghanena praviśyāntarnirmāṃsaṃ jambukaiḥ kṛtam // carmāvaśeṣe tatrāntaḥ pariśrānaḥ praviśya saḥ / lohajaṅgho yayau nidrāṃ praviśadvātaśītale //
english: Not being able to find a tree, he lighted on the body of an elephant which had been stripped of all its flesh[15] by jackals making their way into it by the hind-quarters; accordingly Lohajaṅgha, being worn out, crept into this carcass, which was a mere shell, as only the skin remained, and went to sleep in it, as it was kept cool by the breeze which freely entered.

sanskrit: athākasmātsamutthāya kṣaṇenaiva samantataḥ / meghaḥ pravavṛte tatra dhārāsāreṇa varṣitum //
english: Then suddenly clouds arose from all sides and began to pour down a pelting shower of rain;

sanskrit: tena nirvivaraṃ prāpa saṃkocaṃ hasticarma tat / kṣaṇācca tena mārgeṇa jalaugho bhṛśamāyayau // tenāpahṛtya gaṅgāyāmakṣepi gajacarma tat / tajjalaughena nītvā ca samudrāntarnyadhīyata //
english: that rain made the elephant’s skin contract so that no aperture was left,[16] and immediately a copious inundation came that way, and carrying off the elephant’s hide swept it into the Ganges, so that eventually the inundation bore it into the sea.

sanskrit: tatra dṛṣṭvā ca taccarma nipatyāmiṣaśaṅkayā / hṛtvābdheḥ pāramanayatpakṣī garuḍavaṃśajaḥ //
english: And there a bird of the race of Garuḍa saw that hide and, supposing it to be carrion, took it to the other side of the sea;

sanskrit: tatra cañcvā vidāryaitad gajacarma vilokya ca / antaḥsthaṃ mānuṣaṃ pakṣī palāyya sa tato yayau //
english: there it tore open the elephant’s hide with its claws and, seeing that there was a man inside it, fled away.

sanskrit: tataśca carmaṇastasmātpakṣisaṃrambhabodhitaḥ / taccañcuracitadvārāllohajaṅgho viniryayau //
english: But Lohajaṅgha was awaked by the bird’s pecking and scratching, and came out through the aperture made by its beak.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā samudrapārasthamātmānaṃ ca savismayaḥ / anidrasvapnamiva tat sa samagram amanyata //
english: And finding that he was on the other side of the sea, he was astonished, and looked upon the whole thing as a daydream;

sanskrit: atha dvau rākṣasau tatra ghorau bhīto dadarśa saḥ / tau cāpi rākṣasau dūrāccakitau tamapaśyatām //
english: then he saw there to his terror two horrible Rākṣasas, and those two for their part contemplated him from a distance with feelings of fear.

sanskrit: rāmātparābhavaṃ smṛtvā taṃ tathaiva ca mānuṣam / dṛṣṭvā tīrṇāmbudhiṃ bhūyastau bhayaṃ hṛdi cakratuḥ //
english: Remembering how they were defeated by Rāma, and seeing that Lohajaṅgha was also a man who had crossed the sea,[17] they were once more alarmed in their hearts.

sanskrit: saṃmantrya ca tayormadhyādeko gatvā tadaiva tam / vibhīṣaṇāya prabhave yathādṛṣṭaṃ nyavedayat //
english: So, after they had deliberated together, one of them went off immediately and told the whole occurrence to King Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭarāmaprabhāvaḥ sanso 'pi rājā vibhīṣaṇaḥ / mānuṣāgamanādbhīto rākṣasaṃ tamabhāṣata // gaccha madvacanādbhadra prītyā taṃ brūhi mānuṣam / āgamyatāṃ gṛhe 'smākaṃ prasādaḥ kriyatāmiti // tathetyāgatya tattasmai svaprabhuprārthanāvacaḥ / cakito lohajaṅghāya śaśaṃsa sa ca rākṣasaḥ //
english: King Vibhīṣaṇa, too, as he had seen the prowess of Rāma, being terrified at the arrival of a man, said to that Rākṣasa: “Go, my good friend, and tell that man from me, in a friendly manner, that he is to do me the favour of coming to my palace.” The Rākṣasa said, “I will do so,” and timidly approached Lohajaṅgha, and told him that request of his sovereign’s.

sanskrit: so 'pyaṅgīkṛtya tadvipro lohajaṅghaḥ praśāntadhīḥ / tenaiva sadvitīyena saha laṅkāṃ tato 'gamat //
english: Lohajaṅgha for his part accepted that invitation with unruffled calm, and went to Laṅkā with that Rākṣasa as his companion.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ ca dṛṣṭasauvarṇatattatprāsādavismitaḥ / praviśya rājabhavanaṃ sa dadarśa vibhīṣaṇam //
english: And when he arrived in Laṅkā he was astonished at beholding numerous splendid edifices of gold, and entering the king’s palace he saw Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: so 'pi papraccha rājā taṃ kṛtātithyaḥ kṛtāśiṣam / brahman katham imāṃ bhūmim anuprāpto bhavān iti // tataḥ sa dhūrto 'vādīttaṃ lohajaṅgho vibhīṣaṇam / vipro 'haṃ lohajaṅghākhyo mathurāyāṃ kṛtasthitiḥ //
english: The king welcomed the Brāhman, who blessed him in return, and then Vibhīṣaṇa said: “Brāhman, how did you manage to reach this country?” Then the cunning Lohajaṅgha said to Vibhīṣaṇa: “I am a Brāhman of the name of Lohajaṅgha residing in Mathurā;

sanskrit: so 'haṃ dāridryasaṃtaptastatra nārāyaṇāmataḥ / nirāhāraḥ sthito 'kārṣaṃ gatvā devakulaṃ tapaḥ // vibhīṣaṇāntikaṃ gaccha madbhakaḥ sa hi te dhanam / dāsyatīty ādiśat svapne tato māṃ bhagavān hariḥ // kvāhaṃ vibhīṣaṇaḥ keti mayokte sa punaḥ prabhuḥ / samādiśadvrajādyaiva taṃ drakṣyasi vibhīṣaṇam //
english: and I, Lohajaṅgha, being afflicted at my poverty, went to the temple of the god, and remaining fasting, for a long time performed austerities in the presence of Nārāyaṇa.[18] Then the adorable Hari[18] commanded me in a dream, saying: ‘Go thou to Vibhīṣaṇa, for he is a faithful worshipper of mine, and he will give thee wealth.’ Then I said: ‘Vibhīṣaṇa is where I cannot reach him.’ But the lord continued: ‘To-day shalt thou see that Vibhīṣaṇa.’ So the lord spake to me, and immediately I woke up and found myself upon this side of the sea.

sanskrit: ityuktaḥ prabhuṇā sadyaḥ prabuddho 'hamihāmbudheḥ / pāre 'vasthitamātmānamapaśyaṃ vedmi nāparam // ityukto lohajaṅghena laṅkāmālokya durgamām / satyaṃ divyaprabhāvo 'yamiti mene vibhīṣaṇaḥ //
english: I know no more.” When Vibhīṣaṇa heard this from Lohajaṅgha, reflecting that Laṅkā was a difficult place to reach, he thought to himself: “Of a truth this man possesses divine power.” And he said to that Brāhman: “Remain here;

sanskrit: tiṣṭha dāsyāmi te vittam ity uktvā brāhmaṇaṃ ca tam / matvā ca rakṣasāṃ haste tamapreṣyaṃ nṛghātinām // tatrasthātsvarṇamūlākhyādgireḥ saṃprekṣya rākṣasān / ānāyayat pakṣipotaṃ garuḍānvayasaṃbhavam // taṃ cāsmai lohajaṅghāyā mathurāyāṃ gamiṣyate / tatkālameva pradadau vaśīkārāya vāhanam //
english: I will give you wealth.” Then he committed him to the care of the man-slaying Rākṣasas as an inviolable deposit, and sent some of his subjects to a mountain in his kingdom called Svarṇamūla, who brought from it a young bird belonging to the race of Garuḍa; and he gave it to that Lohajaṅgha (who had to take a long journey to Mathurā) to ride upon, in order that he might in the meanwhile break it in.

sanskrit: lohajaṅgho 'pi laṅkāyāṃ vāhayannadhiruhya tam / kaṃcitkālaṃ viśaśrāma sa vibhīṣaṇasatkṛtaḥ //
english: Lohajaṅgha for his part mounted on its back, and riding about on it in Laṅkā, rested there for some time, being hospitably entertained by Vibhīṣaṇa.

sanskrit: ekadā taṃ ca papraccha rākṣasendraṃ sakautukaḥ / laṅkāyāṃ kāṣṭhamayyeṣā kathaṃ sarvaiva bhūriti //
english: One day he asked the King of the Rākṣasas, feeling curiosity on the point, why the whole ground of Laṅkā was made of wood;

sanskrit: tacchrutvā sa ca tadvṛttaṃ tamuvāca vibhīṣaṇaḥ / yadi te kautukaṃ brahmaṃstadidaṃ śṛṇu vacmi te //
english: and Vibhīṣaṇa, when he heard that, explained the circumstance to him, saying: “Brāhman, if you take any interest in this matter, listen, I will explain it to you.

sanskrit: purā pratijñopanatāṃ nāgānāṃ dāsabhāvataḥ / niṣkraṣṭukāmo jananīṃ garuḍaḥ kaśyapātmajaḥ // tanmūlyabhūtāṃ devebhyaḥ sudhāmāhartumudyataḥ / balasya hetor bhakṣyārthī svapitur nikaṭaṃ yayau // sa cainaṃ yācito 'vādīnmahāntau gajakacchapau / abdhau staḥ putra tau bhuṅkṣva gaccha śāpacutāviti //
english: Long ago Garuḍa, the son of Kaśyapa, wishing to redeem his mother from her slavery to the snakes, to whom she had been subjected in accordance with an agreement,[19] and preparing to obtain from the gods the nectar which was the price of her ransom, wanted to eat something which would increase his strength, and so he went to his father, who, being importuned, said to him: ‘My son, in the sea there is a huge elephant and a huge tortoise.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa garuḍo gatvā bhakṣyāvādāya tāvubhau / mahataḥ kalpavṛkṣasya śākhāyāṃ samupāviśat // tāṃ ca śākhāṃ bharāt sadyo bhagnāṃ cañcvā babhāra saḥ / adhaḥ sthitataponiṣṭhavālakhilyānurodhataḥ //
english: They have assumed their present form in consequence of a curse: go and eat them.’ Then Garuḍa went and brought them both to eat, and then perched on a bough of the great wishing-tree of paradise.[20] And when that bough suddenly broke with his weight, he held it up with his beak, out of regard to the Bālakhilyas[21] who were engaged in austerities underneath it.

sanskrit: lokopamardabhītena tenātha piturājñayā / ānīya vijane tyaktā sā śākheha garutmatā //
english: Then Garuḍa, afraid that the bough would crush mankind if he let it fall at random, by the advice of his father brought the bough to this uninhabited part of the earth and let it drop.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ pṛṣṭhe kṛtā laṅkā tena kāṭhamayīha bhūḥ / etadvibhiṣaṇācchrutvā lohajaṅghastutoṣa saḥ //
english: Laṅkā was built on the top of that bough, therefore the ground here is of wood.” When he heard this from Vibhīṣaṇa, Lohajaṅgha was perfectly satisfied.

sanskrit: tatas tasmai mahārghāṇi ratnāni subahūni ca / vibhīṣaṇo dadāti sma mathurāṃ gantumicchate //
english: Then Vibhīṣaṇa gave to Lohajaṅgha many valuable jewels, as he desired to set out for Mathurā.

sanskrit: bhaktyā ca devasya harer mathurāvartinaḥ kṛte / haste 'syābjagadāśaṅkhacakrān hemamayān dadau //
english: And out of his devotion to the god Viṣṇu, who dwells at Mathurā, he entrusted to the care of Lohajaṅgha a lotus, a club, a shell and a discus all of gold, to be offered to the god.

sanskrit: tadgṛhītvākhilaṃ tasmin vibhīṣaṇasamarpite / āruhya vihage lakṣaṃ yojanānāṃ prayātari // utpatya vyomamārgeṇa laṅkāyāstīrṇavāridhiḥ / sa lohajaṅgho mathurāmakleśenājagāma tām //
english: Lohajaṅgha took all these and mounted the bird given to him by Vibhīṣaṇa, that could accomplish a hundred thousand yojanas,[22] and rising up into the air in Laṅkā, he crossed the sea and without any difficulty arrived at Mathurā.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ śūnye vihāre ca bāhye vyomno 'vatīrya saḥ / sthāpayāmāsa ratnaughaṃ taṃ babandha ca pakṣiṇam //
english: And there he descended from the air into an empty convent outside the town, and deposited there his abundant treasure, and tied up that bird.

sanskrit: āpaṇe ratnam ekaṃ ca gatvā vikrītavāṃs tataḥ / atha vastrāṅgarāgādi krītavān bhojanaṃ tathā //
english: And then he went into the market and sold one of his jewels, and bought garments and scented unguents, and also food.

sanskrit: tadvihāre ca tatraiva bhuktvā dattvā ca pakṣiṇe / vastrāṅgarāgapuṣpādyairātmānaṃ tairabhūṣayat //
english: And he ate the food in that convent where he was, and gave some to his bird; and he adorned himself with the garments, unguents, flowers and other decorations.

sanskrit: pradoṣe cāyayau tasyāstatraivāruhya pakṣiṇi / gṛhaṃ rūpaṇikāyāstāḥ śaṅkhacakragadā vahan // tatropari tataḥ sthitvā sthānavitkhe caraṃś ca saḥ / śabdaṃ cakāra gambhīraṃ rahaḥsthāṃ śrāvayan priyām //
english: And when night came he mounted that same bird and went to the house of Rūpiṇikā, bearing in his hand the shell, discus and mace; then he hovered over it in the air, knowing the place well, and made a low, deep sound to attract the attention of his beloved, who was alone.

sanskrit: taṃ ca śrutvaiva niryātā sāpaśyadratnarājitam / enaṃ nārāyaṇākalpaṃ vyomni rūpaṇikā niśi //
english: But Rūpiṇikā, as soon as she heard that sound, came out, and saw hovering in the air by night a being like Nārāyaṇa, gleaming with jewels.

sanskrit: ahaṃ haririhāyātastvadarthamiti tena sā / uktā praṇamya vakti sma dayāṃ devaḥ karotviti // athāvatīryā saṃyamya lohajaṅgho vihaṃgamam / viveśa vāsabhavanaṃ sa tayā kānayā saha //
english: He said to her: “I am Hari come hither for thy sake”; whereupon she bowed with her face to the earth and said: “May the god have mercy upon me!” Then Lohajaṅgha descended and tied up his bird, and entered the private apartments of his beloved hand in hand with her.
