sanskrit: tatra saṃprāptasaṃbhogaḥ sa niṣkramya kṣaṇāntare / tathaiva vihagārūḍho jagāma nabhasā tataḥ // devatā viṣubhāryāhaṃ martyaiḥ saha na mantraye / iti rūpaṇikā prātas tasthau maunaṃ vidhāya sā // kasmādevaṃvidhaṃ putri vartase kathyatāṃ tvayā / ityapṛcchata sā mātrā tato makaradaṃṣṭrayā //
english: And after remaining there a short time he came out and, mounting the bird as before, went off through the air.[23] In the morning Rūpiṇikā remained observing an obstinate silence, thinking to herself: “I am the wife of the god Viṣṇu, I must cease to converse with mortals.” And then her mother Makaradaṃṣṭrā said to her: “Why do you behave in this way, my daughter?” And after she had been perseveringly questioned by her mother, she caused to be put up a curtain between herself and her parent, and told her what had taken place in the night, which was the cause of her silence.

sanskrit: nirbandhapṛṣṭā tasyai ca sā mātre maunakāraṇam / śaśaṃsa rātrivṛttāntaṃ dāpayitvāntare paṭam // sā tacchrutvā sasaṃdehā svayaṃ taṃ kuṭṭanī niśi / dadarśa vihagārūḍhaṃ lohajaṅghaṃ tataḥ kṣaṇam // prabhāte ca paṭāntaḥsthāmetya rūpaṇikāṃ rahaḥ / prahvā makaradaṃṣṭrā sā kuṭṭanīti vyajijñapat // devasyānugrahātputri tvaṃ devītvamihāgatā / ahaṃ ca te 'tra jananī tanme dehi sutāphalam //
english: When the bawd heard that, she felt doubt on the subject, but soon after, at night, she saw that very Lohajaṅgha mounted on the bird, and in the morning Makaradaṃṣṭrā came secretly to Rūpiṇikā, who still remained behind the curtain, and inclining herself humbly, preferred to her this request: “Through the favour of the god, thou, my daughter, hast obtained here on earth the rank of a goddess, and I am thy mother in this world, therefore grant me a reward for giving thee birth: entreat the god that, old as I am, with this very body I may enter paradise.

sanskrit: tatheti sā rūpaṇikā tamevārthaṃ vyajijñapat / vyājaviṣṇuṃ punarnaktaṃ lohajaṅgahmupāgatam //
english: Do me this favour.” Rūpiṇikā consented, and requested that very boon from Lohajaṅgha, who came again at night disguised as Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa devaveṣas tāṃ lohajaṅgho 'bravītpriyām / pāpā te jananī svargaṃ vyaktaṃ netuṃ na yujyate //
english: Then Lohajaṅgha, who was personating the god, said to that beloved of his: “Thy mother is a wicked woman, it would not be fitting to take her openly to paradise;

sanskrit: ekādaśyāṃ punaḥ prātardvāramudghaṭyate divi / tatra ca praviśantyagre bahavaḥ śāṃbhavā gaṇāḥ //
english: but on the morning of the eleventh day the door of heaven is opened, and many of the Gaṇas, Śiva’s companions, enter into it before anyone else is admitted.

sanskrit: tanmadhye kṛtatadveṣā tvanmātāsau praveśyate / tadasyāḥ pañcacūḍaṃ tvaṃ kṣurakḷptaṃ śiraḥ kuru // kaṇṭhaṃ karaṅkamālāḍhyaṃ pārśvaṃ caikaṃ sakajjalam / anyatsindūraliptaṃ ca kurvasyā vītavāsasaḥ // evaṃ hyenāṃ gaṇākārāṃ sukhaṃ svargaṃ nayāmyaham / ityuktvā sa kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā lohajaṅghastato 'gamat //
english: Among them I will introduce this mother of thine, if she assume their appearance. So shave her head with a razor, in such a manner that five locks[24] shall be left, put a necklace of skulls round her neck, and stripping off her clothes, paint one side of her body with lamp-black and the other with red lead,[25] for when she has in this way been made to resemble a Gaṇa, I shall find it an easy matter to get her into heaven.” When he had said this, Lohajaṅgha remained a short time and then departed.

sanskrit: prātaśca sā rūpaṇikā yathoktaṃ tamakārayat / veṣaṃ māturathaipāpi tasthau svargaikasaṃmukhī //
english: And in the morning Rūpiṇikā attired her mother as he had directed; and then she remained with her mind entirely fixed on paradise.

sanskrit: āyayau ca punastatra lohajaṅgho niśāmukhe / sā ca rūpaṇikā tasmai mātaraṃ tāṃ samarpayat //
english: So when night came Lohajaṅgha appeared again, and Rūpiṇikā handed over her mother to him.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa vihagārūḍhastāmādāyaiva kuṭṭanīm / agnāṃ vikṛtaveṣāṃ ca javādudapatannabhaḥ //
english: Then he mounted on the bird, and took the bawd with him naked, and transformed as he had directed, and he flew up rapidly with her into the air.

sanskrit: gaganasthaśca tatraiva prāṃśuṃ devakulāgrataḥ / sa dadarśa śilāstambhaṃ cakreṇopari lāñchitam //
english: While he was in the air, he beheld a lofty stone pillar in front of a temple, with a discus on its summit.

sanskrit: tasya pṛṣṭhe sa cakraikasālambe tāṃ nyaveśayat / khalikārapratīkārapatākāmiva kuṭṭanīm //
english: So he placed her on the top of the pillar, with the discus as her only support,[26] and there she hung like a banner to blazon forth his revenge for his ill usage.

sanskrit: iha tiṣṭha kṣaṇaṃ yāvatsāṃnidhyānugrahaṃ bhuvi / gatvā karomīty uktvā ca tasyā dṛṣṭipathād yayau //
english: He said to her: “Remain here a moment while I bless the earth with my approach,” and vanished from her sight.

sanskrit: tatas tatraiva devāgre dṛṣṭvā jāgaraṇāgatān / rātrau yātrotsave lokān gaganād evam abravīt // he lokā iha yuṣmākamuparyadya patiṣyati / sarvasaṃhāriṇī māri tadeta śaraṇaṃ harim // śrutvaitāṃ gaganādvāṇīṃ bhītāḥ sarve 'pi tatra te / māthurā devamāśritya tasthuḥ svastyayanādṛtāḥ //
english: Then beholding a number of people in front of the temple, who had come there to spend the night in devout vigils before the festive procession, he called aloud from the air: “Hear, ye people, this very day there shall fall upon you here the all-destroying Goddess of Pestilence, therefore fly to Hari for protection.” When they heard this voice from the air all the inhabitants of Mathurā who were there, being terrified, implored the protection of the god, and remained devoutly muttering prayers to ward off the calamity.

sanskrit: so 'pi vyomno 'vatīryaiva lohajaṅgho 'valokayan / tasthāv adṛṣṭas tanmadhye devaveṣaṃ nivārya tam //
english: Lohajaṅgha for his part descended from the air and encouraged them to pray, and after changing that dress of his came and stood among the people, without being observed.

sanskrit: adyāpi nāgato devo na ca svargamahaṃ gatā / iti ca stambhapṛṣṭhasthā kuṭṭanyevamacintayat // akṣamaivopari sthātuṃ śrāvayantī janānadhaḥ / hā hāhaṃ patitāsmīti sā cakranda ca vibhyatī // tacchrutvā patitā seyaṃ mārītyāśaṅkya cākulāḥ / devi mā mā patetyūcaste devāgragatā janāḥ // tataḥ sabālavṛddhāste māthurāstāṃ vibhāvarīm / mārīpātabhayodbhrāntā kathamapyatyavāhayan //
english: The bawd thought as she sat upon the top of the pillar: “The god has not come as yet, and I have not reached heaven.” At last, feeling it impossible to remain up there any longer, she cried out in her fear, so that the people below heard: “Alas! I am falling, I am falling.” Hearing that, the people in front of the god’s temple were beside themselves, fearing that the destroying goddess was falling upon them, even as had been foretold, and said: “O goddess, do not fall, do not fall.” So those people of Mathurā, young and old, spent that night in perpetual dread that the destroying goddess would fall upon them, but at last it came to an end;

sanskrit: prātaśca dṛṣṭvā stambhasthāṃ kuṭṭanīṃ tāṃ tathāvidhām / pratyabhijñātavānsarvaḥ pauralokaḥ sarājakaḥ //
english: and then beholding that bawd upon the pillar in the state described,[27] the citizens and the king recognised her at once.

sanskrit: sā ca dṛṣṭvā savailaṣyā stambhāgrājjananīṃ nijām / tāmavātārayatsadyastatrasthaiśca janaiḥ saha //
english: And when she saw it she was abashed, and with the help of the people who were there she managed to get that mother of hers down from the top of the pillar immediately.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā kuṭṭanī tatra sarvaistaiḥ sakutūhalaiḥ / apṛcchyata yathāvṛttaṃ sāpi tebhyaḥ śaśaṃsa tat //
english: Then that bawd was asked by all the people there, who were filled with curiosity, to tell them the whole story, and she did so.

sanskrit: tataḥ siddhādicaritaṃ tanmatvādbhutakārakam / sarājavipravaṇijo janās te vākyam abruvan // yeneyaṃ vipralabdhā hi vañcitānekakāmukā / prakaṭaḥ so 'stu tasyeha paṭṭabandho vidhīyate //
english: Thereupon the king, the Brāhmans and the merchants, thinking that that laughable incident must have been brought about by a sorcerer or some person of that description, made a proclamation, that whoever had made a fool of the bawd, who had deceived innumerable lovers, was to show himself, and he would receive a turban of honour on the spot.

sanskrit: tacchrutvā lohajaṅghaḥ sa tatrātmānamadarśayat / pṛṣṭaścāmūlataḥ sarvaṃ vṛttāntaṃ tamavarṇayat //
english: When he heard that, Lohajaṅgha made himself known to those present, and, being questioned, he related the whole story from its commencement.

sanskrit: dadau ca tatra devāya śaṅkhacakrādyupāyanam / vibhīṣaṇena prahitaṃ janavismayakārakam //
english: And he offered to the god the discus, shell, club and lotus of gold, the present which Vibhīṣaṇa had sent, and which aroused the astonishment of the people.

sanskrit: atha tasya sapadi paṭṭaṃ baddhvā saṃtuṣya māthurāḥ sarve / svādhīnāṃ rūpaṇikāṃ rājādeśena tāṃ cakruḥ //
english: Then all the people of Mathurā, being pleased, immediately invested him with a turban of honour, and by the command of the king made that Rūpiṇikā a free woman.

sanskrit: tataś ca tatra priyayā samaṃ tadā samṛddhakoṣo bahuratnasaṃcayaiḥ / sa lohajaṅghaḥ pratikṛtya kuṭṭanī nikāramanyuṃ nyavasadyathāsukham //
english: And then Lohajaṅgha, having wreaked upon the bawd his wrath caused by her ill usage of him, lived in great comfort in Mathurā with that beloved of his, being very well off by means of the large stock of jewels which he had brought from Laṅkā.

sanskrit: ity anyarūpasya vasantakasya mukhāt samākarṇya kathām avāpi / baddhasya vatsādhipateḥ samīpe toṣaḥ paro vāsavadattayāntaḥ // iti mahākaviśrīsomadevabhaṭṭaviracite kathāsaritsāgare kathāpīṭhalambake caturthas taraṅgaḥ / pañcamas taraṅgaḥ / atha vāsavadattā sā śanairvatseśvaraṃ prati / gāḍhaṃ babandha sadbhāvaṃ pitṛpakṣaparāṅmukhī //
english: [M] (Main story line continued) Hearing this tale from the mouth of the transformed Vasantaka, Vāsavadattā, who was sitting at the side of the fettered King of Vatsa, felt extreme delight in her heart. [M] (Main story line continued) AS time went on Vāsavadattā began to feel a great affection for the King of Vatsa, and to take part with him against her father.

sanskrit: tato vatseśanikaṭaṃ punar yaugandharāyaṇaḥ / viveśādarśanaṃ kṛtvā sarvān anyāñ janān prati //
english: Then Yaugandharāyaṇa again came in to see the King of Vatsa, making himself invisible to all the others who were there.

sanskrit: vasantakasamakṣaṃ ca vijane taṃ vyajijñapat / rājan baddho bhavāṃś caṇḍamahāsenena māyayā //
english: And he gave him the following information in private in the presence of Vasantaka only: “King, you were made captive by King Caṇḍamahāsena by means of an artifice.

sanskrit: sutāṃ ca dattvā saṃmānya tvāmayaṃ moktumicchati / tadasyaināṃ svayaṃ hṛtvā gacchāmastanayāṃ vayam //
english: And he wishes to give you his daughter, and set you at liberty, treating you with all honour; so let us carry off his daughter and escape.

sanskrit: evaṃ hyasya pratīkāro dṛptasya vihito bhavet / apauruṣakṛtaṃ loke naiva syāllāghavaṃ ca vaḥ //
english: For in this way we shall have revenged ourselves upon the haughty monarch, and we shall not be thought lightly of in the world for want of prowess.

sanskrit: asti caitena dattāsyās tanayāyāḥ kareṇukā / rājñā vāsavadattāyā nāmnā bhadravatī nṛpa //
english: Now the king has given that daughter of his, Vāsavadattā, a female elephant called Bhadravatī.

sanskrit: sā cānugantuṃ vegena śaktyā nānyena dantinā / muktvā naḍāgiriṃ so 'pi tāṃ dṛṣṭaiva na yudhyate //
english: And no other elephant but Naḍāgiri is swift enough to catch her up, and he will not fight when he sees her.

sanskrit: tasyaścāṣāḍhako nāma hastyāroho 'tra vidyate / sa ca dattvā dhanaṃ bhūri svīkṛtya sthāpito mayā //
english: The driver of this elephant is a man called Āṣāḍhaka, and him I have won over to our side by giving him much wealth.

sanskrit: tadāruhya kareṇuṃ tāṃ saha vāsavadattayā / sāyudhenāpayātavyaṃ naktaṃ guptamitastvayā //
english: So you must mount that elephant with Vāsavadattā, fully armed, and start from this place secretly by night.

sanskrit: ihatyaśca mahāmātro dviradeṅgitavittadā / madyena kṣībatāṃ neyo naitaccetayate yathā //
english: And you must have the superintendent of the royal elephants here made drunk with wine, in order that he may not perceive what is about to take place,[1] for he understands every sign that elephants give.

sanskrit: pulindakasya sakhyuste pārśvamagre ca yāmyaham / mārgarakṣārthamityuktvā yayau yaugandharāyaṇaḥ //
english: I for my part will first repair to your ally Pulindaka in order that he may be prepared to guard the road by which you escape.” When he had said this, Yaugandharāyaṇa departed.

sanskrit: vatsarājo 'pi tatsarvaṃ kartavyaṃ hṛdaye vyadhāt / atha vāsavadattā sā tasyāntikamupāyayau //
english: So the King of Vatsa stored up all his instructions in his heart; and soon Vāsavadattā came to him.

sanskrit: tatastāstāḥ savisrambhāḥ kathāḥ kurvaṃstayā saha / yaugandharāyaṇoktaṃ ca tasyai rājā śaśaṃsa saḥ //
english: Then he made all kinds of confidential speeches to her, and at last told her what Yaugandharāyaṇa had said to him.

sanskrit: sā ca tatpratipadyaiva niścitya gamanaṃ prati / ānāyyāṣāḍhakaṃ sajjaṃ hastyārohaṃ cakāra tam // devapūjāpadeśena dattvā madyaṃ madānvitam / sarvadhoraṇasaṃyuktaṃ mahāmāraṃ ca sākarot //
english: She consented to the proposal, and made up her mind to start, and causing the elephant-driver Āṣāḍhaka to be summoned, she prepared his mind for the attempt, and, on the pretext of worshipping the gods, she gave the superintendent of the elephants, with all the elephant-drivers, a supply of spirits and made them drunk.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradoṣe vilasanmeghaśabdasamākule / āṣāḍhakaḥ kareṇuṃ tāṃ sajjīkṛtyānināya saḥ // sajjyamānā ca sā śabdaṃ cakāra kariṇī kila / taṃ ca hastirutābhijño mahāmātro 'tha so 'śṛṇot //
english: Then in the evening, which was disturbed with the echoing roar of clouds,[2] Āṣāḍhaka brought that female elephant ready harnessed, but she, while she was being harnessed, uttered a cry, which was heard by the superintendent of the elephants, who was skilled in elephant’s language;

sanskrit: triṣaṣṭiyojanānyadya yāsyāmītyāha hastinī / ityuvāca sa coddāmamadaviskhalitākṣaram // vicārārhaṃ punastasya mattasyābhūnna mānasam / tacca hastipakāḥ kṣībāstadvākyaṃ naiva śuśruvuḥ //
english: and he faltered out in a voice indistinct from excessive intoxication: “The female elephant says she is going sixty-three yojanas to-day.” But his mind in his drunken state was not capable of reasoning, and the elephant-drivers, who were also intoxicated, did not even hear what he said.

sanskrit: tataśca vatsarājo 'tra vīṇāmādāya tāṃ nijām / yaugandharāyaṇātprāptairyogaiḥ sraṃsitabandhanaḥ // upanītapraharaṇaḥ svairaṃ vāsavadattayā / kareṇukāyām ārohat sa tasyāṃ savasantakaḥ //
english: Then the King of Vatsa broke his chains by means of the charms which Yaugandharāyaṇa had given him, and took that lute of his, and Vāsavadattā of her own accord brought him his weapons, and then he mounted the female elephant with Vasantaka.

sanskrit: tato vāsavadattāpi saha kāñcanamālayā / sakhyā rahasyadhāriṇyā tasyāmevāruroha sā //
english: And then Vāsavadattā mounted the same elephant with her friend and confidante Kāñcanamālā;

sanskrit: athojjayinyā niragātsa hastipakapañcamaḥ / vatseśo niśi mattebhabhinnaprākāravartmanā //
english: then the King of Vatsa went out from Ujjayinī with five persons in all, including himself and the elephant-driver, by a path which the infuriated elephant clove through the rampart.

sanskrit: tatsthānarakṣiṇau vīrau svairaṃ sa hatavānnṛpaḥ / vīrabāhuṃ tathā tālabhaṭaṃ rājasutāvubhau //
english: And the king attacked and slew the two warriors who guarded that point, the Rājpūts Vīrabāhu and Tālabhaṭa.

sanskrit: tataḥ pratasthe vegena sa rājā dayitāsakhaḥ / hṛṣṭaḥ kareṇukārūḍho dadhatyāṣāḍhake 'ṅkuśam //
english: Then the monarch set out rapidly on his journey in high spirits, mounted on the female elephant, together with his beloved, Āṣāḍhaka holding the elephant-hook.

sanskrit: ujjayinyāṃ ca tau dṛṣṭvā hatau prākārarakṣiṇau / rājñe nyavedayanrātrau kṣubhitāḥ purarakṣiṇaḥ //
english: In the meanwhile in Ujjayinī the city patrol beheld those guards of the rampart lying dead, and in consternation reported the news to the king at night.

sanskrit: so 'pyanviṣya kramāccaṇḍamahāsenaḥ palāyitam / hṛtavāsavadattaṃ taṃ vatsarājamabudhyata //
english: Caṇḍamahāsena inquired into the matter, and found out at last that the King of Vatsa had escaped, taking Vāsavadattā with him.

sanskrit: tatputraḥ pālakākhyo 'tha jātakolāhale pure / anvadhāvatsa vatseśamadhiruhya naḍāgirim //
english: Then the alarm spread through the city, and one of his sons named Pālaka mounted Naḍāgiri and pursued the King of Vatsa.

sanskrit: vatseśo 'pi tamāyāntaṃ pahi bāṇairayodhayat / naḍāgiriḥ kareṇuṃ tāṃ dṛṣṭvā na prajahāra ca //
english: The King of Vatsa for his part combated him with arrows as he advanced, and Naḍāgiri, seeing that female elephant, would not attack her.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa pālako bhrātrā paścādetya nyavartyata / gopālakena vākyajñaḥ pitṛkāryānurodhinā //
english: Then Pālaka, who was ready to listen to reason, was induced to desist from the pursuit by his brother Gopālaka, who had his father’s interests at heart.

sanskrit: vatsarājo 'pi visrabdhaṃ gantuṃ pravavṛte tataḥ / gacchataścātra śanakaiḥ śarvarī paryahīyata // tato vindhyāṭavīṃ prāpya madhyāhne tasya bhūpateḥ / triṣaṣṭiyojanāyātā tṛṣitābhūtkareṇukā //
english: Then the King of Vatsa boldly continued his journey, and as he journeyed the night gradually came to an end. So by the middle of the day the king had reached the Vindhya forest, and his elephant, having journeyed sixty-three yojanas, was thirsty.

sanskrit: avatīrṇe sabhārye ca rājñi tasmiñjalāni sā / pītvā taddoṣataḥ prāpa pañcatāṃ hastinī kṣaṇāt //
english: So the king and his wife dismounted, and the female elephant having drunk water, owing to its being bad, fell dead on the spot.

sanskrit: viṣaṇṇo 'tha sa vatseśaḥ saha vāsavadattayā / gaganādudgatāmetāṃ śṛṇoti sma sarasvatīm // ahaṃ māyāvatī nāma rājanvidyādharāṅganā / iyantaṃ kālamabhavaṃ śāpadoṣeṇa hastinī //
english: Then the King of Vatsa and Vāsavadattā, in their despair, heard this voice coming from the air: “I, O king, am a female Vidyādhara named Māyāvatī, and for this long time I have been a female elephant in consequence of a curse;

sanskrit: upakāraṃ ca vatseśa tavādya ṛtavatyaham / kariṣyāmi ca bhūyo 'pi tvatputrasya bhaviṣyataḥ // eṣā vāsavadattā ca patnī te naiva mānuṣī / devīyaṃ kāraṇavaśādavatīrṇā kṣitāviti //
english: and to-day, O lord of Vatsa, I have done you a good turn, and I will do another to your son that is to be: and this queen of yours, Vāsavadattā, is not a mere mortal;

sanskrit: tataḥ sa hṛṣṭo vyasṛjadvindhyasānuṃ vasantakam / pulindakāya suhṛde vaktuṃ svāgamanaṃ nṛpaḥ // svayaṃ ca pādacārī sansa śanairdayitānvitaḥ / tatraiva gacchann utthāya dasyubhiḥ paryavāryata //
english: she is a goddess for a certain cause incarnate on the earth.” Then the king regained his spirits, and sent on Vasantaka to the plateau of the Vindhya hills to announce his arrival to his ally Pulindaka; and as he was himself journeying along slowly on foot with his beloved he was surrounded by brigands, who sprang out from an ambuscade.

sanskrit: dhanurdvitīyo dasyūnāṃ teṣāṃ pañcottaraṃ śatam / puro vāsavadattāyā vatsarājaḥ sa cāvadhīt //
english: And the king, with only his bow to help him, slew one hundred and five of them before the eyes of Vāsavadattā.

sanskrit: tatkṣaṇaṃ so 'sya rājño 'tra mittraṃ cāgātpulindakaḥ / yaugandharāyaṇasakho vasantakapuraḥsaraḥ //
english: And immediately the king’s ally Pulindaka came up, together with Yaugandharāyaṇa, Vasantaka showing them the way.

sanskrit: sa tāndasyūnnivāryānyānvatseśaṃ praṇipatya tam / nayati sma nijāṃ pallīṃ bhillarājaḥ savallabham //
english: The King of the Bheels ordered the surviving brigands[3] to desist, and after prostrating himself before the King of Vatsa, conducted him with his beloved to his own village.

sanskrit: tatra tāṃ rātrimāraṇyadarbhapāṭitapādayā / sa vatseśo viśaśrāsa saha vāsavadattayā // prātaḥ senāpatiś cāsya rumaṇvān prāpadantikam / yaugandharāyaṇena prāgdūtaṃ saṃpreṣya bodhitaḥ //
english: The king rested there that night with Vāsavadattā, whose foot had been cut with a blade of forest grass, and early in the morning the General Rumaṇvat reached him, who had before been summoned by Yaugandharāyaṇa, who sent a messenger to him.

sanskrit: agācca kaṭakaṃ sarvaṃ tathā vyāptadigantaram / yathā vindhyāṭavī prāpa sā saṃbādharasajñatām //
english: And the whole army came with him, filling the land as far as the eye could reach, so that the Vindhya forest appeared to be besieged.

sanskrit: praviśya kaṭake tasmiṃstasyāmevāṭavībhuvi / tasthāvujjayinīvārtāṃ jñātuṃ vatseśvaro 'tha saḥ //
english: So that King of Vatsa entered into the encampment of his army, and remained in that wild region to wait for news from Ujjayinī.

sanskrit: tatrasthaṃ ca tamabhyāgādujjayinyā vaṇiktadā / yaugandharāyaṇasuhṛtsa cāgatyābravīdidam // deva caṇḍamahāsenaḥ prīto jāmātari tvayi / preṣitaśca pratīhārasteneha bhavadantikam //
english: And while he was there a merchant came from Ujjayinī, a friend of Yaugandharāyaṇa’s, and when he had arrived reported these tidings: “The King Caṇḍamahāsena is pleased to have thee for a son-in-law, and he has sent his warder to thee.

sanskrit: sa cāgacchansthitaḥ paścādahamagrata eva tu / pracchannaḥ satvaraṃ devaṃ vijñāpayitumāgataḥ // etacchrutvā sa vatseśo jaharṣa ca śaśaṃsa ca / sarvaṃ vāsavadattāyāḥ sāpi harṣamagātparam //
english: however, I came secretly on in front of him, as fast as I could, to bring your Highness information.” When he heard this the King of Vatsa rejoiced, and told it all to Vāsavadattā, and she was exceedingly delighted.

sanskrit: kṛtabandhuparityāgā vivāhavidhisatvarā / atha vāsavadattā sā salajjā cotsukā tathā // tataḥ svātmavinodāya nikaṭasthaṃ vasantakam / sā jagāda kathā kācittvayā me varṇyatāmiti // sa ca mugdhadṛśastasyā bhartṛbhaktivivardhinīm / vasantakastadā dhīmānimāmakathayatkathām //
english: Then Vāsavadattā, having abandoned her own relations, and being anxious for the ceremony of marriage, was at the same time bashful and impatient: then she said, in order to divert her thoughts, to Vasantaka, who was in attendance: “Tell me some story.” Then the sagacious Vasantaka told that fair-eyed one the following tale in order to increase her affection for her husband.

sanskrit: astīha nagarī loke tāmraliptīti viśrutā / tasyāṃ ca dhanadattākhyo vaṇigāsīnmadhādhanaḥ //
english: There is a city in the world famous under the name of Tāmraliptā, and in that city there was a very rich merchant named Dhanadatta.

sanskrit: sa cāputro bahūnviprānsaṃghaṭya praṇato 'bravīt / tathā kuruta putro me yathā syādacirāditi // tatas tam ūcur viprāste naitat kiṃcana duṣkaram / sarvaṃ hi sādhayantīha dvijāḥ śrautena karmaṇā //
english: And he, being childless, assembled many Brāhmans and said to them with due respect: “Take such steps as will procure me a son soon.” Then those Brāhmans said to him: “This is not at all difficult, for Brāhmans can accomplish all things in this world by means of ceremonies in accordance with the scriptures.

sanskrit: tathā ca pūrvamabhavadrāja kaścidaputrakaḥ / pañcottaraṃ śataṃ cābhūttasyāntaḥpurayoṣitām //
english: To give you an instance, there was in old time a king who had no sons, and he had a hundred and five wives in his harem.

sanskrit: putrīyeṣṭyā ca tasyaiko janturnāma suto 'jani / tatpatnīnāmaśeṣāṇāṃ nūtanendūdayo dṛśi // jānubhyāṃ paryaṭantaṃ ca bālaṃ jātu pipīlikā / urūdeśe dadaṃśainaṃ muktacūtkārakātaram //
english: And by means of a sacrifice to procure a son there was born to him a son named Jantu, who was like the rising of the new moon to the eyes of his wives. Once on a time an ant bit the boy on the thigh as he was crawling about on his knees, so that he was very un-happy and sobbed loudly.

sanskrit: tāvatā tumulākrandamantaḥ puramajāyata / rājāpi putra putreti cikranda prākṛto yathā //
english: Thereupon the whole harem was full of confused lamentation, and the king himself shrieked out, ‘My son! my son!’ like a common man.

sanskrit: kṣaṇāttasminsamāśvaste bāle 'pāstapipīlike / duḥkhaikakāraṇaṃ rājā sa ninindaikaputratām //
english: The boy was soon comforted, the ant having been removed, and the king blamed the misfortune of his only having one son as the cause of all his grief.

sanskrit: asti kaścidupāyo me yena syurbahavaḥ sutāḥ / iti tatparitāpena papraccha brāhmaṇāṃśca saḥ //
english: And he asked the Brāhmans in his affliction if there was any expedient by which he might obtain a large number of children.

sanskrit: te taṃ pratyabruvanrājannupāyo 'tra tavāstyayam / havaitaṃ tvatsutaṃ vahnau tanmāsaṃ hūyate 'khilam // tadgandhāghrāṇato rājñyaḥ sarvāḥ prāpsyanti te sutān / etac chrutvā sa rājā tat tathā sarvam akārayat //
english: They answered him: ‘O king, there is one expedient open to you: you must slay this son and offer up all his flesh in the fire.[4] By smelling the smell of that sacrifice all thy wives will obtain sons.’ When he heard that, the king had the whole ceremony performed as they directed;

sanskrit: svapatnīsamasaṃkhyāṃś ca sa putrān prāptavān nṛpaḥ / atas tavāpi homena sādhayāmo vayaṃ sutam // ityuktvā dhanadattaṃ te brāhmaṇāḥ kḷptadakṣiṇam / homaṃ cakrustatastasya vaṇijo jātavānsutaḥ //
english: So we can obtain a son for you also by a burnt-offering.” When they had said this to Dhanadatta, the Brāhmans, after a sacrificial fee had been promised them, performed a sacrifice: then a son was born to that merchant. That son was called Guhasena, and he gradually grew up to man’s estate.

sanskrit: guhasenābhidhānaśca sa balo vavṛdhe kramāt / pitātha dhanadatto 'sya bhāryāmanviṣyati sma saḥ // tataḥ sa tatpitā tena tanayena samaṃ yayau / dvīpāntaraṃ snuṣāhetorvaṇijyāvyapadeśataḥ //
english: Then his father Dhanadatta began to look out for a wife for him. Then his father went with that son of his to another country, on the pretence of traffic, but really to get a daughter-in-law;

sanskrit: tatra devasmitāṃ nāma dharmaguptādvaṇigvarāt / svaputraguhasenasya kṛte kanyāmayācata //
english: there he asked an excellent merchant of the name of Dharmagupta to give him his daughter named Devasmitā for his son Guhasena.

sanskrit: dharmaguptastu saṃbandhaṃ na tamaṅgīcakāra saḥ / ālocya tāmraliptīṃ tāṃ durāṃ duhitṛvatsalaḥ //
english: But Dharmagupta, who was tenderly attached to his daughter, did not approve of that connection, reflecting that the city of Tāmraliptā was very far off.

sanskrit: sā tu devasmitā dṛṣṭvā guhasenaṃ tadaiva tam / tadguṇākṛṣṭacittatvādbandhutyāgaikaniścayā // sakhīmukhena kṛtvā ca saṃketaṃ saha tena sā / priyeṇa pitṛyuktena rātrau dvīpāttato yayau //
english: But when Devasmitā beheld that Guhasena, her mind was immediately attracted by his virtues, and she was set on abandoning her relations, and so she made an assignation with him by means of a confidante, and went away from that country at night with her beloved and his father.

sanskrit: tāmraliptīmatha prāpya tayoḥ kṛtavivāhayoḥ / jāyāpatyormithaḥ premapāśabaddhamabhūnmanaḥ //
english: When they reached Tāmraliptā they were married, and the minds of the young couple were firmly knit together by the bond of mutual love.

sanskrit: athāstaṃ pitari prāpte prerito 'bhūtsa bandhubhiḥ / kaṭāhadvīpagamane guhaseno yadṛcchayā //
english: Then Guhasena’s father died, and he himself was urged by his relations to go to the country of Kaṭāha [see notes on the identification of Kaṭāha] for the purpose of trafficking;

sanskrit: taccāsya gamanaṃ bhāryā tadā nāṅgīcakāra sā / serṣyā devasmitā kāmamanyastrīsaṅgaśaṅkinī //
english: but his wife Devasmitā was too jealous to approve of that expedition, fearing exceedingly that he would be attracted by some other lady.

sanskrit: tataḥ patnyāmanicchantyāṃ prerayatsu ca bandhuṣu / kartavyaniścalo mūḍho guhaseno babhūva saḥ //
english: Then, as his wife did not approve of it, and his relations kept inciting him to it, Guhasena, whose mind was firmly set on doing his duty, was bewildered.

sanskrit: aha gatvā nirāhāraścakre devakule vratam / upāyamiha devo me nirdiśatviti cintayan // sāpi devasmitā tadvattena sārdhaṃ vyadhādvratam / tato 'nayoḥ śivaḥ svapne daṃpatyordarśanaṃ dadau //
english: Then he went and performed a vow in the temple of the god, observing a rigid fast, trusting that the god would show him some way out of his difficulty. And his wife Devasmitā also performed a vow with him. Then Śiva was pleased to appear to that couple in a dream;

sanskrit: dve ca raktāmbuje dattvā sa devastāvabhāṣata / haste gṛhṇītamekaikaṃ padmametadubhāvapi //
english: and giving them two red lotuses, the god said to them: “Take each of you one of these lotuses in your hand.

sanskrit: dūrasthatve ca yadyekaḥ śīlatyāgaṃ kariṣyati / tadanyasya kare padmaṃ mlānimeṣyati nānyathā // etacchrutvā prabudhyaiva daṃpatī tāvapaśyatām / anyonyasyeva hṛdayaṃ hastasthaṃ raktamambujam //
english: And if either of you shall be unfaithful during your separation the lotus in the hand of the other shall fade, but not otherwise.”[5] After hearing this the two woke up, and each beheld in the hand of the other a red lotus, and it seemed as if they had got one another’s hearts.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa cakre prasthānaṃ guhaseno dhṛtāmbujaḥ / sā tu devasmitātatra tasthau padmārpitekṣaṇā //
english: Then Guhasena set out, lotus in hand, but Devasmitā remained in the house with her eyes fixed upon her flower.

sanskrit: guhaseno 'pi taṃ prāpa kaṭāhadvīpamāśu saḥ / kartuṃ pravavṛte cātra ratnānāṃ krayavikrayau //
english: Guhasena for his part quickly reached the country of Kaṭāha, and began to buy and sell jewels there.

sanskrit: haste ca tasya taddṛṣṭvā sadaivāmlānamambujam / atra kecidvaṇikputrāścatvāro vismayaṃ yayuḥ //
english: And four young merchants in that country, seeing that that unfading lotus was ever in his hand, were greatly astonished.

sanskrit: te yuktyā taṃ gṛhaṃ nītvā pāyayitvā bhṛśaṃ madhu / papracchuḥ padmavṛttāntaṃ so 'pi kṣībaḥ śaśaṃsa tam //
english: Accordingly they got him to their house by an artifice, and made him drink a great deal of wine, and then asked him the history of the lotus, and he being intoxicated told them the whole story.

sanskrit: tatastaṃ ciranirvāhyaratnādikrayavikrayam / vicintya guhasenaṃ te catvāro 'pi vaṇiksutāḥ // saṃmantrya kautukātpāpāstadbhāryāśīlaviplavam / cikīrṣavo yayuḥ śīghraṃ tāmraliptīmalakṣitāḥ //
english: Then those four young merchants, knowing that Guhasena would take a long time to complete his sales and purchases of jewels and other wares, planned together, like rascals as they were, the seduction of his wife out of curiosity, and eager to accomplish it, set out quickly for Tāmraliptā without their departure being noticed.

sanskrit: tatropāyaṃ vicinvantaḥ sugatāyatanasthitām / pravrājikāmupājagmurnāmnā yogakaraṇḍikām //
english: There they cast about for some instrument, and at last had recourse to a female ascetic of the name of Yogakaraṇḍikā, who lived in a sanctuary of Buddha;

sanskrit: prītipūrvaṃ ca tām ūcur bhagavaty asmadīpsitam / sādhyate cet tvayā tat te dāsyāmo 'rthān bahūn iti // sāpyuvāca dhruvaṃ yūnāṃ kāpi strī vāñchiteha vaḥ / tadbhūta sādhayāmyeva dhanalipsā ca nāsti me //
english: and they said to her in an affectionate manner: “Reverend madam, if our object is accomplished by your help we will give you much wealth.” She answered them: “No doubt you young men desire some woman in this city, so tell me all about it, I will procure you the object of your desire; but I have no wish for money.

sanskrit: asti siddhikarī nāma śiṣyā me buddhiśālinī / atprasādena saṃprāptamasaṃkhyaṃ hi dhanaṃ mayā //
english: I have a pupil of distinguished ability named Siddhikarī;

sanskrit: kathaṃ śiṣyāprasādena bhūri prāptaṃ dhanaṃ tvayā / iti taiḥ sā vaṇikputraiḥ pṛṣṭā pravrājikābravīt // kautukaṃ yadi tatputrāḥ śrūyatāṃ varṇayāmi vaḥ / iha ko'pi vaṇikpūrvamāyayāvuttarāpathāt //
english: owing to her kindness I have obtained untold wealth.” The young merchants asked: “How have you obtained untold wealth by the assistance of a pupil?” Being asked this question, the female ascetic said: “If you feel any curiosity about the matter, listen, my sons, I will tell you the whole story: Long ago a certain merchant came here from the north;

sanskrit: tasyehasthasya macchiṣyā sā gatvā śiśriye gṛhe / yuktyā karmakarībhāvaṃ kṛtarūpavivartanā //
english: while he was dwelling here my pupil went and obtained, with a treacherous object, the position of a serving-maid in his house, having first altered her appearance;

sanskrit: viśvāsya vaṇijaṃ taṃ ca tadgṛhātsvarṇasaṃcayam / sarvaṃ muṣitvā pracchannaṃ pratyūṣe sātha niryayau //
english: and after she had gained the confidence of that merchant she stole all his hoard of gold from his house and went off secretly in the morning twilight.

sanskrit: nagarīnirgatāṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṅkāśīghragatiṃ ca tām / mṛdaṅgahasto moṣāya ḍombaḥ ko 'pyanvagāddrutam //
english: And as she went out from the city, moving rapidly through fear, a certain Ḍomba,[6] with his drum in his hand, saw her, and pursued her at full speed with the intention of robbing her.

sanskrit: nyagrodhasya talaṃ prāpya sā dṛṣṭvā tamupāgatam / ḍombaṃ siddhikarī dhūrtā sadainyevedamabravīt // bhartrā sahādya kalahaṃ kṛtvāhaṃ nigatā gṛhāt / martuṃ tadbhadra pāśo 'tra tvayā me badhyatāmiti //
english: When she had reached the foot of a Nyagrodha tree she saw that he had come up with her, and so the cunning Siddhikarī said this to him in a plaintive manner: “I have had a jealous quarrel with my husband, and I have left his house to die, therefore, my good man, make a noose for me to hang myself with.” Then the Ḍomba thought: “Let her hang herself.

sanskrit: pāśena mriyatāmeṣā kimenāṃ hanmyahaṃ striyam / matveti tatra vṛkṣe 'sau ḍombaḥ pāśamasajjayat //
english: Why should I be guilty of her death, especially as she is a woman?” and so he fastened a noose for her to the tree.

sanskrit: tataḥ siddhikarī ḍombaṃ sā mugdheva jagāda tam / kriyate kathamudbandhastvayā medarśyatāmiti // tataḥ sa ḍombas taṃ dattvā mṛdaṅgaṃ pādayoradhaḥ / itthaṃ kriyata ityuktvā svakaṇṭhe pāśamarpayat //
english: Then Siddhikarī, feigning ignorance, said to the Ḍomba: “How is the noose slipped round the neck? Show me, I entreat you.” Then the Ḍomba placed the drum under his feet, and saying, “This is the way we do the trick,” he fastened the noose round his own throat.

sanskrit: sāpi siddhikarī sadyastaṃ mṛdaṅgamacūrṇayat / pādāghātena ḍombo 'tha so 'pi pāśe vyapadyata // tatkālamāgato 'nveṣṭuṃ vṛkṣamūle dadarśa saḥ / muṣitāśeṣakoṣāṃ tāṃ dūrātsiddhikarīṃ vaṇik //
english: Siddhikarī for her part smashed the drum to atoms with a kick, and that Ḍomba hung till he was dead.[7] At that moment the merchant arrived in search of her, and beheld from a distance Siddhikarī, who had stolen from him untold treasures, at the foot of the tree.

sanskrit: sāpi dṛṣṭvā tamāyāntaṃ vṛkṣe tasminnalakṣitam / āruhya tasthau śākhāyāṃ pattraughacchannavigrahā //
english: She too saw him coming, and climbed up the tree without being noticed, and remained there on a bough, having her body concealed by the dense foliage.

sanskrit: sa cāgatya vaṇigyāvatsabhṛtyaḥ pāśabandhanam / ḍombameva tamadrākṣīnna tu siddhikarīṃ kvacit //
english: When the merchant came up with his servants he saw the Ḍomba hanging by his neck, but Siddhikarī was nowhere to be seen.

sanskrit: mā nāma vṛkṣamārūḍhā sā bhavediti tatkṣaṇam / eko 'sya vaṇijo bhṛtyastarumārohati sma tam //
english: Immediately one of his servants said, “I wonder whether she has got up this tree,” and proceeded to ascend it himself.

sanskrit: sadā tvayyeva me prītirihārūḍhastvameva ca / tatsundara tavaivedaṃ dhanamehi bhajasva mām //
english: Then Siddhikarī said: “I have always loved you, and now you have climbed up where I am, so all this wealth is at your disposal, handsome man;

sanskrit: ityuktvāliṅgya cumbantī sāsya siddhikarī mukham / vaṇigbhṛtyasya daśanairjihvāṃ mūḍhadhiyo 'cchinat //
english: come and embrace me.” So she embraced the merchant’s servant, and as she was kissing his mouth she bit off the fool’s tongue.

sanskrit: sa papāta vyathākrānto mukhena rudhiraṃ vaman / vṛkṣāttasmāllalalleti kimapyaprasphuṭaṃ bruvan // taddṛṣṭvā sa vaṇigbhīto bhūtagrastamavetya tam / svagṛhaṃ bhṛtyasahitaḥ palāyyaiva tato yayau //
english: He, overcome with pain, fell from that tree, spitting blood from his mouth, uttering some indistinct syllables, which sounded like “Lalalla.” When he saw that, the merchant was terrified, and supposing that his servant had been seized by a demon, he fled from that place, and went to his own house with his attendants.

sanskrit: athāvatīrya vṛkṣāgrāttadvadbhītā ca tāpasī / āgādgṛhaṃ samādāya tatsā siddhikarī dhanam //
english: Then Siddhikarī, the female ascetic, equally frightened, descended from the top of the tree, and brought home with her all that wealth.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhā hi macchiṣyā bahuprajñānaśālinī / evaṃ ca tatprasādena putrāḥ prāptaṃ mayā dhanam //
english: Such a person is my pupil, distinguished for her great discernment, and it is in this way, my sons, that I have obtained wealth by her kindness.

sanskrit: ityuktvā tānvaṇikputrānatha pravrājikā nijām / tatkālamāgatāṃ śiṣyāmetebhyastāmadarśayat // jagāda caitāṃs tatputrāḥ sadbhāvaṃ vadatādhunā / kāṃ striyaṃ vāñchatha kṣipraṃ tāmahaṃ sādhayāmi vaḥ // tacchrutvā te ca tāmūcuryaiṣā devasmitābhidhā / guhasenavaṇigbhāryā tayā naḥ saṃgamaṃ kuru // śrutveti pratijajñe tatkāryaṃ pravrājikātha sā / vaṇiksutānāṃ caiteṣāṃ svagṛhaṃ sthitaye dadau //
english: When she had said this to the young merchants the female ascetic showed to them her pupil, who happened to come in at that moment, and said to them: “Now, my sons, tell me the real state of affairs—what woman do you desire? I will quickly procure her for you.” When they heard that they said: “Procure us an interview with the wife of the merchant Guhasena named Devasmitā.” When she heard that, the ascetic undertook to manage that business for them, and she gave those young merchants her own house to reside in.

sanskrit: rañjayitvātha tatratyaṃ janaṃ bhakṣyādidānataḥ / guhasenagṛhaṃ tatsā viveśa saha śiṣyayā //
english: Then she gratified the servants at Guhasena’s house with gifts of sweetmeats and other things, and afterwards entered it with her pupil.

sanskrit: tato devasmitāvāsagṛhadvāramupāgatām / tāṃ śunī śṛṅkhalābaddhā rurodhāpūrvarodhinī //
english: Then, as she approached the private rooms of Devasmitā, a bitch, that was fastened there with a chain, would not let her come near, but opposed her entrance in the most determined way.

sanskrit: tato devasmitā dṛṣṭvā sā tāṃ prāveśayatsvayam / kim āgatā syād eṣeti vicintya preṣya ceṭikām // praviṣṭā cāśiṣaṃ dattvā kṛtvā vyājakṛtādarām / sā tāṃ devasmitāṃ sādhvīṃ pāpā pravrājikābravīt // sadaiva tvaddidṛkṣā me bhavatyadya punarmayā / svapne dṛṣṭāsi tenāhamutkā tvāṃ draṣṭumāgatā //
english: Then Devasmitā seeing her, of her own accord sent a maid, and had her brought in, thinking to herself: “What can this person be come for?” After she had entered, the wicked ascetic gave Devasmitā her blessing, and, treating the virtuous woman with affected respect, said to her: “I have always had a desire to see you, but to-day I saw you in a dream, therefore I have come to visit you with impatient eagerness;

sanskrit: bhartrā vinākṛtāṃ tvāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā me dūyate manaḥ / priyopabhogavandhye hi viphale rūpayauvane // ityādibhirvacobhistāṃ sādhvīmāśvāsya sā ciram / āmantrya cāyayau tāvadgṛhaṃ pravrājikā nijam //
english: and my mind is afflicted at beholding you separated from your husband, for beauty and youth are wasted when one is deprived of the society of one’s beloved.” With this and many other speeches of the same kind she tried to gain the confidence of the virtuous woman in a short interview, and then taking leave of her she returned to her own house.

sanskrit: dvitīye 'hni gṛhītvā ca maricakṣodanirbharam / māṃsakhaṇḍaṃ punaḥ sā tadyayau devasmitāgṛham // dvāraśunyai dadau tasyai māṃsakhaṇḍaṃ ca tatra tam / sāpi taṃ bhakṣayāmāsa sadyaḥ samaricaṃ śunī //
english: On the second day she took with her a piece of meat full of pepper dust, and went again to the house of Devasmitā, and there she gave that piece of meat to the bitch at the door, and the bitch gobbled it up, pepper and all.

sanskrit: tato maricadoṣeṇa tasyā dṛgbhyāmavāritam / aśru pravavṛte tasyāḥ prasnauti sma ca nāsikā //
english: Then owing to the pepper dust the tears flowed in profusion from the animal’s eyes, and her nose began to run.

sanskrit: sāpi pravrājikā tasmin kṣaṇe devasmitāntikam / praviśya tatkṛtātithyā prārebhe rodituṃ śaṭhā //
english: And the cunning ascetic immediately went into the apartment of Devasmitā, who received her hospitably, and began to cry.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭā ca devasmitayā sā kṛcchrādevamabravīt / putri saṃprati paśyaitāṃ bahiḥ prarudatīṃ śunīm // eṣā hyadya parijñāya māṃ janmāntarasaṃgatām / pravṛttā rodituṃ tena kṛpayāśru mamodgatam // tacchrutvā bahirālokya śunīṃ tāṃ rudatīmiva / kimetaccitramiti sā dadhyau devasmitā kṣaṇam // pravrājikātha sāvādītputri pūrvatra janmani / ahameṣā ca bhārye dve viprasyābhūva kasyacit //
english: When Devasmitā asked her why she shed tears she said with affected reluctance: “My friend, look at this bitch weeping outside here.[8] This creature recognised me to-day as having been its companion in a former birth, and began to weep; for that reason my tears gushed through pity.” When she heard that, and saw that bitch outside apparently weeping, Devasmitā thought for a moment to herself: “What can be the meaning of this wonderful sight?” Then the ascetic said to her: “My daughter, in a former birth I and that bitch were the two wives of a certain Brāhman.

sanskrit: sa cāvayoḥ patirdūraṃ deśāntaramitastataḥ / vāraṃ vāraṃ prayāti sma rājādeśena dūtyayā //
english: And our husband frequently went about to other countries on embassies by order of the king.

sanskrit: tatpravāse ca kurvantyā svecchaṃ puruṣasaṃgamam / mayā bhūtendriyagrāmo nopabhogairavañcyata //
english: Now while he was away from home I lived with other men at my pleasure, and so did not cheat the elements, of which I was composed, and my senses, of their lawful enjoyment.

sanskrit: bhūtendriyānabhidroho dharmo hi paramo mataḥ / ato jātismarā putri jātāhamiha janmani //
english: For considerate treatment of the elements and senses is held to be the highest duty. Therefore I have been born in this birth with a recollection of my former existence.

sanskrit: eṣā tu śīlamevaikaṃ rarakṣājñānatastadā / tena śvayonau patitā kiṃ tu jātiṃ smaratyasau //
english: But she in her former life, through ignorance, confined all her attention to the preservation of her character, therefore she has been degraded and born again as one of the canine race;

sanskrit: ko 'yaṃ dharmo dhruvaṃ dhūrtaracaneyaṃ kṛtānayā / iti saṃcintya suprajñā sā tāṃ devasmitābravīt //
english: however, she too remembers her former birth.” The wise Devasmitā said to herself: “This is a novel conception of duty;

sanskrit: patim prayāntam subalasya putrī pati vratā ca anujagāma sādhvī himālayam nyasta daṇḍa praharṣam manasvinām iva sat samprahāraḥ
english: The gentle and chaste Gāndhārī, who was the daughter of King Subala of Kandahar [or Gāndhāra], followed her husband, seeing that he was going to the Himālaya Mountains, which are the delight of those who have accepted the staff of the renounced order like fighters who have accepted a good lashing from the enemy.

sanskrit: ajāta śatruḥ kṛta maitraḥ huta agniḥ viprān natvā tila go bhūmi rukmaiḥ gṛham praviṣṭaḥ guru vandanāya na ca apaśyat pitarau saubalīm ca
english: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, whose enemy was never born, performed his daily morning duties by praying, offering fire sacrifice to the sun-god, and offering obeisances, grains, cows, land and gold to the brāhmaṇas. He then entered the palace to pay respects to the elderly. However, he could not find his uncles or aunt, the daughter of King Subala.

sanskrit: tatra sañjayam āsīnam papraccha udvigna mānasaḥ gāvalgaṇe kva naḥ tātaḥ vṛddhaḥ hīnaḥ ca netrayoḥ
english: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, full of anxiety, turned to Sañjaya, who was sitting there, and said: O Sañjaya, where is our uncle, who is old and blind?

sanskrit: ambā ca hata putrā ārtā pitṛvyaḥ kva gataḥ suhṛt api mayi akṛta prajñe hata bandhuḥ saḥ bhāryayā āśaṁsamānaḥ śamalam gaṅgāyām duḥkhitaḥ apatat
english: Where is my well-wisher, uncle Vidura, and mother Gāndhārī, who is very afflicted due to all her sons’ demise? My uncle Dhṛtarāṣṭra was also very mortified due to the death of all his sons and grandsons. Undoubtedly I am very ungrateful. Did he, therefore, take my offenses very seriously and, along with his wife, drown himself in the Ganges?

sanskrit: pitari uparate pāṇḍau sarvān naḥ suhṛdaḥ śiśūn arakṣatām vyasanataḥ pitṛvyau kva gatau itaḥ
english: When my father, Pāṇḍu, fell down and we were all small children, these two uncles gave us protection from all kinds of calamities. They were always our good well-wishers. Alas, where have they gone from here?

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca kṛpayā sneha vaiklavyāt sūtaḥ viraha karśitaḥ ātma īśvaram acakṣāṇaḥ na pratyāha ati pīḍitaḥ
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Because of compassion and mental agitation, Sañjaya, not having seen his own master, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, was aggrieved and could not properly reply to Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: vimṛjya aśrūṇi pāṇibhyām viṣṭabhya ātmānam ātmanā ajāta śatrum pratyūce prabhoḥ pādau anusmaran
english: First he slowly pacified his mind by intelligence, and wiping away his tears and thinking of the feet of his master, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, he began to reply to Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: sañjayaḥ uvāca na aham veda vyavasitam pitroḥ vaḥ kula nandana gāndhāryāḥ vā mahā bāho muṣitaḥ asmi mahā ātmabhiḥ
english: Sañjaya said: My dear descendant of the Kuru dynasty, I have no information of the determination of your two uncles and Gāndhārī. O King, I have been cheated by those great souls.

sanskrit: atha ājagāma bhagavān nāradaḥ saha tumburuḥ pratyutthāya abhivādya āha sa anujaḥ abhyarcayan munim
english: While Sañjaya was thus speaking, Śrī Nārada, the powerful devotee of the Lord, appeared on the scene carrying his tumburu. Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira and his brothers received him properly by getting up from their seats and offering obeisances.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca na aham veda gatim pitroḥ bhagavan kva gatau itaḥ ambā vā hata putrā ārtā kva gatā ca tapasvinī
english: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira said: O godly personality, I do not know where my two uncles have gone. Nor can I find my ascetic aunt who is griefstricken by the loss of all her sons.

sanskrit: karṇa dhāraḥ iva apāre bhagavān pāra darśakaḥ atha ābabhāṣe bhagavān nāradaḥ muni sat tamaḥ
english: You are like a captain of a ship in a great ocean and you can direct us to our destination. Thus addressed, the godly personality, Devarṣi Nārada, greatest of the philosopher devotees, began to speak.

sanskrit: nāradaḥ uvāca mā kañcana śucaḥ rājan yat īśvara vaśam jagat lokāḥ sa pālāḥ yasya ime vahanti balim īśituḥ saḥ saṁyunakti bhūtāni saḥ eva viyunakti ca
english: Śrī Nārada said: O pious King, do not lament for anyone, for everyone is under the control of the Supreme Lord. Therefore all living beings and their leaders carry on worship to be well protected. It is He only who brings them together and disperses them.

sanskrit: yathā gāvaḥ nasi protāḥ tantyām baddhāḥ ca dāmabhiḥ vāk tantyām nāmabhiḥ baddhāḥ vahanti balim īśituḥ
english: As a cow, bound through the nose by a long rope, is conditioned, so also human beings are bound by different Vedic injunctions and are conditioned to obey the orders of the Supreme.

sanskrit: yathā krīḍa upaskarāṇām saṁyoga vigamau iha icchayā krīḍituḥ syātām tathā eva īśa icchayā nṛṇām
english: As a player sets up and disperses his playthings according to his own sweet will, so the supreme will of the Lord brings men together and separates them.

sanskrit: yat manyase dhruvam lokam adhruvam vā na ca ubhayam sarvathā na hi śocyāḥ te snehāt anyatra moha jāt
english: O King, in all circumstances, whether you consider the soul to be an eternal principle, or the material body to be perishable, or everything to exist in the impersonal Absolute Truth, or everything to be an inexplicable combination of matter and spirit, feelings of separation are due only to illusory affection and nothing more.

sanskrit: tasmāt jahi aṅga vaiklavyam ajñāna kṛtam ātmanaḥ katham tu anāthāḥ kṛpaṇāḥ varteran te ca mām vinā
english: Therefore give up your anxiety due to ignorance of the self. You are now thinking of how they, who are helpless poor creatures, will exist without you.

sanskrit: kāla karma guṇa adhīnaḥ dehaḥ ayam pāñca bhautikaḥ katham anyān tu gopāyet sarpa grastaḥ yathā param
english: This gross material body made of five elements is already under the control of eternal time [kāla], action [karma] and the modes of material nature [guṇa]. How then can it, being already in the jaws of the serpent, protect others?

sanskrit: ahastāni sa hastānām apadāni catuḥ padām phalgūni tatra mahatām jīvaḥ jīvasya jīvanam
english: Those who are devoid of hands are prey for those who have hands; those devoid of legs are prey for the four-legged. The weak are the subsistence of the strong, and the general rule holds that one living being is food for another.

sanskrit: tat idam bhagavān rājan ekaḥ ātmā ātmanām sva dṛk antaraḥ anantaraḥ bhāti paśya tam māyayā urudhā
english: Therefore, O King, you should look to the Supreme Lord only, who is one without a second and who manifests Himself by different energies and is both within and without.

sanskrit: saḥ ayam adya mahārāja bhagavān bhūta bhāvanaḥ kāla rūpaḥ avatīrṇaḥ asyām abhāvāya sura dviṣām
english: That Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, in the guise of all-devouring time [kāla-rūpa] has now descended to the earth to eliminate the envious from the world.

sanskrit: niṣpāditam deva kṛtyam avaśeṣam pratīkṣate tāvat yūyam avekṣadhvam bhavet yāvat iha īśvaraḥ
english: The Lord has already performed His duties to help the demigods, and He is awaiting the rest. You Pāṇḍavas may wait as long as the Lord is here on earth.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ saha bhrātrā gāndhāryā ca sva bhāryayā dakṣiṇena himavataḥ ṛṣīṇām āśramam gataḥ
english: O King, your uncle Dhṛtarāṣṭra, his brother Vidura and his wife Gāndhārī have gone to the southern side of the Himālaya Mountains, where there are shelters of the great sages.

sanskrit: srotobhiḥ saptabhiḥ yā vai svardhunī saptadhā vyadhāt saptānām prītaye nānā sapta srotaḥ pracakṣate
english: The place is called Saptasrota [“divided by seven”] because there the waters of the sacred Ganges were divided into seven branches. This was done for the satisfaction of the seven great ṛṣis.

sanskrit: snātvā anusavanam tasmin hutvā ca agnīn yathā vidhi ap bhakṣaḥ upaśānta ātmā saḥ āste vigata eṣaṇaḥ
english: On the banks at Saptasrota, Dhṛtarāṣṭra is now engaged in beginning aṣṭāṅga-yoga by bathing three times daily, in the morning, noon and evening, by performing the Agni-hotra sacrifice with fire and by drinking only water. This helps one control the mind and the senses and frees one completely from thoughts of familial affection.

sanskrit: jita āsanaḥ jita śvāsaḥ pratyāhṛta ṣaṭ indriyaḥ hari bhāvanayā dhvasta rajaḥ sattva tamaḥ malaḥ
english: One who has controlled the sitting postures [the yogic āsanas] and the breathing process can turn the senses toward the Absolute Personality of Godhead and thus become immune to the contaminations of the modes of material nature, namely mundane goodness, passion and ignorance.

sanskrit: vijñāna ātmani saṁyojya kṣetra jñe pravilāpya tam brahmaṇi ātmānam ādhāre ghaṭa ambaram iva ambare
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra will have to amalgamate his pure identity with intelligence and then merge into the Supreme Being with knowledge of his qualitative oneness, as a living entity, with the Supreme Brahman. Being freed from the blocked sky, he will have to rise to the spiritual sky.

sanskrit: dhvasta māyā guṇa udarkaḥ niruddha karaṇa āśayaḥ nivartita akhila āhāraḥ āste sthāṇuḥ iva acalaḥ tasya antarāyaḥ mā eva abhūḥ sannyasta akhila karmaṇaḥ
english: He will have to suspend all the actions of the senses, even from the outside, and will have to be impervious to interactions of the senses, which are influenced by the modes of material nature. After renouncing all material duties, he must become immovably established, beyond all sources of hindrances on the path.

sanskrit: saḥ vā adya tanāt rājan parataḥ pañcame ahani kalevaram hāsyati svam tat ca bhasmī bhaviṣyati
english: O King, he will quit his body, most probably on the fifth day from today. And his body will turn to ashes.

sanskrit: dahyamāne agnibhiḥ dehe patyuḥ patnī saha uṭaje bahiḥ sthitā patim sādhvī tam agnim anu vekṣyati
english: While outside observing her husband, who will burn in the fire of mystic power along with his thatched cottage, his chaste wife will enter the fire with rapt attention.

sanskrit: viduraḥ tu tat āścaryam niśāmya kuru nandana harṣa śoka yutaḥ tasmāt gantā tīrtha niṣevakaḥ
english: Vidura, being affected with delight and grief, will then leave that place of sacred pilgrimage.

sanskrit: iti uktvā atha āruhat svargam nāradaḥ saha tumburuḥ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ vacaḥ tasya hṛdi kṛtvā ajahāt śucaḥ
english: Having spoken thus, the great sage Nārada, along with his vīṇā, ascended into outer space. Yudhiṣṭhira kept his instruction in his heart and so was able to get rid of all lamentations.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca samprasthite dvārakāyām jiṣṇau bandhu didṛkṣayā jñātum ca puṇya ślokasya kṛṣṇasya ca viceṣṭitam
english: Śrī Sūta Gosvāmī said: Arjuna went to Dvārakā to see Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa and other friends and also to learn from the Lord of His next activities.

sanskrit: vyatītāḥ katicit māsāḥ tadā na āyāt tataḥ arjunaḥ dadarśa ghora rūpāṇi nimittāni kuru udvahaḥ
english: A few months passed, and Arjuna did not return. Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira then began to observe some inauspicious omens, which were fearful in themselves.

sanskrit: kālasya ca gatim raudrām viparyasta ṛtu dharmiṇaḥ pāpīyasīm nṛṇām vārtām krodha lobha anṛta ātmanām
english: He saw that the direction of eternal time had changed, and this was very fearful. There were disruptions in the seasonal regularities. The people in general had become very greedy, angry and deceitful. And he saw that they were adopting foul means of livelihood.

sanskrit: jihma prāyam vyavahṛtam śāṭhya miśram ca sauhṛdam pitṛ mātṛ suhṛt bhrātṛ dam patīnām ca kalkanam
english: All ordinary transactions and dealings became polluted with cheating, even between friends. And in familial affairs, there was always misunderstanding between fathers, mothers and sons, between well-wishers, and between brothers. Even between husband and wife there was always strain and quarrel.

sanskrit: nimittāni ati ariṣṭāni kāle tu anugate nṛṇām lobha ādi adharma prakṛtim dṛṣṭvā uvāca anujam nṛpaḥ
english: In course of time it came to pass that people in general became accustomed to greed, anger, pride, etc. Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, observing all these omens, spoke to his younger brother.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca sampreṣitaḥ dvārakāyām jiṣṇuḥ bandhu didṛkṣayā jñātum ca puṇya ślokasya kṛṣṇasya ca viceṣṭitam
english: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira said to his younger brother Bhīmasena: I sent Arjuna to Dvārakā to meet his friends and to learn from the Personality of Godhead, Kṛṣṇa, of His program of work.

sanskrit: gatāḥ sapta adhunā māsāḥ bhīmasena tava anujaḥ na āyāti kasya vā hetoḥ na aham veda idam añjasā
english: Since he departed, seven months have passed, yet he has not returned. I do not know factually how things are going there.

sanskrit: api deva ṛṣiṇā ādiṣṭaḥ saḥ kālaḥ ayam upasthitaḥ yadā ātmanaḥ aṅgam ākrīḍam bhagavān utsisṛkṣati
english: Is He going to quit His earthly pastimes, as Devarṣi Nārada indicated? Has that time already arrived?

sanskrit: yasmāt naḥ sampadaḥ rājyam dārāḥ prāṇāḥ kulam prajāḥ āsan sapatna vijayaḥ lokāḥ ca yat anugrahāt
english: From Him only, all our kingly opulence, good wives, lives, progeny, control over our subjects, victory over our enemies, and future accommodations in higher planets have become possible. All this is due to His causeless mercy upon us.

sanskrit: paśya utpātān nara vyāghra divyān bhaumān sa daihikān dāruṇān śaṁsataḥ adūrāt bhayam naḥ buddhi mohanam
english: Just see, O man with a tiger’s strength, how many miseries due to celestial influences, earthly reactions and bodily pains — all very dangerous in themselves — are foreboding danger in the near future by deluding our intelligence.

sanskrit: ūru akṣi bāhavaḥ mahyam sphuranti aṅga punaḥ punaḥ vepathuḥ ca api hṛdaye ārāt dāsyanti vipriyam
english: The left side of my body — my thighs, arms and eyes — are all quivering again and again. I am having heart palpitations due to fear. All this indicates undesirable happenings.

sanskrit: śivā eṣā udyantam ādityam abhi rauti anala ānanā mām aṅga sārameyaḥ ayam abhirebhati abhīru vat
english: Just see, O Bhīma, how the she-jackal cries at the rising sun and vomits fire, and how the dog barks at me fearlessly.

sanskrit: śastāḥ kurvanti mām savyam dakṣiṇam paśavaḥ apare vāhān ca puruṣa vyāghra lakṣaye rudataḥ mama
english: O Bhīmasena, tiger amongst men, now useful animals like cows are passing me on my left side, and lower animals like the asses are circumambulating me. My horses appear to weep upon seeing me.

sanskrit: mṛtyu dūtaḥ kapotaḥ ayam ulūkaḥ kampayan manaḥ pratyulūkaḥ ca kuhvānaiḥ viśvam vai śūnyam icchataḥ
english: Just see! This pigeon is like a messenger of death. The shrieks of the owls and their rival crows make my heart tremble. It appears that they want to make a void of the whole universe.

sanskrit: dhūmrāḥ diśaḥ paridhayaḥ kampate bhūḥ saha adribhiḥ nirghātaḥ ca mahān tāta sākam ca stanayitnubhiḥ
english: Just see how the smoke encircles the sky. It appears that the earth and mountains are throbbing. Just hear the cloudless thunder and see the bolts from the blue.

sanskrit: vāyuḥ vāti khara sparśaḥ rajasā visṛjan tamaḥ asṛk varṣanti jaladāḥ bībhatsam iva sarvataḥ
english: The wind blows violently, blasting dust everywhere and creating darkness. Clouds are raining everywhere with bloody disasters.

sanskrit: sūryam hata prabham paśya graha mardam mithaḥ divi sa saṅkulaiḥ bhūta gaṇaiḥ jvalite iva rodasī
english: The rays of the sun are declining, and the stars appear to be fighting amongst themselves. Confused living entities appear to be ablaze and weeping.

sanskrit: nadyaḥ nadāḥ ca kṣubhitāḥ sarāṁsi ca manāṁsi ca na jvalati agniḥ ājyena kālaḥ ayam kim vidhāsyati
english: Rivers, tributaries, ponds, reservoirs and the mind are all perturbed. Butter no longer ignites fire. What is this extraordinary time? What is going to happen?

sanskrit: na pibanti stanam vatsāḥ na duhyanti ca mātaraḥ rudanti aśru mukhāḥ gāvaḥ na hṛṣyanti ṛṣabhāḥ vraje
english: The calves do not suck the teats of the cows, nor do the cows give milk. They are standing, crying, tears in their eyes, and the bulls take no pleasure in the pasturing grounds.

sanskrit: daivatāni rudanti iva svidyanti hi uccalanti ca ime jana padāḥ grāmāḥ pura udyāna ākara āśramāḥ bhraṣṭa śriyaḥ nirānandāḥ kim agham darśayanti naḥ
english: The Deities seem to be crying in the temple, lamenting and perspiring. They seem about to leave. All the cities, villages, towns, gardens, mines and hermitages are now devoid of beauty and bereft of all happiness. I do not know what sort of calamities are now awaiting us.

sanskrit: manye etaiḥ mahā utpātaiḥ nūnam bhagavataḥ padaiḥ ananya puruṣa śrībhiḥ hīnā bhūḥ hata saubhagā
english: I think that all these earthly disturbances indicate some greater loss to the good fortune of the world. The world was fortunate to have been marked with the footprints of the lotus feet of the Lord. These signs indicate that this will no longer be.

sanskrit: iti cintayataḥ tasya dṛṣṭā ariṣṭena cetasā rājñaḥ prati āgamat brahman yadu puryāḥ kapi dhvajaḥ
english: O Brāhmaṇa Śaunaka, while Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira, observing the inauspicious signs on the earth at that time, was thus thinking to himself, Arjuna came back from the city of the Yadus [Dvārakā].

sanskrit: tam pādayoḥ nipatitam ayathā pūrvam āturam adhaḥ vadanam ap bindūn sṛjantam nayana abjayoḥ
english: When he bowed at his feet, the King saw that his dejection was unprecedented. His head was down, and tears glided from his lotus eyes.

sanskrit: vilokya udvigna hṛdayaḥ vicchāyam anujam nṛpaḥ pṛcchati sma suhṛt madhye saṁsmaran nārada īritam
english: Seeing Arjuna pale due to heartfelt anxieties, the King, remembering the indications of the sage Nārada, questioned him in the midst of friends.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraḥ uvāca kaccit ānarta puryām naḥ sva janāḥ sukham āsate madhu bhoja daśārha arha sātvata andhaka vṛṣṇayaḥ
english: Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira said: My dear brother, please tell me whether our friends and relatives, such as Madhu, Bhoja, Daśārha, Ārha, Sātvata, Andhaka and the members of the Yadu family are all passing their days in happiness.

sanskrit: śūraḥ mātāmahaḥ kaccit svasti āste vā atha māriṣaḥ mātulaḥ sa anujaḥ kaccit kuśalī ānaka dundubhiḥ
english: Is my respectable grandfather Śūrasena in a happy mood? And are my maternal uncle Vasudeva and his younger brothers all doing well?

sanskrit: sapta sva sāraḥ tat patnyaḥ mātulānyaḥ saha ātma jāḥ āsate sasnuṣāḥ kṣemam devakī pramukhāḥ svayam
english: His seven wives, headed by Devakī, are all sisters. Are they and their sons and daughters-in-law all happy?

sanskrit: kaccit rājā āhukaḥ jīvati asat putraḥ asya ca anujaḥ hṛdīkaḥ sa sutaḥ akrūraḥ jayanta gada sāraṇāḥ āsate kuśalam kaccit ye ca śatrujit ādayaḥ kaccit āste sukham rāmaḥ bhagavān sātvatām prabhuḥ
english: Are Ugrasena, whose son was the mischievous Kaṁsa, and his younger brother still living? Are Hṛdīka and his son Kṛtavarmā happy? Are Akrūra, Jayanta, Gada, Sāraṇa and Śatrujit all happy? How is Balarāma, the Personality of Godhead and the protector of devotees?

sanskrit: pradyumnaḥ sarva vṛṣṇīnām sukham āste mahā rathaḥ gambhīra rayaḥ aniruddhaḥ vardhate bhagavān uta
english: How is Pradyumna, the great general of the Vṛṣṇi family? Is He happy? And is Aniruddha, the plenary expansion of the Personality of Godhead, faring well?

sanskrit: suṣeṇaḥ cārudeṣṇaḥ ca sāmbaḥ jāmbavatī sutaḥ anye ca kārṣṇi pravarāḥ sa putrāḥ ṛṣabha ādayaḥ
english: Are all the chieftain sons of Lord Kṛṣṇa, such as Suṣeṇa, Cārudeṣṇa, Sāmba the son of Jāmbavatī, and Ṛṣabha, along with their sons, all doing well?

sanskrit: tathā eva anucarāḥ śaureḥ śrutadeva uddhava ādayaḥ sunanda nanda śīrṣaṇyāḥ ye ca anye sātvata ṛṣabhāḥ api svasti āsate sarve rāma kṛṣṇa bhuja āśrayāḥ api smaranti kuśalam asmākam baddha sauhṛdāḥ
english: Also, Śrutadeva, Uddhava and others, Nanda, Sunanda and other leaders of liberated souls who are constant companions of the Lord are protected by Lord Balarāma and Kṛṣṇa. Are they all doing well in their respective functions? Do they, who are all eternally bound in friendship with us, remember our welfare?

sanskrit: bhagavān api govindaḥ brahmaṇyaḥ bhakta vatsalaḥ kaccit pure sudharmāyām sukham āste suhṛt vṛtaḥ
english: Is Lord Kṛṣṇa, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who gives pleasure to the cows, the senses and the brāhmaṇas, who is very affectionate towards His devotees, enjoying the pious assembly at Dvārakā Purī surrounded by friends?

sanskrit: maṅgalāya ca lokānām kṣemāya ca bhavāya ca āste yadu kula ambhodhau ādyaḥ ananta sakhaḥ pumān yat bāhu daṇḍa guptāyām sva puryām yadavaḥ arcitāḥ krīḍanti parama ānandam mahā pauruṣikāḥ iva
english: The original Personality of Godhead, the enjoyer, and Balarāma, the primeval Lord Ananta, are staying in the ocean of the Yadu dynasty for the welfare, protection and general progress of the entire universe. And the members of the Yadu dynasty, being protected by the arms of the Lord, are enjoying life like the residents of the spiritual sky.

sanskrit: yat pāda śuśrūṣaṇa mukhya karmaṇā satya ādayaḥ dvi aṣṭa sahasra yoṣitaḥ nirjitya saṅkhye tri daśān tat āśiṣaḥ haranti vajra āyudha vallabhā ucitāḥ
english: Simply by administering comforts at the lotus feet of the Lord, which is the most important of all services, the queens at Dvārakā, headed by Satyabhāmā, induced the Lord to conquer the demigods. Thus the queens enjoy things which are prerogatives of the wives of the controller of thunderbolts.

sanskrit: yat bāhu daṇḍa abhyudaya anujīvinaḥ yadu pravīrāḥ hi akutobhayāḥ muhuḥ adhikramanti aṅghribhiḥ āhṛtām balāt sabhām sudharmām sura sat tama ucitām
english: The great heroes of the Yadu dynasty, being protected by the arms of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa, always remain fearless in every respect. And therefore their feet trample over the Sudharmā assembly house, which the best demigods deserved but which was taken away from them.

sanskrit: kaccit te anāmayam tāta bhraṣṭa tejāḥ vibhāsi me alabdha mānaḥ avajñātaḥ kim vā tāta ciroṣitaḥ
english: My brother Arjuna, please tell me whether your health is all right. You appear to have lost your bodily luster. Is this due to others disrespecting and neglecting you because of your long stay at Dvārakā?

sanskrit: kaccit na abhihataḥ abhāvaiḥ śabda ādibhiḥ amaṅgalaiḥ na dattam uktam arthibhyaḥ āśayā yat pratiśrutam
english: Has someone addressed you with unfriendly words or threatened you? Could you not give charity to one who asked, or could you not keep your promise to someone?

sanskrit: kaccit tvam brāhmaṇam bālam gām vṛddham rogiṇam striyam śaraṇa upasṛtam sattvam na atyākṣīḥ śaraṇa pradaḥ
english: You are always the protector of the deserving living beings, such as brāhmaṇas, children, cows, women and the diseased. Could you not give them protection when they approached you for shelter?

sanskrit: kaccit tvam na agamaḥ agamyām gamyām vā asat kṛtām striyam parājitaḥ vā atha bhavān na uttamaiḥ na asamaiḥ pathi
english: Have you contacted a woman of impeachable character, or have you not properly treated a deserving woman? Or have you been defeated on the way by someone who is inferior or equal to you?

sanskrit: api svit parya bhuṅkthāḥ tvam sambhojyān vṛddha bālakān jugupsitam karma kiñcit kṛtavān na yat akṣamam
english: Have you not taken care of old men and boys who deserve to dine with you? Have you left them and taken your meals alone? Have you committed some unpardonable mistake which is considered to be abominable?

sanskrit: kaccit preṣṭha tamena atha hṛdayena ātma bandhunā śūnyaḥ asmi rahitaḥ nityam manyase te anyathā na ruk
english: Or is it that you are feeling empty for all time because you might have lost your most intimate friend, Lord Kṛṣṇa? O my brother Arjuna, I can think of no other reason for your becoming so dejected.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca evam kṛṣṇa sakhaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ bhrātrā rājñā vikalpitaḥ nānā śaṅka āspadam rūpam kṛṣṇa viśleṣa karśitaḥ
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Arjuna, the celebrated friend of Lord Kṛṣṇa, was griefstricken because of his strong feeling of separation from Kṛṣṇa, over and above all Mahārāja Yudhiṣṭhira’s speculative inquiries.

sanskrit: śokena śuṣyat vadana hṛt sarojaḥ hata prabhaḥ vibhum tam eva anusmaran na aśaknot pratibhāṣitum
english: Due to grief, Arjuna’s mouth and lotuslike heart had dried up. Therefore his body lost all luster. Now, remembering the Supreme Lord, he could hardly utter a word in reply.

sanskrit: kṛcchreṇa saṁstabhya śucaḥ pāṇinā āmṛjya netrayoḥ parokṣeṇa samunnaddha praṇaya autkaṇṭhya kātaraḥ
english: With great difficulty he checked the tears of grief that smeared his eyes. He was very distressed because Lord Kṛṣṇa was out of his sight, and he increasingly felt affection for Him.

sanskrit: sakhyam maitrīm sauhṛdam ca sārathya ādiṣu saṁsmaran nṛpam agrajam iti āha bāṣpa gadgadayā girā
english: Remembering Lord Kṛṣṇa and His well wishes, benefactions, intimate familial relations and His chariot driving, Arjuna, overwhelmed and breathing very heavily, began to speak.

sanskrit: arjunaḥ uvāca vañcitaḥ aham mahā rāja hariṇā bandhu rūpiṇā yena me apahṛtam tejaḥ deva vismāpanam mahat
english: Arjuna said: O King! The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Hari, who treated me exactly like an intimate friend, has left me alone. Thus my astounding power, which astonished even the demigods, is no longer with me.

sanskrit: yasya kṣaṇa viyogena lokaḥ hi apriya darśanaḥ ukthena rahitaḥ hi eṣaḥ mṛtakaḥ procyate yathā
english: I have just lost Him whose separation for a moment would render all the universes unfavorable and void, like bodies without life.

sanskrit: yat saṁśrayāt drupada geham upāgatānām rājñām svayaṁvara mukhe smara durmadānām tejaḥ hṛtam khalu mayā abhihataḥ ca matsyaḥ sajjī kṛtena dhanuṣā adhigatā ca kṛṣṇā
english: Only by His merciful strength was I able to vanquish all the lusty princes assembled at the palace of King Drupada for the selection of the bridegroom. With my bow and arrow I could pierce the fish target and thereby gain the hand of Draupadī.

sanskrit: yat sannidhau aham u khāṇḍavam agnaye adām indram ca sa amara gaṇam tarasā vijitya labdhā sabhā maya kṛtā adbhuta śilpa māyā digbhyaḥ aharan nṛpatayaḥ balim adhvare te
english: Because He was near me, it was possible for me to conquer with great dexterity the powerful King of heaven, Indradeva, along with his demigod associates and thus enable the fire-god to devastate the Khāṇḍava Forest. And only by His grace was the demon named Maya saved from the blazing Khāṇḍava Forest, and thus we could build our assembly house of wonderful architectural workmanship, where all the princes assembled during the performance of Rājasūya-yajña and paid you tributes.

sanskrit: yat tejasā nṛpa śiraḥ aṅghrim ahan makha artham āryaḥ anujaḥ tava gaja ayuta sattva vīryaḥ tena āhṛtāḥ pramatha nātha makhāya bhūpāḥ yat mocitāḥ tat anayan balim adhvare te
english: Your respectable younger brother, who possesses the strength of ten thousand elephants, killed, by His grace, Jarāsandha, whose feet were worshiped by many kings. These kings had been brought for sacrifice in Jarāsandha’s Mahābhairava-yajña, but they were thus released. Later they paid tribute to Your Majesty.

sanskrit: patnyāḥ tava adhimakha kḷpta mahā abhiṣeka ślāghiṣṭha cāru kabaram kitavaiḥ sabhāyām spṛṣṭam vikīrya padayoḥ patita aśru mukhyāḥ yaḥ tat striyaḥ akṛta hata īśa vimukta keśāḥ
english: It was He only who loosened the hair of all the wives of the miscreants who dared open the cluster of your Queen’s hair, which had been nicely dressed and sanctified for the great Rājasūya sacrificial ceremony. At that time she fell down at the feet of Lord Kṛṣṇa with tears in her eyes.

sanskrit: yaḥ naḥ jugopa vane etya duranta kṛcchrāt durvāsasaḥ ari racitāt ayuta agra bhuk yaḥ śāka anna śiṣṭam upayujya yataḥ tri lokīm tṛptām amaṁsta salile vinimagna saṅghaḥ
english: During our exile, Durvāsā Muni, who eats with his ten thousand disciples, intrigued with our enemies to put us in dangerous trouble. At that time He [Lord Kṛṣṇa], simply by accepting the remnants of food, saved us. By His accepting food thus, the assembly of munis, while bathing in the river, felt sumptuously fed. And all the three worlds were also satisfied.

sanskrit: yat tejasā atha bhagavān yudhi śūla pāṇiḥ vismāpitaḥ sa girijaḥ astram adāt nijam me anye api ca aham amunā eva kalevareṇa prāptaḥ mahā indra bhavane mahat āsana ardham
english: It was by His influence only that in a fight I was able to astonish the personality of god Lord Śiva and his wife, the daughter of Mount Himālaya. Thus he [Lord Śiva] became pleased with me and awarded me his own weapon. Other demigods also delivered their respective weapons to me, and in addition I was able to reach the heavenly planets in this present body and was allowed a half-elevated seat.

sanskrit: tatra eva me viharataḥ bhuja daṇḍa yugmam gāṇḍīva lakṣaṇam arāti vadhāya devāḥ sa indrāḥ śritāḥ yat anubhāvitam ājamīḍha tena aham adya muṣitaḥ puruṣeṇa bhūmnā
english: When I stayed for some days as a guest in the heavenly planets, all the heavenly demigods, including King Indradeva, took shelter of my arms, which were marked with the Gāṇḍīva bow, to kill the demon named Nivātakavaca. O King, descendant of Ajamīḍha, at the present moment I am bereft of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, by whose influence I was so powerful.

sanskrit: yat bāndhavaḥ kuru bala abdhim ananta pāram ekaḥ rathena tatare aham atīrya sattvam pratyāhṛtam bahu dhanam ca mayā pareṣām tejāḥ padam maṇi mayam ca hṛtam śirobhyaḥ
english: The military strength of the Kauravas was like an ocean in which there dwelled many invincible existences, and thus it was insurmountable. But because of His friendship, I, seated on the chariot, was able to cross over it. And only by His grace was I able to regain the cows and also collect by force many helmets of the kings, which were bedecked with jewels that were sources of all brilliance.

sanskrit: yaḥ bhīṣma karṇa guru śalya camūṣu adabhra rājanya varya ratha maṇḍala maṇḍitāsu agecaraḥ mama vibho ratha yūtha pānām āyuḥ manāṁsi ca dṛśā sahaḥ ojaḥ ārcchat
english: It was He only who withdrew the duration of life from everyone and who, in the battlefield, withdrew the speculative power and strength of enthusiasm from the great military phalanx made by the Kauravas, headed by Bhīṣma, Karṇa, Droṇa, Śalya, etc. Their arrangement was expert and more than adequate, but He [Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa], while going forward, did all this.

sanskrit: yat doḥṣu mā praṇihitam guru bhīṣma karṇa naptṛ trigarta śalya saindhava bāhlika ādyaiḥ astrāṇi amogha mahimāni nirūpitāni na upaspṛśuḥ nṛhari dāsam iva asurāṇi
english: Great generals like Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Karṇa, Bhūriśravā, Suśarmā, Śalya, Jayadratha and Bāhlika all directed their invincible weapons against me. But by His [Lord Kṛṣṇa’s] grace they could not even touch a hair on my head. Similarly, Prahlāda Mahārāja, the supreme devotee of Lord Nṛsiṁhadeva, was unaffected by the weapons the demons used against him.

sanskrit: sautye vṛtaḥ kumatinā ātma daḥ īśvaraḥ me yat pāda padmam abhavāya bhajanti bhavyāḥ mām śrānta vāham arayaḥ rathinaḥ bhuvi ṣṭham na prāharan yat anubhāva nirasta cittāḥ
english: It was by His mercy only that my enemies neglected to kill me when I descended from my chariot to get water for my thirsty horses. And it was due to my lack of esteem for my Lord that I dared engage Him as my chariot driver, for He is worshiped and offered services by the best men to attain salvation.

sanskrit: narmāṇi udāra rucira smita śobhitāni he pārtha he arjuna sakhe kuru nandana iti sañjalpitāni nara deva hṛdi spṛśāni smartuḥ luṭhanti hṛdayam mama mādhavasya
english: O King! His jokings and frank talks were pleasing and beautifully decorated with smiles. His addresses unto me as “O son of Pṛthā, O friend, O son of the Kuru dynasty,” and all such heartiness are now remembered by me, and thus I am overwhelmed.

sanskrit: śayya āsana aṭana vikatthana bhojana ādiṣu aikyāt vayasya ṛtavān iti vipralabdhaḥ sakhyuḥ sakhā iva pitṛvat tanayasya sarvam sehe mahān mahitayā kumateḥ agham me
english: Generally both of us used to live together and sleep, sit and loiter together. And at the time of advertising oneself for acts of chivalry, sometimes, if there were any irregularity, I used to reproach Him by saying, “My friend, You are very truthful.” Even in those hours when His value was minimized, He, being the Supreme Soul, used to tolerate all those utterings of mine, excusing me exactly as a true friend excuses his true friend, or a father excuses his son.

sanskrit: saḥ aham nṛpa indra rahitaḥ puruṣa uttamena sakhyā priyeṇa suhṛdā hṛdayena śūnyaḥ adhvani urukrama parigraham aṅga rakṣan gopaiḥ asadbhiḥ abalā iva vinirjitaḥ asmi
english: O Emperor, now I am separated from my friend and dearmost well-wisher, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and therefore my heart appears to be void of everything. In His absence I have been defeated by a number of infidel cowherd men while I was guarding the bodies of all the wives of Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: tat vai dhanuḥ te iṣavaḥ saḥ rathaḥ hayāḥ te saḥ aham rathī nṛpatayaḥ yataḥ ānamanti sarvam kṣaṇena tat abhūt asat īśa riktam bhasman hutam kuhaka rāddham iva uptam ūṣyām
english: I have the very same Gāṇḍīva bow, the same arrows, the same chariot drawn by the same horses, and I use them as the same Arjuna to whom all the kings offered their due respects. But in the absence of Lord Kṛṣṇa, all of them, at a moment’s notice, have become null and void. It is exactly like offering clarified butter on ashes, accumulating money with a magic wand or sowing seeds on barren land.

sanskrit: rājan tvayā anupṛṣṭānām suhṛdām naḥ suhṛt pure vipra śāpa vimūḍhānām nighnatām muṣṭibhiḥ mithaḥ vāruṇīm madirām pītvā mada unmathita cetasām ajānatām iva anyonyam catuḥ pañca avaśeṣitāḥ
english: O King, since you have asked me about our friends and relatives in the city of Dvārakā, I will inform you that all of them were cursed by the brāhmaṇas, and as a result they all became intoxicated with wine made of putrefied rice and fought among themselves with sticks, not even recognizing one another. Now all but four or five of them are dead and gone.

sanskrit: prāyeṇa etat bhagavataḥ īśvarasya viceṣṭitam mithaḥ nighnanti bhūtāni bhāvayanti ca yat mithaḥ
english: Factually this is all due to the supreme will of the Lord, the Personality of Godhead. Sometimes people kill one another, and at other times they protect one another.

sanskrit: jalaukasām jale yadvat mahāntaḥ adanti aṇīyasaḥ durbalān balinaḥ rājan mahāntaḥ balinaḥ mithaḥ evam baliṣṭhaiḥ yadubhiḥ mahadbhiḥ itarān vibhuḥ yadūn yadubhiḥ anyonyam bhū bhārān sañjahāra ha
english: O King, as in the ocean the bigger and stronger aquatics swallow up the smaller and weaker ones, so also the Supreme Personality of Godhead, to lighten the burden of the earth, has engaged the stronger Yadu to kill the weaker, and the bigger Yadu to kill the smaller.

sanskrit: deśa kāla artha yuktāni hṛt tāpa upaśamāni ca haranti smarataḥ cittam govinda abhihitāni me
english: Now I am attracted to those instructions imparted to me by the Personality of Godhead [Govinda] because they are impregnated with instructions for relieving the burning heart in all circumstances of time and space.

sanskrit: sūtaḥ uvāca evam cintayataḥ jiṣṇoḥ kṛṣṇa pāda saroruham sauhārdena ati gāḍhena śāntā āsīt vimalā matiḥ
english: Sūta Gosvāmī said: Thus being deeply absorbed in thinking of the instructions of the Lord, which were imparted in the great intimacy of friendship, and in thinking of His lotus feet, Arjuna’s mind became pacified and free from all material contamination.

sanskrit: vāsudeva aṅghri anudhyāna paribṛṁhita raṁhasā bhaktyā nirmathita aśeṣa kaṣāya dhiṣaṇaḥ arjunaḥ
english: Arjuna’s constant remembrance of the lotus feet of Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa rapidly increased his devotion, and as a result all the trash in his thoughts subsided.

sanskrit: gītam bhagavatā jñānam yat tat saṅgrāma mūrdhani kāla karma tamaḥ ruddham punaḥ adhyagamat prabhuḥ
english: Because of the Lord’s pastimes and activities and because of His absence, it appeared that Arjuna forgot the instructions left by the Personality of Godhead. But factually this was not the case, and again he became lord of his senses.

sanskrit: viśokaḥ brahma sampattyā sañchinna dvaita saṁśayaḥ līna prakṛti nairguṇyāt aliṅgatvāt asambhavaḥ
