english: Formerly the Brāhmaṇa Bhārgava (accompanied by his disciples) had gone to mount Mānasottara for performing penance. Hence he was not aware of that battle.

sanskrit: gataḥ śiṣyaiḥ parivṛtastasmādyuddhaṃ na veda tat | avaśeṣāśca ye daityāste gatā bhārgavaṃ prati || 27 || kathitaṃ vai mahaddhṛttamasurāṇāṃ kṣayāvaham | niśamya manyumāviṣṭo hyāgato bhṛgunaṃdanaḥ || 28 || śiṣyaiḥ parivṛto bhūtvā mṛtāṃstānasurānapi | vidyayā mṛtajīvinyā patitānsamajīvayat || 29 ||
english: 27b-29. Those Daityas who had survived approached Bhārgava. The news of the great destruction of Asuras was conveyed to him. On hearing it, the son of Bhṛgu became furious. He returned surrounded by his disciples. With the Vidyā (magic formula) called Mṛtajīvinī (‘Resuscitator of the dead’), he revived the Asuras who had fallen dead.

sanskrit: nidrāpāyagatā yadvadutthitāste tadā'surāḥ | utthitaḥ sa baliḥ prāha bhārgavaṃ hyamitadyutim || 30 ||
english: 30. Then those Asuras got up as though they had awakened from sleep. Bali who rose up, said to Bhārgava of unmeasured splendour:

sanskrit: jīvitena kimadyaiva mama nāsti prayojanam | pātitastridaśeṃdreṇa yathā kāpuruṣastathā || 31 ||
english: 31. “Of what avail is it to me today to be revived back to life? There is no benefit to me. I have been struck down by the lord of Devas like a mean contemptible wretch.”

sanskrit: balinoktaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā śukro vacanamabravīt | manasvino hi ye śūrāḥ pataṃti samare budhā || 32 || ye śastreṇa hatāḥ sadyo mriyamāṇā vrajaṃti vai | triviṣṭapaṃ na saṃdeha iti vedānuśāsanam || 33 ||
english: 32-33. On hearing the words uttered by Bali, Śukra spoke these words: “Those heroic persons who are high-souled and intelligent, who are learned, and who fall down dead in battle on being struck by a weapon go to heaven. This is undoubtedly the statement of the Vedas.”

sanskrit: evamāśvāsayāmāsa balinaṃ bhṛgunaṃdanaḥ | tapastatāpa vividhaṃ daityānāṃ siddhidāyakam || 34 ||
english: 34. Thus, the son of Bhṛgu consoled Bali. He then performed various kinds of penance conducive to the achievement of Siddhis by Daityas.

sanskrit: tathā daitya gatāḥ sarve bhṛguṇā ca pracoditāḥ | pātālamavasansarve balimukhyāḥ sukhena vai || 35 ||
english: 35. All the Daityas urged by Bhṛgu went to Pātāla. All the Daityas, the chief among whom was Bali, stayed in Pātāla in happiness. FOOTNOTES AND REFERENCES: Arthaśāstra—A treatise on political economy. It is the title of a famous work of Kauṭilya or Ārya Cāṇakya who masterminded the revolution in Pāṭalīputra (Magadha), uprooted the Nanda dynasty and installed Candragupta Maurya as the King. Kauṭilya refers to many predecessors. Hence the Arthaśāstra mentioned here may be a more ancient work than that of Kauṭilya.[Sanskrit text for this chapter is available]

sanskrit: | ṛṣaya ūcuḥ | rājyaṃ prāpto hi deveṃdraḥ kathitaste guruṃ vinā | guroravajñayā jāto rājyabhraṃśo hi tasya tu || 1 || kena praṇoditaśceṃdro babhūva ciramāsane | tatsarvaṃ kathayāśu tvaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ || 2 ||
english: The sages enquired: 1-2. It has been mentioned by you that Devendra regained kingdom without his preceptor. It was on account of disrespect to his preceptor that he had been dethroned from his kingdom. Urged by whom did he retain his position for a long time? Do tell us all these things quickly. We are very eager to hear it.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca | guruṇāpi vinā rājyaṃ kṛtavānsa śacīpatiḥ | viśvarūpoktavidhinā iṃdro rājye sthito mahān || 3 ||
english: Lomaśa replied: 3-4. The consort of Śacī (Indra) ruled over the kingdom (of heaven) without his preceptor (Bṛhaspati). The great Indra (could) continue (to rule) over the kingdom due to the (religious) performance in accordance with the injunctions of Viśvarūpa.

sanskrit: viśvakarmasuto viprā viśvarūpo mahānṛpaḥ | purohito'tha śakrasya yājakaścābhavattadā || 4 ||
english: 5-6. O Brāhmaṇas, Viśvarūpa,[1] a great king, was the son of Viśvakarmā. He became the preceptor and performer of sacrifices for Śakra.

sanskrit: tasminyajñe'vadānaiśca yajane asurānsurān | manuṣyāṃścaiva triśirā aparokṣaṃ śacīpateḥ || 5 ||
english: In that Yajña, Triśiras (one with three heads) performed the worship with partial oblations separately for Asuras, Suras and human beings.

sanskrit: devāndadāti sākrośaṃ daityāṃstūṣṇīmathādadāt | manuṣyānmadhyapātena pratyahaṃ sa grahāndvijaḥ || 6 ||
english: In the direct presence of Indra everyday he used to give ladles (full of Soma) to Devas with a loud shout, to Daityas silently, and to human being in a fallen middle tone.

sanskrit: ekadā tu maheṃdreṇa sūcito gurulāghavāt | alakṣyamāṇena tadā jñātaṃ tasya cikīrṣitam || 7 ||
english: 7-8. Once he was detected due to his partiality (regarding relative importance of oblations) by Indra who remained concealed and unobserved. Then the desired object (of Triśiras) was understood (by Indra).

sanskrit: daityānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthamavadānaṃ prayacchati | asau purohito'smākaṃ pareṣāṃ ca phalapradaḥ || 8 ||
english: (Deveṇdra thought) ‘He is making this piecemeal offering for the sake of accomplishing the task of Daityas. He is our preceptor, but gives the benefit to (our) enemies.’

sanskrit: iti matvā tadā śakro vajreṇa śataparvaṇā | ciccheda tacchirāṃsyeva tatkṣaṇādabhavadvadhaḥ || 9 ||
english: 9. After thinking thus, Śakra cut off his heads instantaneously by means of his Vajra (thunderbolt) of hundred spikes. The death was instantaneous.

sanskrit: yenākarotsomapānamajāyaṃta kapiṃjalāḥ | tatonyena surāpānātkalaviṃkā bhavanmukhāt || 10 || anyānanādajāyaṃta tittirā viśvarūpiṇaḥ | evaṃ hato viśvarūpaḥ śakreṇa maṃdabhāginā || 11 ||
english: 10-11. The Kapiñjala (a sort of partridge) birds were born from the face with which he drank Soma juice. Then from the other face with which-he drank liquor, the Kalaviṅka (sparrow) birds were born. From the other (third) face, the Tittira birds of various forms were born. Thus, Viśvarūpa was killed by Śakra, the ill-fated one.

sanskrit: brahmahatyā tadodbhūtā durdharṣā ca bhayāvahā | durdharṣā durmukhā duṣṭā caṇḍālarajasānvitā || 12 ||
english: 12-14. The female fiend (born of and called) Brahmahatyā (‘Brāhmaṇa-murder’) manifested there. She was terrific and unthwartable. She was evil-faced, wicked, full of Cāṇḍāla impurity and could not be blocked or defeated.

sanskrit: brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṃganāgamaḥ | ityeṣāmapyaghavatāmidameva ca niṣkṛtiḥ || 13 ||
english: The terrible sinners are those who slay Brāhmaṇas, those who drink liquor, those who steal (gold etc.) and those who defile and outrage the modesty of the preceptor’s wife. The means of expiation for these sinners is the utterance of the names of Viṣṇu, since the mind has him for its object.

sanskrit: nāmavyāharaṇaṃ viṣṇoryatastadviṣayā matiḥ | triśirā dhūmrahastā sā śakraṃ grastumupāyayau || 14 ||
english: The three-headed fiend with smoke-coloured hands rushed forth to swallow Indra.

sanskrit: tato bhayena mahatā palāyanaparo'bhavat | palāyamānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā hyanuyātā bhayāvahā || 15 ||
english: 15. Thereupon (Indra) fled from there out of great fear. On seeing him fleeing, the terrible (devil) chased him.

sanskrit: yato dhāvati sā'dhāvattiṣṭhaṃtamanutiṣṭhati | aṃgakṛtā yathā chāyā śakrasyapariveṣṭitum | āyāti tāvatsahasā iṃdro'pyapsu nyamajjata || 16 || śīghratvena yathā viprāściraṃtanajalecaraḥ || 17 ||
english: 16-17. Wherever he ran, she too ran after him. If he stood anywhere, she too stood beside him. She behaved in the manner of a shadow of one’s own body. When she came so close as to envelop him, Indra sank beneath the waters suddenly, O Brāhmaṇas, like an old aquatic being.

sanskrit: evaṃ divyaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ varṣāṇāṃ ca śacīpateḥ | vasatastasya duḥkhena tathā caiva śatadvayam | arājakaṃ tadā jātaṃ nākapṛṣṭhe bhayāvaham || 18 || tadā ciṃtānvitā devā ṛṣayo'pi tapasvinaḥ | trailokyaṃ cā'padā grastaṃ babhūva ca tadā dvijāḥ || 19 ||
english: 18-19. Thus three hundred divine years passed since the consort of Śacī (Indra) began staying (beneath the waters) with great misery. A terrific state of anarchy spread throughout heaven. Thereupon Devas, sages and ascetics became anxious and worried. All the three worlds were overwhelmed by adversity, O Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: eko'pi brahmahā yatra rāṣṭre vasati nirbhayaḥ | akālamaraṇaṃ tatra sādhūnāmupajāyate || 20 ||
english: 20. Even if there is a single Brāhmaṇa-slayer in a kingdom staying there with impunity, untimely death of good men will take place there.

sanskrit: rājā pāpayuto yasminrāṣṭre vasati tatra vai | durbhikṣaṃ caiva maraṇaṃ tathaivopadravā dvijāḥ || 21 ||
english: 21. The king of the state wherein he (the Brāhmaṇa-slayer) lives, becomes contaminated by the sin. There will be (prevalence of) famine, death and calamities.

sanskrit: bhavaṃti bahavo'narthāḥ prajānāṃ nāśahetave | tasmādrājñā tu kartavyo dharmmaḥ śraddhāpareṇa hi || 22 ||
english: 22. There will be many misfortunes causing the destruction of the subjects. Hence, Dharma should be practised by a king with great faith.

sanskrit: tathā prakṛtayo rājñaḥ śucajitvena pratiṣṭhitāḥ | indreṇa ca kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tena pāpena vai dvijāḥ | nānāvidhairmahātāpaiḥ sopadravamabhūjjagat || 23 ||
english: 23. Similarly, the ministers of the king too should be installed with purity. Sin was committeed by Indra and due to that sin, O Brāhmaṇas, the whole of the universe met with calamities along with great distress of diverse kinds.

sanskrit: śaunaka uvāca | aśvamedhaśatenaiva prāptaṃ rājyaṃ mahattaram | devānāmakhilaṃ sūta kasmādvighramajāyata | śakrasya ca mahābhāga yathāvatkathayasva na || 24 ||
english: Śaunaka enquired: 24. It was by performing a hundred horse-sacrifices that the great realm of Devas was acquired by him, O Sūta. Why then did Śakra meet with obstacles, O highly fortunate one? Do tell us exactly as it happened.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca | devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ | karmmaiva sukhaduḥkhānāṃ hetubhūtaṃ na saṃśayaḥ || 25 ||
english: Sūta replied: 25. In the case of Devas, Dānavas and particularly that of human beings, Karman alone is undoubtedly the cause of happiness and misery.

sanskrit: indreṇa ca kṛtaṃ viprā mahadbhūtaṃ jugupsitam | guroravajñā ca kṛtā viśvarūpavadhaḥ kṛtaḥ || 26 || gautamasya guroḥ patnī sevitā tasya tatphalam | prāptaṃ maheṃdreṇa ciraṃ yasya nāsti pratikriyā || 27 ||
english: 26-27. An immensely reprehensible act has been committed by Indra, O Brāhmaṇas, He insulted his Guru (preceptor Bṛhaspati). Viśvarūpa was slain. The wife of Gautama, his Guru (preceptor, elderly one), was carnally approached. It was the fruit of all these sins that was reaped by Mahendra for a long time. There was no way of atonement for the same.

sanskrit: ye hi dṛṣkaṭatakarmmāṇo na kurvaṃti ca niṣkṛtim | durdaśāṃ prapnuvantyete yathaivendraḥ śatakratuḥ || 28 ||
english: 28. If persons committing wicked and sinful deeds, do not perform expiatory rites (for the same), they do incur miseries just like Indra, (though) he had performed a hundred sacrifices.

sanskrit: duṣkṛtopārjitasyā taḥ prāyāścittaṃ hi tatkṣaṇāt | kartavyaṃ vidhivadviprāḥ sarvapāpopaśāṃtaye || 29 ||
english: 29. If sins are committed, atonement should be performed instantaneously in accordance with the injunctions, O Brāhmaṇas, for the sake of quelling all the sins.

sanskrit: tataḥ svadharmaniṣṭhāṃ ca ye kurvaṃti sadā narāḥ | prātarmadhyāhnasāyāhne teṣāṃ pāpaṃ vinaśyati || 31 || prāpnuvaṃtyuttamaṃ lokaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā | tasmādasau durācāraḥ prāpte vai karmaṇaḥ phalam || 32 ||
english: 30-32. If minor sins are repeatedly performed, they turn into major sins. Those men who steadfastly cling to their duties of the morning, midday and dusk can get their sins destroyed. They attain the excellent world. There is no doubt about it. Hence, this person of evil conduct (i.e. Indra) reaped the fruit of his karman.

sanskrit: sa pradhārya tadā sarve lokapālāstvarānvitāḥ | bṛhaspatimupāgamya sarvamātmani dhiṣṭhitam | kathayāmāsuravyagrā iṃdrasya ca guruṃ prati || 33 ||
english: 33. All the Guardians of the Quarters hurriedly deliberated together. They approached Bṛhaspati and reported to the preceptor about Indra everything they had in their mind.

sanskrit: devairuktaṃ vaco viprā niśamya ca bṛhaspatiḥ | arājakaṃ ca saṃprāptaṃ ciṃtayāmāsa buddhimān || 34 ||
english: 34. On hearing the words uttered by Devas, Bṛhaspati, the intelligent (preceptor), thought about the anarchy that had begun to spread.

sanskrit: kiṃ kāryaṃ cādya kartavyaṃ kathaṃ śreyo bhaviṣyati | devānāṃ cādya lokānāmṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām || 35 || manasaiva ca tatsarvaṃ kāryākāryaṃ vicārya ca | jagāma śakraṃ tvarito devaiḥ saha mahāyaśāḥ || 36 ||
english: 35-36. ‘What shall be done now? How will they secure welfare—Devas, the worlds and sages of sanctified souls?’ In his mind, he thought over the details of what should and what should not be done. Accompanied by Devas, the preceptor of great fame went to Indra.

sanskrit: prāpto jalāśayaṃ taṃ ca yatrāste hi puraṃdaraḥ | yasya tīre sthitā hatyā caṃḍālīva bhayāvahā || 37 ||
english: 37. They reached the lake where Purandara (Indra) was lying (hidden) and on the bank of which was staying the (devil of) Brāhmaṇa slaughter terrible like a Caṇḍālī.

sanskrit: tatroviṣṭāste sarve devā ṛṣigaṇānvitāḥ | āhvānaṃ ca kṛtaṃ tasya śakrasya guruṇā svayam || 38 ||
english: 38. All the Devas, accompanied by the groups of sages sat there. Then Śakra was called by the preceptor himself.

sanskrit: samutthitastataḥ śakro dadarśa svaguruṃ tadā | bāṣpapūritavaktro hi bṛhaspatimabhāṣata || 39 ||
english: 39. Thereupon, Indra got up and saw his preceptor. With tears flowing over his face, he spoke to Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: praṇipatya ca tatratyānkṛtāñjalirabhāṣata | tadā dīnamukho bhūtvā manasā saṃvimṛśya ca || 40 || svayameva kṛtaṃ pūrvamajñānalakṣaṇaṃ mahat | adhunaiva mayā kāryaṃ kiṃ kartavyaṃ vada prabho || 41 ||
english: 40-41. He bowed down to all the persons assembled there. He pondered over the great (blunders) committed by himself before, as a result of ignorance. He joined his palms in reverence and with a piteous face spoke: “O Lord, tell me what should be done by me just now?”

sanskrit: prahasyovāca bhagavānbṛhaspati rudāradhīḥ | purā tvayā kṛtaṃ yacca tasyedaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam || 42 || māṃ ca uddiśya bho iṃdra tadbhogādeva saṃkṣayaḥ | prāyaścitaṃ hi hatyāyā na dṛṣṭaṃ smṛtikāribhiḥ || 43 ||
english: 42-43. The holy lord Bṛhaspati of liberal mind laughed and said: “O Indra, this is the result of that act of yours committed previously against me. Only by experiencing its result, can it be annihilated. But, no atonement for Brāhmaṇa-slaughter has been seen (i.e. laid down) by the authors of Smṛti texts.

sanskrit: ajñānato hi yajjātaṃ pāpaṃ tasya pratikriyā | kathitā dharmmaśāstrajñaiḥ sakāmasya na vidyate || 44 ||
english: 44. Expiation has been prescribed by those conversant with Dharma Śāstras (Code of Laws) for the sin committed unknowingly. There is no atonement for an offence wilfully committed.

sanskrit: sakāmena kṛtaṃ pāpamakāmaṃ naiva jāyate | tābhyāṃ viṣayabhedena prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate || 45 ||
english: 45. A sin committed by a person intentionally does not become one committed unintentionally. Expiation is laid down for both based on the differences in the objects.

sanskrit: maraṇāṃto vidhiḥ kāryo kāmena hi kṛtena hi | ajñānajanite pāpe prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate || 46 ||
english: 46. If a sin is committed wilfully (deliberately), the expiation is to be performed up to death. Atonement is laid down in case of sins committed unknowingly.

sanskrit: tasmāttvayā kṛtaṃ yacca svayameva hato dvijaḥ | purohitaśca vidvāṃśca tasmānnāsti pratikriyā || 47 ||
english: 47. Since this has been intentionally done by you, since the twice-born, the learned priest has been killed, there is no atonement.

sanskrit: yāvanmaraṇamapyeti tāvadapsu sthiro bhava || 48 ||
english: 48. Stay in the waters here and wait for your death.

sanskrit: śatāśvamedhasaṃjñaṃ ca yatphalaṃ tava durmate | tannaṣṭaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva ghātito hi dvijo yadā || 49 ||
english: 49. The meritorious deed of yours termed ‘performance of one hundred horse-sacrifices’, O evil-minded one, has already been destroyed at the very moment when the twice-born was killed by you.

sanskrit: sacchidre ca yathā toyaṃ na tiṣṭhati ghaṭe'ṇvapi | tathaiva sukṛtaṃ pāpe hīyate ca pradakṣiṇam || 50 ||
english: 50. Just as not a drop of water remains in a pot with holes, similarly meritorious deeds of a sinner go on reducing every moment.

sanskrit: tasmācca daivasaṃyogātprāptaṃ svargādikaṃ ca yaiḥ | yathoktaṃ tadbhavetteṣāṃ dharmiṣṭhānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ || 51 ||
english: 51. Hence, by good luck, if heaven etc. are attained, those can be retained only by really righteous ones. There is no doubt about it.”

sanskrit: etacchrutvā vacastasya śakro vacanamabravīt | kukarmaṇā madīyena prāptametanna saṃśayaḥ || 52 ||
english: 52. On hearing his statement, Indra spoke these words: “Undoubtedly this has fallen to my lot through my own misdeeds.

sanskrit: amarāvatī māśu tvaṃ gaccha devarṣibiḥ saha | lokānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthe devānāṃ ca bṛhaspate | iṃdraṃ kuru mahābhāga yaste manasi rocate || 53 ||
english: 53. Hasten to Amarāvatī along with the celestial sages, O Bṛhaspati. For the purpose of accomplishing the tasks of the worlds as well as of Devas, O sage of great fortune, crown as Indra, anyone whom you approve in your mind.

sanskrit: yathā mṛtastathā haṃ vai brahmahatyāvṛto mahān | rāgadveṣasamutthena pāpenāsmi pariplutaḥ || 54 ||
english: 54. Enveloped by the great devil of Brahmahatyā, I am just like one who is dead. I have been overwhelmed by the sin arising from Rāga (attachment) and Dveṣa (hatred).

sanskrit: tasmāttvarānvitā yūyaṃ devarājānamāśuḥ vai | kurvatu madanujñātāḥ satyaṃ prativadāmi vaḥ || 55 ||
english: 55. Hence hasten all of you to make someone king of Devas. You have my permission for the same. I am speaking the truth to you.”

sanskrit: evamuktāstadā sarve bṛhaspatipurogamāḥ | etyāmarāvatīṃ tūrṇaṃ puraṃdaraviceṣṭitam | kathayāmāsuravyagrā śacīṃ prati yathā tathā || 56 ||
english: 56. On being told thus, all those (Devas) with Bṛhaspati at their head came to Amarāvatī immediately and coolly told Śacī everything about Indra’s activities as they had taken place.

sanskrit: rājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ kāryaṃ vimṛśaṃtaḥ parasparam || 57 ||
english: 57. They consulted one another and began to deliberate thus: ‘What should be done for the sake of the kingdom?’

sanskrit: evaṃ vimṛśyamānānāṃ devānāṃ tatra nāradaḥ | yadṛcchayāgatastatra devarṣiramitadyutiḥ || 58 ||
english: 58. While Devas were thus deliberating, Nārada, the celestial sage of unmeasured splendour, came there by chance.

sanskrit: uvāca pūjito devānkasmādyūyaṃ vicetasaḥ | tenoktāḥ kathayāmāsuḥ sarvaṃ śakrasya ceṣṭitam || 59 ||
english: 59. On being honoured, he asked Devas: “Why are you all sad and perplexed?” On being enquired (thus) they spoke everything about Śakra’s activities:

sanskrit: gatamiṃdrasya ceṃdratvamenasā parameṇa tu | tataḥ provāca tāndevāndevarṣirnārado vacaḥ || 60 ||
english: 60. “Indra’s status of being the lord (of Devas) has come to an end on account of a great sin.” Thereupon Nārada, the celestial sage, spoke these words to those Devas:

sanskrit: yūyaṃ devāśca sarvajñāstapasā vikrameṇa ca | tasmādiṃdro hi kartavyo nahuṣaḥ somavaṃśajaḥ || 61 || so'sminrāṣṭre pratiṣṭhāpyastvaritenaiva nirjarāḥ | ekonamaśvamedhānāṃ śataṃ tena mahātmanā | kṛtamasti mahābhāgā nahuṣeṇa ca yajvanā || 62 ||
english: 61-62. “You are omniscient Devas endowed with the power of penance and valour. Hence Nahuṣa,[2] born in the Lunar race, should be made Indra. He should be established in this realm, O Devas, immediately. Ninety-nine horse-sacrifices have been performed by that noble-souled Nahuṣa, O highly fortunate ones. Nahuṣa was a regular performer of Yajñas

sanskrit: śacyā śrutaṃ ca tadvākyaṃ nāradasya mukhodgatam | gatāṃtaḥpuramavyagrā bāṣpapūritalocanā || 63 ||
english: 63-67. That statement coming out of the mouth of Nārada was heard by Sacī. With her eyes filled with tears and not engaged in anything (seriously), she went into the inner apartment.

sanskrit: nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarve devānvamodayan || 64 || nahuṣaṃ rājyamāroḍhumaikapadyena te yadā | ānīto hi tadā rājā nahuṣo hyamarāvatīm || 65 || rājyaṃ dattaṃ maheṃdrasya suraiḥ sarvairmaharṣibhiḥ | tadāgastyādayaḥ sarve nahuṣaṃ paryupāsata || 66 ||
english: On hearing the words of Nārada, all the Devas congratulated him. They approved of his suggestion to make Nahuṣa the ruler of the realm unanimously. Then, king Nahuṣa was brought to Amarāvatī and the kingdom of Mahendra was given to him by all the Suras and great sages.

sanskrit: gaṃdharvāpsaraso yakṣā vidyādharamahoragāḥ | yakṣāḥ suparṇāḥ patagā ye cānye svargavāsinaḥ || 67 ||
english: Then all of them served Nahuṣa. Agastya and others (sages), Gandharvas, Apsarās, Yakṣas, Vidyādharas, the great serpents, Rākṣasas, the birds of bright wings (suparṇas like Garuḍa) and other heaven-dwellers (served him).

sanskrit: tadā mahotsavo jāto devapuryāṃ niraṃtaraḥ | śaṃkhatūryamṛdaṃgāni nedurduṃdubhayaḥ samam || 68 ||
english: 68. Then in the city of Devas, there was a continuous grand celebration. Concḥs, musical instruments, Mṛdaṅgas and Dundubhis sounded simultaneously.

sanskrit: gāyakāśca jagustatra tathā vādyāni vādakāḥ | nartakā nanṛtustatra tathā rājyamahotsave || 69 ||
english: 69. In that grand celebration of the kingdom of Devas, musicians sang songs, players of instruments played on them and dancers danced.

sanskrit: abhiṣiktastadā tatra bṛhaspatipurogamaiḥ || 70 ||
english: 70. Then he was coronated there by the sages, of whom Bṛhaspati was the foremost.

sanskrit: arcito devasūktaiśca yathā vadgrahapūjanam | kṛtavāṃścaiva ṛṣibhirvidvadbhirbhāvitātmabhiḥ || 71 ||
english: 71. He was worshipped with Deva-Sūkta and was made to perform the worship of Planets in due procedure and with formalities.

sanskrit: tathā ca sarvaiḥ paripūjito mahānrājā surāṇāṃ nahuṣastadānīm | iṃdrāsane ceṃd samānarūpaḥ saṃstūyamānaḥ parameṇa varcasā || 72 ||
english: 72. The great king Nahuṣa was duly honoured and respected by the learned sages of sanctified souls and by all others also. As the king of Suras, he sat on the throne of Indra. He had the same features as those of Indra. Endowed with the greatest splendour, he was eulogized by all.

sanskrit: sugaṃdhadīpaiśca suvāsasā yuto'laṃkārabhogaiḥ suvirājitāṃgaḥ | babhau tadānīṃ nahuṣo munīdraiḥ saṃstūyamāno hi tathā'mareṃdraiḥ || 73 ||
english: 73. Dressed in excellent sweet-scented bright garments and with his person adorned excellently with ornaments and articles of enjoyment, Nahuṣa appeared resplendent as he was being eulogized by prominent sages and leading Devas.

sanskrit: iti paramakalānvito'sau suramunivaragaṇaiśca pūjyamānaḥ | nahuṣanṛpavaro'bhavattadānīṃ hṛdi mahatā hṛcchayenataptaḥ || 74 ||
english: 74. Thus the great king Nahuṣa who was endowed with great ingenuity and worshipped by groups of great Devas and sages, became severely tormented at heart by intense passion (lust).

sanskrit: nahuṣa uvāca | iṃdrāṇī kathamadyaiva nāyāti mama sannidhau | tāṃ cāhvayata śīghraṃ bho mā vilaṃbitumarhatha || 75 ||
english: Nahuṣa said: 75. How is it that Indrāṇī does not come near me? Call her quickly. It does not behove you to delay.

sanskrit: nahupasya vacaḥ śrutvā bṛhaspatirudāradhīḥ | śacībhavanamāsādya uvāca ca savistaram || 76 ||
english: 76. On hearing the words of Nahuṣa, the liberal-minded Bṛhaspati went to Śacī’s abode and spoke in detail:

sanskrit: śakrasya durnimittena hyanīto nahuṣo'tra vai | rājyārte bhāmini tvaṃ ca arddhāsanagatā bhava || 77 ||
english: 77. “It was on account of the calamity fallen on Indra that Nahuṣa was brought here for the sake of the kingdom. O beautiful lady, occupy half of his seat.”

sanskrit: śacī prahasya covāca bṛhaspatimakalmaṣam | asau na paripūrṇo hi yajñaiḥ śakrāsane sthitaḥ | ekonamaśvamedhānāṃ śataṃ kṛtamanena vai || 78 || tasmānna yogyo prahasya covāca bṛhaspatimakalpaṇaṣam | asau na paripūrṇo hi yajñaiḥ śakrāsane sthitaḥ | avāhyavāhanenaiva atrāgatya labheta mām || 79 ||
english: 78-79. Śacī laughed and spoke to sinless Bṛhaspati: “He has occupied the seat of Indra without completing the quota of (hundred) Yajñas. Only ninety-nine horse-sacrifices have been performed by him. Hence, he is not qualified enough to obtain me. Let this be thought over truthfully. If this senseless fellow still continues to be desirous of me, wife of another person, let him obtain me by coming here by means of a vehicle that is carried by undeserving carriers.”

sanskrit: tatheti gatvā tvarito bṛhaspatiruvāca tam | nahuṣaṃ kāmasaṃtaptaṃ śacyoktaṃ ca yathātatham || 80 ||
english: 80. Saying “So be it”, Bṛhaspati returned hurriedly to Nahuṣa who had been distressed through intense lust. He reported to him what was spoken by Śacī in her own words.

sanskrit: tatheti matvā rājāsau nahuṣaḥ kāmamohitaḥ | vimṛśya parayā buddhyā avāhyaṃ kiṃ praśasyate || 81 || sa buddhyā ca ciraṃ smṛtvā brāhmaṇāścatapasvinaḥ | avāhyāśca bhavaṃtyasmādātmānaṃ vāhayāmyaham || 82 || dvābhyāṃ ca tasyāḥ prāptyarthamiti me hṛdi vartate | śibikāṃ ca dadau tābhyāṃ dvijābhyāṃ kāmamohitaḥ || 83 ||
english: 81-84. Saying “So be it”, Nahuṣa who was deluded by lust, thought over it. He deliberated on this intelligently: ‘Who can be the carrier not worthy of being so?’ After thinking about it intelligently and trying to remember for a long time (he decided thus): “The Brāhmaṇas and the ascetics are not usually thought of as carriers. I shall make two of them bear me in order to reach her. This is my decision.” So (the king) who was deluded by lust gave the palanquin to two Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: upaviśya tadā tasyāṃ śivabikāyāṃ samāhitaḥ | sarpasarpeti vacanānnodayāmāsa tau tadā || 84 ||
english: Seated in that palanquin with great concentration, he urged them on with the words “Sarpa, sarpa” (Move on, move on). (Sarpa means ‘serpent’ also.)

sanskrit: agastyaḥ śibikāvāhī tataḥ kruddho'śapannṛpam | viprāṇāmavamaṃtā tvamunmatto'jagaro bhava || 85 ||
english: 85. Agastya who had been one of the palanquin-bearers became infuriated and cursed the king. “You are a lunatic and despiser of Brāhmaṇas; you be a python.”

sanskrit: śāpoktimātrato rājā patito brāhmaṇasya hi | tatraivājagaro bhūtvā vipraśāpo duratyayaḥ || 86 ||
english: 86. Immediately, after the utterance of the curse by the Brāhmaṇa, the king became a python and fell from there itself. Indeed the curse of a Brāhmaṇa is untransgressable.

sanskrit: yathā hi nahuṣo jātastathā sarve'pi tādṛśāḥ | viprāṇāmavamānena patinti niraye'śucau || 87 ||
english: 87. Just as Nahuṣa became (a python), so also all like him fell into dirty hell by disrespecting Brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: tasmāsarvaprayatnena padaṃ prāpya vicakṣaṇaiḥ | apramattairnarairbhāvyamihāmutra ca labdhaye || 88 ||
english: 88. Hence, in order to attain benefits here and hereafter, a wise, circumspect person who has achieved a position of importance, should refrain in all possible ways from committing blunders.

sanskrit: tathaiva nahuṣaḥ sarppo jātoraṇye mahābhaye | evaṃ caivābhavattatra devaloke hyarājakam || 89 ||
english: 89. Nahuṣa became a serpent in a very dreadful forest. Hence there prevailed anarchy in the world of Devas.

sanskrit: tathaiva te surāḥ sarve vismayāviṣṭacetasaḥ | aho bata mahatkaṣṭaṃ prāptaṃ rājñā hyanena vai || 90 ||
english: 90. Similarly, all the Devas were struck with consternation. “Alas! What a wretched condition the king has fallen into!

sanskrit: na martya loko na svargo jāto hyasya durātmanaḥ | satāmavajñayā sadyaḥ sukṛtaṃ dagdhameva hi || 91 ||
english: 91. This evil-minded fellow has obtained neither the mortal world nor the heavenly world. His (fund of) merits has been instantaneously burnt down,

sanskrit: yājñiko hyaparo loke kathyatāṃ ca mahāmune | tadovāca mahātejā nārado munisattamaḥ || 92 ||
english: 92. If there is any other person who has performed (many) Yajñas, let him be named, O great sage.” Then the excellent sage Nārada of great splendour said:

sanskrit: yayātiṃ ca mahābhāgā ānayadhvaṃ tvarānvitāḥ | devadūtāstu vai tūrṇaṃ yayātiṃ drutamānayan || 93 ||
english: 93. “O highly fortunate ones, hasten to bring Yayāti.[3]” Messengers of Devas went immediately and brought Yayāti quickly.

sanskrit: bhrāmarī ganḍamālī ca śvitry atho piśunas tathā / unmatto 'ndhaś ca varjyāḥ syur vedanindaka eva ca //
english: An epileptic man, who suffers from scrofulous swellings of the glands, one afflicted with white leprosy, an informer, a madman, a blind man, and he who cavils at the Veda must (all) be avoided.

sanskrit: hastigo'śvoṣṭradamako nakṣatrair yaś ca jīvati / pakṣiṇāṃ poṣako yaś ca yuddhācāryas tathaiva ca //
english: A trainer of elephants, oxen, horses, or camels, he who subsists by astrology, a bird-fancier, and he who teaches the use of arms,

sanskrit: srotasāṃ bhedako yaś ca teṣāṃ cāvaraṇe rataḥ / gṛhasaṃveśako dūto vṛkṣāropaka eva ca //
english: He who diverts water-courses, and he who delights in obstructing them, an architect, a messenger, and he who plants trees (for money),

sanskrit: śvakrīḍī śyenajīvī ca kanyādūṣaka eva ca / hiṃsro vṛṣalavṛttiś ca gaṇānāṃ caiva yājakaḥ // ācārahīnaḥ klībaś ca nityaṃ yācanakas tathā / kṛṣijīvī ślīpadī ca sadbhir nindita eva ca // aurabhriko māhiṣikaḥ parapūrvāpatis tathā / pretaniryāpakaś caiva varjanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ //
english: A breeder of sporting-dogs, a falconer, one who defiles maidens, he who delights in injuring living creatures, he who gains his subsistence from Sudras, and he who offers sacrifices to the Ganas, He who does not follow the rule of conduct, a (man destitute of energy like a) eunuch, one who constantly asks (for favours), he who lives by agriculture, a club-footed man, and he who is censured by virtuous men, A shepherd, a keeper of buffaloes, the husband of a remarried woman, and a carrier of dead bodies, (all these) must be carefully avoided.

sanskrit: etān vigarhitācārān apāṅkteyān dvijādhamān / dvijātipravaro vidvān ubhayatra vivarjayet //
english: A Brahmana who knows (the sacred law) should shun at (sacrifices) both (to the gods and to the manes) these lowest of twice-born men, whose conduct is reprehensible, and who are unworthy (to sit) in the company (at a repast).

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo tv anadhīyānas tṛṇāgnir iva śāmyati / tasmai havyaṃ na dātavyaṃ na hi bhasmani hūyate //
english: As a fire of dry grass is (unable to consume the offerings and is quickly) extinguished, even so (is it with) an unlearned Brahmana; sacrificial food must not be given to him, since it (would be) offered in ashes.

sanskrit: apāṅktadāne yo dātur bhavaty ūrdhvaṃ phalodayaḥ / daive haviṣi pitrye vā taṃ pravaksyāmy aśeṣataḥ //
english: I will fully declare what result the giver obtains after death, if he gives food, destined for the gods or manes, to a man who is unworthy to sit in the company.

sanskrit: avratair yad dvijair bhuktaṃ parivetrādibhis tathā / apāṅkteyair yad anyaiś ca tad vai rakṣāṃsi bhuñjate //
english: The Rakshasas, indeed, consume (the food) eaten by Brahmanas who have not fulfilled the vow of studentship, by a Parivettri and so forth, and by other men not admissible into the company.

sanskrit: dārāgnihotrasaṃyogaṃ kurute yo 'graje sthite / parivettā sa vijñeyaḥ parivittis tu pūrvajaḥ //
english: He must be considered as a Parivettri who marries or begins the performance of the Agnihotra before his elder brother, but the latter as a Parivitti.

sanskrit: parivittiḥ parivettā yayā ca parividyate / sarve te narakaṃ yānti dātṛyājakapañcamāḥ //
english: The elder brother who marries after the younger, the younger brother who marries before the elder, the female with whom such a marriage is contracted, he who gives her away, and the sacrificing priest, as the fifth, all fall into hell.

sanskrit: bhrātur mṛtasya bhāryāyāṃ yo 'nurajyeta kāmataḥ / dharmeṇāpi niyuktāyāṃ sa jñeyo didhiṣūpatiḥ //
english: He who lasciviously dallies with the widow of a deceased brother, though she be appointed (to bear a child by him) in accordance with the sacred law, must be known to be a Didhishupati.

sanskrit: paradāreṣu jāyete dvau sutau kuṇḍagolakau / patyau jīvati kuṇḍaḥ syān mṛte bhartari golakaḥ //
english: Two (kinds of) sons, a Kunda and a Golaka, are born by wives of other men; (he who is born) while the husband lives, will be a Kunda, and (he who is begotten) after the husband's death, a Golaka.

sanskrit: tau tu jātau parakṣetre prāṇinau pretya ceha ca / dattāni havyakavyāni nāśayanti pradāyinām //
english: But those two creatures, who are born of wives of other men, cause to the giver the loss (of the rewards), both in this life and after death, for the food sacred to gods or manes which has been given (to them).

sanskrit: apāṅktyo yāvataḥ paṅktyān bhuñjānān anupaśyati / tāvatāṃ na phalaṃ tatra dātā prāpnoti bāliśaḥ //
english: The foolish giver (of a funeral repast) does not reap the reward for as many worthy guests as a man, inadmissible into company, can look on while they are feeding.

sanskrit: vīkṣyāndho navateḥ kāṇaḥ ṣaṣṭeḥ śvitrī śatasya tu / pāparogī sahasrasya dātur nāśayate phalam //
english: A blind man by his presence causes to the giver (of the feast) the loss of the reward for ninety (guests), a one-eyed man for sixty, one who suffers from white leprosy for a hundred, and one punished by a (terrible) disease for a thousand.

sanskrit: yāvataḥ saṃspṛśed aṅgair brāhmaṇāñ śūdrayājakaḥ / tāvatāṃ na bhaved dātuḥ phalaṃ dānasya paurtikam //
english: The giver (of a Sraddha) loses the reward, due for such a non-sacrificial gift, for as many Brahmanas as a (guest) who sacrifices for Sudras may touch (during the meal) with his limbs.

sanskrit: vedavic cāpi vipro 'sya lobhāt kṛtvā pratigraham / vināśaṃ vrajati kṣipram āmapātram ivāmbhasi // somavikrayiṇe viṣṭhā bhiṣaje pūyaśoṇitam / naṣṭaṃ devalake dattam apratiṣṭhaṃ tu vārdhuṣau // yat tu vāṇijake dattaṃ neha nāmutra tad bhavet / bhasmanīva hutaṃ dravyaṃ tathā paunarbhave dvije //
english: And if a Brahmana, though learned in the Veda, accepts through covetousness a gift from such (a man), he will quickly perish, like a vessel of unburnt clay in water.180 (Food) given to a seller of Soma becomes ordure, (that given) to a physician pus and blood, but (that presented) to a temple-priest is lost, and (that given) to a usurer finds no place (in the world of the gods). What has been given to a Brahmana who lives by trade that is not (useful) in this world and the next, and (a present) to a Brahmana born of a remarried woman (resembles) an oblation thrown into ashes.

sanskrit: itareṣu tv apāṅktyeṣu yathoddiṣṭeṣv asādhuṣu / medo'sṛṅmāṃsamajjāsthi vadanty annaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ //
english: But the wise declare that the food which (is offered) to other unholy, inadmissible men, enumerated above, (is turned into) adipose secretions, blood, flesh, marrow, and bone.

sanskrit: apāṅktyopahatā paṅktiḥ pāvyate yair dvijottamaiḥ / tān nibodhata kārtsnyena dvijāgryān paṅktipāvanān //
english: Now hear by what chief of twice-born men a company defiled by (the presence of) unworthy (guests) is purified, and the full (description of) the Brahmanas who sanctify a company.

sanskrit: agryāḥ sarveṣu vedeṣu sarvapravacaneṣu ca / śrotriyānvayajāś caiva vijñeyāḥ paṅktipāvanāḥ //
english: Those men must be considered as the sanctifiers of a company who are most learned in all the Vedas and in all the Angas, and who are the descendants of Srotriyas.

sanskrit: triṇāciketaḥ pañcāgnis trisuparṇaḥ ṣaḍaṅgavit / brahmadeyātmasantāno jyeṣṭhasāmaga eva ca //
english: A Trinakiketa, one who keeps five sacred fires, a Trisuparna, one who is versed in the six Angas, the son of a woman married according to the Brahma rite, one who sings the Gyeshthasaman,

sanskrit: vedārthavit pravaktā ca brahmacārī sahasradaḥ / śatāyuś caiva vijñeyā brāhmaṇāḥ paṅktipāvanāḥ //
english: One who knows the meaning of the Veda, and he who expounds it, a student, one who has given a thousand (cows), and a centenarian must be considered as Brahmanas who sanctify a company.

sanskrit: pūrvedyur aparedyur vā śrāddhakarmaṇy upasthite / nimantrayeta tryavarān samyag viprān yathoditān //
english: On the day before the Sraddha-rite is performed, or on the day when it takes place, let him invite with due respect at least three Brahmanas, such as have been mentioned above.

sanskrit: nimantrito dvijaḥ pitrye niyatātmā bhavet sadā / na ca chandāṃsy adhīyīta yasya śrāddhaṃ ca tad bhavet //
english: A Brahmana who has been invited to a (rite) in honour of the manes shall always control himself and not recite the Veda, and he who performs the Sraddha (must act in the same manner).

sanskrit: nimantritān hi pitara upatiṣṭhanti tān dvijān / vāyuvac cānugacchanti tathāsīnān upāsate //
english: For the manes attend the invited Brahmanas, follow them (when they walk) like the wind, and sit near them when they are seated.

sanskrit: ketitas tu yathānyāyaṃ havye kavye dvijottamaḥ / kathaṃ cid apy atikrāman pāpaḥ sūkaratāṃ vrajet // āmantritas tu yaḥ śrāddhe vṛśalyā saha modate / dātur yad duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃ cit tat sarvaṃ pratipadyate //
english: But a Brahmana who, being duly invited to a rite in honour of the gods or of the manes, in any way breaks (the appointment), becomes guilty (of a crime), and (in his next birth) a hog. But he who, being invited to a Sraddha, dallies with a Sudra woman, takes upon himself all the sins which the giver (of the feast) committed.

sanskrit: akrodhanāḥ śaucaparāḥ satataṃ brahmacāriṇaḥ / nyastaśastrā mahābhāgāḥ pitaraḥ pūrvadevatāḥ //
english: The manes are primeval deities, free from anger, careful of purity, ever chaste, averse from strife, and endowed with great virtues.

sanskrit: yasmād utpattir eteṣāṃ sarveṣām apy aśeṣataḥ / ye ca yair upacaryāḥ syur niyamais tān nibodhata //
english: Now learn fully from whom all these (manes derive) their origin, and with what ceremonies they ought to be worshipped.

sanskrit: manor hairaṇyagarbhasya ye marīcyādayaḥ sutāḥ / teṣām ṛṣīṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ putrāḥ pitṛgaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ //
english: The (various) classes of the manes are declared to be the sons of all those sages, Mariki and the rest, who are children of Manu, the son of Hiranyagarbha.

sanskrit: virāṭsutāḥ somasadaḥ sādhyānāṃ pitaraḥ smṛtāḥ / agniṣvāttāś ca devānāṃ mārīcā lokaviśrutāḥ //
english: The Somasads, the sons of Virag, are stated to be the manes of the Sadhyas, and the Agnishvattas, the children of Mariki, are famous in the world (as the manes) of the gods.

sanskrit: daityadānavayakṣāṇāṃ gandharvoragarakṣasām / suparṇakinnarāṇāṃ ca smṛtā barhiṣado 'trijāḥ //
english: The Barhishads, born of Atri, are recorded to be (the manes) of the Daityas, Danavas, Yakshas, Gandharvas, Snake-deities,Rakshasas, Suparnas, and a Kimnaras,

sanskrit: somapā nāma viprāṇāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ havirbhujaḥ / vaiśyānām ājyapā nāma śūdrāṇāṃ tu sukālinaḥ //
english: The Somapas those of the Brahmanas, the Havirbhugs those of the Kshatriyas, the Agyapas those of the Vaisyas, but the Sukalins those of the Sudras.

sanskrit: somapās tu kaveḥ putrā haviṣmanto 'ṅgiraḥsutāḥ / pulastyasyājyapāḥ putrā vasiṣṭhasya sukālinaḥ //
english: The Somapas are the sons of Kavi (Bhrigu), the Havishmats the children of Angiras, the Agyapas the offspring of Pulastya, but the Sukalins (the issue) of Vasishtha.

sanskrit: agnidagdhānagnidagdhān kāvyān barhiṣadas tathā / agniṣvāttāṃś ca saumyāṃś ca viprāṇām eva nirdiśet //
english: One should know that (other classes), the Agnidagdhas, the Anagnidagdhas, the Kavyas, the Barhishads, the Agnishvattas, and the Saumyas, are (the manes) of the Brahmanas alone.

sanskrit: ya ete tu gaṇā mukhyāḥ pitṝṇāṃ parikīrtitāḥ / teṣām apīha vijñeyaṃ putrapautram anantakam //
english: But know also that there exist in this (world) countless sons and grandsons of those chief classes of manes which have been enumerated.

sanskrit: ṛṣibhyaḥ pitaro jātāḥ pitṛbhyo devamānavāḥ / devebhyas tu jagat sarvaṃ caraṃ sthāṇv anupūrvaśaḥ //
english: From the sages sprang the manes, from the manes the gods and the Danavas, but from the gods the whole world, both the movable and the immovable in due order.

sanskrit: rājatair bhājanair eṣām atho vā rajatānvitaiḥ / vāry api śraddhayā dattam akṣayāyopakalpate //
english: Even water offered with faith (to the manes) in vessels made of silver or adorned with silver, produces endless (bliss).

sanskrit: daivakāryād dvijātīnāṃ pitṛkāryaṃ viśiṣyate / daivaṃ hi pitṛkāryasya pūrvam āpyāyanaṃ smṛtam //
english: For twice-born men the rite in honour of the manes is more important than the rite in honour of the gods; for the offering to the gods which precedes (the Sraddhas), has been declared to be a means of fortifying (the latter).

sanskrit: teṣām ārakṣabhūtaṃ tu pūrvaṃ daivaṃ niyojayet / raksāṃsi vipralumpanti śrāddham ārakṣavarjitam //
english: Let him first invite a (Brahmana) in honour of the gods as a protection for the (offering to the manes); for the Rakshasas destroy a funeral sacrifice which is left without such a protection.

sanskrit: daivādyantaṃ tad īheta pitrādyantaṃ na tad bhavet / pitrādyantaṃ tv īhamānaḥ kṣipraṃ naśyati sānvayaḥ //
english: Let him make (the Sraddha) begin and end with (a rite) in honour of the gods; it shall not begin and end with a (rite) to the manes; for he who makes it begin and end with a (rite) in honour of the manes, soon perishes together with his progeny.

sanskrit: śuciṃ deśaṃ viviktaṃ ca gomayenopalepayet / dakṣināpravaṇaṃ caiva prayatnenopapādayet //
english: Let him smear a pure and secluded place with cowdung, and carefully make it sloping towards the south.

sanskrit: avakāśeṣu cokṣeṣu jalatīreṣu caiva hi / vivikteṣu ca tuṣyanti dattena pitaraḥ sadā //
english: The manes are always pleased with offerings made in open, naturally pure places, on the banks of rivers, and in secluded spots.

sanskrit: āsaneṣūpakḷpteṣu barhiṣmatsu pṛthakpṛthak / upaspṛṣṭodakān samyag viprāṃs tān upaveśayet // upaveśya tu tān viprān āsaneṣv ajugupsitān / gandhamālyaiḥ surabhibhir arcayed daivapūrvakam // teṣām udakam ānīya sapavitrāṃs tilān api / agnau kuryād anujñāto brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇaiḥ saha //
english: The (sacrificer) shall make the (invited) Brahmanas, who have duly performed their ablutions, sit down on separate, prepared seats, on which blades of Kusa grass have been placed. Having placed those blameless Brahmanas on their seats, he shall honour them with fragrant garlands and perfumes, beginning with (those who are invited in honour of) the gods. Having presented to them water, sesamum grains, and blades of Kusa grass, the Brahmana (sacrificer) shall offer (oblations) in the sacred fire, after having received permission (to do so) from (all) the Brahmana (guests) conjointly.

sanskrit: agneḥ somayamābhyāṃ ca kṛtvāpyāyanam āditaḥ / havirdānena vidhivat paścāt saṃtarpayet pitṝn //
english: Having first, according to the rule, performed, as a means of protecting (the Sraddha), oblations to Agni, to Soma, and to Yama, let him afterwards satisfy the manes by a gift of sacrificial food.

sanskrit: agnyabhāve tu viprasya pāṇāv evopapādayet / yo hy agniḥ sa dvijo viprair mantradarśibhir ucyate //
english: But if no (sacred) fire (is available), he shall place (the offerings) into the hand of a Brahmana; for Brahmanas who know the sacred texts declare, 'What fire is, even such is a Brahmana.'

sanskrit: akrodhanān suprasādān vadanty etān purātanān / lokasyāpyāyane yuktān śrāddhadevān dvijottamān //
english: They (also) call those first of twice-born men the ancient deities of the funeral sacrifice, free from anger, easily pleased, employed in making men prosper.

sanskrit: apasavyam agnau kṛtvā sarvam āvṛtya vikramam / apasavyena hastena nirvaped udakaṃ bhuvi //
english: After he has performed (the oblations) in the fire, (and) the whole series of ceremonies in such a manner that they end in the south, let him sprinkle water with his right hand on the spot (where the cakes are to be placed).

sanskrit: trīṃs tu tasmād dhaviḥśeṣāt piṇḍān kṛtvā samāhitaḥ / audakenaiva vidhinā nirvaped dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ //
english: But having made three cakes out of the remainder of that sacrificial food, he must, concentrating his mind and turning towards the south, place them on (Kusa grass) exactly in the same manner in which (he poured out the libations of) water.

sanskrit: nyupya piṇḍāṃs tatas tāṃs tu prayato vidhipūrvakam / teṣu darbheṣu taṃ hastaṃ nirmṛjyāl lepabhāginām //
english: Having offered those cakes according to the (prescribed) rule, being pure, let him wipe the same hand with (the roots of) those blades of Kusa grass for the sake of the (three ancestors) who partake of the wipings (lepa).

sanskrit: ācamyodakparāvṛtya trir āyamya śanair asūn / ṣaḍ ṛtūṃś ca namaskuryāt pitṝn eva ca mantravat //
english: Having (next) sipped water, turned round (towards the north), and thrice slowly suppressed his breath, (the sacrificer) who knows the sacred texts shall worship (the guardian deities of) the six seasons and the manes.

sanskrit: udakaṃ ninayec cheṣaṃ śanaiḥ piṇḍāntike punaḥ / avajighrec ca tān piṇḍān yathānyuptān samāhitaḥ //
english: Let him gently pour out the remainder of the water near the cakes, and, with fixed attention, smell those cakes, in the order in which they were placed (on the ground).

sanskrit: piṇḍebhyas tv alpikāṃ mātrāṃ samādāyānupūrvaśaḥ / tān eva viprān āsīnān vidhivat pūrvam āśayet //
english: But taking successively very small portions from the cakes, he shall make those seated Brahmana eat them, in accordance with the rule, before (their dinner).

sanskrit: dhriyamāṇe tu pitari pūrveṣām eva nirvapet / vipravad vāpi taṃ śrāddhe svakaṃ pitaram āśayet //
english: But if the (sacrificer's) father is living, he must offer (the cakes) to three remoter (ancestors); or he may also feed his father at the funeral sacrifice as (one of the) Brahmana (guests).

sanskrit: pitā yasya nivṛttaḥ syāj jīvec cāpi pitāmahaḥ / pituḥ sa nāma saṅkīrtya kīrtayet prapitāmaham //
english: But he whose father is dead, while his grandfather lives, shall, after pronouncing his father's name, mention (that of) his great-grandfather.

sanskrit: pitāmaho vā tacchrāddhaṃ bhuñjītety abravīn manuḥ / kāmaṃ vā samanujñātaḥ svayam eva samācaret //
english: Manu has declared that either the grandfather may eat at that Sraddha (as a guest), or (the grandson) having received permission, may perform it, as he desires.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ dattvā tu hasteṣu sapavitraṃ tilodakam / tatpiṇḍāgraṃ prayaccheta svadhaiṣām astv iti bruvan // pāṇibhyāṃ tūpasaṃgṛhya svayam annasya vardhitam / viprāntike pitṝn dhyāyan śanakair upanikṣipet //
english: Having poured water mixed with sesamum, in which a blade of Kusa grass has been placed, into the hands of the (guests), he shall give (to each) that (above-mentioned) portion of the cake, saying, 'To those, Svadha!' But carrying (the vessel) filled with food with both hands, the (sacrificer) himself shall gently place it before the Brahmanas, meditating on the manes.

sanskrit: ubhayor hastayor muktaṃ yad annam upanīyate / tad vipralumpanty asurāḥ sahasā duṣṭacetasaḥ //
english: The malevolent Asuras forcibly snatch away that food which is brought without being held with both hands.

sanskrit: guṇāṃś ca sūpaśākādyān payo dadhi ghṛtaṃ madhu / vinyaset prayataḥ pūrvaṃ bhūmāv eva samāhitaḥ //
english: Let him, being pure and attentive, carefully place on the ground the seasoning (for the rice), such as broths and pot herbs, sweet and sour milk, and honey,

sanskrit: bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca vividhaṃ mūlāni ca phalāni ca / hṛdyāni caiva māṃsāni pānāni surabhīṇi ca //
english: (As well as) various (kinds of) hard food which require mastication, and of soft food, roots, fruits, savoury meat, and fragrant drinks.

sanskrit: upanīya tu tat sarvaṃ śanakaiḥ susamāhitaḥ / pariveṣayeta prayato guṇān sarvān pracodayan //
english: All this he shall present (to his guests), being pure and attentive, successively invite them to partake of each (dish), proclaiming its qualities.

sanskrit: nāsram āpātayej jātu na kupyen nānṛtaṃ vadet / na pādena spṛśed annaṃ na caitad avadhūnayet //
english: Let him on no account drop a tear, become angry or utter an untruth, nor let him touch the food with his foot nor violently shake it.

sanskrit: asraṃ gamayati pretān kopo 'rīn anṛtaṃ śunaḥ / pādasparśas tu rakṣāṃsi duṣkṛtīn avadhūnanam //
english: A tear sends the (food) to the Pretas, anger to his enemies, a falsehood to the dogs, contact with his foot to the Rakshasas, a shaking to the sinners.

sanskrit: yad yad roceta viprebhyas tat tad dadyād amatsaraḥ / brahmodyāś ca kathāḥ kuryāt pitṝṇām etad īpsitam //
english: Whatever may please the Brahmanas, let him give without grudging it; let him give riddles from the Veda, for that is agreeable to the manes.

sanskrit: svādhyāyaṃ śrāvayet pitrye dharmaśāstrāṇi caiva hi / ākhyānānītihāsāṃś ca purāṇāni khilāni ca //
english: At a (sacrifice in honour) of the manes, he must let (his guests) hear the Veda, the Institutes of the sacred law, legends, tales, Puranas, and Khilas.

sanskrit: harṣayed brāhmaṇāṃs tuṣṭo bhojayec ca śanaiḥśanaiḥ / annādyenāsakṛc caitān guṇaiś ca paricodayet //
english: Himself being delighted, let him give delight to the Brahmanas, cause them to partake gradually and slowly (of each dish), and repeatedly invite (them to eat) by (offering) the food and (praising) its qualities.

sanskrit: vratastham api dauhitraṃ śrāddhe yatnena bhojayet / kutapaṃ cāsanaṃ dadyāt tilaiś ca vikiren mahīm //
english: Let him eagerly entertain at a funeral sacrifice a daughter's son, though he be a student, and let him place a Nepal blanket on the on the seat (of each guest), scattering sesamum grains on the ground.

sanskrit: trīṇi śrāddhe pavitrāṇi dauhitraḥ kutapas tilāḥ / trīṇi cātra praśaṃsanti śaucam akrodham atvarām //
english: There are three means of sanctification, (to be used) at a Sraddha, a daughter's son, a Nepal blanket, and sesamum grains; and they recommend three (other things) for it, cleanliness, suppression of anger, and absence of haste.

sanskrit: atyuṣṇaṃ sarvam annaṃ syād bhuñjīraṃs te ca vāgyatāḥ / na ca dvijātayo brūyur dātrā pṛṣṭā havirguṇān //
english: All the food must be very hot, and the (guests) shall eat in silence; (even though) asked by the giver (of the feast), the Brahmanas shall not proclaim the qualities of the sacrificial food.

sanskrit: yāvad uṣmā bhavaty annaṃ yāvad aśnanti vāgyatāḥ / pitaras tāvad aśnanti yāvan noktā havirguṇāḥ //
english: As long as the food remains warm, as long as they eat in silence, as long as the qualities of the food are not proclaimed, so long the manes partake (of it).

sanskrit: yad veṣṭitaśirā bhuṅkte yad bhuṅkte dakṣiṇāmukhaḥ / sopānatkaś ca yad bhuṅkte tad vai rakṣāṃsi bhuñjate //
english: What (a guest) eats, covering his head, what he eats with his face turned towards the south, what he eats with sandals on (his feet), that the Rakshasas consume.

sanskrit: cāṇḍālaś ca varāhaś ca kukkuṭaḥ śvā tathaiva ca / rajasvalā ca ṣaṇḍhaś ca nekṣerann aśnato dvijān //
english: A Kandala, a village pig, a cock, a dog, a menstruating woman, and a eunuch must not look at the Brahmanas while they eat.

sanskrit: home pradāne bhojye ca yad ebhir abhivīkṣyate / daive haviṣi pitrye vā tad gacchaty ayathātatham //
english: What (any of) these sees at a burnt-oblation, at a (solemn) gift, at a dinner (given to Brahmanas), or at any rite in honour of the gods and manes, that produces not the intended result.

sanskrit: ghrāṇena sūkaro hanti pakṣavātena kukkuṭaḥ / śvā tu dṛṣṭinipātena sparśeṇāvaravarṇajaḥ //
english: A boar makes (the rite) useless by inhaling the smell (of the offerings), a cock by the air of his wings, a dog by throwing his eye (on them), a low-caste man by touching (them).

sanskrit: khañjo vā yadi vā kāṇo dātuḥ preṣyo 'pi vā bhavet / hīnātiriktagātro vā tam apy apanayet punaḥ //
english: If a lame man, a one-eyed man, one deficient in a limb, or one with a redundant limb, be even the servant of the performer (of the Sraddha), he must be removed from that place (where the Sraddha is held).

sanskrit: brāhmaṇaṃ bhikṣukaṃ vāpi bhojanārtham upasthitam / brāhmaṇair abhyanujñātaḥ śaktitaḥ pratipūjayet //
english: To a Brahmana (householder), or to an ascetic who comes for food, he may, with the permission of (his) Brahmana (guests), show honour according to his ability.

sanskrit: sārvavarṇikam annādyaṃ saṃnīyāplāvya vāriṇā / samutsṛjed bhuktavatām agrato vikiran bhuvi //
english: Let him mix all the kinds of food together, sprinkle them with water and put them, scattering them (on Kusa grass), down on the ground in front of (his guests), when they have finished their meal.

sanskrit: asaṃskṛtapramītānāṃ tyāgināṃ kulayoṣitām / ucchiṣṭaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ syād darbheṣu vikiraś ca yaḥ // uccheṣaṇāṃ bhūmigatam ajihmasyāśaṭhasya ca / dāsavargasya tat pitrye bhāgadheyaṃ pracakṣate //
english: The remnant (in the dishes), and the portion scattered on Kusa grass, shall be the share of deceased (children) who received not the sacrament (of cremation) and of those who (unjustly) forsook noble wives. They declare the fragments which have fallen on the ground at a (Sraddha) to the manes, to be the share of honest, dutiful servants.

sanskrit: āsapiṇḍakriyākarma dvijāteḥ saṃsthitasya tu / adaivaṃ bhojayec chrāddhaṃ piṇḍam ekaṃ ca nirvapet //
english: But before the performance of the Sapindikarana, one must feed at the funeral sacrifice in honour of a (recently-) deceased Aryan (one Brahmana) without (making an offering) to the gods, and give one cake only.

sanskrit: sahapiṇḍakriyāyāṃ tu kṛtāyām asya dharmataḥ / anayaivāvṛtā kāryaṃ piṇḍanirvapanaṃ sutaiḥ //
english: But after the Sapindikarana of the (deceased father) has been performed according to the sacred law, the sons must offer the cakes with those ceremonies, (described above.)

sanskrit: śrāddhaṃ bhuktvā ya ucchiṣṭaṃ vṛṣalāya prayacchati / sa mūḍho narakaṃ yāti kālasūtram avākśirāḥ //
english: The foolish man who, after having eaten a Sraddha (-dinner), gives the leavings to a Sudra, falls headlong into the Kalasutra hell.

sanskrit: śrāddhabhug vṛṣalītalpaṃ tad ahar yo 'dhigacchati / tasyāḥ purīṣe taṃ māsaṃ pitaras tasya śerate //
english: If the partaker of a Sraddha (-dinner) enters on the same day the bed of a Sudra female, the manes of his (ancestors) will lie during that month in her ordure.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭvā svaditam ity evaṃ tṛptān ācāmayet tataḥ / ācāntāṃś cānujānīyād abhito ramyatām iti //
english: Having addressed the question, 'Have you dined well?' (to his guests), let him give water for sipping to them who are satisfied, and dismiss them, after they have sipped water, (with the words) 'Rest either (here or at home)!'

sanskrit: svadhāstv ity eva taṃ brūyur brāhmaṇās tadanantaram / svadhākāraḥ parā hy āṣīḥ sarveṣu pitṛkarmasu //
english: The Brahmana (guests) shall then answer him, 'Let there be Svadha;' for at all rites in honour of the manes the word Svadha is the highest benison.

sanskrit: tato bhuktavatāṃ teṣām annaśeṣaṃ nivedayet / yathā brūyus tathā kuryād anujñātas tato dvijaiḥ //
english: Next let him inform (his guests) who have finished their meal, of the food which remains; with the permission of the Brahmanas let him dispose (of that), as they may direct.

sanskrit: pitrye svaditam ity eva vācyaṃ goṣṭhe tu suśṛtam / saṃpannam ity abhyudaye daive rucitam ity api // aparāhṇas tathā darbhā vāstusaṃpādanaṃ tilāḥ / sṛṣṭir mṛṣṭir dvijāś cāgryāḥ śrāddhakarmasu saṃpadaḥ //
english: At a (Sraddha) in honour of the manes one must use (in asking of the guests if they are satisfied, the word) svaditam; at a Goshthi-sraddha, (the word) susrutam; at a Vriddhi-sraddha, (the word) sampannam; and at (a rite) in honour of the gods, (the word) rukitam. The afternoon, Kusa grass, the due preparation of the dwelling, sesamum grains, liberality, the careful preparation of the food, and (the company of) distinguished Brahmanas are true riches at all funeral sacrifices.

sanskrit: darbhāḥ pavitraṃ pūrvāhṇo haviṣyāṇi ca sarvaśaḥ / pavitraṃ yac ca pūrvoktaṃ vijñeyā havyasaṃpadaḥ //
english: Know that Kusa grass, purificatory (texts), the morning, sacrificial viands of all kinds, and those means of purification, mentioned above, are blessings at a sacrifice to the gods.

sanskrit: munyannāni payaḥ somo māṃsaṃ yac cānupaskṛtam / aksāralavaṇaṃ caiva prakṛtyā havir ucyate //
english: The food eaten by hermits in the forest, milk, Soma-juice, meat which is not prepared (with spices), and salt unprepared by art, are called, on account of their nature, sacrificial food.

sanskrit: visṛjya brāhmaṇāṃs tāṃs tu niyato vāgyataḥ śuciḥ / dakṣiṇāṃ diśam ākāṅkṣan yācetemān varān pitṝn //
english: Having dismissed the (invited) Brahmanas, let him, with a concentrated mind, silent and pure, look towards the south and ask these blessings of the manes:

sanskrit: dātāro no 'bhivardhantāṃ vedāḥ saṃtatir eva ca / śraddhā ca no mā vyagamad bahudeyaṃ ca no 'stv iti //
english: 'May liberal men abound with us! May (our knowledge of) the Vedas and (our) progeny increase! May faith not forsake us! May we have much to give (to the needy)!'

sanskrit: evaṃ nirvapaṇaṃ kṛtvā piṇḍāṃs tāṃs tadanantaram / gāṃ vipram ajam agniṃ vā prāśayed apsu vā kṣipet //
english: Having thus offered (the cakes), let him, after (the prayer), cause a cow, a Brahmana, a goat, or the sacred fire to consume those cakes, or let him throw them into water.

sanskrit: piṇḍanirvapaṇaṃ ke cit parastād eva kurvate / vayobhiḥ khādayanty anye prakṣipanty anale 'psu vā //
english: Some make the offering of the cakes after (the dinner); some cause (them) to be eaten by birds or throw them into fire or into water.

sanskrit: pativratā dharmapatnī pitṛpūjanatatparā / madhyamaṃ tu tataḥ piṇḍam adyāt samyak sutārthinī // āyuṣmantaṃ sutaṃ sūte yaśomedhāsamanvitam / dhanavantaṃ prajāvantaṃ sāttvikaṃ dhārmikaṃ tathā //
english: The (sacrificer's) first wife, who is faithful and intent on the worship of the manes, may eat the middle-most cake, (if she be) desirous of bearing a son. (Thus) she will bring forth a son who will be long-lived, famous, intelligent, rich, the father of numerous offspring, endowed with (the quality of) goodness, and righteous.

sanskrit: praksālya hastāv ācāmya jñātiprāyaṃ prakalpayet / jñātibhyaḥ satkṛtaṃ dattvā bāndhavān api bhojayet //
english: Having washed his hands and sipped water, let him prepare (food) for his paternal relations and, after giving it to them with due respect, let him feed his maternal relatives also.

sanskrit: uccheṣaṇaṃ tu tat tiṣṭhed yāvad viprā visarjitāḥ / tato gṛhabaliṃ kuryād iti dharmo vyavasthitaḥ //
english: But the remnants shall be left (where they lie) until the Brahmanas have been dismissed; afterwards he shall perform the (daily) domestic Bali-offering; that is a settled (rule of the) sacred law.

sanskrit: havir yac cirarātrāya yac cānantyāya kalpate / pitṛbhyo vidhivad dattaṃ tat pravakṣyāmy aśeṣataḥ //
english: I will now fully declare what kind of sacrificial food, given to the manes according to the rule, will serve for a long time or for eternity.

sanskrit: tilair vrīhiyavair māṣair adbhir mūlaphalena vā / dattena māsaṃ tṛpyanti vidhivat pitaro nṛnām //
english: The ancestors of men are satisfied for one month with sesamum grains, rice, barley, masha beans, water, roots, and fruits, which have been given according to the prescribed rule,

sanskrit: dvau māsau matsyamāṃsena trīn māsān hāriṇena tu / aurabhreṇātha caturaḥ śākunenātha pañca vai //
english: Two months with fish, three months with the meat of gazelles, four with mutton, and five indeed with the flesh of birds,

sanskrit: ṣaṇmāsāṃś chāgamāṃsena pārṣatena ca sapta vai / aṣṭāv enasya māṃsena rauraveṇa navaiva tu //
english: Six months with the flesh of kids, seven with that of spotted deer, eight with that of the black antelope, but nine with that of the (deer called) Ruru,

sanskrit: daśamāsāṃs tu tṛpyanti varāhamahiṣāmiṣaiḥ / śaśakūrmayos tu māṃsena māsān ekādaśaiva tu // saṃvatsaraṃ tu gavyena payasā pāyasena ca / vārdhrīṇasasya māṃsena tṛptir dvādaśavārṣikī //
english: Ten months they are satisfied with the meat of boars and buffaloes, but eleven months indeed with that of hares and tortoises, One year with cow-milk and milk-rice; from the flesh of a long-eared white he-goat their satisfaction endures twelve years.

sanskrit: kālaśākaṃ mahāśalkāḥ khaṅgalohāmiṣaṃ madhu / ānantyāyaiva kalpyante munyannāni ca sarvaśaḥ //
english: The (vegetable called) Kalasaka, (the fish called) Mahasalka, the flesh of a rhinoceros and that of a red goat, and all kinds of food eaten by hermits in the forest serve for an endless time.

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cin madhunā miśraṃ pradadyāt tu trayodaśīm / tad apy akṣayam eva syād varṣāsu ca maghāsu ca //
english: Whatever (food), mixed with honey, one gives on the thirteenth lunar day in the rainy season under the asterism of Maghah, that also procures endless (satisfaction).

sanskrit: api naḥ sa kule bhūyād yo no dadyāt trayodaśīm / pāyasaṃ madhusarpirbhyāṃ prāk chāye kuñjarasya ca //
english: 'May such a man (the manes say) be born in our family who will give us milk-rice, with honey and clarified butter, on the thirteenth lunar day (of the month of Bhadrapada) and (in the afternoon) when the shadow of an elephant falls towards the east.'

sanskrit: yad yad dadāti vidhivat samyak śraddhāsamanvitaḥ / tat tat pitṝṇāṃ bhavati paratrānantam akṣayam //
english: Whatever (a man), full of faith, duly gives according to the prescribed rule, that becomes in the other world a perpetual and imperishable (gratification) for the manes.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇapakṣe daśamyādau varjayitvā caturdaśīm / śrāddhe praśastās tithayo yathaitā na tathetarāḥ //
english: The days of the dark half of the month, beginning with the tenth, but excepting the fourteenth, are recommended for a funeral sacrifice; (it is) not thus (with) the others.

sanskrit: yukṣu kurvan dinarkṣeṣu sarvān kāmān samaśnute / ayukṣu tu pitṝn sarvān prajāṃ prāpnoti puṣkalām //
english: He who performs it on the even (lunar) days and under the even constellations, gains (the fulfilment of) all his wishes; he who honours the manes on odd (lunar days) and under odd (constellations), obtains distinguished offspring.

sanskrit: yathā caivāparaḥ pakṣaḥ pūrvapakṣād viśiṣyate / tathā śrāddhasya pūrvāhṇād aparāhṇo viśiṣyate //
english: As the second half of the month is preferable to the first half, even so the afternoon is better for (the performance of) a funeral sacrifice than the forenoon.

sanskrit: prācīnāvītinā samyag apasavyam atandriṇā / pitryam ā nidhanāt kāryaṃ vidhivad darbhapāṇinā //
english: Let him, untired, duly perform the (rites) in honour of the manes in accordance with the prescribed rule, passing the sacred thread over the right shoulder, proceeding from the left to the right (and) holding Kusa grass in his hands, up to the end (of the ceremony).

sanskrit: rātrau śrāddhaṃ na kurvīta rākṣasī kīrtitā hi sā / saṃdhyayor ubhayoś caiva sūrye caivācirodite //
english: Let him not perform a funeral sacrifice at night, because the (night) is declared to belong to the Rakshasas, nor in the twilight, nor when the sun has just risen.

sanskrit: anena vidhinā śrāddhaṃ trir abdasyeha nirvapet / hemantagrīṣmavarṣāsu pāñcayajñikam anvaham //
english: Let him offer here below a funeral sacrifice, according to the rule given above, (at least) thrice a year, in winter, in summer, and in the rainy season, but that which is included among the five great sacrifices, every day.

sanskrit: na paitṛyajñiyo homo laukike 'gnau vidhīyate / na darśena vinā śrāddham āhitāgner dvijanmanaḥ //
english: The burnt-oblation, offered at a sacrifice to the manes, must not be made in a common fire; a Brahmana who keeps a sacred fire (shall) not (perform) a funeral sacrifice except on the new-moon day.

sanskrit: yad eva tarpayaty adbhiḥ pitṝn snātvā dvijottamaḥ / tenaiva kṛtsnam āpnoti pitṛyajñakriyāphalam //
english: Even when a Brahmana, after bathing, satisfies the manes with water, he obtains thereby the whole reward for the performance of the (daily) Sraddha.

sanskrit: vasūn vadanti tu pitṝn rudrāṃś caiva pitāmahān / prapitāmahāṃs tathādityān śrutir eṣā sanātanī //
english: They call (the manes of) fathers Vasus, (those of) grandfathers Rudras, and (those of) great-grandfathers Adityas; thus (speaks) the eternal Veda.

sanskrit: vighasāśī bhaven nityaṃ nityaṃ vāmṛtabhojanaḥ / vighaso bhuktaśeṣaṃ tu yajñaśeṣaṃ tathāmṛtam //
english: Let him daily partake of the vighasa and daily eat amrita (ambrosia); but vighasa is what remains from the meal (of Brahmana guests) and the remainder of a sacrifice (is called) amrita.

sanskrit: etad vo 'bhihitaṃ sarvaṃ vidhānaṃ pāñcayajñikam / dvijātimukhyavṛttīnāṃ vidhānaṃ śrūyatām iti //
english: Thus all the ordinances relating to the five (daily great) sacrifices have been declared to you; hear now the law for the manner of living fit for Brahmanas.

sanskrit: caturtham āyuṣo bhāgam uṣitvādyaṃ gurau dvijāḥ / dvitīyam āyuṣo bhāgaṃ kṛtadāro gṛhe vaset //
english: Having dwelt with a teacher during the fourth part of (a man's) life, a Brahmana shall live during the second quarter (of his existence) in his house, after he has wedded a wife.

sanskrit: adroheṇaiva bhūtānām alpadroheṇa vā punaḥ / yā vṛttis tāṃ samāsthāya vipro jīved anāpadi //
english: A Brahmana must seek a means of subsistence which either causes no, or at least little pain (to others), and live (by that) except in times of distress.

sanskrit: yātrāmātraprasiddhyarthaṃ svaiḥ karmabhir agarhitaiḥ / akleśena śarīrasya kurvīta dhanasaṃcayam //
english: For the purpose of gaining bare subsistence, let him accumulate property by (following those) irreproachable occupations (which are prescribed for) his (caste), without (unduly) fatiguing his body.

sanskrit: ṛtāmṛtābhyāṃ jīvet tu mṛtena pramṛtena vā / satyānṛtābhyām api vā na śvavṛttyā kadā cana //
english: He may subsist by Rita (truth), and Amrita (ambrosia), or by Mrita (death) and by Pramrita (what causes many deaths); or even by (the mode) called Satyanrita (a mixture of truth and falsehood), but never by Svavritti (a dog's mode of life).

sanskrit: ṛtam uñchaśilaṃ jñeyam amṛtaṃ syād ayācitam / mṛtaṃ tu yācitaṃ bhaikṣaṃ pramṛtaṃ karṣaṇaṃ smṛtam //
english: By Rita shall be understood the gleaning of corn; by Amrita, what is given unasked; by Mrita, food obtained by begging and agriculture is declared to be Pramrita.

sanskrit: satyānṛtaṃ tu vāṇijyaṃ tena caivāpi jīvyate / sevā śvavṛttir ākhyātā tasmāt tāṃ parivarjayet //
english: But trade and (money-lending) are Satyanrita, even by that one may subsist. Service is called Svavritti; therefore one should avoid it.

sanskrit: kusūladhānyako vā syāt kumbhīdhānyaka eva vā / tryahaihiko vāpi bhaved aśvastanika eva vā //
english: He may either possess enough to fill a granary, or a store filling a grain-jar; or he may collect what suffices for three days, or make no provision for the morrow.

sanskrit: caturṇām api caiteṣāṃ dvijānāṃ gṛhamedhinām / jyāyān paraḥ paro jñeyo dharmato lokajittamaḥ //
english: Moreover, among these four Brahmana householders, each later-(named) must be considered more distinguished, and through his virtue to have conquered the world more completely.

sanskrit: ṣaṭkarmaiko bhavaty eṣāṃ tribhir anyaḥ pravartate / dvābhyām ekaś caturthas tu brahmasattreṇa jīvati //
english: One of these follows six occupations, another subsists by three, one by two, but the fourth lives by the Brahmasattra.

sanskrit: vartayaṃś ca śiloñchābhyām agnihotraparāyaṇaḥ / iṣṭīḥ pārvāyaṇāntīyāḥ kevalā nirvapet sadā //
english: He who maintains himself by picking up grains and ears of corn, must be always intent on (the performance of) the Agnihotra, and constantly offer those Ishtis only, which are prescribed for the days of the conjunction and opposition (of the moon), and for the solstices.

sanskrit: na lokavṛttaṃ varteta vṛttihetoḥ kathaṃ cana / ajihmām aśathāṃ śuddhāṃ jīved brāhmaṇajīvikām //
english: Let him never, for the sake of subsistence, follow the ways of the world; let him live the pure, straightforward, honest life of a Brahmana.

sanskrit: saṃtoṣaṃ param āsthāya sukhārthī saṃyato bhavet / saṃtoṣamūlaṃ hi sukhaṃ duḥkhamūlaṃ viparyayaḥ //
english: He who desires happiness must strive after a perfectly contented disposition and control himself; for happiness has contentment for its root, the root of unhappiness is the contrary (disposition).

sanskrit: ato 'nyatamayā vṛttyā jīvaṃs tu snātako dvijaḥ / svargāyuṣyayaśasyāni vratāṇīmāni dhārayet //
english: A Brahmana, who is a Snataka and subsists by one of the (above-mentioned) modes of life, must discharge the (following) duties which secure heavenly bliss, long life, and fame.

sanskrit: vedoditaṃ svakaṃ karma nityaṃ kuryād atandritaḥ / tad dhi kurvan yathāśakti prāpnoti paramāṃ gatim //
english: Let him, untired, perform daily the rites prescribed for him in the Veda; for he who performs those according to his ability, attains to the highest state.

sanskrit: nehetārthān prasaṅgena na viruddhena karmaṇā / na vidyamāneṣv artheṣu nārtyām api yatas tataḥ //
english: Whether he be rich or even in distress, let him not seek wealth through pursuits to which men cleave, nor by forbidden occupations, nor (let him accept presents) from any (giver whosoever he may be).

sanskrit: indriyārtheṣu sarveṣu na prasajyeta kāmataḥ / atiprasaktiṃ caiteṣāṃ manasā saṃnivartayet //
english: Let him not, out of desire (for enjoyments), attach himself to any sensual pleasures, and let him carefully obviate an excessive attachment to them, by (reflecting on their worthlessness in) his heart.

sanskrit: sarvān parityajed arthān svādhyāyasya virodhinaḥ / yathā tathādhyāpayaṃs tu sā hy asya kṛtakṛtyatā //
english: Let him avoid all (means of acquiring) wealth which impede the study of the Veda; (let him maintain himself) anyhow, but study, because that (devotion to the Veda-study secures) the realisation of his aims.

sanskrit: vayasaḥ karmaṇo 'rthasya śrutasyābhijanasya ca / veṣavāgbuddhisārūpyam ācaran vicared iha //
english: Let him walk here (on earth), bringing his dress, speech, and thoughts to a conformity with his age, his occupation, his wealth, his sacred learning, and his race.

sanskrit: buddhivṛddhikarāṇy āśu dhanyāni ca hitāni ca / nityaṃ śāstrāṇy avekṣeta nigamāṃś caiva vaidikān //
english: Let him daily pore over those Institutes of science which soon give increase of wisdom, those which teach the acquisition of wealth, those which are beneficial (for other worldly concerns), and likewise over the Nigamas which explain the Veda.

sanskrit: yathā yathā hi puruṣaḥ śāstraṃ samadhigacchati / tathā tathā vijānāti vijñānaṃ cāsya rocate //
english: For the more a man completely studies the Institutes of science, the more he fully understands (them), and his great learning shines brightly.

sanskrit: ṛṣiyajñaṃ devayajñaṃ bhūtayajñaṃ ca sarvadā / nṛyajñaṃ pitṛyajñaṃ ca yathāśakti na hāpayet //
english: Let him never, if he is able (to perform them), neglect the sacrifices to the sages, to the gods, to the Bhutas, to men, and to the manes.

sanskrit: etān eke mahāyajñān yajñaśāstravido janāḥ / anīhamānāḥ satatam indriyeṣv eva juhvati //
english: Some men who know the ordinances for sacrificial rites, always offer these great sacrifices in their organs (of sensation), without any (external) effort.

sanskrit: vācy eke juhvati prāṇaṃ prāṇe vācaṃ ca sarvadā / vāci prāṇe ca paśyanto yajñanirvṛttim akṣayām //
english: Knowing that the (performance of the) sacrifice in their speech and their breath yields imperishable (rewards), some always offer their breath in their speech, and their speech in their breath.

sanskrit: jñānenaivāpare viprā yajanty etair makhaiḥ sadā / jñānamūlāṃ kriyām eṣāṃ paśyanto jñānacakṣuṣā //
english: Other Brahmanas, seeing with the eye of knowledge that the performance of those rites has knowledge for its root, always perform them through knowledge alone.

sanskrit: agnihotraṃ ca juhuyād ādyante dyuniśoḥ sadā / darśena cārdhamāsānte paurṇāmāsena caiva hi //
english: A Brahmana shall always offer the Agnihotra at the beginning or at the end of the day and of the night, and the Darsa and Paurnamasa (Ishtis) at the end of each half-month,

sanskrit: nāniṣṭvā navasasyeṣṭyā paśunā cāgnimān dvijaḥ / navānnam adyān māṃsaṃ vā dīrgham āyur jijīviṣuḥ //
english: A Brahmana, who keeps sacred fires, shall, if he desires to live long, not eat new grain or meat, without having offered the (Agrayana) Ishti with new grain and an animal-(sacrifice).

sanskrit: navenānarcitā hy asya paśuhavyena cāgnayaḥ / prāṇān evāttum icchanti navānnāmiṣagardhinaḥ //
english: For his fires, not being worshipped by offerings of new grain and of an animal, seek to devour his vital spirits, (because they are) greedy for new grain and flesh.

sanskrit: āsanāśanaśayyābhir adbhir mūlaphalena vā / nāsya kaś cid vased gehe śaktito 'narcito 'tithiḥ // pāṣāṇḍino vikarmasthān baiḍālavratikāñ śaṭhān / haitukān bakavṛttīṃś ca vāṅgātreṇāpi nārcayet //
english: No guest must stay in his house without being honoured, according to his ability, with a seat, food, a couch, water, or roots and fruits. Let him not honour, even by a greeting, heretics, men who follow forbidden occupations, men who live like cats, rogues, logicians, (arguing against the Veda,) and those who live like herons.

sanskrit: vedavidyāvratasnātāñ śrotriyān gṛhamedhinaḥ / pūjayed dhavyakavyena viparītāṃś ca varjayet //
english: Those who have become Snatakas after studying the Veda, or after completing their vows, (and) householders, who are Srotriyas, one must worship by (gifts of food) sacred to gods and manes, but one must avoid those who are different.

sanskrit: śaktito 'pacamānebhyo dātavyaṃ gṛhamedhinā / saṃvibhāgaś ca bhūtebhyaḥ kartavyo 'nuparodhataḥ //
english: A householder must give (as much food) as he is able (to spare) to those who do not cook for themselves, and to all beings one must distribute (food) without detriment (to one's own interest).

sanskrit: rājato dhanam anvicchet saṃsīdan snātakaḥ kṣudhā / yājyāntevāsinor vāpi na tv anyata iti sthitiḥ //
english: A Snataka who pines with hunger, may beg wealth of a king, of one for whom he sacrifices, and of a pupil, but not of others; that is a settled rule.

sanskrit: na sīdet snātako vipraḥ kṣudhā śaktaḥ kathaṃ cana / na jīrṇamalavadvāsā bhavec ca vibhave sati //
english: A Snataka who is able (to procure food) shall never waste himself with hunger, nor shall he wear old or dirty clothes, if he possesses property.

sanskrit: kḷptakeśanakhaśmaśrur dāntaḥ śuklāmbaraḥ śuciḥ / svādhyāye caiva yuktaḥ syān nityam ātmahiteṣu ca // vaiṇavīṃ dhārayed yaṣṭiṃ sodakaṃ ca kamaṇḍalum / yajñopavītaṃ vedaṃ ca śubhaṃ raukme ca kuṇḍale //
english: Keeping his hair, nails, and beard clipped, subduing his passions by austerities, wearing white garments and (keeping himself) pure, he shall be always engaged in studying the Veda and (such acts as are) conducive to his welfare. He shall carry a staff of bamboo, a pot full of water, a sacred string, a bundle of Kusa grass, and (wear) two bright golden ear-rings.

sanskrit: nekṣetodyantam ādityaṃ nāstaṃ yāntaṃ kadā cana / nopasṛṣṭaṃ na vāristhaṃ na madhyaṃ nabhaso gatam //
english: Let him never look at the sun, when he sets or rises, is eclipsed or reflected in water, or stands in the middle of the sky.

sanskrit: na laṅghayed vatsatantrīṃ na pradhāvec ca varṣati / na codake nirīkṣeta svarūpam iti dhāraṇā //
english: Let him not step over a rope to which a calf is tied, let him not run when it rains, and let him not look at his own image in water; that is a settled rule.

sanskrit: mṛdaṃ gāṃ daivataṃ vipraṃ ghṛtaṃ madhu catuṣpatham / pradakṣiṇāni kurvīta prajñātāṃś ca vanaspatīn //
english: Let him pass by (a mound of) earth, a cow, an idol, a Brahmana, clarified butter, honey, a crossway, and well-known trees, turning his right hand towards them.

sanskrit: nopagacchet pramatto 'pi striyam ārtavadarśane / samānaśayane caiva na śayīta tayā saha //
english: Let him, though mad with desire, not approach his wife when her courses appear; nor let him sleep with her in the same bed.

sanskrit: rajasābhiplutāṃ nārīṃ narasya hy upagacchataḥ / prajñā tejo balaṃ cakṣur āyuś caiva prahīyate //
english: For the wisdom, the energy, the strength, the sight, and the vitality of a man who approaches a woman covered with menstrual excretions, utterly perish.

sanskrit: tāṃ vivarjayatas tasya rajasā samabhiplutām / prajñā tejo balaṃ cakṣur āyuś caiva pravardhate //
english: If he avoids her, while she is in that condition, his wisdom, energy, strength, sight, and vitality will increase.

sanskrit: nāśnīyād bhāryayā sārdhaṃ nainām īkṣeta cāśnatīm / kṣuvatīṃ jṛmbhamāṇāṃ vā na cāsīnāṃ yathāsukham //
english: Let him not eat in the company of his wife, nor look at her, while she eats, sneezes, yawns, or sits at her ease.

sanskrit: nāñjayantīṃ svake netre na cābhyaktām anāvṛtām / na paśyet prasavantīṃ ca tejaskāmo dvijottamaḥ //
english: A Brahmana who desires energy must not look at (a woman) who applies collyrium to her eyes, has anointed or uncovered herself or brings forth (a child).

sanskrit: nānnam adyād ekavāsā na nagnaḥ snānam ācaret / na mūtraṃ pathi kurvīta na bhasmani na govraje //
english: Let him not eat, dressed with one garment only; let him not bathe naked; let him not void urine on a road, on ashes, or in a cow-pen,

sanskrit: na phālakṛṣṭe na jale na cityāṃ na ca parvate / na jīrṇadevāyatane na valmīke kadā cana //
english: Nor on ploughed land, in water, on an altar of bricks, on a mountain, on the ruins of a temple, nor ever on an ant-hill,

sanskrit: na sasattveṣu garteṣu na gacchann api na sthitaḥ / na nadītīram āsādya na ca parvatamastake //
english: Nor in holes inhabited by living creatures, nor while he walks or stands, nor on reaching the bank of a river, nor on the top of a mountain.

sanskrit: vāyvagnivipram ādityam apaḥ paśyaṃs tathaiva gāḥ / na kadā cana kurvīta viṇmūtrasya visarjanam //
english: Let him never void faeces or urine, facing the wind, or a fire, or looking towards a Brahmana, the sun, water, or cows.

sanskrit: tiraskṛtyoccaret kāṣṭha- loṣṭhapatratṛṇādinā / niyamya prayato vācaṃ saṃvītāṅgo 'vaguṇṭhitaḥ //
english: He may ease himself, having covered (the ground) with sticks, clods, leaves, grass, and the like, restraining his speech, (keeping himself) pure, wrapping up his body, and covering his head.

sanskrit: mūtroccārasamutsargaṃ divā kuryād udaṅmukhaḥ / dakṣiṇābhimukho rātrau saṃdhyāyoś ca yathā divā //
english: Let him void faeces and urine, in the daytime turning to the north, at night turning towards the south, during the two twilights in the same (position) as by day.

sanskrit: chāyāyām andhakāre vā rātrāv ahani vā dvijaḥ / yathāsukhamukhaḥ kuryāt prāṇabādhabhayeṣu ca //
english: In the shade or in darkness a Brahmana may, both by day and at night, do it, assuming any position he pleases; likewise when his life is in danger.

sanskrit: pratyagniṃ pratisūryaṃ ca pratisomodakadvijam / pratigu prativātaṃ ca prajñā naśyati mehataḥ //
english: The intellect of (a man) who voids urine against a fire, the sun, the moon, in water, against a Brahmana, a cow, or the wind, perishes.

sanskrit: nāgniṃ mukhenopadhamen nagnāṃ nekṣeta ca striyam / nāmedhyaṃ prakṣiped agnau na ca pādau pratāpayet //
english: Let him not blow a fire with his mouth; let him not look at a naked woman; let him not throw any impure substance into the fire, and let him not warm his feet at it.

sanskrit: adhastān nopadadhyāc ca na cainam abhilaṅghayet / na cainaṃ pādataḥ kuryān na prāṇābādham ācaret // nāśnīyāt saṃdhivelāyāṃ na gacchen nāpi saṃviśet / na caiva pralikhed bhūmiṃ nātmano 'paharet srajam //
