english: Let him not place (fire) under (a bed or the like); nor step over it, nor place it (when he sleeps) at the foot-(end of his bed); let him not torment living creatures. Let him not eat, nor travel, nor sleep during the twilight; let him not scratch the ground; let him not take off his garland.

sanskrit: nāpsu mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā ṣṭhīvanaṃ vā samutsṛjet / amedhyaliptam anyad vā lohitaṃ vā viṣāṇi vā //
english: Let him not throw urine or faeces into the water, nor saliva, nor (clothes) defiled by impure substances, nor any other (impurity), nor blood, nor poisonous things.

sanskrit: naikaḥ supyāc chūnyagehe na śreyāṃsaṃ prabodhayet / nodakyayābhibhāṣeta yajñaṃ gacchen na cāvṛtaḥ //
english: Let him not sleep alone in a deserted dwelling; let him not wake (a superior) who is sleeping; let him not converse with a menstruating woman; nor let him go to a sacrifice, if he is not chosen (to be officiating priest).

sanskrit: agnyagāre gavāṃ goṣṭhe brāhmaṇānāṃ ca saṃnidhau / svādhyāye bhojane caiva dakṣinaṃ pāṇim uddharet //
english: Let him keep his right arm uncovered in a place where a sacred fire is kept, in a cow-pen, in the presence of Brahmanas, during the private recitation of the Veda, and at meals.

sanskrit: na vārayed gāṃ dhayantīṃ na cācakṣīta kasya cit / na divīndrāyudhaṃ dṛṣṭvā kasya cid darśayed budhaḥ //
english: Let him not interrupt a cow who is suckling (her calf), nor tell anybody of it. A wise man, if he sees a rainbow in the sky, must not point it out to anybody.

sanskrit: nādharmike vased grāme na vyādhibahule bhṛśam / naikaḥ prapadyetādhvānaṃ na ciraṃ parvate vaset //
english: Let him not dwell in a village where the sacred law is not obeyed, nor (stay) long where diseases are endemic; let him not go alone on a journey, nor reside long on a mountain.

sanskrit: na śūdrarājye nivasen nādhārmikajanāvṛte / na pāṣaṇḍigaṇākrānte nopasṣṛṭe 'ntyajair nṛbhiḥ //
english: Let him not dwell in a country where the rulers are Sudras, nor in one which is surrounded by unrighteous men, nor in one which has become subject to heretics, nor in one swarming with men of the lowest castes.

sanskrit: na bhuñjītoddhṛtasnehaṃ nātisauhityam ācaret / nātiprage nātisāyaṃ na sāyaṃ prātarāśitaḥ // na kurvīta vṛthāceṣṭāṃ na vāry añjalinā pibet / notsaṅge bhakṣayed bhakṣyān na jātu syāt kutūhalī //
english: Let him not eat anything from which the oil has been extracted; let him not be a glutton; let him not eat very early (in the morning), nor very late (in the evening), nor (take any food) in the evening, if he has eaten (his fill) in the morning. Let him not exert himself without a purpose; let him not drink water out of his joined palms; let him not eat food (placed) in his lap; let him not show (idle) curiosity.

sanskrit: na nṛtyed atha vā gāyen na vāditrāṇi vādayet] / nāsphoṭayen na ca kṣveḍen na ca rakto virāvayet //
english: Let him not dance, nor sing, nor play musical instruments, nor slap (his limbs), nor grind his teeth, nor let him make uncouth noises, though he be in a passion.

sanskrit: na pādau dhāvayet kāṃsye kadā cid api bhājane / na bhinnabhāṇḍe bhuñjīta na bhāvapratidūṣite //
english: Let him never wash his feet in a vessel of white brass; let him not eat out of a broken (earthen) dish, nor out of one that (to judge) from its appearance (is) defiled.

sanskrit: upānahau ca vāsaś ca dhṛtam anyair na dhārayet / upavītam alaṅkāraṃ srajaṃ karakam eva ca //
english: Let him not use shoes, garments, a sacred string, ornaments, a garland, or a water-vessel which have been used by others.

sanskrit: nāvinītair bhajed dhuryair na ca kṣudhvyādhipīḍitaiḥ / na bhinnaśṛṅgākṣikhurair na vāladhivirūpitaiḥ //
english: Let him not travel with untrained beasts of burden, nor with (animals) that are tormented by hunger or disease, or whose horns, eyes, and hoofs have been injured, or whose tails have been disfigured.

sanskrit: vinītais tu vrajen nityam āśugair lakṣaṇānvitaiḥ / varṇarūpopasaṃpannaiḥ pratodenātudan bhṛśam //
english: Let him always travel with (beasts) which are well broken in, swift, endowed with lucky marks, and perfect in colour and form, without urging them much with the goad.

sanskrit: bālātapaḥ pretadhūmo varjyaṃ bhinnaṃ tathāsanam / na chindyān nakharomāṇi dantair notpāṭayen nakhān //
english: The morning sun, the smoke rising from a (burning) corpse, and a broken seat must be avoided. Let him not clip his nails or hair, and not tear his nails with his teeth.

sanskrit: na mṛlloṣṭhaṃ ca mṛdnīyān na chindyāt karajais tṛṇam / na karma niṣphalaṃ kuryān nāyatyām asukhodayam //
english: Let him not crush earth or clods, nor tear off grass with his nails; let him not do anything that is useless or will have disagreeable results in the future.

sanskrit: loṣṭhamardī tṛṇacchedī nakhakhādī ca yo naraḥ / sa vināśaṃ vrajaty āśu sūcakāśucir eva ca //
english: A man who crushes clods, tears off grass, or bites his nails, goes soon to perdition, likewise an informer and he who neglects (the rules of) purification.

sanskrit: na vigarhya kathāṃ kuryād bahir mālyaṃ na dhārayet / gavāṃ ca yānaṃ pṛṣṭhena sarvathaiva vigarhitam //
english: Let him not wrangle; let him not wear a garland over (his hair). To ride on the back of cows (or of oxen) is anyhow a blamable act.

sanskrit: advāreṇa ca nātīyād grāmaṃ vā veśma vāvṛtam / rātrau ca vṛkṣamūlāni dūrataḥ parivarjayet //
english: Let him not enter a walled village or house except by the gate, and by night let him keep at a long distance from the roots of trees.

sanskrit: nākṣair dīvyet kadā cit tu svayaṃ nopānahau haret / śayanastho na bhuñjīta na pāṇisthaṃ na cāsane // sarvaṃ ca tilasaṃbaddhaṃ nādyād astam ite ravau / na ca nagnaḥ śayīteha na cocchiṣṭaḥ kva cid vrajet //
english: Let him never play with dice, nor himself take off his shoes; let him not eat, lying on a bed, nor what has been placed in his hand or on a seat. Let him not eat after sunset any (food) containing sesamum grains; let him never sleep naked, nor go anywhere unpurified (after meals).

sanskrit: ārdrapādas tu bhuñjīta nārdrapādas tu saṃviśet / ārdrapādas tu bhuñjāno dīrgham āyur avāpnuyāt //
english: Let him eat while his feet are (yet) wet (from the ablution), but let him not go to bed with wet feet. He who eats while his feet are (still) wet, will attain long life.

sanskrit: acakṣurviṣayaṃ durgaṃ $ na prapadyeta karhi cit / na viṇmūtram udīkṣeta na bāhubhyāṃ nadīṃ taret //
english: Let him never enter a place, difficult of access, which is impervious to his eye; let him not look at urine or ordure, nor cross a river (swimming) with his arms.

sanskrit: adhitiṣṭhen na keśāṃs tu na bhasmāsthikapālikāḥ / na kārpāsāsthi na tuṣān dīrgham āyur jijīviṣuḥ //
english: Let him not step on hair, ashes, bones, potsherds, cotton-seed or chaff, if he desires long life.

sanskrit: na saṃvasec ca patitair na cāṇḍālair na pulkasaiḥ / na mūrkhair nāvaliptaiś ca nāntyair nāntyāvasāyibhiḥ //
english: Let him not stay together with outcasts, nor with Kandalas, nor with Pukkasas, nor with fools, nor with overbearing men, nor with low-caste men, nor with Antyavasayins.

sanskrit: na śūdrāya matiṃ dadyān nocchiṣṭaṃ na haviṣkṛtam / na cāsyopadiśed dharmaṃ na cāsya vratam ādiśet //
english: Let him not give to a Sudra advice, nor the remnants (of his meal), nor food offered to the gods; nor let him explain the sacred law (to such a man), nor impose (upon him) a penance.

sanskrit: yo hy asya dharmam ācaṣṭe yaś caivādiśati vratam / so 'saṃvṛtaṃ nāma tamaḥ saha tenaiva majjati //
english: For he who explains the sacred law (to a Sudra) or dictates to him a penance, will sink together with that (man) into the hell (called) Asamvrita.

sanskrit: na saṃhatābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ kaṇḍūyed ātmanaḥ śiraḥ / na spṛśec caitad ucchiṣṭo na ca snāyād vinā tataḥ // keśagrahān prahārāṃś ca śirasy etān vivarjayet / śiraḥsnātaś ca tailena nāṅgaṃ kiṃ cid api spṛśet //
english: Let him not scratch his head with both hands joined; let him not touch it while he is impure, nor bathe without (submerging) it. Let him avoid (in anger) to lay hold of (his own or other men's) hair, or to strike (himself or others) on the head. When he has bathed (submerging) his head, he shall not touch any of his limbs with oil.

sanskrit: na rājñaḥ pratigṛhṇīyād arājanyaprasūtitaḥ / sūnācakradhvajavatāṃ veśenaiva ca jīvatām //
english: Let him not accept presents from a king who is not descended from the Kshatriya race, nor from butchers, oil-manufacturers, and publicans, nor from those who subsist by the gain of prostitutes.

sanskrit: daśasūnāsamaṃ cakraṃ daśacakrasamo dhvajaḥ / daśadhvajasamo veśo daśaveśasamo nṛpaḥ //
english: One oil-press is as (bad) as ten slaughter-houses, one tavern as (bad as) ten oil-presses, one brothel as (bad as) ten taverns, one king as (bad as) ten brothels.

sanskrit: daśa sūṇāsahasrāṇi yo vāhayati saunikaḥ / tena tulyaḥ smṛto rājā ghoras tasya pratigrahaḥ //
english: A king is declared to be equal (in wickedness) to a butcher who keeps a hundred thousand slaughter-houses; to accept presents from him is a terrible (crime).

sanskrit: yo rājñaḥ pratigṛhṇāti lubdhasyocchāstravartinaḥ / sa paryāyeṇa yātīmān narakān ekaviṃśatim //
english: He who accepts presents from an avaricious king who acts contrary to the Institutes (of the sacred law), will go in succession to the following twenty-one hells:

sanskrit: tāmisram andhatāmisraṃ mahārauravarauravau / narakaṃ kālasūtraṃ ca mahānarakam eva ca //
english: Tamisra, Andhatamisra, Maharaurava, Raurava, the Kalasutra hell, Mahanaraka,

sanskrit: saṃjīvanaṃ mahāvīciṃ tapanaṃ saṃpratāpanam / saṃhātaṃ ca sakākolaṃ kuḍmalaṃ pratimūrtikam //
english: Samgivana, Mahaviki, Tapana, Sampratapana, Samghata, Sakakola, Kudmala, Putimrittika,

sanskrit: lohaśaṅkum ṛjīṣaṃ ca panthānaṃ śālmalīṃ nadīm / asipatravanaṃ caiva lohadārakam eva ca //
english: Lohasanku, Rigisha, Pathin, the (flaming) river, Salmala, Asipatravana, and Lohakaraka.

sanskrit: etad vidanto vidvāṃso brāhmaṇā brahmavādinaḥ / na rājñaḥ pratigṛhṇanti pretya śreyo 'bhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ // brāhme muhūrte budhyeta dharmārthau cānucintayet / kāyakleśāṃś ca tanmūlān vedatattvārtham eva ca //
english: Learned Brahmanas, who know that, who study the Veda and desire bliss after death, do not accept presents from a king. Let him wake in the muhurta, sacred to Brahman, and think of (the acquisition of) spiritual merit and wealth, of the bodily fatigue arising therefrom, and of the true meaning of the Veda.

sanskrit: utthāyāvaśyakaṃ kṛtvā kṛtaśaucaḥ samāhitaḥ / pūrvāṃ saṃdhyāṃ japaṃs tiṣṭhet svakāle cāparāṃ ciram //
english: When he has risen, has relieved the necessities of nature and carefully purified himself, let him stand during the morning twilight, muttering for a long time (the Gayatri), and at the proper time (he must similarly perform) the evening (devotion).

sanskrit: ṛṣayo dīrghasaṃdhyatvād dīrgham āyur avāpnuyuḥ / prajñāṃ yaśaś ca kīrtiṃ ca brahmavarcasam eva ca //
english: By prolonging the twilight devotions, the sages obtained long life, wisdom, honour, fame, and excellence in Vedic knowledge.

sanskrit: śrāvaṇyāṃ prauṣṭhapadyāṃ vāpy upākṛtya yathāvidhi / yuktaś chandāṃsy adhīyīta māsān vipro 'rdhapañcamān //
english: Having performed the Upakarman according to the prescribed rule on (the full moon of the month) Sravana, or on that of Praushthapada (Bhadrapada), a Brahmana shall diligently study the Vedas during four months and a half.

sanskrit: puṣye tu chandasāṃ kuryād bahir utsarjanaṃ dvijaḥ / māghaśuklasya vā prāpte pūrvāhṇe prathame 'hani //
english: When the Pushya-day (of the month Pausha), or the first day of the bright half of Magha has come, a Brahmana shall perform in the forenoon the Utsargana of the Vedas.

sanskrit: yathāśāstraṃ tu kṛtvaivam utsargaṃ chandasāṃ bahiḥ / viramet pakṣiṇīṃ rātriṃ tad evaikam aharniśam //
english: Having performed the Utsarga outside (the village), as the Institutes (of the sacred law) prescribe, he shall stop reading during two days and the intervening night, or during that day (of the Utsarga) and (the following) night.

sanskrit: ata ūrdhvaṃ tu chandāṃsi śukleṣu niyataḥ paṭhet / vedāṅgāni ca sarvāṇi kṛṣṇapakṣeṣu saṃpaṭhet //
english: Afterwards he shall diligently recite the Vedas during the bright (halves of the months), and duly study all the Angas of the Vedas during the dark fortnights.

sanskrit: nāvispaṣṭam adhīyīta na śūdrajanasannidhau / na niśānte pariśrānto brahmādhītya punaḥ svapet //
english: Let him not recite (the texts) indistinctly, nor in the presence of Sudras; nor let him, if in the latter part of the night he is tired with reciting the Veda, go again to sleep.

sanskrit: yathoditena vidhinā nityaṃ chandaskṛtaṃ paṭhet / brahma chandaskṛtaṃ caiva dvijo yukto hy anāpadi // imān nityam anadhyāyān adhīyāno vivarjayet / adhyāpanaṃ ca kurvāṇaḥ śiṣyāṇāṃ vidhipūrvakam // karṇaśrave 'nile rātrau divā pāṃsusamūhane / etau varṣāsv anadhyāyāv adhyāyajñāḥ pracakṣate //
english: According to the rule declared above, let him recite the daily (portion of the) Mantras, and a zealous Brahmana, (who is) not in distress, (shall study) the Brahmana and the Mantrasamhita. Let him who studies always avoid (reading) on the following occasions when the Veda-study is forbidden, and (let) him who teaches pupils according to the prescribed rule (do it likewise). Those who know the (rules of) recitation declare that in the rainy season the Veda-study must be stopped on these two (occasions), when the wind is audible at night, and when it whirls up the dust in the day-time.

sanskrit: vidyutstanitavarṣeṣu maholkānāṃ ca saṃplave / ākālikam anadhyāyam eteṣu manur abravīt //
english: Manu has stated, that when lightning, thunder, and rain (are observed together), or when large fiery meteors fall on all sides, the recitation must be interrupted until the same hour (on the next day, counting from the occurrence of the event).

sanskrit: etāṃs tv abhyuditān vidyād yadā prāduṣkṛtāgniṣu / tadā vidyād anadhyāyam anṛtau cābhradarśane // nirghāte bhūmicalane jyotiṣāṃ copasarjane / etān ākālikān vidyād anadhyāyān ṛtāv api // prāduṣkṛteṣv agniṣu tu vidyutstanitaniḥsvane / sajyotiḥ syād anadhyāyaḥ śeṣe rātrau yathā divā //
english: When one perceives these (phenomena) all together (in the twilight), after the sacred fires have been made to blaze (for the performance of the Agnihotra), then one must know the recitation of the Veda to be forbidden, and also when clouds appear out of season. On (the occasion of) a preternatural sound from the sky, (of) an earthquake, and when the lights of heaven are surrounded by a halo, let him know that (the Veda-study must be) stopped until the same hour (on the next day), even if (these phenomena happen) in the (rainy) season.

sanskrit: nityānadhyāya eva syād grāmeṣu nagareṣu ca / dharmanaipuṇyakāmānāṃ pūtigandhe ca sarvadā //
english: For those who wish to acquire exceedingiy great merit, a continual interruption of the Veda-study (is prescribed) in villages and in towns, and (the Veda-study must) always (cease) when any kind of foul smell (is perceptible).

sanskrit: antargataśave grāme vṛṣalasya ca sannidhau / anadhyāyo rudyamāne samavāye janasya ca //
english: In a village where a corpse lies, in the presence of a (man who lives as unrighteously as a) Sudra, while (the sound of) weeping (is heard), and in a crowd of men the (recitation of the Veda must be) stopped.

sanskrit: udake madhyarātre ca viṇmūtrasya visarjane / ucchiṣṭaḥ śrāddhabhuk caiva manasāpi na cintayet //
english: In water, during the middle part of the night, while he voids excrements, or is impure, and after he has partaken of a funeral dinner, a man must not even think in his heart (of the sacred texts).

sanskrit: pratigṛhya dvijo vidvān ekoddiṣṭasya ketanam / tryahaṃ na kīrtayed brahma rājño rāhoś ca sūtake //
english: A learned Brahmana shall not recite the Veda during three days, when he has accepted an invitation to a (funeral rite) in honour of one ancestor (ekoddishta), or when the king has become impure through a birth or death in his family (sutaka), or when Rahu by an eclipse makes the moon impure.

sanskrit: yāvad ekānudiṣṭasya gandho lepaś ca tiṣṭhati / viprasya viduṣo dehe tāvad brahma na kīrtayet //
english: As long as the smell and the stains of the (food given) in honour of one ancestor remain on the body of a learned Brahmana, so long he must not recite the Veda.

sanskrit: śayānaḥ prauḍhapādaś ca kṛtvā caivāvasakthikām / nādhīyītāmiṣaṃ jagdhvā sūtakānnādyam eva ca // nīhāre bāṇaśabde ca saṃdhyayor eva cobhayoḥ / amāvāsyācaturdaśyoḥ paurṇamāsyaṣṭakāsu ca //
english: While lying on a bed, while his feet are raised (on a bench), while he sits on his hams with a cloth tied round his knees, let him not study, nor when he has eaten meat or food given by a person impure on account of a birth or a death, Nor during a fog, nor while the sound of arrows is audible, nor during both the twilights, nor on the new-moon day, nor on the fourteenth and the eighth (days of each half-month), nor on the full-moon day.

sanskrit: amāvāsyā guruṃ hanti śiṣyaṃ hanti caturdaśī / brahmāṣṭakapaurṇamāsyau tasmāt tāḥ parivarjayet //
english: The new-moon day destroys the teacher, the fourteenth (day) the pupil, the eighth and the full-moon days (destroy all remembrance of) the Veda; let him therefore avoid (reading on) those (days).

sanskrit: pāṃsuvarṣe diśāṃ dāhe gomāyuvirute tathā / śvakharoṣṭre ca ruvati paṅktau ca na paṭhed dvijaḥ // nādhīyīta śmaśānānte grāmānte govraje 'pi vā / vasitvā maithunaṃ vāsaḥ śrāddhikaṃ pratigṛhya ca //
english: A Brahmana shall not recite (the Veda) during a dust-storm, nor while the sky is preternaturally red, nor while jackals howl, nor while the barking of dogs, the braying of donkeys, or the grunting of camels (is heard), nor while (he is seated) in a company. Let him not study near a burial-ground, nor near a village, nor in a cow-pen, nor dressed in a garment which he wore during conjugal intercourse, nor after receiving a present at a funeral sacrifice.

sanskrit: prāṇi vā yadi vāprāṇi yat kiṃ cic chrāddhikaṃ bhavet / tad ālabhyāpy anadhyāyaḥ pāṇyāsyo hi dvijaḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: Be it an animal or a thing inanimate, whatever be the (gift) at a Sraddha, let him not, having just accepted it, recite the Veda; for the hand of a Brahmana is his mouth.

sanskrit: corair upadrute grāme saṃbhrame cāgnikārite / ākālikam anadhyāyaṃ vidyāt sarvādbhuteṣu ca //
english: When the village has been beset by robbers, and when an alarm has been raised by fire, let him know that (the Veda-study must be) interrupted until the same hour (on the next day), and on (the occurrence of) all portents.

sanskrit: upākarmaṇi cotsarge trirātraṃ kṣepaṇaṃ smṛtam / aṣṭakāsu tv ahorātram ṛtvantāsu ca rātriṣu //
english: On (the occasion of) the Upakarman and (of) the Vedotsarga an omission (of the Veda-study) for three days has been prescribed, but on the Ashtakas and on the last nights of the seasons for a day and a night.

sanskrit: nādhīyītāśvam ārūḍho na vṛkṣaṃ na ca hastinam / na nāvaṃ na kharaṃ noṣṭraṃ neriṇastho na yānagaḥ //
english: Let him not recite the Veda on horseback, nor on a tree, nor on an elephant, nor in a boat (or ship), nor on a donkey, nor on camel, nor standing on barren ground, nor riding in a carriage,

sanskrit: na vivāde na kalahe na senāyāṃ na saṃgare / na bhuktamātre nājīrṇe na vamitvā na śuktake //
english: Nor during a verbal altercation, nor during a mutual assault, nor in a camp, nor during a battle, nor when he has just eaten, nor during an indigestion, nor after vomiting, nor with sour eructations,

sanskrit: atithiṃ cānanujñāpya mārute vāti vā bhṛśam / rudhire ca srute gātrāc chastreṇa ca parikṣate // sāmadhvanāv ṛgyajuṣī nādhīyīta kadā cana / vedasyādhītya vāpy antam āraṇyakam adhītya ca //
english: Nor without receiving permission from a guest (who stays in his house), nor while the wind blows vehemently, nor while blood flows from his body, nor when he is wounded by a weapon. Let him never recite the Rig-veda or the Yagur-veda while the Saman (melodies) are heard; (let him stop all Veda-study for a day and a night) after finishing a Veda or after reciting an Aranyaka.

sanskrit: ṛgvedo devadaivatyo yajurvedas tu mānuṣaḥ / sāmavedaḥ smṛtaḥ pitryas tasmāt tasyāśucir dhvaniḥ //
english: The Rig-veda is declared to be sacred to the gods, the Yagur-veda sacred to men, and the Sama-veda sacred to the manes; hence the sound of the latter is impure (as it were).

sanskrit: etad vidvanto vidvāṃsas trayīniṣkarṣam anvaham / kramataḥ pūrvam abhyasya paścād vedam adhīyate //
english: Knowing this, the learned daily repeat first in due order the essence of the three (Vedas) and afterwards the (text of the) Veda.

sanskrit: paśumaṇḍūkamārjāra- śvasarpanakulākhubhiḥ / antarāgamane vidyād anadhyāyam aharniśam //
english: Know that (the Veda-study must be) interrupted for a day and a night, when cattle, a frog, a cat, a dog, a snake, an ichneumon, or a rat pass between (the teacher and his pupil).

sanskrit: dvāv eva varjayen nityam anadhyāyau prayatnataḥ / svādhyāyabhūmiṃ cāśuddham ātmānaṃ cāśuciṃ dvijaḥ //
english: Let a twice-born man always carefully interrupt the Veda-study on two (occasions, viz.) when the place where he recites is impure, and when he himself is unpurified.

sanskrit: amāvāsyām aṣṭamīṃ ca paurṇamāsīṃ caturdaśīm / brahmacārī bhaven nityam apy ṛtau snātako dvijaḥ //
english: A twice-born man who is a Snataka shall remain chaste on the new-moon day, on the eighth (lunar day of each half-month), on the full-moon day, and on the fourteenth, even (if they fall) in the period (proper for conjugal intercourse).

sanskrit: na snānam ācared bhuktvā nāturo na mahāniśi / na vāsobhiḥ sahājasraṃ nāvijñāte jalāśaye //
english: Let him not bathe (immediately) after a meal, nor when he is sick, nor in the middle of the night, nor frequently dressed in all his garments, nor in a pool which he does not perfectly know.

sanskrit: devatānāṃ guro rājñaḥ snātakācāryayos tathā / nākrāmet kāmataś chāyāṃ babhruṇo dīkṣitasya ca //
english: Let him not intentionally step on the shadow of (images of) the gods, of a Guru, of a king, of a Snataka, of his teacher, of a reddish-brown animal, or of one who has been initiated to the performance of a Srauta sacrifice (Dikshita).

sanskrit: madhyaṃdine 'rdharātre ca śrāddhaṃ bhuktvā ca sāmiṣam / saṃdhyayor ubhayoś caiva na seveta catuṣpatham //
english: At midday and at midnight, after partaking of meat at a funeral dinner, and in the two twilights let him not stay long on a cross-road.

sanskrit: udvartanam apasnānaṃ viṇmūtre raktam eva ca / śleśmaniṣṭhyūtavāntāni nādhitiṣṭhet tu kāmataḥ //
english: Let him not step intentionally on things used for cleansing the body, on water used for a bath, on urine or ordure, on blood, on mucus, and on anything spat out or vomited.

sanskrit: vairiṇaṃ nopaseveta sahāyaṃ caiva vairiṇaḥ / adhārmikaṃ taskaraṃ ca parasyaiva ca yoṣitaṃ //
english: Let him not show particular attention to an enemy, to the friend of an enemy, to a wicked man, to a thief, or to the wife of another man.

sanskrit: na hīdṛśam anāyuṣyaṃ loke kiṃ cana vidyate / yādṛśaṃ puruṣasyeha paradāropasevanam //
english: For in this world there is nothing so detrimental to long life as criminal conversation with another man's wife.

sanskrit: kṣatriyaṃ caiva sarpaṃ ca brāhmaṇaṃ ca bahuśrutam / nāvamanyeta vai bhūṣṇuḥ kṛśān api kadā cana //
english: Let him who desires prosperity, indeed, never despise a Kshatriya, a snake, and a learned Brahmana, be they ever so feeble.

sanskrit: etat trayaṃ hi puruṣaṃ nirdahed avamānitam / tasmād etat trayaṃ nityaṃ nāvamanyeta buddhimān //
english: Because these three, when treated with disrespect, may utterly destroy him; hence a wise man must never despise them.

sanskrit: nātmānam avamanyeta purvābhir asamṛddhibhiḥ / ā mṛtyoḥ śriyam anvicchen naināṃ manyeta durlabhām //
english: Let him not despise himself on account of former failures; until death let him seek fortune, nor despair of gaining it.

sanskrit: satyaṃ brūyāt priyaṃ brūyān na brūyāt satyam apriyam / priyaṃ ca nānṛtaṃ brūyād eṣa dharmaḥ sanātanaḥ //
english: Let him say what is true, let him say what is pleasing, let him utter no disagreeable truth, and let him utter no agreeable falsehood; that is the eternal law.

sanskrit: bhadraṃ bhadram iti brūyād bhadram ity eva vā vadet / śuṣkavairaṃ vivādaṃ ca na kuryāt kena cit saha //
english: (What is) well, let him call well, or let him say 'well' only; let him not engage in a useless enmity or dispute with anybody.

sanskrit: nātikalyaṃ nātisāyaṃ nātimadhyaṃdine sthite / nājñātena samaṃ gacchen naiko na vṛṣalaiḥ saha //
english: Let him not journey too early in the morning, nor too late in the evening, nor just during the midday (heat), nor with an unknown (companion), nor alone, nor with Sudras.

sanskrit: hīnāṅgān atiriktāṅgān vidyāhīnān vayo'dhikān / rūpadraviṇahīnāṃś ca jātihīnāṃś ca nākṣipet //
english: Let him not insult those who have redundant limbs or are deficient in limbs, nor those destitute of knowledge, nor very aged men, nor those who have no beauty or wealth, nor those who are of low birth.

sanskrit: na spṛśet pāṇinocchiṣṭo vipro gobrāhmaṇānalāṇ / na cāpi paśyed aśuciḥ sustho jyotirgaṇān divā //
english: A Brahmana who is impure must not touch with his hand a cow, a Brahmana, or fire; nor, being in good health, let him look at the luminaries in the sky, while he is impure.

sanskrit: spṛṣṭvaitān aśucir nityam adbhiḥ prāṇān upaspṛśet / gātrāṇi caiva sarvāṇi nābhiṃ pāṇitalena tu //
english: If he has touched these, while impure, let him always sprinkle with his hand water on the organs of sensation, all his limbs, and the navel.

sanskrit: anāturaḥ svāni khāni na spṛśed animittataḥ / romāṇi ca rahasyāni sarvāṇy eva vivarjayet // maṅgalācārayuktaḥ syāt prayatātmā jitendriyaḥ / japec ca juhuyāc caiva nityam agnim atandritaḥ //
english: Except when sick he must not touch the cavities (of the body) without a reason, and he must avoid (to touch) the hair on the secret (parts). Let him eagerly follow the (customs which are) auspicious and the rule of good conduct, be careful of purity, and control all his organs, let him mutter (prayers) and, untired, daily offer oblations in the fire.

sanskrit: maṅgalācārayuktānāṃ nityaṃ ca prayatātmanām / japatāṃ juhvatāṃ caiva vinipāto na vidyate //
english: No calamity happens to those who eagerly follow auspicious customs and the rule of good conduct, to those who are always careful of purity, and to those who mutter (sacred texts) and offer burnt-oblations.

sanskrit: vedam evābhyasen nityaṃ yathākālam atandritaḥ / taṃ hy asyāhuḥ paraṃ dharmam upadharmo 'nya ucyate //
english: Let him, without tiring, daily mutter the Veda at the proper time; for they declare that to be one's highest duty; (all) other (observances) are called secondary duties.

sanskrit: vedābhyāsena satataṃ śaucena tapasaiva ca / adroheṇa ca bhūtānāṃ jātiṃ smarati paurvikīm //
english: By daily reciting the Veda, by (the observance of the rules of) purification, by (practising) austerities, and by doing no injury to created beings, one (obtains the faculty of) remembering former births.

sanskrit: paurvikīṃ saṃsmaran jātiṃ brahmaivābhyasyate punaḥ / brahmābhyāsena cājasram anantaṃ sukham aśnute //
english: He who, recollecting his former existences, again recites the Veda, gains endless bliss by the continual study of the Veda.

sanskrit: sāvitrāñ śāntihomāṃś ca kuryāt parvasu nityaśaḥ / pitṝṃś caivāṣṭakāsv arcen nityam anvaṣṭakāsu ca //
english: Let him always offer on the Parva-days oblations to Savitri and such as avert evil omens, and on the Ashtakas and Anvashtakas let him constantly worship the manes.

sanskrit: dūrād āvasathān mūtraṃ dūrāt pādāvasecanam / ucchiṣṭānnaniṣekaṃ ca dūrād eva samācaret //
english: Far from his dwelling let him remove urine (and ordure), far (let him remove) the water used for washing his feet, and far the remnants of food and the water from his bath.

sanskrit: maitraṃ prasādhanaṃ snānaṃ dantadhāvanam añjanam / pūrvāhṇa eva kurvīta devatānāṃ ca pūjanam //
english: Early in the morning only let him void faeces, decorate (his body), bathe, clean his teeth, apply collyrium to his eyes, and worship the gods.

sanskrit: daivatāny abhigacchet tu dhārmikāṃś ca dvijottamān / īśvaraṃ caiva rakṣārthaṃ gurūn eva ca parvasu //
english: But on the Parva-days let him go to visit the (images of the) gods, and virtuous Brahmanas, and the ruler (of the country), for the sake of protection, as well as his Gurus.

sanskrit: abhivādayed vṛddhāṃś ca dadyāc caivāsanaṃ svakam / kṛtāñjalir upāsīta gacchataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nviyāt //
english: Let him reverentially salute venerable men (who visit him), give them his own seat, let him sit near them with joined hands and, when they leave, (accompany them), walking behind them.

sanskrit: śrutismṛtyuditaṃ samyaṅ nibaddhaṃ sveṣu karmasu / dharmamūlaṃ niṣeveta sadācāram atandritaḥ //
english: Let him, untired, follow the conduct of virtuous men, connected with his occupations, which has been fully declared in the revealed texts and in the sacred tradition (Smriti) and is the root of the sacred law.

sanskrit: ācārāl labhate hy āyur ācārād īpsitāḥ prajāḥ / ācārād dhanam akṣayyam ācāro hanty alakṣaṇam //
english: Through virtuous conduct he obtains long life, through virtuous conduct desirable offspring, through virtuous conduct imperishable wealth; virtuous conduct destroys (the effect of) inauspicious marks.

sanskrit: durācāro hi puruṣo loke bhavati ninditaḥ / duḥkhabhāgī ca satataṃ vyādhito 'lpāyur eva ca //
english: For a man of bad conduct is blamed among people, constantly suffers misfortunes, is afflicted with diseases, and short-lived.

sanskrit: sarvalakṣaṇahīno 'pi yaḥ sadācāravān naraḥ / śraddadhāno 'nasūyaś ca śataṃ varṣāṇi jīvati //
english: A man who follows the conduct of the virtuous, has faith and is free from envy, lives a hundred years, though he be entirely destitute of auspicious marks.

sanskrit: yad yat paravaśaṃ karma tat tad yatnena varjayet / yad yad ātmavaśaṃ tu syāt tat tat seveta yatnataḥ //
english: Let him carefully avoid all undertakings (the success of) which depends on others; but let him eagerly pursue that (the accomplishment of) which depends on himself.

sanskrit: sarvaṃ paravaśaṃ duḥkhaṃ sarvam ātmavaśaṃ sukham / etad vidyāt samāsena lakṣaṇaṃ sukhaduḥkhayoḥ //
english: Everything that depends on others (gives) pain, everything that depends on oneself (gives) pleasure; know that this is the short definition of pleasure and pain.

sanskrit: yat karma kurvato 'sya syāt paritoṣo 'ntarātmanaḥ / tat prayatnena kurvīta viparītaṃ tu varjayet //
english: When the performance of an act gladdens his heart, let him perform it with diligence; but let him avoid the opposite.

sanskrit: ācāryaṃ ca pravaktāraṃ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ gurum / na hiṃsyād brāhmaṇān gāś ca sarvāṃś caiva tapasvinaḥ //
english: Let him never offend the teacher who initiated him, nor him who explained the Veda, nor his father and mother, nor (any other) Guru, nor cows, nor Brahmanas, nor any men performing austerities.

sanskrit: nāstikyaṃ vedanindāṃ ca devatānāṃ ca kutsanam / dveṣaṃ dambhaṃ ca mānaṃ ca krodhaṃ taikṣṇyaṃ ca varjayet //
english: Let him avoid atheism, cavilling at the Vedas, contempt of the gods, hatred, want of modesty, pride, anger, and harshness.

sanskrit: parasya daṇḍaṃ nodyacchet kruddho nainaṃ nipātayet / anyatra putrāc chiṣyād vā śiṣṭyarthaṃ tāḍayet tu tau //
english: Let him, when angry, not raise a stick against another man, nor strike (anybody) except a son or a pupil; those two he may beat in order to correct them.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāyāvaguryaiva dvijātir vadhakāmyayā / śataṃ varṣāṇi tāmisre narake parivartate //
english: A twice-born man who has merely threatened a Brahmana with the intention of (doing him) a corporal injury, will wander about for a hundred years in the Tamisra hell.

sanskrit: tāḍayitvā tṛṇenāpi saṃrambhān matipūrvakam / ekaviṃśatīm ājātīḥ pāpayoniṣu jāyate //
english: Having intentionally struck him in anger, even with a blade of grass, he will be born during twenty-one existences in the wombs (of such beings where men are born in punishment of their) sins.

sanskrit: ayudhyamānasyotpādya brāhmaṇasyāsṛg aṅgataḥ / duḥkhaṃ sumahad āpnoti pretyāprājñatayā naraḥ //
english: A man who in his folly caused blood to flow from the body of a Brahmana who does not attack him, will suffer after death exceedingly great pain.

sanskrit: śoṇitaṃ yāvataḥ pāṃsūn saṃgṛhṇāti mahītalāt / tāvato 'bdān amutrānyaiḥ śoṇitotpādako 'dyate //
english: As many particles of dust as the blood takes up from the ground, during so many years the spiller of the blood will be devoured by other (animals) in the next world.

sanskrit: na kadā cid dvije tasmād vidvān avagured api / na tāḍayet tṛṇenāpi na gātrāt srāvayed asṛk //
english: A wise man should therefore never threaten a Brahmana, nor strike him even with a blade of grass, nor cause his blood to flow.

sanskrit: adhārmiko naro yo hi yasya cāpy anṛtaṃ dhanam / hiṃsārataś ca yo nityaṃ nehāsau sukham edhate //
english: Neither a man who (lives) unrighteously, nor he who (acquires) wealth (by telling) falsehoods, nor he who always delights in doing injury, ever attain happiness in this world.

sanskrit: na sīdann api dharmeṇa mano 'dharme niveśayet / adhārmikānāṃ pāpānām āśu paśyan viparyayam //
english: Let him, though suffering in consequence of his righteousness, never turn his heart to unrighteousness; for he will see the speedy overthrow of unrighteous, wicked men.

sanskrit: nādharmaś carito loke sadyaḥ phalati gaur iva / śanair āvartyamānas tu kartur mūlāni kṛntati //
english: Unrighteousness, practised in this world, does not at once produce its fruit, like a cow; but, advancing slowly, it cuts off the roots of him who committed it.

sanskrit: yadi nātmani putreṣu na cet putreṣu naptṛṣu / na tv eva tu kṛto 'dharmaḥ kartur bhavati niṣphalaḥ //
english: If (the punishment falls) not on (the offender) himself, (it falls) on his sons, if not on the sons, (at least) on his grandsons; but an iniquity (once) committed, never fails to produce fruit to him who wrought it.

sanskrit: adharmeṇaidhate tāvat tato bhadrāṇi paśyati / tataḥ sapatnān jayati samūlas tu vinaśyati //
english: He prospers for a while through unrighteousness, then he gains great good fortune, next he conquers his enemies, but (at last) he perishes (branch and) root.

sanskrit: satyadharmāryavṛtteṣu śauce caivāramet sadā / śiṣyāṃś ca śiṣyād dharmeṇa vāgbāhūdarasaṃyataḥ //
english: Let him always delight in truthfulness, (obedience to) the sacred law, conduct worthy of an Aryan, and purity; let him chastise his pupils according to the sacred law; let him keep his speech, his arms, and his belly under control.

sanskrit: parityajed arthakāmau yau syātāṃ dharmavarjitau / dharmaṃ cāpy asukhodarkaṃ lokasaṃkruṣṭam eva ca //
english: Let him avoid (the acquisition of) wealth and (the gratification of his) desires, if they are opposed to the sacred law, and even lawful acts which may cause pain in the future or are offensive to men.

sanskrit: na pāṇipādacapalo na netracapalo 'nṛjuḥ / na syād vākcapalaś caiva na paradrohakarmadhīḥ //
english: Let him not be uselessly active with his hands and feet, or with his eyes, nor crooked (in his ways), nor talk idly, nor injure others by deeds or even think of it.

sanskrit: yenāsya pitaro yātā yena yātāḥ pitāmahāḥ / tena yāyāt satāṃ mārgaṃ tena gacchan na riṣyati //
english: Let him walk in that path of holy men which his fathers and his grandfathers followed; while he walks in that, he will not suffer harm.

sanskrit: ṛtvikpurohitācāryair mātulātithisaṃśritaiḥ / bālavṛddhāturair vaidyair jñātisaṃbandhibāndhavaiḥ //
english: With an officiating or a domestic priest, with a teacher, with a maternal uncle, a guest and a dependant, with infants, aged and sick men, with learned men, with his paternal relatives, connexions by marriage and maternal relatives,

sanskrit: mātāpitṛbhyāṃ jāmībhir bhrātrā putreṇa bhāryayā / duhitrā dāsavargeṇa vivādaṃ na samācaret //
english: With his father and his mother, with female relatives, with a brother, with his son and his wife, with his daughter and with his slaves, let him not have quarrels.

sanskrit: etair vivādān saṃtyajya sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate / etair jitaiś ca jayati sarvāṃl lokān imān gṛhī //
english: If he avoids quarrels with these persons, he will be freed from all sins, and by suppressing (all) such (quarrels) a householder conquers all the following worlds.

sanskrit: ācāryo brahmalokeśaḥ prājāpatye pitā prabhuḥ / atithis tv indralokeśo devalokasya ca rtvijaḥ //
english: The teacher is the lord of the world of Brahman, the father has power over the world of the Lord of created beings (Pragapati), a guest rules over the world of Indra, and the priests over the world of the gods.

sanskrit: jāmayo 'psarasāṃ loke vaiśvadevasya bāndhavāḥ / saṃbandhino hy apāṃ loke pṛthivyāṃ mātṛmātulau //
english: The female relatives (have power) over the world of the Apsarases, the maternal relatives over that of the Visve Devas, the connexions by marriage over that of the waters, the mother and the maternal uncle over the earth.

sanskrit: ākāśeśās tu vijñeyā bālavṛddhakṛśāturāḥ / bhrātā jyeṣṭhaḥ samaḥ pitrā bhāryā putraḥ svakā tanuḥ // chāyā svo dāsavargaś ca duhitā kṛpaṇaṃ param / tasmād etair adhikṣiptaḥ sahetāsaṃjvaraḥ sadā //
english: Infants, aged, poor and sick men must be considered as rulers of the middle sphere, the eldest brother as equal to one's father, one's wife and one's son as one's own body, One's slaves as one's shadow, one's daughter as the highest object of tenderness; hence if one is offended by (any one of) these, one must bear it without resentment.

sanskrit: pratigrahasamartho 'pi prasaṅgaṃ tatra varjayet / pratigraheṇa hy asyāśu brāhmaṃ tejaḥ praśāmyati //
english: Though (by his learning and sanctity) he may be entitled to accept presents, let him not attach himself (too much) to that (habit); for through his accepting (many) presents the divine light in him is soon extinguished.

sanskrit: na dravyāṇām avijñāya vidhiṃ dharmyaṃ pratigrahe / prājñaḥ pratigrahaṃ kuryād avasīdann api kṣudhā //
english: Without a full knowledge of the rules, prescribed by the sacred law for the acceptance of presents, a wise man should not take anything, even though he may pine with hunger.

sanskrit: hiraṇyaṃ bhūmim aśvaṃ gām annaṃ vāsas tilān ghṛtam / pratigṛhṇann avidvāṃs tu bhasmībhavati dāruvat //
english: But an ignorant (man) who accepts gold, land, a horse, a cow, food, a dress, sesamum-grains, (or) clarified butter, is reduced to ashes like (a piece of) wood.

sanskrit: hiraṇyam āyur annaṃ ca bhūr gauś cāpy oṣatas tanum / aśvaś cakṣus tvacaṃ vāso ghṛtaṃ tejas tilāh prajāḥ //
english: Gold and food destroy his longevity, land and a cow his body, a horse his eye (sight), a garment his skin, clarified butter his energy, sesamum-grains his offspring.

sanskrit: atapās tv anadhīyānaḥ pratigraharucir dvijaḥ / ambhasy aśmaplaveneva saha tenaiva majjati //
english: A Brahmana who neither performs austerities nor studies the Veda, yet delights in accepting gifts, sinks with the (donor into hell), just as (he who attempts to cross over in) a boat made of stone (is submerged) in the water.

sanskrit: tasmād avidvān bibhiyād yasmāt tasmāt pratigrahāt / svalpakenāpy avidvān hi paṅke gaur iva sīdati //
english: Hence an ignorant (man) should be afraid of accepting any presents; for by reason of a very small (gift) even a fool sinks (into hell) as a cow into a morass.

sanskrit: na vāry api prayacchet tu baiḍālavratike dvije / na bakavratike pāpe nāvedavidi dharmavit //
english: (A man) who knows the law should not offer even water to a Brahmana who acts like a cat, nor to a Brahmana who acts like a heron, nor to one who is unacquainted with the Veda.

sanskrit: triṣv apy eteṣu dattaṃ hi vidhināpy arjitaṃ dhanam / dātur bhavaty anarthāya paratrādātur eva ca //
english: For property, though earned in accordance with prescribed rules, which is given to these three (persons), causes in the next world misery both to the giver and to the recipient.

sanskrit: yathā plavenāupalena nimajjaty udake taran / tathā nimajjato 'dhastād ajñau dātṛpratīcchakau //
english: As he who (attempts to) cross water in a boat of stone sinks (to the bottom), even so an ignorant donor and an ignorant donee sink low.

sanskrit: dharmadhvajī sadā lubdhaś chādmiko lokadambhakaḥ / baiḍālavratiko jñeyo hiṃsraḥ sarvābhisaṃdhakaḥ //
english: (A man) who, ever covetous, displays the flag of virtue, (who is) a hypocrite, a deceiver of the people, intent on doing injury, (and) a detractor (from the merits) of all men, one must know to be one who acts like a cat.

sanskrit: adhodṛṣṭir naiṣkṛtikaḥ svārthasādhanatatparaḥ / śaṭho mithyāvinītaś ca bakavratacaro dvijaḥ //
english: That Brahmana, who with downcast look, of a cruel disposition, is solely intent on attaining his own ends, dishonest and falsely gentle, is one who acts like a heron.

sanskrit: ye bakavratino viprā ye ca mārjāraliṅginaḥ / te patanty andhatāmisre tena pāpena karmaṇā //
english: Those Brahmanas who act like herons, and those who display the characteristics of cats, fall in consequence of that wicked mode of acting into (the hell called) Andhatamisra.

sanskrit: na dharmasyāpadeśena pāpaṃ kṛtvā vrataṃ caret / vratena pāpaṃ pracchādya kurvan strīśūdradambhanam //
english: When he has committed a sin, let him not perform a penance under the pretence (that the act is intended to gain) spiritual merit, (thus) hiding his sin under (the pretext of) a vow and deceiving women and Sudras.

sanskrit: pretyeha cedṛśā viprā garhyante brahmavādibhiḥ / chadmanā caritaṃ yac ca vrataṃ rakṣāṃsi gacchati //
english: Such Brahmanas are reprehended after death and in this (life) by those who expound the Veda, and a vow, performed under a false pretence, goes to the Rakshasas.

sanskrit: aliṅgī liṅgiveṣeṇa yo vṛttim upajīvati / sa liṅgināṃ haraty enas tiryagyonau ca jāyate //
english: He who, without being a student, gains his livelihood by (wearing) the dress of a student, takes upon himself the guilt of (all) students and is born again in the womb of an animal.

sanskrit: parakīyanipāneṣu na snāyād dhi kadā cana / nipānakartuḥ snātvā tu duṣkṛtāṃśena lipyate //
english: Let him never bathe in tanks belonging to other men; if he bathes (in such a one), he is tainted by a portion of the guilt of him who made the tank.

sanskrit: yānaśayyāsanāny asya kūpodyānagṛhāṇi ca / adattāny upayuñjāna enasaḥ syāt turīyabhāk //
english: He who uses without permission a carriage, a bed, a seat, a well, a garden or a house belonging to an (other man), takes upon himself one fourth of (the owner's) guilt.

sanskrit: nadīṣu devakhāteṣu taḍāgeṣu saraḥsu ca / snānaṃ samācaren nityaṃ gartaprasravaṇeṣu ca //
english: Let him always bathe in rivers, in ponds, dug by the gods (themselves), in lakes, and in waterholes or springs.

sanskrit: yamān seveta satataṃ na nityaṃ niyamān budhaḥ / yamān pataty akurvāṇo niyamān kevalān bhajan //
english: A wise man should constantly discharge the paramount duties (called yama), but not always the minor ones (called niyama); for he who does not discharge the former, while he obeys the latter alone, becomes an outcast.

sanskrit: nāśrotriyatate yajñe grāmayājikṛte tathā / striyā klībena ca hute bhuñjīta brāhmaṇaḥ kva cit //
english: A Brahmana must never eat (a dinner given) at a sacrifice that is offered by one who is not a Srotriya, by one who sacrifices for a multitude of men, by a woman, or by a eunuch.

sanskrit: aślīkam etat sādhūnāṃ yatra juhvaty amī haviḥ / pratīpam etad devānāṃ tasmāt tat parivarjayet //
english: When those persons offer sacrificial viands in the fire, it is unlucky for holy (men) it displeases the gods; let him therefore avoid it.

sanskrit: mattakruddhāturāṇāṃ ca na bhuñjīta kadā cana / keśakīṭāvapannaṃ ca padā spṛṣṭaṃ ca kāmataḥ // bhrūṇaghnāvekṣitaṃ caiva saṃspṛṣṭaṃ cāpy udakyayā / patatriṇāvalīḍhaṃ ca śunā saṃspṛṣṭam eva ca //
english: Let him never eat (food given) by intoxicated, angry, or sick (men), nor that in which hair or insects are found, nor what has been touched intentionally with the foot, Nor that at which the slayer of a learned Brahmana has looked, nor that which has been touched by a menstruating woman, nor that which has been pecked at by birds or touched by a dog,

sanskrit: gavā cānnam upaghrātaṃ ghuṣṭānnaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ / gaṇānnaṃ gaṇikānnaṃ ca viduṣā ca jugupsitam //
english: Nor food at which a cow has smelt, nor particularly that which has been offered by an invitation to all comers, nor that (given) by a multitude or by harlots, nor that which is declared to be had by a learned (man),

sanskrit: stenagāyanayoś cānnaṃ takṣṇo vārdhuṣikasya ca / dīkṣitasya kadaryasya baddhasya nigaḍasya ca //
english: Nor the food (given) by a thief, a musician, a carpenter, a usurer, one who has been initiated (for the performance of a Srauta sacrifice), a miser, one bound with fetters,

sanskrit: abhiśastasya ṣaṇḍhasya puṃścalyā dāmbhikasya ca / śuktaṃ paryuṣitaṃ caiva śūdrasyocchiṣṭam eva ca // cikitsakasya mṛgayoḥ krūrasyocchiṣṭabhojinaḥ / ugrānnaṃ sūtikānnaṃ ca paryācāntam anirdaśam // anarcitaṃ vṛthāmāṃsam avīrāyāś ca yoṣitaḥ / dviṣadannaṃ nagaryannaṃ patitānnam avakṣutam //
english: Nor (the food given) by a physician, a hunter, a cruel man, one who eats the fragments (of another's meal), nor the food of an Ugra, nor that prepared for a woman in childbed, nor that (given at a dinner) where (a guest rises) prematurely (and) sips water, nor that (given by a woman) whose ten days of impurity have not elapsed, Nor (food) given without due respect, nor (that which contains) meat eaten for no sacred purpose, nor (that given) by a female who has no male (relatives), nor the food of an enemy, nor that (given) by the lord of a town, nor that (given) by outcasts, nor that on which anybody has sneezed;

sanskrit: piśunānṛtinoś cānnaṃ kratuvikrayiṇas tathā / śailūṣatunnavāyānnaṃ kṛtaghnasyānnam eva ca // karmārasya niṣādasya raṅgāvatārakasya ca / suvarṇakartur veṇasya śastravikrayiṇas tathā //
english: Nor the food (given) by an informer, by one who habitually tells falsehoods, or by one who sells (the rewards for) sacrifices, nor the food (given) by an actor, a tailor, or an ungrateful (man), By a blacksmith, a Nishada, a stage-player, a goldsmith, a basket-maker, or a dealer in weapons,

sanskrit: śvavatāṃ śauṇḍikānāṃ ca cailanirṇejakasya ca / rañjakasya nṛśaṃsasya yasya copapatir gṛhe //
english: By trainers of hunting dogs, publicans, a washerman, a dyer, a pitiless (man), and a man in whose house (lives) a paramour (of his wife),

sanskrit: mṛṣyanti ye copapatiṃ strījitānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ / anirdaśaṃ ca pretānnam atuṣṭikaram eva ca //
english: Nor (the food given) by those who knowingly bear with paramours (of their wives), and by those who in all matters are ruled by women, nor food (given by men) whose ten days of impurity on account of a death have not passed, nor that which is unpalatable.

sanskrit: rājānnaṃ teja ādatte śūdrānnaṃ brahmavarcasam / āyuḥ suvarṇakārānnaṃ yaśaś carmāvakartinaḥ //
english: The food of a king impairs his vigour, the food of a Sudra his excellence in sacred learning, the food of a goldsmith his longevity, that of a leather-cutter his fame;

sanskrit: kārukānnaṃ prajāṃ hanti balaṃ nirṇejakasya ca / gaṇānnaṃ gaṇikānnaṃ ca lokebhyaḥ parikṛntati //
english: The food of an artisan destroys his offspring, that of a washerman his (bodily) strength; the food of a multitude and of harlots excludes him from (the higher) worlds.

sanskrit: pūyaṃ cikitsakasyānnaṃ puṃścalyās tv annam indriyam / viṣṭhā vārdhuṣikasyānnaṃ śastravikrayiṇo malam //
english: The food of a physician (is as vile as) pus, that of an unchaste woman (equal to) semen, that of a usurer (as vile as) ordure, and that of a dealer in weapons (as bad as) dirt.

sanskrit: ya ete 'nye tv abhojyānnāḥ kramaśaḥ parikīrtitāḥ / teṣāṃ tvagasthiromāṇi vadanty annaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ //
english: The food of those other persons who have been successively enumerated as such whose food must not be eaten, the wise declare (to be as impure as) skin, bones, and hair.

sanskrit: bhuktvāto 'nyatam asyānnam amatyā kṣapaṇaṃ tryaham / matyā bhuktvācaret kṛcchraṃ retoviṇmūtram eva ca //
english: If he has unwittingly eaten the food of one of those, (he must) fast for three days; if he has eaten it intentionally, or (has swallowed) semen, ordure, or urine, he must perform a Krikkhra penance.

sanskrit: nādyāc chūdrasya pakvānnaṃ vidvān aśrāddhino dvijaḥ / ādadītāmam evāsmād avṛttāv ekarātrikam //
english: A Brahmana who knows (the law) must not eat cooked food (given) by a Sudra who performs no Sraddhas; but, on failure of (other) means of subsistence, he may accept raw (grain), sufficient for one night (and day).

sanskrit: śrotriyasya kadaryasya vadānyasya ca vārdhuṣeḥ / mīmāṃsitvobhayaṃ devāḥ samam annam akalpayan //
english: The gods, having considered (the respective merits) of a niggardly Srotriya and of a liberal usurer, declared the food of both to be equal (in quality).

sanskrit: tān prajāpatir āhaitya mā kṛdhvaṃ viṣamaṃ samam / śraddhāpūtaṃ vadānyasya hatam aśraddhayetarat //
english: The Lord of created beings (Pragapati) came and spake to them, 'Do not make that equal, which is unequal. The food of that liberal (usurer) is purified by faith; (that of the) of the) other (man) is defiled by a want of faith.'

sanskrit: śraddhayeṣṭaṃ ca pūrtaṃ ca nityaṃ kuryād atandritaḥ / śraddhākṛte hy akṣaye te bhavataḥ svāgatair dhanaiḥ // dānadharmaṃ niṣeveta nityam aiṣṭikapaurtikam / parituṣṭena bhāvena pātram āsādya śaktitaḥ //
english: Let him, without tiring, always offer sacrifices and perform works of charity with faith; for offerings and charitable works made with faith and with lawfully-earned money, (procure) endless rewards. Let him always practise, according to his ability, with a cheerful heart, the duty of liberality, both by sacrifices and by charitable works, if he finds a worthy recipient (for his gifts.)

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cid api dātavyaṃ yācitenānasūyayā / utpatsyate hi tat pātraṃ yat tārayati sarvataḥ //
english: If he is asked, let him always give something, be it ever so little, without grudging; for a worthy recipient will (perhaps) be found who saves him from all (guilt).

sanskrit: vāridas tṛptim āpnoti sukham akṣayyam annadaḥ / tilapradaḥ prajām iṣṭāṃ dīpadaś cakṣur uttamam //
english: A giver of water obtains the satisfaction (of his hunger and thirst), a giver of food imperishable happiness, a giver of sesamum desirable offspring, a giver of a lamp a most excellent eyesight.

sanskrit: bhūmido bhūmim āpnoti dīrgham āyur hiraṇyadaḥ / gṛhado 'gryāṇi veśmāni rūpyado rūpam uttamam //
english: A giver of land obtains land, a giver of gold long life, a giver of a house most excellent mansions, a giver of silver (rupya) exquisite beauty (rupa),

sanskrit: vāsodaś candrasālokyam aśvisālokyam aśvadaḥ / anaḍuhaḥ śriyaṃ puṣṭāṃ godo bradhnasya viṣṭapam // yānaśayyāprado bhāryām aiśvaryam abhayapradaḥ / dhānyadaḥ śāśvataṃ saukhyaṃ brahmado brahmasārṣṭitām // sarveṣām eva dānānāṃ brahmadānaṃ viśiṣyate / vāryannagomahīvāsas- tilakāñcanasarpiṣām //
english: A giver of a garment a place in the world of the moon, a giver of a horse (asva) a place in the world of the Asvins, a giver of a draught-ox great good fortune, a giver of a cow the world of the sun; A giver of a carriage or of a bed a wife, a giver of protection supreme dominion, a giver of grain eternal bliss, a giver of the Veda (brahman) union with Brahman; The gift of the Veda surpasses all other gifts, water, food, cows, land, clothes, sesamum, gold, and clarified butter.

sanskrit: yena yena tu bhāvena yad yad dānaṃ prayacchati / tat tat tenaiva bhāvena prāpnoti pratipūjitaḥ //
english: For whatever purpose (a man) bestows any gift, for that same purpose he receives (in his next birth) with due honour its (reward).

sanskrit: yo 'rcitaṃ pratigṛhṇāti dadāty arcitam eva vā / tāv ubhau gacchataḥ svargaṃ narakaṃ tu viparyaye //
english: Both he who respectfully receives (a gift), and he who respectfully bestows it, go to heaven; in the contrary case (they both fall) into hell.

sanskrit: na vismayeta tapasā vaded iṣṭvā ca nānṛtam / nārto 'py apavaded viprān na dattvā parikīrtayet //
english: Let him not be proud of his austerities; let him not utter a falsehood after he has offered a sacrifice; let him not speak ill of Brahmanas, though he be tormented (by them); when he has bestowed (a gift), let him not boast of it.

sanskrit: yajño 'nṛtena kṣarati tapaḥ kṣarati vismayāt / āyur viprāpavādena dānaṃ ca parikīrtanāt //
english: By falsehood a sacrifice becomes vain, by self-complacency (the reward for) austerities is lost, longevity by speaking evil of Brahmanas, and (the reward of) a gift by boasting.

sanskrit: dharmaṃ śanaiḥ saṃcinuyād valmīkam iva puttikāḥ / paralokasahāyārthaṃ sarvabhūtāny apīḍayan //
english: Giving no pain to any creature, let him slowly accumulate spiritual merit, for the sake (of acquiring) a companion to the next world, just as the white ant (gradually raises its) hill.

sanskrit: nāmutra hi sahāyārthaṃ pitā mātā ca tiṣṭhataḥ / na putradāraṃ na jñātir dharmas tiṣṭhati kevalaḥ //
english: For in the next world neither father, nor mother, nor wife, nor sons, nor relations stay to be his companions; spiritual merit alone remains (with him).

sanskrit: ekaḥ prajāyate jantur eka eva pralīyate / eko 'nubhuṅkte sukṛtam eka eva ca duṣkṛtam //
english: Single is each being born; single it dies; single it enjoys (the reward of its) virtue; single (it suffers the punishment of its) sin.

sanskrit: mṛtaṃ śarīram utsṛjya kāṣṭhaloṣṭasamaṃ kṣitau / vimukhā bāndhavā yānti dharmas tam anugacchati //
english: Leaving the dead body on the ground like a log of wood, or a clod of earth, the relatives depart with averted faces; but spiritual merit follows the (soul).

sanskrit: tasmād dharmaṃ sahāyārthaṃ nityaṃ saṃcinuyāc chanaiḥ / dharmeṇa hi sahāyena tamas tarati dustaram //
english: Let him therefore always slowly accumulate spiritual merit, in order (that it may be his) companion (after death); for with merit as his companion he will traverse a gloom difficult to traverse.

sanskrit: dharmapradhānaṃ puruṣaṃ tapasā hatakilbiṣam / paralokaṃ nayaty āśu bhāsvantaṃ khaśarīriṇam //
english: (That companion) speedily conducts the man who is devoted to duty and effaces his sins by austerities, to the next world, radiant and clothed with an ethereal body.

sanskrit: uttamair uttamair nityaṃ saṃbandhān ācaret saha / ninīṣuḥ kulam utkarṣam adhamān adhamāṃs tyajet //
english: Let him, who desires to raise his race, ever form connexions with the most excellent (men), and shun all low ones.

sanskrit: uttamān uttamān eva gacchan hīnāṃs tu varjayan / brāhmaṇaḥ śreṣṭhatām eti pratyavāyena śūdratām //
english: A Brahmana who always connects himself with the most excellent (ones), and shuns all inferior ones, (himself) becomes most distinguished; by an opposite conduct he becomes a Sudra.

sanskrit: dṛḍhakārī mṛdur dāntaḥ krūrācārair asaṃvasan / ahiṃsro damadānābhyāṃ jayet svargaṃ tathāvrataḥ //
english: He who is persevering, gentle, (and) patient, shuns the company of men of cruel conduct, and does no injury (to living creatures), gains, if he constantly lives in that manner, by controlling his organs and by liberality, heavenly bliss.

sanskrit: edhodakaṃ mūlaphalam annam abhyudyataṃ ca yat / sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyān madhv athābhayadakṣiṇām //
english: He may accept from any (man), fuel, water, roots, fruit, food offered without asking, and honey, likewise a gift (which consists in) a promise of protection.

sanskrit: āhṛtābhyudyatāṃ bhikṣāṃ purastād apracoditām / mene prajāpatir grāhyām api duṣkṛtakarmaṇaḥ //
english: The Lord of created beings (Pragapati) has declared that alms freely offered and brought (by the giver himself) may be accepted even from a sinful man, provided (the gift) had not been (asked for or) promised beforehand.

sanskrit: nāśnanti pitaras tasya daśavarṣāṇi pañca ca / na ca havyaṃ vahaty agnir yas tām abhyavamanyate //
english: During fifteen years the manes do not eat (the food) of that man who disdains a (freely-offered gift), nor does the fire carry his offerings (to the gods).

sanskrit: śayyāṃ gṛhān kuśān gandhān apaḥ puṣpaṃ maṇīn dadhi / dhānā matsyān payo māṃsaṃ śākaṃ caiva na nirṇudet //
english: A couch, a house, Kusa grass, perfumes, water, flowers, jewels, sour milk, grain, fish, sweet milk, meat, and vegetables let him not reject, (if they are voluntarily offered.)

sanskrit: gurūn bhṛtyāṃś cojjihīrṣann arciṣyan devatātithīn / sarvataḥ pratigṛhṇīyān na tu tṛpyet svayaṃ tataḥ // guruṣu tv abhyatīteṣu vinā vā tair gṛhe vasan / ātmano vṛttim anvicchan gṛhṇīyāt sādhutaḥ sadā //
english: He who desires to relieve his Gurus and those whom he is bound to maintain, or wishes to honour the gods and guests, may accept (gifts) from anybody; but he must not satisfy his (own hunger) with such (presents). But if his Gurus are dead, or if he lives separate from them in (another) house, let him, when he seeks a subsistence, accept (presents) from good men alone.

sanskrit: ārdhikaḥ kulamitraṃ ca gopālo dāsanāpitau / ete śūdreṣu bhojyānnā yāś cātmānaṃ nivedayet //
english: His labourer in tillage, a friend of his family, his cow-herd, his slave, and his barber are, among Sudras, those whose food he may eat, likewise (a poor man) who offers himself (to be his slave).

sanskrit: yādṛśo 'sya bhaved ātmā yādṛśaṃ ca cikīrṣitam / yathā copacared enaṃ tathātmānaṃ nivedayet //
english: As his character is, as the work is which he desires to perform, and as the manner is in which he means to serve, even so (a voluntary slave) must offer himself.

sanskrit: yo 'nyathā santam ātmānam anyathā satsu bhāṣate / sa pāpakṛttamo loke stena ātmāpahārakaḥ //
english: He who describes himself to virtuous (men), in a manner contrary to truth, is the most sinful (wretch) in this world; he is a thief who makes away with his own self.

sanskrit: vācy arthā niyatāḥ sarve vāṅgūlā vāgviniḥsṛtāḥ / tāṃs tu yaḥ stenayed vācaṃ sa sarvasteyakṛn naraḥ //
english: All things (have their nature) determined by speech; speech is their root, and from speech they proceed; but he who is dishonest with respect to speech, is dishonest in everything.

sanskrit: maharṣipitṛdevānāṃ gatvānṛṇyaṃ yathāvidhi / putre sarvaṃ samāsajya vasen mādhyasthyam āśritaḥ //
english: When he has paid, according to the law, his debts to the great sages, to the manes, and to the gods, let him make over everything to his son and dwell (in his house), not caring for any worldly concerns.

sanskrit: ekākī cintayen nityaṃ vivikte hitam ātmanaḥ / ekākī cintayāno hi paraṃ śreyo 'dhigacchati //
english: Alone let him constantly meditate in solitude on that which is salutary for his soul; for he who meditates in solitude attains supreme bliss.

sanskrit: eṣoditā gṛhasthasya vṛttir viprasya śāśvatī / snātakavratakalpaś ca sattvavṛddhikaraḥ śubhaḥ //
english: Thus have been declared the means by which a Brahmana householder must always subsist, and the summary of the ordinances for a Snataka, which cause an increase of holiness and are praiseworthy.

sanskrit: anena vipro vṛttena vartayan vedaśāstravit / vyapetakalmaṣo nityaṃ brahmaloke mahīyate //
english: A Brahmana who, being learned in the lore of the Vedas, conducts himself in this manner and daily destroys his sins, will be exalted in Brahman's world.

sanskrit: śrutvaitān ṛṣayo dharmān snātakasya yathoditān / idam ūcur mahātmānam analaprabhavaṃ bhṛgum //
english: The sages, having heard the duties of a Snataka thus declared, spoke to great-souled Bhrigu, who sprang from fire:

sanskrit: evaṃ yathoktaṃ viprāṇāṃ svadharmam anutiṣṭhatām / kathaṃ mṛtyuḥ prabhavati vedaśāstravidāṃ prabho //
english: 'How can Death have power over Brahmanas who know the sacred science, the Veda, (and) who fulfil their duties as they have been explained (by thee), O Lord? '

sanskrit: sa tān uvāca dharmātmā maharṣīn mānavo bhṛguḥ / śrūyatāṃ yena doṣeṇa mṛtyur viprān jighāṃsati //
english: Righteous Bhrigu, the son of Manu, (thus) answered the great sages: 'Hear, (in punishment) of what faults Death seeks to shorten the lives of Brahmanas!'

sanskrit: anabhyāsena vedānām ācārasya ca varjanāt / ālasyād annadoṣāc ca mṛtyur viprāñ jighāṃsati //
english: 'Through neglect of the Veda-study, through deviation from the rule of conduct, through remissness (in the fulfilment of duties), and through faults (committed by eating forbidden) food, Death becomes eager to shorten the lives of Brahmanas.'

sanskrit: laśunaṃ gṛñjanaṃ caiva palāṇḍuṃ kavakāni ca / abhakṣyāṇi dvijātīnām amedhyaprabhavāni ca //
english: Garlic, leeks and onions, mushrooms and (all plants), springing from impure (substances), are unfit to be eaten by twice-born men.

sanskrit: lohitān vṛkṣaniryāsān vṛścanaprabhavāṃs tathā / śeluṃ gavyaṃ ca peyūṣaṃ prayatnena vivarjayet //
english: One should carefully avoid red exudations from trees and (juices) flowing from incisions, the Selu (fruit), and the thickened milk of a cow (which she gives after calving).

sanskrit: vṛthā kṛsarasaṃyāvaṃ pāyasāpūpam eva ca / anupākṛtamāṃsāni devānnāni havīṃṣi ca // anirdaśāyā goḥ kṣīram auṣṭram aikaśaphaṃ tathā / āvikaṃ saṃdhinīkṣīraṃ vivatsāyāś ca goḥ payaḥ //
english: Rice boiled with sesamum, wheat mixed with butter, milk and sugar, milk-rice and flour-cakes which are not prepared for a sacrifice, meat which has not been sprinkled with water while sacred texts were recited, food offered to the gods and sacrificial viands, The milk of a cow (or other female animal) within ten days after her calving, that of camels, of one-hoofed animals, of sheep, of a cow in heat, or of one that has no calf with her,

sanskrit: āraṇyānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ mṛgāṇāṃ māhiṣaṃ vinā / strīkṣīraṃ caiva varjyāni sarvaśuktāni caiva hi //
english: (The milk) of all wild animals excepting buffalo-cows, that of women, and all (substances turned) sour must be avoided.

sanskrit: dadhi bhakṣyaṃ ca śukteṣu sarvaṃ ca dadhisaṃbhavam / yāni caivābhiṣūyante puṣpamūlaphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ //
english: Among (things turned) sour, sour milk, and all (food) prepared of it may be eaten, likewise what is extracted from pure flowers, roots, and fruit.

sanskrit: kravyādāñ śakunān sarvāṃs tathā grāmanivāsinaḥ / anirdiṣṭāṃś caikaśaphāṃṣ ṭiṭṭibhaṃ ca vivarjayet //
english: Let him avoid all carnivorous birds and those living in villages, and one-hoofed animals which are not specially permitted (to be eaten), and the Tittibha (Parra Jacana),

sanskrit: kalaviṅkaṃ plavaṃ haṃsaṃ cakrāhvaṃ grāmakukkuṭam / sārasaṃ rajjuvālaṃ ca dātyūhaṃ śukasārike //
english: The sparrow, the Plava, the Hamsa, the Brahmani duck, the village-cock, the Sarasa crane, the Raggudala, the woodpecker, the parrot, and the starling,

sanskrit: pratudāñ jālapādāṃś ca koyaṣṭinakhaviṣkirān / nimajjataś ca matsyādān saunaṃ vallūram eva ca //
english: Those which feed striking with their beaks, web-footed birds, the Koyashti, those which scratch with their toes, those which dive and live on fish, meat from a slaughter-house and dried meat,

sanskrit: bakaṃ caiva balākāṃ ca kākolaṃ khañjarīṭakam / matsyādān viḍvarāhāṃś ca matsyān eva ca sarvaśaḥ //
english: The Baka and the Balaka crane, the raven, the Khangaritaka, (animals) that eat fish, village-pigs, and all kinds of fishes.

sanskrit: yo yasya māṃsam aśnāti sa tanmāṃsāda ucyate / matsyādaḥ sarvamāṃsādas tasmān matsyān vivarjayet //
english: He who eats the flesh of any (animal) is called the eater of the flesh of that (particular creature), he who eats fish is an eater of every (kind of) flesh; let him therefore avoid fish.

sanskrit: pāṭhīnarohitāv ādyau niyuktau havyakavyayoḥ / rājīvān siṃhatuṇḍāś ca saśalkāś caiva sarvaśaḥ //
english: (But the fish called) Pathina and (that called) Rohita may be eaten, if used for offerings to the gods or to the manes; (one may eat) likewise Ragivas, Simhatundas, and Sasalkas on all (occasions).

sanskrit: na bhakṣayed ekacarān ajñātāṃś ca mṛgadvijān / bhakṣyeṣv api samuddiṣṭān sarvān pañcanakhāṃs tathā // śvāvidhaṃ śalyakaṃ godhāṃ khaḍgakūrmaśaśāṃs tathā / bhakṣyān pañcanakheṣv āhur anuṣṭrāṃś caikatodatah //
english: Let him not eat solitary or unknown beasts and birds, though they may fall under (the categories of) eatable (creatures), nor any five-toed (animals). The porcupine, the hedgehog, the iguana, the rhinoceros, the tortoise, and the hare they declare to be eatable; likewise those (domestic animals) that have teeth in one jaw only, excepting camels.

sanskrit: chatrākaṃ viḍvarāhaṃ ca laśunaṃ grāmakukkuṭam / palāṇḍuṃ gṛñjanaṃ caiva matyā jagdhvā pated dvijaḥ //
english: A twice-born man who knowingly eats mushrooms, a village-pig, garlic, a village-cock, onions, or leeks, will become an outcast.

sanskrit: amatyaitāni ṣaḍ jagdhvā kṛcchraṃ sāntapanaṃ caret / yaticāndrāyāṇaṃ vāpi śeṣeṣūpavased ahaḥ //
english: He who unwittingly partakes of (any of) these six, shall perform a Samtapana (Krikkhra) or the lunar penance (Kandrayana) of ascetics; in case (he who has eaten) any other (kind of forbidden food) he shall fast for one day (and a night ).

sanskrit: saṃvatsarasyaikam api caret kṛcchraṃ dvijottamaḥ / ajñātabhuktaśuddhyarthaṃ jñātasya tu viṣeśataḥ //
english: Once a year a Brahmana must perform a Krikkhra penance, in order to atone for unintentionally eating (forbidden food) but for intentionally (eating forbidden food he must perform the penances prescribed) specially.

sanskrit: yajñārthaṃ brāhmaṇair vadhyāḥ praśastā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ / bhṛtyānāṃ caiva vṛttyartham agastyo hy ācarat purā // babhūvur hi puroḍāśā bhakṣyāṇāṃ mṛgapakṣiṇām / purāṇeṣv api yajñeṣu brahmakṣatrasaveṣu ca //
english: Beasts and birds recommended (for consumption) may be slain by Brahmanas for sacrifices, and in order to feed those whom they are bound to maintain; for Agastya did this of old. For in ancient (times) the sacrificial cakes were (made of the flesh) of eatable beasts and birds at the sacrifices offered by Brahmanas and Kshatriyas.

sanskrit: yat kiṃ cit snehasaṃyuktaṃ bhakṣyaṃ bhojyam agarhitam / tat paryuṣitam apy ādyaṃ haviḥśeṣaṃ ca yad bhavet //
english: All lawful hard or soft food may be eaten, though stale, (after having been) mixed with fatty (substances), and so may the remains of sacrificial viands.

sanskrit: cirasthitam api tv ādyam asnehāktaṃ dvijātibhiḥ / yavagodhūmajaṃ sarvaṃ payasaś caiva vikriyā //
english: But all preparations of barley and wheat, as well as preparations of milk, may be eaten by twice-born men without being mixed with fatty (substances), though they may have stood for a long time.

sanskrit: etad uktaṃ dvijātīnāṃ bhakṣyābhakṣyam aśeṣataḥ / māṃsasyātaḥ pravakṣyāmi vidhiṃ bhakṣaṇavarjane // prokṣitaṃ bhakṣayen māṃsaṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca kāmyayā / yathāvidhi niyuktas tu prāṇānām eva cātyaye //
english: Thus has the food, allowed and forbidden to twice-born men, been fully described; I will now propound the rules for eating and avoiding meat. One may eat meat when it has been sprinkled with water, while Mantras were recited, when Brahmanas desire (one's doing it), when one is engaged (in the performance of a rite) according to the law, and when one's life is in danger.

sanskrit: prāṇasyānnam idaṃ sarvaṃ prajāpatir akalpayat / sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva sarvaṃ prāṇasya bhojanam //
english: The Lord of creatures (Pragapati) created this whole (world to be) the sustenance of the vital spirit; both the immovable and the movable (creation is) the food of the vital spirit.

sanskrit: carāṇām annam acarā daṃṣṭriṇām apy adaṃṣṭriṇaḥ / ahastāś ca sahastānāṃ śūrāṇāṃ caiva bhīravaḥ //
english: What is destitute of motion is the food of those endowed with locomotion; (animals) without fangs (are the food) of those with fangs, those without hands of those who possess hands, and the timid of the bold.

sanskrit: nāttā duṣyaty adann ādyān prāṇino 'hanyahany api / dhātraiva sṛṣṭā hy ādyāś ca prāṇino 'ttāra eva ca //
english: The eater who daily even devours those destined to be his food, commits no sin; for the creator himself created both the eaters and those who are to be eaten (for those special purposes).

sanskrit: yajñāya jagdhir māṃsasyety eṣa daivo vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ / ato 'nyathā pravṛttis tu rākṣaso vidhir ucyate //
english: 'The consumption of meat (is befitting) for sacrifices,' that is declared to be a rule made by the gods; but to persist (in using it) on other (occasions) is said to be a proceeding worthy of Rakshasas.

sanskrit: krītvā svayaṃ vāpy utpādya paropakṛtam eva vā / devān pitṝṃś cārcayitvā khādan māṃsaṃ na duṣyati //
english: He who eats meat, when he honours the gods and manes, commits no sin, whether he has bought it, or himself has killed (the animal), or has received it as a present from others.

sanskrit: nādyād avidhinā māṃsaṃ vidhijño 'nāpadi dvijaḥ / jagdhvā hy avidhinā māṃsaṃ pretas tair adyate 'vaśaḥ //
english: A twice-born man who knows the law, must not eat meat except in conformity with the law; for if he has eaten it unlawfully, he will, unable to save himself, be eaten after death by his (victims).

sanskrit: na tādṛśaṃ bhavaty eno mṛgahantur dhanārthinaḥ / yādṛśaṃ bhavati pretya vṛthāmāṃsāni khādataḥ //
english: After death the guilt of one who slays deer for gain is not as (great) as that of him who eats meat for no (sacred) purpose.

sanskrit: niyuktas tu yathānyāyaṃ yo māṃsaṃ nātti mānavaḥ / sa pretya paśutāṃ yāti saṃbhavān ekaviṃśatim //
english: But a man who, being duly engaged (to officiate or to dine at a sacred rite), refuses to eat meat, becomes after death an animal during twenty-one existences.

sanskrit: asaṃskṛtān paśūn mantrair nādyād vipraḥ kadā cana / mantrais tu saṃskṛtān adyāc chāśvataṃ vidhim āsthitaḥ //
english: A Brahmana must never eat (the flesh of animals unhallowed by Mantras; but, obedient to the primeval law, he may eat it, consecrated with Vedic texts.

sanskrit: kuryād ghṛtapaśuṃ saṅge kuryāt piṣṭapaśuṃ tathā / na tv eva tu vṛthā hantuṃ paśum icchet kadā cana //
english: If he has a strong desire (for meat) he may make an animal of clarified butter or one of flour, (and eat that); but let him never seek to destroy an animal without a (lawful) reason.

sanskrit: yāvanti paśuromāṇi tāvatkṛtvo ha māraṇam / vṛthāpaśughnaḥ prāpnoti pretya janmani janmani //
english: As many hairs as the slain beast has, so often indeed will he who killed it without a (lawful) reason suffer a violent death in future births.

sanskrit: yajñārthaṃ paśavaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ svayam eva svayaṃbhuvā / yajño 'sya bhūtyai sarvasya tasmād yajñe vadho 'vadhaḥ //
english: Svayambhu (the Self-existent) himself created animals for the sake of sacrifices; sacrifices (have been instituted) for the good of this whole (world); hence the slaughtering (of beasts) for sacrifices is not slaughtering (in the ordinary sense of the word).

sanskrit: oṣadhyaḥ paśavo vṛkṣās tiryañcaḥ pakṣiṇas tathā / yajñārthaṃ nidhanaṃ prāptāḥ prāpnuvanty utsṛtīḥ punaḥ //
english: Herbs, trees, cattle, birds, and (other) animals that have been destroyed for sacrifices, receive (being reborn) higher existences.

sanskrit: madhuparke ca yajñe ca pitṛdaivatakarmaṇi / atraiva paśavo hiṃsyā nānyatrety abravīn manuḥ //
english: On offering the honey-mixture (to a guest), at a sacrifice and at the rites in honour of the manes, but on these occasions only, may an animal be slain; that (rule) Manu proclaimed.

sanskrit: eṣv artheṣu paśūn hiṃsan vedatattvārthavid dvijaḥ / ātmānaṃ ca paśuṃ caiva gamayaty uttamaṃ gatim //
english: A twice-born man who, knowing the true meaning of the Veda, slays an animal for these purposes, causes both himself and the animal to enter a most blessed state.

sanskrit: gṛhe gurāv araṇye vā nivasann ātmavān dvijaḥ / nāvedavihitāṃ hiṃsām āpady api samācaret //
english: A twice-born man of virtuous disposition, whether he dwells in (his own) house, with a teacher, or in the forest, must never, even in times of distress, cause an injury (to any creature) which is not sanctioned by the Veda.

sanskrit: yā vedavihitā hiṃsā niyatāsmiṃś carācare / ahiṃsām eva tāṃ vidyād vedād dharmo hi nirbabhau //
english: Know that the injury to moving creatures and to those destitute of motion, which the Veda has prescribed for certain occasions, is no injury at all; for the sacred law shone forth from the Veda.

sanskrit: yo 'hiṃsakāni bhūtāni hinasty ātmasukhecchayā / sa jīvāṃś ca mṛtaś caiva na kva cit sukham edhate //
english: He who injures innoxious beings from a wish to (give) himself pleasure, never finds happiness, neither living nor dead.

sanskrit: yo bandhanavadhakleśān prāṇināṃ na cikīrṣati / sa sarvasya hitaprepsuḥ sukham atyantam aśnute //
english: He who does not seek to cause the sufferings of bonds and death to living creatures, (but) desires the good of all (beings), obtains endless bliss.

sanskrit: yad dhyāyati yat kurute ratiṃ badhnāti yatra ca / tad avāpnoty ayatnena yo hinasti na kiṃ cana //
english: He who does not injure any (creature), attains without an effort what he thinks of, what he undertakes, and what he fixes his mind on.

sanskrit: nākṛtvā prāṇināṃ hiṃsāṃ māṃsam utpadyate kva cit / na ca prāṇivadhaḥ svargyas tasmān māṃsaṃ vivarjayet //
english: Meat can never be obtained without injury to living creatures, and injury to sentient beings is detrimental to (the attainment of) heavenly bliss; let him therefore shun (the use of) meat.

sanskrit: samutpattiṃ ca māṃsasya vadhabandhau ca dehinām / prasamīkṣya nivarteta sarvamāṃsasya bhakṣaṇāt //
english: Having well considered the (disgusting) origin of flesh and the (cruelty of) fettering and slaying corporeal beings, let him entirely abstain from eating flesh.

sanskrit: na bhakṣayati yo māṃsaṃ vidhiṃ hitvā piśācavat / na loke priyatāṃ yāti vyādhibhiś ca na pīḍyate //
english: He who, disregarding the rule (given above), does not eat meat like a Pisaka, becomes dear to men, and will not be tormented by diseases.

sanskrit: anumantā viśasitā nihantā krayavikrayī / saṃskartā copahartā ca khādakaś ceti ghātakāḥ //
english: He who permits (the slaughter of an animal), he who cuts it up, he who kills it, he who buys or sells (meat), he who cooks it, he who serves it up, and he who eats it, (must all be considered as) the slayers (of the animal).

sanskrit: svamāṃsaṃ paramāṃsena yo vardhayitum icchati / anabhyarcya pitṝn devāṃs tato 'nyo nāsty apuṇyakṛt //
english: There is no greater sinner than that (man) who, though not worshipping the gods or the manes, seeks to increase (the bulk of) his own flesh by the flesh of other (beings).

sanskrit: varṣe varṣe 'śvamedhena yo yajeta śataṃ samāḥ / māṃsāni ca na khāded yas tayoḥ puṇyaphalaṃ samam //
english: He who during a hundred years annually offers a horse-sacrifice, and he who entirely abstains from meat, obtain the same reward for their meritorious (conduct).

sanskrit: phalamūlāśanair medhyair munyannānāṃ ca bhojanaiḥ / na tat phalam avāpnoti yan māṃsaparivarjanāt //
english: By subsisting on pure fruit and roots, and by eating food fit for ascetics (in the forest), one does not gain (so great) a reward as by entirely avoiding (the use of) flesh.

sanskrit: māṃ sa bhakṣayitāmutra yasya māṃsam ihādmy aham / etan māṃsasya māṃsatvaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ //
english: 'Me he (mam sah)' will devour in the next (world), whose flesh I eat in this (life); the wise declare this (to be) the real meaning of the word 'flesh' (mamsah).

sanskrit: na māṃsabhakṣaṇe doṣo na madye na ca maithune / pravṛttir eṣā bhūtānāṃ nivṛttis tu mahāphalā //
english: There is no sin in eating meat, in (drinking) spirituous liquor, and in carnal intercourse, for that is the natural way of created beings, but abstention brings great rewards.

sanskrit: pretaśuddhiṃ pravakṣyāmi dravyaśuddhiṃ tathaiva ca / caturṇām api varṇānāṃ yathāvad anupūrvaśaḥ //
english: I will now in due order explain the purification for the dead and the purification of things as they are prescribed for the four castes (varna).

sanskrit: dantajāte 'nujāte ca kṛtacūḍe ca saṃsthite / aśuddhā bāndhavāḥ sarve sūtake ca tathocyate //
english: When (a child) dies that has teethed, or that before teething has received (the sacrament of) the tonsure (Kudakarana) or (of the initiation), all relatives (become) impure, and on the birth (of a child) the same (rule) is prescribed.

sanskrit: daśāhaṃ śāvam āśaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu vidhīyate / arvāk saṃcayanād asthnāṃ tryaham ekāham eva vā //
english: It is ordained (that) among Sapindas the impurity on account of a death (shall last) ten days, (or) until the bones have been collected, (or) three days or one day only.

sanskrit: sapiṇḍatā tu puruṣe saptame vinivartate / samānodakabhāvas tu janmanāmnor avedane //
english: But the Sapinda-relationship ceases with the seventh person (in the ascending and descending lines), the Samanodaka-relationship when the (common) origin and the (existence of a common family)-name are no (longer) known.

sanskrit: yathedaṃ śāvam āśaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu vidhīyate / janane 'py evam eva syān nipuṇaṃ śuddhim icchatām //
english: As this impurity on account of a death is prescribed for (all) Sapindas, even so it shall be (held) on a birth by those who desire to be absolutely pure.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ śāvam āśaucaṃ mātāpitros tu sūtakam / sūtakaṃ mātur eva syād upaspṛśya pitā śuciḥ //
english: (Or while) the impurity on account of a death is common to all (Sapindas), that caused by a birth (falls) on the parents alone; (or) it shall fall on the mother alone, and the father shall become pure by bathing;

sanskrit: nirasya tu pumāñ śukram upaspṛsyaiva śudhyati / baijikād abhisaṃbandhād anurundhyād aghaṃ tryaham //
english: But a man, having spent his strength, is purified merely by bathing; after begetting a child (on a remarried female), he shall retain the impurity during three days.

sanskrit: ahnā caikena rātryā ca trirātrair eva ca tribhiḥ / śavaspṛśo viśudhyanti tryahād udakadāyinaḥ //
english: Those who have touched a corpse are purified after one day and night (added to) three periods of three days; those who give libations of water, after three days.

sanskrit: guroḥ pretasya śiṣyas tu pitṛmedhaṃ samācaran / pretahāraiḥ samaṃ tatra daśarātreṇa śudhyati //
english: A pupil who performs the Pitrimedha for his deceased teacher, becomes also pure after ten days, just like those who carry the corpse out (to the burial-ground).

sanskrit: rātribhir māsatulyābhir garbhasrāve viśudhyati / rajasy uparate sādhvī snānena strī rajasvalā //
english: (A woman) is purified on a miscarriage in as many (days and) nights as months (elapsed after conception), and a menstruating female becomes pure by bathing after the menstrual secretion has ceased (to flow).

sanskrit: nṛṇām akṛtacūḍānāṃ viśuddhir naiśikī smṛtā / nirvṛttacūḍakānāṃ tu trirātrāc chuddhir iṣyate //
english: (On the death) of children whose tonsure (Kudakarman) has not been performed, the (Sapindas) are declared to become pure in one (day and) night; (on the death) of those who have received the tonsure (but not the initiation, the law) ordains (that) the purification (takes place) after three days.

sanskrit: ūnadvivārṣikaṃ pretaṃ nidadhyur bāndhavā bahiḥ / alaṃkṛtya śucau bhūmāv asthisaṃcayanād ṛte //
english: A child that has died before the completion of its second year, the relatives shall carry out (of the village), decked (with flowers, and bury it) in pure ground, without collecting the bones (afterwards).

sanskrit: nāsya kāryo 'gnisaṃskāro na ca kāryodakakriyā / araṇye kāṣṭhavat tyaktvā kṣapeyus tryaham eva tu // nātrivarṣasya kartavyā bāndhavair udakakriyā / jātadantasya vā kuryur nāmni vāpi kṛte sati //
