english: Such (a child) shall not be burnt with fire, and no libations of water shall be offered to it; leaving it like a (log of) wood in the forest, (the relatives) shall remain impure during three days only. The relatives shall not offer libations to (a child) that has not reached the third year; but if it had teeth, or the ceremony of naming it (Namakarman) had been performed, (the offering of water is) optional.

sanskrit: sabrahmacāriṇy ekāham atīte kṣapaṇaṃ smṛtam / janmany ekodakānāṃ tu trirātrāc chuddhir iṣyate //
english: If a fellow-student has died, the Smriti prescribes an impurity of one day; on a birth the purification of the Samanodakas is declared (to take place) after three (days and) nights.

sanskrit: strīṇām asaṃskṛtānāṃ tu tryahāc chudhyanti bāndhavāḥ / yathoktenaiva kalpena śudhyanti tu sanābhayaḥ //
english: (On the death) of females (betrothed but) not married (the bridegroom and his) relatives are purified after three days, and the paternal relatives become pure according to the same rule.

sanskrit: akṣāralavaṇānnāḥ syur nimajjeyuś ca te tryaham / māṃsāśanaṃ ca nāśnīyuḥ śayīraṃś ca pṛthak kṣitau //
english: Let (mourners) eat food without factitious salt, bathe during three days, abstain from meat, and sleep separate on the ground.

sanskrit: saṃnidhāv eṣa vai kalpaḥ śāvāśaucasya kīrtitaḥ / asaṃnidhāv ayaṃ jñeyo vidhiḥ saṃbandhibāndhavaiḥ //
english: The above rule regarding impurity on account of a death has been prescribed (for cases where the kinsmen live) near (the deceased); (Sapinda) kinsmen and (Samanodaka) relatives must know the following rule (to refer to cases where deceased lived) at a distance (from them).

sanskrit: vigataṃ tu videśasthaṃ śṛṇuyād yo hy anirdaśam / yac cheṣaṃ daśarātrasya tāvad evāśucir bhavet //
english: He who may hear that (a relative) residing in a distant country has died, before ten (days after his death have elapsed), shall be impure for the remainder of the period of ten (days and) nights only.

sanskrit: atikrānte daśāhe ca trirātram aśucir bhavet / saṃvatsare vyatīte tu spṛṣṭvaivāpo viśudhyati //
english: If the ten days have passed, he shall be impure during three (days and) nights; but if a year has elapsed (since the occurrence of the death), he becomes pure merely by bathing.

sanskrit: nirdaśaṃ jñātimaraṇaṃ śrutvā putrasya janma ca / savāsā jalam āplutya śuddho bhavati mānavaḥ //
english: A man who hears of a (Sapinda) relative's death, or of the birth of a son after the ten days (of impurity have passed), becomes pure by bathing, dressed in his garments.

sanskrit: bāle deśāntarasthe ca pṛthakpiṇḍe ca saṃsthite / savāsā jalam āplutya sadya eva viśudhyati //
english: If an infant (that has not teethed), or a (grownup relative who is) not a Sapinda, die in a distant country, one becomes at once pure after bathing in one's clothes.

sanskrit: antardaśāhe syātāṃ cet punar maraṇajanmanī / tāvat syād aśucir vipro yāvat tat syād anirdaśam //
english: If within the ten days (of impurity) another birth or death happens, a Brahmana shall remain impure only until the (first) period of ten days has expired.

sanskrit: trirātram āhur āśaucam ācārye saṃsthite sati / tasya putre ca patnyāṃ ca divārātram iti sthitiḥ // śrotriye tūpasaṃpanne trirātram aśucir bhavet / mātule pakṣiṇīṃ rātriṃ śiṣyartvigbāndhaveṣu ca //
english: They declare that, when the teacher (akarya) has died, the impurity (lasts) three days; if the (teacher's) son or wife (is dead, it lasts) a day and a night; that is a settled (rule). For a Srotriya who resides with (him out of affection), a man shall be impure for three days; for a maternal uncle, a pupil, an officiating priest, or a maternal relative, for one night together with the preceding and following days.

sanskrit: prete rājani sajyotir yasya syād viṣaye sthitaḥ / aśrotriye tv ahaḥ kṛtsnam anūcāne tathā gurau //
english: If the king in whose realm he resides is dead, (he shall be impure) as long as the light (of the sun or stars shines), but for (an intimate friend) who is not a Srotriya (the impurity lasts) for a whole day, likewise for a Guru who knows the Veda and the Angas.

sanskrit: śuddhyed vipro daśāhena dvādaśāhena bhūmipaḥ / vaiśyaḥ pañcadaśāhena śūdro māsena śudhyati //
english: A Brahmana shall be pure after ten days, a Kshatriya after twelve, a Vaisya after fifteen, and a Sudra is purified after a month.

sanskrit: na vardhayed aghāhāni pratyūhen nāgniṣu kriyāḥ / na ca tatkarma kurvāṇaḥ sanābhyo 'py aśucir bhavet //
english: Let him not (unnecessarily) lengthen the period of impurity, nor interrupt the rites to be performed with the sacred fires; for he who performs that (Agnihotra) rite will not be impure, though (he be) a (Sapinda) relative.

sanskrit: divākīrtim udakyāṃ ca patitaṃ sūtikāṃ tathā / śavaṃ tatspṛṣṭinaṃ caiva spṛṣṭvā snānena śudhyati //
english: When he has touched a Kandala, a menstruating woman, an outcast, a woman in childbed, a corpse, or one who has touched a (corpse), he becomes pure by bathing.

sanskrit: ācamya prayato nityaṃ japed aśucidarśane / saurān mantrān yathotsāhaṃ pāvamānīś ca śaktitaḥ //
english: He who has purified himself by sipping water shall, on seeing any impure (thing or person), always mutter the sacred texts, addressed to Surya, and the Pavamani (verses).

sanskrit: nāraṃ spṛṣṭvāsthi sasnehaṃ snātvā vipro viśudhyati / ācamyaiva tu niḥsnehaṃ gām ālabhyārkam īkṣya vā //
english: A Brahmana who has touched a human bone to which fat adheres, becomes pure by bathing; if it be free from fat, by sipping water and by touching (afterwards) a cow or looking at the sun.

sanskrit: ādiṣṭī nodakaṃ kuryād ā vratasya samāpanāt / samāpte tūdakaṃ kṛtvā trirātreṇaiva śudhyati //
english: He who has undertaken the performance of a vow shall not pour out libations (to the dead) until the vow has been completed; but when he has offered water after its completion, he becomes pure in three days only.

sanskrit: vṛthāsaṃkarajātānāṃ pravrajyāsu ca tiṣṭhatām / ātmanas tyāgināṃ caiva nivartetodakakriyā // pāṣaṇḍam āśritānāṃ ca carantīnāṃ ca kāmataḥ / garbhabhartṛdruhāṃ caiva surāpīnāṃ ca yoṣitām //
english: Libations of water shall not be offered to those who (neglect the prescribed rites and may be said to) have been born in vain, to those born in consequence of an illegal mixture of the castes, to those who are ascetics (of heretical sects), and to those who have committed suicide, To women who have joined a heretical sect, who through lust live (with many men), who have caused an abortion, have killed their husbands, or drink spirituous liquor.

sanskrit: ācāryaṃ svam upādhyāyaṃ pitaraṃ mātaraṃ gurum / nirhṛtya tu vratī pretān na vratena viyujyate //
english: A student does not break his vow by carrying out (to the place of cremation) his own dead teacher (akarya), sub-teacher (upadhyaya), father, mother, or Guru.

sanskrit: dakṣiṇena mṛtaṃ śūdraṃ puradvāreṇa nirharet / paścimottarapūrvais tu yathāyogaṃ dvijanmanaḥ //
english: Let him carry out a dead Sudra by the southern gate of the town, but (the corpses of) twice-born men, as is proper, by the western, northern, or eastern (gates).

sanskrit: na rājñām aghadoṣo 'sti vratināṃ na ca sattriṇām / aindraṃ sthānam upāsīnā brahmabhūtā hi te sadā //
english: The taint of impurity does not fall on kings, and those engaged in the performance of a vow, or of a Sattra; for the (first are) seated on the throne of Indra, and the (last two are) ever pure like Brahman.

sanskrit: rājño mahātmike sthāne sadyaḥśaucaṃ vidhīyate / prajānāṃ parirakṣārtham āsanaṃ cātra kāraṇam //
english: For a king, on the throne of magnanimity, immediate purification is prescribed, and the reason for that is that he is seated (there) for the protection of (his) subjects.

sanskrit: ḍimbhāhavahatānāṃ ca vidyutā pārthivena ca / gobrāhmaṇasya caivārthe yasya cecchati pārthivaḥ //
english: (The same rule applies to the kinsmen) of those who have fallen in a riot or a battle, (of those who have been killed) by lightning or by the king, and (of those who perished fighting) for cows and Brahmanas, and to those whom the king wishes (to be pure).

sanskrit: somāgnyarkānilendrāṇāṃ vittāppatyor yamasya ca / aṣṭānāṃ lokapālānāṃ vapur dhārayate nṛpaḥ //
english: A king is an incarnation of the eight guardian deities of the world, the Moon, the Fire, the Sun, the Wind, Indra, the Lords of wealth and water (Kubera and Varuna), and Yama.

sanskrit: lokeśādhiṣṭhito rājā nāsyāśaucaṃ vidhīyate / śaucāśaucaṃ hi martyānāṃ lokebhyaḥ prabhavāpyayau //
english: Because the king is pervaded by those lords of the world, no impurity is ordained for him; for purity and impurity of mortals is caused and removed by (those) lords of the world.

sanskrit: udyatair āhave śastraiḥ kṣatradharmahatasya ca / sadyaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate yajñas tathāśaucam iti sthitiḥ //
english: By him who is slain in battle with brandished weapons according to the law of the Kshatriyas, a (Srauta) sacrifice is instantly completed, and so is the period of impurity (caused by his death); that is a settled rule.

sanskrit: vipraḥ śudhyaty apaḥ spṛṣṭvā kṣatriyo vāhanāyudham / vaiśyaḥ pratodaṃ raśmīn vā yaṣṭiṃ śūdraḥ kṛtakriyaḥ //
english: (At the end of the period of impurity) a Brahmana who has performed the necessary rites, becomes pure by touching water, a Kshatriya by touching the animal on which he rides, and his weapons, a Vaisya by touching his goad or the nose-string (of his oxen), a Sudra by touching his staff.

sanskrit: etad vo 'bhihitaṃ śaucaṃ sapiṇḍeṣu dvijottamāḥ / asapiṇḍeṣu sarveṣu pretaśuddhiṃ nibodhata //
english: Thus the purification (required) on (the death of) Sapindas has been explained to you, O best of twice-born men; hear now the manner in which men are purified on the death of any (relative who is) not a Sapinda.

sanskrit: asapiṇḍaṃ dvijaṃ pretaṃ vipro nirhṛtya bandhuvat / viśudhyati trirātreṇa mātur āptāṃś ca bāndhavān //
english: A Brahmana, having carried out a dead Brahmana who is not a Sapinda, as (if he were) a (near) relative, or a near relative of his mother, becomes pure after three days;

sanskrit: yady annam atti teṣāṃ tu daśāhenaiva śudhyati / anadann annam ahnaiva na cet tasmin gṛhe vaset //
english: But if he eats the food of the (Sapindas of the deceased), he is purified in ten days, (but) in one day, if he does not eat their food nor dwells in their house.

sanskrit: anugamyecchayā pretaṃ jñātim ajñātim eva ca / snātvā sacailaḥ spṛṣṭvāgniṃ ghṛtaṃ prāśya viśudhyati //
english: Having voluntarily followed a corpse, whether (that of) a paternal kinsman or (of) a stranger, he becomes pure by bathing, dressed in his clothes, by touching fire and eating clarified butter.

sanskrit: na vipraṃ sveṣu tiṣṭhatsu mṛtaṃ śūdreṇa nāyayet / asvargyā hy āhutiḥ sā syāc chūdrasaṃsparśadūṣitā //
english: Let him not allow a dead Brahmana to be carried out by a Sudra, while men of the same caste are at hand; for that burnt-offering which is defiled by a Sudra's touch is detrimental to (the deceased's passage to) heaven.

sanskrit: jñānaṃ tapo 'gnir āhāro mṛn mano vāry upāñjanam / vāyuḥ karmārkakālau ca śuddheḥ kartṝṇi dehinām //
english: The knowledge (of Brahman) austerities, fire, (holy) food, earth, (restraint of) the internal organ, water, smearing (with cowdung), the wind, sacred rites, the sun, and time are the purifiers of corporeal (beings).

sanskrit: sarveṣām eva śaucānām arthaśaucaṃ paraṃ smṛtaṃ / yo 'rthe śucir hi sa śucir na mṛdvāriśuciḥ śuciḥ //
english: Among all modes of purification, purity in (the acquisition of) wealth is declared to be the best; for he is pure who gains wealth with clean hands, not he who purifies himself with earth and water.

sanskrit: kṣāntyā śudhyanti vidvāṃso dānenākāryakāriṇaḥ / pracchannapāpā japyena tapasā vedavittamāḥ //
english: The learned are purified by a forgiving disposition, those who have committed forbidden actions by liberality, secret sinners by muttering (sacred texts), and those who best know the Veda by austerities.

sanskrit: mṛttoyaiḥ śudhyate śodhyaṃ nadī vegena śudhyati / rajasā strī manoduṣṭā saṃnyāsena dvijottamāḥ //
english: By earth and water is purified what ought to be made pure, a river by its current, a woman whose thoughts have been impure by the menstrual secretion, a Brahmana by abandoning the world (samnyasa).

sanskrit: adbhir gātrāṇi śudhyanti manaḥ satyena śudhyati / vidyātapobhyāṃ bhūtātmā buddhir jñānena śudhyati //
english: The body is cleansed by water, the internal organ is purified by truthfulness, the individual soul by sacred learning and austerities, the intellect by (true) knowledge.

sanskrit: eṣa śaucasya vaḥ proktaḥ śarīrasya vinirṇayaḥ / nānāvidhānāṃ dravyāṇāṃ śuddheḥ śṛṇuta nirṇayam //
english: Thus the precise rules for the purification of the body have been declared to you; hear now the decision (of the law) regarding the purification of the various (inanimate) things.

sanskrit: taijasānāṃ maṇīnāṃ ca sarvasyāśmamayasya ca / bhasmanādbhir mṛdā caiva śuddhir uktā manīṣibhiḥ //
english: The wise ordain that all (objects) made of metal, gems, and anything made of stone are to be cleansed with ashes, earth, and water.

sanskrit: nirlepaṃ kāñcanaṃ bhāṇḍam adbhir eva viśudhyati / abjam aśmamayaṃ caiva rājataṃ cānupaskṛtam //
english: A golden vessel which shows no stains, becomes pure with water alone, likewise what is produced in water (as shells and coral), what is made of stone, and a silver (vessel) not enchased.

sanskrit: apām agneś ca saṃyogād dhaimaṃ raupyaṃ ca nirbabhau / tasmāt tayoḥ svayonyaiva nirṇeko guṇavattaraḥ //
english: From the union of water and fire arose the glittering gold and silver; those two, therefore, are best purified by (the elements) from which they sprang.

sanskrit: tāmrāyaḥkāṃsyaraityānāṃ trapuṇaḥ sīsakasya ca / śaucaṃ yathārhaṃ kartavyaṃ kṣārāmlodakavāribhiḥ // dravāṇāṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ śuddhir utpavanaṃ smṛtam / prokṣaṇaṃ saṃhatānāṃ ca dāravāṇāṃ ca takṣaṇam //
english: Copper, iron, brass, pewter, tin, and lead must be cleansed, as may be suitable (for each particular case), by alkaline (substances), acids or water. The purification prescribed for all (sorts of) liquids is by passing two blades of Kusa grass through them, for solid things by sprinkling (them with water), for (objects) made of wood by planing them.

sanskrit: mārjanaṃ yajñapātrāṇāṃ pāṇinā yajñakarmaṇi / camasānāṃ grahāṇāṃ ca śuddhiḥ prakṣālanena tu //
english: At sacrifices the purification of (the Soma cups called) Kamasas and Grahas, and of (other) sacrificial vessels (takes place) by rubbing (them) with the hand, and (afterwards) rinsing (them with water).

sanskrit: carūṇāṃ sruksruvāṇāṃ ca śuddhir uṣṇena vāriṇā / sphyaśūrpaśakaṭānāṃ ca musalolūkhalasya ca //
english: The Karu and (the spoons called) Sruk and Sruva must be cleaned with hot water, likewise (the wooden sword, called) Sphya, the winnowing-basket (Surpa), the cart (for bringing the grain), the pestle and the mortar.

sanskrit: adbhis tu prokṣaṇaṃ śaucaṃ bahūnāṃ dhānyavāsasām / prakṣālanena tv alpānām adbhiḥ śaucaṃ vidhīyate //
english: The manner of purifying large quantities of grain and of cloth is to sprinkle them with water; but the purification of small quantities is prescribed (to take place) by washing them.

sanskrit: cailavac carmaṇāṃ śuddhir vaidalānāṃ tathaiva ca / śākamūlaphalānāṃ ca dhānyavac chuddhir iṣyate // kauśeyāvikayor ūṣaiḥ kutapānām ariṣṭakaiḥ / śrīphalair aṃśupaṭṭānāṃ kṣaumāṇāṃ gaurasarṣapaiḥ //
english: Skins and (objects) made of split cane must be cleaned like clothes; vegetables, roots, and fruit like grain; Silk and woollen stuffs with alkaline earth; blankets with pounded Arishta (fruit); Amsupattas with Bel fruit; linen cloth with (a paste of) yellow mustard.

sanskrit: kṣaumavac chaṅkhaśṛṅgāṇām asthidantamayasya ca / śuddhir vijānatā kāryā gomūtreṇodakena vā // prokṣaṇāt tṛṇakāṣṭhaṃ ca palālaṃ caiva śudhyati / mārjanopāñjanair veśma punaḥpākena mṛnmayam //
english: A man who knows (the law) must purify conch-shells, horn, bone and ivory, like linen cloth, or with a mixture of cow's urine and water. Grass, wood, and straw become pure by being sprinkled (with water), a house by sweeping and smearing (it with cowdung or whitewash), an earthen (vessel) by a second burning.

sanskrit: madyair mūtraiḥ purīṣair vā ṣṭhīvanaih pūyaśoṇitaiḥ / saṃspṛṣṭaṃ naiva śuddhyeta punaḥpākena mṛnmayam //
english: An earthen vessel which has been defiled by spirituous liquor, urine, ordure, saliva, pus or blood cannot be purified by another burning.

sanskrit: saṃmārjanopāñjanena sekenollekhanena ca / gavāṃ ca parivāsena bhūmiḥ śudhyati pañcabhiḥ //
english: Land is purified by (the following) five (modes, viz.) by sweeping, by smearing (it with cowdung), by sprinkling (it with cows' urine or milk), by scraping, and by cows staying (on it during a day and night).

sanskrit: pakṣijagdhaṃ gavā ghrātam avadhūtam avakṣutam / dūṣitaṃ keśakīṭaiś ca mṛtprakṣepeṇa śudhyati //
english: (Food) which has been pecked at by birds, smelt at by cows, touched (with the foot), sneezed on, or defiled by hair or insects, becomes pure by scattering earth (over it).

sanskrit: yāvan nāpaity amedhyāktād gandho lepaś ca tatkṛtaḥ / tāvan mṛdvāri cādeyaṃ sarvāsu dravyaśuddhiṣu //
english: As long as the (foul) smell does not leave an (object) defiled by impure substances, and the stain caused by them (does not disappear), so long must earth and water be applied in cleansing (inanimate) things.

sanskrit: trīṇi devāḥ pavitrāṇi brāhmaṇānām akalpayan / adṛṣṭam adbhir nirṇiktaṃ yac ca vācā praśasyate //
english: The gods declared three things (to be) pure to Brahmanas, that (on which) no (taint is) visible, what has been washed with water, and what has been commended (as pure) by the word (of a Brahmana).

sanskrit: āpaḥ śuddhā bhūmigatā vaitṛṣṇyaṃ yāsu gor bhavet / avyāptāś ced amedhyena gandhavarṇarasānvitāḥ //
english: Water, sufficient (in quantity) in order to slake the thirst of a cow, possessing the (proper) smell, colour, and taste, and unmixed with impure substances, is pure, if it is collected on (pure) ground.

sanskrit: nityaṃ śuddhaḥ kāruhastaḥ paṇye yac ca prasāritam / brahmacārigataṃ bhaikṣyaṃ nityaṃ medhyam iti sthitiḥ //
english: The hand of an artisan is always pure, so is (every vendible commodity) exposed for sale in the market, and food obtained by begging which a student holds (in his hand) is always fit for use; that is a settled rule.

sanskrit: nityam āsyaṃ śuci strīṇāṃ śakuniḥ phalapātane / prasrave ca śucir vatsaḥ śvā mṛgagrahaṇe śuciḥ //
english: The mouth of a woman is always pure, likewise a bird when he causes a fruit to fall; a calf is pure on the flowing of the milk, and a dog when he catches a deer.

sanskrit: śvabhir hatasya yan māṃsaṃ śuci tan manur abravīt / kravyādbhiś ca hatasyānyaiś caṇḍālādyaiś ca dasyubhiḥ //
english: Manu has declared that the flesh (of an animal) killed by dogs is pure, likewise (that) of a (beast) slain by carnivorous (animals) or by men of low caste (Dasyu), such as Kandalas.

sanskrit: ūrdhvaṃ nābher yāni khāni tāni medhyāni sarvaśaḥ / yāny adhas tāny amedhyāni dehāc caiva malāś cyutāḥ //
english: All those cavities (of the body) which lie above the navel are pure, (but) those which are below the navel are impure, as well as excretions that fall from the body.

sanskrit: makṣikā vipruṣaś chāyā gaur aśvaḥ sūryaraśmayaḥ / rajo bhūr vāyur agniś ca sparśe medhyāni nirdiśet //
english: Flies, drops of water, a shadow, a cow, a horse, the rays of the sun, dust, earth, the wind, and fire one must know to be pure to the touch.

sanskrit: viṇmūtrotsargaśuddhyarthaṃ mṛdvāry ādeyam arthavat / daihikānāṃ malānāṃ ca śuddhiṣu dvādaśasv api //
english: In order to cleanse (the organs) by which urine and faeces are ejected, earth and water must be used, as they may be required, likewise in removing the (remaining ones among) twelve impurities of the body.

sanskrit: vasā śukram asṛṅ majjā mūtraviṭ ghrāṇakarṇaviṭ / śleśma aśru dūṣikā svedo dvādaśaite nṛṇāṃ malāḥ //
english: Oily exudations, semen, blood, (the fatty substance of the) brain, urine, faeces, the mucus of the nose, ear-wax, phlegm, tears, the rheum of the eyes, and sweat are the twelve impurities of human (bodies).

sanskrit: ekā liṅge gude tisras tathaikatra kare daśa / ubhayoḥ sapta dātavyā mṛdaḥ śuddhim abhīpsatā //
english: He who desires to be pure, must clean the organ by one (application of) earth, the anus by (applying earth) three (times), the (left) hand alone by (applying it) ten (times), and both (hands) by (applying it) seven (times).

sanskrit: etac chaucaṃ gṛhasthānāṃ dviguṇaṃ brahmacāriṇām / triguṇaṃ syād vanasthānāṃ yatīnāṃ tu caturguṇam //
english: Such is the purification ordained for householders; (it shall be) double for students, treble for hermits, but quadruple for ascetics.

sanskrit: kṛtvā mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā khāny ācānta upaspṛśet / vedam adhyeṣyamāṇaś ca annam aśnaṃś ca sarvadā //
english: When he has voided urine or faeces, let him, after sipping water, sprinkle the cavities, likewise when he is going to recite the Veda, and always before he takes food.

sanskrit: trir ācāmed apaḥ pūrvaṃ dviḥ pramṛjyāt tato mukham / śarīraṃ śaucam icchan hi strī śūdras tu sakṛt sakṛt //
english: Let him who desires bodily purity first sip water three times, and then twice wipe his mouth; but a woman and a Sudra (shall perform each act) once (only).

sanskrit: śūdrāṇāṃ māsikaṃ kāryaṃ vapanaṃ nyāyavartinām / vaiśyavac chaucakalpaś ca dvijocchiṣṭaṃ ca bhojanam //
english: Sudras who live according to the law, shall each month shave (their heads); their mode of purification (shall be) the same as that of Vaisyas, and their food the fragments of an Aryan's meal.

sanskrit: nocchiṣṭaṃ kurvate mukhyā vipruṣo 'ṅgaṃ na yānti yāḥ / na śmaśrūṇi gatāny āsyaṃ na dantāntaradhiṣṭhitam //
english: Drops (of water) from the mouth which do not fall on a limb, do not make (a man) impure, nor the hair of the moustache entering the mouth, nor what adheres to the teeth.

sanskrit: spṛśanti bindavaḥ pādau ya ācāmayataḥ parān / bhaumikais te samā jñeyā na tair āprayato bhavet //
english: Drops which trickle on the feet of him who offers water for sipping to others, must be considered as equal to (water collected on the ground; they render him not impure.

sanskrit: ucchiṣṭena tu saṃspṛṣṭo dravyahastaḥ kathaṃ cana / anidhāyaiva tad dravyam ācāntaḥ śucitām iyāt //
english: He who, while carrying anything in any manner, is touched by an impure (person or thing), shall become pure, if he performs an ablution, without putting down that object.

sanskrit: vānto viriktaḥ snātvā tu ghṛtaprāśanam ācaret / ācāmed eva bhuktvānnaṃ snānaṃ maithuninaḥ smṛtam // suptvā kṣutvā ca bhuktvā ca niṣṭhīvyoktvānṛtāni ca / pītvāpo 'dhyeṣyamāṇaś ca ācāmet prayato 'pi san //
english: He who has vomited or purged shall bathe, and afterwards eat clarified butter; but if (the attack comes on) after he has eaten, let him only sip water; bathing is prescribed for him who has had intercourse with a woman. Though he may be (already) pure, let him sip water after sleeping, sneezing, eating, spitting, telling untruths, and drinking water, likewise when he is going to study the Veda.

sanskrit: eṣāṃ śaucavidhiḥ kṛtsno dravyaśuddhis tathaiva ca / ukto vaḥ sarvavarṇānāṃ strīṇāṃ dharmān nibodhata //
english: Thus the rules of personal purification for men of all castes, and those for cleaning (inanimate) things, have been fully declared to you: hear now the duties of women.

sanskrit: bālayā vā yuvatyā vā vṛddhayā vāpi yoṣitā / na svātantryeṇa kartavyaṃ kiṃ cid kāryaṃ gṛheṣv api //
english: By a girl, by a young woman, or even by an aged one, nothing must be done independently, even in her own house.

sanskrit: bālye pitur vaśe tiṣṭhet pāṇigrāhasya yauvane / putrāṇāṃ bhartari prete na bhajet strī svatantratām // pitrā bhartrā sutair vāpi necched viraham ātmanaḥ / eṣāṃ hi viraheṇa strī garhye kuryād ubhe kule //
english: In childhood a female must be subject to her father, in youth to her husband, when her lord is dead to her sons; a woman must never be independent. She must not seek to separate herself from her father, husband, or sons; by leaving them she would make both (her own and her husband's) families contemptible.

sanskrit: sadā prahṛṣṭayā bhāvyaṃ gṛhakārye ca dakṣayā / susaṃskṛtopaskarayā vyaye cāmuktahastayā //
english: She must always be cheerful, clever in (the management of her) household affairs, careful in cleaning her utensils, and economical in expenditure.

sanskrit: yasmai dadyāt pitā tv enāṃ bhrātā vānumate pituḥ / taṃ śuśrūṣeta jīvantaṃ saṃsthitaṃ ca na laṅghayet //
english: Him to whom her father may give her, or her brother with the father's permission, she shall obey as long as he lives, and when he is dead, she must not insult (his memory).

sanskrit: maṅgalārthaṃ svastyayanaṃ yajñaś cāsāṃ prajāpateḥ / prayujyate vivāhe tu pradānaṃ svāmyakāraṇam //
english: For the sake of procuring good fortune to (brides), the recitation of benedictory texts (svastyayana), and the sacrifice to the Lord of creatures (Pragapati) are used at weddings; (but) the betrothal (by the father or guardian) is the cause of (the husband's) dominion (over his wife).

sanskrit: anṛtāv ṛtukāle ca mantrasaṃskārakṛt patiḥ / sukhasya nityaṃ dāteha paraloke ca yoṣitaḥ //
english: The husband who wedded her with sacred texts, always gives happiness to his wife, both in season and out of season, in this world and in the next.

sanskrit: viśīlaḥ kāmavṛtto vā guṇair vā parivarjitaḥ / upacāryaḥ striyā sādhvyā satataṃ devavat patiḥ //
english: Though destitute of virtue, or seeking pleasure (elsewhere), or devoid of good qualities, (yet) a husband must be constantly worshipped as a god by a faithful wife.

sanskrit: nāsti strīṇāṃ pṛthag yajño na vrataṃ nāpy upoṣaṇam / patiṃ śuśrūṣate yena tena svarge mahīyate //
english: No sacrifice, no vow, no fast must be performed by women apart (from their husbands); if a wife obeys her husband, she will for that (reason alone) be exalted in heaven.

sanskrit: pāṇigrāhasya sādhvī strī jīvato vā mṛtasya vā / patilokam abhīpsantī nācaret kiṃ cid apriyam //
english: A faithful wife, who desires to dwell (after death) with her husband, must never do anything that might displease him who took her hand, whether he be alive or dead.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ tu ksapayed dehaṃ puṣpamūlaphalaiḥ śubhaiḥ / na tu nāmāpi gṛhṇīyāt patyau prete parasya tu //
english: At her pleasure let her emaciate her body by (living on) pure flowers, roots, and fruit; but she must never even mention the name of another man after her husband has died.

sanskrit: āsītā maraṇāt ksāntā niyatā brahmacāriṇī / yo dharma ekapatnīnāṃ kāṅkṣantī tam anuttamam //
english: Until death let her be patient (of hardships), self-controlled, and chaste, and strive (to fulfil) that most excellent duty which (is prescribed) for wives who have one husband only.

sanskrit: anekāni sahasrāṇi kumārabrahmacāriṇām / divaṃ gatāni viprāṇām akṛtvā kulasaṃtatim //
english: Many thousands of Brahmanas who were chaste from their youth, have gone to heaven without continuing their race.

sanskrit: mṛte bhartari sāḍhvī strī brahmacarye vyavasthitā / svargaṃ gacchaty aputrāpi yathā te brahmacāriṇaḥ // apatyalobhād yā tu strī bhartāram ativartate / seha nindām avāpnoti paralokāc ca hīyate //
english: A virtuous wife who after the death of her husband constantly remains chaste, reaches heaven, though she have no son, just like those chaste men. But a woman who from a desire to have offspring violates her duty towards her (deceased) husband, brings on herself disgrace in this world, and loses her place with her husband (in heaven).

sanskrit: nānyotpannā prajāstīha na cāpy anyaparigrahe / na dvitīyaś ca sādhvīnāṃ kva cid bhartopadiśyate //
english: Offspring begotten by another man is here not (considered lawful), nor (does offspring begotten) on another man's wife (belong to the begetter), nor is a second husband anywhere prescribed for virtuous women.

sanskrit: patiṃ hitvāpakṛṣṭaṃ svam utkṛṣṭaṃ yā niṣevate / nindyaiva sā bhavel loke parapūrveti cocyate //
english: She who cohabits with a man of higher caste, forsaking her own husband who belongs to a lower one, will become contemptible in this world, and is called a remarried woman (parapurva).

sanskrit: vyabhicārāt tu bhartuḥ strī loke prāpnoti nindyatām / śṛgālayoniṃ prāpnoti pāparogaiś ca pīḍyate //
english: By violating her duty towards her husband, a wife is disgraced in this world, (after death) she enters the womb of a jackal, and is tormented by diseases (the punishment of) her sin.

sanskrit: uddāmakallolaravā dehādrau vahatīha me / taraṅgataralākārā tarattṛṣṇātaraṅgiṇī //
english: The stream of worldly avarice flows like a rapid current within the rock of my body, with precipitate force (in my actions), and loud resounding waves.

sanskrit: vegaṃ saroddhumudito vātyayeva jarattṛṇam / nītaḥ kaluṣayā kvāpi tṛṣṇayā cittacātakaḥ //
english: Our minds are driven by foul avarice from one place to another, as the dusty dry hays are borne away by the winds, and as the Chatakas are impelled by thirst to fly about.

sanskrit: yāṃ yāmahamatīvāsthāṃ saṃśrayāmi guṇaśriyām / tāṃ tāṃ kṛntati me tṛṣṇā tantrīmiva kumūṣikā //
english: It is avarice which destroys all the good qualities and grace which we adopted to ourselves in good faith, just as the mischievous mouse severs the wires.

sanskrit: payasīva jaratparṇaṃ vāyāviva jarattṛṇam / nabhasīva śaranmeghaścintācakre bhramāmyaham //
english: We turn about upon the wheel of our cares, like withered leaves (floating) upon the water, and like dry grass uplifted by the wind, and as autumnal clouds (moving) in the sky.

sanskrit: gantumāspadamātmīyamasamarthadhiyo vayam / cintājāle vimuhyāmo jāle śakunayo yathā //
english: Being over powered by avarice, we are disable to reach the goal (of perfection), as a bird entangled in the snare, is kept from its flight.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇābhidhānayā tāta dagdho'smi jvālayā tathā / yathā dāhopaśamanamāśaṃke nāmṛtairapi //
english: I am so greatly burnt by the flame of avarice, that I doubt whether this inflammation may be assuaged even by administration of nectar itself.

sanskrit: dūraṃ dūramito gatvā sametya ca punaḥpunaḥ / bhramatyāśu diganteṣu tṛṣṇonmattā turaṅgamī //
english: Avarice like a heated-mare takes me far and farther still from my place, and brings me back to it again and again. Thus it hurries me up and down and to and fro in all directions for ever.

sanskrit: jaḍasaṃsargiṇī tṛṣṇā kṛtordhvādhogamāgamā / kṣubdhā granthimatī nityamāraghaṭṭāgrarajjuvat //
english: We are pulled up and cast down again like a bucket in the well, by the string of avarice.

sanskrit: antargrathitayā dehe sarvaduśchedayā'nayā / rajjvevāśu balīvardastṛṣṇayā vāhyate janaḥ //
english: Man is led about like a bullock of burthen by his avarice, which bends his heart as fast as the string does the beast, and which it is hard for him to break.

sanskrit: putramitrakalatrāditṛṣṇayā nityakṛṣṭayā / khageṣviva kirātyedaṃ jālaṃ lokeṣu racyate //
english: As the huntress spreads her net to catch birds in it, so does our affection for our friends, wives and children stretch these snares to entrap us every day.

sanskrit: bhīṣayatyapi dhīraṃ māmandhayatyapi sekṣaṇam / khedayatyapi sānandaṃ tṛṣṇākṛṣṇeva śarvarī //
english: Avarice like a dark night terrifies even the wise, blindfolds the keen-sighted, and depresses the spirit of the happiest of men.

sanskrit: kuṭilā komalasparśā viṣavaiṣamyaśaṃsinī / daśatyapi manākspṛṣṭā tṛṣṇā kṛṣṇeva bhoginī //
english: Our appetite is as heinous as a serpent, soft to feel, but full of deadly poison, and bites us as soon as it is felt.

sanskrit: bhindatī hṛdayaṃ puṃsāṃ māyāmayavidhāyinī / daurbhāgyadāyinī dīnā tṛṣṇā kṛṣṇeva rākṣasī //
english: It is also like a black sorceress that deludes men by her magic, but pierces him in his heart, and exposes him to danger afterwards.

sanskrit: tandrītantrīgaṇaiḥ kośaṃ dadhānā pariveṣṭitam / nānande rājate brahmaṃstṛṣṇā jarjaravallakī //
english: This body of ours shattered by our avarice is like a worn out lute, fastened by arteries resembling the wires, but emitting no pleasing sound.

sanskrit: nityamevātimalinā kaṭukonmādadāyinī / dīrghatantrī ghanasnehā tṛṣṇā gahvaravallarī //
english: Our avarice is like the long fibered, dark and juicy poisonous creeper called Kaduka, that grows in the caverns of mountains, and maddens men by its flavour.

sanskrit: anānandakarī śūnyā niṣphalā vyarthamunnatā / amaṅgalakarī krūrā tṛṣṇā kṣīṇeva mañjarī //
english: Avarice is as vain and inane, fruitless and aspiring, unpleasant and perilous, as the dry twig of a tree, which (bears no fruit or flower) but is hurtful with its prickly point.

sanskrit: anāvarjitacittāpi sarvamevānudhāvati / na cāpnoti phalaṃ kiṃcittṛṣṇā jīrṇeva kāminī //
english: Venality is like a churlish old woman, who from the incontinence of her heart, courts the company of every man, without gaining the object of her desire.

sanskrit: saṃsāravṛnde mahati nānārasasamākule / bhuvanābhogaraṅgeṣu tṛṣṇā jaraṭhanartakī //
english: Greediness as an old actress plays her various parts in the vast theatre of world, in order to please the different tastes of her audience.

sanskrit: jarākusumitārūḍhā pātotpātaphalāvaliḥ / saṃsārajaṃgale dīrghe tṛṣṇā viṣalatā tatā //
english: Parsimony is as a poisonous plant growing in the wide wilderness of the world, bearing old age and infirmity as its flowers, and producing our troubles as its fruits.

sanskrit: yanna śakroti tatrāpi dhatte tāṇḍavitāṃ gatim / nṛtyatyānandarahitaṃ tṛṣṇā jīrṇeva nartakī //
english: Our churlishnesss resembles an aged actress, attempting a manly feat she has not the strength to perform, yet keeping up the dance without pleasing.

sanskrit: bhṛśaṃ sphurati nīhāre śāmyatyāloka āgate / durlaṅghayeṣu padaṃ dhatte cintā capalabarhiṇī //
english: Our fleeting thoughts are as fickle as pea-hens, soaring over inaccessible heights under the clouds (of ignorance); but ceasing to fly in the day light.

sanskrit: jaḍakallolabahulā ciraṃ śūnyāntarāntarā / kṣaṇamullāsamāyāti tṛṣṇā prāvṛṭtaraṅgiṇī //
english: Avarice is like a river in the rains, rising for a time with its rolling waves, and afterwards lying low in its empty bed.

sanskrit: naṣṭamutsṛjya tiṣṭhantaṃ tṛṣṇā vṛkṣamivāparam / puruṣātpuruṣaṃ yāti tṛṣṇā loleva pakṣiṇī //
english: Avarice is as inconstant as a female bird, which changes her mates at times, and quits the arbor that no longer bears any fruit.

sanskrit: padaṃ karotyalaṅghye'pi tṛptāpi phalamīhate / ciraṃ tiṣṭhati naikatra tṛṣṇā capalamarkaṭī //
english: The greedy are as unsteady as the flouncing monkey, which is never restive at any place, but moves to places impassable by others, and craving for fruits even when satiate.

sanskrit: idaṃ kṛtvedamāyāti sarvamevāsamañjasam / anārataṃ ca yatate tṛṣṇā ceṣṭeva daivikī //
english: The acts of avarice are as inconstant as those of chance, both of which are ever on the alert, but never attended with their sequence.

sanskrit: kṣaṇamāyāti pātālaṃ kṣaṇaṃ yāti nabhasthalam / kṣaṇaṃ bhramati dikkuñje tṛṣṇā hṛtpadmaṣaṭpadī //
english: Our venality is like a black-bee sitting upon the lotus of our hearts, and thence making its rambles above, below and all about us in a moment.

sanskrit: sarvasaṃsāradoṣāṇāṃ tṛṣṇaikā dīrghaduḥkhadā / antaḥpurasthamapi yā yojayatyatisaṃkaṭe //
english: Of all worldly evils, avarice is the source of the longest woe. She exposes to peril even the most secluded man.

sanskrit: prayacchati paraṃ jāḍyaṃ paramālokarodhinī / mohanīhāragahanā tṛṣṇā jaladamālikā //
english: Avarice like a group of clouds, is fraught with a thick mist of error, obstructing the light of heaven, and causing a dull insensibility.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ jantujātānāṃ saṃsāravyavahāriṇām / pariprotamanomālā tṛṣṇā bandhanarajjuvat //
english: Penury which seems to gird the breasts of worldly people with chains of gems and jewels, binds them as beasts with halters about the necks.

sanskrit: vicitravarṇā viguṇā dīrghā malinasaṃsthitiḥ / śūnyā śūnyapadā tṛṣṇā śakrakārmukadharmiṇī //
english: Covetousness stretches itself long and wide and presents to us a variety of hues as the rainbow. It is equally unsubstantial and without any property as the iris, resting in vapour and vacuum and being but a shadow itself.

sanskrit: aśanirguṇasasyānāṃ phalitā śaradāpadām / himaṃ saṃvitsarojānāṃ tamasāṃ dīrghayāminī //
english: It burns away our good qualities as electric fire does the hay; it numbs our good sense as the frost freezes the lotus; it grows our evils as autumn does the grass; and it increases our ignorance as the winter prolongs the night.

sanskrit: saṃsāranāṭakanaṭī kāryālayavihaṃgamī / mānasāraṇyahariṇī smarasaṃgītavallakī //
english: Greediness is as an actress in the stage of the world; she is as a bird flying out of the nest of our houses; as a deer running about in the desert of our hearts; and as a lute making us sing and dance at its tune.

sanskrit: vyavahārābdhilaharī mohamātaṅgaśrṛṅkhalā / sarganyagrodhasulatā duḥkhakairavacandrikā //
english: Our desires like billows toss us about in the ocean of our earthly cares; they bind us fast to delusion as fetters do the elephant. Like the ficus indicus they produce the roots of our regeneration, and like moon beams they put our budding woes to bloom.

sanskrit: jarāmaraṇaduḥkhānāmekā ratnasamudgikā / ādhivyādhivilāsānāṃ nityaṃ mattā vilāsinī //
english: Avarice like (Pandora's) box is filled with miseries, decrepitude and death, and is full of disorder and disasters like a mad bacchanal.

sanskrit: kṣaṇamālokavimalā sāndhakāralavā kṣaṇam / vyomavīthyupamā tṛṣṇā nīhāragahanā kṣaṇam //
english: Our wishes are sometimes as pure as light and at others as foul as darkness; now they are as clear as the milky way, and again as obscure as thickest mists.

sanskrit: gacchatyupaśamaṃ tṛṣṇā kāyavyāyāmaśāntaye / tamī ghanatamaḥkṛṣṇā yathā rakṣonivṛttaye //
english: All our bodily troubles are avoided by our abstaining from avarice, as we are freed from fear of night goblins at the dispersion of darkness.

sanskrit: tāvanmuhyatyayaṃ mūko loko vilulitāśayaḥ / yāvadevānusaṃdhatte tṛṣṇā viṣaviṣūcikā //
english: So long do men remain in their state of (dead like) dumbness and mental delirium, as they are subject to the poisonous cholic of avarice.

sanskrit: loko'yamakhilaṃ duḥkhaṃ cintayojjhitayojjhati / tṛṣṇāviṣūcikāmantraścintātyāgo hi kathyate //
english: Men may get rid of their misery by their being freed from anxieties. It is the abandonment of cares which is said to be the best remedy of avarice.

sanskrit: tṛṇapāṣāṇakāṣṭhādisarvamāmiṣaśaṅkayā / ādadānā sphuratyante tṛṣṇā matsyī hrade yathā //
english: As the fishes in a pond fondly grasp the bait in expectation of a sop, so do the avaricious lay hold on any thing, be it wood or stone or even a straw.

sanskrit: rogārtiraṅganātṛṣṇā gambhīramapi mānavam / uttānatāṃ nayantyāśu sūryāṃśava ivāmbujam //
english: Avarice like an acute pain excites even the gravest of men to motion, just as the rays of the sun raise the lotus blossoms.

sanskrit: antaḥśūnyā granthimatyo dīrghasvāṅkurakaṇṭakāḥ / muktāmaṇipriyā nityaṃ tṛṣṇā veṇulatā iva //
english: It is compared with the bamboo in its length, hollowness, hard knots, and thorny prickles, and yet it is entertained in expectation of its yielding the manna and a pearly substance.

sanskrit: aho bata mahaccitraṃ tṛṣṇāmapi mahādhiyaḥ / ducchedāmapi kṛntanti vivekenāmalāsinā //
english: Yet it is a wonder that high-minded men, have been able to cut off this almost unseverable knot of avarice, by the glittering sword of reason:

sanskrit: nāsidhārā na vajrārcirna taptāyaḥkaṇārciṣaḥ / tathā tīkṣṇā yathā brahmaṃstṛṣṇeyaṃ hṛdi saṃsthitā //
english: As neither the edge of the sword, nor the fire of lightning, nor the sparks of the red-hot iron, are sharp enough to sever the keen avarice seated in our hearts.

sanskrit: ujjvalā'sitatīkṣṇāgrā snehadīrghadaśā parā / prakāśā dāhaduḥsparśā tṛṣṇā dīpaśikhā iva //
english: It is like the flame of a lamp which is bright but blackening and acutely burning at its end. It is fed by the oily wicks (of years), is vivid in all, but never handled by any body.

sanskrit: api merusamaṃ prājñamapi śūramapi sthiram / tṛṇīkaroti tṛṣṇaikā nimeṣeṇa narottamam //
english: Penury has the power of bemeaning the best of men to (the baseness of) straws in a moment, notwithstanding their wisdom, heroism and gravity in other respects.

sanskrit: saṃstīrṇagahanā bhīmā ghanajālarajomayī / sāndhakārogranīhārā tṛṣṇā vindhyamahātaṭī //
english: Avarice is like the great valley of the Vindhya hills, that is beset with deserts and impenetrable forests, is terrible and full of snares laid by the hunters, and filled with the dust and mist.

sanskrit: ekaiva sarvabhuvanāntaralabdhalakṣyā durlakṣyatāmupagataiva vapuḥsthitaiva / tṛṣṇā sthitā jagati cañcalavīcimāle kṣīrodakāmbutarale madhureva śaktiḥ //
english: One single avarice has every thing in the world for its object, and though seated in the breast, it is imperceptible to all. It is as the undulating Milky ocean in this fluctuating world, sweeping all things yet regaling mankind with its odorous waves.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / ārdrāntratantrīgahano vikārī paripātavān / dehaḥ sphurati saṃsāre so'pi duḥkhāya kevalam //
english: This body of ours that struts about on earth, is but a mass of humid entrails and tendons, tending to decay and disease, and to our torment alone.

sanskrit: ajño'pi tajjñasadṛśo valitātmacamatkṛtiḥ / yuktyā bhavyo'pyabhavyo'pi na jaḍo nāpi cetanaḥ //
english: It is neither quiescent nor wholly sentient, neither ignorant nor quite intelligent. Its inherent soul is a wonder, and it is reason (and its absence) that makes it graceful or otherwise.

sanskrit: jaḍājaḍadṛśormadhye dolāyitadurāśayaḥ / avivekī vimūḍhātmā mohameva prayacchati //
english: The sceptic is doubtful of its inertness and intellection: and the unreasonable and ignorant people are ever subject to error and illusion.

sanskrit: stokenānandamāyāti stokenāyāti kheditām / nāsti dehasamaḥ śocyo nīco guṇabahiṣkṛtaḥ //
english: The body is as easily gratified with a little, as it is exhausted in an instant, hence there is nothing so pitiable, abject and worthless as our bodies.

sanskrit: āgamāpāyinā nityaṃ dantakesaraśālinā / vikāsasmitapuṣpeṇa pratikṣaṇamalaṃkṛtaḥ //
english: The face is as frail as a fading flower: now it shoots forth its teeth like filaments, and now it dresses itself with blooming and blushing smiles as blossoms.

sanskrit: bhujaśākho ghanaskandho dvijastambhaśubhasthitiḥ / locanālivilākrāntaḥ śiraḥpīṭhabṛhatphalaḥ //
english: The body is as a tree, having its arms resembling the branches, the shoulder-blades like stems, the teeth as rows of birds, the eye-holes like its hollows, and the head as a big fruit.

sanskrit: śravadantarasagrasto hastapādasupallavaḥ / gulmavānkāryasaṃghāto vihaṅgamakṛtāspadaḥ //
english: The ears are as two wood-peckers, the fingers of both hands and feet as so many leaves of the branches, the diseases as (parasite) plants, and the acts of the body are as axes felling this tree, which is the seat of the two birds the soul and intelligence.

sanskrit: sacchāyo dehavṛkṣo'yaṃ jīvapānthagaṇāspadaḥ / kasyātmīyaḥ kasya para āsthānāsthe kilātra ke //
english: This shady arbor of the body, is but the temporary resort of the passing soul, what then whether it be akin to or apart from anybody, or whether one would rely in it or not.

sanskrit: tāta saṃtaraṇārthena gṛhītāyāṃ punaḥpunaḥ / nāvi dehalatāyāṃ ca kasya syādātmabhāvanā //
english: What man is there, O venerable fathers! that would stoop to reflect within himself, that this body is repeatedly assumed only to serve him as a boat to pass over the sea of the world.

sanskrit: dehanāmni vane śūnye bahugartasamākule / tanūruhāsaṃkhyatarau viśvāsaṃ ko'dhigacchati //
english: Who can rely any confidence in his body, which is as a forest full of holes, and abounds in hairs resembling its trees?

sanskrit: māṃsasnāyvasthivalite śarīrapaṭahe'dṛḍhe / mārjāravadahaṃ tāta tiṣṭhāmyatra gatadhvanau //
english: The body composed of flesh, nerves and bones, resembles a drum without any musical sound, and yet I sit watching it as a cat.

sanskrit: saṃsārāraṇyasaṃrūḍho vilasaccittamarkaṭaḥ / cintāmañjaritākāro dīrghaduḥkhaghuṇakṣataḥ //
english: Our bodies are as trees growing in the forest of the world, bearing the flowers of anxiety, and perforated by the worms of woe and misery, and mounted upon by the apish mind.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇābhujaṅgamīgehaṃ kopa kāka kṛtālayaḥ / smitapuṇyodgamaḥ śrīmāñchubhāśubhamahāphalaḥ //
english: The body with its smiling face appears a goodly plant, bearing the fruits both of good and evil; but it has become the abode of the dragon of avarice, and a rookery of the ravens of anger.

sanskrit: suskandhoghalatājālo hastastabakasundaraḥ / pavanaspanditāśeṣasvāṅgāvayavapallavaḥ //
english: Our arms are as the boughs of trees, and our open palms like beautiful clusters of flowers, the other limbs are as twigs and leaves, and are continually shaken by the breath of life.

sanskrit: sarvendriyakhagādhāraḥ sujānustambha unnataḥ / sarasacchāyayā yuktaḥ kāmapānthaniṣevitaḥ //
english: The two legs are the erect stems (of the arbor of the body), and the organs are the seats of the birds of sense. Its youthful bloom is a shade for the passing traveller of love.

sanskrit: mūrdhasaṃjanitā''dīrghaśiroruhatṛṇāvaliḥ / ahaṃkāragṛdhrakṛtakulāyaḥ suṣirodaraḥ //
english: The hanging hairs of the head resemble the long grass growing on the tree (of the body); and egoism like a vulture (in hollow), cracks the ear with its hideous shrieks.

sanskrit: vicchinnavāsanājālamūlatvāddurlavākṛtiḥ / vyāyāmavirasaḥ kāyaplakṣo'yaṃ na sukhāya me //
english: Our various desires like the pendant roots and fibres of the fig tree, seem to support its trunk of the body, though it is worn out by labour to unpleasantness.

sanskrit: kalevaramahaṃkāragṛhasthasya mahāgṛham / luṭhatvabhyetu vā sthairyaṃ kimanena mune mama //
english: The body is the big abode of its owner's egoism, and therefore it is of no interest to me whether it lasts or falls.

sanskrit: paṅktibaddhendriyapaśuṃ valattṛṣṇāgṛhāṅganam / rāgarañjitasarvāṅgaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: This body which is linked with its limbs like beasts of burthen labour, and is the abode of its mistress Avarice—painted over by her taints of passions, affords me no delight whatever.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭhāsthikāṣṭhasaṃghaṭṭaparisaṃkaṭakoṭaram / āntrarajjubhirābaddhaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: This abode of the body which is built by the frame-work of the back-bone and ribs, and composed of cellular vessels, tied together by ropes of the entrails, is no way desirable to me.

sanskrit: prasṛtasnāyutantrīkaṃ raktāmbukṛtakardamam / jarāmaṅkoladhavalaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: This mansion of the body, which is tied with strings of the tendons, and built with the clay of blood and moisture, and plastered white with old age, is no way suited to my liking.

sanskrit: cittabhṛtyakṛtānantaceṣṭāvaṣṭabdhasaṃsthiti / mithyāmohamahāsthūṇaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: The mind is the architect and master of this bodily dwelling, and our activities are its supports and servants; it is filled with errors and delusions which I do not like.

sanskrit: duḥkhārbhakakṛtākrandaṃ sukhaśayyāmanoramam / durīhādagdhadāsīkaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: I do not like this dwelling of the body with its bed of pleasure on one side, and the cries of pain as those of its children on the other, and where our evil desires are at work like its bawling hand-maids.

sanskrit: malāḍhyaviṣayavyūhabhāṇḍopaskarasaṃkaṭam / ajñānakṣāravalitaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: I cannot like this body, which like a pot of filth, is full of the foulness of worldly affairs, and mouldering under the rust of our ignorance.

sanskrit: gulphagugguluviśrāntajānūrdhvastambhamastakam / dīghadordārusudṛḍhaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: It is a hovel standing on the two props of our heels, and supported by the two posts of our legs.

sanskrit: prakaṭākṣagavākṣāntaḥ krīḍatprajñāgṛhāṅganam / cintāduhitṛkaṃ brahmanneṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: It is no lovely house where the external organs are playing their parts, while its mistress the understanding sits inside with her brood of anxieties.

sanskrit: mūrdhajācchādanacchannakarṇaśrīcandraśālikam / ādīrghāṅgulinirvyūhaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: It is a hut which is thatched over with the hairs on the head, decorated with the turrets of the ears, and adorned with jewels on the crest, which I do not like.

sanskrit: sarvāṅgakuḍyasaṃghātaghanaromayavāṅkuram / saṃśūnyapeṭavivaraṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: This house of the body is walled about by all its members, and beset by hairs growing like ears of corn on it. It has an empty space of the belly within (which is never full), and which I do not like.

sanskrit: nakhorṇanābhinilayaṃ saramāraṇitāntaram / bhāṅkārakāripavanaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: This body with its nails as those of spiders, and its entrails growling within like barking dogs, and the internal winds emitting fearful sounds, is never delightsome to me.

sanskrit: praveśanirgamavyagravātavegamanāratam / vitatākṣagavākṣaṃ tanneṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: What is this body but a passage for the ceaseless inhaling and breathing out of the vital air? Its eyes are as two windows which are continually oped and closed by the eyelids. I do not like such a mansion as this.

sanskrit: jihvāmarkaṭikākrāntavadanadvārabhīṣaṇam / dṛṣṭadantāsthiśakalaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛha mama //
english: This mansion of the body with its formidable (wide-open) door of the mouth, and (ever-moving) bolt of the tongue and bars of the teeth, is not pleasant to me.

sanskrit: tvaksudhālepamasṛṇaṃ yantrasaṃcāracañcalam / manaḥ sadākhunotkhātaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: This house of the body, having the white-wash of ointments on the outer skin, and the machinery of the limbs in continued motion, and the restless mind burrowing its base like the mischievous mouse, is not liked by me.

sanskrit: smitadīpaprabhodbhāsi kṣaṇamānandasundaram / kṣaṇaṃ vyāptaṃ tamaḥpūrairneṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: Sweet smiles like shining lamps, serve to lighten this house of the body for a moment, but it is soon darkened by a cloud of melancholy, wherefore I cannot be pleased with it.

sanskrit: samastarogāyatanaṃ valīpalitapattanam / sarvādhisāragahanaṃ neṣṭaṃ dehagṛhaṃ mama //
english: This body which is the abode of diseases, and subject to wrinkles and decay, and all kinds of pain, is a mansion wherewith I am not pleased.

sanskrit: akṣarkṣakṣobhaviṣamā śūnyā niḥsārakoṭarā / tamogahanadikkuñjā neṣṭā dehāṭavī mama //
english: I do not like this wilderness of the body, which is infested by the bears of the senses. It is empty and hollow within, with dark groves (of entrails) in the inside.

sanskrit: dehālayaṃ dhārayituṃ na śaknomi munīśvara / paṅkamagnaṃ samuddhartuṃ gajamalpabalo yathā //
english: I am unable, O chief of sages! to drag my domicile of the body, just as a weak elephant is incapable to draw out another immerged in a muddy pit.

sanskrit: kiṃ śriyā kiṃ ca rājyena kiṃ kāyena kimīhitaiḥ / dinaiḥ katipayaireva kālaḥ sarvaṃ nikṛntati //
english: Of what good is affluence or royalty, this body and all its efforts to one, when the hand of time must destroy them all in a few days.

sanskrit: raktamāṃsamayasyāsya sabāhyābhyantaraṃ mune / nāśaikadharmiṇo brūhi kaiva kāyasya ramyatā //
english: Tell me, O sage! what is charming in this body, that is only a composition of flesh and blood both within and without it and frail in its nature.

sanskrit: maraṇāvasare kāyā jīvaṃ nānusaranti ye / teṣu tāta kṛtaghneṣu kaivāsthā vada dhīmatām //
english: The body does not follow the soul upon death; tell me Sir, what regard should the learned have for such an ungrateful thing as this.

sanskrit: mattebhakarṇāgracalaḥ kāyo lambāmbubhaṅguraḥ / na saṃtyajati māṃ yāvattāvadenaṃ tyajāmyaham //
english: It is as unsteady as the ears of an infuriate elephant, and as fickle as drops of water that trickle on their tips. I should like therefore to abandon it, before it comes to abandon me.

sanskrit: pavanaspandataralaḥ pelavaḥ kāyapallavaḥ / jarjarastanuvṛttaśca neṣṭo me kaṭunīrasaḥ //
english: It is as tremulous as the leaves of a tree shaken by the breeze, and oppressed by diseases and fluctuations of pleasure and pain. I have no relish in its pungency and bitterness.

sanskrit: bhuktvā pītvā ciraṃ kālaṃ bālapallavapelavām / tanutāmetya yatnena vināśamanudhāvati //
english: With all its food and drink for evermore, it is as tender as a leaflet and is reduced to leanness in spite of all our cares, and runs fast towards its dissolution.

sanskrit: tānyeva sukhaduḥkhāni bhāvābhāvamayānyasau / bhūyo'pyanubhavankāyaḥ prākṛto hi na lajjate //
english: It is repeatedly subjected to pleasure and pain, and to the succession of affluence and destitution, without being ashamed of itself as the shameless vulgar herd.

sanskrit: suciraṃ prabhutāṃ kṛtvā saṃsevya vibhavaśriyam / nocchrāyameti na sthairyaṃ kāyaḥ kimiti pālyate //
english: Why nourish this body any longer, when it acquires no excellence nor durability of its state, after its enjoyment of prosperity and exercise of authority for a length of time.

sanskrit: jarākāle jarāmeti mṛtyukāle tathā mṛtim / sama evāviśeṣajñaḥ kāyo bhogidaridrayoḥ //
english: The bodies of the rich as well as those of the poor, are alike subject to decay and death at their appointed times.

sanskrit: saṃsārāmbhodhijaṭhare tṛṣṇākuharakāntare / suptastiṣṭhati mukteho mūko'yaṃ kāyakacchapaḥ //
english: The body lies as a tortoise in the cave of avarice amidst the ocean of the world. It remains there in the mud in a mute and torpid state, without an effort for its liberation.

sanskrit: dahanaikārthayogyāni kāyakāṣṭhāni bhūriśaḥ / saṃsārābdhāvihohyante kaṃcitteṣu naraṃ viduḥ //
english: Our bodies floating as heaps of wood on the waves of the world, serve at last for the fuel of funeral fire (on the pile); except a few of these which pass for human bodies in the sight of the wise.

sanskrit: dīrghadaurātmyavalayā nipātaphalapātayā / na dehalatayā kāryaṃ kiṃcidasti vivekinaḥ //
english: The wise have little to do with this tree of the body, which is beset by evils like noxious orchids about it, and produces the fruit of perdition.

sanskrit: majjankardamakośeṣu jhaṭityeva jarāṃ gataḥ / na jñāyate yātyacirātkaḥ kathaṃ dehadarduraḥ //
english: The body like a frog, lies merged in the mire of mortality, where it perishes no sooner it is known to have lived and gone.

sanskrit: niḥsārasakalārambhāḥ kāyāścapalavāyavaḥ / rajomārgeṇa gacchanto dṛśyante neha kenacit //
english: Our bodies are as empty and fleeting as gusts of wind, passing over a dusty ground, where nobody knows whence they come, and whither they go.

sanskrit: vāyordīpasya manaso gacchato jñāyate gatiḥ / āgacchataśca bhagavañcharīrasya kadācana //
english: We know not the course of our bodies (their transmigrations), as we do not know those of the winds, light and our thoughts; they all come and go, but from where and whither, we know nothing of.

sanskrit: baddhāsthā ye śarīreṣu baddhāsthā ye jagatsthitau / tānmohamadironmattāndhigdhigastu punaḥpunaḥ //
english: Fie and shame to them, that are so giddy with the ebriety of their error, as to rely on any state or durability of their bodies.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ dehasya no deho mama nāyamahaṃ tathā / iti viśrāntacittā ye te mune puruṣottamāḥ //
english: They are the best of men, O sage! whose minds are at rest with the thought, that their ego does not subsist in their bodies, nor are the bodies theirs at the end.

sanskrit: mānāvamānabahulā bahulābhamanoramāḥ / śarīramātrabaddhāsthaṃ ghnanti doṣadṛśo naram //
english: Those mistaken men that have a high sense of honor and fear dishonor, and take a pleasure in the excess of their gains, are verily the killers both of their bodies and souls.

sanskrit: śarīraśvabhraśāyinyā piśācyā peśalāṅgayā / ahaṃkāracamatkṛtyā chalena chalitā vayam //
english: We are deceived by the delusion of egoism, which like a female fiend (sorceress) lies hid within the cavity of the body with all her sorcery.

sanskrit: prajñā varākā sarvaiva kāyabaddhāsthayānayā / mithyājñānakurākṣasyā chalitā kaṣṭamekikā //
english: Our reason unaided (by religion) is kept in bondage like a female slave within the prison of our bodies, by the malicious fiend of false knowledge.

sanskrit: na kiṃcidapi dṛśye'sminsatyaṃ tena hatātmanā / citraṃ dagdhaśarīreṇa janatā vipralabhyate //
english: It is certain that whatever we see here is unreal, and yet it is a wonder, that the mass of men are led to deception by the vile body, which has injured the cause of the soul.

sanskrit: dinaiḥ katipayaireva nirjharāmbukaṇo yathā / patatyayamayatnena jaraṭhaḥ kāyapallavaḥ //
english: Our bodies are as fleeting as the drops of a water-fall, and they fall off in a few days like the withered leaves of trees.

sanskrit: kāyo'yamacirāpāyo budbudo'mbunidhāviva / vyarthaṃ kāryaparāvarte parisphurati niṣphalaḥ //
english: They are as quickly dissolved as bubbles in the ocean; it is in vain therefore that it should hurl about in the whirlpool of business.

sanskrit: mithyājñānavikāre'sminsvapnasaṃbhramapattane / kāye sphuṭatarāpāye kṣaṇamāsthā na me dvija //
english: I have not a moment's reliance in this body, which is ever hastening to decay;and I regard its changeful delusions as a state of dreaming.

sanskrit: taḍitsu śaradabhreṣu gandharvanagareṣu ca / sthairyaṃ yena vinirṇītaṃ sa viśvasitu vigrahe //
english: Let those who have any faith in the stability of the lightning, of the autumn clouds, and in glacial castles, place their reliance in this body.

sanskrit: satatabhaṅgurakāryaparamparā vijayijātajayaṃ haṭhavṛttiṣu / prabaladoṣamidaṃ tu kalevaraṃ tṛṇamivāhamapohya sukhaṃ sthitaḥ //
english: It has outdone all other things that are doomed to destruction in its instability and perishableness. It is moreover subject to very many evils; wherefore I have set it at naught as a straw, and thereby obtained my repose.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / labdhvāpi taralākāre kāryabhārataraṃgiṇi / saṃsārasāgare janma bālyaṃ duḥkhāya kevalam //
english: One receiving his birth in the unstable ocean of the world, which is disturbed by the billows of the bustle of business, has to pass his boyhood in sufferings only.

sanskrit: aśaktirāpadastṛṣṇā mūkatā mūḍhabuddhitā / gṛdhnutā lolatā dainyaṃ sarvaṃ bālye pravartate //
english: Want of strength and sense, and subjection to diseases and dangers, muteness and appetence, joined with longings and helplessness, are the concomitants of infancy.

sanskrit: roṣarodanaraudrāsu dainyajarjaritāsu ca / daśāsu bandhanaṃ bālyamālānaṃ kariṇāmiva //
english: Childhood is chained to fretting and crying, to fits of anger, craving and every kind of incapacity, as an elephant when tied to the post by its shackles.

sanskrit: na mṛtau na jarāroge na cāpadi na yauvane / tāścintāḥ parikṛntanti hṛdayaṃ śaiśaveṣu yāḥ //
english: The vexations which tease the infant breast, are far greater than those which trouble us in youth and old age, or disturb one in disease, danger or at the approach of death.

sanskrit: tiryagjātisamārambhaḥ sarvairevāvadhīritaḥ / lolo bālasamācāro maraṇādapi duḥkhadaḥ //
english: The acts of a boy are as those of young animals, that are always restless and snubbed by every body. Hence boyhood is more intolerable than death itself.

sanskrit: pratibimbaghanājñānaṃ nānāsaṃkalpapelavam / bālyamālūnasaṃśīrṇamanaḥ kasya sukhāvaham //
english: How can boyhood be pleasing to any body, when it is but a semblance of gross ignorance, and full of whims and hobbies, and ever subject to miscarriages.

sanskrit: jalavahnayanilājasrajātabhītyā pade pade / yadbhayaṃ śaiśave'buddhyā kasyāpadi hi tadbhavet //
english: It is this silly boyhood which is in constant dread of dangers arising at every step from fire, water and air, and which rarely betide us in other states of life.

sanskrit: līlāsu durvilāseṣu durīhāsu durāśaye / paramaṃ mohamādhatte bālo balavadāpatan //
english: Boys are liable to very many errors in their plays and wicked frolics, and in all their wishes and attempts beyond their capacities:hence boyhood is the most perilous state.

sanskrit: vikalpakalpitārambhaṃ durvilārasaṃ durāspadam / śaiśavaṃ śāsanāyaiva puruṣasya na śāntaye //
english: Boys are engaged in false pursuits and wicked sports, and are subject to all foolish puerilities. Hence boyhood is fit for the rod and not for rest.

sanskrit: ye doṣā ye durācārā duṣkramā ye durādhayaḥ / te sarve saṃsthitā bālye durgarta iva kauśikāḥ //
english: All faults, misconduct, transgressions and heart-aches, lie hidden in boyhood like owls in hollow caves.

sanskrit: bālyaṃ ramyamiti vyarthabuddhayaḥ kalpayanti ye / tānmūrkhapuruṣānbrahmandhigastu hṛtacetasaḥ //
english: Fie to those ignorant and foolish people, who are falsely led to imagine boyhood as the most pleasant period of life.

sanskrit: yatra dolākṛti manaḥ parisphurati vṛttiṣu / trailokyā'bhavyamapi tatkathaṃ bhavati tuṣṭaye //
english: How can boyhood appear pleasing to any one, when the mind swings like a cradle towards every object of desire, however wrong it is deemed to be in both worlds.

sanskrit: sarveṣāmeva sattvānāṃ sarvāvasthābhya eva hi / manaścañcalatāmeti bālye daśaguṇaṃ mune //
english: The minds of all living beings are ever restless, but those of young people are ten times more at unrest.

sanskrit: manaḥ prakṛtyaiva calaṃ bālyaṃ ca calatāṃ varam / tayoḥ saṃśliṣyatostrātā ka ivāntaḥ kucāpale //
english: The mind is naturally unsteady, and so is boyhood also. Say what can save us from that state of life, when both these vagrant things combine to our destruction.

sanskrit: strīlocanaistaḍitpuñjairjvalājālaistaraṅgakaiḥ / cāpalaṃ śikṣitaṃ brahmañchaiśavākrāntacetasaḥ //
english: The glances of women, the flashes of lightning, the flame of fire, and the ever-rolling waves, have all imitated the fickleness of boyhood.

sanskrit: śaiśavaṃ ca manaścaiva sarvāsveva hi vṛttiṣu / bhrātarāviva lakṣyete satataṃ bhaṅgurasthitī //
english: Minority seems to be a twin brother to the mind, and resembles it in the unsteadiness and frailty of all its purposes.

sanskrit: sarvāṇi duḥkhabhūtāni sarve doṣā durādhayaḥ / bālamevopajīvanti śrīmantamiva mānavāḥ //
english: All kinds of miseries, misdeeds and miscarriages await on boyhood, as all sorts of men hang upon the rich.

sanskrit: navaṃ navaṃ prītikaraṃ na śiśuḥ pratyahaṃ yadi / prāpnoti tadasau yāti viṣavaiṣamyamūrcchanām //
english: Boys are fond of fresh things at all times, and on their failing to get the same, they fall to a fainting fit, as if from the effect of poison.

sanskrit: stokena vaśamāyāti stokenaiti vikāritām / amedhya eva ramate bālaḥ kauleyako yathā //
english: A boy like a dog, is as easily tamed as he is irritated at a little, and he is as glad to lie in the dust, as to play with dirt.

sanskrit: ajasravāṣpavadanaḥ kardamākto jaḍāśayaḥ / varṣokṣitasya taptasya sthalasya sadṛśaḥ śiśuḥ //
english: A foolish fretful boy with his body daubed in mire with the tears in his eyes, appears as a heap of dry clay soiled by a shower of rain.

sanskrit: bhayāhāraparaṃ dīnaṃ dṛṣṭādṛṣṭābhilāṣi ca / lolabuddhi vapurdhatte bālyaṃ duḥkhāya kevalam //
english: Boys are subject to fear and voracity; they are helpless but fond of every thing they have seen or heard, and equally fickle in their bodies and mind. Hence boyhood is a source of troubles only.

sanskrit: svasaṃkalpābhilaṣitānbhāvānaprāpya taptadhīḥ / duḥkhametyabalo bālo viniṣkṛtta ivāśaye //
english: The foolish and helpless child, becomes as sad and sour when he fails to get the object of his fancy, as when he is thwarted from the thing desired.

sanskrit: durīhālabdhalakṣāṇi bahuvakrolbaṇāni ca / bālasya yāni duḥkhāni mune tāni na kasyacit //
english: Children have much difficulty to get at the things they want, and which they can ask only by indistinct words. Hence no one suffers so much as boys.

sanskrit: bālo balavatā svena manorathavilāsinā / manasā tapyate nityaṃ grīṣmeṇeva vanasthalī //
english: A boy is as much irritated by the eagerness of his whimsical desires, as a patch of ground in the desert is parched by the summer heat.

sanskrit: vidyāgṛhagato bālo parāmeti kadarthanām / ālāna iva nāgendro viṣavaiṣamyabhīṣaṇām //
english: A boy on entering his school, is subjected to corrections, which are as painful to him as the goading and fetters to the elephant.

sanskrit: nānāmanorathamayī mithyākalpitakalpanā / duḥkhāyātyantadīrghāya bālatā pelavāśayā //
english: A great many whims and hobbies, and a variety of false fancies, tend continually to afflict boyhood, which is ever fond of toys and trifles.

sanskrit: saṃhṛṣṭo bhuvanaṃ bhoktamindumādātumambarāt / vāñchate yena maurkhyeṇa tatsukhāya kathaṃ bhavet //
english: How can senseless childhood be said to be a happy state of life, when the child is led by its ignorance to swallow everything in the world, and to wish to lay hold on the moon in the sky.

sanskrit: antaścitteraśaktasya śītātapanivāraṇe / ko viśeṣo mahābuddhe bālasyorvīruhastathā //
english: Say great sage! what difference is there between a child and a tree, both of which have sensitiveness, but unable to defend themselves from heat and cold.

sanskrit: uḍḍītumabhivāñchanti pakṣābhyāṃ kṣutparāyaṇāḥ / bhayāhāraparā nityaṃ bālā vihagadharmiṇaḥ //
english: Boys are of the nature of birds, being both subject to fear and hunger, and ready to fly about when impelled by them.

sanskrit: śaiśave guruto bhītirmātṛtaḥ pitṛtastathā / janato jyeṣṭhabālācca śaiśavaṃ bhayamandiram //
english: Again boyhood is the abode of fear from all sides; such as from the tutor, father, mother, elder brother and elderly boys, and from every body besides.

sanskrit: sakaladoṣadaśāvihatāśayaṃ śaraṇamapyavivekavilāsinaḥ / iha na kasyacideva mahāmune bhavati bālyamalaṃ parituṣṭaye //
english: Hence the hopeless state of childhood, which is full of faults and errors, and addicted to sports and thoughtlessness, cannot be satisfactory to any body.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / bālyānarthamatha tyaktvā pumānabhihatāśayaḥ / ārohati nipātāya yauvanaṃ saṃbhrameṇa tu //
english: Rama continued:—The boy having passed his state of blemishes, gladly steps to his youth with hopes of gaining his objects that tend only to his ruin.

sanskrit: tatrānantavilāsasya lolasya svasya cetasaḥ / vṛttīranubhavanyāti duḥkhādduḥkhāntaraṃ jaḍaḥ //
english: The insensible youth feels at this time the wanton inclinations of his loose mind, and goes on falling from one tribulation to another.

sanskrit: svacittabilasaṃsthena nānāsaṃbhramakāriṇā / balātkāmapiśācena vivaśaḥ paribhūyate //
english: He is overcome as one subdued by the power of delusive cupid, lying hidden in the cavity of the heart.

sanskrit: cintānāṃ lolavṛttīnāṃ lalanānāmivā'vṛtīḥ / arpayatyavaśaṃ ceto bālānāmañjanaṃ yathā //
english: His ungoverned mind gives rise to loose thoughts like those of voluptuous women, and these serve to beguile him like the magic collyrium (in the hand) of boys.

sanskrit: te te doṣā durārambhāstatra taṃ tādṛśāśayam / tadrūpaṃ pratilumpanti duṣṭāstenaiva ye mune //
english: Vices of the most heinous kind betake persons of such (perverse) minds in their youth, and lead them to their ruin.

sanskrit: mahānarakabījena saṃtatabhramadāyinā / yauvanena na ye naṣṭā naṣṭā nānyena te janāḥ //
english: The paths of youth lead them to the gate of hell through a maze of errors. Those that have been left uncorrupt by their youth, are not to be corrupted by anything else.

sanskrit: nānārasamayī citravṛttāntanicayombhitā / bhīmā yauvanabhūryena tīrṇā dhīraḥ sa ucyate //
english: Whoso has passed the dreadfully enchanted coast of youth, fraught with various flavours and wonders, are said to be truly wise.

sanskrit: nimeṣabhāsurākāramālolaghanagarjitam / vidyutprakāśamaśivaṃ yauvanaṃ me na rocate //
english: I take no delight in our unwelcome youth, which appears to us in the form of a momentary flash of lightning, and soon succeeded by the loud roaring of the clouds.

sanskrit: madhuraṃ svādu tiktaṃ ca dūṣaṇaṃ doṣabhūṣaṇam / surākallolasadṛśaṃ yauvanaṃ me na rocate //
english: Youth like rich wine is sweet and delicious (at first), but becomes bitter, insipid and noxious in a short time. Hence it is not delectable to me.

sanskrit: asatyaṃ satyasaṃkāśamacirādvipralambhadam / svapnāṅganāsaṅgasamaṃ yauvanaṃ me na rocate //
english: Youth appearing (at first) as a reality, is found to be a false, transient thing, as deceptive as a fairy dream by night. Hence I like it not.

sanskrit: sarvasyāgre sarvapuṃsaḥ kṣaṇamātramanoharam / gandharvanagaraprakhyaṃ yauvanaṃ me na rocate //
english: It is the most charming of all things to men, but its charm is soon lost and fled. Therefore the phantasmagoria of youth is not pleasing to me.

sanskrit: iṣuprapātamātraṃ hi sukhadaṃ duḥkhabhāsuram / dāhapoṣapradaṃ nityaṃ yauvanaṃ me na rocate //
english: Youth as an arrow shot is pleasant to see, but painful to feel its smart. Hence I do not like youth that produces blood heat.

sanskrit: āpātamātraramaṇaṃ sadbhāvarahitāntaram / veśyāstrīsaṃgamaprakhyaṃ yauvanaṃ me na rocate //
english: Youth as a harlot is charming at first sight, but turning heartless soon after. Hence it is not to my liking.

sanskrit: ye kecana samārambhāste sarve sarvaduḥkhadāḥ / tāruṇye saṃnidhiṃ yānti mahotpātā iva kṣaye //
english: As the efforts of a dying man are all for his torment, so the exertions of the young are portentous of his destruction.

sanskrit: hārdāndhakārakāriṇyā bhairavākāravānapi / yauvanājñānayāminyā bibheti bhagavānapi //
english: Puberty advances as a dark night spreading the shadow of destruction. It darkens the heart and mind by its hedious appearance, and intimidates even the god.

sanskrit: suvismṛtaśubhācāraṃ buddhivaidhuryadāyinam / dadātyatitarāmeṣa bhramaṃ yauvanasaṃbhramaḥ //
english: Errors growing in youth, cause copious mistakes in life, by upsetting good sense and setting at naught the approved good manners.

sanskrit: kāntāviyogajātena hṛdi duḥsparśavahninā / yauvane dahyate jantustarurdāvāgninā yathā //
english: The raging fire in the hearts of the young, caused by separation of their mates, burns them down like trees by a wild fire.

sanskrit: sunirmalāpi vistīrṇā pāvanyapi hi yauvane / matiḥ kaluṣatāmeti prāvṛṣīva taraṅgiṇī //
english: As a clear, sacred and wide stream, becomes muddy in the rains, so doth the mind of man however clear, pure and expanded it may be, gets polluted in his youth.

sanskrit: śakyate ghanakallolā bhīmā laṅghayituṃ nadī / na tu tāruṇyataralā tṛṣṇātaralitāntarā //
english: It is possible for one to cross over a river made terrible by its waves, but no way possible to him to get over the boisterous expanse of his youthful desires.

sanskrit: sā kāntā tau stanau pīnau te vilāsāstadānanam / tāruṇya iti cintābhiryāti jarjaratāṃ janaḥ //
english: O how (lamentably) is one's youth worn out with the thoughts of his mistress, her swollen breasts, her beautiful face and her sweet caresses.

sanskrit: naraṃ taralatṛṣṇārti yuvānamiha sādhavaḥ / pūjayanti na tu cchinnaṃ jarattṛṇalavaṃ yathā //
english: The young man afflicted with the pain of soft desire, is regarded by the wise in no better light than a fragment of (useless) straw.

sanskrit: nāśāyaiva madārtasya doṣamauktikadhāriṇaḥ / abhimānamahebhasya nityālānaṃ hi yauvanam //
english: Youth is the stake of haughty self-esteem, as the rack is for the immolation of the elephant giddy with its frontal pearl.

sanskrit: manovipulamūlānāṃ doṣāśīviṣadhāriṇām / śoṣarodanavṛkṣāṇāṃ yauvanaṃ bata kānanam //
english: Youth is a lamentable forest, where the mind as the root of all, gives growth to jungles of (love sick) groans and sighs, and tears of sorrow. The vices of this time, are as venomous snakes of the forest.

sanskrit: rasakesarasaṃbādhaṃ kuvikalpadalākulam / duścintācañcarīkāṇāṃ puṣkaraṃ viddhi yauvanam //
english: Know youthful bloom of the person to resemble the blooming lotus of the lake said:—the one is full of affections, bad desires and evil intents, as the other is fraught with bees, filaments, petals and leaves.

sanskrit: kṛtākṛtakupakṣāṇāṃ hṛtsarastīracāriṇām / ādhivyādhivihaṃgānāmālayo navayauvanam //
english: The new bloom of youth is the resort of anxiety and disease, which like two birds with their (black and white) plumage of vice and virtue, frequent the fountain of the young man's heart.

sanskrit: jaḍānāṃ gatasaṃkhyānāṃ kallolānāṃ vilāsinām / anapekṣitamaryādo vāridhirnavayauvanam //
english: Early youth resembles a deep sea, disturbed by the waves of numberless amusements, transgressing all bounds, and regardless of death and disease.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ guṇasargāṇāṃ parirūḍharajastamāḥ / apanetuṃ sthitiṃ dakṣo viṣamo yauvanānilaḥ //
english: Youth is like a furious gust of wind, over-loaded with the dust of pride and vanity, and sweeps away every trace of the good qualities.

sanskrit: nayanti pāṇḍutāṃ vakramākulāvakarotkaṭāḥ / ārohanti parāṃ koṭiṃ rūkṣā yauvanapāṃsavaḥ //
english: The rude dust of the passions of youths, disfigures their face, and the hurricane of their sensualities cover their good qualities.

sanskrit: udvodhayati doṣāliṃ nikṛntati guṇāvalim / narāṇāṃ yauvanollāso vilāso duṣkṛtaśriyām //
english: Youthful vigour awakens a series of faults, and destroys a group of good qualities, by increasing the vice of pleasures.

sanskrit: śarīrapaṅkajarajaścañcalāṃ matiṣaṭpadīm / nibadhnanmohayatyeṣa navayauvanacandramāḥ //
english: Youthful bloom confines the fickle mind to some beauteous person, as the bright moon-beams serve to shut the flitting bee in the dust of the closing lotus.

sanskrit: śarīrakhaṇḍakodbhūtā ramyā yauvanavallarī / lagnameva manobhṛṅgaṃ madayatyunnatiṃ gatā //
english: Youth like a delightsome cluster of flowers, growing in the arbour of human body, attracts the mind as the bee to it, and makes it giddy.

sanskrit: śarīramarutāpotthāṃ yuvatāmṛgatṛṣṇikām / manomṛgāḥ pradhāvantaḥ patanti viṣayāvaṭe //
english: The human mind anxious to derive pleasure from the youthfulness of the body, falls into the cave of sensuality, as a deer running after the mirage of desert heat, falls down into a pit.

sanskrit: śarīraśarvarījyotsnā cittakesariṇaḥ saṭā / laharī jīvitāmbhodheryuvatā me na tuṣṭaye //
english: I take no delight in moony youth, which guilds the dark body with its beams, and resembles the stern mane of the leonine mind. It is a surge in the ocean of our lives.

sanskrit: dināni katicidyeyaṃ phalitā dehajaṅgale / yuvatā śaradasyāṃ hi na samāśvāsamarhatha //
english: There is no reliance in youth, which fades away as soon as summer flowers in this desert of the body.

sanskrit: jhaṭityeva prayātyeva śarīrādyuvatākhagaḥ / kṣaṇenaivālpabhāgyasya hastāccintāmaṇiryathā //
english: Youth is as a bird, and as soon flies away from our bodily cage as the philosopher's stone, which quickly disappears from the hands of the unfortunate.

sanskrit: yadā yadā parāṃ koṭimadhyārohati yauvanam / valganti sajvarāḥ kāmāstadā nāśāya kevalam //
english: As youth advances to its highest pitch, so the feverish passions wax stronger for our destruction only.

sanskrit: tāvadeva vivalganti rāgadveṣapiśācakāḥ / nāstameti samastaiṣā yāvadyauvanayāminī //
english: As long as the night (delusion) of youth does not come to its end, so long the fiends of our passion do not cease to rage in the desert of the body.

sanskrit: nānāvikārabahule varāke kṣaṇanāśini / kāruṇyaṃ kuru tāruṇye mriyamāṇe sutai yathā //
english: Pity me, O sage! in this state of youth, which is so full of perturbations, as to have deprived me of the sight (light) of reason. O pity me as thou wouldst for thy dying son.

sanskrit: harṣamāyāti yo mohātpuruṣaḥ kṣaṇabhaṅginā / yauvanena mahāmugdhaḥ sa vai naramṛgaḥ smṛtaḥ //
english: The foolish man who ignorantly rejoices at his transient youth, is considered as a human beast.

sanskrit: mānamohānmadonmattaṃ yauvanaṃ yo'bhilaṣyati / acireṇa sa durbuddhiḥ paścāttāpena yujyate //
english: The foolish fellow who is fond of his youth which is flushed with pride and fraught with errors, comes to repent (of his folly) in a short time.

sanskrit: te pūjyāste mahātmānasta eva puruṣā bhuvi / ye sukhena samuttīrṇāḥ sādho yauvanasaṃkaṭāt //
english: Those great minded men are honoured on earth, who have safely passed over the perils of youth.

sanskrit: sukhena tīryate'mbhodhirutkṛṣṭamakarākaraḥ / na kallolabalollāsi sadoṣaṃ hatayauvanam //
english: One crosses over with ease the wide ocean which is the horrible habitation of huge whales; but it is hard to pass over our youth, that is so full of vices and the billows.

sanskrit: vinayabhūṣitamāryajanāspadaṃ karuṇayojjvalamāvalitaṃ guṇaiḥ / iha hi durlabhamaṅga suyauvanaṃ jagati kānanamambaragaṃ yathā //
english: It is very rare to have that happy youth which is fraught with humility, and spent in the company of respectable men; which is distinguished by feelings of sympathy, and is joined with good qualities and virtues.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / māṃsapāñcālikāyāstu yantralole'ṅgapañjare / snāyvasthigranthiśālinyāḥ striyāḥ kimiva śobhanaṃ //
english: Rama added:—What beauty is there in the person of a woman, composed of nerves, bones and joints? She is a mere statue of flesh, and a frame of moving machinery with her ribs and limbs.

sanskrit: tvaṅmāṃsaraktabāṣpāmbu pṛthakkṛtvā vilocanam / samālokaya ramyaṃ cetkiṃ mudhā parimuhyasi //
english: Can you find any thing beautiful in the female form, separated from its (component parts of the) flesh, skin, blood and water, that is worth beholding? Why then dote upon it?

sanskrit: itaḥ keśā ito raktamitīyaṃ pramadātanuḥ / kimetayā ninditayā karoti vipulāśayaḥ //
english: This fairy frame consisting of hairs in one part and blood in the other, cannot engage the attention of a high-minded man to its blemishes.

sanskrit: vāsovilepanairyāni lālitāni punaḥ punaḥ / tānyaṅgānyaṅga luṇṭhanti kravyādāḥ sarvadehinām //
english: The bodies of females, that are so covered with clothing and repeatedly besmeared with paints and perfumes, are (at last) devoured by carnivorous.

sanskrit: meruśrṛṃgataṭollāsigaṃgājalarayopamā / dṛṣṭā yasminstane muktāhārasyollāsaśālitā //
english: The breasts of women decorated with strings of pearl, appear as charming as the pinnacles of Sumeru, washed by the waters of Ganges falling upon them.

sanskrit: śmaśāneṣu diganteṣu sa eva lalanāstanaḥ / śvabhirāsvādyate kāle laghupiṇḍa ivāndhasaḥ //
english: The breasts of women decorated with strings of pearl, appear as charming as the pinnacles of Sumeru, washed by the waters of Ganges falling upon them.

sanskrit: raktamāṃsāsthidigdhāni karabhasya yathā vane / tathaivāṅgāni kāminyāstāṃ pratyapi hi ko grahaḥ //
english: There is no difference between a woman and a young elephant that lives in the jungle, both of them being made of blood, flesh and bones. Then why hunt after her.

sanskrit: āpātaramaṇīyatvaṃ kalpate kevalaṃ striyāḥ / manye tadapi nāstyatra mune mohaikakāraṇam //
english: A woman is charming only for a short time, and does not long last to be so. I look upon her merely as a cause of delusion.

sanskrit: vipulollāsadāyinyā madamanmathapūrvakam / ko viśeṣo vikāriṇyā madirāyāḥ striyāstathā //
english: There is no difference between wine and a woman, both of them tending equally to produce high-flown mirth and jollity, and creating revelry and lust.

sanskrit: lalanālānasaṃlīnā mune mānavadantinaḥ / prabodhaṃ nādhigacchanti dṛḍhairapi śamāṅkuśaiḥ //
english: Uxorious men are like chained elephants among mankind, that will never come to sense however goaded by the hooks of reason.
