sanskrit: keśakajjaladhāriṇyo duḥsparśā locanapriyāḥ / duṣkṛtāgniśikhā nāryo dahanti tṛṇavannaram //
english: Women are the flames of vice, their black-dyed eye and hairs are as their smoke and soot. They are as intangible as fire, though pleasing to the sight. They burn the man as fire consumes the straw.

sanskrit: jvalatāmatidūre'pi sarasā api nīrasāḥ / striyo hi narakāgnīnāmindhanaṃ cāru dāruṇam //
english: They burn from afar (more than fire), and are as dry as bones (in their hearts), though appearing as soft and juicy to sight. They serve as fuel to the fire of hell, and are dangerous with their charmingness.

sanskrit: vikīrṇākārakabarī tarattārakalocanā / purṇendubimbavadanā kusumotkarahāsinī //
english: The woman resembles a moon-light night, veiled over by her loosened locks, and looking through her starry eyes. She shows her moon-like face amidst her flowery smiles.

sanskrit: līlāvilolapuruṣā kāryasaṃhārakāriṇī / paraṃ vimohanaṃ buddheḥ kāminī dīrghayāminī //
english: Her soft dalliance destroys all manly energy, and her caresses overpower the good sense of men, as the shade of night does the sleeping.

sanskrit: puṣpābhirāmamadhurā karapallavaśālinī / bhramarākṣivilāsāḍhyā stanastabakadhāriṇī //
english: The woman is as lovely as a creeper in its flowering time. Her palm are the leaves and her eyes as the black-bees (on the flower). Her breasts are as the uplifted tops of the plant.

sanskrit: puṣpakesaragaurāṅgī naramāraṇatatparā / dadātyunmattavaivaśyaṃ kāntā viṣalatā yathā //
english: The lovely damsel is like a poisonous creeper, fair as the filament of a flower but destructive of life, by causing inebriation and insensibility.

sanskrit: satkāryocchvāsamātreṇa bhujaṅgadalanotkayā / kāntayoddhriyate jantuḥ karabhyevorago bilāt //
english: As the snake-catcher entices the snake by his breath and brings it out of its hole, so does the woman allure the man by her officious civilities, and gets him under her control.

sanskrit: kāmanāmnā kirātena vikīrṇā mugdhacetasām / nāryo naravihaṃgānāmaṅgabandhanavāgurāḥ //
english: Concupiscence as a huntsman, has spread his nets in the forms of women, for the purpose of ensnaring the persons of deluded men like silly birds.

sanskrit: lalanāvipulālāne manomattamataṃgajaḥ / ratiśṛṅkhalayā brahmanbaddhastiṣṭhati mūkavat //
english: The mind of man though as fierce as that of a furious elephant, is tied fast by the chain of love to the fulcrum of women, just as an elephant is fastened (by his leg) to the post, where he remains dull and dumb for ever.

sanskrit: janmapalvalamatsyānāṃ cittakardamacāriṇām / puṃsāṃ durvāsanārajjurnārī baḍiśapiṇḍikā //
english: Human life is as a pool in which the mind moves about in its mud and mire (as a fish). Here it is caught by the bait of woman, and dragged along by the thread of its impure desires.

sanskrit: manduraṃ ca turaṅgāṇāmālānamiva dantinām / puṃsāṃ mantra ivāhīnāṃ bandhanaṃ vāmalocanā //
english: The beauteous-eyed damsel is a bondage to man, as the stable is to the horse, the fastening post to the elephant, and as spells are to the snakes.

sanskrit: nānārasavatī citrā bhogabhūmiriyaṃ mune / striyamāśritya saṃyātā parāmiha hi saṃsthitim //
english: This wondrous world, with all its delights and enjoyments, began with woman and depends on women for its continuance.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ doṣaratnānāṃ susamudgikayā'nayā / duḥkhaśṛṅkhalayā nityamalamastu mama striyā //
english: A woman is the casket of all gems of vice (Pandora's box), she is the cause of the chain of our everlasting misery, and is of no use to me.

sanskrit: kiṃ stanena kimakṣṇā vā kiṃ nitambena kiṃ bhuvā / māṃsamātraikasāreṇa karomyahamavastunā //
english: What shall I do with her breast, her eyes, her loins, her eyebrows, the substance of which is but flesh, and which therefore is altogether unsubstantial.

sanskrit: ito māṃsamito raktamito'sthīnīti vāsaraiḥ / brahmankatipayaireva yāti strī viśarārutām //
english: Here and there, O Brahman! her flesh and blood and bones undergo a change for the worse in course of a few days.

sanskrit: yāstāta puruṣaiḥ sthūlairlalitā manujaiḥ priyāḥ / tā mune pravibhaktāṅgyaḥ svapanti pitṛbhūmiṣu //
english: You see sir, those dearly beloved mistresses, who are so much fondled by foolish men, lying at last in the cemetery, and the members of their bodies all mangled and falling off from their places.

sanskrit: yasminghanatarasnehaṃ mukhe patrāṅkurāḥ striyaḥ / kāntena racitā brahmanpīyate tena jaṅgale //
english: O Brahman! those dear objects of love—the faces of damsels, so fondly decorated by their lovers with paints and pastes, are at last to be singed on the piles.

sanskrit: keśāḥ śmaśānavṛkṣeṣu yānti cāmaralekhikām / asthīnyuḍuvadābhānti dinairavanimaṇḍale //
english: Their braided hairs now hang as flappers of chowry on the arbors of the cemetery, and their whitened bones are strewn about as shining stars after a few days.

sanskrit: pibanti pāṃsavo raktaṃ kravyādāścāpyanekaśaḥ / carmāṇi ca śivā bhuṅkte khaṃ yānti prāṇavāyavaḥ //
english: Behold their blood sucked in by the dust of the earth, voracious beasts and worms feeding upon their flesh, jackals tearing their skin, and their vital air wafted in the vacuum.

sanskrit: ityeṣā lalanāṅgānāmacireṇaiva bhāvinī / sthitirmayā vaḥ kathitā kiṃ bhrāntimanudhāvatha //
english: This is the state to which the members of the female body must shortly come to pass, you say all existence to be delusion, tell me therefore why do you allow yourselves to fall into error?

sanskrit: bhūtapañcakasaṃghaṭṭasaṃsthānaṃ lalanābhidham / rasādabhipatatvetatkathaṃ nāma dhiyānvitaḥ //
english: A woman is no other than a form composed of the five elements, then why should intelligent men be fondly attached to her (at the risk of their ruin)?

sanskrit: śākhāpratānagahanā kaṭvamlaphalamālinī / sutālottālatāmeti cintā kāntānusāriṇī //
english: Men's longing for women is likened to the creeper called Suta, which stretches its sprigs to a great length, but bears plenty of bitter and sour fruits.

sanskrit: kāndigbhūtatayā ceto ghanagardhāndhamākulam / paraṃ mohamupādatte yūthabhraṣṭamṛgo yathā //
english: A man blinded by avarice (for the supportance of his mate) is as a stray deer from its herd; and not knowing which way to go, is lost in the maze of illusion.

sanskrit: śocyatāṃ paramāṃ yāti taruṇastaruṇīparaḥ / nibaddhaḥ kariṇīlolo vindhyakhāte yathā gajaḥ //
english: A young man under the control of a young woman, is as much lamentable as an elephant fallen into a pit of the Vindhya mountain in pursuit of his mate.

sanskrit: yasya strī tasya bhogecchā niḥstrīkasya kva bhogabhūḥ / striyaṃ tyaktvā jagattyaktaṃ jagattyaktvā sukhī bhavet //
english: He that has a wife, has an appetite for enjoyment on earth; but one without her has no object of desire. Abandonment of the wife amounts to the abandoning of the world, and forsaking the world is the path to true happiness.

sanskrit: āpātamātraramaṇeṣu sudustareṣu bhogeṣu nāhamalipakṣaticañcaleṣu / brahmanrame maraṇarogajarādibhītyā śāmyāmyahaṃ paramupaimi padaṃ prayatnāt //
english: I am not content, O Brahman! with these unmanageable enjoyments which are as flickering as the wings of bees, and are as soon at an end as they are born (like the ephemerids of a day). I long only for the state of supreme bliss, from my fear of repeated births transmigration), decay and death.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / aparyāptaṃ hi bālatvaṃ balātpibati yauvanam / yauvanaṃ ca jarā paścātpaśya karkaśatāṃ mithaḥ //
english: Boyhood has scarcely lost its boyishness when it is overtaken by youth, which is soon followed by a ruthless old age, devouring the other two.

sanskrit: himāśanirivāmbhojaṃ vātyeva śaradambukam / dehaṃ jarā nāśayati nadī tīrataruṃ yathā //
english: Old age withers the body like a frost freezing the lake of lilies. It drives away the beauty of the person as a storm does the autumnal clouds; and it pulls down the body, as a current carries away a tree on the bank.

sanskrit: jarjarīkṛtasarvāṅgī jarā jaraṭharūpiṇī / virūpatāṃ nayatyāśu dehaṃ viṣalavo yathā //
english: The old man with his limbs slackened and worn out by age, and his body weakened by infirmity, is treated by women as a useless beast.

sanskrit: śithilādīrṇasarvāṅgaṃ jarājīrṇakalevaram / samaṃ paśyanti kāminyaḥ puruṣaṃ karabhaṃ yathā //
english: ?missing text?

sanskrit: anāyāsakadarthinyā gṛhīte jarasā jane / palāyya gacchati prajñā sapatnyevāhatāṅganā //
english: Old age drives a man's good sense, as a good wife is driven away by her step dame.

sanskrit: dāsāḥ putrāḥ striyaścaiva bāndhavāḥ suhṛdastathā / hasantyunmattakamiva naraṃ vārdhakakampitam //
english: A man in his state of tottering old age, is scoffed at as a dotard by his own sons and servants, and even by his wife, and all his friends and relations.

sanskrit: duṣprekṣyaṃ jaraṭhaṃ dīnaṃ hīnaṃ guṇaparākramaiḥ / gṛdhro vṛkṣamivādīrghaṃ gardho hyabhyeti vṛddhakam //
english: Insatiable avarice like a greedy vulture alights on the heads of the aged, when their appearance grows uncouth, and their bodies become helpless, and devoid of all manly qualities and powers.

sanskrit: dainyadoṣamayī dīrghā hṛdi dāhapradāyinī / sarvāpadāmekasakhī vārdhake vardhate spṛhā //
english: Appetite the constant companion of my youth, is thriving along with my age, accompanied with her evils of indigence, and heart-burning cares and restlessness.

sanskrit: kartavyaṃ kiṃ mayā kaṣṭaṃ paratretyatidāruṇam / apratīkārayogyaṃ hi vardhate vārdhake bhayam //
english: Ah me! what must I do to remove my present and future pains? It is this fear which increases with old age, and finds no remedy.

sanskrit: ko'haṃ varākaḥ kimiva karomi kathameva ca / tiṣṭhāmi maunameveti dīnatodeti vārdhake //
english: What am I that am brought to this extremity of senselessness, what can I do in this state. I must remain dumb and silent. Under these reflections there is an increased sense of helplessness in old age.

sanskrit: kathaṃ kadā me kimiva svādu syādbhojanaṃ janāt / ityajasraṃ jarā caiṣā ceto dahati vārdhake //
english: How and when and what shall I eat, and what is sweet to taste? These are the thoughts which trouble the mind of one when old age comes upon him.

sanskrit: gardho'bhyudeti sollāsamupabhoktuṃ na śakyate / hṛdayaṃ dahyate nūnaṃ śaktidausthyena vārdhake //
english: There is an insatiable desire for enjoyments, but the powers to enjoy them are lacking. It is the want of strength which afflicts the heart in old age.

sanskrit: jarājīrṇabakī yāvatkāyakleśāpakāriṇī / rauti rogoragākīrṇā kāyadrumaśiraḥsthitā //
english: Hoary old age sits and shrieks as a heron on the top of the tree of this body, which is infested within it by the serpents of sickness.

sanskrit: tāvadāgata evāśu kuto'pi paridṛśyate / ghanāndhyatimirākāṅkṣī mune maraṇakauśikaḥ //
english: As the grave owl—the bird of night, appears unexpectedly to our sight soon as the evening shades cover the landscape, so does the solemn appearance of death overtake us in the eve of our life.

sanskrit: sāyaṃsaṃdhyāṃ prajātāṃ vai tamaḥ samanudhāvati / jarāṃ vapuṣi dṛṣṭvaiva mṛtiḥ samanudhāvati //
english: As darkness prevails over the world at the eve of the day, so doth death overtake the body at the eve of the life.

sanskrit: jarākusumitaṃ dehadrumaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva dūrataḥ / adhyāpatati vegena mune maraṇamarkaṭaḥ //
english: Death overtakes a man in his hoary old age, just as an ape alights on a tree covered with pearly flowers.

sanskrit: śūnyaṃ nagaramābhāti bhāti cchinnalato drumaḥ / bhātyanāvṛṣṭimāndeśo na jarājarjaraṃ vapuḥ //
english: Even a deserted city, a leafless tree and parched up land may present a fair aspect, but never does the body look well that is pulled down by hoary age.

sanskrit: kṣaṇānnigaraṇāyaiva kāsakvaṇitakāriṇī / gṛdhrīvāmiṣamādatte tarasaiva naraṃ jarā //
english: Old age with its hooping cough lays hold on a man, just as a vulture seizes its prey with loud shrieks in order to devour it.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva sotsukevāśu pragṛhya śirasi kṣaṇam / pralunāti jarā dehaṃ kumārī kairavaṃ yathā //
english: As a girl eagerly lays hold on a lotus flower whenever she meets with one, and then plucks it from its stalk and tears it to pieces, so does old age overtake the body of a person and break it down at last.

sanskrit: sītkārakāriṇī pāṃsuparuṣā parijarjaram / śarīraṃ śātayatyeṣā vātyeva tarupallavam //
english: As the chill blast of winter shakes a tree and covers its leaves with dust, so does old age seize the body with a tremor and fill all its limbs with the rust of diseases.

sanskrit: jarasopahato deho dhatte jarjaratāṃ gataḥ / tuṣāranikarākīrṇaparimlānāmbujaśriyam //
english: The body overtaken by old age becomes as pale and battered, as a lotus flower beaten by frost becomes withered and shattered.

sanskrit: jarā jyotsnoditaiveyaṃ śiraḥśikharipṛṣṭhataḥ / vikāsayati saṃrabdhaṃ vātakāsakumudvatī //
english: As moon-beams contribute to the growth of Kumuda flowers on the top of mountains, so does old age produce grey hairs resembling casla flowers on the heads of men.

sanskrit: paripakvaṃ samālokya jarākṣāravidhūsaram / śiraḥkūṣmāṇḍakaṃ bhuṅkte puṃsāṃ kālaḥ kileśvaraḥ //
english: Death the lord of all beings, views the grey head of a man as a ripe pumpkin seasoned with the salt of old age, and devours it with zest.

sanskrit: jarājahnusutodyuktā mūlānyasya nikṛntati / śarīratīravṛkṣasya calatyāyuṣi satvaram //
english: As the Ganges upsets a neighbouring tree by its rapid course, so does old age destroy the body, as the current of our life runs fast to decay.

sanskrit: jarāmārjārikā bhuṅkte yauvanākhuṃ tathoddhatā / paramullāsamāyāti śarīrāmiṣagardhinī //
english: Old age which preys on the flesh of the human body, takes as much delight in devouring its youthful bloom as a cat does in feeding upon a mouse.

sanskrit: kācidasti jagatyasminnāmaṅgalakarī tathā / yathā jarākrośakarī dehajaṅgalajambukī //
english: Decrepitude raises its ominous hoarse sound of hiccough in the body, as the jackal sends forth her hideous cry amidst the forest.

sanskrit: kāsaśvāsasasītkārā duḥkhadhūmatamomayī / jarājvālā jvalatyeṣā yasyāsau dagdha eva hi //
english: Dotage as an inward flame consumes the living body as a wet log of wood, which thereupon emits its hissing sounds of hiccough and hard breathing, and sends up the gloomy fumes of woe and sighs.

sanskrit: jarasā vakratāmeti śuklāvayavapallavā / tāta tanvī tanurnṛṇāṃ latā puṣpānatā yathā //
english: The body like a flowering creeper, bends down under the pressure of age, turns to grey like the fading leaves of a plant, and becomes as lean and thin as a plant after its flowering time is over.

sanskrit: jarākarpūradhavalaṃ dehakarpūrapādapam / mune maraṇamātaṅgo nūnamuddharati kṣaṇāt //
english: As the infuriate elephant upsets the white plantain tree in a moment, so does old age destroy the body that becomes as white as camphor all over.

sanskrit: maraṇasya mune rājño jarādhavalacāmarā / āgacchato'gre niryāti svādhivyādhipatākinī //
english: Senility, O sage! is as the standard bearer of the king of death, flapping his chowry of grey hairs before him, and bringing in his train an army of diseases and troubles.

sanskrit: na jitāḥ śatrubhiḥ saṃkhye praviṣṭā ye'drikoṭare / te jarājīrṇarākṣasyā paśyāśu vijitā mune //
english: The monster of old age, will even overcome those that were never defeated in wars by their enemies, and those that hide themselves in the inaccessible caverns of mountains.

sanskrit: jarātuṣāravalite śarīrasadanāntare / śaknuvantyakṣaśiśavaḥ spandituṃ na manāgapi //
english: As infants cannot play in a room that has become cold with snow, so the senses can have no play in the body that is stricken with age.

sanskrit: daṇḍatṛtīyapādena praskhalantī muhurmuhuḥ / kāsādhovāyumurajā jarā yoṣitpranṛtyati //
english: Old age like a juggling girl, struts on three legs at the sound of coughing and whiffing, beating as a tymbal on both sides.

sanskrit: saṃsārasaṃsṛterasyā gandhakuṭyāṃ śirogatā / dehayaṣṭyāṃ jarānāmnī cāmaraśrīrvirājate //
english: The tuft of grey hairs on the head of the aged body, represents a white flapper (chowry) fastened to the top of a handle of white sandal wood, to welcome the despot of death.

sanskrit: jarācandrodayasite śarīranagare sthite / kṣaṇādvikāsamāyāti mune maraṇakairavam //
english: As hoary age makes his advance like moon-light on the site of the body, he calls forth the hidden death to come out of it, as the moon-light makes the nilumbium to unfold its buds.

sanskrit: jarāsudhālepasite śarīrāntaḥpurāntare / aśaktirārtirāpacca tiṣṭhanti sukhamaṅganāḥ //
english: Again as the white wash of old age whitens the outer body, so debility, diseases and dangers become its inmates in the inner typo apartment.

sanskrit: abhāvo'gresarī yatra jarā jayati jantuṣu / kastatreha samāśvāso mama mandamatermune //
english: It is the extinction of being that is preceded by old age; therefore I as a man of little understanding, can have no reliance in old age (though extolled by some){GL_NOTE:73106:}

sanskrit: kiṃ tena durjīvitadurgraheṇa jarāgatenāpi hi jīvyate yat / jarājagatyāmajitā janānāṃ sarvaiṣaṇāstāta tiraskaroti //
english: What then is the good of this miserable life, which lives under the subjection of old age? Senility is irresistable in this world, and defies all efforts to avoid or overcome it.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / vikalpakalpanānalpajalpitairalpabuddhibhiḥ / bhedairuddhuratāṃ nītaḥ saṃsārakuhare bhramaḥ //
english: Men of little understandings are found to fall into grave errors in this pit of the world, by their much idle talk, ever doubting scepticism, and schisms.

sanskrit: satāṃ kathamivāstheha jāyate jālapañjare / bālā evāttumicchanti phalaṃ mukurabimbitam //
english: Good people can have no more confidence in the net work of their ribs, than little children may have a liking for fruits reflected in a mirror.

sanskrit: ihāpi vidyate yeṣāṃ pelavā sukhabhāvanā / ākhustantumivāśeṣaṃ kālastāmapi kṛntati //
english: Time is a rat that cuts off the threads of all thoughts (prospects), which men may entertain here about the contemptible pleasures of this world.

sanskrit: na tadastīha yadayaṃ kālaḥ sakalaghasmaraḥ / grasate tajjagajjātaṃ protthābdhimiva vāḍavaḥ //
english: There is nothing in this world which the all-devouring time will spare. He devours all things as the submarine fire consumes the over-flowing sea.

sanskrit: samastasāmānyatayā bhīmaḥ kālo maheśvaraḥ / dṛśyasattāmimāṃ sarvāṃ kavalīkartumudyataḥ //
english: Time is the sovran lord of all, and equally terrible to all things. He is ever ready to devour all visible beings.

sanskrit: mahatāmapi no devaḥ pratipālayati kṣaṇam / kālaḥ kavalitānantaviśvo viśvātmatāṃ gataḥ //
english: Time as master of all, spares not even the greatest of us for a moment. He swallows the universe within himself, whence he is known as the universal soul.

sanskrit: yugavatsarakalpākhyaiḥ kiṃcitprakaṭatāṃ gataḥ / rūpairalakṣyarūpātmā sarvamākramya tiṣṭhati //
english: Time pervades all things, but has no perceptible feature of his own, except that he is imperfectly known by the names of years, ages and kalpas.

sanskrit: ye ramyā ye śubhārambhāḥ sumeruguravo'pi ye / kālena vinigīrṇāste garuḍeneva pannagāḥ //
english: All that was fair and good, and as great as the mount of Meru, have gone down in the womb of eternity, as the snakes are gorged by the greedy Garuda.

sanskrit: nirdayaḥ kaṭhinaḥ krūraḥ karkaśaḥ kṛpaṇo'dhamaḥ / na tadasti yadadyāpi na kālo nigiratyayam //
english: There was no one ever so unkind, hard-hearted, cruel, harsh or miserly, whom time has not devoured.

sanskrit: kālaḥ kavalanaikāntamatiratti girannapi / anantairapi lokaughairnāyaṃ tṛpto mahāśanaḥ //
english: Time is ever greedy although he should devour the mountains. This great gourmand is not satiated with gorging every thing in all the worlds.

sanskrit: haratyayaṃ nāśayati karotyatti nihanti ca / kālaḥ saṃsāranṛttaṃ hi nānārūpaṃ yathā naṭaḥ //
english: Time like an actor plays many parts on the stage of the world. He abstracts and kills, produces and devours and at last destroys every thing.

sanskrit: bhinatti pravibhāgasthabhūtabījānyanāratam / jagatyasattayā bandhāddāḍimāni yathā śukaḥ //
english: Time is incessantly picking up the seeds of all the four kinds of living beings from this unreal world, as a parrot picks up the seeds from under the cracked shell of a pomegranate.

sanskrit: śubhāśubhaviṣāṇāgravilūnajanapallavaḥ / sphūrjati sphītajanatājīvarājīvanīgajaḥ //
english: Time like a wild elephant uproots all proud living beings in this world, as the other pulls up the trees of the forest with their tusks.

sanskrit: viriñcimūlabrahmāṇḍabṛhaddevaphaladrumam / brahmakānanamābhogi paramāvṛtya tiṣṭhati //
english: This creation of God is like a forest, having Brahma for its foundation and its trees full of the great fruits of gods. Time commands it throughout its length and breadth.

sanskrit: yāminī bhramarāpūrṇā racayandinamañjarīḥ / varṣakalpakalāvallīrna kadācana khidyate //
english: Time glides along incessantly as a creeping plant, composed of years and ages as its parts, and the sable nights as black bees chasing after them.

sanskrit: bhidyate nāvabhagno'pi dagdho'pi hi na dahyate / dṛśyate nāpi dṛśyo'pi dhūrtacūḍāmaṇirmune //
english: Time, O sage, is the subtlest of all things. It is divided though indivisible, it is consumed though incombustible, it is perceived though imperceptible in its nature.

sanskrit: ekenaiva nimeṣeṇa kiṃcidutthāpayatyalam / kiṃcidvināśayatyuccairmanorājyavadātataḥ //
english: Time like the mind is strong enough to create and demolish any thing in a trice, and its province is equally extensive with it.

sanskrit: durvilāsavilāsinyā ceṣṭayā kaṣṭaṣuṣṭayā / dravyaikarūpakṛdrūpaṃ janamāvartayansthitaḥ //
english: Time is a whirlpool to men; and being accompanied with desire his insatiable and ungovernable mistress and delighting in illicit enjoyments, he makes them do and undo the same thing over and over again.

sanskrit: tṛṇaṃ pāṃsuṃ mahendraṃ ca sumeruṃ parṇamarṇavam / ātmaṃbharitayā sarvamātmasātkartumudyataḥ //
english: Time is prompted by his rapacity to appropriate every thing to himself, from the meanest straw, dust, leaves and worms, to the greatest Indra and the mount Meru itself.

sanskrit: krauryamatraiva paryāptaṃ lubdhatātraiva saṃsthitā / sarvadaurbhāgyamatraiva cāpalaṃ vāpi duḥsaham //
english: Time is the source of all malice and greediness, and the spring of all misfortunes, and intolerable fluctuations of our states.

sanskrit: preraya~llīlayārkendū krīḍatīva nabhastale / nikṣiptalīlāyugalo nije bāla ivāṅgaṇe //
english: As boys with their balls play about their play-ground, so does time in his arena of the sky, play with his two balls of the sun and moon.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtāsthimālābhirāpādavalitākṛtiḥ / vilasatyeva kalpānte kālaḥ kalitakalpanaḥ //
english: Time at the expiration of the kalpa age, will dance about with a long chain of the bones of the dead hanging from his neck to the feet.

sanskrit: asyoḍḍāmaravṛttasya kalpānte'ṅgavinirgataiḥ / prasphuratyambare merurbhūrjatvagiva vāyubhiḥ //
english: The gale of desolation rising from the body of this desolator of the world at the end of a kalpa age, causes the fragments of mount Meru to fly about in the air like the rinds of the bhoja-petera tree.

sanskrit: rudro bhūtvā bhavatyeṣa mahendro'tha pitāmahaḥ / śakro vaiśravaṇaścāpi punareva na kiṃcana //
english: Time then assumes his terrific form of fire ([Sanskrit: pralayagni]), to dissolve the world in empty space, when the gods Brahma and Indra and all others cease to exist.

sanskrit: dhatte'jasrotthitoddhvastānsargānamitabhāsvarān / anyāndadhaddivānaktaṃ vīcīrabdhirivātmani //
english: As the sea shows himself in a continued series of waves rising and falling one after another, so it is time that creates and dissolves the world, and appears to rise and fall in the rotation of days and nights.

sanskrit: mahākalpābhidhānebhyo vṛkṣebhyaḥ pariśātayan / devāsuragaṇānpakvānphalabhārāniva sthitaḥ //
english: Time plucks the gods and demigods as ripe fruits, from their great arbor of existence, at the end of the world,

sanskrit: kālo'yaṃ bhūtamaśakaghuṃghumānāṃ prapātinām / brahmāṇḍodumbaraughānāṃ bṛhatpādapatāṃ gataḥ //
english: Time resembles a large fig tree (Ficus religiosa), studded with all the worlds as its fruits, and resonant with the noise of living beings like the hissing of gnats about them.

sanskrit: sattāmātrakumudvatyā cijjyotsnāpariphullayā / vapurvinodayatyekaṃ kriyāpriyatamānvitaḥ //
english: Time accompanied by Action as his mate, regales himself in the garden of the world, blossoming with the moon-beams of the Divine Spirit.

sanskrit: anantāpāraparyantabaddhapīṭhaṃ nijaṃ vapuḥ / mahāśailavaduttuṅgamavalambya vyavasthitaḥ //
english: As the high and huge rock supports its body upon the basis of the earth, so does time rest itself in endless and interminable eternity.

sanskrit: kvacicchayāmatamaḥśyāmaṃ kvacitkāntiyutaṃ tatam / dvayenāpi kvacidriktaṃ svabhāvaṃ bhāvayan sthitaḥ //
english: Time assumes to himself various hues of black, white and red (at night, day and midday) which serve for his vestures.

sanskrit: saṃlīnāsaṃkhyasaṃsārasārayā svātmasattayā / urvyeva bhāraghanayā nibaddhapadatāṃ gataḥ //
english: As the earth is the great support of hills which are fixed upon it, so is time the support of all the innumerable ponderous worlds that constitute the universe.

sanskrit: na khidyate nādriyate nāyāti na ca gacchati / nāstameti na codeti mahākalpaśatairapi //
english: Hundreds of great kalpa ages (of the creation and dissolution of the world) may pass away, yet there is nothing that can move eternity to pity or concern, or stop or expedite his course. It neither sets nor rises.

sanskrit: kevalaṃ jagadārambhalīlayā ghanahelayā / pālayatyātmanātmānamanahaṃkāramātatam //
english: Time is never proud to think, that it is he who without the least sense of pain and labor, brings this world into play and makes it to exist.

sanskrit: yāminīpaṅkakalitāṃ dinakokanadāvalīm / meghabhramarikāmātmasarasyāropayansthitaḥ //
english: Time is like a reservoir in which the nights are as mud, the days as lotuses, and the clouds as bees.

sanskrit: gṛhītvā kṛpaṇaḥ kṛṣṇāṃ rajanīṃ jīrṇamārjanīm / ālokakanakakṣodānāharatyabhito girim //
english: As a covetous man, with worn out broom sticks in hand, sweeps over a mountain to gather the particles of gold strewn over it, so does time with his sweeping course of days and nights, collect in one mass of the dead all living beings in the world.

sanskrit: saṃcārayankriyāṅgulyā koṇakeṣvarkadīpikām / jagatsadmani kārpaṇyātkva kimastīti vīkṣate //
english: As a miserly man trims and lights a lamp with his own fingers, to look into his stores at each corner of the room; so does time light the lamps of the sun and moon to look into the living beings in every nook and corner of the world.

sanskrit: prekṣyāharvinimeṣeṇa sūryākṣṇā pākavantyalam / lokapālaphalānyatti jagajjīrṇavanādayam //
english: As one ripens the raw fruits in sun and fire in order to devour them, so does time ripen men by their sun and fire worship, to bring them under his jaws at last.

sanskrit: jagajjīrṇakuṭīkīrṇānarpayatyugrakoṭare / krameṇa guṇavallokamaṇīnmṛtyusamudgake //
english: The world is a dilapidated cottage and men of parts are rare gems in it. Time hides them in the casket of his belly, as a miser keeps his treasure in a coffer.

sanskrit: guṇairāpūryate yaiva lokaratnāvalī bhṛśam / bhūṣārthamiva tāmaṅge kṛtvā bhūyo nikṛntati //
english: Good men are like a chaplet of gems, which time puts on his head for a time with fondness, and then tears and tramples it down.

sanskrit: dinahaṃsānusṛtayā niśendīvaramālayā / tārakesarayājasraṃ capalo valayatyalam //
english: Strings of days, nights and stars, resembling beads and bracelets of white and black lotuses, are continually turning round the arm of time.

sanskrit: śailārṇadyudharāśṛṅgajagadūrṇāyusaunikaḥ / pratyahaṃ pibate prekṣya tārāraktakaṇānapi //
english: Time (as a vulture) looks upon the world as (the carcase of) a ram, with its mountains, seas, sky and earth as its four horns, and the stars as its drops of blood which it drinks day by day.

sanskrit: tāruṇyanalinīsoma āyurmātaṅgakesarī / na tadasti na yasyāyaṃ tucchātucchasya taskaraḥ //
english: Time destroys youth as the moon shuts the petals of the lotus. It destroys life as the lion kills the elephant: there is nothing however insignificant that time steals not away.

sanskrit: kalpakelivilāsena piṣṭapātitajantunā / abhāvo bhāvabhāsena ramate svātmanātmani //
english: Time after sporting for a Kalpa period in the act of killing and crushing of all living beings, comes to lose its own existence and becomes extinct in the eternity of the Spirit of spirits.

sanskrit: kartā bhoktātha saṃhartā smartā sarvapadaṃ gataḥ //
english: Time after a short rest and respite reappears as the creator, preserver, destroyer and remembrancer of all. He shows the shapes of all things whether good or bad, keeping his own nature beyond the knowledge of all. Thus doth time expand and preserve and finally dissolve all things by way of sport.

sanskrit: sakalamapyakalākalitāntaraṃ subhagadurbhagarūpadharaṃ vapuḥ / prakaṭayansahasaiva ca gopayan vilasatīha hi kālabalaṃ nṛṣu //
english: ?missing text?

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / asyoḍḍāmaralīlasya dūrāstasakalāpadaḥ / saṃsāre rājaputrasya kālasyākalitaujasaḥ //
english: Rama rejoined:—Time is a self-willed sportsman as a prince, who is inaccessible to dangers and whose powers are unlimited.

sanskrit: asyaivācarato dīnairmugdhairbhūtamṛgabrajaiḥ / ākheṭakaṃ jarjarite jagajjaṅgalajālake //
english: This world is as it were a forest and sporting ground of time, wherein the poor deluded worldlings are caught in his snare like bodies of wounded stags.

sanskrit: ekadeśollasaccāruvaḍavānalapaṅkajā / krīḍāpuṣkariṇī ramyā kalpakālamahārṇavaḥ //
english: The ocean of universal deluge is a pleasure-pond of time, and the submarine fires bursting therein as lotus flowers.

sanskrit: kaṭutiktāmlabhūtādyaiḥ sadadhikṣīrasāgaraiḥ / taireva taiḥ paryuṣitairjagadbhiḥ kalvavartanam //
english: Time makes his breakfast of this vapid and stale earth, flavoured with the milk and curd of the seas of those names.

sanskrit: caṇḍī caturasaṃcārā sarvamātṛgaṇānvitā / saṃsāravanavinyastā vyāghrī bhūtaughaghātinī //
english: His wife Chandi (Hecate) with her train of Matris (furies), ranges all about this wide world as a ferocious tigress.

sanskrit: jñadhvī karatale jñathvī pānapātrī rasānvitā / kamalotpalakahlāralolajālakamālitā //
english: The earth with her waters is like a bowl of wine in the hand of time, dressed and flavoured with all sorts of lilies and lotuses.

sanskrit: virāvī vikaṭāsphoṭo nṛsiṃho bhujapañjare / saṭāvikaṭapīnāṃsaḥ kṛtaḥ krīḍāśakuntakaḥ //
english: The lion with his huge body and startling mane, his loud roaring and tremendous groans, seems as a caged bird of sport in the hand of time.

sanskrit: alābuvīṇāmadhuraḥ śaradvyomalasacchaviḥ / devaḥ kila mahākālo līlākokilabālakaḥ //
english: The Mahakala like a playful young Kokila (cuckoo), appears in the figure of the blue autumnal sky, and warbling as sweet as the notes of a lute of gourd.

sanskrit: ajasrasphūrjitākāro vāntaduḥkhaśarāvaliḥ / abhāvanāmakodaṇḍaḥ parisphurati sarvataḥ //
english: The restless bow of death is found flinging its woeful arrows (darts of death) with ceaseless thunder claps on all sides.

sanskrit: anuttamastvadhikavilāsapaṇḍito bhramaccalanparivilasanvidārayan / jarajjagajjanitavilolamarkaṭaḥ parisphuradvapuriha kāla īhate //
english: This world is like a forest, wherein sorrows are ranging about as playful apes, and time like a sportive prince in this forest, is now roving, now walking, now playing and now killing his game.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca atraiva durvilāsānāṃ cūḍamaṇirihāparaḥ / karotyattīti loke'smindaivaṃ kālaśca kathyate //
english: Time stands the foremost of all deceitful players in this world. He acts the double parts of creation and destruction, and of action and fate.

sanskrit: kriyāmātrādṛte yasya svaparispandarūpiṇaḥ / nānyadālakṣyate rūpaṃ na karma na samīhitam //
english: Time has no other character but those of action and motion by which his existence is known to us, and which bind all beings.

sanskrit: teneyamakhilā bhūtasaṃtatiḥ paripelavā / tāpena himamāleva nītā vidhuratāṃ bhṛśam //
english: Fate is that which frustrates (the necessary consequences of) the acts of all created beings, as the solar heat serves to dissolve the conglomeration of snows.

sanskrit: yadidaṃ dṛśyate kiṃcijjagadābhogi maṇḍalam / tattasya nartanāgāramihāsāvatinṛtyati //
english: This wide world is the stage wherein the giddy mob dance about.

sanskrit: tṛtīyaṃ ca kṛtānteti nāma bibhratsudāruṇam / kāpālikavapurmattaṃ daivaṃ jagati nṛtyati //
english: Time has a third name of a terrifying nature known as Kritantah (Fate), who in the form of a Kapalika (one holding human skulls in his hand), dances about in the world.

sanskrit: nṛtyato hi kṛtāntasya nitāntamiva rāgiṇaḥ / nityaṃ niyatikāntāyāṃ mune paramakāmitā //
english: This dancing and loving Kritantah (Fate), is accompanied by his consort called Destiny to whom he is greatly attached.

sanskrit: śeṣaḥ śaśikalāśubhro gaṅgāvāhaśca tau tridhā / upavīte avīte ca ubhau saṃsāravakṣasi //
english: Time (as Siva), wears on his bosom of the world, the triplicate white and holy thread composed of the serpent named Ananta and the stream of Ganges, and the digit of the moon on his forehead.

sanskrit: candrārkamaṇḍale hemakaṭakau karamūlayoḥ / līlāsarasijaṃ haste brahmanbrahmāṇḍakarṇikā //
english: The sun and the moon are the golden armlets of time, who holds in his palm the mundane world as the paltry plaything of a nosegay.

sanskrit: tārābinducitaṃ lolapuṣkarāvartapallavam / ekārṇavapayodhau tamekamambaramambaram //
english: The firmament with its stars appears like a garment with coloured spots in it; the clouds called Pushkara and Avarta are as the skirts of that garment, which are washed by Time in the waters of the universal deluge.

sanskrit: evaṃrūpasya tasyāgre niyatirnityakāminī / anastamitasaṃrambhamārambhaiḥ parinṛtyati //
english: Before him, dances his beloved Destiny with all her arts for ever, to beguile the living that are fond of worldly enjoyments.

sanskrit: tasyā nartanalolāyā jaganmaṇḍapakoṭare / aruddhaspandarūpāyā āgamāpāyacañcure //
english: People hurry up and down to witness the dance of Destiny, whose unrestrained motion keeps them at work, and causes their repeated births and deaths.

sanskrit: cārubhūṣaṇamaṅgeṣu devalokāntarāvalī / āpātālaṃ nabholambaṃ kabarīmaṇḍalaṃ bṛhat //
english: The people of all the worlds are studded about her person as her ornaments, and the sky stretching from the heaven of gods to the infernal regions, serves for the veil on her head.

sanskrit: narakālī ca mañjīramālā kalakalojjvalā / protā duṣkṛtasūtreṇa pātālacaraṇe sthitā //
english: Her feet are planted in the infernal regions, and the hell-pits ring at her feet like trinkets, tied by the string of evil deeds or sins.

sanskrit: kastūrikātilakakaṃ kriyāsaṃkhyopakalpitam / citritaṃ citraguptena yame vadanapaṭṭake //
english: She is painted all over from head to foot by the god Chitra Gupta with ornamental marks prepared by her attendants (the deeds of men), and perfumed with the essence of those deeds.

sanskrit: kālāsyaṃ samupādāya kalpānteṣu kilākulā / nṛtyatyeṣā punardevī sphuṭacchailaghanāravam //
english: She dances and reels at the nod of her husband at the end of the Kalpas, and makes the mountains crack and crash at her foot-falls.

sanskrit: paścātprālambavibhrāntakaumārabhṛtabarhibhiḥ / netratrayavṛhadrandhrabhūribhāṅkārabhīṣaṇaiḥ //
english: Behind her dance the peacocks of the god Kumara; and Kala the god of death staring with his three wide open eyes, utters his hideous cries.

sanskrit: lambalolajaṭācandravikīrṇaharamūrdhabhiḥ / uccaraccārumandāragaurīkabaracāmaraiḥ //
english: Death dances about in the form of the five headed Hara, with the loosened braids of hair upon him; while Destiny in the form of Gauri, and her locks adorned with Mandara flowers keeps her pace with him.

sanskrit: uttāṇḍavācalākārabhairavodaratumbakaiḥ / raṇatsaśatarandhrendradehabhikṣākapālakaiḥ //
english: This Destiny in her war-dance, bears a capacious gourd representing her big belly, and her body is adorned with hundreds of hollow human skulls jingling like the alms-pots of the Kapali mendicants.

sanskrit: śuṣkaśārīrakhaṭvāṅgabharairāpūritāmbaram / bhīṣayatyātmanātmānaṃ sarvasaṃhārakāriṇī //
english: She has filled (reached) the sky with the emaciated skeleton of her body, and gets terrified at her all destructive figure.

sanskrit: viśvarūpaśiraścakracārupuṣkaramālayā / tāṇḍaveṣu vivalgantyā mahākalpeṣu rājate //
english: The skulls of the dead of various shapes adorn her body like a beautiful garland of lotuses, which keep hanging to and fro during her dance at the end of a Kalpa age.

sanskrit: pramattapuṣkarāvartaḍamaroḍḍāmarāravaiḥ / tasyāḥ kila palāyante kalpānte tumburādayaḥ //
english: The horrible roaring of the giddy clouds Pushkara and Avarta at the end of the Kalpa, serves to represent the beating of her Damaru drum, and put to flight the heavenly choir of Tumburu.

sanskrit: nṛtyato'ntaḥ kṛtāntasya candramaṇḍalabhāsinaḥ / tārakācandrikācāruvyomapicchāvacūlinaḥ //
english: As death dances along, the moon appears like his ear-ring, and the moon-beams and stars appear like his crest made of peacocks' feathers.

sanskrit: ekasmiñchravaṇe dīptā himavānasthimudrikā / apare ca mahāmeruḥ kāntā kāñcanakarṇikā //
english: The snow-capt Himalaya, appears like a circlet of bones in the upper loop of his right ear, and the mount Meru as a golden areola in that of the left.

sanskrit: atraiva kuṇḍale lole candrārkau gaṇḍamaṇḍale / lokālokācalaśreṇī sarvataḥ kaṭimekhalā //
english: Under their lobes are suspended the moon and the sun, as pendant ear-rings glittering over his cheeks. The mountain ranges called the lokaloka are fastened like chains around his waist.

sanskrit: itaścetaśca gacchantī vidyudvalayakarṇikā / anilāndolitā bhāti nīradāṃśukapaṭṭikā //
english: The lightnings are the bracelets and armlets of Destiny, which move to and fro as she dances along. The clouds are her wrappers that fly about her in the air.

sanskrit: musalaiḥ paṭṭiśaiḥ prāsaiḥ śūlaistomaramudgaraiḥ / tīkṣṇaiḥ kṣīṇajagadvāntakṛtāntairiva saṃbhṛtaiḥ //
english: Death is furnished with many weapons, as clubs, axes, missiles, spears, shovels, mallets and sharp swords, all of which are sure weapons of destruction.

sanskrit: saṃsārabandhanādīrghe pāśe kālakaracyute / śeṣabhogamahāsūtraprote mālāsya śobhate //
english: Mundane enjoyments are no other than long ropes dropped down by the hand of death, and keeping all mankind fast bound to the world; while the great thread of infinity (ananta) is worn by him as his wreath of flowers.

sanskrit: jīvollasanmakarikāratnatejobhirujjvalā / saptābdhikaṅkaṇaśreṇī bhujayorasya bhūṣaṇam //
english: The belts of the seven oceans are worn about the arms of Death as his bracelets resplendent with the living sea-animals, and the bright gems contained in their depths.

sanskrit: vyavahāramahāvartā sukhaduḥkhaparamparā / rajaḥpūrṇatamaḥśyāmā romālī tasya rājate //
english: The great vortices of customs, the successions of joy and grief, the excess of pride and the darkness of passions, form the streaks of hair on his body.

sanskrit: evaṃprāyaḥ sa kalpānte kṛtāntastāṇḍavodbhavām / upasaṃhṛtya nṛtyehāṃ sṛṣṭvā saha maheśvaram //
english: After the end of the world, he ceases to dance, and creates anew all things from the lowest animal that lives in the earth, to the highest Brahma and Siva.

sanskrit: punarlāsyamayīṃ nṛtyalīlāṃ sargasvarūpiṇīm / tanotīmāṃ jarāśokaduḥkhābhibhavabhūṣitām //
english: Destiny as an actress, acts by turns her parts of creation and destruction, diversified by scenes of old age, sorrow and misery.

sanskrit: bhūyaḥ karoti bhuvanāni vanāntarāṇi lokāntarāṇi janajālakakalpanāṃ ca / ācāracārukalanāmacalāṃ calāṃ ca paṅkādyathārbhakajano racanāmakhinnaḥ //
english: Time repeatedly creates the worlds and their woods, with the different abodes and localities teeming with population. He forms the moveable and immovable substances, establishes customs and again dissolves them, as boys make their dolls of clay and break them soon afterwards.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / vṛtte'sminnevameteṣāṃ kālādīnāṃ mahāmune / saṃsāranāmni kaivāsthā mādṛśānāṃ vadatviha //
english: Rama said:—Such being the all destructive conduct of time and others (as already described), what confidence, O great sage, can men like me, have upon them?

sanskrit: vikrītā iva tiṣṭhāma etairdaivādibhirvayam / mune prapañcaracanairmugdhā vanamṛgā iva //
english: We all remain here, O sage! as slaves sold to Fate and Destiny, and are deceived by their allurements as beasts of the forest.

sanskrit: eṣo'nāryasamāmnāyaḥ kālaḥ kavalanonmukhaḥ / jagatyavirataṃ lokaṃ pātayatyāpadarṇave //
english: This Fate whose conduct is so very inhuman, is always up to devour all beings, and is incessantly throwing men into the sea of troubles.

sanskrit: dahatyantardurāśābhirdevo dāruṇaceṣṭayā / lokamuṣṇaprakāśābhijvālābhirdahano yathā //
english: He is led by his malicious attempts to inflame the mind with inordinary desires, as the fire raises its flames to burn down a habitation.

sanskrit: dhṛtiṃ vidhurayatyeṣā maryādārūpavallabhā / strītvātsvabhāvacapalā niyatirniyatonmukhī //
english: Destiny the faithful and obedient wife of Fate, is naturally fickle on account of her being a female, and is always bent on mischief and disturbing the patience.

sanskrit: grasate'virataṃ bhūtajālaṃ sarpa ivānilam / kṛtāntaḥ karkaśācāro jarāṃ nītvā'jaraṃ vapuḥ //
english: As the heinous serpent feeds upon the air, so does cruel Death ever swallow the living. He ripens the body with old age to create his zest, and then devours all animals warm with life.

sanskrit: yamo nirghṛṇarājendro nārtaṃ nāmānukampate / sarvabhūtadayodāro jano durlabhatāṃ gataḥ //
english: Death is called a relentless tyrant, having no pity even for the sick and weak; nor any regard for any one in any state of life.

sanskrit: sarvā eva mune phalguvibhavā bhūtajātayaḥ / duḥkhāyaiva durantāya dāruṇā bhogabhūmayaḥ //
english: Every one in this world is fond of affluence and pleasures, not knowing that these are only calculated to lead him to his ruin.

sanskrit: āyuratyantacapalaṃ mṛtyurekāntaniṣṭhuraḥ / tāruṇyaṃ cātitaralaṃ bālyaṃ jaḍatayā hṛtam //
english: Life is very unsteady. Death is very cruel. Youth is very frail and fickle, and boyhood is full of dullness and insensibility.

sanskrit: kalākalaṅkito loko bandhavo bhavabandhanam / bhogā bhavamahārogāstṛṣṇāśca mṛgatṛṣṇikāḥ //
english: Man is defiled by his worldliness, his friends are ties to the world, his enjoyments are the greatest of his diseases in life, and his avarice and ambition are the mirage that always allures him.

sanskrit: śatravaścendriyāṇyeva satyaṃ yātamasatyatām / praharatyātmanaivātmā manasaiva mano ripuḥ //
english: Our very senses are our enemies, before which even truth appears as falsehood; the mind is the enemy of the mind and self is the enemy of self.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāraḥ kalaṅkāya buddhayaḥ paripelavāḥ / kriyā duṣphaladāyinyo līlāḥ strīniṣṭhatāṃ gatāḥ //
english: Self-esteem is stained (with the name of selfishness), intelligence is blamed for its fallaciousness, our actions are attended with bad results, and our pleasures tend only to effeminacy.

sanskrit: vāñchāviṣayaśālinyaḥ saccamatkṛtayaḥ kṣatāḥ / nāryo doṣapatākinyo rasā nīrasatāṃ gatāḥ //
english: All our desires are directed to enjoyments; our love of truth is lost; our women are the ensigns of vice, and all that were once so sweet, have become tasteless and vapid.

sanskrit: vastvavastutayā jñātaṃ dattaṃ cittamahaṃkṛtau / abhāvavedhitā bhāvā bhāvānto nādhigamyate //
english: Things that are not real, are believed as real, and have become the cause of our pride, by hardening us in untruth, and keeping us from the light of truth.

sanskrit: tapyate kevalaṃ sādho matirākulitāntarā / rāgarogo vilasati virāgo nopagacchati //
english: My mind is at a loss to think what to do; it regrets at its increased appetite for pleasure, and for want of that self-denial.

sanskrit: rajoguṇahatā dṛṣṭistamaḥ saṃparivardhate / na cādhigamyate sattvaṃ tattvamatyantadūrataḥ //
english: My sight is dimmed by the dust of sensuality: the darkness of self-esteem prevails upon me: the purity of mind is never reached to, and truth is far off from me.

sanskrit: sthitirasthiratāṃ yātā mṛtirāgamanonmukhī / dhṛtirvaidhuryamāyātā ratirnityamavastuni //
english: Life is become uncertain and death is always advancing nigh; my patience is disturbed, and there is an increased appetite for whatever is false.

sanskrit: matirmāndyena malinā pātaikaparamaṃ vapuḥ / jvalatīva jarā dehe pratisphurati duṣkṛtam //
english: The mind is soiled by dullness, and the body is cloyed with surfeit and ready to fall; old age exults over the body, and sins are conspicuous at every step.

sanskrit: yatnena yāti yuvatā dūre sajjanasaṃgatiḥ / gatirna vidyate kācitkvacinnodeti satyatā //
english: Youth flies fast away with all our care to preserve it; the company of the good is at a distance; the light of truth shines from no where;and I can have recourse to nothing in this world.

sanskrit: mano vimuhyatīvāntarmuditā dūratāṃ gatā / nojjvalā karuṇodeti dūrādāyāti nīcatā //
english: The mind is stupified within itself, and its contentment has fled from it: there is no rise of enlightened sentiments in it, and meanness makes its advance to it from a distance.

sanskrit: dhīratā'dhīratāmeti pātotpātaparo janaḥ / sulabho durjanāśleṣo durlabhaḥ satsamāgamaḥ //
english: Patience is converted into impatience; man is liable to the states of birth and death; good company is rare, but bad company is ever within the reach of every body.

sanskrit: āgamāpāyino bhāvā bhāvanā bhavabandhanī / nīyate kevalaṃ kvāpi nityaṃ bhūtaparamparā //
english: All individual existences are liable to appear and disappear; all desires are chains to the world, and all worldly beings are ever seen to be led away per force where no body can tell.

sanskrit: diśo'pi hi na dṛśyante deśo'pyanyāpadeśabhāk / śailā api viśīryante kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
english: What reliance can there be on human life, when the points of the compass become indistinct and undiscernible; when the countries and places change their positions and names, and when mountains even are liable to be dilapidated?

sanskrit: adyate sattayāpi dyaurbhu'vana cāpi ūyate / dharāpi yāti vaidhuryaṃ kevāsthā mādṛśe jane //
english: What reliance can there be on man, when the heavens are swallowed in infinity, when this world is absorbed in nothingness, and the very earth loses her stability?

sanskrit: śuṣyantyapi samudrāśca śīryante tārakā api / siddhā api vinaśyanti kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
english: What reliance can there be on men like ourselves, when the very seas are liable to be dried up, when the stars are doomed to fade away and disappear, and when the most perfect of beings are liable to dissolution?

sanskrit: dānavā api dīryante dhruvo'pyadhruvajīvitaḥ / amarā api māryante kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
english: What reliance can there be on men like us, when even the demigods are liable to destruction, when the polar star is known to change its place, and when the immortal gods are doomed to mortality?

sanskrit: śakro'pyākramyate vakrairyamo'pi hi niyamyate / vāyurapyetyavāyutvaṃ kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
english: What reliance can there be on men like us, when Indra is doomed to be defeated by demons; when even death is hindered from his aim, and when the current air ceases to breathe?

sanskrit: somo'pi vyomatāṃ yāti mārtaṇḍo'pyeti khaṇḍatām / magnatāmagnirapyeti kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
english: What reliance can there be on men like us, when the very moon is to vanish with the sky, when the very sun is to be split into pieces, and when fire itself is to become frigid and cold?

sanskrit: parameṣṭhyapi niṣṭhāvānhriyate hīrarapyajaḥ / bhavo'pyabhāvamāyāti kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
english: What reliance can there be on men like us, when the very Hari and Brahma are to be absorbed into the Great One, and when Siva himself is to be no more.

sanskrit: kālaḥ saṃkālyate yena niyatiścāpi nīyate / khamapyālīyate'nantaṃ kaivāsthā mādṛśe jane //
english: What reliance can there be on men like us, when the duration of time comes to be counted, when Destiny is destined to her final destiny, and when all vacuity loses itself in infinity?

sanskrit: aśrāvyāvācyadurdarśatattvenājñātamūrtinā / bhuvanāni viḍambyante kenacidbhramadāyinā //
english: That which is inaudible, unspeakable, invisible, and unknowable in his real form, displays to us these wondrous worlds by some fallacy.

sanskrit: ahaṃkārakalāmetya sarvatrāntaravāsinā / na so'sti triṣu lokeṣu yasteneha na bādhyate //
english: No one conscious of himself (his egoism), can disown his subjection to that Being, that dwells in the hearts of every one.

sanskrit: śilāśailakavapreṣu sāśvabhūto divākaraḥ / vanapāṣāṇavannityamavaśaḥ paricodyate //
english: This sun said:—the lord of worlds, is impelled (by that power) to run over hills, rocks and fields, like an inert piece of stone, hurled down from a mountain and borne away by a current stream.

sanskrit: dharāgolakamantasthasurāsuragaṇāspadam / veṣṭyate dhiṣṇyacakreṇa pakvākṣoṭamiva tvacā //
english: This globe of earth, the seat of all the Suras and Asuras, and surrounded by the luminous sphere in the manner of a walnut covered by its hard crust, subsists under His command.

sanskrit: divi devā bhuvi narāḥ pātāleṣu ca bhoginaḥ / kalpitāḥ kalpamātreṇa nīyante jarjarāṃ daśām //
english: The Gods in the heavens, the men on earth and the serpents in the nether world, are brought into existence and led to decay by His will only.

sanskrit: kāmaśca jagadīśānaraṇalabdhaparākramaḥ / akrameṇaiva vikrānto lokamākramya valgati //
english: Kama (Cupid) that is arbitrarily powerful, and has forcibly overpowered on all the living world, has derived his unconquerable might from the Lord of worlds.

sanskrit: vasanto mattamātaṅgo madaiḥ kusumavarṣaṇaiḥ / āmoditakakupcakraśceto nayati cāpalam //
english: As the heated elephant regales the air with his spirituous exudation, so does the spring perfume the air with his profusion of flowers, unsettling the minds of men.

sanskrit: anuraktāṅganālolalocanālokitākṛti / svasthīkartuṃ manaḥ śakto na viveko mahānapi //
english: So are the loose glances of loving damsels directed to inflict deep wounds in the heart of man, which his best reason is unable to heal.

sanskrit: paropakārakāriṇyā parārtiparitaptayā / buddha eva sukhī manye svātmaśītalayā dhiyā //
english: One whose best endeavour is always to do good to others, and who feels for others' woes, is really intelligent and happy under the influence of his cool judgement.

sanskrit: utpannadhvaṃsinaḥ kālavaḍavānalapātinaḥ / saṃkhyātuṃ kena śakyante kallolā jīvitāmbudhau //
english: Who can count the number of beings resembling the waves of the ocean, and on whom death has been darting the submarine fire of destruction.

sanskrit: sarva eva narā mohāddurāśāpāśapāśinaḥ / doṣagulmakasāraṅgā viśīrṇā janmajaṅgale / saṃkṣīyate jagati janmaparamparāsu lokasya tairiha kukarmabhirāyuretat //
english: All mankind are deluded to entrap themselves in the snare of avarice, and to be afflicted with all evils in life, as the deer entangled in the thickets of a jungle.

sanskrit: ākāśapādapalatākṛtapāśakalpaṃ yeṣāṃ phalaṃ nahi vicāravido'pi vidmaḥ //
english: The term of human life in this world, is decreased in each generation in proportion to (the increase of their wicked acts). The desire of fruition is as vain as the expectation of reaping fruits from a creeper growing in the sky: yet I know not why men of reason would not understand this truth.

sanskrit: adyotsavo'yamṛtureṣa tatheha yātrā te bandhavaḥ sukhamidaṃ saviśeṣabhogam / itthaṃ mudhaiva kalayansuvikalpajālamālolapelavamatirgalatīha lokaḥ //
english: This is a day of festivity, a season of joy and a time of procession. Here are our friends, here the pleasures and here the variety of our entertainments. Thus do men of vacant minds amuse themselves with weaving the web of their desires, until they become extinct.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / anyacca tātā'titarāmaramye manorame ceha jagatsvarūpe / na kiṃcidāyāti tadarthajātaṃ yenātiviśrāntimupaiti cetaḥ //
english: Rama said:—O sage! this seemingly pleasing but actually unpleasant world, has nothing in it that is productive of such a thing as can afford tranquility to the soul.

sanskrit: bālye gate kalpitakelilole manomṛge dāradarīṣu jīrṇe / śarīrake jarjaratāṃ prayāte vidūyate kevalameva lokaḥ //
english: After the playful boyhood is over, the mind wastes itself in the society of women like the deer fallen in a cavern, then the body bends down under old age, and the man has only to grieve.

sanskrit: jarātuṣārābhihatāṃ śarīrasarojinīṃ dūratare vimucya / kṣaṇādgate jīvitacañcarīke janasya saṃsārasaro'vaśuṣkam //
english: As the body is stricken with the frost of old age, its beauty flies afar from it like the bloom of the fading lotus, and then the fountain of man's worldliness is at once dried up.

sanskrit: yadā yadā pākamupaiti nūnaṃ tadā tadeyaṃ ratimātanoti / jarābharā'nalpanavaprasūnā vijarjarā kāyalatā narāṇām //
english: As the body gets towards its decline, so much doth death rejoice in it. The body grows lean with grey hairs upon the head, just as a creeper fades away with the flowers upon it.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇānadī sāratarapravāhagrastākhilānantapadārthajātā / taṭasthasaṃtoṣasuvṛkṣamūlanikāṣadakṣā vahatīha loke //
english: All living creatures are borne away by the stream of avarice, which upsets the tree of contentment growing on the bank and flows on for ever in this world.

sanskrit: śārīranauścarmanibandhabaddhā bhavāmbudhāvālulitā bhramantī / praloḍyate pañcabhirindriyākhyairadhobhavantī makarairadhīrā //
english: Human body is like a vessel covered with skin; and glides over the ocean of the world (without its helmsman of reason). It is tossed about by sensual pleasures, and goes down under the water by the pressure of its whale-like passions.

sanskrit: tṛṣṇālatākānanacāriṇo'mī śākhāśataṃ kāmamahīruheṣu / paribhramantaḥ kṣapayanti kālaṃ manomṛgā no phalamāpnuvanti //
english: The world is a wilderness abounding in creepers of avarice and trees of sensuality, with hundreds of desires as their branches. Our minds like monkeys pass their time in roving about this forest without getting the fruits.

sanskrit: kṛcchreṣu dūrāstaviṣādamohāḥ svāsthyeṣu notsiktamanobhirāmāḥ / sudurlabhāḥ saṃprati sundarībhiḥ ranāhatāntaḥkaraṇā mahāntaḥ //
english: Those that do not yield to grief in troubles, that are not elated with prosperity, nor smitten at heart by women, are rare in this world.

sanskrit: taranti mātaṅgaghaṭātaraṅgaṃ raṇāmbudhiṃ ye mayi te na śūrāḥ / śūrāsta eveha manastaraṅgaṃ dehendriyāmbhodhimimaṃ taranti //
english: Those who fight boldly in the battle fields and withstand the war-elephants, are not so very brave in my opinion, as those who withstand the surges of the mind amidst the streams of carnal appetites.

sanskrit: akliṣṭaparyantaphalābhirāmā na dṛśyate kasyacideva kācit / kriyādurāśāhatacittavṛttiryāmetya viśrāntimupaiti lokaḥ //
english: I see no such deeds in the world which endure to the last (or final emancipation) of men. Actions proceeding from a desire of fruition in fools, serve only for their restlessness on earth.

sanskrit: kīrtyā jagaddikkuharaṃ pratāpaiḥ śriyā gṛhaṃ sattvabalena lakṣmīm / ye pūrayantyakṣatadhairyabandhā na te jagatyāṃ sulabhā mahāntaḥ //
english: Such men are rare in the world, that have filled the corners of the world with their fame and valour, who have filled their houses with true riches acquired by honest means and an unwavering patience.

sanskrit: apyantarasthaṃ giriśailabhittervajrālayābhyantarasaṃsthitaṃ vā / sarvaṃ samāyānti sasiddhivegāḥ sarvāḥ śriyaḥ santatamāpadaśca //
english: Good and bad fortune always overtake a man, even if he were living in an aperture of the rock or within the walls of mountains, or even if he were enclosed within an iron built closet.

sanskrit: putrāśca dārāśca dhanaṃ ca buddhyā prakalpyate tāta rasāyanābham / sarvaṃ tu tannopakarotyathānte yatrātiramyā viṣamūrcchanaiva //
english: Our sons and riches are mere objects of delight to us. It is as erroneous to suppose them to be of any good to us at the end, as to expect any benefit from the decoction of poison.

sanskrit: viṣādayukto viṣamāmavasthā mupāgataḥ kāyavayovasāne / bhāvānsmaransvāniha dharmariktān janturjarāvāniha dahyate'ntaḥ //
english: Old people being reduced to calamitous circumstances at the pitiable state of the decay of their bodies and decline of life, have greatly to be tormented at the thoughts of the impious deeds.

sanskrit: kāmārthadharmāptikṛtāntarābhiḥ kriyābhirādau divasāni nītvā / cetaścaladbarhiṇapicchalolaṃ viśrāntimāgacchatu kena puṃsaḥ //
english: Men having passed their early days in the gratification of their desires and other worldly pursuits at the expense of the acts of virtue and piety, are as much troubled with anxieties at the end, that their minds are seized with a tremor like that of the plumage of a peacock shaken by the breeze. How then can a man attain to tranquility at any time?

sanskrit: purogatairapyanavāptarūpaistaraṅgiṇītuṅgataraṅgakalpaiḥ / kriyāphalairdaivavaśādupetairviḍambyate bhinnarucirhi lokaḥ //
english: Wealth whether forthcoming or unattainable, whether got by labour or given by fortune, is all as deceitful to the worldly minded, as the high waters of rivers.

sanskrit: imānyamūnīhi vibhāvitāni kāryāṇyaparyantamanoramāṇi / janasya jāyājanarañjanena javājjarāntaṃ jarayanti cetaḥ //
english: That such and such desirable acts are to be done, are the constant thoughts of men, who desire to please their sons and wives, until they are worn out with age and become crazy in their minds.

sanskrit: parṇāni jīrṇāni yathā tarūṇāṃ sametya janmāśu layaṃ prayānti / tathaiva lokāḥ svavivekahīnāḥ sametya gacchanti kuto'pyahobhiḥ //
english: Like leaves on trees that grow to fall, and falling make room for others to shoot forth, are those men who devoid of reason, die away daily to be born again.

sanskrit: itastato dūrataraṃ vihṛtya praviśya gehaṃ divasāvasāne / vivekilokāśrayasādhukarma rikte'hni rātrau ka upaiti nidrām //
english: Men having travelled here and there and far and near, return to their homes at the end of the day; but none of them can have rest by day or night, except the virtuous few that live by honest dealings.

sanskrit: vidrāvite śatrujane samaste samāgatāyāmabhitaśca lakṣmyām / sevyanta etāni sukhāni yāvattāvatsamāyāti kuto'pi mṛtyuḥ //
english: After quelling his enemies and getting enough of riches in his clutches, the rich man just sits down to enjoy his gains; when death comes upon him, and interrupts his joy.

sanskrit: kuto'pi saṃvardhitatuccharūpairbhāvairamībhiḥ kṣaṇanaṣṭadṛṣṭaiḥ / viloḍyamānā janatā jagatyāṃ navetyupāyātamaho na pātam //
english: Seeing the vile trash of worldly gains earned and accumulated by the basest means to be but transitory, the infatuated mob do not perceive their approaching dissolution.

sanskrit: priyāsubhiḥ kālamukhaṃ kriyante janaiḍakāste hatakarmabaddhāḥ / yaiḥ pīnatāmeva balādupetya śarīrabādhena na te bhavanti //
english: Men loving their own lives, and making mouths at the demise of others, are like a herd of sheep bound to the stake, and staring at the slaughter of their fellows, yet feeding themselves to fall as fattened victims to death.

sanskrit: ajasramāgacchati satvaraivamanārataṃ gacchati satvaraiva / kuto'pi lolā janatā jagatyāṃ taraṅgamālā kṣaṇabhaṅgureva //
english: The multitude of people on earth, is ever seen to appear in and disappear from it as fast as the passing waves of the sea, but who can tell whence they come and whither they return.

sanskrit: prāṇāpahāraikaparā narāṇāṃ mano manohāritayā haranti / raktacchadāścañcalaṣaṭpadākṣyo viṣadrumālolalatāḥ striyaśca //
english: Women are as delicate as poisonous creepers, that with their red petaled lips and garments, and their eyes as busy as fluttering bees, are killers of mankind and stealers of their ravished hearts.

sanskrit: ito'nyataścopagatā mudhaiva samānasaṃketanibaddhabhāvā / yātrāsamāsaṃgasamā narāṇāṃ kalatramitravyavahāramāyā //
english: Men are as passengers in a procession, repairing from this side and that to join at the place of their meeting. Such is the delusive union of our wives and friends here.

sanskrit: pradīpaśāntiṣviva bhuktabhūridaśāsvatisnehanibandhanīṣu / saṃsāramālāsu calācalāsu na jñāyate tattvamatāttvikīṣu //
english: As the burning and extinguishing of the lamp depend on the wick and its moistening oil; so does our course in this transitory world (depend on our acts and affections only). Nobody knows the true cause of this mysterious existence.

sanskrit: saṃsārasaṃrambhakucakrikeyaṃ prāvṛṭpayobudbudabhaṅgurapi / asāvadhānasya janasya buddhau cirasthirapratyayamātanoti //
english: The revolution of the world is comparable with that of the potter's wheel and the floating bubbles of rain water; that appear to be lasting to the ignorant observer only.

sanskrit: śobhojjvalā daivavaśādvinaṣṭā guṇāḥ sthitāḥ saṃprati jarjaratve / āśvāsanādūrataraṃ prayātā janasya hemanta ivāmbujasya //
english: The blooming beauty and graces (of youth), are destined to be snatched away at the approach of old age. The youthful hopes also of men fly at a distance like the bloom of lotus buds in winter.

sanskrit: punaḥpunardaivavaśādupetya svadehabhāreṇa kṛtopakāraḥ / vilūyate yatra taruḥ kuṭhārairāśvāsane tatra hi kaḥ prasaṅgaḥ //
english: The tree which is ordained to be useful to mankind by the loads of fruits and flowers that it bears upon its body, is fated also to be hewn down by the cruel axe at last. How then can beneficent men expect to avoid the cruel hand of death.

sanskrit: manoramasyāpyatidoṣavṛtterantarviṃghātāya samutthitasya / viṣadrumasyeva janasya saṅgādāsādyate saṃprati mūrcchanaiva //
english: Society with relatives is (of all others) as perilous as that of a poisonous plant; it is pleasant for its domestic affections, which are in reality but delusions of the soul.

sanskrit: kāstā dṛśo yāsu na santi doṣāḥ kāstā diśo yāsu na duḥkhadāhaḥ / kāstāḥ prajā yāsu na bhaṅguratvaṃ kāstāḥ kriyā yāsu na nāma māyā //
english: What is that thing in the world, which has no fault in it; and what is that which does not afflict or grieve us; what being is born that is not subjected to death, and what are those acts that are free from deceit?

sanskrit: kalpābhidhānakṣaṇajīvino hi kalpaughasaṃkhyākalane viriñcayāḥ / ataḥ kalāśālini kālajāle laghutvadīrghatvadhiyo'pyasatyāḥ //
english: Those living a Kalpa age are reckoned as short-lived, compared with those living for many Kalpas, and they again are so in respect to Brahma. Hence the parts of time being all finite, the ideas of their length or shortness are altogether false.

sanskrit: sarvatra pāṣāṇamayā mahīdhrā mṛdā mahī dārubhireva vṛkṣāḥ / māṃsairjanāḥ pauruṣabaddhabhāvā nāpūrvamastīha vikārahīnam //
english: Things that are called mountains are made of rocks, those that are called trees are made of wood, and those that are made of flesh are called animals, and man is the best of them. But they are all made of matter, and doomed to death and decay.

sanskrit: ālokyate cetanayā'nuviddhā payonubaddho'stanayo nabhaḥ sthāḥ / pṛthagvibhāgena padārthalakṣmyā etajjagannetaradasti kiṃcit //
english: Many things appear to be endued with intelligence, and the heavenly bodies seem to be full of water; but physicists have found out by analysis that, there is no other thing any where except (minutiae of) matter.

sanskrit: camatkṛtiśceha manasvilokacetaścamatkārakarī narāṇām / svapne'pi sādho viṣayaṃ kadācitkeṣāṃcidabhyeti na citrarūpā //
english: It is no wonder that this (unreal world) should appear a miraculous (reality) to the wise, and seem marvelously striking in the minds of mankind; since the visions in our dreams also appear so very fascinating to every one in their state of dreaming.

sanskrit: adyāpi yāte'pi ca kalpanāyā ākāśavallīphalavanmahattve / udeti no lobhalavāhatānāmudāravṛttāntamayī kathaiva //
english: Those that are corrupted in their greediness (after worldly enjoyments), will not even in their old age, receive the sermons on their eternal concerns, which they think to be false chimeras as those of a flower or a creeper growing in the sky.

sanskrit: ādātumicchanpadamuttamānāṃ svacetasaivāpahato'dya lokaḥ / patatyaśaṅkaṃ paśuradrikūṭādānīlavallīphalavāñchayaiva //
english: People are still deluded in their minds in wishing to attain the state of their superiors; but they fall down still lower like beasts (goats) from the top of a hill, in wishing to lay hold on the fruits of a verdant creeper out of their reach.

sanskrit: avāntaranyastanirarthakāṃśacchāyālatāpatraphalaprasūnāḥ / śarīra eva kṣatasaṃpadaśca śvabhradrumā adyatanā narāśca //
english: Young men spending their wealth in personal gratifications, are as useless as plants growing in the bowels of a deep and inaccessible cavern, which spread their fruits and flowers, leaves and branches and their shades to the use of nobody.

sanskrit: kvacijjanā mārdavasundareṣu kvacitkaṭhoreṣu ca saṃcaranti / deśāntarāleṣu nirantareṣu vanāntakhaṇḍeṣviva kṛṣṇasārāḥ //
english: Men are found to resemble the black antelopes (in their wanderings):some of them roving about the sweet, soft and beautiful sceneries of the country, and others roaming in sterile tracts and parts of boundless forests.

sanskrit: dhāturnavāni divasaṃ prati bhīṣaṇāni ramyāṇi vā vilulitāntatamākulāni / kāryāṇi kaṣṭaphalapākahatodayāni vismāpayanti na śavasya manāṃsi keṣām //
english: The daily and diversified acts of nature are all pernicious in their nature; they appear pleasant and ravishing to the heart for a time, but are attended with pain in the end, and fill the mind of the wise with dismay.

sanskrit: janaḥ kāmāsakto vividhakukalāceṣṭanaparaḥ sa tu svapne'pyasmiñjagati sulabho nādya sujanaḥ / kriyā duḥkhāsaṅgā'vidhuravidhurā nūnamakhilā na jāne netavyā kathamiva daśā jīvitamayī //
english: Man is addicted to greediness, and is prone to a variety of wicked shifts and plots; a good man is not now to be seen even in a dream, and there is no act which is free from difficulty. I know not how to pass this state of human life.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / yaccedaṃ dṛśyate kiṃcijjagatsthāvarajaṃgamam / tatsarvamasthiraṃ brahmansvapnasaṃgamasaṃnibham //
english: Rama said:—Whatever we see of all moveable or immovable things in this world, they are all as evanescent as things viewed in a dream.

sanskrit: śuṣkasāgarasaṃkāśo nikhāto yo'dya dṛśyate / sa prātarabhrasaṃvīto nagaḥ saṃpadyate mune //
english: The hollow desert that appears as the dried bed of a sea to-day, will be found to-morrow to be a running flood by the accumulation of rain-water in it.

sanskrit: yo vanavyūhavistīrṇo vilīḍhagagano mahān / dinaireva sa yātyurvīsamatāṃ kūpatāṃ ca vā //
english: What is to-day a mountain reaching the sky and with extensive forests on it, is in course of time levelled to the ground, and is afterwards dug into pit.

sanskrit: yadaṅgamadya saṃvītaṃ kauśeyasragvilepanaiḥ / digambaraṃ tadeva śvo dūre viśaritā'vaṭe //
english: The body that is clothed to-day with garments of silk, and decorated with garlands and fragrance, is to be cast away naked into a ditch to-morrow.

sanskrit: yatrādya nagaraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vicitrācāracañcalam / tatraivodeti divasaiḥ saṃśūnyāraṇyadharmatā //
english: What is seen to be a city to-day, and busy with the bustle of various occupations, passes in course of a few days into the condition of an uninhabited wilderness.

sanskrit: yaḥ pumānadya tejasvī maṇḍalānyadhitiṣṭhati / sa bhasmakūṭatāṃ rājandivasairadhigacchati //
english: The man who is very powerful to-day and presides over principalities, is reduced in a few days to a heap of ashes.

sanskrit: araṇyānī mahābhīmā yā nabhomaṇḍalopamā / patākācchāditākāśā saiva saṃpadyate purī //
english: The very forest which is so formidable to-day and appears as blue as the azure skies, turns to be a city in the course of time, with its banners hoisted in the air.

sanskrit: yā latāvalitā bhīmā bhātyadya vipināvalī / divasaireva sā yāti punarmarumahīpadam //
english: What is (to-day) a formidable jungle of thick forests, turns in time to be a table-land as on the mount Meru.

sanskrit: salilaṃ sthalatāṃ yāti sthalībhavati vāribhūḥ / viparyasyati sarvaṃ hi sakāṣṭhāmbutṛṇaṃ jagat //
english: Water becomes land and land becomes water. Thus the world composed of wood, grass and water becomes otherwise with all its contents in course of time.

sanskrit: anityaṃ yauvanaṃ bālyaṃ śarīraṃ dravyasaṃcayāḥ / bhāvādbhāvāntaraṃ yānti taraṅgavadanāratam //
english: Our boyhood and youth, bodies and possessions are all but transient things, and they change from one state to another, as the ever fluctuating waves of the ocean.

sanskrit: vātāntardīpakaśikhālolaṃ jagati jīvitam / taḍitsphuraṇasaṃkāśā padārthaśrīrjagatrtraye //
english: Our lives in this (mortal) world, are as unsteady as the flame of a lamp placed at the window, and the splendour of all the objects in the three worlds, is as flickering as the flashing of the lightning.

sanskrit: viparyāsamiyaṃ yāti bhūribhūtaparamparā / bījarāśirivājasraṃ pūryamāṇaḥ punaḥpunaḥ //
english: As a granary stored with heaps of grains is exhausted by its continued waste, so is the stock of life spent away by its repeated respirations.

sanskrit: manaḥpavanaparyastabhūribhūtarajaḥpaṭā / pātotpātaparāvartaparābhinayabhūṣitā //
english: The mind of man is as fluctuating as a flag waving in the air and filled with the dust of sin, to indicate its wavering between the paths of heaven and hell.

sanskrit: ālakṣyate sthitiriyaṃ jāgatī janitabhramā / nṛttāveśavivṛtteva saṃsārārabhaṭīnaṭī //
english: The existence of this delusive world, is as the appearance of an actress on the stage, shuffling her vests as she trudges along in her dancing.

sanskrit: gandharvanagarākāraviparyāsavidhāyinī / apāṅgabhaṅgurodāravyavahāramanoramā //
english: It's scenes are as changeful and fascinating as those of a magic city; and its dealings as bewitching and momentary as the glances of a giggling girl.

sanskrit: taḍittaralamālokamātanvānā punaḥpunaḥ / saṃsāraracanā rājannṛttasakteva rājate //
english: The stage of the world presents us a scene of continued dancing (of the sorceress of deception), and the deceptive glances of her eyes resembling the fleeting flashes of lightning.

sanskrit: divasāste mahāntaste saṃpadastāḥ kriyāśca tāḥ / sarvaṃ smṛtipathaṃ yātaṃ yāmo vayamapi kṣaṇāt //
english: The days, the great men, their hey-days and deeds (that are past and gone), are now retained in our memory only, and such must be our cases also in a short time.

sanskrit: pratyahaṃ kṣayamāyāti pratyahaṃ jāyate punaḥ / adyāpi hatarūpāyā nānto'syā dagdhasaṃsṛteḥ //
english: Many things are going to decay and many coming anew day by day; and there is yet no end of this accursed course of events in this ever-changeful world.

sanskrit: tiryaktvaṃ puruṣā yānti tiryañco naratāmapi / devāścādevatāṃ yānti kimiveha vibho sthiram //
english: Men degenerate into lower animals, and those again rise to humanity (by metempsychosis), gods become no-gods, and there is nothing that remains the same.

sanskrit: racayanraśmijālena rātryahāni punaḥpunaḥ / ativāhya raviḥ kālo vināśāvadhimīkṣate //
english: The sun displays every thing to light by his rays, and watches over the rotations of days and nights, to witness like time the dissolution of all things.

sanskrit: brahmā viṣṇuśca rudraśca sarvā vā bhūtajātayaḥ / nāśamevānudhāvanti salilānīva vāḍavam //
english: The gods Brahma, Vishnu and Siva and all material productions, are reduced to nothingness, like the submarine fire subsiding under the waters of the deep.

sanskrit: dyauḥ kṣamā vāyurākāśaṃ parvatāḥ sarito diśaḥ / vināśavāḍavasyaitatsarvaṃ saṃśuṣkamindhanam //
english: The heaven, the earth, the air, the sky, the mountains, the rivers, and all the quarters of the globe, are subject to destruction like the dry fuel by the all-destroying fire of the last day.

sanskrit: dhanāni bāndhavā bhṛtyā mitrāṇi vibhavāśca ye / vināśabhayabhītasya sarvaṃ nīrasatāṃ gatam //
english: Riches and relatives, friends, servants and affluence, are of no pleasure to him who is in constant dread of death.

sanskrit: svadante tāvadevaite bhāvā jagati dhīmate / yāvatsmṛtipathaṃ yāti na vināśakurākṣasaḥ //
english: All these are so long delightful to a sensible man, as the monster of death does not appear before the eye of his mind.

sanskrit: kṣaṇamaiśvaryamāyāti kṣaṇameti daridratām / kṣaṇaṃ vigatarogatvaṃ kṣaṇamāgatarogatām //
english: We have prosperity at one moment, succeeded by adversity at another; so we have health at one time, followed by sickness soon after.

sanskrit: pratikṣaṇaviparyāsadāyinā nihatātmanā / jagadbhrameṇa ke nāma dhīmanto hi na mohitāḥ //
english: What intelligent being is there, that is not misled by these delusions of the world, which represent things otherwise than what they are, and serve to bewilder the mind?

sanskrit: tamaḥpaṅkasamālabdhaṃ kṣaṇamākāśamaṇḍalam / kṣaṇa kanakaniṣyandakomalālokasundaram //
english: (The world is as varying) as the face of the skies; it is now as black as dark clay, and in the next moment bright with the golden hues of fair light.

sanskrit: kṣaṇaṃ jaladanīlābjamālāvalitakoṭaram / kṣraṇamuḍḍāmararavaṃ kṣaṇaṃ mūkamiva sthitam //
english: It is now over-cast by azure clouds resembling the blue lotuses of the lake, and roaring loudly for a time and then being dumb and silent on a sudden:

sanskrit: kṣaṇaṃ tārāviracitaṃ kṣaṇamarkeṇa bhūṣitam / kṣaṇamindukṛtāhlādaṃ kṣaṇaṃ sarvabahiṣkṛtam //
english: Now studded with stars, and now glowing with the glory of the sun;then graced by the pleasant moonbeams, and at last without any light at all.

sanskrit: āgamāpāyaparayā kṣaṇasaṃsthitināśayā / na bibheti hi saṃsāre dhīro'pi ka ivānayā //
english: Who is there so sedate and firm, that is not terrified at these sudden appearances and their disappearance, and the momentary durations and final dissolution of worldly things?

sanskrit: āpadaḥ kṣaṇamāyānti kṣaṇamāyānti saṃpadaḥ / kṣaṇaṃ janma kṣaṇaṃ mṛtyurmune kimiva na kṣaṇam //
english: What is the nature of this world, where we are overtaken by adversity at one moment, and elated by prosperity at another, where one is born at a time, and dies away at another?

sanskrit: prāgāsīdanya eveha jātastvanyo naro dinaiḥ / sadaikarūpaṃ bhagavankiṃcidasti na susthiram //
english: One that was something else before, is born as a man in this life, and is changed to another state in course of a few days; thus there is no being that remains steadily in the same state.

sanskrit: ghaṭasya paṭatā dṛṣṭā paṭasyāpi ghaṭasthitiḥ / na tadasti na yaddṛṣṭaṃ viparyasyati saṃsṛtau //
english: A pot is made of clay, and cloth is made of cotton, and they are still the same dull materials of which they are composed: thus there is nothing new in this world that was not seen or known before, and that changes not its form.

sanskrit: tanotyutpādayatyatti nihatyāsṛjati kramāt / satataṃ rātryahānīva nivartante naraṃ prati //
english: The acts of creation and destruction, of diffusion, production, and sustentation follow one another, as the revolution of day and night to man.

sanskrit: aśūreṇa hataḥ śūra ekenāpi hataṃ śatam / prākṛtāḥ prabhutāṃ yātāḥ sarvamāvartyate jagat //
english: It happens sometimes, that an impotent man slays a hero, and that hundreds are killed by one individual; so also a commoner becomes a noble man, and thus every thing is changeful in this varying world.

sanskrit: janateyaṃ viparyāsamajasramanugacchati / jaḍaspandaparāmarśāttaraṅgāṇāmivāvalī //
english: These bodies of men that are always changing their states, are as bodies of waters rising and falling in waves by motion of the winds.

sanskrit: bālyamalpadinaireva yauvanaśrīstato jarā / dehe'pi naikarūpatvaṃ kāsthā bāhyeṣu vastuṣu //
english: Boyhood lasts but a few days, and then it is succeeded by youth which is as quickly followed by old age: thus there being no identity of the same person, how can one rely on the uniformity of external objects?

sanskrit: kṣaṇamānanditāmeti kṣaṇameti viṣāditām / kṣaṇaṃ saumyatvamāyāti sarvasminnaṭavanmanaḥ //
english: The mind that gets delighted in a moment and becomes dejected in the next, and assumes likewise its equanimity at another, is indeed as changeful as an actor.

sanskrit: itaścānyaditaścānyaditaścānyadayaṃ vidhiḥ / racayanvastunāyāti khedaṃ līlāsvivārbhakaḥ //
english: The creator who is ever turning one thing into another in his work of creation, is like a child who makes and breaks his doll without concern.

sanskrit: cinotyutpādayatyatti nihatyāsṛjati kramāt / satataṃ rātryahānīva nivartante naraṃ prati //
english: The actions of producing and collecting (of grains), of feeding (one's self) and destroying (others), come by turns to mankind like the rotation of day and night.

sanskrit: āvirbhāvatirobhāvabhāgino bhavabhāginaḥ / janasya sthiratāṃ yānti nāpado na ca saṃpadaḥ //
english: Neither adversity nor prosperity is of long continuance in the case of worldly people, but they are ever subject to appearance and disappearance by turns.

sanskrit: kālaḥ krīḍatyayaṃ prāyaḥ sarvamāpadi pātayan / helāvicalitāśeṣacaturācāracañcuraḥ //
english: Time is a skilful player and plays many parts with ease; but he is chiefly skilled in tragedy, and often plays his tragic part in the affairs of men.

sanskrit: samaviṣamavipākato vibhinnāstribhuvanabhūtaparamparāphalaughāḥ / samayapavanapātitāḥ patanti pratidinamātatasaṃsṛtidrumebhyaḥ //
english: All beings are produced as fruits in the great forest of the universe, by virtue of their good and bad acts (of past lives): and time like a gust of wind blasts them day by day before their maturity.

sanskrit: śrīrāma uvāca / iti me doṣadāvāgnidagdhe mahati cetasi / prasphuranti na bhogāśā mṛgatṛṣṇāḥ saraḥsviva //
english: Thus is my heart consumed by the wild-fire of those great worldly evils, and there rises in me no desire of enjoying them, as there rises no mirage from a lake.

sanskrit: pratyahaṃ yāti kaṭutāmeṣā saṃsārasaṃsthitiḥ / kālapākavaśāllolā rasā nimbalatā yathā //
english: My existence upon earth gets bitter day by day, and though I have got some experience in it, yet its associations have made me as sour as the Nimba plant by its immersion in water.

sanskrit: vṛddhimāyāti daurjanyaṃ saujanyaṃ yāti tānavam / karañjakarkaśe rājanpratyahaṃ janacetasi //
english: I see wickedness on the increase, and righteousness on the decline in the mind of man, which like the sour Karanja (crab) fruit, becomes sourer every day.

sanskrit: bhajyate bhuvi maryādā jhaṭityeva dinaṃ prati / śuṣkeva māṣaśimbīkā ṭaṅkārakaravaṃ vinā //
english: I see honour is eaten up every day by mutual altercations of men, using harsh words to each other as they crack the nuts under their teeth.

sanskrit: rājyebhyo bhogapūgebhyaścintāvadbhyo munīśvara / nirastacintākalitā varamekāntaśīlatā //
english: Too much eagerness for royalty and worldly enjoyments, is equally prejudicial to our welfare; as we loose our future prospects by the former, and our present happiness by the latter.

sanskrit: nānandāya mamodyānaṃ na sukhāya mama striyaḥ / na harṣāya mamārthāśā śāmyāmi manasā saha //
