english: Then ordered by the lord of Rākşasas, the sons of his counsellors, seven (in number) in splendour reseinbling fire, issued forth that mansion.

sanskrit: mahadbalaparīvārā dhanuṣmanto mahābalāḥ| kṛtāstrāstravidāṃ śreṣṭhāḥ parasparajayaiṣiṇaḥ|| hemajālaparikṣiptairdhvajavadbhiḥ patākibhiḥ| toyadasvananirghoṣairvājiyuktairmahārathaiḥ|| taptakāñcanacitrāṇi cāpānyamitavikramāḥ| visphārayantaḥ saṃhṛṣṭāstaḍidvanta ivāmbudāḥ|| jananyastāstatasteṣāṃ viditvā kiṃkarān hatān| babhūvuḥ śokasambhrāntāḥ sabāndhavasuhṛjjanāḥ||
english: And surrounded by a mighty army, furnished with bows, endowed with wondrous strength, and accomplished in arms— the foremost of those acquainted with weapons-each burning for victory, with mighty cars yoked with steeds, covered with golden net-works, bearing pennons and standards, and having sounds like those proceeding from clouds, exultingly stretching with immeasurable prowess bows decked with gold, resembling clouds surcharged with lightning, those warriors sallied out. Learning that the servants had been slain, their (i.e. the mothers of the sons of the councillors) mothers, along with their friends and kindred, were overpowered with grief.

sanskrit: te parasparasaṃgharṣāstaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ| abhipeturhanūmantaṃ toraṇasthamavasthitam||
english: And vieing with each other in eagerness, those (warriors) decked in ornaments of polished gold, confronted Hanumān staying at the gate.

sanskrit: sṛjanto bāṇavṛṣṭiṃ te rathagarjitani:svanāḥ| prāvṛṭkāla ivāmbhodā vicerunairṛtāmbudāḥ||
english: And with their cars sending roars, the Rākşasas, pouring showers of shafts, ranged (the field), resembling clouds during the rainy season.

sanskrit: avakīrṇastatastābhirhanūmāñśaravṛṣṭibhiḥ| abhavatsaṃvṛtākāraḥ śailarāḍiva vṛṣṭibhiḥ||
english: Covered with those arrowy showers, Hanuman had his person concealed, like the monarch of mountains hidden by a downpour.

sanskrit: sa śarānvañcayāmāsa teṣāmāśucaraḥ kapiḥ| rathavegāṃśca vīrāṇāṃ vicaranvimale'mbare||
english: That swift-speeding monkey, coursing the cloudless sky, evaded those shafts of those heroes, as well as the impetuosity of their cars.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ krīḍandhanuṣmadbhiomni vīraḥ prakāśate| dhanuṣmadbhiryathā medhairmārutaḥ prabhurambare||
english: That hero, playing pranks with those bowmen, appeared like the masterful Wind playing tricks with the bow-bearing clouds. (i.e. having the iris.)

sanskrit: sa kṛtvā ninadaṃ ghoraṃ trāsayaṃstāṃ mahācamūm| cakāra hanūmānvegaṃ teṣu rakṣaḥsu vīryavān||
english: Sending up a dreadful shout, and thereby filling that vast host with fright, the energetic Hanumān rushed on that Rākşasa army.

sanskrit: talenābhihanat kāṃścitpādaiḥ kāṃścitparaṃtapaḥ| muṣṭibhiścāhanatkāṃścinnakhaiḥ kāṃścid vyadārayat|| pramamāthorasā kāṃścidūrubhyāmaparānapi| kecittasyaiva nādena tatraiva patitā bhuvi||
english: That subduer of enemies slew some with slaps, and some he rived with nails, and some he killed by blows, and others with (the pressure of) his chest. And some dropped down on the ground at the very same spot at the sounds that he emitted.

sanskrit: tatasteṣvavapanneṣu bhūmau nipatiteṣu ca| tatsainyamagamatsarvaṃ diśo daśa bhayāditam||
english: And on their being slain or falling on the earth, that army, afflicted with affright, began to fly in all directions.

sanskrit: vinedurvisvaraṃ nāgā nipeturbhuvi vājinaḥ| bhagnanīḍadhvajacchatrairbhūśca kīrṇābhavad rathaiḥ ||
english: The elephants roared in frightful tones, and the steeds fell down on the earth. And the Earth was covered with broken boxes, flag-staffs, and umbrellas, (belonging to the cars), as also with the cars themselves.

sanskrit: stravatā rudhireṇātha sravantyo darśitāḥ pathi| vividhaiśca svanairlaṅkā nanāda vikṛtaṃ tadā||
english: And rivers running gore were seen on the way, and Lankā uttered various frightful cries.

sanskrit: sa tānpravṛddhān vinihatya rākṣasān mahābalaścaṇḍaparākramaḥ kapiḥ| stadeva vīro'bhijagāma toraṇam||
english: Having slain those overgrown Rākşasas, that exceedingly powerful and heroic monkey of terrific power, desirous of again coping with other Rākşasas, retraced his steps to the selfsame entrance.

sanskrit: tathāgatāṃ tāṃ vyathitāmaninditāṃ vyatītaharṣāṃ paridīnamānasām| śubhāṃ nimittāni śubhāni bhejire naraṃ śriyā juṣṭamivopasevinaḥ||
english: Like to servants waiting upon a wealthy person various auspicious omens waited upon Sītā of a blameless and comely person, racked with grief and divested of joy.

sanskrit: rājyāvṛtaṃ kṛṣṇaviśālaśuklam| prāspandataikaṃ nayanaṃ sukeśyā mīnāhataṃ padmamivābhitāmram||
english: And the large left eye of that dame having graceful hairs, having dark pupils, white ends and thick eye-lashes, began to dance like a lotus shaken by a fish.

sanskrit: bhujaśca cārvañcitavṛttapīnaḥ parāyaṃkālāgurucandanāhaḥ| anuttamenādhyuṣitaḥ priyeṇa cireṇa vāmaḥ samavepatāśu||
english: And her beautiful, round, plump left hand, which, ere this, sprinkled with costly aguru and sandal, used to serve for a pillow to Rāma, began to dance now again and again after a long time.

sanskrit: stayordvayoḥ saṃhatayostu jātaḥ| praspandamānaḥ punarūrurasyā rāmaṃ purastāt sthitamācacakṣe||
english: And her well built plump left thigh, resembling the trunk of an elephant, dancing, announced that she would soon behold Rāma.

sanskrit: mīṣadrajodhvastamivātulākṣyāḥ| vāsaḥ sthitāyāḥ śikharāgradantyāḥkiṃcit paristraṃsatacārugātryāḥ||
english: And the gold-hued cloth, now covered with dust, of that damsel of a comely person, having teeth like pomegranate seeds, slipped a little off its place.

sanskrit: etairnimittairaparaiśca subhrūḥ saṃcoditā prāgapi sādhusiddhaiḥ| vātātapaklāntamiva praṇaṣṭaṃ varṣeṇa bījaṃ pratisaṃjaharṣa||
english: And being enlivened by those and various other auspicious omens, she attained joy like to a seed, spoiled by the wind and the sun, growing afresh in the rainy season.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ punarbimbaphalopamoṣṭhaṃ svakṣibhukeśāntamarālapakṣma| vaktraṃ babhāse sitaśukladaṃṣṭra rāhormukhāccandra iva pramuktaḥ||
english: And her countenance, having lips red as Bimba fruits, beautiful eyes, eye-brows extending to ears, curling eye-lashes and white teeth, again appeared graceful like to the Moon released from the full grasp of Rahu. (Like the Moon when full eclipse is just over-In mythology Rāhu is the son of Sinika, a Daitya, with the tail of a dragon whose head was severed from-his body by Vişnu, but being immortal this head and tail retained their separate existence and being transferred to the stellar sphere, became the authors of eclipses.)

sanskrit: sā vītaśokā vyapanītatandrā śāntajvarā harṣavibuddhasattvā| aśobhatāryā vadanena śukle śītāṃśunā rātririvoditena ||
english: Her grief and exhaustion were removed. sorrow was pacified and her heart was filled with joy. And she with her countenance appeared beautiful like a lunar night beautified by the rays of the Moon.

sanskrit: tataḥ śūrpaṇakhā ghorā rāghavāśramamāgatā| rākṣasānācacakṣe tau bhrātarau saha sītayā||
english: Then the grim Śūrpanakhā, coming to Rāghava's asylum pointed out to the Rākşasas those brother in company with Sītā.

sanskrit: te rāmaṃ parṇaśālāyāmupaviṣṭaṃ mahābalam| dadṛśuḥ sītayā sārdhaṃ lakṣmaṇenāpi sevitam||
english: And they saw the mighty Rāma seated in the cottage in company with Sītā, and ministered to by Laksmana.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ śrīmānāgatāṃstāṃśca rākṣasān| abravīd bhrātaraṃ rāmo lakṣmaṇaṃ dīptatejasam||
english: And seeing her, as well as the Rākşasas who had come, Rāma remarked to his brother, Lakşınaņa of flaming energy.

sanskrit: muhūrte bhava saumitre sītāyāḥ pratyanantaraḥ| imānasyā vadhiṣyāmi padavīmāgatāniha||
english: O Sumitrā's son, do you for a while guard Sītā. I shall slay these that have come to this asylum here.

sanskrit: vākyametat tataḥ śrutvā rāmasya viditātmanaḥ| tatheti lakṣmaṇo vākyaṃ rāghavasya prapūjayan||5
english: Hearing these words of Rāma versed in the knowledge of self, Lakşmaņa honoured his speech by saying, So be it.

sanskrit: rāghavo'pi mahaccāpaṃ cāmīkaravibhūṣitam| cakāra sajyaṃ dharmātmā tāni rakṣāṃsi cābravīt||
english: And the righteous Rāghava strung his mighty bow decked with gold; and addressed the Raksasas.

sanskrit: putrau daśarathasyāvāṃ bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau| praviṣṭau sītayā sārdhaṃ duścaraṃ daṇḍakāvanam|| phalamūlāśanau dāntau tāpasau brahmacāriṇau| vasantau daṇḍakāraṇye kimarthamupahiṃsatha||
english: We that have entered into this untraceable forest of Dandaka in company with Sītā are the sons of Dasaratha, the brothers, Rama and Lakşmana. Why do you intend to do injury to us. Subsisting on fruits and roots, having our senses under control, carrying on asceticism and leading a Brahmacarya life, we are passing our days in the forest of Dandaka.

sanskrit: yuṣmān pāpātmakān hantuṃ viprakārān mahāhave| ṛṣīṇāṃ tu niyogena samprāptaḥ saśarāsanaḥ||
english: It is do destroy you, wicked, and troublesome that I equipped with the bow have come here at the desire of the saints.

sanskrit: tiṣṭhataivātra saṃtuṣṭā nopavartitumarhatha| yadi prāṇairihārtho vo nivartaghnāḥ||
english: Stay there content you should not move further. If you have a care for your lives, desist, you rangers of the night.

sanskrit: tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasāste caturdaśa| ūcurvācaṃ susaṃkruddhā brahmaghnāḥ śūlapāṇayaḥ|| saṃraktanayanā ghorā rāmaṃ saṃraktalocanam| paruṣā madhurābhāṣaṃ hṛṣṭā dṛṣṭaparākramam||
english: Hearing those words of his, those fourteen grim Rākşasas bearing darts in their hands, exceedingly enraged, with their eyes reddened, breathing high spirits, harshly said to the sweetspeeched Rāma, having his eyes reddened whose prowess they had not seen before.

sanskrit: krodhamutpādya no bhartuḥ kharasya sumahātmanaḥ| tvameva hāsyase prāṇān sadyo'smābhirhato yudhi ||
english: Having excited there our lord. the high-souled Khara, it is you that shal: lose your life no later than this day, being slain by us in battle.

sanskrit: kā hi te śaktirekasya bahūnāṃ raṇamūrdhani | asmākamagrataḥ sthātuṃ kiṃ punaryo māhave||
english: What power hast you, being one to stay before us many in the field, what shall I say of your coping with us in conflict?

sanskrit: ebhirbāhuprayuktaiśca parighaiḥ śūlapaṭṭiśaiḥ| prāṇāṃstyakṣyasi vīryaṃ ca dhanuśca karapīḍitam||
english: In consequence of the parighas (iron-clubs), darts, and pattisas (a kind of sharp-edged sword) discharged by our arms, you will surely lose your life, along with your prowess, and this bow which you press with your hand.

sanskrit: ityevamuktvā saṃrabdhā rākṣasāste caturdaśa| udyatāyudhanistriṃśā rāmamevābhidudruvuḥ||
english: Having said this in wrath, those fourteen Rākşasas, uplifting their weapons and daggers rushed towards Rāma.

sanskrit: cikṣipustāni śūlāni rāghavaṃ prati durjayam| tāni śūlāni kākutsthaḥ samastāni caturdaśa||
english: And discharged darts at the invincible Rāghava. Thereupon Kākutstha by means of shafts decked with gold, cut off those fourteen darts of theirs.

sanskrit: tāvadbhireva ciccheda śaraiḥ kāñcanabhūṣitaiḥ| tataḥ paśyānmahātejā nārācān sūryasaṃnibhān|| jagrāha paramakuddhaścaturdaśa śilāśitān| gṛhītvā dhanurāyamya lakṣyānuddiśya rākṣasān|| mumoca rāghavo bāṇān vajrāniva śatakratuḥ|
english: Seeing this, that exceedingly cnergetic one, waxing highly enraged, look out fourteen darts with many golden arrows, whetted on stone, resembling the sun. And even as Satakratu hurls the thunder bolt, Rāghava drawing his bow and taking his aim at the Rākşasas, let go those shafts.

sanskrit: te bhitvā rakṣasāṃ vegād vakṣāṃsi rudhiraplutāḥ|| viniṣpetustadā bhūmau valmīkādiva pannagāḥ|
english: And those Rākşasas, their breasts pierced with vehemence, and themselves bathed in blood, fell down to the carth, like snakes dropping down from an ant hill.

sanskrit: tairbhagnahadayā bhūmau chinnamūlā iva drumāḥ|| nipetuḥ śoṇitasnātā vikṛtā vigatāsavaḥ|
english: And with their breasts pierced, they, dripping with blood, deformed and deprived of their lives, lay on the ground like trees whose roots have been severed.

sanskrit: tān bhūmau patitān dṛṣṭvā rākṣasī krodhamūchitāḥ|| upagamya kharaṃ sā tu kiṃcitsaṃśuṣkaśoṇitā| papāta punarevārtā saniryāseva vallarī||
english: Seeing them fallen-on the ground, the Rākşasī, beyond herself in wrath, approaching Khara, with her blood a little dried up, again in distressful guise threw herself on the earth, like a plant exuding gum.

sanskrit: bhrātuḥ samīpe śokārtā sasarja ninadaṃ mahat| sasvaraṃ mumuce vāṣpaṃ vivarṇavadanā tadā||
english: And in presence of her brother, she set up a mighty roar; and then her face grown pallid, she dropped tears, emitting cries.

sanskrit: nipātitān prekṣya raṇe tu rākṣasān pradhāvitā śūrpaṇakhā punastataḥ| vadhaṃ ca teṣāṃ nikhilena rakṣasāṃ śaśaṃsa sarvaṃ bhaginī kharasya sā||
english: Seeing those Rākşasas slain in battle, Śūrpanakhā again hastened (to his brother); and the sister of Khara, related in detail the slaughter of those Rākşasas.

sanskrit: ṛṣyamūkāt tu hanumān gatvā taṃ malayaṃ girim| ācacakṣe tadā vīrau kapirājāya rāghavau||
english: Having departed from Rşyamuka, and arrived at the Malaya hill, Hanumān informed the king of monkeys of (the arrival of) the descendants of Raghu.

sanskrit: ayaṃ rāmo mahāprājña samprāpto dṛḍhavikramaḥ| lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā rāmo'yaṃ satyavikramaḥ||
english: O exceedingly wise one, this one that has come here is Rāma having truth for his prowess.

sanskrit: ikvākūṇāṃ kule jāto rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ| dharme nigaditaścaiva piturnideśakārakaḥ||
english: This is Rāma having truth for his prowess, in company with his brother, Lakşmaņa. Rāma the son of Dasaratha, is born in the race of the Ikş wākus. Ever doing the will of his sire, he has been sent hither, in order that his father's verity may stand in tact.

sanskrit: rājasūyāśvamedhaiśca vahniryenābhitarpitaḥ| dakṣiṇāśca tathotsṛṣṭā gāvaḥ śatasahasraśaḥ|| tapasā satyavākyena vasudhā yena pālitā| strīhetostasya putro'yaṃ rāmo'raṇyaṃ samāgataḥ||
english: Raima, who has come to the forest, is the son of him who has propitiated Fire with Rājasuyas and horse sacrifices,-dispensing Dakshinas and kine by hundreds and thousands-and who has governed the earth by asceticism and truthful speech. His son Rāma has come to the forest through a woman.

sanskrit: tasyāsya vasato'raṇye niyatasya mahātmanaḥ| rāvaṇena hṛtā bhāryā sa tvāṃ śaraṇamāgataḥ||
english: While that high-souled one having his senses under control was dwelling in the woods, his wife was carried off by Rāvana; and he (Rāma) has (in consequence) sought your protection.

sanskrit: bhavatā satyakāmo tau bhrātarau rāmalakṣmaṇau| pragṛhya cārcayasvaitau pūjanīyatamābubhau||
english: Do you, granting an interview to the brothers Rāma and Lakşmaņa-both of them worthy of homage-who pe eager for your friendship, receive them respectfully.

sanskrit: śrutvā hanūmato vākyaṃ sugrīvo vānarādhipaḥ| darśanīyatamo bhūtvā prītyovāca ca rāghavam|| bhavān dharmavinītaśca sutapāḥ sarvavatsalaḥ| ākhyātā vāyuputreṇa tattvato me bhavadguṇāḥ||
english: Hearing Hanuman's words, Sugrīva-lord of monkeys, becoming visible (at his will), gladly spoke to Rāghava, sir, you are versed in morality, and bear love towards all. The son of the wind-god has faithfully described your virtues to me.

sanskrit: tanmamaivaiṣa satkāro lābhaścaivottamaḥ prabho| yattvamicchasi sauhārda vānareṇa mayā saha ||
english: That you, O lord, are anxious to contract friendship with me who am a monkey does me honour and is my gain.

sanskrit: rocate yadi me sakhyaṃ bāhureṣa prasāritaḥ| gṛhyatāṃ pāṇinā pāṇirmaryādā badhyatāṃ dhruvā||
english: If you relish friendship with me, do you take this stretched arm and my hand with yours, and bind yourself fast with a vow.

sanskrit: etat tu vacanaṃ śrutvā sugrīvasya subhāṣitam| samprahṛṣṭamanā hastaṃ pīḍayāmāsa pāṇinā|| hṛṣṭaḥ sauhṛdamālambya paryaṣvajata pīḍitam|
english: Hearing these sweet words of Sugrīva, (Rāma) exceedingly delighted, pressed Sugrīva's hand with his. And contracting friendship with Surgrīva, Rāma experiencing great joy embraced him warmly.

sanskrit: tato hanūmān saṃtyajya bhikṣurūpamariṃdamaḥ|| kāṣṭhayoḥ svena rūpeṇa janayāmāsa pāvakam|
english: Then that subduer of foes, Hanumān, leaving off the guise of a beggar, in his native shape produced a fire with two pieces of wood.

sanskrit: dīpyamānaṃ tato vahni puṣpairabhyarcya satkṛtam|| tayormadhye tu suprīto nidadhau susamāhitaḥ| tato'gniṃ dīpyamānaṃ tau cakratuśca pradakṣiṇam|| sugrīvo rāghavaścaiva vayasyatvamupāgatau|
english: Then worshipping that flaming fire with flowers, he, well pleased, carefully placed it between them (Rāma and Sugrīva). Then Sugrīva and Rāghava went round the fire; and (thus) were fastened in friendship.

sanskrit: tataḥ suprītamanasau tābubhau harirāghavau|| anyonyamabhivīkṣantau na tṛptimabhijagmatuḥ|
english: And with delighted hearts, both of them-the monkey and Rāghava began to gaze at each other, yet they did not feel satiated.

sanskrit: tvaṃ vayasyo'si hṛdyo me hyekaṃ duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ ca nau||17| sugrīvo rāghavaṃ vākyamityuvāca prahṛṣṭavat|
english: You are the friend of my heart. Our happiness and misery are common,-Sugriva, rejoicing greatly, said these words to Rāghava.

sanskrit: tataḥ suparṇabahulā bhaṅktvā śākhāṃ supuṣpitām|| sālasyāstīrya sugrīvo niṣasāda sarāghavaḥ|
english: Then spreading a beautifully blossoming spray of Sala, full of foliage, Sugriva made an awning and sat down with Rāghava.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇāyātha saṃhṛṣṭo hanumān mārutātmajaḥ|| śākhāṃ candanavṛkṣasya dadau paramapuṣpitām|
english: Hanumăn, the son of the wind-god with great joy gave to Lakşmaņa a bough of a sandal tree, plentifully blossoming.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahṛṣṭaḥ sugrīvaḥ ślakṣṇaṃ madhurayā girā|| pratyuvāca tadā rāmaṃ harṣavyākulalocanaḥ|
english: Next Sugriva, feeling high rapture, with his eyes expanded with joy, answered Rāma blandly in sweet words.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vinikṛto rāma carāmīha bhayāditaḥ|| hṛtabhāryo vane trasto durgametadupāśritaḥ|
english: Oppressed have I been, O Rama; and here am always afflicted with fear. Deprived of my wife, I have, agitated with apprehension, sought refuge in this dense wilderness.

sanskrit: so'haṃ trasto vane bhīto vasāmyubhrāntacetanaḥ|| vālinā nikṛto bhrātrā kṛtavairaśca rāghava|
english: I am afflicted with fright, and worried by fear, with my senses bewildered in this wood. Wronged have I been by Vāli, my brother; and I have incurred his hostility, O Raghava.

sanskrit: vālino me mahābhāga bhayārtasyābhayaṃ kuru|| kartumarhasi kākutstha bhayaṃ me na bhaved yathā|
english: And, O exalted one, do you dispel the fear of me, who am tormented with fear on account of Vali. And, O Kakutstha, it behoves you so to act that I may not become subject to fear.

sanskrit: evamuktastu tejasvī dharmajño dharmavatsalaḥ|| pratyabhāṣata kākutsthaḥ sugrīvaṃ prahasanniva|
english: Thus addressed, the powerful Kākutstha, knowing righteousness, and devoted to virtue, answered Sugriva, smiling,

sanskrit: upakāraphalaṃ mitraṃ viditaṃ me mahākape|| vālinaṃ taṃ vadhiṣyāmi tava bhāryāpahāriṇam|
english: O mighty monkey, that the outcome of amity is good offices I am well aware of. I will slay that captor of your wife Vāli.

sanskrit: amoghāḥ sūryasaṃkāśā mameme nicitāḥ śarāḥ|| tasmin vālini durvṛtte nipatiṣyanti vegitāḥ| kaṅkapatrapraticchannā mahendrāśanisaṃnibhāḥ|| tīkṣṇāgrā ṛjuparvāṇaḥ saroṣā bhujagā iva|
english: These infallible sharpened shafts of inine, resembling the sun, feathered with the plumes of the Kanka, like to the thunderbolt of the great Indra, having sharp heads and even knots, like in infuriated serpents,-being let go with vehermence, shall alight upon the impious Vali.

sanskrit: tamadya vālinaṃ paśya tīkṣṇairāśīviṣopamaiḥ|| śarairvinihataṃ bhūmau prakīrṇamiva parvatam|
english: Do you today behold Vāli slain with sharpened shafts, resembling snakes,—like to a torn hill lying on the ground.

sanskrit: sa tu tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rāghavasyātmano hitam| sugrīvaḥ paramaprītaḥ paramaṃ vākyamabravīt||
english: Hearing those words of Răghava fraught with his welfare, Sugrīva supremely rejoiced, said these words, informed with rapture, You hero!

sanskrit: tava prasādena nṛsiṃha vīra priyāṃ ca rājyaṃ ca samāpnuyāmaham| tathā kuru tvaṃ naradeva vairiṇaṃ yathā na hiṃsyāt sa punarmamāgrajam ||
english: You lion among men! by your grace shall I obtain both my beloved and my monarchy. O God among men, do you so deal with that foe, my elder brother, that he may not again wrong venomous me.

sanskrit: sītākapīndrakṣaṇadācarāṇāṃ rājīvahemajvalanopamāni| sugrīvarāmapraṇayaprasaṅge vāmāni netrāṇi samaṃ sphuranti||
english: The left eyes of Sītā, the lord of apes, and night rangers-respectively like the lotus, gold, and flaming fire, throbbed when the friendship between Rāma and Sugrīva was contracted.

sanskrit: atha rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ| āpṛṣṭvā tau ca rājānau jagāmottaraparvatam||
english: Then when the right had passed away, the mighty Muni Viśvāmitra, having greeted the monarchs, yet out for the Northern mountains.

sanskrit: viśvāmitre gate rājā vaidehaṃ mithilādhipam| āpṛṣdaiva jagāmāśu rājā daśarathaḥ purīm||
english: When Viśvāmitra had gone away, king Dasaratha, greeting Mithila's lord, Vaideha, actively prepared for setting out for his own capital.

sanskrit: atha rājā videhānāṃ dadau kanyādhanaṃ bahu| gavāṃ śatasahasrāṇi bahūni mithileśvaraḥ|| kambalānāṃ ca mukhyānāṃ kṣaumān koṭyambarāṇi ca| hastyaśvarathapādātaṃ divyarūpaṃ svalaṃkṛtam|| dadau kanyāśataṃ tāsāṃ dāsīdāsamanuttamam| hiraṇyasya suvarṇasya muktānāṃ vidrumasya ca ||
english: Then the king of the Videhas gave a dower consisting of various things. And Mithilā's lord gave many hundred thousands of kine, and excellent woollen stuffs, and Koțis of common cloths; and elephants, and horses, and cars, and footmen, as well as an hundred damsels adorned, endowed with elegance to form goodly waitingmaids. And well-pleased the king gave as a noble dower gold and silver and pearls and coral.

sanskrit: dadau rājā susaṃhṛṣṭaḥ kanyādhanamanuttamam| dattvā bahuvidhaṃ rājā samanujñāpya pārthivam|| praviveśa svanilayaṃ mithilāṃ mithileśvaraḥ| rājāpyayodhyādhipatiḥ saha putrairmahātmabhiḥ|| ṛṣīn sarvān puraskṛtya jagāma sabalānugaḥ|
english: Having given divers kinds of articles, that king, the lord of Mithila, bidding adieu to the monarch (Dasaratha), re-entered his own capital. And the master of Ayodhyā accompanied with his high-souled sons, and headed by the saints in a body, started on the journey, followed by his own army.

sanskrit: gacchantaṃ tu naravyāghra sarṣisaṅgha sarāghavam|| ghorāstu pakṣiṇo vāco vyāharanti samantataḥ| bhaumāścaiva mṛgāḥ sarve gacchanti sma pradakṣiṇam||
english: As that tiger-like one was on his way, in company with Rāghava and the saints, the fowls began to utter frightful cries all around, and the beasts on earth to stream in a Southern direction.

sanskrit: tān dṛṣṭvā rājaśārdūlo vasiṣṭhaṃ paryapṛcchata| asaumyāḥ pakṣiṇo ghorā mṛgāścāpi pradakṣiṇāḥ|| kimidaṃ hṛdayotkampi mano mama viṣīdati|
english: Beholding them, that tiger-like monarch asked Vasistha, saying, Those birds of fierce aspects emit frightful cries and beasts stream in a Southerly direction. What is this? My heart tremble and my mind is not at ease.

sanskrit: rājño daśarathasyaitacchrutvā vākyaṃ mahānṛṣiḥ|| uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇī śrūyatāmasya yat phalam| upasthitaṃ bhayaṃ ghoraṃ divyaṃ pakṣimukhāccyutam|| mṛgāḥ praśamayantyete saṃtāpastyajyatāmayam|
english: Hearing the speech of king Dasaratha, that mighty saint spoke sweetly, saying, 'These fowls of the air by their cries presage some dreadful impending evil; but these beasts betoken peace restored. Therefore do you renounce anxiety'

sanskrit: teṣāṃ: saṃvadatāṃ tatra vāyuḥ prādurbabhūva ha|| kampayan medinī sarvāṃ pātayaṃśca mahādumān| tamasā saṃvṛtaḥ sūryaḥ sarve nāvediṣurdiśaḥ|| bhasmanā cāvṛtaṃ sarvaṃ sammūḍhamiva tadbalam|
english: As they were thus conversing, there blew a strong wind; and all the earth began to speak; and the trees to topple down. And a deep gloom enveloped the sun; and no quarter could be discovered. And enveloped in ashes, that host became stupefied.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha ṛṣayaścānye rājā ca sasutastadā|| sasaṃjñā iva tatrāsan sarvamanyadvicetanam| tasmiṃstamasi ghore tu bhasmacchanneva sā camūḥ||
english: At that dreadful hour, Vasiştha and the other saints and the king alone retained their senses, all else were deprived of their senses, and the army was enveloped with ashes.

sanskrit: dadarśa bhīmasaṃkāśaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam| bhārgavaṃ jāmadagnyeyaṃ rājā rājavimardanam|| kailāsamiva durdharṣaṃ kālāgnimiva duḥsaham| jvalantamiva tejobhirdurnirīkṣyaṃ pṛthagjanaiḥ|| skandhe cāsajjya paraśuṃ dhanurvidyudgaṇopamam| pragṛhya śaramugraṃ ca tripuraghnaṃ yathā śivam ||
english: The king saw that repressor of kings, the descendant of Bhrgu, Jamadagni's son, dreadful to behold, wearing a head of matted locks, like to the Kailāsa, had to baffle, resembling the fire at the universal dissolution, difficult to bear, flaming in energy, incapable of being looked at by the unrighteous, with his axe on his shoulder, equipped with a bow like to the lighting, and fierce arrows, looking like Śiva the slayer of Tripura.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasaṃkāśaṃ jvalantamiva pāvakam| vasiṣṭhapramukhā viprā japahomaparāyaṇāḥ|| saṃgatā munayaḥ sarve saṃjajalpuratho mithaḥ|
english: Beholding him of dreadful appearance like to flaming fire, the Vipras headed by Viśvāmitra, engaged in reciting mantras and and offering oblations to the fire, those saints assembled together, began to converse with each other.

sanskrit: kaccit pitṛvadhāmarṣī kṣatraṃ notsādayiṣyati|| pūrvaṃ kṣatravadhaṃ kṛtvā gatamanyurgatajvaraḥ| kṣatrasyotsādanaṃ bhūyo na khalvasya cikīrṣitam||
english: Is this one, enraged because of the slaughter of this sire, intent upon exterminating the Kș atriyas? Formerly, having slaughtered the Kșatriyas, he pacified his ire and mental ferment, 'therefore, the annihilate the Ksatriya once again can never be his endeavour.

sanskrit: evamuktvāya̭mādāya bhārgavaṃ bhīmadarśanam| ṛṣayo rāmarāmeti madhuraṃ vākyamabruvan||
english: Having said this, the saints offered Arghya to Bhrgu's son of dreadful appearance; and addressed him in soothing words, saying, 'Q Rāma! O Rāma.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ pūjāmṛṣidattāṃ pratāpavān| rāmaṃ dāśarathiṃ rāmo jāmadagnyo'bhyabhāṣata||
english: Accepting that homage rendered to him by the saints, that puissant one, Jamadagni's son, Rāma, addressed Rāma, the son of Dasaratha.

sanskrit: niviṣṭāyāṃ tu senāyāmutsuko bharatastataḥ| jagāma bhrātaraṃ draṣṭuṃ śatrughnamanudarśayan||
english: Having quartered his forces, Bharata eager (to go to Rāma's place), went to see his brother, showing to Satrughna the signs of Rāma's abode being in the vicinity.

sanskrit: ṛṣi vasiṣṭhaṃ saṃdiśya mātṛmeṃ śīghramānaya| iti tvaritamagre sa jagāma guruvatsalaḥ||
english: "And having desired Vasistha, saying, “Bring my mothers without delay,"" that one attached to his superiors went before."

sanskrit: sumantrastvapi śatrughnamadūrādanvapadyata| rāmadarśanajastoṃ bharatasyeva tasya ca||
english: And eager to see Rāma even like Bharata himself, Sumantra followed Bharata at a short distance.

sanskrit: gacchannevātha bharatastāpasālayasaṃsthitām| bhrātuḥ parṇakuṭī śrīmānuṭajaṃ ca dadarśa ha||
english: As Bharata passed on, he observed a neat cottage of leaves stationed among the asylums of anchorets, furnished with a portion having a wall with a door.

sanskrit: śālāyāstvagratastasyā dadarśa bharatastadā| kāṣṭhāni cāvabhagnāni puṣpāṇyapacitāni ca|| sa lakṣmaṇasya rāmasya dadarśāśramamīyuṣaḥ| kṛtaṃ vṛkṣeṣvabhijñānaṃ kuśacīraiḥ kvacit kvacit||
english: Before the cottage, Bharata saw fuel broken up, and flowers gathered. And he saw at places signs of Kuśa and bark set up on trees when Rāma and Lakşmaņa (first) arrived at their asylum.

sanskrit: dadarśa bhavane tasmin mahataḥ saṃcayān kṛtān| mṛgāṇāṃ mahiṣāṇāṃ ca karīṣaiḥ śītakāraṇāt||7
english: And in that habitation, Bharata saw great heaps of dry dung of deer and buffaloes, gathered for preventing cold.

sanskrit: gacchanneva mahābāhuryutimān bharatastadā| śatrughnaṃ cābravīddhṛṣṭastānamātyāṃśca sarvaśaḥ||
english: As he proceeded, the intelligent and mightyarmed Bharata with a cheerful heart remarked to Śatrughna and all the courtiers.

sanskrit: manye prāptāḥ sma taṃ deśaṃ bharadvājo yamabravīt| nātidūre hi manye'haṃ nadī mandākinīmitaḥ||
english: I conceive, we have reached the tract that was mentioned by Bharadvāja. Hard by this spot, I fancy, is the river Mandākini.

sanskrit: uccairbaddhāni cīrāṇi lakṣmaṇena bhavedayam| abhijñānakṛtaḥ panthā vikāle gantumicchatā||
english: On high are barks set up by Lakşmaņa. Having to pass by the way at unusual hours, (Laksmana) has marked it with signs.

sanskrit: itaścodāttadantānāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ tarasvinām| śailapārśve parikrāntamanyonyamabhigarjatām||
english: On the side of the hill is the way by which long-tusked elephants pass to and fro with vehemence, roaring at each other.

sanskrit: yamevādhātumicchanti tāpasāḥ satataṃ vane| tasyāsau dṛśyate dhūmaḥ saṃkulaḥ kṛṣṇavartmanaḥ||
english: Here is seen the dense and dark smoke of that which the anchorets are ever anxious to preserve in the forest, fire.

sanskrit: atrāhaṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ gurusatkārakāriṇam| ārya drakṣyāmi saṃhṛṣṭaṃ maharṣimiva rāghavam||
english: Even here shall I with a delighted heart see that foremost of men, the noble Rāghava resembling a Maharși, ever engaged in serving his superiors.

sanskrit: atha gatvā muhūrta tu citrakūṭaṃ sa rāghavaḥ| mandākinīmanu prāptastaṃ janaṃ cedamabravīt||
english: Then going to Citrakuta, that descendant of Raghu, coming to the Mandakini, said to the men.

sanskrit: jagatyāṃ puruṣavyāghra āste vīrāsane rataḥ| janendro nirjanaṃ prāpya dhiṅme janma sajīvitam||
english: That foremost of men in all the world, the lord of all, coming into seclusion, is in his yoga posture. O fie upon my birth and my life!

sanskrit: matkṛte vyasanaṃ prāpto lokanātho mahādyutiḥ| sarvān kāmān parityajya vane vasati rāghavaḥ||
english: For me, having come by misfortune, and renounced every comfort, the effulgent lord of men, Rāghava, is dwelling in the woods.

sanskrit: iti lokasamānuṣṭaḥ pādeṣvadya prasādayan| rāmaṃ tasya patiṣyāmi sītāyā lakṣmaṇasya ca ||
english: I shall be taxed of men on the score. To-day (first) pacifying him, I will fall at the feet of Rāma as well as of Sitã and Lakşmaņa.

sanskrit: evaṃ sa vilapaṃstasmin vane daśarathātmajaḥ| dadarśa mahatīṃ puṇyāṃ parṇaśālāṃ manoramām||
english: Having thus bewailed, Dasaratha's son saw a splendid, charming, and holy dwelling in that forest, composed of leaves.

sanskrit: sālatālāśvakarṇānāṃ parṇairbahubhirāvṛtām| viśālāṃ mṛdubhistīrṇāṃ kuśairvedimivādhvare|| śakrāyudhanikāśaiśca kārmukai rasādhanaiḥ| rukmapṛṣṭhairmahāsāraiḥ śobhitāṃ śatrubādhakaiḥ|| arkaraśmipratīkāśaioraistūṇagataiḥ śaraiḥ| śobhitāṃ dīptavadanaiḥ sarbhogavatīmiva|| mahārajatavāsobhyāmasibhyāṃ ca virājitām| rukmabinduvicitrābhyāṃ carmabhyāṃ cāpi śobhitām|| godhāṅgaliaurāsaktaiścitrakāñcanabhūṣitaiḥ| arisaṃdhairanādhṛṣyāṃ mṛgaiḥ siṃhaguhāmiva || prāgudakapravaṇāṃ vediṃ viśālāṃ dīptapāvakām| dadarśa bharatastatra puṇyāṃ rāmaniveśane||
english: And Bharata beheld in Rāma's habitation a sacred structure made of leaves, covered with a profusion of Sāla, palm, and Aśvakarņa leaves; spread with soft Kuśa, like a dais in a sacrifice; adorned with bows resembling the iris, plaited on the back with gold, of mighty force, and capable of achieving arduous feets and destroying foes; and garnished with arrows in quivers, seeming like the rays of the sun, with flaming mouths, like to the Bhogavatī with serpents; and exceedingly beautified with golden sheaths and scimitars and shields spangled with gold and nice guana finger-fences decked with gold; inaccessible to foes like a lion's den to deer; and furnished with a spacious dais inclined on the north-east, with a fire flaming on it.

sanskrit: nirīkṣya sa muhūrtaṃ tu dadarśa bharato gurum| uṭaje rāmamāsīnaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍaladhāriṇam|| kṛṣṇājinadharaṃ taṃ tu cīravalkalavāsasam| dadarśa rāmamāsīnamabhitaḥ pāvakopamam|| siṃhaskandhaṃ mahābāhuṃ puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇam| pṛthivyāḥ sāgarāntāyā bhartāraṃ dharmacāriṇam|| upaviṣṭaṃ mahābāhuṃ brahmāṇamiva śāśvatam| sthaṇḍile darbhasaṃstīrṇe sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca||
english: And looking around, anon Bharata saw his superior Rāma seated in the cottage bearing a head of matted locks, clad in a black deer-skin, and having tattered cloth and bark for his garment. And he saw Råma seated like to a flame, with leonine shoulders, mighty arms, and eyes resembling lotuses, the righteous lord of this world bounded by the seas, saw the mightyarmed on like to the eternal Brahma, seated on a skin-seat on the ground along with Sītā and Lakş mana.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā bharataḥ śrīmānśokamohapariplutaḥ| abhyadhāvata dharmātmā bharataḥ kekayīsutaḥ||
english: And seeing him, overwhelmed with grief and affliction, the righteous and graceful son of Kaikeyi, Bharata, rushed (towards him).

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva vilalāpā” bāṣpasaṃdigdhayā girā| aśaknuvan vārayituṃ dhairyād vacanamabruvan ||
english: And soon as Bharata saw Rāma, he, exceedingly distressed, broke out into lamentations in words choked with sorrow. And incapable of holding himself in patience, he said.

sanskrit: yaḥ saṃsadi prakṛtibhirbhaved yukta upāsitum| vanyairmṛgairupāsīnaḥ so'yamāste mamāgrajaḥ||
english: That elder brother of mine, who (seated) in court should be surrounded by the subjects intent upon paying him homage, is now surrounded by wild deer.

sanskrit: vāsobhirbahusāhauryo mahātmā purocitaḥ| mṛgājine so'yamiha pravaste dharmamācaran||
english: He that used to adorn his person with attire worth many thousands (of things), engaged in observing morality, is clad in deer-skin.

sanskrit: adhārayad yo vividhāścitrāḥ sumanasaḥ sadā| so'yaṃ jaṭābhāramimaṃ sahate rāghapaḥ katham||
english: Why does he that always wore variegated blossoms, Rāghava, bears this burthen of matted locks?

sanskrit: yasya yajñairyathādiṣṭairyukto dharmasya saṃcayaḥ| śarīrakleśasambhūtaṃ sa dharma parimārgate||
english: He who is worthy of acquiring religious merit by celebrating sacrifices according to the ordinance, is now following morality by afflicting his person.

sanskrit: candanena mahārheṇa yasyāṅgamupasevitam| malena tasyāṅgamidaṃ kathamāryasya sevyate||
english: How is the person of that one whose body used to be daubed with costly sandal, covered with dust.

sanskrit: manimittamidaṃ duḥkhaṃ prāpto rāmaḥ sukhocitaḥ| dhigjīvitaṃ nṛśaṃsasya mama lokavigarhitam||
english: It is for me that Rama, although deserving of comfort, has come by this misfortune. Wicked that I am, fie upon my life despised of men!

sanskrit: ityevaṃ vilapana dīnaḥ prasvinamukhapaṅkajaḥ| pādāvaprāpya rāmasya papāta bharato rudan||
english: Thus lamenting in woeful guise, with the lotus of his countenance covered with sweat, Bharata coming at Rāma's feet, fell at them bewailing.

sanskrit: duḥkhābhitapto bharato rājaputro mahābalaḥ| uktvā''ryeti sakṛddīnaṃ punarnovāca kiṃcana||
english: And inflamed with grief, the exceedingly powerful prince Bharata, having in distress of spirit uttered, O noble one, again said nothing.

sanskrit: bāṣpaiḥ pihitakaṇṭhaśca prekṣya rāmaṃ yaśasvinam| āryetyevābhisaṃkruśya vyāhatu nāśakat tataḥ||
english: And beholding the illustrious Rāma, Bharata with his utterance choked with emotion, exclaimed, O noble one, and was unable to say anything further.

sanskrit: śatrughnaścāpi rāmasya vavande caraṇau rudan| tāvubhau ca samāliṅgaya rāmo'pyaśrūṇyavartayat|| tataḥ sumantreṇa guhena caiva samīyatū rājasutāvaraṇye| divākaraścaiva niśākaraśca yathāmbare śukrabṛhaspatibhyām||
english: Then Śatrughna also weeping paid homage unto the feet of Rāma. And shedding tears, Rāma embraced them both. Then as in the sky, the Sun and the Moon meet with śukra and Brhaspati, those two princes (Rāma and Laks mana) met with Sumantra and Guha in the forest.

sanskrit: tān pārthivān vāraṇayūthapārhān samāgatāṃstatra mahatyaraṇye| vanaukasaste'bhisamīkṣya sarve tvaśrūṇyamuñcan pravihāya harṣam||
english: And beholding those kings resembling leaders of elephant-herds met together in that mighty forest, the dwellers in the woods, resigning their cheerfulness, began to shed tears. forest, the dwellers in the woods, resigning their cheerfulness, began to shed tears.

sanskrit: sa jitvā dhanadaṃ rāma bhrātaraṃ rākṣasādhipaḥ| mahāsenaprasūtiṃ tadyayau śaravaṇaṃ mahat||
english: O Rāma, having, vanquished his brother, the lord of riches, the king of Räkşasas went to the great wood of reeds, where Mahasena was born.

sanskrit: athāpaśyaddaśagrīvo raukmaṃ śaravaṇaṃ mahat| gabhastijālasaṃvītaṃ dvitīyamiva bhāskaram|| sa parvataṃ samāruhya kaṃcidramyavanāntaram| prekṣate puṣpakaṃ tatra rāmaviṣṭambhitaṃ tadā||
english: The Ten-necked Rāvana saw the great golden wood of reeds. Furnished with networks of solar rays, and appearing like a second Sun, and ascending the mountain, he was surveying the heart of the forest, when, O Rama, Puspaka was (suddenly) deprived of its motion.

sanskrit: viṣṭabdhaṃ kimidaṃ kasmānāgamatkāmagaṃ kṛtam| acintayadrākṣasendraḥ sacivaistaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ|| kinimittamicchayā me nedaṃ gacchati puṣpakam| parvatasyopariṣṭhasya karmedaṃ kasyacidbhavet|| tato'bravīttadā rāma mārīco buddhikovidaḥ| nedaṃ niṣkāraṇaṃ rājanpuṣpakaṃ yanna gacchati|| atha vā puṣpakamidaṃ dhanadānānyavāhanam| ato nispandamabhavaddhanādhyakṣavinākṛtam||
english: The lord of Räkşasas, could not comprehend how the car which had been so made as to course in accordance with the wish of the rider, could have its course impeded; and thereat he in company with his. councillors thought, 'Wherefore does not his Puşpaka course at my desire over this mountain? Whose act is this?' Thereat Mārīca foremost of intelligent ones said, 'That Puspaka does not course cannot, sire, be without cause; or it may be that in consequence of Puşpaka not having borne any other than the bestower of riches, it has ceased its course not having the lord of wealth for its rider.'

sanskrit: iti vākyāntare tasya karālaḥ kṛṣṇapiṅgalaḥ| vāmano vikaṭo muṇḍī nandī hasvabhujo balī|| tataḥ pārśvamupāgabhya bhavasyānucaro'bravīt| nandīśvaro vacaścedaṃ rākṣasendramaśaṅkitaḥ||
english: As they were speaking thus, that attendant of Bhava, Nandi, terrific, of yellow black hue, dwarfish, frightful, with his head shaven, having short arms, and stout, coming up to them, said (this). And the lordly Nandi, undaunted, addressed the sovereign of the Raksasas, saying.

sanskrit: nivartasva daśagrīva śaile krīḍati śaṃkaraḥ| suparṇanāgayakṣāṇāṃ devagandharvarakṣasām|| sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāmagamyaḥ parvataḥ kṛtaḥ|
english: Desist you O Ten-necked one; Śankara sport in the mountain; and (now) He is incapable of being approached by every one, birds, serpents and Yaksas; gods, Gandharvas and Raksasas?

sanskrit: iti nandivacaḥ śrutvā krodhātkampitakuṇḍalaḥ|| roṣāttu tāmranayanaḥ puṣpakādavaruhya saḥ| ko'yaṃ śaṃkara ityuktvā śailamūlamupāgataḥ|| so'paśyannandinaṃ tatra devasyādūrataḥ sthitam| dīptaṃ śūlamavaṣṭabhya dvitīyamiva śaṃkaram||
english: Hearing Nandi's speech, (Ravana), wrought up with wrath, his eyes coppery, and his earrings shaking, leapt down from Puspaka. And saying, 'who is this Sankara? and he came down to the base of the mount. He beheld there Nandi stationed at the side of the deity, supporting himself on his flaming dart, resembling a second Sankara.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vānaramukhamavajñāya sa rākṣasaḥ| prahāsaṃ mumuce tatra satoya iva toyadaḥ||
english: And seeing that one having the face of a monkey, the Raksasas, deriding him, burst out into laughter, and seemed as if a mass of clouds were sending roars.

sanskrit: taṃ kuddho bhagavānandī śaṃkarasyāparā tanuḥ| abravīttatra tadrakṣo daśānanamupasthitam||
english: Thereat, growing enraged, the reverend Nandi Sankara's other body spoke into that Rākṣasa The Ten-necked one present there.

sanskrit: yasmādvānararūpaṃ māmavajñāya daśānana| aśanīpātasaṃkāśamapahāsaṃ pramuktavān|| tasmānmavīryasaṃyuktā madrūpasamatejasaḥ| utpatsyanti vadhārtha hi kulasya tava vānarāḥ||
english: “As O Daśānana, deriding me for my monkery-form, you have indulged in a laughter resembling the bursting of thunder, do monkeys endowed with prowess, and possessed of my form and energy shall be born for compassing the destruction of your race.

sanskrit: nakhadaṃṣṭrāyudhāḥ krūra mana:saṃpātaraṃhasaḥ| yuddhonmattā balodriktāḥ śailā iva visarpiṇaḥ|| te tava prabalaṃ darpamutsedhaṃ ca pṛthagvidham| vyapaneṣyanti saṃbhūya sahāmātyamutasya ca||
english: And armed with teeth and claws, and fierce and furnished with the fleetness of thought, and mad for encounter, and bursting with vigour, and resembling moving mountains and being born, they shall crush your high pride and power along with your courtiers and sons.

sanskrit: kiṃ tvidānī mayā śakyaṃ hantuṃ tvāṃ he niśācara| na hantavyo hatastvaṃ hi pūrvameva svakarmabhiḥ||
english: But, O night-ranger, I can even now end you quite; yet I must not slay you for you have ere this been slain by your acts.

sanskrit: ityudīritavākye tu deve tasminmahātmani| devadundubhyo neduḥ puṣpavṛṣṭiśca khāccyutā||
english: When that high-souled god had spoken thus celestial kettle-drums sounded and a blossomy shower rained from the sky.

sanskrit: acintayitvā sa tadā nandivākyaṃ mahābalaḥ| parvataṃ tu samāsādya vākyamāha daśānanaḥ||
english: But without heeding Nandi's speech, that highly powerful one Daśānana coming to the mountain, said.

sanskrit: puṣpakasya gatiśchinnā yatkṛte mama gacchataḥ| tamimaṃ śailamunmūlaṃ karomi tava gopate||
english: 'O Gopati, I will even uproot this mountain, for whom Pușpaka was deprived of its motion as I was journeying.

sanskrit: kena prabhāveṇa bhavā nityaṃ krīḍati rājavat| vijñātavyaṃ na jānīte bhayasthānamupasthitam||
english: It must be known by what influence Bhavasvara sport here king-like. He does not know that an occasion of fear has presented itself?'

sanskrit: evamuktvā taṃ rāma bhujānvikṣipya parvate| tolayāmāsa taṃ śīghraṃ sa śailaṃ samakampata||
english: Having said this, O Rama, Ravana seizing the mountain with his arms, lifted it up at once; and then the mountain trembled greatly.

sanskrit: cā nātpartatasyaiva rāṇā devasya kampitāḥ| cacāla pārvatī cāpi tadāśliṣṭā maheśvaram||
english: And in consequence of the mountain shaking the attendants of the deity (dwelling in it) also shook. And Pārvatí also trembled and embraced Mahesvara. as

sanskrit: tato rāma mahādavo devānāṃ pravaro haraḥ| pādāṅguṣṭhena taṃ śailaṃ pīḍayāmāsa līlayā||
english: Then, O Rāma, Mahadeva foremost of the deities even Hara, as in sport pressed the mount with his great toe.

sanskrit: pīḍitāstu tatastasya śailastambhopamā bhujāḥ| vismitāścābhavaṃstatra sacivāstasya rakṣasaḥ||
english: Thereat his arms, resembling blocks of stone felt the shock and then there the councillors of that Rākşasa were struck with amaze.

sanskrit: rakṣasā tena roṣācca bhujānāṃ pīḍanāttathā| mukto virāvaḥ sahasā trailokyaṃ yena kampitam||29
english: The Rākṣasa, from wrath and the pain felt in his arms, set up a shout that shook the entire triune world.

sanskrit: menire vajraniṣpeṣaṃ tasyāmātyā yugakṣaye| tadā vartmasu calitā devā indrapurogamāḥ|| samudrāścāpi saṃkṣubdhāścalitāścāpi parvatāḥ| yakṣā vidyādharāḥ siddhāḥ kimetaditi cābruvan||31
english: "His councillors considered it the concussion of the thunder at the universal disruption. And then the celestials with Indra at their head shook on their way; and the sea was wild and the mountains shook. And Yakşas and Vidyadharas and Siddhas asked, ""What is this.'"

sanskrit: toṣayasva mahādevaṃ nīlakaṇṭhamumāpatim| tamṛte śaraṇaṃ nānyaṃ paśyāmo'tra daśānana||
english: 'Do you propitiate Uma's lord the bluethroated Mahādeva; for, O Daśānana, save him your refuge see we none in this matter.

sanskrit: stutibhiḥ praṇato bhūtvā tameva śaraṇaṃ vraja| kṛpāluḥ śaṃkarastuṣṭaḥ prasādaṃ te vidhāsyati ||
english: Bowing yourself down, do you seek him as your shelter. Then the kind Sankara, on being gratified, will confer on you his favour.

sanskrit: evamuktastadāmātyaistuṣṭāva vṛṣabhadhvajam | samābhirvividhaiḥ stotraiḥ praṇabhya sa daśānanaḥ| saṃvatsarasahasraṃ tu rudato rakṣaso gatam||
english: Thus accosted by his councillors, the Tenfaced one, bowing down to him having the bull for his standard, began to hymn him with various soma hymns; and the Rākşasa passed away a good thousand years in lamentations.

sanskrit: tataḥ prīto mahādevaḥ śailāne viṣṭhitaṃ prabhuḥ| muktvā cāsya bhujārāma prāha vākyaṃ daśānanam||
english: Thereat that Lord Mahādeva, pleased, set free the hands of Daśānana stationed at the top of the mount, and O Rāma, addressed him, saying.

sanskrit: prīto'smi tava vīrasya śauṭīryācca daśānana| śailākrāntena yo muktastvayārāvaḥ sudāruṇaḥ|| yasmāllokatrayaṃ caitadrāvitaṃ bhayamāgatam| tasmāttvaṃ rāvaṇo nāma nāmnā rājanbhaviṣyasi ||
english: O Daśānana, pleased am I with you on account of your hymns. And as in consequence of your arms having been hurt by the mountain, you have uttered a terrific yell, which struck horror into the worlds and put them shaking, therefore, o King, your name shall be Ravana.

sanskrit: devatā mānuṣā yakṣā ye cānye jagatītale| evaṃ tvāmabhidhāsyanti rāvaṇaṃ lokarāvaṇam||
english: And deities and men, Yakşas and others living on earth shall call you Rāvana terror to creatures,

sanskrit: gaccha paulastya visrabdhaṃ pathā yena tvamicchasi| mayā caivābhyanujñāto rākṣasādhipa gamyatām||
english: Go, O Paulastya, which way you wish with confidence, and permitted by me, O Lord of Raksasas, go you.

sanskrit: evamuktastu laṅkeśaḥ : śaṃbhunā svayamabravīt| prīto yadi mahādeva varaṃ me dehi yācataḥ||
english: Thus accosted by Sambhu, Larkā's lord said of himself. 'If you are pleased with me, grant me a boon, who ask you for it.

sanskrit: avadhyatvaṃ mayā prāptaṃ devagandharvadānavaiḥ| rākṣasairguhyakai gairye cānye balavattarāḥ||
english: I have already obtained a boon, bestowing on me immunity from death at the hands of gods, Gandharvas and Dānavas; and Rākşasas and Guyhakas and Nāgas; and others also that are of more than ordinary strength.

sanskrit: mānuṣāna gaṇe deva svalpāste mama saṃmatāḥ| dīrghamāyuśca meṃ prāptaṃ brahmaṇastripurāntaka| vāñchitaṃ cāyuṣaḥ śeṣaṃ śastraṃ tvaṃ ca prayaccha me||
english: Man count I not ogod: They, I deem, are insignificant. I have also, O destroyer of Tripura, received a long lease of life from Brahmä. Now I wish to pass the remainder of my days in peace: and do you grant me a weapon.

sanskrit: evamuktastatastena rāvaṇena sa śaṃkaraḥ| dadau khaṅgaṃ mahādīptaṃ candrahāsamiti śrutam| āyuṣaścāvaśaṣaṃ ca dadau bhūtapatistadā||
english: Thus addressed by him, (Ravana,) Sankara gave him an exceedingly effulgent sword, famed as Candrahāsa; and the master of spectres then also granted him peace for the rest of his life.

sanskrit: dattvovāca tataḥ śaṃbhu vajñeyamidaṃ tvayā| avajñātaṃ yadi hi te māmevaiṣyatyasaṃśayaḥ||
english: And making (the sword) over to him, Sambhu said, “You must not disregard this. If disregarded, it will for certain come (back) to me?'

sanskrit: evaṃ maheśveṇaiva kṛtanāmā sa rāvaṇaḥ| abhivādya mahādevamārurohātha puṣpakam||
english: Having thus received his his name from Mahesvara, Rāvana, saluting Mahadeva, ascended Puspaka.

sanskrit: tato mahītalaṃ rāma paryakrāmata rāvaṇaḥ| kṣatriyānsumahāvīryānbādhamānastatastataḥ|| kecittejasvinaḥ śūrāḥ kṣatriyā yuddhadurmadāḥ| tacchāsanamakurvanto vineśuḥ saparicchadāḥ||
english: Then, O Rāma, Rāvaņa, began to go round the earth. And opposed at places, by the heroic Kșatriyas endowed with energy and irrepressible in fight, fight, who refused submission, he exterminated them along with their retainers.

sanskrit: apare durjayaṃ rakṣo jānantaḥ prājñasaṃmatāḥ| jitāḥ sma ityabhāṣanta rākṣasaṃ baladarpitam||
english: "While other men of wisdom, knowing the Räkşasa to be invincible, said to the Rākṣasas elated with strength, ""We have been conquered?”"

sanskrit: te dūtā rāmavākyena coditā laghuvikramāḥ| prajagmurmadhurāṃ śīghraṃ cakrurvāsaṃ na cādhvani||
english: Having been despatched by Rama, quickmoving emissaries speedily arrived at Mathurā.

sanskrit: tatastribhirahorātraiḥ saṃprāpya mathurāmatha| śatrughnāya yathātattvamācakhyuḥ sarva eva tat||
english: Continually travelling for three nights and days, they arrived there and communicated to Šatrughna the intelligence.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇasya parityāgaṃ pratijñāṃ rāghavasya ca| putrayorabhiṣekaṃ ca paurānugamanaṃ tathā|| kuśasya nagarī ramyā vindhyaparvatarodhasi| kuśāvatīti nāmnā sā kṛtā rāmeṇa dhīmatā||
english: Having informed him of the renouncing of Lakşmaņa, Rāma's promise and the following of the citizens they said:-The intelligent Rāma has reared for Kuśī the spacious city of Kuśavati at the foot of the Vindhya range.

sanskrit: śrāvastīti purī ramyā śrāvitā ca lavasya ha| ayodhyā vijanāṃ kṛtvā rāghavo bharatastathā|| svargasya samanodyogaṃ kṛtavantau mahārathau|
english: The city of Śrāvasti has been reared for Lava, and the mighty car-warriors Rama and Bharata, making Ayodhyā void of men, have addressed themselves for repairing to heaven. Having speedily communicated to him this intelligence the emissaries took rest.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvaṃ nivedyāśu śatrughnāya mahātmane|| viremuste tato dūtāstvara rājeti cābruvan| tacchrutvā ghorasaṃkāśaṃ kulakṣayamupasthitam|| prakṛtīstu samānīya kāñcanaṃ ca purodhasam| teṣāṃ sarvaṃ yathāvṛttamabravīdraghunandanaḥ|||||
english: There upon they asked Satrughna to proceed soon. Observing the dreadful destruction of his race, Satrughna sent for his subjects and priests and informed them of everything.

sanskrit: ātmanaśca viparyāsaṃ bhaviṣyaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha| tataḥ putradvayaṃ vīraḥ so'bhyaṣiñcannarādhipaḥ||
english: He also communicated to them his own destruction with his brothers. There upon the king Satrughna determined upon installing his two sons in the kingdom.

sanskrit: subāhurmathurāṃ lebhe śatrughātī ca vai diśam| dvidhā kṛtvā tu tāṃ senāṃ mādhurī putrayordvayoḥ| dhanaṃ ca yuktaṃ kṛtvā sthāpayāmāsa pārthivaḥ|| subāhuṃ madhurāyāṃ ca vaidiśe śatrughātinam| yayau sthāpya tadāyodhyāṃ rathenaikena rāghavaḥ||
english: Subāhu was placed on the throne of Mathurā and Satrughāti became the king of Vidiśā. Having thus established Subāhu in Mathură, and Śatrughātī in Vidiśā, the great hero Satrughna ascended his car and went to Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: vai sa dadarśa mahātmānaṃ jvalantamiva pāvakam| sūkṣmakṣaumāmbaradharaṃ munibhiḥ sārdhamakṣayaiḥ|| so'bhivādya tato rāmaṃ prāñjaliḥ prayatendriyaḥ| uvāca vākyaṃ dharmajñaṃ dharmamevānucintayan||
english: And there he saw the great Rāma, clothed in silk raiment burning like fire in the midst of the ascetics. There upon remembering his duty he saluted Rāma, conversant with piety and with folded hands said.

sanskrit: kṛtvāviṣekaṃ sutayordvayo rāghavanandana| tavānugamane rājanviddhimāṃ kṛtaniścayam|| na cānyadadya vaktavyamato vīra na śāsanam| vihanyamānamicchāmi madvidhena viśeṣataḥ|| tasya tāṃ buddhimaklībāṃ vijñāya raghunandanaḥ| bāḍhamityeva śatrughnaṃ rāmo vākyamuvāca ha||
english: I have placed my two sons on the throne of my kingdom. I have now resolved upon following you, O King. O hero, do not command me otherwise. I pray only that I may not neglect your command. There upon understanding the firm resolution of Satrughna, the descendant of Raghu agreed.

sanskrit: tasya vākyasya vākyānte vānarāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ| ṛkṣarākṣasasaṅghāśca samāpeturanekaśaḥ||
english: Immediately after Råma had said this, monkeys assuming shapes at will bears and Rākşasas, began to assemble there.

sanskrit: sugrīvaṃ te puraskṛtya sarva eva samāgatāḥ| taṃ rāmaṃ draṣṭumanasaḥ svargāyābhimukhaṃ sthitam|| devaputrā ṛṣisutā gandharvāṇāṃ sutāstathā|
english: Apprised of Rama's determination of going to heaven, monkeys, born of the celestials, Rșis and Gandharvas taking Sugriva before them, came there to see Rama.

sanskrit: rāmakṣayaṃ viditvā te sarva eva samāgatāḥ|| tavānugamane rājansaṃprāptāḥ sma samāgatāḥ| yadi rāma vināsmābhirgacchestvaṃ puruṣocama|| yamadaṇḍamivodyamya tvayā sma vinipātitāḥ| etasminnantare rāmaṃ sugrīvo'pi mahābalaḥ| praṇamya vidhivadvīraṃ vijñāpayitumudyataḥ|21|| abhiṣicyāṅgadaṃ vīramāgato'smi nareśvara| tavānugamane rājanviddhimāṃ kṛtaniścayam||
english: "All they came there knowing the departure of Rāma to heaven and said: ""O Răma, O foremost of men, if you do repair to heaven forsaking us all, it will be hurling Yama's rod upon us.” The highly powerful Sugrīva too saluting Rāma said:— lord of men, having placed Angada on the throne I have come hither. I have determined upon following you, O King."

sanskrit: tairevamuktaḥ kākutstho bāḍhamityabravītsmayan| bibhīṣaṇamathovāca rākṣasendraṃ mahāyaśāḥ|| yāvatprajā dhariṣyanti tāvattvaṃ vai bibhīṣaṇa| rākṣasendra mahāvīrya laṅkāsthaḥ svaṃ dhariṣyasi|| yāvaccandraśca sūryaśca yāvattiṣṭhati medinī| yāvacca matkathā loke tāvadrājyaṃ tavāstviha||25
english: Hearing the words of monkeys, Rāma said that their desire would be fulfilled. He then said to Vibhīşaņa the king of Räkşasas:-As long as people shall breathe, O Vibhisana, O highly powerful lord of Rakşasas, you shall preserve your body in Lankä. As long as the moon, the sun and the earth shall exist and as long as my story shall remain current, your kingdom shall be in existence.

sanskrit: śāsitaśca sakhitvena kārya te mama śāsanam| prajāḥ saṃrakṣa dharmeṇa nottaraṃ vaktumarhasi|| kiṃcānyadvaktumicchāmi rākṣasendra mahābala| ārādhaya jagatrāthamikṣvākukuladaivatam|| ārādhanīyamaniśaṃ deverapi savāsavaiḥ| tatheti pratijagrāha rāmavākyaṃ bibhīṣaṇaḥ| rājā rākṣasamukhyānāṃ rāghavājñāmanusmaran|28||
english: You did, out of friendship, carry out my behests and perform my works. Do you piously govern your subjects. I should not speak any thing else. What shall I say more to you, O highly powerful lord of Rakşasas. Worshhip Jagannath (the lord of the world), the presiding deity of the Ikşvāku race.

sanskrit: tamevamuktvā kākutstho hanūmantamathābravīt| jīvite kṛtabuddhistvaṃ mā pratijñāṃ vṛthā kṛthāḥ||29 matkathāḥ parcariṣyanti yāvalloke harīśvara| tāvadramasva suprīto madvākyamanupālayan|30|| evamuktastu hanumānarāghaveṇa mahātmanā| vākyaṃ vijñāpayāmāsa paraṃ harṣamavāpa ca|31|| yāvattava kathā loke vicariṣyati pāvanī| tāvatsthāsyāmi medinyāṃ tavājñāmanupālayan||
english: Having thus addressed the king of Rakşasas always obeying Rāghava's command, Käkutstha said to Hanumān:— It is settled that you shall live forever, do you, now observe your promise. As long as my history shall run current in this world do you at my command live happily. Being thus addressed by the high-souled Rāghava Hanumān attained to great delight and said. As long as the sacred theme shall pass current in this world I shall live here carrying out your commands.

sanskrit: yāvatkaliśca saṃprāptastāvajjīvata sarvadā|| jāmbavantaṃ tathoktvā tu vṛddhaṃ brahmasutaṃ tadā| maindaṃ ca dvividaṃ caiva pañca jāmbavatā saha|
english: There upon he said to the Jämbavān, Brahma's son, Mainda, Dvivida and five others in his company: “As long as the Kali age exists do you all live.”

sanskrit: tadevamuktvā kākutsthaḥ sarvāṃstānṛkṣavānarān| uvāca bāḍhaṃ gacchadhvaṃ mayā sādhaṃ yathoditam||
english: Having thus addressed them all Kākuthstha said to bears and monkeys. Do you come all with me.

sanskrit: kṛtabuddhiṃ nivāsāya tatraiva sa munistadā| bharataṃ kekayīputramātithyena nyamantrayat||
english: Then the ascetic asked Bharata, the son of Kaikeyi, when he had decided for staying there, to receive his hospitality.

sanskrit: abravīd bharatastvenaṃ nanvidaṃ bhavatā kṛtam| pādyamaya̭mathātithyaṃ vane yadupapadyate||
english: Thereat Bharata said, “You have for certain done this, (have offered me) water for washing my feet, Arghya, and hospitality with what can be procured in the forest.

sanskrit: athovāca bharadvājo bharataṃ prahasanniva| jāne tvāṃ prītisaṃyuktaṃ tuṣyestvaṃ yena kenacit||
english: "Then Bharadvāja as if in jest, said to Bharata, ""I know you to be of a complacent disposition; and that you are pleased with anything and everything."""

sanskrit: senāyāstu tavaivāsyāḥ kartumicchāmi bhojanam| mama prītiyathārūpā tvamarho manujarṣabha||
english: But I wish to feast your forces. And, O best of men, it behoves you to act in harmony with my desire.

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ cāpi nikṣipya dūre balamihāgataḥ| kasmānnehopayāto'si sabalaḥ puruṣarṣabha||
english: Why did you coming higher, leave your army at a distance:? And, you man of men, why did you not come accompanied with your forces?

sanskrit: bharataḥ pratyuvācedaṃ prāñjalistaṃ tapodhanam| na sainyenopayāto'smi bhagavan bhagavadbhayāt||
english: Bharata replied to him, saying, “I had not come accompanied with my forces, from fear of you, O reverend Sir.”

sanskrit: rājñā hi bhagavan nityaṃ rājaputreṇa vā tathā| yatnataḥ parihartavyā viṣayeṣu tapasvinaḥ||
english: O worshipful one, kings and their sons should always carefully avoid the regions of ascetics.

sanskrit: vājimukhyā manuṣyāśca mattāśca varavāraṇāḥ| pracchādya bhagavan bhūmiṃ mahatīmanuyānti mām||
english: Choice steeds, men, and mad elephants of the best kind, covering a spacious tract of country, come in my train, respected Sir.

sanskrit: te vṛkṣānudakaṃ bhūmimāśrameṣūṭajāṃstathā| na hiṃsyuriti tenāhameka evāgatastataḥ||
english: That these might not injure trees or water or the grounds of the cottages pertaining to the asylums, have I come hither alone.

sanskrit: ānīyatāmitaḥ senetyājñaptaḥ paramarṣiṇā| tathānucakre bharataḥ senāyāḥ samupāgamam||
english: """Bring the forces here,"", thus desired by the mighty ascetic, Bharata accordingly caused the troops to be brought in."

sanskrit: agniśālāṃ praviśyātha pītvāpaḥ parimṛjya ca| ātithyasya kriyāhetorviśvakarmāṇamāhvayat||
english: Then entering the chamber of the sacrificial fire, (Bharadvāja) having sipped water and rubbed his lips therewith, invoked Viśvakarmā for the purpose of entertaining his guest.

sanskrit: āhvaye viśvakarmāṇamahaṃ tvaṣṭārameva ca| ātithyaṃ kartumicchāmi tatra me saṃvidhīyatām||
english: I invoke Visvakarmā; even Tvasta himself. I wish to entertain guests. Let him accomplish this for me.

sanskrit: āhvayelokapālāṃstrīn devāśakrapurogamān| ātithyaṃ kartumicchāmi tatra me saṃvidhīyatām||
english: I invoke the three guardians of the worlds, gods headed by Sakra. I wish to entertain guests. Let them accomplish this for me,

sanskrit: prāksrotasaśca yā nadyastiryaksrotasa eva ca| pṛthivyāmantarikṣe ca samāyāntvadya sarvaśaḥ||
english: Let those rivers that flow westwards, and those that move tortuously on the earth and in the sky, come hither in a body.

sanskrit: anyāḥ sravantu maireyaṃ surāmanyāḥ suniṣṭhitām| aparāścodakaṃ śītamikṣukāṇḍarasopamam||
english: And let others run Maireya, and others refined wine, and others again cool waters resembling the juice of the sugarcane.

sanskrit: āhvaye devagandharvān viśvāvasuhahāhuhūn| tathaivāpsaraso devagandharvaiścāpi sarvaśaḥ||
english: I invoke the celestials and the Gandharvas and Viśvāvasu and Hahā and Huhu and also the divine Apsaras and Gandharvis all.

sanskrit: ghṛtācīmatha viśvācī miśrakeśīmalambuṣām| nāgadattāṃ ca hemāṃ ca somāmadrikṛtasthalīm||
english: And Ghịtâcī, Viśvācī, Misrakesi and Alambuşā; and Nāgadattā and Hemā and Somā residing in the mountain.

sanskrit: śakraṃ yāścopatiṣṭhanti brahmāṇaṃ yāśca bhāminīḥ| sarvāstumburuṇā sārdhamāhvaye saparicchadāḥ||
english: And those ladies that attend Sakra, and those that attend Brahmā. I invoke all these females well attired, in company with Tumuru.

sanskrit: vanaṃ kuruṣu yad divyaṃ vāsobhūṣaṇapatravat| divyanārīphalaṃ śaśvat tatkauberamihaiva tu||
english: And let that beautiful forest of Kubera in the north Kuru, having its foliage resembling attires and ornaments, and its fruits debonair damsels, exist even at this very spot.

sanskrit: iha bhagavān somo vidhattāmannamuttamam| bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca coṣyaṃ ca lehyaṃ ca vividhaṃ bahu|| vicitrāṇi ca mālyāni pādapapracyutāni ca| surādīni ca peyāni māṃsāni vividhāni ca|||
english: And here let the worshipful Soma yield me excellent viands of diverse kinds in plenty; things; that may be eaten or enjoyed, sucked or licked; and variegated blossoms growing in the trees, and wines and (other) drinks, and meats of various kinds.

sanskrit: evaṃ samādhinā yuktastejasāpratimena ca| śikṣāsvarasamāyuktaṃ suvrataścābravīnmuniḥ||
english: Thus, furnished with unrivalled ascetic energy, did that anchorite observing excellent vows, express himself orthoepically in consonance with Śikṣā.

sanskrit: manasā dhyāyatastasya prāmukhasya kṛtāñjaleḥ| ājagmustāni sarvāṇi daivatāni pṛthak pṛthak || me
english: And as he sat with joined hands facing the west with a rapt mind, there came separately all those deities.

sanskrit: malayaṃ darduraṃ caiva tataḥ svedanudo'nilaḥ| upaspṛśya vavau yuktyā supriyātmā sukhaṃ śivaḥ||
english: And then touching Malaya and Dardura, and laden (with perfumes), a delicious and welcome wind began to blow delightfully, removing sweat.

sanskrit: tato'bhyavarṣanta ghanā divyāḥ kusumavṛṣṭayaḥ| devadundubhighoṣaśca dikṣu sarvāsu śuśruve||
english: And the clouds poured down a pleasant shower of blossoms; and from all sides were heard sounds of celestial kettle-drums.

sanskrit: pravavuścottamā vātā nanṛtuścāpsarogaṇāḥ| prajagurdevagandharvā vīṇāḥ pramumucuḥ svarān ||
english: And a rare breeze set in, and the multitudes of Apsaras danced; and the celestials and the Gandharvas sang, and the Vinas let out their notes.

sanskrit: sa śabdo dyāṃ ca bhūmī ca prāṇināṃ śravaṇāni ca| viveśoccāvacaḥ ślakṣṇaḥ samo layaguṇānvitaḥ||
english: And the dulcet sounds high and low furnished with Sama and measure, entered the Earth and the firmament and the ears of all creatures.

sanskrit: tasminnevaṃgate śabde divye śrotrasukhe nṛṇām| dadarśa bhārataṃ sainyaṃ vidhānaṃ viśvakarmaṇaḥ||
english: When that celestial symphony delightful to the ears of men, had thus developed itself, Bharata's forces saw the workmanship of Visvakarman.

sanskrit: babhūva hi samā bhūmiḥ samantāt pañcayojanam| śādvalairbahubhiśchannā nīlavaidūryasaṃnibhaiḥ||
english: That spot widening into a level plain measuring five Yojanas was covered with thick grass resembling blue lapises.

sanskrit: tasmin bilvāḥ kapitthāśca panasā bījapūrakāḥ| āmalakyo babhūvuśca cūtāśca phalabhūṣitāḥ||
english: And on it stood Bilvas, and Kapitthas, Panasas, citrons, and Amalakas, and mangoes, embellished with fruits.

sanskrit: uttarebhyaḥ kurubhyaśca vanaṃ divyopabhogavat| ājagāma nadī saumyā tīrajairbahubhirvṛtā||
english: From the north Kuru had spread a wood capable of conferring every enjoyment; and a beautiful river coursed through bordered by many a tree.

sanskrit: catuḥśālāni śubhrāṇi śālāśca gajavājinām| harmyaprāsādasaṃyuktatoraṇāni śubhāni ca|| sitameghanibhaṃ cāpi rājaveśma sutoraṇam| śuklamālyakṛtākāraṃ divyagandhasamukṣitam|| caturasramasambādhaṃ śayanāsanayānavat| divyaiḥ sarvarasairyuktaṃ divyabhojanavastravat|| upakalpitasarvānnaṃ dhautanirmalabhājanam| klṛptasarvāsanaṃ śrīmatsvāstīrṇaśayanottamam||
english: And there had arisen white edifices having four divisions; and stables for horses and elephants; and grand gateways belonging to places and mansions; and royal residences with graceful gates, resembling white clouds, bearing white garlands and washed with fragrant waters, having four corners, and spacious, fitted up with beds, seats, and vehicles, having every kind of excellent sapid food, stocked with excellent edibles and apparels, having every variety of food, possessing washed and bright vessels, with every description of seats, graceful, and accommodated with choice beds with coverlets.

sanskrit: praviveśa mahābāhuranujñāto maharṣiṇā| veśma tad ratnasampūrṇa bharataḥ kaikayīsutaḥ|| anujagmuśca te sarve mantriṇaḥ sapurohitāḥ| babhūvuśca mudā yuktāstaṃ dṛṣṭvā veśmasaṃvidhim||
english: Permitted by the Maharsi, Kaikeyi's son, Bharata, entered that mansion abounding in gems. And he was followed by the counsellors and the priests; and the latter beholding the arrangements of the palace, were filled with delight.

sanskrit: tatra rājāsanaṃ divyaṃ vyajanaṃ chatrameva ca| bharato mantribhiḥ sārdhamabhyavartata rājavat||
english: And Bharata in company with the counsellors there went round the august royal seat, the chowri, and the umbrella, worthy of a king. And having bowed down to Rāma, he worshipped that seat.

sanskrit: āsanaṃ pūjayāmāsa rāmāyābhipraṇamya ca| vālavyajanamādāya nyaṣīdat sacivāsane||
english: And then holding the chowri of hair, he sat down on the seat of a minister.

sanskrit: ānupūrvyāniṣeduśca sarve mantripurohitāḥ| tataḥ senāpatiḥ paścāt praśāstā ca nyaṣīdata||
english: Then the counsellors and priests seated themselves according to rank. And thereafter the general and the protector of the encampment (got themselves seated).

sanskrit: tatastatra muhūrtena nadyaḥ pāyasakardamāḥ| upātiṣṭhanta bharataṃ bharadvājasya śāsanāt||
english: Then at Bharadvāja's command, came into being near Bharata streams having Pāyasa for their slime.

sanskrit: āsāmubhayataḥ kūlaṃ pāṇḍumṛttikalepanāḥ| ramyāścāvasathā divyā brāhmaṇasya prasādajāḥ||
english: And at the pleasure of the Brāhmaṇa, on both their banks arose charming dwellings, covered with pale clay.

sanskrit: tenaiva ca muhūrtena divyābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ| āgurviṃśatisāhasrā brāhmaṇā prahitāḥ striyaḥ|||
english: And at that very moment there came twenty thousand women commissioned by Brahma, adorned with divine ornaments.

sanskrit: suvarṇamaṇimuktena pravālena ca śobhitāḥ| āgurviṃśatisāhasrāḥ kuberaprahitāḥ striyaḥ|| yābhirgṛhītaḥ puruṣaḥ sonmāda iva lakṣyate|
english: And there came also twenty thousand females sent by Kuvera, decked out in gold and gems, pearls and corals. The sight of these was capable of filling men's mind with enchanting ravishment.

sanskrit: āgurviṃśatisāhasrā nandanādapsarogaṇāḥ|| nāradastumbururgopaḥ prabhayā sūryavarcasaḥ| ete gandharvarājāno bharatasyāgrato jaguḥ||
english: And there came from Nandana twenty thousand damsels; and Nārada and Tumburů and Gopa, resembling the sun in splendour. The Gandharba kings began to sing before Bharata.

sanskrit: alambuṣā miśrakeśī puṇḍarīkātha vāmanā| upānṛtyanta bharataṃ bharadvājasya śāsanāt||
english: And Alambusa, and Misrakesi, and Puņdarīka, and Vāmana danced before Bharata, at the command of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: yāni mālyāni deveṣu yāni caitrarathe vane| prayāge tānyadṛśyanta bharadvājasya tejasā||
english: And those blossoms that are in the celestial regions, and that bloom in the forest of Caitraratha, became visible in Prayāga at the energy of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: bilvā mārdaṅgikā āsan śamyāgrāhā bibhītakāḥ| aśvatthā nartakāścāsan bharadvājasya tejasā||
english: And Vilwas did the office of players of the Mặdanga, and Bibhitakas, that of keepers of Soma, and Asvatthas became dancers, at the energy of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: tataḥ saralatālāśca tilakāḥ satamālakāḥ| prahṛṣṭāstatra sampetuḥ kubjā bhūtvātha. vāmanāḥ||
english: And Saralas, Tālas, Tilakas, and Tamālas, being delighted, became hump-backed ones and dwarfs.

sanskrit: śiṃśapāmalakī jambūryāścānyāḥ kānane latāḥ| mālatī mallikā jātiyaścānyāḥ kānane latāḥ| pramadāvigrahaṃ kṛtvā bharadvājāśrame'vasan||
english: And Sinsapās, Āmalakīs, Jambūs and other plants of the forest, wearing the forms of females, stood at the mansion of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: surāṃ surāpāḥ pibata pāyasaṃ ca bubhukṣitāḥ| māṃsāni ca sumedhyāni bhakṣyantāṃ yo yadicchati||
english: Let wine-drinkers drink wine, the hungry eat Pāyasa, and those that are inclined to it, feed on clean meat.

sanskrit: ucchodya snāpayanti sma nadītīreṣu valguṣu | apyekamekaṃ puruṣaṃ pramadāḥ sapta cāṣṭa ca||
english: And every seven or eight females taking a man, bathed him on the lovely banks of the rivers.

sanskrit: saṃvāhantyaḥ samāpeturnāryo vipulalocanāḥ| parimṛjya tadānyonyaṃ pāyayanti varāṅganāḥ||
english: And damsels furnished with expansive eyes, having wiped the persons (of the bathers), pressed their legs, and those magnificent women made them drink (wine).

sanskrit: hayān gajān kharānuṣṭrāṃstathaiva surabheḥ sutān| abhojayan vāhanapāsteṣāṃ bhojyaṃ yathāvidhi||
english: And the keepers duly fed excellent horses, elephants, camels and Surabhi's sons (oxen), with their (proper) food.

sanskrit: ikhūśca madhulājāṃśca bhojayanti sma vāhanān| ikṣvākuvarayodhānāṃ codayanto mahābalāḥ||
english: And some persons possessed of mighty strength, being directed thereto, fed the bearers of the foremost Ikşvāku warriors with sugercanes, honey, and fried paddy.

sanskrit: nāśvabandho'śvamājānānna gajaṃ kuñjaragrahaḥ| mattapramattamuditā sā camūstatra sambabhau||
english: And the groom forgot his horse, and the elephant-keeper his elephant: that army there became transported with wine and exhilaration.

sanskrit: tarpitāḥ sarvakāmaiśca raktacandanaruṣitāḥ| apsarogaṇasaṃyuktāḥ sainyā vācamudīrayan||
english: And sumptuously entertained with every enjoyment, with their bodies decked with red sandal, the soldiery in the company of bevies of Apsaras, exclaimed.

sanskrit: naivāyodhyāṃ gamiṣyāmo na gamiṣyāma daṇḍakān| kuśalaṃ bharatasyāstu rāmasyāstu tathā sukham||
english: To Ayodhyā will we not go, nor yet to Dandaka. Peace be to Bharata, and may Rāma reap happiness!

sanskrit: iti pādātayodhāśca hastyaśvārohabandhakāḥ| anāthāstaṃ vidhiṃ labdhvā vācametāmudīrayan||
english: Thus did footmen and the riders and keepers of elephants and horses, as well as others, having experienced such a state, utter words.

sanskrit: samprahṛṣṭā vineduste narāstatra sahasraśaḥ| bharatasyānuyātāraḥ svargo'yamiti cābruvan|| nṛtyantaśca hasantaśca gāyantaścaiva sainikāḥ| samantāt paridhāvanto mālyopetāḥ sahasraśaḥ||
english: And men by thousand, exceedinly delighted, sent up shouts. And saying. “This is heaven,” the retiune of Bharata, the soldiers, began to dance and laugh and sing; and bearing garlands, they on all sides rushed by thousands.

sanskrit: tato bhuktavatāṃ teṣāṃ tadannamamṛtopamam| divyānudvīkṣya bhakṣyāṃstānabhavad bhakṣaṇe matiḥ||
english: And beholding the inviting viands resembling ambrosia, they although already fed, became desirous of eating once again.

sanskrit: preṣyāśceṭyaśca vadhvaśca balasthāścāpi sarvaśaḥ| babhūvuste bhṛśaṃ prītāḥ sarve cāhatavāsasaḥ||
english: And wearing new clothes, all the servants, and maids, and females of the household, became exceedingly well pleased.

sanskrit: kuñjarāśca khagoṣṭrāśca go'śvāśca mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ| babhūvuḥ subhṛtāstatra nāto hyanyamakalpayam||
english: And elephants, and asses, camels, kine and horses, and beats and birds, being fed their fill, did not hunger after anything else.

sanskrit: nāśuklavāsāstatrāsīt kṣudhito malino'pi vā| rajasā dhvastakeśo vā naraḥ kaścidadṛśyata||
english: And there appeared no one who wore a soiled habit, or who was hungry, or melancholy, or whose hair was covered with dust.

sanskrit: ājaiścāpi,ca vārāhairniṣṭhānavarasaṃcayaiḥ| phalaniṣūhasaṃsiddhaiḥ sūpairgandharasānvitaiḥ|| puṣpadhvajavatīḥ pūrṇāḥ śuklasyānasya cābhitaḥ| dadṛśurvismitāstatra narā lauhīḥ sahasraśaḥ||
english: And the people with wonder beheld before them vessels of precious metals by thousands graceful with chaplets of flowers, filled with essences of fruits and fragrant soups and curries and the flesh of goats and bears, and white rice.

sanskrit: babhūvurvanapārveṣu kūpāḥ pāyasakardamāḥ| tāśca kāmadudhā gāvo dumāścāsan madhucyutaḥ||
english: And there were on the skirts of the wood wells having Pāyasa for their slime; and the kine yeilded whatever was asked and all the trees dropped honey.

sanskrit: vāpyo maireyapūrṇāśca mṛṣṭamāṃsacayairvṛtāḥ| prataptapiṭharaiścāpi mārgamāyūrakaukkuṭaiḥ||
english: And the tanks were filled with Maireya as well as with clean hot meat of dear, peacocks, and cocks, dressed in pans.

sanskrit: pātrīṇāṃ ca sahasrāṇi sthālīnāṃ niyutāni ca| nyarbudāni ca pātrāṇi śātakumbhamayāni ca|71||
english: And there were rice-holders by thousands, and curry-pots by hundred thousands, and golden vessels by Arbudas.

sanskrit: sthālyaḥ kumbhyaḥ karambhyaśca dadhipūrṇāḥ susaṃskṛtāḥ| yauvanasthasya gaurasya kapitthasya sugandhinaḥ|| hradāḥ pūrṇā rasālasya danaḥ śvetasya cāpare| babhūvuḥ pāyasasyānye śarkarāṇāṃ ca saṃcayāḥ||
english: And there were pitchers and water-pots and cleaned vessels for churning curd, filled with the same. And there were tanks of savoury and yellow butter-milk, well-tempered. And there were tanks filled with Rasāla;* and others filled with milk, and with sugar. *A preparation of butter-milk.

sanskrit: kalkāṃścūrṇakaṣāyāṃśca snānāni vividhāni ca| dadṛśurbhājanasthāni tīrtheṣu saritāṃ narāḥ|| śuklānaṃśumataścāpi dantadhāvanasaṃcayān| śuklāṃścandanakalkāṃśca samudreṣvavatiṣṭhataḥ|| darpaṇān parimṛṣṭāṃśca vāsasāṃ cāpi saṃcayān| pādukopānahaṃ caiva yugmānyatra sahasraśaḥ|| āñjanīḥ kaṅkatān kūrcāśchatrāṇi ca dhanūṃṣi ca| marmatrāṇāni citrāṇi śayanānyāsanāni ca||
english: And men saw sediments, acrid powders and various others things in vessels, for the purpose of bath, on the terraces of tanks; and toothcleaning sticks of Ansuman and other (trees); and white sandal paste lying before; and cleaned mirros; and lots of cloths; and sandals; and shoes in pairs by thousand; and collyrium-pots; and combs; and brushes; and bows at some places; and mail; and various kinds of seats and beds.

sanskrit: pratipānahvadān pūrṇān kharoṣṭragajavājinām| avagāhya sutīrthāṃśca hradān sotpalapuṣkarān| ākāśavarṇapratimān svacchatoyān sukhāplavān|| nīlavaidūryavarṇāśca mṛdūn yavasasaṃcayān| nirvāpārthaṃ paśūnāṃ te dadṛśustatra sarvaśaḥ|79 ||
english: And they saw reservoirs for asses, camels, elephants, and horses, with easy descents, filled with water to assist their digestion; and pools furnished with lotuses, of the hue of the firmament, with transparent water, comfortable for ablutions; and tender (plots of) grass all around coloured like blue lapises, to serve as pasture for beasts.

sanskrit: 'vyasmayanta manuṣyāste svapnakalpaṃ tadadbhutam| dṛṣṭvā'tithyaṃ kṛtaṃ tādṛg bharatasya maharṣiṇā||
english: Witnessing the wonderful hospitality provided by the Maharşi Bharadvāja, like to a vision, the men marvelled.

sanskrit: ityevaṃ ramamāṇānāṃ devānāmiva nandane| bharadvājāśrame ramye sā rātrirvyatyavartata ||
english: Thus entertained like to celestials in Nandana, they passed the night at the hermitage of Bharadvāja.

sanskrit: pratijagmuśca tā nadyo gandharvāśca yathāgatam| bharadvājamanujñāpya tāśca sarvā varāṅganāḥ||
english: Then taking the permission of Bharadvāja, all the Gandharvas as well as the superb damsels went away as they had come.

sanskrit: stathaiva divyāgurucandanokṣitāḥ| tathaiva divyā vividhāḥ sraguttamāḥ pṛthagvikīrṇā manujaiḥ pramarditāḥ||
english: And the men remained intoxicated and highly inebriate with the liquor, their persons daubed with goodly aguru and sandal; and the various elegant garlands beautiful to behold, lay by themselves all around, crushed by the people.

sanskrit: svabalaṃ vyathitaṃ dṛṣṭvā tumulaṃ lomaharṣaṇam| bhrātṛ̭śca nihatāndṛṣṭvā śakratulyaparākramān|| pitṛvyau cāpi saṃdṛśya samare saṃnipātitau| yuddhonmattaṃ ca mattaṃ ca bhrātarau rākṣasottamau|2|| cukopa ca mahātejā brahmadattavaro yudhi| atikāyo'drisaṃkāśo devadānavadarpahā||
english: Seeing in sore straits his own mighty forces capable of making people's down stand on end, and seeing his brothers resembling Sakra in prowess, routed; and seeing also his uncles brought down in battle, as well as his brothersYuddhonmatta and Matta— foremost of Råkş asas, that crusher of the pride of deities and Dānavas-the exceedingly energetic Atikāya-resembling a hill, who had obtained from Brahmă a boon in battle, was fired with wrath.

sanskrit: sa bhāskarasahasrasya saṃghātamiva bhāsvaram| rathamāruhya śakrārirabhidudrāva vānarān||
english: Ascending a car effulgent like a thousand suns mingling their rays into a burst of brilliance, that enemy of Sakra, charged the monkeys.

sanskrit: sa visphārya tadā cāpaṃ kirīṭī mṛṣṭakuṇḍalaḥ| nāma saṃśrāvayāmāsa nanāda ca mahāsvanam||
english: Stretching his bow, (Atikāya) decked with a diadem wearing polished ear-rings, proclaimed his name (among the monkey-ranks) and shouted in lofty tones.

sanskrit: tena siṃhapraṇādena nāmaviśrāvaṇena ca| jyāśabdena ca bhīmena trāsayāmāsa vānarān|6||
english: And with his leonine roars and the proclamation of his name, and the tremendous twang of his bow-string, he struck terror into the monkeys.

sanskrit: te dṛṣṭvā dehamāhātmyaṃ kumbhakarmo'yamutthitaḥ| bhayārtā vānarāḥ sarve saṃśrayante parasparam||
english: Seeing the magnitude of his person, the monkeys thinking that it was Kumbhakarna who had come, and affrighted thereat, sought the shelter of each other.

sanskrit: te tasya rūpamālokya yathā viṣṇostrivikrame| bhayādvānarayodhāste vidravanti tatastataḥ|||||
english: Seeing his form like to that of Vişnu when he displayed his threefold energy, the monkeywarriors seized with fear, began to scour on all sides.

sanskrit: te'tikārya samāsādya vānarā mūḍhacetasaḥ| śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ jagmurlakṣmaṇāgrajamāhave||
english: On Atikāya appearing before them, the monkeys stupefied in that conflict, saught the shelter of Laksmana's elder brother.

sanskrit: tato'tikāyaṃ kākutstho rathasthaṃ parvatopamam| dadarśa dhanvinaṃ dūrāgarjantaṃ kālameghavat||
english: And from a distance Kakutstha saw the mountain-like Atikāya mounted on the car and equipped with his bow, like to roaring clouds (seen) on the occasion of the universal disruption.

sanskrit: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahākāyaṃ rāghavastu suvismitaḥ| vānarānsāntvayitvā ca vibhīṣaṇamuvāca ha|||
english: Seeing that huge-bodied one, Rāghava struck with surprise, comforting the monkeys, addressed Vibhisana, saying.

sanskrit: ko'sau parvatasaṃkāśo dhanuṣmānharilocanaḥ| yukte hayasahasreṇa viśāle syandane sthitaḥ|| ya eṣa niśitaiḥ śūlaiḥ sutīkṣṇaiḥ prāsatomaraiḥ| arciṣmadbhirvṛto bhāti bhūtairiva maheśvaraḥ|| kālajihvāprakāśābhirya eṣo'bhivirājate| āvṛto rathaśaktībhirvidyudbhiriva toyadaḥ||
english: Who is this one resembling a mountain, furnished with a bow and having leonine eyes, that is stationed on a large car hoked with a thousand steeds, he that with effulgent sharpened darts and keen práśas and tomaras, shine like Maheśvara environed by spectres-he that displaying his fatal tongue appear splendid surrounded with darts in his car; like a mass of clouds graced with lightning.

sanskrit: dhanūṃṣi cāsya sajjāni hemapṛṣṭhāni sarvaśaḥ| śobhayanti rathaśreṣṭhaṃ śakracāpamivāmbaram||
english: And his bows adorned and backed with gold all over, beautify his car even as Indra's bow beautify the firmament.

sanskrit: ya eṣa rakṣaḥśārdūlo raṇabhūmiṃ virājayat| abhyeti rathināṃ śreṣṭho rathenādityavarcasā|| dhvajaśṛṅgapratiṣṭhena rāhuṇābhivirājate| sūryaraśmiprabhairbāṇardiśo daśa virājayan|| trinataṃ meghanidiṃ hemapṛṣṭhamalaṃkṛtam| śatakratudhanuḥprakhyaṃ dhanuścāsya virājate||
english: Who is this foremost of Räkşasas and best of bowmen that embellishing the field of battle, approach on a car glorious as the sun; who, . displaying the ten cardinal points with his shafts resembling the rays of the sun, appear handsome with his peak of a banner bearing the figure of Rāhu, whose bow bent in three places, emitting roars resembling the rumbling of clouds, and plated with gold, look like the bow itself of Satakratu?

sanskrit: sadhvajaḥ sapatākaśca sānukarṣoṃ mahārathaḥ| catuḥsādisamāyukto meghastanitaniḥsvanaḥ||
english: His mighty car furnished with a banner and ensign and bottom, and having clatter resembling the roaring of clouds, has four horsemen (attached to it).

sanskrit: viṃśatirdaśa cāṣṭau ca tūṇāsya rathamāsthitāḥ| kārmukāṇi ca bhīmāni jyāśca kāñcanapiṅgalāḥ||
