english: There are on the car eight and thirty quivers and dreadful bows and yellow-golden bowstrings.

sanskrit: dvau ca khaṅgau ca pārśvasthau pradīpau pārśvaśobhitau| caturhastatsarucitau vyaktahastadaśāyatau||
english: There are (in that car) two effulgent swords at iis side, illumining it, their hafts measuring four lands and their blades ten each.

sanskrit: raktakaṇṭhaguṇo dhīro mahāparvatasaṃnibhaḥ| kālaḥ kālamahāvakro meghastha iva bhāskaraḥ||
english: That calm (warrior) wears red garlands about is neck, and resembles-a mighty mountain. And very destroyer, he has a mighty mouth, appearing like that of the destroyer himself; and he look like the sun stationed on clouds.

sanskrit: kāñcanāṅgadanadvābhyāṃ bhujābhyāmeṣa śobhane| śṛṅgābhyāmiva tuṅgābhyāṃ himavānparvatottamaḥ||
english: With his arms adorned with golden angadas, he appear splendid like that best of mountains the Himavān with its towering summits.

sanskrit: kuṇḍalābhyāmubhābhyāṃ ca bhāti vakraṃ subhīṣaṇam| punarvasvantaragataḥ paripūrṇo niśākaraḥ||
english: With his pair of ear-rings, his charming yet terrific countenance shine like the full Moon entering into Punarvasu.* *The seventh lunar asterism.

sanskrit: ācakṣva me mahābāho tvamenaṃ rākṣasottamam| yaṃ dṛṣṭvā vānarāḥ sarve bhayārtā vidrutā diśaḥ||
english: O mighty-armed one, tell me all about this foremost of Rākşasas, seeing whom the monkeys, overwhelmed with fear, fly away in all directions.

sanskrit: sa pṛṣṭo rājaputreṇa rāmeṇāmitatejasā| ācacakṣe mahātejā rāghavāya vibhīṣaṇaḥ||
english: Asked by the king's son Rāma of immeasurable prowess, the exceedingly energetic Vibhīşaņa spoke to Rāma, informing him.

sanskrit: daśagrīvo mahātejā rājā vaiśravaṇānujaḥ| bhīmakarmā mahātmā hi rāvaṇo rākṣaseśvaraḥ|| tasyāsīdvīryavānputro rāvaṇapratimo bale| vṛddhasevī śrutidharaḥ sarvastraviduṣāṃ varaḥ||
english: The highly powerful .king, Vaisravana's younger brother of dreadful deeds, the highsouled Rävaņa, is the sovereign of the Rāks asas. This one is his mighty son, like to Rāvaņa himself in strength. He serve the aged, is of wide celebrity and is the prime of those versed in all branches of knowledge.

sanskrit: aśvapṛṣṭhe nāgapṛṣṭhe khaḍne dhanuṣi karṣaṇe| bhede sāntve ca dāne ca naye mantre ca saṃmataḥ|| yasya bāhuṃ samāśritya laṅkā bhavati nirbhayā| tanayaṃ dhānyamālinyā atikāyamimaṃ viduḥ||
english: He is competent to ride horses and elephants, to wield the sword or draw the bcw, or in sowing dissensions, or giving away, or in counsel, he reposing in whose arm Lanka has cast off fear. Know him to be Atikāya, son to Dhānyamāli.

sanskrit: etenārādhito brahmā tapasā bhāvitātmanā| astrāṇi cāpyavāptāni ripavaśca parājitāḥ||
english: Having adored the pure-souled Brahma with austerities, he has obtained weapons, and has defeated his foes (in fight).

sanskrit: surāsurairavadhyatvaṃ dattamasmai svayaṃbhuvā| etacca kavacaṃ divyaṃ rathaśca ravibhāsvaraḥ||
english: You shall be incapable of being slain by celestials and Asura's was the boon conferred on him by the self-sprung; and he also gave him this celestial mail and this car resembling the effulgent Sun himself.

sanskrit: etena śataśo devā dānavāśca parājitāḥ| rakṣitāni ca rakṣāṃsi yakṣāścāpi niṣūditāḥ||
english: He has vanquished (in battle) hundreds of deities and Dänavas; and he has always) protected the Rakşasas, and destroyed Yakşas.

sanskrit: vajaṃ viṣṭambhitaṃ yena bāṇairindrasya dhīmatā| pāśaḥ salilarājasya yuddhe pratihatastathā ||
english: This intelligent one resisted the thunder-bolt itself of Indra; and in encounter baffled the very noonse of the king of waters.

sanskrit: eṣo'tikāyo balavānrākṣasānāmatharṣabhaḥ| sa rāvaṇasuto dhīmāndevadānavadarpahā||
english: This one is Atikāya-foremost of Raksasas; and that son of Rāvana is the humbler of the hauteur of deities and Dänavas.

sanskrit: tadasminkriyatāṃ yatnaḥ kṣipraṃ puruṣapuṅgava| purā vānarasainyāni kṣayaṃ nayati sāyakaiḥ||
english: Therefore, O best of persons, do you endeavour your best. This one with his shafts slaughter the monkey-hosts before (us).

sanskrit: tato'tikāyo balavānpraviśya harivāhinīm| visphārayāmāsa dhanurnanāda ca punaḥ punaḥ||
english: Then the powerful Atikāya entering that monkey-force, stretched his bow and shouted again and again.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmavapuṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā rathasthaṃ rathināṃ varam| abhipeturmahātmānaḥ pradhānā ye vanaukasaḥ|| kumudo dvivido maindo nīlaḥ śarabha eva ca| pādapairgiriśṛṅgaiśca yugapatsamabhidravan||
english: The high-souled principal monkeys, seeing that (hero) possessed of a dreadful person, that best of car-warriors-stationed on his car, rushed forward. And Kumuda and Dvivida and Mainda and Nila and Sarabha dashed on at one time with trees and mountain-peaks.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vṛkṣāṃśca śailāṃśca śaraiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ| atikāyo mahātejāścicchedāstravidāṃ varaḥ|4||
english: Thereupon that foremost of those skilled in weapons, the exceedingly energetic Atikāya, severed those trees and rocks by means of shafts dight with gold.

sanskrit: tāṃścaiva sarvānsa harīśaraiḥ sarvāyasaibalī| vivyādhābhimukhānsaṃkhye bhīmakāyo viśāradaḥ||
english: In that encounter that powerful one possessed of a gigantic person, skilled in arms, pierced all those monkeys staying before him with arrows entirely made of iron.

sanskrit: te'rditā bāṇavarṣeṇa bhinnagātrāḥ parājitāḥ| na śekuratikāyasya pratikatuṃ mahāhave|||
english: And agonised, having their persons pierced in that mighty conflict by that arrowy shower, they were incapable of resisting the same.

sanskrit: tatsainyaṃ harivīrāṇāṃ trāsayāmāsa rākṣasaḥ| mṛgayūthamiva kruddho hariyauvanadarpitaḥ|||
english: The Rakşasas terrified that host of monkeyheroes, even as an enraged lion priding in his youth terrify a society of deer.

sanskrit: sa rākṣasendro hariyūthamadhye nāyudhyamānaṃ nijaghāna kaṃcit| utpatya rāmaṃ ca dhanu:kalāpī sagarvitaṃ vākyamidaṃ babhāṣe||
english: In the midst of those bands of monkeys, that lord of Raksasas did not slay anyone without battle. And then springing up before Rāma, that one furnished with his bow and quiver, addressed him in haughty words, saying.

sanskrit: naprākṛtaṃ kaṃcana yodhayāmi| yasyāsti śaktirvyavasāyayukto dadātu me śīghramihādya yuddham||
english: Stationed in this car holding the bow and arrows in my hands, I will not fight any that is ignoble. Him that has strength, and that also understand this business, let him today speedily give me battle.

sanskrit: tattasya vākyaṃ bruvato niśamya cukopa saumitriramitrahantā| amṛṣyamāṇaśca samutpapāta jagrāha cāpaṃ ca tataḥ smayitvā ||
english: Hearing his speech, that slayer of foesSumitrā's son, was fired with wrath. And not bearing him, he sprang forward disregarding his antagonist's words, and took up his bow.

sanskrit: kruddhaḥ saumitrirutpatya tūṇādākṣipya sāyakam| purastādatikāyasya vicakarṣa mahaddhanuḥ||
english: And flying to fury, Sumitra's son, darting up, took out arrows from his quiver, and stretched his mighty bow in front of Atikāya.

sanskrit: pūrayansa mahīṃ sarvāmākāśaṃ sāgaraṃ diśaḥ| jyāśabdo lakṣmaṇasyograstrāsayanrajanīcarān||
english: Filling the entire earth and the sky and the ocean and all the cardinal quarters, the terrific twang of Lakşmaņa's bow struck terror into the (hearts of the) night-rangers.

sanskrit: saumitreścāpanirghoṣaṃ śrutvā pratibhayaṃ tadā| visiṣmiye mahātejā rākṣasendrātmajo balī||
english: Hearing the dreadful twang of the bow of Sumitrā's son , the exceedingly energetic and powerful son of the lord of Rākşasas was struck with surprise.

sanskrit: tadātikāyaḥ kupito dṛṣṭvā lakṣmaṇamutthitam| ādāya niśitaṃ bāṇamidaṃ vacanamabravīt||
english: Then Atikāya, enraged, seeing Lakşmaņa advance, taking sharpened shafts, spoke to him.

sanskrit: bālastvamasi saumitre vikrameṣvavicakṣaṇaḥ| gaccha kiṃ kālasaṃkāśaṃ māṃ yodhayitumicchasi||
english: You are a bc/, O Sumitra's sons and as such know not how to display prowess. Go you. Why wish you to fight with me resembling death itself.

sanskrit: nahi madbāhusṛṣṭānāṃ bāṇānāṃ himavānapi| soḍhumutsahate vegamantarikṣamatho mahī||
english: Not Himālaya itself or the firmament or the earth is capable of bearing the impetuosity of shafts shot by my arms.

sanskrit: sukhaprasuptaṃ kālāgni vibodhayitumicchasi| nyasya cāpaṃ nivartasva prāṇānna jahimadgataḥ||
english: You wish to rouse a fire slumbering sweetly. Leaving alone your bow, do you return. Do not lose your life by coming in contact with me.

sanskrit: athavā tvaṃ pratistabdho na nivartitumicchasi| tiṣṭha prāṇānparityajya gamiṣyasi yamakṣayam||
english: Or it may be that you are proud; and therefore, have no mind to return. Stay then. Renouncing your life, you shall go to Yama's mansion.

sanskrit: paśya me niśitānbāṇānirapudarpaniṣūdanān| īśvarāyudhasaṃkāśāṃstaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇān| 55 ||
english: Behold my whetted arrows-crushers of the insolence of foes resembling the weapon itself of the Lord,* adorned with burnished gold. *Isvara, Siva, His weapon is the trident.

sanskrit: eṣa te sarpasaṃkāśo bāṇaḥ pāsyati śoṇitam| mṛgarāja iva kruddho nāgarājasya śoṇitam| ityevamuktvā saṃkruddhaḥ śaraṃ dhanuṣi saṃdadhe||
english: Even as a lion enraged shedded the blood of a mighty elephant, this arrow of mine resembling a serpent shall shed your blood. Having delivered himself thus, he fired with wrath set his shaft on his bow.

sanskrit: śrutvātikāyasya vacaḥ saroṣaṃ sagarvitaṃ saṃyati rājaputraḥ| sa saṃcukopātibalo manasvī uvāca vākyaṃ ca tato bṛhacchrīḥ||
english: Hearing in that encounter Atikāya's wrathful speech fraught with hauteur, the highly powerful and intelligent son of the king possessed of exceeding grace, was transported with passion; and he said.

sanskrit: na vākyamātreṇa bhavānpradhāno na katthanātsatpuruṣā bhavanti| mayi sthite dhanvini bāṇapāṇau nidarśayasvātmabalaṃ durātman||
english: You can not attain pre-eminence solely by virtue of your speech. One cannot be a worthy person simply by say. O wicked-minded one, do you display your strength on me equipped with the bow and holding arrows in my hands.

sanskrit: karmaṇā sūcayātmānaṃ na vikasthitumarhasi | pauruṣeṇa tu yo yuktaḥ sa tu śūra iti smṛtaḥ| 59||
english: Manifest yourself by your valour, you ought not to blow your own trumpet. He, who is actually powerful identified as a real gallant.

sanskrit: sarvāyudhasamāyukto dhanvī tvaṃ rathamāsthitaḥ| śarairvā yadi vāpyastrairdarśayasva parākramam||
english: Seated on a chariot and skilled in archery you are equipped with all weapons, therefore, you display your own prowess either with your arrows or with arms.

sanskrit: tataḥ śiraste niśitaiḥ pātayiṣyāmyahaṃ śaraiḥ| mārutaḥ kālasaṃyuktaṃ vṛntāttālaphalaṃ yathā||
english: Then, I shall cut off your head with my sharpened arrows like wind falls down a palm fruit from its stalk, ripened in the process of time.

sanskrit: adya te māmakā bāṇāstaptakāñcanabhūṣaṇāḥ| pāsyanti rudhiraṃ gātrābāṇaśalyāntarotthitam||
english: To-day shall my shafts decked in gold, drink your blood flowing from your person and issuing of wounds inflicted by my resembling darts.

sanskrit: bālo'yamiti vijñāya na cāvajñātumarhasi| bālo vā yadi vā vṛddho mṛtyu jānīhi saṃyuge||
english: "'This one is a boy', thinking this, you ought not to slight me. Whether I am a boy or an old* man' death shall you know in the conflict. *The commentator says the passage means-""You know (me) for death itself.” I prefer the sense given."

sanskrit: bālena viṣṇunā lokāstrayaḥ krāntāstrivikramaiḥ| lakṣmaṇasya vacaḥ śrutvā hetumatparamārthavat|| atikāyaḥ pracukrodha bāṇaṃ cottamamādade|| tato vidyādharā bhūtā devadaityā maharṣayaḥ| guhyakāśca mahātmānastadyuddhaṃ dadṛśustadā||
english: It was as a boy that Vişņu had overpowered the triune world with his prowess.” Hearing Laksmana's words, fraught with reason and high sense, Vidyadharas and ghosts, deities, Daityas out arrows and Maharşis, and the high-souled Guhyakas then beheld that marvel.* *The encounter that ensued between Lakşmaņa and Atikāya.

sanskrit: tato'tikāyaḥ kupitaścāpamāropya sāyakam| lakṣmaṇāya pracikṣepa saṃkṣipanniva cāmbaram||
english: Then Atikāya, enraged, setting his arrow on his bow, shot it at Lakşmaņa, as if devouring up the welkin.

sanskrit: tamāpatantaṃ niśitaṃ śaramāśīviṣopamam| ardhacandreṇa ciccheda lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā||
english: Thereat, Lakşmaņa-slayer of hostile heroes-with a crescent severed that sharpened shaft resembling a venomous serpent, as it was descending.

sanskrit: taṃ nikṛttaṃ śaraṃ dṛṣṭvā kṛttabhogamivoragam| atikāyo bhṛśaṃ kruddhaḥ pañca bāṇānsamādadhe|| tāśarānsaṃpracikṣepa lakṣmaṇāya niśācaraḥ| tānaprāptāśitairbāṇaiściccheda bharatānujaḥ||
english: Seeing the shaft severed, like a serpent having its person cut off, Atikāya waxing exceedingly enraged, took up five arrow; and the nightranger discharged them at Lakşmaņa. Thereat Bharata's younger brother cut off the approaching arrows with whetted shafts.

sanskrit: sa tāñchittvā śitairbāṇairlakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā| ādade niśitaṃ bāṇaṃ jvalantamiva tejasā ||
english: Having severed them with sharpened shafts, Lakşmaņa— slayer of hostile heroes-took up a sharpened arrow, as if flaming in energy.

sanskrit: tamādāya dhanuḥśreṣṭhe yojayāmāsa lakṣmaṇaḥ| vicakarṣa ca vegena visasarja ca sāyakam||
english: And taking it, Lakşmaņa set it on his excellent bow; and drawing the latter, vigorously discharged the shaft.

sanskrit: pūrṇāyatavisṛṣṭena śareṇa nataparvaṇā| lalāṭe rākṣasaśreṣṭhamājaghāna sa vīryavān|72||
english: That hero endowed with prowess hit that foremost of Rākşasas in the forehead with that i shaft having bent knots, discharged from his bow drawn to its full bent.

sanskrit: sa lalāṭe śaro magnatasya bhīmasya rakṣasaḥ| dadṛśe śoṇitenāktaḥ pannagendra ivācale|73||
english: That arrow piercing the forehead of that dreadful Raksasas, and smeared with blood, appeared like the lord of serpents in a mountain.

sanskrit: rākṣasaḥ pracakampe'tha lakṣmaṇeṣuprapīḍitaḥ| rudrabāṇahataṃ ghoraṃ yathā tripuragopuram|| cintayāmāsa cāśvasya vimṛśya ca mahābalaḥ|74|| sādhu bāṇanipātena ślāghanīyo'si me ripuḥ|
english: The Raksasas, smarting under Laksmana's shaft, showered, like the dreadful gateway of Tripura battered by Rudra. Then recovering himself and reflecting, he said.* *Cintayāmasa-thought, I apprehend, means said in this connection.

sanskrit: vidhāyaivaṃ vidāryāsyaṃ vinamya ca mahābhujau| sa rathopasthamāsthāya rathena pracacāra ha!75 ||
english: Excellent well! By this discharge of your shaft, you approve yourself as a foe in whom I can well glory. Having spoken thus candidly, he, folding his hands at ease, and seated on the platform of his car, began to range in it.

sanskrit: ekaṃ trīpañca saptati sāyakānrākṣasarṣabhaḥ| ādade saṃdadhe cāpi vicakarṣotsasarja ca|76 ||
english: Then that foremost of Raksasas began to take up, set and shoot one, three, five, or seven shafts.

sanskrit: te bāṇāḥ kālasaṃkāśā rākṣasendradhanuścyutāḥ| hemapuṅkhā raviprakhyāścardīptamivāmbaram||
english: Those shafts resembling Fate itself, plated with gold at the feathered parts, and looking like the Sun himself (in splendour), discharged from the bow of the lord of Rakşasas, lighted up the heavens.

sanskrit: tatastārākṣasotsṛṣṭāśaraughānarāghavānujaḥ| asaṃbhrāntaḥ praciccheda niśitairbahubhiḥ śaraiḥ||
english: Thereat Raghava's younger brother by means of many a sharpened shaft calmly cut off all those vollies of arrows shot by the Rakşasas.

sanskrit: tāśarānyudhi saṃprekṣya nikṛttānrāvaṇātmajaḥ| cukopa tridaśendrārirjagrāha niśitaṃ śaram||
english: And finding all those arrows riven in the encounter, that enemy of the lord of the immortals, Ravana's son, was fired with wrath, and took up a whetted shaft.

sanskrit: sa saṃdhāya mahātejāstaṃ bāṇaṃ sahasotsṛjat| tena saumitrimāyāntamājaghāna stanāntare||
english: Then aiming that arrow, that highly powerful one suddenly shot it; and with that, rushing on, hit Sumitra's son in the chest.

sanskrit: atikāyena saumitristāḍito yudhi vakṣasi| susrāva rudhiraṃ tīvra madaṃ matta iva dvipaḥ||
english: Struck in the encounter by Atikaya, the son of Sumitra began to bleed copiously, like a mad elephant discharging the temporal jouice.

sanskrit: sa cakāra tadātmānaṃ viśalyaṃ sahasā vibhuḥ| jagrāha ca śaraṃ tīkṣṇamastreṇāpi samādade|8||
english: Then that lord at once extricated the arrow; and then took up a keen shaft and fixed the same on his weapon.* *i.e. the bow.

sanskrit: āgneyena tadātreṇa yojayāmāsa sāyakam| sa jajvāla tadā bāṇo dhanuścāsya tadātmanaḥ||
english: Then he set a shaft (on his bow-string) reciting a formula for the Agneya* (Belonging to the god of Fire.) weapon; and thereat his arrow as well as bow flamed up.

sanskrit: atikāyo'titejasvī raudramalaṃ samādade| tena bāṇaṃ bhujaṃgābhaṃ hemapukhamayojayat||
english: Then the highly powerful Atikaya took up a Ruadra* weapon; and thereon fixed a shaft plated with gold at the feathered part, and resembling a serpent in sheen. *Relative to Rudra.

sanskrit: tadalaṃ jvalitaṃ ghoraṃ lakṣmaṇaḥ śaramāhitam| atikāyāya cikṣepa kāladaṇḍamivāntakaḥ||
english: And even as the reaper hurled his rod, did Lakşmaņa hurl that weapon inspired with divine energy, dreadful and aflame, at Atikaya.

sanskrit: āgneyāstrābhisaṃyuktaṃ dṛṣṭvā bāṇaṃ niśācaraḥ| utsasarja tadā bāṇaṃ raudraṃ sūryāstrayojitam||
english: Seeing that shaft set upon an Āgneya weapon, that night-ranger discharged a Raudra arrow set upon a Solar weapon.

sanskrit: tāvubhāvambare bāṇāvanyonyamabhijannatuḥ| tejasā saṃpradīptāgro kuddhāviva bhuṃjagamau|| tāvanyonya vinirdahya petatuḥ pṛthivītale|| nirarciṣau bhasmakṛtau na bhrājete śarottamau| tāvubhau dīpyamānau sma na bhrājete mahītale||
english: There like a pair of infuriated serpents, those arrows with their heads flaming in energy, baffled each other in the sky. And burning each other, the shafts fell on the earth; and those best of arrows, shorn of brilliance and reduced to ashes, were deprived of their splendour. And having blazed in the welkin, those two fell down to the earth reft of their lustre.

sanskrit: tato'tikāyaḥ saṃkruddhastvāṣṭramaiṣīkamutsṛjat| tataściccheda saumitrirastramaindreṇa vīryavān|||
english: Then Atikāya wrought up with wrath discharged an arrow called Aişīka dedicated to Tvaştā. Thereat the powerful son of Sumitrā severed that shaft by an Aindra* weapon. *Belonging to Indra.

sanskrit: aiṣīkaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā kumāro rāvaṇātmajaḥ| yāmyenāstreṇa saṃkuddho yojayāmāsa sāyakam|| tatastadatraṃ cikṣepa lakṣmaṇāya niśācaraḥ| vāyavyena tadatreṇa nijaghāna sa lakṣmaṇaḥ||
english: Seeing Aisika baffled, that Prince-son to Rāvana-fired with rage, fixed an arrow on a Yămya' weapon; and then the night-ranger shot that weapon at Lakşmaņa. And Lakşmaņa resisted it by a Vāyavya' weapon. 1. What could this be like? The commentator is silent over this important point. 2. Belonging to the wind-god.

sanskrit: athainaṃ śaradhārābhirdhārābhiriva toyadaḥ| abhyavarṣata saṃkruddho lakṣmaṇo rāvaṇātmajam|12||
english: Then as a mass of clouds poured down showers, Laksmana, enraged, poured volleys of shafts on Rāvana's son.

sanskrit: te'tikāyaṃ samāsādya kavace vajrabhūṣite| bhagnāgraśalyāḥ sahasā peturbāṇā mahītale|13||
english: Thereupon, hitting Atikāya, those arrows coming in contact with his mail, had their barbs broken, and fell down to the earth.

sanskrit: tānmoghānabhisaṃprekṣya lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā| abhyavarṣata bāṇānāṃ sahasreṇa mahāyaśāḥ|14||
english: Seeing them baffled, that slayer of hostile heroes-the renowned Laksmana-began to shower shafts by thousands.

sanskrit: sa vṛṣyamāṇo bāṇaudhairatikāyo mahābalaḥ| avadhyakavacaḥ saṃkhye rākṣaso naiva vivyathe|| na śaśāka rujaṃ kartuṃ yudhi tasya narottamaḥ|
english: And albeit showered with those arrows, that Raksasas, the mighty Atikāya-in that encounter was not pierced by them on account of his impenetrable mail; and that best of men failed to hurt him in the contest.

sanskrit: athainamabhyupāgamya vāyurvākyamuvāca ha|| brahmadattavaro hyeṣa avadhyakavacāvṛtaḥ| brāhmaṇāstreṇa bhindhyenameṣa vadhyo hi nānyathā|| avadhya eṣa hyanyeṣāmastrāṇāṃ kavacī balī||
english: "Then approaching him, the wind-god spoke to him, saying, ""This one has received a boon from Brahmā, and is covered with an impenetrable mail. Pierce him with a Brahma* weapon. He cannot otherwise be slain. This one clad in mail and endowed with prowess is forsooth incapable of being slain by others."" *Belonging to Brahma."

sanskrit: tatastu vāyorvacanaṃ niśamya saumitririndrapratimānavīryaḥ| samādadhe bāṇamathogravegaṃ tadbrāhmamastraṃ sahasā niyujya|18||
english: Hearing the words of the wind-god, Sumitrā's son like to Indra in prowess took an arrow endowed with fierce impetuosity, and at once set it on a Brahma weapon.

sanskrit: tasminvarāstre tu niyujyamāne saumitriṇā bāṇavare śitāo| diśaśca candrārkamahāgrahāśca nabhaśca tatrāsa rarāsa corvī||
english: On that sharp-headed best of arrows being fixed on that foremost of weapons, the cardinal quarters and the Moon and the sun and the mighty planets and the sky were saized with affright; and the earth shook.

sanskrit: taṃ brahmaṇo'streṇa niyujya cāpe śaraṃ sapuvaṃ yamadūtakalpam| saumitririndrārisutasya tasya sasarja bāṇaṃ yudhi vajrakalpam||
english: And inspiring that arrow furnished with a feathered part and resembling an emissary of Yama himself, and fixing the same on his bow, Sumitrā's son in that encounter discharged that shaft like to the thunder-bolt at the son of the enemy of Indra.

sanskrit: taṃ lakṣmaṇotsṛṣṭavivṛddhavegaṃ samāpatantaṃ śvasanogravegam| suparṇavajrottamacitrapuṅkha tadātikāyaḥ samare dadarśa||
english: And in that conflict Atikāya beheld that shaft fair-feathered and having its feathered part dight with splendid diamonds, acquiring enhanced vehemence arising from its having been discharged by Lakşmaņa, and hissing and rushing on with tremendous impetuosity.

sanskrit: taṃ prekṣamāṇaḥ sahasātikāyo jaghāna bāṇainiśitairanekaiḥ| stathātivegena jagāma pārśvam||
english: Seeing it, Atikäya swiftly resisted it with countless sharpened shafts. But endowed with the energy of Suparna himself, that shaft vehemently went to him.

sanskrit: tamāgataṃ prekṣya tadātikāyo bāṇaṃ pradīptāntakakālakalpam| jaghāna śaktyaṣṭigadākuṭhāraiḥ śūlaiḥ śaraścāpyavipanaceṣṭaḥ||
english: Seeing that shaft flaming and resembling the Fatal destroyer himself, coming, he, exerting himself to the utmost resisted it with darts and Rştis and maces and adzes and javelins and arrows.

sanskrit: tānyāyudhānyadbhutavigrāhaṇi moghāni kṛtvā sa śaro'gnidīpaḥ| pragṛhya tasyaiva kirīṭajuṣṭaṃ tadātikāyasya śiro jahāra||
english: But beating down all those weapons of wonderful forms, that arrow alive with flames, coming to the diadem-decked head of Atikāya, severed the same (in twain).

sanskrit: tacchiraḥ saśirastrāṇāṃ lakṣmaṇeṣupramarditam| papāta sahasā bhūmau śṛṅga himavato yathā||
english: That head furnished with a corsalet, cut off by Laksmana's arrow, suddenly dropped to the earth, like a summit of Himavān toppling (to the ground).

sanskrit: taṃ bhūmau patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā vikṣiptāmbarabhūṣaṇam| babhūvurvyathitāḥ sarve hataśeṣā niśācarāḥ||
english: Seeing him rolling on the earth, with his attire and ornaments scattered about, those nightrangers that survived were overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: te viṣaṇṇamukhā dīnāḥ prahārajanitaśramāḥ| vineduruccairbahavaḥ sahasā visvaraiḥ svaraiḥ||
english: And with pale forces and distressed, they, fatigued in consequence of the thrashing they had undergone, suddenly began to cry in frightful accents.

sanskrit: tatastatparito yātā nirapekṣā niśācarāḥ| purīmabhimukhā bhītā dravanto nāyake hate||
english: On their leader having been slain, those nightrangers that were about (Atikāya), without waiting any longer, overwhelmed with panic, rushed towards the city.

sanskrit: praharṣayuktā bahavastu vānarāḥ praphullapadmapratimānanāstadā| apūjayallakṣmaṇamiṣṭabhāginaṃ hate ripau bhīmabale durāsade||
english: On their foe endowed with terrific prowess and incapable of being conformed, having been slain, innumerable monkeys filled with excess of joy, and displaying countenances resembling blown lotuses, paid homage to Lakşmaņa working out their welfare.

sanskrit: vīkṣamāṇastato laṅkāṃ kapiḥ kṛtamanorathaḥ| vardhamānasamutsāhaḥ kāryaśeṣamacintayat||
english: Casting his eyes on Lankā, the monkey, his wish attained, increasing his person and bursting with spirits, considered as to how to give the coup de grace to his exertions.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu khalvaśiṣṭaṃ me kartavyamiha sāmpratam| yadeṣāṃ rakṣasāṃ bhūyaḥ saṃtāpajananaṃ bhavet||
english: What recently is to done by me here to finish this business, that may afflict them the more?

sanskrit: vanaṃ tāvatpramathitaṃ prakṛṣṭā rākṣasā hatāḥ| balaikadeśaḥ kṣapitaḥ śeṣaṃ durgavināśanam||
english: I have ravaged the wood, and slain the choice Rākşasas, and destroyed by main force a portion of the army. Now it remains to demolish the fortifications.

sanskrit: durge vināśite karma bhavet sukhapariśramam| alpayatnena kārye'smin mama syāt saphalaḥ śramaḥ||
english: On the fortifications being destroyed, my work shall nave its toils crowned with joy. By undergoing slight labour in this business, I shall have my pains furnished with fruit.

sanskrit: yo hyayaṃ mama lāṅgule dīpyate havyavāhanaḥ| asya saṃtarpaṇaṃ nyāyyaṃ kartumebhirgṛhottamaiḥ||
english: That bearer of sacrificial offerings (Vide ante) who flame on my tail, it is my duty to propitiate him with these excellent edifices.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradīptalāṅgulaḥ savidyudiva toyadaḥ| bhavanāgreṣu laṅkāyā vicacāra mahākapiḥ||
english: Thereat that mighty monkey, with his tail aglow, and resembling a cloud (luminous) with lightning, began to range before the dwellings in Lankā.

sanskrit: gṛhād gṛhaṃ rākṣasānāmudyānāni ca vānaraḥ| vīkṣamāṇo hyasaṃtrastaḥ prāsādāṃśca cacāra saḥ||
english: And that monkey with a calm mind, eyeing (all round), ranged one house from another, and gardens, and stately piles.

sanskrit: avaplutya mahāvegaḥ prahastasya niveśanam| agni tatra vinikṣipya śvasanena samo valī|| tato'nyat pupluve veśma mahāpārśvasya vīryavān| mumoca hanumānagni kālānalaśikhopamam||
english: And that one gifted with exceeding vehemence, and in strength resembling the Wind, bounding up set fire to the dwelling of Prahasta. Then Hanuman endowed with prowess, leaping up, set to Mahaparsva's mansion fire resembling that at the universal dissolution.

sanskrit: vajradaṃṣṭrasya ca tathā pupluve sa mahākapiḥ| śukasya ca mahātejāḥ sāraṇasya ca dhīmataḥ||
english: And (then) the mighty monkey darting up, set fire to Vajradanştra's; and (then) that highly energetic one set fire to Suka's and to the intelligent Sārana's.

sanskrit: tathā cendrajito veśma dadāha hariyūthapaḥ| jambumāleḥ sumāleśca dadāha bhavanaṃ tataḥ|| raśmiketośca bhavanaṃ sūryaśatrostathaiva ca| hrasvakarṇasya daṃṣṭrasya romaśasya ca rakṣasaḥ|| yuddhonmattasya mattasya dhvajagrīvasya rakṣasaḥ| vidyujjihvasya ghorasya tathā hastimukhasya ca|| karālasya viśālasya śoṇitākṣasya caiva hi| kumbhakarṇasya bhavanaṃ makarākṣasya caiva hi|| narāntakasya kumbhasya nikumbhasya durātmanaḥ| yajñaśatrośca bhavanaṃ brahmaśatrostathaiva ca||
english: And the leader of monkey bands in the same way burnt down Indrajit's mansion; and then he burnt the abodes of Sumāli and Jambumălī; and Rasmiketu's mansion and Suryasatru's, and Hrasvakarma's, and the Raksasa Romasa's; and the houses of Yuddhonmatta, and Matta, and the Rākṣasa Dhvajagrīva, and the calm Vidyujjihva, and Hastimukha; and of Karāla, and of Viśāla, and of Sonitāksa; and Kumbhakarma's mansion, and Nikumbha's, and the residence of Yajnasatru, and of Brahmasatru.

sanskrit: varjayitvā mahātejā vibhīṣaṇagṛhaṃ prati| kramamāṇaḥ krameṇaiva dadāha haripuṅgavaḥ||
english: And leaving alone the dwelling of Vibhişaņa, that exceedingly energetic one-foremost of monkeys-by and by burnt (all the houses there).

sanskrit: teṣu teṣu mahārheṣu bhavaneṣu mahāyaśāḥ| gṛheṣvṛddhimatāmṛddhiṃ dadāha kapikuñjaraḥ||
english: In those costly mansions and dwellings, that famous one, that foremost of monkeys, burnt all the wealth of those affluent persons.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ samatikramya rākṣasendrasya vīryavān| āsasādātha lakṣmīvān rāvaṇasya niveśanam||
english: Having passed the dwellings of all, that powerful and auspicious one approached the residence of the lord of Rākşasas, Rāvaņa.

sanskrit: tatastasmin gṛhe mukhye nānāratnavibhūṣite| merumandarasaṃkāśe nānāmaṅgalaśobhite || pradīptamagnimutsṛjya lāṅgulāgre pratiṣṭhitam| nanāda hanumān vīro yugāntajalado yathā||
english: And in that foremost of mansions, adorned or with various gems, resembling Meru Mandara, graced with diverse auspicious things, he set to the same, fire flaming at the end of his tail. And the heroic Hanumān roars, resembling a cloud (appearing) at the end of a Yuga.

sanskrit: śvasanena ca saṃyogādativego mahābalāḥ| kālāgniriva jajvāla prāvardhata hutāśanaḥ||
english: And assisted by the wind, that highly powerful and vehement one (Fire) flaimed up, like fire at the wreck of all, and the fire attained energy.

sanskrit: pradīptamagniṃ pavanasteṣu veśmasu cārayan| tāni kāñcanajālāni muktāmaṇimayāni ca|| bhavanāni vyaśīryanta ratnavanti mahānti ca| tāni bhagnavimānāni nipeturvasudhātale||
english: The wind spreading the flaming fire all round those dwellings, those mansions furnished with golden networks; and containing pearls and gems; enjewelled and magnificent, were shorn of their splendour.

sanskrit: bhavanānīva siddhānāmambarāt puṇyasaṃkṣaye| saṃjajñe tumulaḥ śabdo rākṣasānāṃ pradhāvatām|| sve sve gṛhaparitrāṇe bhagnotsāhojjhitaśriyām| nūnameṣo'gnirāyātaḥ kapirūpeṇa hā iti|| krandantyaḥ sahasā petuḥ stanaṃdhayadharāḥ striyaḥ|
english: "And cracked edifices began to topple down to the ground, like the mansions of Siddhās falling from the firmament of the exhaustion of their righteousness. And there arose a mighty uproar of those Rākşasas, as, bereft of their good fortune, despairing of preserving their abodes, they rushed in all directions, ""Forsooth it is Fire himself that has come hither in the form of a monkey.” And females crying with babes on their breasts, suddenly plunged (into the fire)."

sanskrit: kāścidagniparītāṅgayo haryebhyo muktamūrdhajāḥ|| patantyo rejire'bhrebhyaḥ saudāmanya ivāmbarāt|
english: And some fair ones with hair dishevelled, and surrounded on all sides with fire, as they fell down from dwellings, looked lovely like lightning from the welkin.

sanskrit: vajravidrumavaidūryamuktārajatasaṃhatān|| vicitrān bhavanāddhātūnsyandamānān dadarśa saḥ|
english: And he (Hanuman) saw various kinds of metals, mixed with diamonds, and coral, and lapises and pearls and silver, running down in streams from the mansions.

sanskrit: nāgnistṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ tṛṇānāṃ ca yathā tathā|| hanūmān rākṣasendrāṇāṃ vadhe kiṃcinna tṛpyati| na hanūmadviśastānāṃ rākṣasānāṃ vasundharā ||
english: And as Fire is not cloyed with wood and straw, Hanumān never at all felt satiety on slaying those foremost of Räkşasas. And the Earth could not contain the Rākşasas slain by Hanumăn.

sanskrit: hanūmatā vegavatā vānareṇa mahātmanā| laṅkāpuraṃ pradagdhaṃ tad rudreṇa tripuraṃ yathā||
english: And as Rudra had burnt down Tripura, the vehement and high-souled monkey, Hanumān, burnt down Lankā.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa laṅkāpuraparvatāgre samutthito bhīmaparākramo'gniḥ| prasārya cūḍāvalayaṃ pradīpto hanūmatā vegavatopasṛṣṭaḥ||
english: And rising to the brow of Lanka's mount, (Trikūţa on which Lankā rested) the fire of terrific energy kindled by the impetuous Hanumān, spread wide his tongues.

sanskrit: yugāntakālānalatulyarūpaḥ samāruto'gnirvavṛdhe divaspṛk | vidhūmaraśmirbhavaneṣu sakto rakṣaḥśarīrājyasamarpitārciḥ||
english: With the Wind assisting him, the smokeless Fire in the dwellings, with his flames feeding on the bodies of the Rākşasas representing sacrificial offerings, spread his magnitude, touching the horizen-resembling the conflagration kindled the universal dissolution.

sanskrit: ādityakoṭīsadṛśaḥ sutejā laṅkāṃ samastāṃ parivārya tiṣṭhan| bhindannivāṇḍaṃ prababhau mahāgniḥ||
english: And possessing the fierce energy of a koti suns, the nighty Fire completely encompassing the entire Lanka, increased (in volume), riving at the mundane Egg with various sounds resembling thunder-claps.

sanskrit: tatrāmbarādagniratipravṛddho rūkṣaprabhaḥ kiṃśukapuṣpacūḍaḥ| nirvāṇadhūmākularājayaśca nīlotpalābhāḥ pracakāśire'bhrāḥ||
english: And the Fire of terrific might, having his flames resembling Kinsuka blossoms, rising up to the sky, clouds caused by volumes of smoke arising from extinguished fire, in hue resembling blue lotuses, looked exceedingly beautiful.

sanskrit: kjrī mahendrastridaśeśvaro vā sākṣād yamo vā varuṇo'nilo vā| raudro'gnirarko dhanadaśca somo na vānaro'yaṃ svayameva kālaḥ|| kiṃ brahmaṇaḥ sarvapitāmahasya lokasya dhātuścaturānanasya| ihāgato vānararūpadhārī rakṣopasaṃhārakaraḥ prakopaḥ|| kiṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ vā kapirūpametya rakṣovināśāya paraṃ sutejaḥ| acintyamavyaktamanantamekaṃ svamāyayā sāmpratamāgataṃ vā|| ityevamūcurbahavo viśiṣṭā rakṣogaṇāstatra sametya sarve| saprāṇisaṅgha sagṛhāṃ savṛkṣā dagdhāṃ purī tāṃ sahasā samīkṣya||
english: "Either the thunder-bolt-bearing Indra the Great-chief of celestials, or Yama himself, or Varuna, or the Wind-god, or the Fire generated by Rudra's third eye, or the Sun, or Dhanda, or Soma. This is no monkey, this is verily Kāla (A name of Yama) himself or is this the Rākşasa annihilating Fire or Brahmä himself, the Great sire of all, the four-faced Disposer of the world's destinies, come hither, wearing the form of a monkey? Or is this Visnu's Energy, inconceivable, unutterable, infinite and sole, and of surpassing power, now come hither in its own illusory nature, assuming a monkey-form?"" Seeing that city suddenly consumed, with her souls, dwellings, and trees, Raksasas of note, assembled together, thus talked to each other."

sanskrit: tatastu laṅkāṃ sahasā pradagdhā sarākṣasā sāśvarathā sanāgā| sapakṣisaṅghā samṛgā savṛkṣā ruroda dīnā tumulaṃ saśabdam||
english: And then Lankä, suddenly consumed with Raksasas, horses, cars, serpents, crowds of birds, beasts and trees, began to bewail tumultuously and loud in forlorn guise.

sanskrit: hā tāta hā putraka kānta mitra hā jīviteśāṅga hataṃ supuṇyam| rakṣobhirevaṃ bahudhā bruvadbhiḥ śabdaḥ kṛto ghorataraḥ subhīmaḥ||
english: "O father! O son! O love! O friend! O lord of my life and frame! all our religious merit is abolished ""Indulging in various lamentations, the Rākşas thus created a mighty and frightful uproar."""

sanskrit: hutāśanajvālasamāvṛtā sā hatapravīrā parivṛttayodhā| hanūmataḥ krodhabalābhibhūtā babhūva śāpopahateva laṅkā ||
english: And with the flames encircling her, and her foremost heroes fallen, and her warriors destroyed, Lankā, overcome by the might of Hanumān's wrath, became as if she had been blighted by an imprecation.

sanskrit: sasambhramaṃ trastaviṣaṇṇarākṣasāṃ samujjvalajjvālahutāśanāṅkitām| dadarśa laṅkāṃ hanumānmahāmanāḥ svayaṃbhuroṣāpahatāmivāvanim|||
english: Then the mighty-minded Hanumān beheld the Rākşasas in terror and trepidation and cast down, and Lankā marked by fire and bright flames, even as the Self-sprung eye the world destroyed by his rage.

sanskrit: bhaṅkatvā vanaṃ pādaparatnasaṃkulaṃ hatvā tu rakṣāṃsi mahānti saṃyuge| dagdhvā purī tāṃ gṛharatnamālinī tasthau hanūmānpavanātmajaḥ kapiḥ|||
english: And devastating the forest filled with many excellent trees, slaying many a terrible Rākşasa in conflict, and burning down the city of Lankā filled with picturesque houses, the monkey, Hanumān, Wind-god's son, stationed himself there.

sanskrit: sa rākṣasāṃstānsubahūṃśca hatvā vanaṃ ca bhaṅktvā bahupādapaṃ tat| visṛjya rakṣobhavaneṣu cāgni jagāma rāmaṃ manasā mahātmā||
english: And destroying many a Rākṣasa, felling many trees in the forest and setting fire to the houses of the Raksasas, the high-souled (monkey) became engaged in thoughts touching Rāma.

sanskrit: tatastu taṃ vānaravīramukhyaṃ mahābalaṃ mārutatulyavegam| mahāmatiṃ vāyusutaṃ variṣṭhaṃ pratuṣṭavurdevagaṇāśca sarve||
english: Thereupon all the celestials praised highly the high-souled, excellent and mighty son of the Wind-god, foremost of heroic monkeys, gifted with the velocity of the of the Wind.

sanskrit: devāśca sarve munipuṅgavāśca gandharvavidyādharapannagāśca| bhūtāni sarvāṇi sahānti tatra jagmuḥ parāṃ prītimatulyarūpām||
english: All the celestials, the foremost ascetics, the Gandharvas, the Vidyādharas, the Pannāgas, and all other great heroes, attained excess of delight.

sanskrit: bhaṅktvā vanaṃ mahātejā hatvā rakṣāṃsi saṃyuge| dagdhvā laṅkāpurīṃ bhīmāṃ rarāja sa mahākapiḥ||
english: And having devastated the forest, slain the Rākşasas in conflict and burnt the grand city of Lankā, the great monkey appeared there.

sanskrit: gṛhāryaśṛṅgāgratale vicitre pratiṣṭhito vānararājasiṃhaḥ| pradīptalāṅgulakṛtārcimālī vyarājatāditya ivārcimālī||
english: And seated on the variegated top of a splendid and high mansion, the foremost of monkeys, spreading the rays of his burning tail, looked like to the sun of many rays.

sanskrit: laṅkāṃ samastāṃ sampīḍya lāṅgulāgniṃ mahākapiḥ| nirvāpayāmāsa tadā samudre haripuṅgavaḥ||
english: And having consumed ihe city of Lankä, the great monkey quenched the fire of his tail in the Ocean.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ| dṛṣṭvā laṅkāṃ pradagdhāṃ tāṃ vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ||
english: Thereupon beholding Lankā burnt down, the celestials along with Gandharvas, Siddhās, and the great ascetics, were struck with wonder. And having consumed ihe city of Lankä, the great monkey quenched the fire of his tail in the Ocean.

sanskrit: tato devāḥ sagandharvāḥ siddhāśca paramarṣayaḥ| dṛṣṭvā laṅkāṃ pradagdhāṃ tāṃ vismayaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ||
english: Thereupon beholding Lankā burnt down, the celestials along with Gandharvas, Siddhās, and the great ascetics, were struck with wonder.

sanskrit: parituṣṭastu sugrīvastena vākyena harṣitaḥ| lakṣmaṇasyāgrajaṃ śūramidaṃ vacanamabravīt||
english: Sugrīva, rejoiced at the words of Rāma, said to that hero, the elder brother of Laksmana; who was well pleased.

sanskrit: sarvathāhamanugrāhyo devatānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ| upapanno guṇopetaḥ sakhā yasya bhavān mama||
english: I am, without doubt, worthy of being favoured by the gods, since you accomplished and furnished with virtues are my friend.

sanskrit: śakyaṃ khalu bhaved rāma sahāyena tvayānagha| surarājyamapi prāptuṃ svarājyaṃ kimuta prabho||
english: By your help, O Rama, one can, O sinless one, obtain the kingdom of the celestials,-what is to be said of one's kingdom, O lord?

sanskrit: so'haṃ sabhājyo bandhūnāṃ suhṛdāṃ caiva rāghava| yasyāgnisākṣikaṃ mitraṃ labdhaṃ rāghavavaṃśajam||
english: I, who have, in the presence of Fire, gained for my friend (you) sprung from the Rāghava race, am, O Rāghava worthy of being honoured by my friends and relations.

sanskrit: ahamapyanurūpaste vayasyo jñāsyase śanaiḥ| na tu vaktuṃ samartho'haṃ tvayi ātmagatān guṇān||
english: You also shall by and by learn that I am a fit friend for you; but I can not speak to you of the qualities that abide in me.

sanskrit: mahātmanāṃ tu bhūyiṣṭhaṃ tvadvidhānāṃ kṛtātmanām| niścalā bhavati prītidhairyamātmavatāṃ vara||
english: O free one, the felicity of high-souled and self-governed friends like you abounds and is enduring.

sanskrit: rajataṃ vā suvarṇaṃ vā śubhānyābharaṇāni ca| avibhaktāni sādhūnāmavagacchanti sādhava :|7||
english: Pious friends look upon the silver, and gold, and the elegant ornaments of pious friends as common property.

sanskrit: āḍhyo vāpi daridro vā duḥkhitaḥ sukhito'pi vā| nirdoṣaśca sadoṣaśca vayasyaḥ paramā gatiḥ||
english: Whether rich or poor, happy or miserable, good or bad, a friend is the greatest refuge (of his friend).

sanskrit: traividyavidyāmaṇḍa esa niravaśeṣatvāt kleśānām,
english: It is the seat of the three knowledges, because in it no passions remain.

sanskrit: ekacittaniravaśeṣasarvadharmānubodhamaṇḍa eṣa sarvajñajñānasamudāgamatvāt /
english: It is the seat of instantaneous, total understanding of all things, because it realizes fully the gnosis of omniscience.

sanskrit: iti hi kulaputra yāvanto bodhisatvāḥ pāramitāpratisaṃyuktaṃ satvaparipākapratisaṃyuktaṃ saddharmaparigrahapratisaṃyuktaṃ kuśalamūlapratisaṃyuktaṃ kramam utkṣipanti nikṣipanti ca / sarve te bodhimaṇḍād āgacchanti,
english: “ ‘Noble son, when bodhisattvas are thus endowed with the transcendences, the roots of virtue, the ability to develop living beings, and the incorporation of the holy Dharma, whether they lift up their feet or put them down, they all come from the seat of enlightenment.

sanskrit: buddhadharmebhya āgacchanti, buddhadharmeṣu ca pratiṣṭhante /
english: They come from the qualities of the Buddha, and stand on the qualities of the Buddha.’

sanskrit: iha bhagavan nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne pañcamātrair devamanuṣyaśatair bodhāya cittāny utpāditāni / ahaṃ ca niṣpratibhāno 'bhūvam /
english: “Lord, when Vimalakīrti had explained this teaching, five hundred gods and men conceived the spirit of enlightenment, and I became speechless.

sanskrit: tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Therefore, Lord, I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: tatra bhagavān jagatindharaṃ bodhisatvam āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ jagatindhara vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: The Buddha then said to the bodhisattva Jagatindhara, “Jagatindhara, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: jagatindharo 'py āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Jagatindhara replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

sanskrit: abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan ekasmin samaye svake vihāre viharāmi / atha māraḥ pāpīyān dvādaśabhir apsaraḥsahasraiḥ parivṛtaḥ śakraveṣeṇa tūryasaṃgītisaṃpravāditena
english: Lord, I remember that one day, when I was at home, the wicked Māra, disguised as Śakra and surrounded with twelve thousand heavenly maidens, approached me with the sounds of music and singing.

sanskrit: yenāhaṃ tenopasaṃkramya mama pādau śirasā vanditvā saparivāro māṃ puraskṛtyaikānte 'sthāt /
english: Having saluted me by touching my feet with his head, he withdrew with his retinue to one side.

sanskrit: tam enam ahaṃ jānāmi ḥ śakra eṣa devendra iti / tam aham etad avocam svāgataṃ te kauśika,
english: I then, thinking he was Śakra, the king of the gods, said to him, ‘Welcome, O Kauśika!

sanskrit: apramattena te bhavitavyaṃ sarvakāmaratiṣu, anityapratyavekṣanābahulenāttasāreṇa te bhavitavyaṃ kāyajīvitabhogebhyaḥ /
english: You should remain consciously aware in the midst of the pleasures of desire. You should often think on impermanence and strive to utilize the essential in body, life, and wealth.’

sanskrit: sa mām evam āha pratīccha tvaṃ satpuruṣa imāni dvādaśāpsaraḥsahasrāṇi mamāntikāt,
english: “Māra then said to me, ‘Good sir, accept from me these twelve thousand divine maidens and make them your servants.’

sanskrit: tam aham etad avocam mā tvaṃ kauṣika akalpikena vastunā śramaṇān śākyaputrīyān nimantraya,
english: “I replied, ‘O Kauśika, do not offer me, who am religious and a son of the Śākya, things which are not appropriate.

sanskrit: yathā na hy etā asmākaṃ kalpyanta iti /
english: It is not proper for me to have these maidens.’

sanskrit: vimalakīrtir licchavir upasaṃkrāntaḥ / sa mām evam āha mā atra kulaputra śakrasaṃjñām utpādaya /
english: “No sooner had I said these words than the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there and said to me, ‘‌Noble son, do not think that this is Śakra!

sanskrit: māra eṣa pāpīyāṃs tava viheṭhanābhiprāya upasaṃkrāntaḥ, naiṣa śakra iti /
english: This is not Śakra but the evil Māra, who has come to ridicule you.’

sanskrit: atha vimalakīrtir licchavis taṃ māraṃ pāpīyāṃsam etad avocat asmabhyaṃ pāpīyan etā apsaraso niryātaya / asmākam etāḥ kalpyante, na śramaṇānāṃ śākyaputrīyāṇām iti /
english: “Then the Licchavi Vimalakīrti said to Māra, ‘Evil Māra, since these heavenly maidens are not suitable for this religious devotee, a son of the Śākya, give them to me.’

sanskrit: atha māraḥ pāpīyān bhītas trastaḥ saṃvignaḥ / mā vimalakīrtinā licchavinā vipralapsya iti,
english: “Then Māra was terrified and distressed, thinking that the Licchavi Vimalakīrti had come to expose him.

sanskrit: icchati cāntardhātum, na ca śaknoti sarvarddhim api darśayitvāntardhātum /
english: He tried to make himself invisible, but, try as he might with all his magical powers, he could not vanish from sight.

sanskrit: so 'ntarīkṣāc chabdam aśrauṣīt niryātaya tvam etāḥ pāpīyan apsarasa etasmai satpuruṣāya, tataḥ śakṣyasi svabhavanaṃ gantum /
english: Then a voice resounded in the sky, saying, ‘Evil One, give these heavenly maidens to the good man Vimalakīrti, and only then will you be able to return to your own abode.’

sanskrit: atha māro bhītas trasto 'kāmako 'smai tā apsaraso niryātayati /
english: “Then Māra was even more frightened and, much against his will, gave the heavenly maidens.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca vimalakīrtis tā apsarasa etad avocat niryātitā yūyaṃ mahyaṃ māreṇa pāpīyasā,
english: “The Licchavi Vimalakīrti, having received the goddesses, said to them, ‘Now that you have been given to me by Māra, you should all conceive the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.’

sanskrit: utpādayatedānīm anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam / sa tāsāṃ tadānulomikīṃ bodhiparipācanīṃ kathāṃ kṛtvā bodhau cittam utpādayati sma /
english: “He then exhorted them with discourse suitable for their development toward enlightenment, and soon they conceived the spirit of enlightenment.

sanskrit: sa tā evam āha utpāditam idānīṃ yuṣmābhir bodhicittam,
english: He then said to them, ‘You have just conceived the spirit of enlightenment.

sanskrit: dharmārāmaratiratābhir idānīṃ yuṣmābhir bhavitavyam, na kāmaratiratābhiḥ /
english: From now on, you should devote yourselves to finding joy in the pleasures of the Dharma, and should take no pleasure in desires.’

sanskrit: tāhuḥ katamā ca punar dharmārāmaratiḥ /
english: “They then asked him, ‘What is “joy in the pleasures of the Dharma”?’

sanskrit: sa āha buddhe 'bhedyaprasādaratiḥ, dharme śuśrūṣaṇaratiḥ, saṃgha upasthānaratiḥ, guruṣu gauravopasthānaratiḥ,
english: “He declared, ‘It is the joy of unbreakable faith in the Buddha, of wishing to hear the Dharma, of serving the Saṅgha and honoring the spiritual benefactors without pride.

sanskrit: skandheṣu vadhakānityapratyavekṣaṇāratiḥ, dhātuṣv āśīviṣaparitulanāratiḥ, āyataneṣu śūnyagrāmavivekaratiḥ, bodhicittārakṣaṇaratiḥ, satveṣu hitavastutāratiḥ,
english: It is the joy of renunciation of the whole world, of not being fixed in objects, of considering the five aggregates to be like murderers, of considering the elements to be like venomous serpents, and of considering the sensemedia to be like an empty town. It is the joy of always guarding the spirit of enlightenment, of helping living beings,

sanskrit: bodhau vistīrṇaratiḥ, mārasya nigraharatiḥ, kleśānāṃ praghātanāratiḥ, buddhakṣetrasya viśodhanāratiḥ,
english: It is the joy of extending enlightenment, of conquering the māras, of destroying the afflictions, and of purifying the buddhafield.

sanskrit: lakṣaṇānuvyañjanapariniṣpattyarthaṃ sarvakuśalamūlopacayaratiḥ,
english: It is the joy of accumulating all virtues, in order to cultivate the auspicious marks and signs.

sanskrit: gambhīradharmaśravaṇānuttrāsaratiḥ,
english: It is the joy of the liberation of nonintimidation when hearing the profound teaching.

sanskrit: trivimokṣamukhaparijayaratiḥ,
english: It is the joy of exploration of the three doors of liberation, and of the realization of liberation.

sanskrit: nirvāṇārambaṇaratiḥ, bodhimaṇḍālaṃkāraratiḥ, na cākālaprāptiratiḥ,
english: It is the joy of being an ornament of the seat of enlightenment, and of not attaining liberation at the wrong time.

sanskrit: sabhāgajanasevanāratiḥ, viṣabhāgeṣv adoṣāpratighātaratiḥ, kalyāṇamitreṣu sevāratiḥ, pāpamitreṣu visarjanāratiḥ,
english: It is the joy of serving those of equal fortune, of not hating or resenting those of superior fortune, of serving the spiritual benefactors, and of avoiding sinful friends.

sanskrit: dharmaprītiprāmodyaratiḥ, upāye saṃgraharatiḥ,
english: It is the joy of the superior gladness of faith and devotion to the Dharma.

sanskrit: apramādabodhipakṣyadharmasevanāratiḥ /
english: It is the joy of acquiring liberative arts and of the conscious cultivation of the aids to enlightenment.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi bodhisatvo dharmārāmaratirato bhavati /
english: Thus, the bodhisattva admires and finds joy in the delights of the Dharma.’

sanskrit: atha māraḥ pāpīyāṃs tā apsarasa etad avocat āgacchata /
english: “Thereupon, Māra said to the goddesses, ‘Now come along and let us return home.’

sanskrit: niryātitā idānīṃ tvayā vayam asmai gṛhapataye /
english: “They said, ‘You gave us to this householder.

sanskrit: dharmārāmaratiratābhir asmābhir idānīṃ bhavitavyam, na kāmaratiratābhiḥ /
english: Now we should enjoy the delights of the Dharma and should no longer enjoy the pleasures of desires.’

sanskrit: atha māraḥ pāpīyān vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim evam āha niḥsṛja tvaṃ gṛhapate imā apsarasaḥ / sarvasvaparityāgino bodhisatvā mahāsatvā bhavanti /
english: “Then Māra said to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti, ‘If it is so that the bodhisattva, the spiritual hero, has no mental attachment, and gives away all his possessions, then, householder, please give me these goddesses.’

sanskrit: vimalakīrtir āha avasṛṣṭā bhavantu /
english: “Vimalakīrti replied, ‘They are given, Māra.

sanskrit: gaccha pāpīyan /
english: Go home with your retinue.

sanskrit: sarvasatvānāṃ dhārmikā abhiprāyāḥ paripūryantām /
english: May you fulfill the religious aspirations of all living beings!’

sanskrit: atha tā apsaraso vimalakīrtiṃ namaskṛtyaivam āhuḥ kathaṃ vayaṃ gṛhapate mārabhavane 'vatiṣṭhema /
english: “Then the goddesses, saluting Vimalakīrti, said to him, ‘Householder, how should we live in the abode of the māras?’

sanskrit: āha asti bhaginyaḥ akṣayapradīpaṃ nāma dharmamukham / tatra pratipadyadhvam /
english: “Vimalakīrti replied, ‘Sisters, there is a door of the Dharma called “The Inexhaustible Lamp.” Practice it!

sanskrit: tat punaḥ katamat /
english: What is it?

sanskrit: tadyathā bhaginyaḥ ekasmāt tailapradīpād dīpaśatasahasrāṇy ādīpyante /
english: Sisters, a single lamp may light hundreds of thousands of lamps without itself being diminished.

sanskrit: evam eva bhaginyaḥ eko bodhisatvo bahūni satvaśatasahasrāṇi bodhau pratiṣṭhāpayati / na ca tasya bodhisatvasya cittasmṛtir hīyate,
english: Likewise, sisters, a single bodhisattva may establish many hundreds of thousands of living beings in enlightenment without his mindfulness being diminished.

sanskrit: na parihīyate, uta ca vardhate /
english: In fact, not only does it not diminish, it grows stronger.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvān kuśalān dharmān yathā yathā pareṣām ārocayati deśayati, tathā tathā vivardhate sarvaiḥ kuśalair dharmaiḥ /
english: Likewise, the more you teach and demonstrate virtuous qualities to others, the more you grow with respect to these virtuous qualities.

sanskrit: idaṃ tad akṣayapradīpaṃ nāma dharmamukham / tatra yuṣmābhir mārabhavane sthitābhir aparimāṇānāṃ devaputrāṇām apsarasāṃ ca bodhicittaṃ rocayitavyam /
english: This is the door of the Dharma called “The Inexhaustible Lamp.” When you are living in the realm of Māra, inspire innumerable gods and goddesses with the spirit of enlightenment.

sanskrit: evaṃ yūyaṃ tathāgatasya kṛtajñā bhaviṣyatha / sarvasatvānāṃ copajīvyā bhaviṣyatha /
english: In such a way, you will repay the kindness of the Tathāgata, and you will become the benefactors of all living beings.’

sanskrit: atha tā apsaraso vimalakīrter licchaveḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā sārdhaṃ māreṇa prakrāntāḥ /
english: “Then, those goddesses bowed at the feet of the Licchavi Vimalakīrti and departed in the company of Māra.

sanskrit: ime bhagavan vimalakīrter licchaver vikurvaṇaviśeṣāḥ, yān ahaṃ nājñāsiṣam / tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Thus, Lord, I saw the supremacy of the magical power, wisdom, and eloquence of the Licchavi Vimalakīrti, and therefore I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: tatra bhagavān sudattaṃ śreṣṭhiputram āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ kulaputra vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: The Buddha then said to the merchant’s son, Sudatta, “‌Noble son, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: sudatto 'py āha nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Sudatta replied, “Lord, I am indeed reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.

sanskrit: abhijānāmy ahaṃ bhagavan svake paitṛke niveśane mahāyajñaṃ yajāmi / sarvadaridraduḥkhitebhyaḥ sarvaśramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīyakayācanakebhyo dānaṃ dadāmi /
english: Lord, I remember one day in my father’s house when, in order to celebrate a great sacrifice, I was bestowing gifts upon religious devotees, brahmins, the poor, the wretched, the unfortunate, beggars, and all the needy.

sanskrit: tatra saptame divase vimalakīrtir licchavis tāṃ mahāyajñaśālāṃ praviśya mām etad avocat na śreṣṭhiputra evaṃ yajño yaṣṭavyo yathā tvaṃ yajase /
english: On the seventh and final day of this great sacrifice, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti came there and said, ‘Merchant’s son, you should not celebrate a sacrifice in this way.

sanskrit: dharmayajñas te yaṣṭavyaḥ /
english: You should celebrate a Dharmasacrifice.

sanskrit: kiṃ ta āmiṣayajñena /
english: What is the use of the sacrifice of material things?’

sanskrit: kathaṃ punar dharmayajño yaṣṭavyaḥ /
english: ‘How does one give a Dharmasacrifice?’

sanskrit: sa mām evam āha / yena dharmayajñenāpūrvācaramaṃ sarvasatvāḥ paripācyante, ayaṃ dharmayajñaḥ / sa punaḥ katamaḥ /
english: “He replied, ‘A Dharmasacrifice is that which develops living beings without beginning or end, giving gifts to them all simultaneously. What is that?

sanskrit: yad idaṃ bodhyākārābhinirhṛtā mahāmaitrī, saddharmasaṃgrahābhinirhṛtā mahākaruṇā, sarvasatvaprāmodyārambanābhinirhṛtā mahāmuditā, jñānasaṃgrahābhinirhṛtā mahopekṣā,
english: It consists of the great love which is consummated in enlightenment of the great compassion consummated in the concentration of the holy Dharma on the liberation of all living beings of the great joy consummated in the awareness of the supreme happiness of all living beings and of the great equanimity consummated in concentration through knowledge.

sanskrit: yatra dharmayajñe pratiṣṭhitā bodhisatvā iṣṭayajñayājūkā dakṣiṇīyā bhavanti sadevakasya lokasya /
english: The bodhisattva who lives by this Dharmasacrifice is the best of sacrificers, and, through his extreme sacrifice, is himself worthy of offerings from all people, including the gods.’

sanskrit: evaṃ hi bhagavan tasya gṛhapater nirdiśatas tasyā brāhmaṇaparṣado dvayor brāhmaṇaśatayor anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni /
english: “Lord, as soon as the householder had discoursed thus, two hundred brahmins among the crowd of brahmins present conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: ahaṃ cāścaryaprasādapratilabdhas tasya satpuruṣasya caraṇau praṇamya śatasahasramūlyaṃ muktāhāraṃ kaṇṭhād avatārya dadāmi / sa taiḥ muktāhāraṃ na pratigṛhṇāti sma /
english: And I, full of astonishment, having saluted this good man by touching his feet with my head, took from around my neck a necklace of pearls worth one hundred thousand pieces of gold and offered it to him. But he would not accept it.

sanskrit: tam aham etad avocam pratigṛhyemam, yatra te prasādo bhavati tasmai prayaccheti /
english: I then said to him, ‘Please accept, good man, this necklace of pearls, out of compassion for me, and give it to whomsoever you wish.’

sanskrit: tena sa muktāhāro gṛhītvā dvidhākṛtaḥ /
english: “Then, Vimalakīrti took the pearls and divided them into two halves.

sanskrit: eko bhāgo yas tatra yajñaśālāyāṃ sarvalokajugupsito nagaradaridras tasmai dattaḥ /
english: He gave one half of them to the lowliest poor of the city, who had been disdained by those present at the sacrifice.

sanskrit: dvitīyaś ca bhāgo duṣprasahāya tathāgatāya dattaḥ /
english: The other half he offered to the Tathāgata Duṣprasaha.

sanskrit: yathā ca sarvā parṣat paśyati taṃ ca marīciṃ lokadhātuṃ taṃ ca duṣprasahaṃ tathāgataṃ
english: And he performed a miracle such that all present beheld the universe called Marīci and the Tathāgata Duṣprasaha.

sanskrit: taṃ ca muktāhāraṃ duṣprasahasya mūrdhasaṃdhau muktāhārakūṭāgāraṃ prādurbhūtaṃ citraṃ darśanīyaṃ caturasraṃ catuḥsthūṇaṃ samaṃbhāgaśaḥ suvibhaktam /
english: On the head of the Tathāgata Duṣprasaha, the pearl necklace took the form of a pavilion, decorated with strings of pearls, resting on four bases, with four columns, symmetrical, well constructed, and lovely to behold.

sanskrit: sa idaṃ prātihāryaṃ saṃdarśyemāṃ vācam abhāṣata yasya dāyakasya dānapater yādṛśī tathāgate dakṣiṇīyasaṃjñā tādṛśī nagaradaridre nirnānātvena samā, mahākaruṇācittena vipākāpratikāṅkṣaṇatayā parityāgaḥ / iyaṃ dharmayajñasya paripūriḥ /
english: Having shown such a miracle, Vimalakīrti said, ‘The giver who makes gifts to the lowliest poor of the city, considering them as worthy of offering as the Tathāgata himself, and the giver who gives without any discrimination, impartially, with no expectation of reward, and with great lovethat giver, I say, totally fulfills the Dharmasacrifice.’

sanskrit: tatrāsau nagaradaridra idaṃ prātihāryaṃ dṛṣṭvā, imaṃ ca dharmanirdeśaṃ śrutvā, anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittam utpādayati sma /
english: “Then the poor of the city, having seen that miracle and having heard that teaching, conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: tan nāhaṃ bhagavan utsahe tasya satpuruṣasya glānaparipṛcchako gantum /
english: Therefore, Lord, I am reluctant to go to that good man to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: iti hi sarve te bodhisatvā mahāsatvāḥ svakasvakān nirdeśān nirdiśanti sma, ye caiṣāṃ tena satpuruṣeṇa sārdham antarākathāsamudāhārā abhūvan, na cotsahante gantum // //
english: In the same way, all the bodhisattvas, the great spiritual heroes, told the stories of their conversations with Vimalakīrti and declared their reluctance to go to him.

sanskrit: tatra bhagavān mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam āmantrayate sma gaccha tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ vimalakīrter licchaver glānaparipṛcchakaḥ /
english: Then, the Buddha said to the crown prince, Mañjuśrī, “Mañjuśrī, go to the Licchavi Vimalakīrti to inquire about his illness.”

sanskrit: mañjuśrīr apy āha kiṃ cāpi durāsado 'sau bhagavan vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ,
english: Mañjuśrī replied, “Lord, it is difficult to attend upon the Licchavi Vimalakīrti.

sanskrit: gambhīranayapratibhānapraviṣṭaḥ, vyastasamastavacananirhārakuśalaḥ, aviṣṭhitapratibhānaḥ, apratimabuddhiḥ sarvasatveṣu,
english: He is gifted with marvelous eloquence concerning the law of the profound. He is extremely skilled in full expressions and in the reconciliation of dichotomies.

sanskrit: sarvabodhisatvakriyāsu niryātaḥ,
english: He accomplishes all the activities of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: sarvabodhisatvasarvabuddhaguhyasthāneṣu supraviṣṭaḥ, sarvamārasthānavivartanakuśalamahābhijñāvikrīḍitaḥ,
english: He penetrates all the secret mysteries of the bodhisattvas and the buddhas. He is skilled in civilizing all the abodes of devils.

sanskrit: advayāsaṃbhedadharmadhātugocaraparamapāramiprāptaḥ, ekavyūhadharmadhātvanantākāravyūhadharmanirdeśakaḥ,
english: He has attained the supreme excellence of the indivisible, nondual sphere of the ultimate realm. He is skilled in teaching the Dharma with its infinite modalities within the uniform ultimate.

sanskrit: sarvasatvendriyavyūhasaṃprāpaṇajñānakuśalaḥ, upāyakauśalyagatiṃgataḥ,
english: He is skilled in granting means of attainment in accordance with the spiritual faculties of all living beings.

sanskrit: prāptapraśnaviniścayaḥ /
english: He has attained decisiveness with regard to all questions.

sanskrit: sa na śakyo 'lpakena saṃnāhenābhirādhayitum / atha ca punar gamiṣyāmi buddhādhiṣṭhānena, tatra yathāśakti yathābalaṃ nirdekṣyāmi /
english: Thus, although he cannot be withstood by someone of my feeble defenses, still, sustained by the grace of the Buddha, I will go to him and will converse with him as well as I can.”

sanskrit: atha tataḥ parṣadas teṣāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ teṣāṃ ca śrāvakāṇāṃ teṣāṃ ca śakrabrahmalokapālānāṃ teṣāṃ ca devaputrāṇām etad abhavat
english: Thereupon, in that assembly, the bodhisattvas, the great disciples, the Śakras, the Brahmās, the Lokapālas, and the gods and goddesses, all had this thought

sanskrit: niścayena tatra mahādharmaśravaṇasāṃkathyaṃ bhaviṣyati, yatra mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtaḥ sa ca satpuruṣa ubhau saṃlapiṣyataḥ /
english: “Surely the conversations of the crown prince Mañjuśrī and that good man will result in a profound teaching of the Dharma.”

sanskrit: tatrāṣṭau ca bodhisatvasahasrāṇi pañcamātrāṇi ca śrāvakaśatāni saṃbahulāś ca śakrabrahmalokapālāḥ saṃbahulāni ca devaputraśatasahasrāṇi mañjuśriyam anubaddhāni dharmaśravaṇāya /
english: Thus, eight thousand bodhisattvas, five hundred disciples, a great number of Śakras, Brahmās, Lokapālas, and many hundreds of thousands of gods and goddesses, all followed the crown prince Mañjuśrī to listen to the Dharma.

sanskrit: atha mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūtas tair bodhisatvair mahāsatvais taiś ca śrāvakais taiś ca śakrabrahmalokapālair devaputraiś ca parivṛto vaiśālīṃ mahānagarīṃ praviśati sma /
english: And the crown prince Mañjuśrī, surrounded and followed by these bodhisattvas, disciples, Śakras, Brahmās, Lokapālas, gods, and goddesses, entered the great city of Vaiśālī.

sanskrit: atha vimalakīrter etad abhavat ayaṃ mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūta āgacchati mahatā parivāreṇa /
english: Meanwhile, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti thought to himself, “Mañjuśrī, the crown prince, is coming here with numerous attendants.

sanskrit: yan nv ahaṃ śūnyaṃ gṛham adhitiṣṭheyam /
english: Now, may this house be transformed into emptiness!”

sanskrit: tena taṃ gṛhaṃ śūnyam adhiṣṭhitam apagatadvārapālam /
english: Then, magically his house became empty.

sanskrit: upasaṃkramya praviśati sma /
english: Even the doorkeeper disappeared.

sanskrit: na cātra mañcān vā pīṭhān vāpaśyad anyatraikamañcāt, yatra vimalakīrtiḥ śayitaḥ /
english: And, except for the invalid’s couch upon which Vimalakīrti himself was lying, no bed or couch or seat could be seen anywhere.

sanskrit: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam adrākṣīt / dṛṣṭvā ca punar evam āha
english: Then, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti saw the crown prince Mañjuśrī and addressed him thus “Mañjuśrī!

sanskrit: svāgataṃ mañjuśriyo 'svāgataṃ mañjuśriyo 'nāgatasyādṛṣṭaśrutapūrvasya darśanam /
english: Welcome, Mañjuśrī! You are very welcome! Here you are, without previously having come, been seen, or been heard.

sanskrit: mañjuśrir āha evam etad gṛhapate yathā vadasi /
english: Mañjuśrī declared, “Householder, it is as you say.

sanskrit: ya āgato na sa bhūya āgamiṣyati / yaś ca gato na sa bhūyo gamiṣyati /
english: Who comes, ultimately comes not. Who goes, ultimately goes not.

sanskrit: na cāgatasyāgamanaṃ prajñāyate, na ca gatasya gamanam,
english: Coming is not really known in coming, and going is not really known in going.

sanskrit: yaś ca dṛṣṭo na bhūyo draṣṭavyaḥ /
english: What is seen is not to be seen again, ultimately.

sanskrit: api tu kaccit te satpuruṣa kṣapaṇīyam,
english: “Good sir, is your condition tolerable?

sanskrit: kaccid yāpanīyam,
english: Is it livable?

sanskrit: kaccid vātena pratikupyanti dhātavaḥ, kaccid apagacchati vyādhir na vivardhate /
english: Are your physical elements not disturbed? Is your sickness diminishing? Is it not increasing?

sanskrit: bhagavāṃs te 'lpābādhatāṃ paripṛcchati, alpātaṅkatāṃ cālpaglānyatāṃ ca laghūtthānatāṃ ca yatrāṃ ca balaṃ ca sukhaṃ cānavadyatāṃ ca sparśavihāratāṃ ca /
english: The Buddha asks about youif you have slight trouble, slight discomfort, slight sickness, if your distress is light, if you are cared for, strong, at ease, without selfreproach, and if you are living in touch with the supreme happiness.

sanskrit: kutra te gṛhapate idaṃ vyādhisamutthānam / kiyacciram upādāya te vyādhiḥ /
english: “Householder, whence came this sickness of yours? How long will it continue? How does it stand?

sanskrit: kadā copaśamiṣyati /
english: How can it be alleviated?”

sanskrit: vimalakirtir āha yāvacciram upādāya mañjuśrīḥ avidyā bhavatṛṣṇā ca tāvacciram upādāya mamaiṣa vyādhiḥ /
english: Vimalakīrti replied, “Mañjuśrī, my sickness comes from ignorance and the thirst for existence and it will last as long as do the sicknesses of all living beings.

sanskrit: yadā ca sarvasatvā vigatavyādhayo bhaviṣyanti tadā mama vyādhiḥ praśrabdho bhaviṣyati /
english: Were all living beings to be free from sickness, I also would not be sick.

sanskrit: satvādhiṣṭhāno hi mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvasya saṃsāraḥ / saṃsāraniśritaś ca vyādhiḥ /
english: Mañjuśrī, for the bodhisattva, the world consists only of living beings, and sickness is inherent in living in the world.

sanskrit: yadā sarvasatvā vigatavyādhayo bhaviṣyanti tadā bodhisatvo 'rogo bhaviṣyati /
english: Were all living beings free of sickness, the bodhisattva also would be free of sickness.

sanskrit: tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ śreṣṭhina ekaputrako glāno bhavet / tasya mātāpitarāv api glānau syātām /
english: For example, Mañjuśrī, when the only son of a merchant is sick, both his parents become sick on account of the sickness of their son.

sanskrit: tāvac ca duḥkhitau bhavetāṃ yāvan nāsāv ekaputrakas tayor vigatavyādhiḥ syāt /
english: And the parents will suffer as long as that only son does not recover from his sickness.

sanskrit: evaṃ mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvasya sarvasatveṣv ekaputrakaprema /
english: Just so, Mañjuśrī, the bodhisattva loves all living beings as if each were his only child.

sanskrit: sa satvaglānyena glāno bhavati, satvārogyāt tv arogaḥ /
english: He becomes sick when they are sick and is cured when they are cured.

sanskrit: yat punar mañjuśriḥ evaṃ vadasi ḥ kutaḥ samutthito vyādhir iti, mahākaruṇāsamutthito bodhisatvānāṃ vyādhiḥ /
english: You ask me, Mañjuśrī, whence comes my sickness the sicknesses of the bodhisattvas arise from great compassion.”

sanskrit: mañjuśrīr āha
english: Mañjuśrī

sanskrit: śūnyaṃ te gṛhapate gṛham /
english: Householder, why is your house empty?

sanskrit: na ca te kaścid upasthāyakaḥ /
english: Why have you no servants?

sanskrit: āha sarvabuddhakṣetrāṇy api mañjuśriḥ śūnyāni /
english: Vimalakīrti Mañjuśrī, all buddhafields are also empty. Mañjuśrī

sanskrit: āha kena śūnyāni /
english: What makes them empty?

sanskrit: āha śūnyatayā śūnyāni /
english: They are empty because of emptiness.

sanskrit: āha śūnyatāyāḥ kā śūnyatā /
english: What is “empty” about emptiness?

sanskrit: āha aparikalpanāś ca śūnyatāyāḥ śūnyatāḥ /
english: Constructions are empty, because of emptiness.

sanskrit: āha śakyā punaḥ śūnyatā parikalpayitum /
english: Can emptiness be conceptually constructed?

sanskrit: āha yenāpi parikalpyeta tad api śūnyam / na ca śūnyatā śūnyatāṃ parikalpayati /
english: Even that concept is itself empty, and emptiness cannot construct emptiness.

sanskrit: āha śūnyatā gṛhapate kuto mārgitavyā /
english: Householder, where should emptiness be sought?

sanskrit: āha śūnyatā mañjuśrīḥ dvāṣaṣṭibhyo dṛṣṭigatebhyo mārgitavyā /
english: Mañjuśrī, emptiness should be sought among the sixtytwo convictions. Mañjuśrī

sanskrit: āha dvāṣaṣṭiḥ punar dṛṣṭigatāni kuto mārgitavyāni /
english: Where should the sixtytwo convictions be sought?

sanskrit: āha tathāgatavimuktito mārgitavyāni /
english: They should be sought in the liberation of the tathāgatas.

sanskrit: āha tathāgatavimuktiḥ punaḥ kuto mārgitavyā /
english: Where should the liberation of the tathāgatas be sought?

sanskrit: āha sarvasatvacittacaritebhyo mārgitavyā /
english: It should be sought in the prime mental activity of all living beings.

sanskrit: yat punar mañjuśrīḥ evaṃ vadasi ḥ kas ta upasthāyaka iti / sarvamārāḥ sarvaparapravādinaś ca mamopasthāyakāḥ /
english: Mañjuśrī, you ask me why I am without servants, but all māras and opponents are my servants.

sanskrit: mārā hi saṃsārasya varṇavādinaḥ / saṃsāraś ca bodhisatvasyopasthāyakaḥ /
english: The māras advocate this life of birth and death and the bodhisattva does not avoid life.

sanskrit: parapravādino dṛṣṭigatānāṃ varṇavādinaḥ / bodhisatvaś ca sarvadṛṣṭigatebhyo na calati /
english: The outsider opponents advocate convictions, and the bodhisattva is not troubled by convictions.

sanskrit: tasmāt sarvamārāḥ sarvaparapravādinaś ca mamopasthāyakāḥ /
english: Therefore, all māras and opponents are my servants.

sanskrit: mañjuśrīr āha
english: Mañjuśrī

sanskrit: kidṛśo 'yaṃ te gṛhapate vyādhiḥ /
english: Householder, of what sort is your sickness?

sanskrit: āha adṛśyo 'nidarśanaḥ /
english: It is immaterial and invisible.

sanskrit: āha kim eṣa vyādhiḥ kāyasaṃprayukta uta cittasaṃprayuktaḥ /
english: Is it physical or mental?

sanskrit: āha na kāyasaṃprayuktaḥ kāyaviviktatayā /
english: It is not physical, since the body is insubstantial in itself.

sanskrit: na cittasaṃprayukto māyādharmatayā cittasya /
english: It is not mental, since the nature of the mind is like illusion.

sanskrit: āha catvāra ime gṛhapate dhātavaḥ / katame catvāraḥ,
english: Householder, which of the four main elements is disturbed

sanskrit: yad uta pṛthivīdhātur abdhātus tejodhātur vāyudhātur iti /
english: earth, water, fire, or air?

sanskrit: āha ya evaṃ dhātuko mañjuśrīḥ sarvasatvānāṃ vyādhis tenāhaṃ vyādhitaḥ /
english: Mañjuśrī, I am sick only because the elements of living beings are disturbed by sicknesses.

sanskrit: api tu khalu punar mañjuśrīḥ kathaṃ bodhisatvena glānako bodhisatvaḥ pratisaṃmoditavyaḥ /
english: Householder, how should a bodhisattva console another bodhisattva who is sick?

sanskrit: mañjuśrīr āha
english: Vimalakīrti

sanskrit: kāyānityatayā na ca nirvidvirāgatayā,
english: He should tell him that the body is impermanent, but should not exhort him to renunciation or disgust.

sanskrit: kāyaduḥkhatayā na ca nirvāṇābhinandanatayā, kāyānātmatayā satvaparipācanatayā ca, kāyaśāntatayā na cātyantaśamatayā,
english: He should tell him that the body is miserable, but should not encourage him to find solace in liberation that the body is selfless, but that living beings should be developed that the body is peaceful, but not to seek any ultimate calm.

sanskrit: sarvaduścaritadeśanatayā na ca saṃkrāntitaḥ, svaglānyena parasatvaglānakaruṇatayā, pūrvāntakoṭīduḥkhānusmaraṇatayā, satvārthakriyānusmaraṇatayā,
english: He should tell him to confess his evil deeds, but not just to escape them. He should encourage his empathy for all living beings on account of his own sickness, his remembrance of suffering experienced from beginningless time, and his consciousness of working for the welfare of living beings.

sanskrit: kuśalamūlābhimukhīkaraṇatayā, ādiviśuddhatayā, aparitarṣaṇatayā, sadāvīryāraṃbhāc ca, vaidyarājo bhaviṣyasi sarvavyādhīnāṃ śamayiteti /
english: He should encourage him to manifest the roots of virtue, to maintain the primal purity and the lack of craving, and thus to always strive to become the king of healers, who can cure all sicknesses.

sanskrit: evaṃ bodhisatvena bodhisatvo glānaḥ pratisaṃmoditavyaḥ /
english: Thus should a bodhisattva console a sick bodhisattva, in such a way as to make him happy.

sanskrit: mañjuśrīr āha kathaṃ kulaputra bodhisatvena glānena svacittaṃ nidhyapayitavyam /
english: Mañjuśrī asked, “‌Noble sir, how should a sick bodhisattva control his own mind?”

sanskrit: vimalakīrtir āha iha mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvena glānenaivaṃ svacittaṃ nidhyapayitavyam /
english: Vimalakīrti replied, “Mañjuśrī, a sick bodhisattva should control his own mind with the following consideration

sanskrit: pūrvāntāsadviparyāsakarmasamutthānasamutthito 'yaṃ vyādhir abhūtaparikalpakleśasamutthitaḥ /
english: Sickness arises from total involvement in the process of misunderstanding from beginningless time.

sanskrit: na punar atra kaścit paramārthato dharma upalabhyate yasyaiṣa vyādhiḥ / tat kasmād dhetoḥ /
english: It arises from the afflictions that result from unreal mental constructions, and hence ultimately nothing is perceived which can be said to be sick.

sanskrit: cāturmahābhautiko 'yaṃ samucchrayaḥ / na caiṣāṃ dhātūnāṃ kaścit svāmī na samutthāpayitā / anātmā hy ayaṃ samucchrayaḥ / yo 'yaṃ vyādhir nāma nāyaṃ paramārthata upalabhyate, anyatrātmābhiniveśāt /
english: The body is the issue of the four main elements, and in these elements there is no owner and no agent. There is no self in this body, and, except for arbitrary insistence on self, ultimately no ‘I’ which can be said to be sick can be apprehended.

sanskrit: uta nātmany abhiviniṣṭā vihariṣyāmo vyādhimūlaparijñātāvinaḥ / tenātmasaṃjñāṃ viṣṭhāpya dharmasaṃjñotpādayitavyā / dharmasaṃghāto 'yaṃ kāyaḥ /
english: Therefore, thinking, ‘ “I” should not adhere to any self, and “I” should rest in the knowledge of the root of illness,’ he should abandon the conception of himself as a personality and produce the conception of himself as a thing, thinking, ‘This body is an aggregate of many things.

sanskrit: dharmā evotpadyamānā utpadyante / dharmā eva nirudhyamānā nirudhyante /
english: When it is born, only things are born when it ceases, only things cease.

sanskrit: te ca dharmāḥ parasparaṃ na cetayanti na jānanti /
english: These things have no awareness or feeling of each other.

sanskrit: na ca teṣām utpadyamānānām evaṃ bhavaty utpadyāmaha iti / na nirudhyamānānām evaṃ bhavati nirudhyāmaha iti /
english: When they are born, they do not think, “I am born” when they cease, they do not think, “I cease.” ’

sanskrit: tena dharmasaṃjñāyā evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyam /
english: “Furthermore, he should understand thoroughly the conception of himself as a thing by cultivating the following consideration

sanskrit: yāpy eṣā dharmasaṃjñā so 'pi viparyāsaḥ / viparyāsaś ca mahāvyādhiḥ / vigatavyādhikena ca mayā bhavitavyam / vyādhiprahāṇāya ca yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ /
english: ‘Just as in the case of the conception of “self,” so the conception of “thing” is also a misunderstanding, and this misunderstanding is also a grave sickness I should free myself from this sickness and should strive to abandon it.’

sanskrit: tatra katamad vyādhiprahāṇam,
english: “What is the elimination of this sickness?

sanskrit: yad idam ahaṃkāramamakāraprahāṇam /
english: It is the elimination of egoism and possessiveness.

sanskrit: tac ca katamad ahaṃkāramamakāraprahāṇam,
english: What is the elimination of egoism and possessiveness?

sanskrit: yad idaṃ dvayavigamaḥ /
english: It is the freedom from dualism.

sanskrit: tatra katamo dvayavigamaḥ,
english: What is freedom from dualism?

sanskrit: yad idam adhyātmaṃ bahirdhā ca samudācāraḥ /
english: It is the absence of involvement with either the external or the internal.

sanskrit: tatra katamo 'dhyātmaṃ bahirdhā samudācāraḥ,
english: What is absence of involvement with either external or internal?

sanskrit: yad uta samatayācalanatāpracalanatā /
english: It is nondeviation, nonfluctuation, and nondistraction from sameness.

sanskrit: katamā ca samatā /
english: What is sameness?

sanskrit: ātmasamatayā ca nirvāṇasamatā /
english: It is the sameness of everything from self to liberation.

sanskrit: ubhe 'py ete śūnye, yad utātmā nirvāṇaṃ ca /
english: Because both self and liberation are void.

sanskrit: kenaite śūnye /
english: How can both be void?

sanskrit: nāmodāhāreṇaite śūnye / ubhāv apy etāv apariniṣpannau,
english: As verbal designations, they both are void, and neither is established in reality.

sanskrit: tena samadarśinā nānyo vyādhir nānyā śūnyatā kartavyā / vyādhir eva śūnyatā /
english: Therefore, one who sees such sameness makes no difference between sickness and voidness his sickness is itself voidness, and that sickness as voidness is itself void.

sanskrit: aviditā ca sā vedanā veditavyā / na cānena vedanānirodhaḥ sākṣātkartavyaḥ /
english: “The sick bodhisattva should recognize that sensation is ultimately nonsensation, but he should not realize the cessation of sensation.

sanskrit: aparipūrṇeṣu buddhadharmeṣūbhe vedane notsraṣṭavye / na ca durgatyupapannānāṃ satvānām antike mahākaruṇā notpādayitavyā /
english: Although both pleasure and pain are abandoned when the buddhaqualities are fully accomplished, there is then no sacrifice of the great compassion for all living beings living in the bad migrations.

sanskrit: tathā kariṣyāmo yathaiṣāṃ satvānām evam ayoniśonidhyaptyā vyādhim apaneṣyāmaḥ /
english: Thus, recognizing in his own suffering the infinite sufferings of these living beings, the bodhisattva correctly contemplates these living beings and resolves to cure all sicknesses.

sanskrit: na caiṣāṃ kaṃcid dharmam upaneṣyāmo nāpaneṣyāmaḥ / yato nidānāc ca punar vyādhir utpadyate tasya parijñāyai tebhyo dharmaṃ deśayiṣyāmaḥ /
english: “As for these living beings, there is nothing to be applied, and there is nothing to be removed one has only to teach them the Dharma for them to realize the basis from which sicknesses arise.

sanskrit: katamac ca punar nidānam,
english: What is this basis?

sanskrit: yad idam adhyālambananidānam / yāvatādhyālambananidānam adhyālambate, tāvad vyādhinidānam /
english: It is objectperception. To the extent that a basis of objectperception is objectified, it is the basis of sickness.

sanskrit: kiṃ cādhyālambate,
english: What is it that is objectified?

sanskrit: traidhātukam adhyālambate /
english: The three realms of existence are objectified.

sanskrit: tasyādhyālambanatayā kā parijñā,
english: What is the thorough understanding of the basis of that objectperception?

sanskrit: yad idam ālambanānupalambhaḥ / yaṃ hi nopalabhyate taṃ nālambate /
english: It is its nonperception, as one does not objectify a thing that is not perceived.

sanskrit: kiṃ ca nopalabhate,
english: What does one not perceive?

sanskrit: ubhe dṛṣṭī nopalabhate, yad idam ātmadṛṣṭiṃ paradṛṣṭiṃ ca /
english: One does not perceive the two views, the view of the self and the view of the other.

sanskrit: tad ucyate 'nupalambha iti /
english: Therefore, it is called nonperception.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi mañjuśrīḥ glānena bodhisatvena svacittaṃ nidhyapayitavyaṃ jarāvyādhimaraṇopapattiprahāṇāya /
english: “Mañjuśrī, thus should a sick bodhisattva control his own mind in order to overcome old age, sickness, death, and birth.

sanskrit: evaṃ ca mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvānāṃ bodhir yadi na bhavet,
english: Such, Mañjuśrī, is the sickness of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: nirarthako nanu vyāyāmo bhavet /
english: If he takes it otherwise, all his efforts will be in vain.

sanskrit: yathā pratyarthikanirghātāc churā ity ucyante, evam eva jarāvyādhimaraṇaduḥkhopaśamanād bodhisatvā ity ucyante /
english: Just as one is called ‘hero’ when one overcomes all enemies, so, too, one is called ‘bodhisattva’ when one conquers the miseries of aging, sickness, and death.

sanskrit: tena bodhisatvena vyādhitenaivaṃ pratyavekṣitavyam /
english: “The sick bodhisattva should tell himself

sanskrit: yathā mama vyādhir abhūto 'sann evaṃ sarvasatvānām api vyādhir abhūto 'sann iti / tasyaivaṃ pratyavekṣamāṇasya nānuśaṃsādṛṣṭipatitā satveṣu mahākaruṇotpadyate, anyatrāgantukakleśaprahāṇābhiyuktyā satveṣu mahākaruṇotpadyate /
