english: ‘Just as my sickness is unreal and nonexistent, so the sicknesses of all living beings are unreal and nonexistent.’ Through such considerations, he arouses the great compassion toward all living beings without falling into any sentimental compassion, but instead, arouses great compassion toward all living beings through striving to eliminate the incidental afflictions.

sanskrit: anuśaṃsadṛṣṭipatitayaiva hi mahākaruṇayā bodhisatvasya khedo bhavaty upapattiṣu /
english: Because great compassion that falls into sentimentally purposive views only exhausts the bodhisattva in his reincarnations.

sanskrit: anuśaṃsadṛṣṭiparyutthānavigatayā punar mahākaruṇayā bodhisatvasya khedo na bhavaty upapattiṣu / so 'yam upapadyate, na ca dṛṣṭiparyutthānaparyutthita upapadyate /
english: But the great compassion that is free of involvement with sentimentally purposive views does not exhaust the bodhisattva in all his reincarnations. He does not reincarnate through involvement with such views but reincarnates with his mind free of involvement.

sanskrit: so 'paryutthitacitta upapadyamāno mukta evotpadyate mukta eva jāyate /
english: Hence, even his reincarnation is like a liberation.

sanskrit: sa mukta evotpadyamāno mukta eva jāyamāno baddhānāṃ satvānāṃ śaktaḥ pratibalo bandhamokṣāya dharmaṃ deśayitum /
english: Being reincarnated as if being liberated, he has the power and ability to teach the Dharma that liberates living beings from their bondage.

sanskrit: yathoktaṃ bhagavatā sa tāvad ātmanā baddhaḥ paraṃ bandhanān mocayiṣyatīti nādaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate /
english: As the Lord declares ‘It is not possible for one who is himself bound to deliver others from their bondage.

sanskrit: yas tv ātmanā muktaḥ paraṃ bandhanān mocayiṣyatīti sthānam etad vidyate tasmān muktena bodhisatvena bhavitavyam, na baddhena /
english: But one who is himself liberated is able to liberate others from their bondage.’ Therefore, the bodhisattva should participate in liberation and should not participate in bondage.

sanskrit: tatra katamo bandhaḥ,
english: “What is bondage?

sanskrit: katamo mokṣaḥ /
english: And what is liberation?

sanskrit: anupāyād bhavagatiparigraho bodhisatvasya bandhaḥ,
english: To indulge in liberation from the world without employing liberative art is bondage for the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: upāyād bhavagatigamanaṃ mokṣaḥ /
english: To engage in life in the world with full employment of liberative art is liberation for the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: anupāyād dhyānasamādhyāsvādanatā bodhisatvasya bandhaḥ,
english: To experience the taste of contemplation, meditation, and concentration without skill in liberative art is bondage.

sanskrit: upāyena dhyānasamādhyāsvādanatā mokṣaḥ /
english: To experience the taste of contemplation and meditation with skill in liberative art is liberation.

sanskrit: anupāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā bandhaḥ, upāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā mokṣaḥ /
english: Wisdom not integrated with liberative art is bondage, but wisdom integrated with liberative art is liberation.

sanskrit: prajñayāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo bandhanam, prajñāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo mokṣaḥ /
english: Liberative art not integrated with wisdom is bondage, but liberative art integrated with wisdom is liberation.

sanskrit: tatra katamo 'nupāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā bandhaḥ,
english: “How is wisdom not integrated with liberative art a bondage?

sanskrit: yad idaṃ śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitanidhyaptiḥ, na ca lakṣaṇānuvyañjanabuddhakṣetrālaṃkārasatvaparipācananidhyaptiḥ / iyam anupāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā bandhaḥ /
english: Wisdom not integrated with liberative art consists of concentration on voidness, signlessness, and wishlessness, and yet it fails to concentrate on cultivation of the auspicious signs and marks, on the adornment of the buddhafield, and on the work of development of living beingsand it is bondage.

sanskrit: tatra katamopāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā mokṣaḥ,
english: “How is wisdom integrated with liberative art a liberation?

sanskrit: yad idaṃ lakṣanānuvyañjanabuddhakṣetrālaṃkārasatvaparipācananidhyapticittaṃ ca śūnyatānimittāpraṇihitaparijayaś ca / iyam upāyasaṃgṛhītā prajñā mokṣaḥ /
english: Wisdom integrated with liberative art consists of concentration on cultivation of the auspicious signs and marks, on the adornment of the buddhafield, and on the work of development of living beings, all the while concentrating on deep investigation of voidness, signlessness, and wishlessnessand it is liberation.

sanskrit: tatra katamaḥ prajñayāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo bandhaḥ,
english: “What is the bondage of liberative art not integrated with wisdom?

sanskrit: yad idaṃ sarvadṛṣṭikleśaparyutthānānuśayānunayapratighapratiṣṭhitasya sarvakuśalamūlārambho bodhau cāpariṇāmanā / ayaṃ prajñayāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo bandhaḥ /
english: The bondage of liberative art not integrated with wisdom consists of the bodhisattva’s planting of the roots of virtue without dedicating them for the sake of enlightenment, while living in the grip of dogmatic convictions, passions, attachments, resentments, and their subconscious instincts.

sanskrit: tatra katamaḥ prajñāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo mokṣaḥ,
english: “What is the liberation of liberative art integrated with wisdom?

sanskrit: yad idaṃ sarvadṛṣṭikleśaparyutthānānuśayānunayapratighaprahīṇasya sarvakuśalamūlārambho bodhau pariṇāmitas tasya cāparāmarśaḥ / ayaṃ bodhisatvasya prajñāsaṃgṛhīta upāyo mokṣaḥ /
english: The liberation of liberative art integrated with wisdom consists of the bodhisattva’s dedication of his roots of virtue for the sake of enlightenment, without taking any pride therein, while forgoing all convictions, passions, attachments, resentments, and their subconscious instincts.

sanskrit: tatra mañjuśrīḥ glānena bodhisatvenaivam ime dharmā nidhyapayitavyāḥ /
english: “Mañjuśrī, thus should the sick bodhisattva consider things.

sanskrit: kāyasya cittasya ca vyādheś cānityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmapratyavekṣaṇā, iyam asya prajñā /
english: His wisdom is the consideration of body, mind, and sickness as impermanent, miserable, empty, and selfless.

sanskrit: yat punaḥ kāyavyādhipariharaṇatayā na khidyate, na pratibadhnāti saṃsāram, satvārthayogam anuyuktaḥ, ayam asyopāyaḥ /
english: His liberative art consists of not exhausting himself by trying to avoid all physical sickness, and of applying himself to accomplish the benefit of living beings, without interrupting the cycle of reincarnations.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ yat kāyasya vyādheś cittasya cānyonyaparāparatāṃ na nirnavatāniḥpurāṇatāṃ pratyavekṣate, iyam asya prajñā /
english: Furthermore, his wisdom lies in understanding that body, mind, and sickness are neither new nor old, whether considered simultaneously or sequentially.

sanskrit: yat punaḥ kāyasya vyādheś cittasya ca nātyantopaśamaṃ nirodham atyayati,
english: And his liberative art lies in not seeking pacification or cessation of body, mind, or sicknesses.

sanskrit: evaṃ hi mañjuśriḥ glānena bodhisatvena cittaṃ nidhyapayitavyam / na ca tena nidhyaptau vānidhyaptau vā sthātavyam /
english: “That, Mañjuśrī, is the way a sick bodhisattva should concentrate his mind he should live neither in control of his mind, nor in indulgence of his mind.

sanskrit: yadi hy anidhyaptau tiṣṭhed bāladharma eṣaḥ / atha nidhyaptau tiṣṭhec chrāvakadharma eṣaḥ /
english: To live by indulging the mind is proper for fools and to live in control of the mind is proper for the disciples.

sanskrit: tasmād bodhisatvena na nidhyaptau sthātavyam /
english: Therefore, the bodhisattva should live neither in control nor in indulgence of his mind.

sanskrit: yad atrāsthānam ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: Not living in either of the two extremes is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yan na pṛthagjanagocaro nāryagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yat saṃsāragocaraś ca na ca kleśagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: “Not the domain of the ordinary individual and not the domain of the arhat, such is the domain of the bodhisattva. The domain of the world yet not the domain of the afflictions, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yan nirvāṇapratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca na cātyantaparinirvāṇagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: Where one understands liberation, yet does not enter final and complete liberation, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yac caturmārasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca sarvamāraviṣayātikrāntagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: Where the four māras manifest, yet where all the works of māras are transcended, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat sarvajñajñānaparyeṣṭigocaraś ca na cākāle jñānaprāptigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: Where one seeks the gnosis of omniscience, yet does not attain this gnosis at the wrong time, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yac catuḥsatyajñānagocaraś ca na cākāle satyaprativedhagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: Where one knows the four noble truths, yet does not realize those truths at the wrong time, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yad adhyātmapratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca saṃcintyabhavopapattiparigrahagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: A domain of introspective insight, wherein one does not arrest voluntary reincarnation in the world, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yad ajātipratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca na ca niyāmāvakrāntigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: A domain where one realizes birthlessness, yet does not become destined for the ultimate, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat pratītyasamutpādagocaraś ca sarvadṛṣṭivigatagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: Where one sees relativity without entertaining any convictions, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat sarvasatvasaṃgaṇikāgocaraś ca na ca kleśānuśayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: Where one associates with all beings, yet keeps free of all afflictive instincts, there is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yad vivekagocaraś ca na ca kāyacittakṣayaniśrayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: A domain of solitude with no place for the exhaustion of body and mind, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat traidhātukagocaraś ca na ca dharmadhātusaṃbhedagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of the triple world, yet indivisible from the ultimate realm, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yac chūnyatāgocaraś ca sarvākāraguṇaparyeṣṭigocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad ānimittagocaraś ca satvapramocanārambaṇavitarkagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of voidness, yet where one cultivates all types of virtues, such is the domain of the bodhisattva. The domain of signlessness, where one keeps in sight the deliverance of all living beings, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yad apraṇihitagocaraś ca saṃcintyabhavagatisaṃdarśanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of wishlessness, where one voluntarily manifests lives in the world, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yad anabhisaṃskāragocaraś ca sarvakuśalamūlābhisaṃskārāpratiprasrabdhigocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: “A domain essentially without undertaking, yet where all the roots of virtue are undertaken without interruption, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat ṣaṭpāramitāgocaraś ca sarvasatvacittacaritapāragamanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of the six transcendences, where one attains the transcendence of the thoughts and actions of all living beings, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat ṣaḍanusmṛtigocaraś ca na ca sarvāsravakṣayagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of the six superknowledges, wherein defilements are not exhausted, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat saddharmapratiṣṭhānagocaraś ca na ca kumārgādhyālambanagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of living by the holy Dharma, without even perceiving any evil paths, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yac caturapramāṇagocaraś ca na ca brahmalokopapattisparśanagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of the four immeasurables, where one does not accept rebirth in the heaven of Brahmā, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yad dhyānasamādhisamāpattigocaraś ca na ca samādhisamāpattivaśenopapattigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of contemplation, concentration, and absorption, where one does not reincarnate in the formless realms by force of these concentrations and absorptions, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat smṛtyupasthānagocaraś ca na ca kāyavedanācittadharmātyarthagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of the four foci of mindfulness, where body, sensation, mind, and things are not ultimately of concern, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat samyakprahāṇagocaraś ca na ca kuśalākuśaladvayopalambhagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of the four right efforts, where the duality of good and evil is not apprehended, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yad ṛddhipādābhinirhāragocaraś cānābhogarddhipādavaśavartigocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of the four bases of magical powers, where they are effortlessly mastered, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat pañcendriyagocaraś ca sarvasatvendriyaparāparajñānagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of the five spiritual faculties, where one knows the degrees of the spiritual faculties of living beings, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat pañcabalapratiṣṭhānagocaraś ca daśatathāgatabalābhisaṃdarśanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of living with the five powers, where one delights in the ten powers of the tathāgata, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yat saptabodhyaṅgapariniṣpattigocaraś ca buddhiprabhedajñānakauśalyagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of perfection of the seven factors of enlightenment, where one is skilled in the knowledge of fine intellectual distinctions, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yan mārgapratiṣṭhānagocaraś ca kumārgānadhyālambanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yac chamathavidarśanāsaṃbhāraparyeṣṭigocaraś ca na cātyantaśāntipatanagocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of living by the eightfold path, without even perceiving any evil paths, such is the domain of the bodhisattva. The domain of the cultivation of the aptitude for mental quiescence and transcendental analysis, where one does not fall into extreme quietism, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yad anutpādalakṣaṇasarvadharmamīmāṃsanagocaraś ca rūpalakṣanānuvyañjanabuddhakāyālaṃkārapariniṣpattigocaraḥ, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of the realization of the unborn nature of all things, yet of the perfection of the body, the auspicious signs and marks, and the ornaments of the Buddha, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yac chrāvakapratyekabuddhākalpasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca buddhadharmātyajanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of manifesting the attitudes of the disciples and the solitary sages without sacrificing the qualities of the Buddha, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yad atyantaviśuddhiprakṛtisamāpannasarvadharmānugamanagocaraś ca yathādhimuktisarvasatveryāpathasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca, ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain of conformity to all things utterly pure in nature while manifesting behavior that suits the inclinations of all living beings, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: yad atyantāsaṃvartavivartākāśasvabhāvasarvabuddhakṣetrapratyavekṣaṇagocaraś ca nānāvyūhānekavyūhabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca,
english: A domain where one realizes that all the buddhafields are indestructible and uncreatable, having the nature of infinite space, yet where one manifests the establishment of the qualities of the buddhafields in all their variety and magnitude, such is the domain of the bodhisattva.

sanskrit: ayaṃ bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ / yad dharmacakrapravartanamahāparinirvāṇasaṃdarśanagocaraś ca bodhisatvacaryātyajanagocaraś ca, ayam api bodhisatvasya gocaraḥ /
english: The domain where one turns the wheel of the holy Dharma and manifests the magnificence of ultimate liberation, yet never forsakes the career of the bodhisattva, such is the domain of the bodhisattva!”

sanskrit: iha nirdeśe nirdiśyamāne ye mañjuśriyā kumārabhūtena sārdham āgatā devaputrās tato 'ṣṭānāṃ devaputrasahasrāṇām anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni // //
english: When Vimalakīrti had spoken this discourse, eight thousand of the gods in the company of the crown prince Mañjuśrī conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: glānapratisaṃmodanāparivartaś caturthaḥ //
english: The Inconceivable Liberation

sanskrit: athāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasyaitad abhavat
english: Thereupon, the venerable Śāriputra had this thought

sanskrit: kutreme bodhisatvā niṣatsyanti, ime ca mahāśrāvakāḥ / neha gṛha āsanāni saṃvidyante /
english: “There is not even a single chair in this house. Where are these disciples and bodhisattvas going to sit?”

sanskrit: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya cetovitarkam ājñāyāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram etad avocat
english: The Licchavi Vimalakīrti read the thought of the venerable Śāriputra and said, “Reverend Śāriputra, did you come here for the sake of the Dharma?

sanskrit: kiṃ bhadantaśāriputro dharmārthika āgata utāsanārthikaḥ / āha dharmārthikā vayam āgatā nāsanārthikāḥ /
english: Or did you come here for the sake of a chair?” Śāriputra replied, “I came for the sake of the Dharma, not for the sake of a chair.”

sanskrit: āha tena hi bhadantaśāriputra yo dharmarthiko bhavati, nāsau svakāyārthiko bhavati /
english: Vimalakīrti continued, “Reverend Śāriputra, he who is interested in the Dharma is not interested even in his own body, much less in a chair.

sanskrit: yo bhadantaśāriputra dharmārthiko bhavati, na sa rūpavedanāsaṃjñāsaṃskāravijñānārthiko bhavati,
english: Reverend Śāriputra, he who is interested in the Dharma has no interest in matter, sensation, intellect, motivation, or consciousness.

sanskrit: na skandhadhātvāyatanārthikaḥ /
english: He has no interest in these aggregates, or in the elements, or in the sensemedia.

sanskrit: yo dharmārthikaḥ, na sa kāmadhāturupadhātvārūpyadhātvarthiko bhavati,
english: Interested in the Dharma, he has no interest in the realm of desire, the realm of pure matter, or the immaterial realm.

sanskrit: nāsau buddhābhiniveśārthiko bhavati, na dharmasaṃghābhiniveśārthikaḥ /
english: Interested in the Dharma, he is not interested in attachment to the Buddha, attachment to the Dharma, or attachment to the Saṅgha.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra yo dharmārthikaḥ, nāsau duḥkhaparijñānārthiko na samudayaprahāṇārthiko na nirodhasākṣātkriyārthiko na mārgabhāvanārthiko bhavati /
english: Reverend Śāriputra, he who is interested in the Dharma is not interested in recognizing suffering, abandoning its origination, realizing its cessation, or practicing the path.

sanskrit: aprapañco hi dharmo nirakṣaraḥ /
english: The Dharma is ultimately without formulation and without verbalization.

sanskrit: tatra yaḥ prapañcayati ḥ duḥkhaṃ parijñāsyāmi samudayaṃ prahāsyāmi nirodhaṃ sākṣātkariṣyāmi mārgaṃ bhāvayiṣyāmīti, nasau dharmārthikaḥ, prapañcārthiko 'sau /
english: Who verbalizes ‘Suffering should be recognized, origination should be eliminated, cessation should be realized, the path should be practiced,’ is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in verbalization.

sanskrit: dharmo hi bhadantaśāriputra upaśāntaḥ /
english: “Reverend Śāriputra, the Dharma is calm and peaceful.

sanskrit: tatra ya utpādavyaye caranti, na te dharmārthikā na vivekārthikāḥ, utpādavyayārthikās te /
english: Those who are engaged in production and destruction are not interested in the Dharma, are not interested in solitude, but are interested in production and destruction.

sanskrit: dharmo hy arajo rajo'pagataḥ / tatra ye kvacid dharme rakṣante 'ntaśo nirvāṇe 'pi, na te dharmārthikāḥ,
english: He who is attached to anything, even to liberation, is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in the taint of desire.

sanskrit: dharmo hy aviṣayaḥ /
english: The Dharma is not an object.

sanskrit: ye viṣayasaṃkhyātāḥ, na te dharmārthikāḥ, viṣayārthikās te /
english: He who pursues objects is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in objects.

sanskrit: dharmo nāyūho niryūhaḥ /
english: The Dharma is without acceptance or rejection.

sanskrit: ye kecid dharmaṃ gṛhṇanti vā muñcanti vā, na te dharmārthikāḥ, udgrahaniḥsargārthikās te /
english: He who holds on to things or lets go of things is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in holding and letting go.

sanskrit: dharmo 'nālayaḥ /
english: The Dharma is not a secure refuge.

sanskrit: ya ālayārāmāḥ, na te dharmārthikāḥ, ālayārthikās te /
english: He who enjoys a secure refuge is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in a secure refuge.

sanskrit: dharmo nirnimittaḥ /
english: The Dharma is without sign.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ nimittānusārivijñānam, na te dharmārthikāḥ, nimittārthikās te /
english: He whose consciousness pursues signs is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in signs.

sanskrit: dharmo 'saṃvāsaḥ /
english: The Dharma is not a society.

sanskrit: ye kecid dharmeṇa sārdhaṃ saṃvasanti, na te dharmārthikāḥ, saṃvāsārthikās te /
english: He who seeks to associate with the Dharma is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in association.

sanskrit: dharmo 'dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātaḥ /
english: The Dharma is not a sight, a sound, a category, or an idea.

sanskrit: ye dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñāteṣu caranti, na te dharmārthikāḥ, dṛṣṭaśrutamatavijñātārthikās te /
english: He who is involved in sights, sounds, categories, and ideas is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in sights, sounds, categories, and ideas.

sanskrit: dharmo bhadantaśāriputra asaṃskṛtaḥ saṃskṛtāpagataḥ /
english: Reverend Śāriputra, the Dharma is free of compounded things and uncompounded things.

sanskrit: ye saṃskṛtagocarāḥ, na te dharmārthikāḥ, saṃskṛtodgrahaṇārthikās te /
english: He who adheres to compounded things and uncompounded things is not interested in the Dharma but is interested in adhering to compounded things and uncompounded things.

sanskrit: tasmād iha bhadantaśāriputra dharmārthikena te bhavitukāmena sarvadharmānarthikena bhavitavyam /
english: “Thereupon, reverend Śāriputra, if you are interested in the Dharma, you should take no interest in anything.”

sanskrit: iha dharmanirdeśe nirdiśyamāne pañcānāṃ devaputraśatānāṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur viśuddham /
english: When Vimalakīrti had spoken this discourse, five hundred gods obtained the purity of the Dharmaeye in viewing all things.

sanskrit: tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ daśasu dikṣv asaṃkhyeyeṣu buddhakṣetraśatasahasreṣu buddhakṣetracārikāṃ carasi / tat katarasmin buddhakṣetre tvayā sarvaviśiṣṭāni sarvaguṇopetāni siṃhāsanāni dṛṣṭāni /
english: Then, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti said to the crown prince, Mañjuśrī, “Mañjuśrī, you have already been in innumerable hundreds of thousands of buddhafields throughout the universes of the ten directions. In which buddhafield did you see the best lionthrones with the finest qualities?”

sanskrit: evam ukte mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim etad avocat asti kulaputra pūrve digbhāge ṣaṭtriṃśadgaṅgānadīvālikāsamāni buddhakṣetrāṇy atikramya merudhvajā nāma lokadhātuḥ /
english: Mañjuśrī replied, “‌Noble sir, if one crosses the buddhafields to the east, which are more numerous than all the grains of sand of thirtytwo Ganges rivers, one will discover a universe called Merudhvaja.

sanskrit: tatra merupradīparājo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddhas tiṣṭhati dhriyate yāpayati /
english: There dwells a tathāgata called Meru­pradīpa­rāja.

sanskrit: tasya tathāgatasya caturaśītiyojanaśatasahasra ātmabhāvaḥ / aṣṭaṣaṣṭiyojanaśatasahasraṃ tasya bhagavataḥ siṃhāsanam /
english: His body measures eightyfour hundred thousand leagues in height, and the height of his throne is sixtyeight hundred thousand leagues.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ ca bodhisatvānāṃ catvāriṃśadyojanaśatasahasra ātmabhāvaḥ / catustriṃśadyojanaśatasahāsrāni teṣāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ siṃhāsanāni /
english: The bodhisattvas there are fortytwo hundred thousand leagues tall and their own thrones are thirtyfour hundred thousand leagues high.

sanskrit: merudhvajāyāṃ lokadhātau tasya bhagavato merupradīparājasya tathāgatasya buddhakṣetre sarvaviśiṣṭāni sarvagunopetāni siṃhāsanāni /
english: ‌Noble sir, the finest and most superb thrones exist in that universe Merudhvaja, which is the buddhafield of the Tathāgata Meru­pradīpa­rāja.”

sanskrit: atha vimalakīrtir licchavis tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathārūpaṃ samanvāhāraṃ samanvāharati sma / tādṛśaṃ carddhyabhisaṃskāram abhisaṃskṛtavān, yat tato merudhvajālokadhātor dvātriṃśatsiṃhāsanaśatasahasrāṇi tena bhagavatā merupradīparājena tathāgatena preṣitāni /
english: At that moment, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti, having focused himself in concentration, performed a miraculous feat such that the Lord Tathāgata Meru­pradīpa­rāja, in the universe Merudhvaja, sent to this universe thirtytwo hundred thousand thrones.

sanskrit: tāvad udviddhāni tāvad vistīrṇāni tāvad darśanīyāni yad apūrvāṇi tair bodhisatvais taiś ca mahāśrāvakais taiś ca śakrabrahmalokapālair devaputraiś ca /
english: These thrones were so tall, spacious, and beautiful that the bodhisattvas, great disciples, Śakras, Brahmās, Lokapālas, and other gods had never before seen the like.

sanskrit: tāny upary antarīkṣeṇāgatya vimalakirter licchaver niveśane pratyatiṣṭhan /
english: The thrones descended from the sky and came to rest in the house of the Licchavi Vimalakīrti.

sanskrit: yatra tāni dvātriṃśatsiṃhāsanaśatasahasrāṇi vicitrāṇy anutpīḍanatayā /
english: The thirtytwo hundred thousand thrones arranged themselves without crowding and the house seemed to enlarge itself accordingly.

sanskrit: na ca vaiśālyā mahānagaryā āvaraṇaṃ kṛtam, na jambūdvīpasya, na cāturdvīpikasyāvaraṇam /
english: The great city of Vaiśālī did not become obscured neither did the land of Jambudvīpa, nor the world of four continents.

sanskrit: sarve te tathaiva saṃdṛśyante yathā pūrvaṃ tathā paścāt /
english: Everything else appeared just as it was before.

sanskrit: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir mañjuśriyaṃ kumārabhūtam etad avocat niṣida tvaṃ mañjuśrīḥ siṃhāsane sārdham etair bodhisatvaiḥ /
english: Then, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti said to the crown prince Mañjuśrī, “Mañjuśrī, let the bodhisattvas be seated on these thrones, having transformed their bodies to a suitable size!”

sanskrit: atha ye 'bhijñāpratilabdhā bodhisatvās te dvācatvāriṃśadyojanaśatasahasram ātmabhāvam adhiṣṭhāya teṣu siṃhāsaneṣu nisīdanti sma /
english: Then, those bodhisattvas who had attained the superknowledges transformed their bodies to a height of fortytwo hundred thousand leagues and sat upon the thrones.

sanskrit: ye cādikarmikā bodhisatvās te na śaknuvanti sma teṣu siṃhāsaneṣu niṣattum /
english: But the beginner bodhisattvas were not able to transform themselves to sit upon the thrones.

sanskrit: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram āmantrayate sma niṣīda bhadantaśāriputra siṃhāsane /
english: The Licchavi Vimalakīrti said to the venerable Śāriputra, “Reverend Śāriputra, take your seat upon a throne.”

sanskrit: āha na śaknomi satpuruṣa niṣattum uccāni pragṛhitāni cemāni siṃhāsanāni /
english: He replied, “Good sir, the thrones are too big and too high, and I cannot sit upon them.”

sanskrit: āha tena hi bhadantaśāriputra tasyaiva bhagavato merupradīparājasya tathāgatasya namaskāraṃ kuru /
english: Vimalakīrti said, “Reverend Śāriputra, bow down to the Tathāgata Meru­pradīpa­rāja, and you will be able to take your seat.”

sanskrit: atha te mahāśrāvakās tasya bhagavato merupradīparājasya tathāgatasya namaskāraṃ kurvanti sma /
english: Then, the great disciples bowed down to the Tathāgata Merupradīparāja and they were seated upon the thrones.

sanskrit: vimalakīrtir āha asti bhadantaśāriputra tathāgatānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ cācintyo nāma vimokṣaḥ, yatrācintyavimokṣe pratiṣṭhito bodhisatvaḥ sumeruṃ parvatarājaṃ tāvad uccaṃ tāvat pragṛhītaṃ tāvad udviddhaṃ tāvad vistīrṇaṃ sarṣapaphalakośe praveśayet /
english: The Licchavi Vimalakīrti replied, “Reverend Śāriputra, for the tathāgatas and the bodhisattvas, there is a liberation called ‘inconceivable.’ The bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation can put the king of mountains, Sumeru, which is so high, so great, so noble, and so vast, into a mustard seed.

sanskrit: na ca sarṣapaphalakośaṃ vivardhayet / na ca sumeruṃ hāpayet /
english: He can perform this feat without enlarging the mustard seed and without shrinking Mount Sumeru.

sanskrit: na cāturmahārājakāyikā devās trayastriṃśato vā jānīran ḥ kasmin vayaṃ prakṣiptāḥ / anye ca satvā ṛddhivineyā jānīyuḥ paśyeyus taṃ sumeruṃ parvatarājaṃ sarśapaphalakośapraviṣṭam /
english: And the deities of the assembly of the four Mahārājas and of the Trayastriṃśa heavens do not even know where they are. Only those beings who are destined to be disciplined by miracles see and understand the putting of the king of mountains, Sumeru, into the mustard seed.

sanskrit: ayaṃ bhadantaśāriputra bodhisatvānām acintyasya vimokṣasya viṣayapraveśaḥ /
english: That, reverend Śāriputra, is an entrance to the domain of the inconceivable liberation of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvo yaś caturṣu mahāsamudreṣv apskandhas tam ekasmin romakūpe prakṣipet na ca matsyakacchapaśiśumāramaṇḍūkānām anyeṣāṃ vaudakānāṃ prāṇināṃ pīḍā bhavet / na ca nāgayakṣagandharvāsurāṇām evaṃ bhavet ḥ kasmin vayaṃ prakṣiptāḥ /
english: “Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, the bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation can pour into a single pore of his skin all the waters of the four great oceans, without injuring the wateranimals such as fish, tortoises, crocodiles, frogs, and other creatures, and without the nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, and asuras even being aware of where they are.

sanskrit: sā ca kriyā prajñāyeta / na ca kaścit satvo vihiṃsito viheṭhito vā bhavet /
english: And the whole operation is visible without any injury or disturbance to any of those living beings.

sanskrit: imaṃ ca trisāhasramahāsāhasraṃ lokadhātuṃ bhārgavacakram iva parigṛhya dakṣiṇe pāṇāv avabhrāmya gaṅgānadīvālikāsamān lokadhātūn kṣipet na ca satvā jānīran ḥ kasmin vayaṃ nītāḥ, kuto vāgatā iti / punar api cānāyya yathāsthānaṃ sthāpayet / na ca gamanāgamanaṃ saṃjānīran /
english: “Such a bodhisattva can pick up with his right hand this billionworld galactic universe as if it were a potter’s wheel and, spinning it round, throw it beyond universes as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, without the living beings therein knowing their motion or its origin, and he can catch it and put it back in its place, without the living beings suspecting their coming and going and yet the whole operation is visible.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra santi satvā apramāṇasaṃsāravainayikāḥ / santi saṃkṣiptasaṃsāravainayikāḥ /
english: “Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, there are beings who become disciplined after an immense period of evolution, and there are also those who are disciplined after a short period of evolution.

sanskrit: tatrācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvo 'pramāṇasaṃsāravainayikānāṃ satvānāṃ vainayikavaśam upādāya saptarātraṃ kalpam atikrāntam ādarśayet saṃkṣiptasaṃsāravainayikānāṃ satvānāṃ vainayikavaśam upādāya kalpaṃ saptarātram atikrāntam ādarśayet /
english: The bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation, for the sake of disciplining those living beings who are disciplined through immeasurable periods of evolution, can make the passing of a week seem like the passing of an eon, and he can make the passing of an eon seem like the passing of a week for those who are disciplined through a short period of evolution.

sanskrit: tatrāpramāṇasaṃsāravineyāḥ satvāḥ saptarātraṃ kalpam atikrāntaṃ saṃjānīran I saṃkṣiptasaṃsāravineyāḥ satvāḥ kalpaṃ saptarātram atikrāntaṃ saṃjānīran
english: The living beings who are disciplined through an immeasurable period of evolution actually perceive a week to be the passing of an eon, and those disciplined by a short period of evolution actually perceive an eon to be the passing of a week.

sanskrit: iti hy acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvaḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhān ekasmin buddhakṣetre saṃdarśayati /
english: “Thus, a bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation can manifest all the splendors of the virtues of all the buddhafields within a single buddhafield.

sanskrit: sarvasatvān api dakṣiṇe karatale pratiṣṭhāpya cittajāyikayarddhyā kramet / sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu ca saṃdarśanaṃ dadyāt /
english: Likewise, he can place all living beings in the palm of his right hand and can show them with the supernatural speed of thought all the buddhafields without ever leaving his own buddhafield.

sanskrit: yāvatyaś ca daśasu dikṣu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūjā vartante, tāḥ sarvā ekaromakūpa ādarśayet / yāvantaś ca daśasu dikṣu candrasūryās tārārūpāni ca,
english: He can display in a single pore all the offerings ever offered to all the buddhas of the ten directions, and the orbs of all the suns, moons, and stars of the ten directions.

sanskrit: yāvatyaś ca daśasu dikṣu vātamaṇḍalyaḥ pravānti, tā api sarvā mukhadvāre praveśayet / na cāsya kāyo vikīryeta / na ca tatra buddhakṣetre tṛṇavanaspatayo nameyuḥ /
english: He can inhale all the hurricanes of the cosmic windatmospheres of the ten directions into his mouth without harming his own body and without letting the forests and the grasses of the buddhafields be flattened.

sanskrit: yāni ca daśasu dikṣu buddhakṣetrāṇy uddahyante kalpoddāhena, tad api sarvam agniskandhaṃ svamukhe prakṣipet / yac ca tena karma kartavyaṃ bhavet,
english: He can take all the masses of fire of all the supernovas that ultimately consume all the universes of all the buddhafields into his stomach without interfering with their functions.

sanskrit: yac cāvastād gaṅgānadīvālikākoṭīsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣv atikramya buddhakṣetram, tad abhyutkṣipyordhaṃ digbhāgaṃ gaṅgānadīvālikākoṭīsameṣu buddhakṣetreṣu pratiṣṭhāpayet / tadyathāpi nāma balavān puruṣaḥ sūcyagreṇa badarīpatram utkṣipet /
english: Having crossed buddhafields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges downward, and having taken up a buddhafield, he can rise up through buddhafields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and place it on high, just as a strong man may pick up a jujube leaf on the point of a needle.

sanskrit: evam acṃtyavimokṣapratiṣṭhito bodhisatvaḥ sarvasatvāni cakravartyādirūpāṇy adhitiṣṭhet /
english: “Thus, a bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation can magically transform any kind of living being into a universal monarch, a Lokapāla, a Śakra, a Brahmā, a disciple, a solitary sage, a bodhisattva, and even into a buddha.

sanskrit: yāvantaś ca daśasu dikṣu śabdāvabhāsāḥ śabdaprajñāptayaḥ, tāḥ sarvā hīnamadhyaviśiṣṭānāṃ satvānāṃ sarvabuddhaghoṣarutaracitāny adhitiṣṭhan, tataś ca rutaghoṣād anityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmaśabdarutāni niścārayet /
english: The bodhisattva can transform miraculously all the cries and noisessuperior, mediocre, and inferior, of all living beings of the ten directions, into the voice of the Buddha, with the words of the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, having them proclaim, ‘Impermanent! Selfless!’

sanskrit: yāvadbhiś cākāranirdeśair daśasu dikṣu buddhā bhagavanto dharmaṃ deśayanti, tāṃs tato rutanirghoṣān niścārayet /
english: And he can cause them to recite the words and sounds of all the teachings taught by all the buddhas of the ten directions.

sanskrit: ayaṃ bhadantaśāriputra acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ yatkiṃcinmātro viṣayāvatāranirdeśaḥ /
english: “Reverend Śāriputra, I have shown you only a small part of the entrance into the domain of the bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation.

sanskrit: api tu kalpam ahaṃ bhadantaśāriputra kalpāvaśesaṃ vācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ viṣayānāṃ viṣayāvatāranirdeśaṃ nirdiśeyam,
english: Reverend Śāriputra, to explain to you the teaching of the full entrance into the domain of the bodhisattva who lives in the inconceivable liberation would require more than an eon, and even more than that.”

sanskrit: atha khalu sthaviro mahākāśyapa imaṃ bodhisatvānām acintyavimokṣaṃ śrutvāścaryaprāptaḥ sthaviraṃ śāriputram etad avocat tadyathāpi nāma āyuṣmañ śāriputra jātyandhasya puruṣasya purastāt kaścid eva sarvarūpagatāny upadarśayet /
english: Then, the patriarch Mahākāśyapa, having heard this teaching of the inconceivable liberation of the bodhisattvas, was amazed, and he said to the venerable Śāriputra, “Venerable Śāriputra, if one were to show a variety of things to a person blind from birth, he would not be able to see a single thing.

sanskrit: evam eva āyuṣmañ śāriputra ihācintyavimokṣe nirdiśyamāne sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhā iha jātyandhā iva cakṣurvihīnā ekasminn apy acintyakāraṇe na pratyakṣāḥ /
english: Likewise, venerable Śāriputra, when this door of the inconceivable liberation is taught, all the disciples and solitary sages are sightless, like the man blind from birth, and cannot comprehend even a single cause of the inconceivable liberation.

sanskrit: ko nāma vidvān imam acintyaṃ vimokṣaṃ śrutvānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittaṃ notpādayet /
english: Who is there among the wise who, hearing about this inconceivable liberation, does not conceive the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment?

sanskrit: tat kiṃ nu bhūyaḥ kariṣyāmo 'tyantopahatendriyā dagdhavinaṣṭānīva bījāny abhājanībhūtā iha mahāyāne /
english: As for us, whose faculties are deteriorated, like a burned and rotten seed, what else can we do if we do not become receptive to this Great Vehicle?

sanskrit: sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhair imaṃ dharmanirdeśaṃ śrutvā rudadbhis trisāhasramahāsāhasro lokadhātur vijñāpayitavyaḥ / sarvabodhisatvaiś ca pramuditair imam acintyavimokṣaṃ śrutvā mūrdhnā saṃpratyetavyaḥ, adhimuktibalaṃ ca saṃjanayitavyam /
english: We, all the disciples and solitary sages, upon hearing this teaching of the Dharma, should utter a cry of regret that would shake this billionworld galactic universe! And as for the bodhisattvas, when they hear this inconceivable liberation they should be as joyful as a young crown prince when he takes the diadem and is anointed, and they should increase to the utmost their devotion to this inconceivable liberation.

sanskrit: yasyaiṣācintyavimokṣādhimuktiḥ sarvamārās tasya kiṃ kariṣyanti /
english: Indeed, what could the entire host of māras ever do to one who is devoted to this inconceivable liberation?”

sanskrit: imaṃ nirdeśaṃ nirdiśataḥ sthavirasya mahākāśyapasya dvātriṃśatā devaputrasahasrair anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau cittāny utpannāni /
english: When the patriarch Mahākāśyapa had uttered this discourse, thirtytwo thousand gods conceived the spirit of unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: atha vimalakīrtir licchaviḥ sthaviraṃ mahākāśyapam evam āha yāvanto bhadantamahākāśyapa daśasu dikṣv aprameyeṣu lokadhātuṣu mārā māratvaṃ kārayanti, sarve te yadbhūyasācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitā bodhisatvā upāyakauśalyena satvaparipācanāya māratvaṃ kārayanti / yāvadbhir bhadantamahākāśyapa daśasu dikṣv aprameyeṣu lokadhātuṣu bodhisatvā yācanakair
english: Then, the Licchavi Vimalakīrti said to the patriarch Mahākāśyapa, “Reverend Mahākāśyapa, the māras who play the devil in the innumerable universes of the ten directions are all bodhisattvas dwelling in the inconceivable liberation, who are playing the devil in order to develop living beings through their skill in liberative art.

sanskrit: śirāṃsi vāṅgapratyaṅgāni vā rājyarāṣṭrajanapadān vā bhāryāputraduhitṝr vā dāsadāsīr vā hayagajarathavāhanāni vā suvarṇamaṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṅkhaśilāpravāḍamaṇiratnajātaṃ vānnapānāni rasān vā, vastrāṇi cotpīḍya yācyante, sarve te yācanakā yadbhūyasācintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitā bodhisatvā upāyakauśalyenemāṃ dṛḍhādhyāśayatāṃ darśayanti /
english: Reverend Mahākāśyapa, all the miserable beggars who come to the bodhisattvas of the innumerable universes of the ten directions to ask for a hand, a foot, an ear, a nose, some blood, muscles, bones, marrow, an eye, a torso, a head, a limb, a member, a throne, a kingdom, a country, a wife, a son, a daughter, a slave, a slavegirl, a horse, an elephant, a chariot, a cart, gold, silver, jewels, pearls, conches, crystal, coral, beryl, treasures, food, drink, elixirs, and clothesthese demanding beggars are usually bodhisattvas living in the inconceivable liberation who, through their skill in liberative art, wish to test and thus demonstrate the firmness of the high resolve of the bodhisattvas.

sanskrit: ugratapaso hi bhadantamahākāśyapa bodhisatvās ta evaṃ darśayanti /
english: Reverend Mahākāśyapa, the bodhisattvas demonstrate that firmness by means of terrible austerities.

sanskrit: nāsti hi prākṛtajanasyāsthānānavakāśakṛtasya bodhisatvam utpīḍayitum /
english: Ordinary persons have no power to be thus demanding of bodhisattvas, unless they are granted the opportunity.

sanskrit: tadyathāpi nāma bhadantamahākāśyapa na śaktir asti khadyotakasya sūryamaṇḍalaprabhām abhibhavitum / evam eva bhadantamahākāśyapa na śaktir asti prākṛtasya janasya bodhisatvenānavakāśakṛtasyopasaṃkramituṃ yācituṃ vā /
english: “Reverend Mahākāśyapa, just as a glowworm cannot eclipse the light of the sun, so, reverend Mahākāśyapa, it is not possible without special allowance that an ordinary person can thus attack and deprive a bodhisattva.

sanskrit: tadyathā bhadantamahākāśyapa yo hastināgasya prahāro na sa śakyo gardabhena soḍhum / evam eva bhadantamahākāśyapa na śakyam abodhisatvena bodhisatvasyotpīḍanaṃ soḍhum /
english: Reverend Mahākāśyapa, just as a donkey could not muster an attack on a wild elephant, even so, reverend Mahākāśyapa, one who is not himself a bodhisattva cannot harass a bodhisattva.

sanskrit: bodhisatva eva bodhisatvotpīḍāṃ sahate /
english: Only one who is himself a bodhisattva can harass another bodhisattva, and only a bodhisattva can tolerate the harassment of another bodhisattva.

sanskrit: ayaṃ bhadantamahākāśyapa acintyavimokṣapratiṣṭhitānāṃ bodhisatvānām upāyajñānabalapraveśaḥ // //
english: Reverend Mahākāśyapa, such is the introduction to the power of the knowledge of liberative art of the bodhisattvas who live in the inconceivable liberation.”

sanskrit: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim etad avocat
english: Thereupon, Mañjuśrī, the crown prince, addressed the Licchavi Vimalakīrti

sanskrit: kathaṃ satpuruṣa bodhisatvena sarvasatvā avekṣitavyāḥ /
english: “Good sir, how should a bodhisattva regard all living beings?”

sanskrit: tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ marīcikāyām udakam, evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvā avekṣitavyāḥ / tadyathā mañjuśrīḥ māyākāro māyākāranirmitaṃ puruṣam avekṣeta,
english: Vimalakīrti replied, “Mañjuśrī, a bodhisattva should regard all living beings as a wise man regards the reflection of the moon in water or as magicians regard men created by magic.

sanskrit: evaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ /
english: “Precisely thus, Mañjuśrī, does a bodhisattva who realizes ultimate selflessness consider all beings.”

sanskrit: āha yadi kulaputraivaṃ bodhisatvena sarvasatvāḥ pratyavekṣitavyāḥ, kathaṃ punar asya mahāmaitrī bhavati sarvasatveṣu /
english: Mañjuśrī then asked further, “‌Noble sir, if a bodhisattva considers all living beings in such a way, how does he generate the great love toward them?”

sanskrit: āha yadā mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatva evaṃ pratyavekṣate,
english: Vimalakīrti replied, “Mañjuśrī, when a bodhisattva considers all living beings in this way, he thinks

sanskrit: iyaṃ mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvasya mahāmaitrī /
english: Such, Mañjuśrī, is the great love of a bodhisattva.”

sanskrit: āha katarā punar asya mahākaruṇā /
english: What is the great compassion of a bodhisattva?

sanskrit: āha yat kṛtaṃ kṛtaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ sarvasatvebhya utsṛjati /
english: It is the giving of all accumulated roots of virtue to all living beings.

sanskrit: āha katarā punar asya mahāmuditā /
english: Mañjuśrī What is the great joy of a bodhisattva?

sanskrit: āha yad datvāttamanā bhavati, na vipratisārī /
english: Vimalakīrti It is to be joyful and without regret in giving.

sanskrit: āha katarā punar asya mahopekṣā /
english: What is the equanimity of a bodhisattva?

sanskrit: āha yobhayato 'rthatā /
english: It is what benefits both self and others.

sanskrit: āha saṃsārabhayabhītena kiṃ pratipattavyam /
english: To what should one resort when terrified by fear of life?

sanskrit: āha saṃsārabhayabhītena mañjuśriḥ bodhisatvena buddhamāhātmyaṃ pratipattavyam /
english: Mañjuśrī, a bodhisattva who is terrified by fear of life should resort to the magnanimity of the Buddha.

sanskrit: āha buddhamāhātmye sthātukāmena kutra sthātavyam /
english: Where should he who wishes to resort to the magnanimity of the Buddha take his stand?

sanskrit: āha buddhamāhātmye sthātukāmena sarvasatvasamatāyāṃ sthātavyam /
english: He should stand in equanimity toward all living beings.

sanskrit: āha sarvasatvasamatāyāṃ sthātukāmena kutra sthātavyam /
english: Where should he who wishes to stand in equanimity toward all living beings take his stand?

sanskrit: āha sarvasatvasamatāyāṃ sthātukāmena sarvasatvapramokṣāya sthātavyam /
english: He should live for the liberation of all living beings.

sanskrit: āha sarvasatvapramokṣaṃ kartukāmena kiṃ kartavyam /
english: What should he who wishes to liberate all living beings do?

sanskrit: āha sarvasatvapramokṣaṃ kartukāmena kleśapramokṣaḥ kartavyaḥ /
english: He should liberate them from their afflictions.

sanskrit: āha kleśān utsraṣṭukāmena kathaṃ prayuktena bhavitavyam /
english: How should he who wishes to eliminate afflictions apply himself?

sanskrit: āha kleśān utsraṣṭukāmena yoniśaḥ prayuktena bhavitavyam /
english: He should apply himself appropriately.

sanskrit: āha kathaṃ prayuktaḥ punar yoniśaḥ prayukto bhavati /
english: How should he apply himself, to “apply himself appropriately”?

sanskrit: āha anutpādānirodhaprayukto yoniśaḥ prayukto bhavati /
english: He should apply himself to productionlessness and to destructionlessness.

sanskrit: āha kiṃ notpādayati,
english: What is not produced?

sanskrit: kiṃ na nirodhayati /
english: And what is not destroyed?

sanskrit: āha akuśalaṃ notpādayati, kuśalaṃ na nirodhayati /
english: Evil is not produced and good is not destroyed.

sanskrit: āha kuśalasyākuśalasya ca kiṃ mūlam /
english: What is the root of good and evil?

sanskrit: āha satkāyo mūlam /
english: Materiality is the root of good and evil.

sanskrit: āha satkāyasya ca punaḥ kiṃ mūlam /
english: What is the root of materiality?

sanskrit: āha satkāyasyecchālobhau mūlam /
english: Desire is the root of materiality.

sanskrit: āha icchālobhayoḥ kiṃ mūlam /
english: What is the root of desire and attachment?

sanskrit: āha icchālobhayor abhūtaparikalpo mūlam /
english: Vimalakīrti Unreal construction is the root of desire.

sanskrit: āha abhūtaparikalpasya kiṃ mūlam /
english: What is the root of unreal construction?

sanskrit: āha abhūtaparikalpasya viparyastā saṃjñā mūlam /
english: Vimalakīrti The false concept is its root.

sanskrit: āha viparyastāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ kiṃ mūlam /
english: What is the root of the false concept?

sanskrit: āha viparyastāyāḥ saṃjñāyā apratiṣṭhā mūlam /
english: Vimalakīrti Baselessness.

sanskrit: āha apratiṣṭhāyāḥ kiṃ mūlam /
english: What is the root of baselessness?

sanskrit: āha yan mañjuśrīḥ apratiṣṭhānaṃ tasya kiṃ mūlaṃ bhaviṣyati /
english: Mañjuśrī, when something is baseless, how can it have any root?

sanskrit: iti hy apratiṣṭhānamūlapratiṣṭhitāḥ sarvadharmāḥ /
english: Therefore, all things stand on the root that is baseless.

sanskrit: atha yā tatra gṛhe devatā prativasati, sā teṣāṃ bodhisatvānāṃ mahāsatvānām imaṃ dharmanirdeśaṃ śrutvā tuṣṭodagrāttamanā, audārikam ātmabhāvaṃ saṃdarśya divyaiḥ puṣpais tān mahāsatvāṃs tāṃś ca mahāśrāvakān abhyavakirati sma /
english: Thereupon, a certain goddess who lived in that house, having heard this teaching of the Dharma of the great heroic bodhisattvas, and being delighted, pleased, and overjoyed, manifested herself in a material body and showered the great spiritual heroes, the bodhisattvas, and the great disciples with heavenly flowers.

sanskrit: abhyavakīrṇānāṃ ca tatra yāni bodhisatvānāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi patitāni, tāni dharaṇitale pratiṣṭhitāni / yāni punar mahāśrāvakāṇāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi patitāni, tāni tatraiva sthitāni na bhūmau patitāni /
english: When the flowers fell on the bodies of the bodhisattvas, they fell off on the floor, but when they fell on the bodies of the great disciples, they stuck to them and did not fall.

sanskrit: tatas te mahāśrāvakā ṛddhiprātihāryaiḥ tāni puṣpāṇy utsṛjanti, na ca patanti /
english: The great disciples shook the flowers and even tried to use their magical powers, but still the flowers would not shake off.

sanskrit: atha sā devatāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram evam āha kiṃ bhadantaśāriputra,
english: Then, the goddess said to the venerable Śāriputra, “Reverend Śāriputra, why do you shake these flowers?”

sanskrit: etāni puṣpāṇy utsṛjasi / āha akalpikāni devate etāni puṣpāṇi / tasmād aham etāni puṣpāṇy apanayāmi /
english: Śāriputra replied, “Goddess, these flowers are not proper for religious persons and so we are trying to shake them off.”

sanskrit: devatāha mā bhadantaśāriputra evaṃ vocaḥ /
english: The goddess said, “Do not say that, reverend Śāriputra.

sanskrit: etāni hi puṣpāṇi kalpikāni /
english: These flowers are proper indeed!

sanskrit: tathā hy etāni puṣpāṇi na kalpayanti na vikalpayanti /
english: Such flowers have neither constructual thought nor discrimination.

sanskrit: sthaviraḥ punaḥ śāriputraḥ kalpayati vikalpayati ca /
english: But the elder Śāriputra has both constructual thought and discrimination.

sanskrit: ye bhadantaśāriputra svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyāṃ kalpayanti vikalpayanti ca, te 'kalpikāḥ / sthaviras tu kalpayati vikalpayati ca /
english: “Reverend Śāriputra, impropriety for one who has renounced the world for the discipline of the rightly taught Dharma consists of constructual thought and discrimination, yet the elders are full of such thoughts.

sanskrit: ye punar na kalpayanti na vikalpayanti, te kalpikāḥ /
english: One who is without such thoughts is always proper.

sanskrit: paśya bhadantaśāriputra eṣāṃ mahāsatvānāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi na śliṣyanti /
english: “Reverend Śāriputra, see how these flowers do not stick to the bodies of these great spiritual heroes, the bodhisattvas!

sanskrit: yathāpi nāma sarvakalpavikalpaprahīṇatvāt /
english: This is because they have eliminated constructual thoughts and discriminations.

sanskrit: tadyathāpi nāma bhīrukajātīyasya puruṣasyāmanuṣyā avatāraṃ Iabhante / evam eva saṃsārabhayabhītānāṃ rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāny avatāraṃ labhante / ye punaḥ sarvasaṃsārakleśabhayavigatāḥ,
english: “In the same way that evil spirits have power over fearful men but cannot disturb the fearless, those intimidated by fear of the world are in the power of forms, sounds, smells, tastes, and textures, which do not disturb those who are free from fear of the passions inherent in the constructive world.

sanskrit: kiṃ teṣāṃ rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyāni kariṣyanti / yeṣāṃ vāsanāprahīṇā, teṣāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi śliṣyanti /
english: Thus, these flowers stick to the bodies of those who have not eliminated their instincts for the passions and do not stick to the bodies of those who have eliminated their instincts.

sanskrit: tasmāt sarvavāsanāprahīṇānāṃ kāye puṣpāṇi na śliṣyanti /
english: Therefore, the flowers do not stick to the bodies of these bodhisattvas, who have abandoned all instincts.”

sanskrit: atha khalv āyuṣmāñ śāriputras tāṃ devatām etad avocat kiyacciraniviṣṭā punas tvaṃ devate iha gṛhe /
english: Then the venerable Śāriputra said to the goddess, “Goddess, how long have you been in this house?”

sanskrit: āha yāvacciraniviṣṭā sthavirasyāryā vimuktiḥ /
english: The goddess replied, “I have been here as long as the elder has been in liberation.”

sanskrit: āha na cirasthitā tvaṃ devate iha gṛhe / āha kiyacciraniviṣṭā punaḥ sthavirasyāryā vimuktiḥ /
english: The goddess said, “Has the elder been in liberation for quite some time?”

sanskrit: tataḥ sthaviras tūṣṇīm abhūt /
english: At that, the elder Śāriputra fell silent.

sanskrit: āha kim idānīṃ mahāprajñānām agryaḥ sthaviras tūṣṇīm abhūt /
english: The goddess continued, “Elder, you are ‘foremost of the wise!’ Why do you not speak?

sanskrit: prāptakālaṃ praśnaṃ na visarjayati /
english: Now, when it is your turn, you do not answer the question.”

sanskrit: āha apravyāhārā hi devate vimuktiḥ / tan na jāne kiṃ vyāharāmīti /
english: Since liberation is inexpressible, goddess, I do not know what to say. Goddess

sanskrit: sarvāṇy etāny akṣarāṇi vimuktilakṣaṇāni /
english: All the syllables pronounced by the elder have the nature of liberation.

sanskrit: yā hi sā vimuktiḥ, sā nādhyātmaṃ na bahir nobhayam antareṇopalabhyate / evam akṣarāṇy api /
english: Liberation is neither internal nor external, nor can it be apprehended apart from them. Likewise, syllables are neither internal nor external, nor can they be apprehended anywhere else.

sanskrit: tasmāt tarhi bhadantaśāriputra mā akṣarāpanayena vimuktiṃ nirdiśa /
english: Therefore, reverend Śāriputra, do not point to liberation by abandoning speech! Why?

sanskrit: sarvadharmasamatā hi vimuktiḥ /
english: The holy liberation is the equality of all things!

sanskrit: āha nanu devate rāgadoṣamohavigamād vimuktiḥ /
english: Goddess, is not liberation the freedom from desire, hatred, and folly?

sanskrit: devatāha abhimānikānām eṣa nirdeṣo rāgadoṣamohavigamād vimuktir iti / ye nirabhimānikāḥ, teṣāṃ rāgadoṣamohaprakṛtir eva vimuktiḥ /
english: “Liberation is freedom from desire, hatred, and folly”that is the teaching for the excessively proud. But those free of pride are taught that the very nature of desire, hatred, and folly is itself liberation.

sanskrit: atha khalv āyuṣmāñ śāriputras tāṃ devatām etad avocat
english: Śāriputra

sanskrit: sādhu sādhu devate kiṃ tvayā prāptaṃ kiṃ vā sākṣātkṛtam, yasyās ta īdṛśaṃ pratibhānam /
english: Excellent! Excellent, goddess! Pray, what have you attained, what have you realized, that you have such eloquence? Goddess

sanskrit: āha na mayā bhadantaśāriputra kiṃcit prāptaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ vā /
english: I have attained nothing, reverend Śāriputra. I have no realization.

sanskrit: tena ma īdṛśaṃ pratibhānam /
english: Therefore I have such eloquence.

sanskrit: yeṣām evaṃ bhavaty asmābhiḥ prāptaṃ vā sākṣātkṛtaṃ ceti,
english: Whoever thinks, “I have attained!

sanskrit: te svākhyāte dharmavinaya ābhimānikā ity ucyante /
english: I have realized!” is overly proud in the discipline of the well taught Dharma.

sanskrit: āha kiṃ tvaṃ devate śrāvakayānikā pratyekabuddhayānikā mahāyānikā vā /
english: Goddess, do you belong to the Disciple Vehicle, to the Solitary Sage Vehicle, or to the Great Vehicle? Goddess

sanskrit: āha śrāvakāyānikāsmi śrāvakayānasūcanatayā,
english: I belong to the Disciple Vehicle when I teach it to those who need it.

sanskrit: pratyekabuddhayānikāsmi pratītyadharmāvatāreṇa, mahāyānikāsmi mahākaruṇānutsṛjanatayā /
english: And, since I never abandon the great compassion, I belong to the Great Vehicle, as all need that teaching to attain ultimate liberation.

sanskrit: api tu khalu punar bhadantaśāriputra na campakavanaṃ praviṣṭā eraṇḍagandhaṃ jighranti / campakavanaṃ tu praviṣṭāś campakagandham eva jighranti / evam eva bhadantaśāriputra neha gṛhe buddhadharmaguṇagandhike vasantaḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhagandhaiḥ jighranti /
english: Nevertheless, reverend Śāriputra, just as one cannot smell the castor plant in a magnolia wood, but only the magnolia flowers, so, reverend Śāriputra, living in this house, which is redolent with the perfume of the virtues of the buddha qualities, one does not smell the perfume of the disciples and the solitary sages.

sanskrit: ye 'pi bhadantaśāriputra śakrabrahmalokapālā devanāgayakṣagandharvāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragā idaṃ gṛhaṃ praviśanti, te 'py asya satpuruṣasya dharmaśravaṇena buddhadharmaguṇagandhenotpāditabodhicittā niṣkrāmanti /
english: Reverend Śāriputra, the Śakras, the Brahmās, the Lokapālas, the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, and mahoragas who live in this house hear the Dharma from the mouth of this holy man and, enticed by the perfume of the virtues of the buddha qualities, proceed to conceive the spirit of enlightenment.

sanskrit: dvādaśavarṣāṇy upādāya bhadantaśāriputra prativasantyā me na jātu śrāvakapratyekabuddhasaṃprayuktā kathā śrutapūrvā, nānyatra mahāmaitrīmahākaruṇāpratisaṃyuktaivācintyadharmapratisaṃyuktaiva /
english: Reverend Śāriputra, I have been in this house for twelve years, and I have heard no discourses concerning the disciples and solitary sages but have heard only those concerning the great love, the great compassion, and the inconceivable qualities of the Buddha.

sanskrit: iha bhadantaśāriputra gṛhe 'ṣṭāv āścaryādbhutā dharmāḥ satatasamitaṃ saṃdṛśyante /
english: Reverend Śāriputra, eight strange and wonderful things manifest themselves constantly in this house.

sanskrit: katame 'ṣṭau /
english: What are these eight?

sanskrit: neha rātrir vā divaso vā prajñāyate sadāvabhāsitam idaṃ gṛhaṃ suvarṇavarṇayā prabhayā / neha sūryācandramasau prajñāyete, na bhrājete /
english: A light of golden hue shines here constantly, so bright that it is hard to distinguish day and night, and neither the moon nor the sun shines here distinctly.

sanskrit: ayaṃ prathama āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
english: That is the first wonder of this house.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra ye praviśantīdaṃ gṛham, teṣāṃ samanantarapraviṣṭānāṃ sarvakleśā na bādhante /
english: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, whoever enters this house is no longer troubled by his afflictions from the moment he is within.

sanskrit: ayaṃ dvitīya āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
english: That is the second strange and wonderful thing.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra idaṃ gṛham avirahitaṃ śakrabrahmalokapālair anyabuddhakṣetrasaṃnipatitaiś ca bodhisatvaiḥ /
english: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, this house is never forsaken by Śakra, Brahmā, the Lokapālas, and the bodhisattvas from all the other buddhafields.

sanskrit: ayaṃ tṛtīya āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
english: That is the third strange and wonderful thing.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra idaṃ gṛhaṃ satatasamitam avirahitaṃ dharmaśravaṇena ṣaṭpāramitāpratisaṃyuktayā kathayāvivartyadharmakathayā ca
english: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, this house is never empty of the sounds of the Dharma, the discourse on the six transcendences, and the discourses of the irreversible wheel of the Dharma.

sanskrit: ayaṃ caturtha āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
english: That is the fourth strange and wonderful thing.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra iha gṛhe yās tūryasaṃgītayo divyamānuṣyakāṇi vā vādyāni vādyante, tebhyas tūryebhyo 'pramāṇo dharmaśabdanirhāro niścarati sārvakālikaḥ /
english: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, in this house one always hears the rhythms, songs, and music of gods and men, and from this music constantly resounds the sound of the infinite Dharma of the Buddha.

sanskrit: ayaṃ pañcama āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
english: That is the fifth strange and wonderful thing.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra iha gṛhe catvāri mahānidhānāni sarvaratnaparipūrṇāny akṣayāṇi yato niṣyandaṃ sarvadaridrakṛpaṇā ādāya prakrāmanti, na ca kṣīyante /
english: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, in this house there are always four inexhaustible treasures, replete with all kinds of jewels, which never decrease, although all the poor and wretched may partake of them to their satisfaction.

sanskrit: ayaṃ ṣaṣṭha āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
english: That is the sixth strange and wonderful thing.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra iha gṛhe śākyamunis tathāgato 'mitābho 'kṣobhyo ratnaśrī ratnārcī ratnacandro ratnavyūho duḥprasahaḥ sarvārthasiddhaḥ prabhūtaratnaḥ siṃhanādanādī siṃhaghoṣas tathāgata evaṃ pramukhā daśasu dikṣv apramāṇās tathāgatā ye 'sya satpuruṣasya cintitamātreṇāgacchanti / āgatya ca tathāgataguhyaṃ nāma dharmamukhapraveśaṃ deśayitvā prakrāmanti /
english: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, at the wish of this good man, to this house come the innumerable tathāgatas of the ten directions, such as the Tathāgatas Śākyamuni, Amitābha, Akṣobhya, Ratnaśrī‌, Ratnārcis, Ratnacandra, Ratnavyūha, Duḥprasāha, Sarvārtha­siddha, Prabhūtaratna, Siṃhanādanādī, Siṃhaghoṣa, and so forth, and when they come they teach the door of Dharma called The Secrets of the Tathāgatas, and then depart.

sanskrit: punar aparaṃ bhadantaśāriputra iha gṛhe sarvadevabhavanavyūhāḥ sarvabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhāś ca saṃdṛśyante /
english: Furthermore, reverend Śāriputra, all the splendors of the abodes of the gods and all the splendors of the fields of the buddhas shine forth in this house.

sanskrit: ayam aṣṭama āścaryādbhuto dharmaḥ /
english: That is the eighth strange and wonderful thing.

sanskrit: ime bhadantaśāriputra aṣṭāv āścaryādbhutā dharmāḥ satatasamitam iha gṛhe saṃdṛśyante /
english: Reverend Śāriputra, these eight strange and wonderful things are seen in this house.

sanskrit: ka imām acintyadharmatāṃ paśyañ śrāvakadharmatāyai spṛhayet /
english: Who then, seeing such inconceivable things, would believe the teaching of the disciples?

sanskrit: āha kiṃ tvaṃ devate strībhāvaṃ na nivartayasi /
english: Goddess, what prevents you from transforming yourself out of your female state?

sanskrit: āha paripūrṇāni me dvādaśavarṣāṇy upādāya strībhāvaṃ paryeṣamāṇāyā na cainaṃ labhe /
english: Although I have sought my “female state” for these twelve years, I have not yet found it.

sanskrit: api ca bhadantaśāriputra yā māyākāreṇa strīnirmitā yas tām evaṃ vadet kiṃ tvaṃ strībhāvaṃ na nivartayasīti, sa kiṃ vadet /
english: Reverend Śāriputra, if a magician were to incarnate a woman by magic, would you ask her, “What prevents you from transforming yourself out of your female state?”

sanskrit: āha na tasyāḥ kācit bhūtā pariniṣpattiḥ /
english: Such a woman would not really exist, so what would there be to transform?

sanskrit: āha evam eva bhadantaśāriputra apariniṣpanneṣu sarvadharmeṣu māyānirmitasvabhāveṣu kutas tavaivaṃ bhavati kiṃ tvaṃ strībhāvaṃ na nivartayasīti /
english: Just so, reverend Śāriputra, all things do not really exist. Now, would you think, “What prevents one whose nature is that of a magical incarnation from transforming herself out of her female state?”

sanskrit: atha sā devatā tādṛśam adhiṣṭhānam adhitiṣṭhati sma / yathā sthaviraḥ śāriputro yādṛśī sā devatā tādṛśaḥ saṃdṛśyate,
english: Thereupon, the goddess employed her magical power to cause the elder Śāriputra to appear in her form and to cause herself to appear in his form.

sanskrit: atha sā devatā śāriputrarūpā śāriputraṃ devatārūpadhāriṇam apṛcchat kiṃ bhadantaśāriputra strībhāvaṃ na nivartayasi / śāriputro devatārūpy āha
english: Then the goddess, transformed into Śāriputra, said to Śāriputra, transformed into a goddess, “Reverend Śāriputra, what prevents you from transforming yourself out of your female state?”

sanskrit: na jāne kiṃ vinivartayāmīti /
english: I do not know what to transform!”

sanskrit: āha yadi sthaviraḥ śakṣyati strībhāvaṃ vinivartayitum, tataḥ sarvāḥ striyo 'pi strībhāvaṃ vinivartayiṣyanti /
english: The goddess continued, “If the elder could again change out of the female state, then all women could also change out of their female states.

sanskrit: yathā sthaviro na strī strīva saṃdṛśyate, evaṃ sarvastrīṇām api strīrūpaṃ na ca striyaḥ strīrūpāś ca saṃdṛśyante /
english: All women appear in the form of women in just the same way as the elder appears in the form of a woman. While they are not women in reality, they appear in the form of women.

sanskrit: idaṃ saṃdhāya bhagavān āha ḥsarvadharmā na strī na puruṣaḥ iti /
english: With this in mind, the Buddha said, ‘In all things, there is neither male nor female.’ ”

sanskrit: atha sā devatā tad adhiṣṭhānam avāsṛjat /
english: Then, the goddess released her magical power and each returned to their ordinary form.

sanskrit: atha sā devatāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram evam āha kva nu te bhadantaśāriputra strīrūpaṃ kṛtaṃ gatam /
english: She then said to him, “Reverend Śāriputra, what have you done with your female form?” Śāriputra

sanskrit: āha na tat kṛtaṃ na vikṛtam /
english: I neither made it nor did I change it.

sanskrit: āha evam eva sarvadharmā na kṛtā na vikṛtāḥ / yatra ca na kṛtir na vikṛtis tad buddhavacanam /
english: Just so, all things are neither made nor changed, and that they are not made and not changed, that is the teaching of the Buddha.

sanskrit: āha itas tvaṃ devate cyutā kutropapatsyase /
english: Goddess, where will you be born when you transmigrate after death?

sanskrit: āha yatraiva tathāgatanirmita upapatsyate, tatraivāham upapatsye /
english: I will be born where all the magical incarnations of the Tathāgata are born.

sanskrit: āha tathāgatanirmitasya na cyutir nopapattiḥ /
english: But the emanated incarnations of the Tathāgata do not transmigrate nor are they born.

sanskrit: āha evam eva sarvadharmāṇāṃ na cyutir nopapattiḥ /
english: All things and living beings are just the same they do not transmigrate nor are they born!

sanskrit: āha kiyaccireṇa punar devate bodhim abhisaṃbhotsyase /
english: Goddess, how soon will you attain the perfect enlightenment of buddhahood?

sanskrit: āha yadā sthaviraḥ pṛthagjanadharmasamanvāgato bhaviṣyati, tadāhaṃ bodhim abhisaṃbhotsye /
english: At such time as you, elder, become endowed once more with the qualities of an ordinary individual, then will I attain the perfect enlightenment of buddhahood.

sanskrit: āha asthānam etad devate yad ahaṃ pṛthagjanadharmasamanvāgataḥ syām /
english: Goddess, it is impossible that I should become endowed once more with the qualities of an ordinary individual.

sanskrit: āha evam eva bhadantaśāriputra asthānam etad yad ahaṃ bodhim abhisaṃbhotsye /
english: Just so, reverend Śāriputra, it is impossible that I should attain the perfect enlightenment of buddhahood!

sanskrit: asthānasthitaiva hi bodhiḥ /
english: Because perfect enlightenment stands upon the impossible.

sanskrit: tasmād asthānaṃ na kaścid abhisaṃbhotsyate /
english: Because it is impossible, no one attains the perfect enlightenment of buddhahood.

sanskrit: sthavira āha
english: Śāriputra

sanskrit: uktaṃ devate tathāgatena ḥgaṅgānadīvālikāsamās tathāgatā abhisaṃbuddhā abhisaṃbudhyante 'bhisaṃbhotsyante caḥ /
english: But the Tathāgata has declared “The tathāgatas, who are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, have attained perfect buddhahood, are attaining perfect buddhahood, and will go on attaining perfect buddhahood.”

sanskrit: devatāha akṣaragaṇanāsaṃketādhivacanam etad bhadantaśāriputra atītānāgatapratyutpannā buddhā iti /
english: Goddess Reverend Śāriputra, the expression “the buddhas of the past, present, and future” is a conventional expression made up of a certain number of syllables.

sanskrit: na punar buddhā atītā vānāgatā vā vartamānā vā /
english: The buddhas are neither past, nor present, nor future.

sanskrit: tryadhvasamatikrāntā hi bodhiḥ /
english: Their enlightenment transcends the three times!

sanskrit: api ca prāptaṃ sthavireṇārhatvam /
english: But tell me, elder, have you attained the state of arhat?

sanskrit: āha prāptam asaṃprāptikāraṇena /
english: It is attained, because there is no attainment.

sanskrit: āha evam evābhisaṃbodhir anabhisaṃbodhikāraṇena /
english: Just so, there is perfect enlightenment because there is no attainment of perfect enlightenment.

sanskrit: atha vimalakīrtir licchavir āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram evam āha dvānavatibuddhakoṭīparyupāsitā bhadantaśāriputra eṣā devatābhijñājñānavikrīḍitā praṇidhānasamucchritā
english: Then the Licchavi Vimalakīrti said to the venerable elder Śāriputra, “Reverend Śāriputra, this goddess has already served ninetytwo million billion buddhas. She plays with the superknowledges. She has truly succeeded in all her vows.

sanskrit: kṣāntipratilabdhāvaivartikasamavasaraṇā praṇidhānavaśena yathecchati tathā tiṣṭhati satvaparipākāya // //
english: She has gained the tolerance of the birthlessness of things. She has actually attained irreversibility. She can live wherever she wishes on the strength of her vow to develop living beings.”

sanskrit: atha khalu mañjuśrīḥ kumārabhūto vimalakīrtiṃ licchavim evam āha kathaṃ kulaputra bodhisatvo gatiṃgato bhavati buddhadharmeṣu /
english: Then, the crown prince Mañjuśrī asked the Licchavi Vimalakīrti, “‌Noble sir, how does the bodhisattva follow the way to attain the qualities of the Buddha?”

sanskrit: āha yadā mañjuśrīḥ bodhisatvo 'gatigamanaṃ gacchati, tadā bodhisatvo gatiṃgato bhavati buddhadharmeṣu /
english: Vimalakīrti replied, “Mañjuśrī, when the bodhisattva follows the wrong way, he follows the way to attain the qualities of the Buddha.”

sanskrit: āha katamac ca bodhisatvasyāgatigamanam /
english: Mañjuśrī continued, “How does the bodhisattva follow the wrong way?”

sanskrit: āha yadā pañcānantaryagatiṃ ca gacchati, na ca vyāpādavihiṃsāpraduṣṭo bhavati /
english: Vimalakīrti replied, “Even should he enact the five deadly sins, he feels no malice, violence, or hate.

sanskrit: nirayagatiṃ ca gacchati, sarvarajaḥkleśavigataś ca bhavati /
english: Even should he go into the hells, he remains free of all taint of afflictions.

sanskrit: apoddhāra vyavahṛtiḥ pṛthak tva ādyā tu kalpyate / kāraṇāt sā vibhinna ātma bhāva niṣṭhā na kim matā //
english: The notion of ‘being apart’, which is assumed as being due to the quality of ‘separateness’,—why has it not been held to rest in the various things of divergent characters?

sanskrit: paraspara vibhinnāḥ hi yathā buddhi sukha ādayaḥ / pṛthak vācyāḥ tad aṅgam ca vinā anyena tathā apare //
english: Just as cognition, pleasure and the rest, being different from one another, are spoken of as ‘separate’, and hence become the basis of that notion (of separateness), independently of anything else,—so would other things also

sanskrit: yau saṃyoga vibhāgau ca dravyeṣu niyatau paraiḥ / saṃyukta ādi dhiyaḥ hetū kalpitau tau anarthakau //
english: Conjunction and disjunction as restricted to substances have been postulated by others as causes of the notions of ‘being joined’ and the like; these are entirely useless

sanskrit: bīja udaka pṛthivyādi sarvadā kārya kārakam / prasaktam nirviśeṣa tvāt saṃyoga asaṃbhavena tu // kṣetra bīja jala ādīni sāpekṣāṇi iti gamyate / sva kārya karaṇāt nityam daṇḍa cakra udaka ādi vat // yaḥ taiḥ apekṣyate bhāvaḥ sa saṃyogaḥ bhaviṣyati / sa viśeṣaṇa bhāvāt ca bhinnaḥ eva iti gamyate // saṃyukte āhara iti ukte saṃyogam prekṣate yayoḥ / tad anya parihāreṇa te eva āharati hi ayam
english: If there were no conjunction, then the soil, the seed, the water and the earth and such things should be always producing their effects; as there would be no ground for differentiation.—As a matter of fact however, the soil, the seed, the water and such things are always found to require something else in the producing of their effects;—like the stick, the wheel and water, etc. (in the making of jar). That thing which they require is conjunction; and as it has a particular characteristic, it is regarded as distinct (from other things). when one is told to ‘bring two conjoined things’, he brings only those two things in which he perceives the conjunction, avoiding everything else.”

sanskrit: nirantaram idam vastu sāntaram ca idam iti ayam / buddhi bhedaḥ ca kena eṣa vidyate tau na ced iha //
english: If conjunction and disjunction were not there, then to what would such distinct notions be due as—‘this thing is attached to it’—‘this is detached from it’?”

sanskrit: yā ca iyam sāntare buddhiḥ nairantarya avasāyinī / nirantare api yā ca anyā mithyābuddhiḥ iyam dvidhā // mithyābuddhiḥ ca sarvā eva pradhāna artha anukāriṇī / pradhānam ca iha vaktavyam tad uktau tau ca siddhyataḥ //
english: It sometimes happens that even when one thing is really detached from another, it is perceived as attached to it,—and when the thing is really close to another, it is perceived as detached from it;—there are these two misconceptions. and a misconception has always some primary factor as its counterpart. this primary factor has to be pointed out in the two misconceptions cited. if such a primary factor is asserted, conjunction and disjunction become established.”

sanskrit: kuṇḍalī iti matiḥ ca iyam kid nimittā upajāyate / nara kuṇḍala bhāvāt no sarvadā tad prasaṅgataḥ // anyatra dṛṣṭa bhāvasya niṣedhaḥ anyatra yujyate  / saṃyogaḥ ca bhavet dṛṣṭaḥ sa katham pratiṣidhyate  // caitraḥ akuṇḍalaḥ iti evam tasmāt asti eva vāstavaḥ / yad niṣedha vidhāna ādi vibhāgena pravarttate
english: Then again, on what basis is the notion of ‘the man with earrings’ produced? It could not proceed from the mere presence of the man and the ear-ring; for in that case, the said notion would be there always.—Further, it is only something that has been perceived to be present in one place that is denied in another place. If conjunction has not been perceived, then how does it come to be denied in such expressions as ‘caitra is without ear-rings’? Hence it follows that there is some such real thing in the shape of conjunction, whose affirmation and denial proceed with due distinction.”

sanskrit: ucyate kṣaṇika tvena na aviśeṣāḥ jala ādayaḥ / sattve api avyavadhāna ādi te apekṣante daśā antaram //
english: The answer to the above is as follows:—The water and the rest do not remain the same, as all things are momentary.—Even when existent, they stand in need of that condition in which there is nothing intervening between them

sanskrit: saṃyoga mātra sāpekṣāḥ yadi tu syuḥ jala ādayaḥ / yoga anantaram eva syāt kāryam etena vā bhavet //
english: If the water, etc. needed the conjunction only, then they would appear immediately on their coming together (conjunction),—or not appear at all

sanskrit: prāpta avasthā viśeṣe hi nairantaryeṇa jātitaḥ / ye paśyati āharati eṣa vastunī te tathāvidhe //
english: When a man sees two things having come close together by themselves, he brings those things in that condition (when told to do so)

sanskrit: vicchinnam anyathā ca eva jātam eti nimitta tām  / sāntara anantara jñāne geha vindhya hima adri vat //
english: When a thing is produced in the detached form, it becomes the basis for the notion op being ‘detached’; on the other hand, when it is produced in the attached form, it becomes the basis of the notion of being ‘attached’;—just as in the case of the house, the vindhya mountain and the himalaya mountain

sanskrit: mithyābuddhiḥ na sarvā eva pradhāna artha anusāriṇī / sādharmya nirapekṣā api kācid antar upaplavāt // anyatra gata cittasya dvi candra ādi matiḥ yathā / avicchinna ādi jātam vā pradhānam iha vidyate //
english: A misconception does not appear always in accordance with a primary conception; for instance, the notion of ‘two moons’ appears independently of its similarity to any other (primary) notion, through some internal derangement, while the mind is turned elsewhere.—Or, the requisite ‘primary’ in the case in question may be that same thing which has been produced in the attached form and the like (but is misconceived as being detached or otherwise)

sanskrit: kuṇḍalī iti matiḥ ca iyam jāta avasthā viśeṣayoḥ / caitra kuṇḍalayoḥ eva saṃyogaḥ iva jāyate //
english: The notion of ‘the man with the ear-ring’ arises only with reference to caitra (the man) and the ear-ring, in whom a particular condition has come about; and it only appears as if the cognition were of ‘conjunction’ (between the two)

sanskrit: saḥ avasthā atiśayaḥ tādṛś dṛṣṭaḥ anyatra niṣidhyate / caitre kuṇḍale ityādau na saṃyogaḥ tu adṛṣṭitaḥ //
english: It is the one peculiar condition seen in one place which is denied in another place.—as regards the notion ‘caitra is without the ear-ring’, it is not conjunction that is denied; for the simple reason that this conjunction has never been seen

sanskrit: na para abhimatāt yogāt jāyate yukta vastu dhīḥ / yukta buddhi tayā yadvat prāsāda ādiṣu yukta dhīḥ // aneka vastu sadbhāve jāyamāna tayā athavā  / vibhakta aneka tantu ādi viṣayāḥ iva būddhayaḥ // vibhāge api yathāyogam vācyam etat pramā dvayam / ekasya aneka vṛttiḥ ca na yuktā iti prabādhakam //
english: The notion of things being ‘conjunct’ cannot be due to the conjunction postulated by the other party,a) because it is the notion op ‘being conjunct’,—like the notion op ‘being conjunct’ in connection with the mansion and such things;—or (b) because it appears only when there is more than one thing,—like the cognitions op several differentiated yarns.—The same two arguments may be urged mutatis mutandis, against disjunction also.—And the reason annulling (both these conceptions op conjunction and disjunction) consists in the pact that it cannot be right for one thing to subsist in more things than one

sanskrit: para apara abhidhāna ādi nimittam yat ca kalpyate / para tvam apara tvam ca diś kālau adhikam na tat // yathā nīla ādi rūpāṇi krama bhāva vyavasthiteḥ / anya upādhi viveke api tathā u acyante tathā apare //
english: The name (and idea) of ‘priority’ and ‘posteriority’ have been assumed as the basis of the notions of ‘fore’ and ‘aft’,—as these notions cannot be determined in reference to space and time.—But just as the blue and other colours, which come into existence in succession (one after the other), come to be spoken of ‘fore’ and ‘aft’, without reference to distinctions due to any other conditions,—so would the said notions be in regard to other things also

sanskrit: saṅkhyā yoga ādayaḥ sarve na dravya avyatirekiṇaḥ / tad vyavacchedaka tvena daṇḍa ādiḥ iva ced matam // teṣām saṃvṛti sattvena varṇana ādiṣṭa sādhanam / tattva anya tvena nirvācyam na eva saṃvṛti sadyataḥ //
english: If it be held that—“number, conjunction and the rest cannot be non-different from substance, because they serve to characterise and differentiate this latter,—like the stick”,—then [our answer is that] there is proving of what is admitted by us, if what is meant is that they have an ‘illusory existence’; because what is ‘imaginary’ cannot be defined either as ‘this’ or ‘not this

sanskrit: atha anirvacanīya tvam samūha ādeḥ niṣidhyate / yasmāt niyata dharma tvam rūpa śabda rasa ādi vat //
english: If the fact of the ‘group’ and such things being undefinable is denied (by the opponent) on the ground that they have distinctive features,—just like colour, sound, taste and other things,—[then our answer is as given in the next text]

sanskrit: niḥsvabhāva tayā tasya tattvataḥ ambara padma vat / na siddhāḥ niyatāḥ dharmāḥ kalpanā āropitāḥ tu te // tathā eva uktau anekāntaḥ viyat padma ādibhiḥ yatas  / abhedaḥ vyatirekaḥ ca vastuni eva vyavasthitaḥ //
english: In reality, the ‘group’ is absolutely feature-less; hence, like the ‘sky-lotus’, it can have no specific properties; they are all figments of imagination.—Even when stated in this form, the reasoning adduced would be ‘fallible’, in view of things like the ‘sky-lotus in fact, ‘non-difference’ as well as ‘difference’ rests always in an object

sanskrit: saṅkhyā ādeḥ dravyataḥ anya tvam evam ced pratipādyate / āśraya asiddha tā hetoḥ saṅkhyā ādīnām asiddhitaḥ //
